item.subject: b1.6: repair section 232 primary heading memberships

triage.commit_summary: The commit repairs the two generated Section 232 membership modules (note 16 steel, note 19 aluminum) whose primary-article tables had silently dropped every HTS number the notes print at a width other than a dotted 8/10-digit atom, adding 26 steel 4-digit heading rows, two steel 6-digit subheading rows, and the entire seven-row aluminum heading table plus its one 8-digit row. It does so by widening the generator's tokenizer (tools/generate_incidence_tables.py) to preserve the 4-, 6-, 8- and 10-digit widths as printed in notes 16(c)(iii) and 19(b), emitting the recovered rows into separate *_heading_membership and *_subheading6_membership tables with companion tests.

modules.description_quote: b1.6: repair section 232 primary heading memberships
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The Section 232 primary-steel membership encoding covered only the eleven dotted 8-digit entries in note 16(c)(iii)'s "Articles of steel" list and omitted the 26 bare 4-digit headings (7206-7229, 7304-7306) and the two 6-digit subheadings (7302.10, 7302.90) that the same list enumerates, so nearly all primary steel was encoded as a non-member of the Section 232 action list.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read and confirmed. Rev-15 notes page-236 (axiom-corpus commit 60de5efa, data/corpus/provisions/us/statute/2026-08-04-usitc-hts-2026-rev15-notes.jsonl, the file the generator pins via RELPATH) prints the note 16(c) list "(iii) Articles of steel: 7209 7208 7207 7206 7213 7212 7211 7210 7216.21.00 7216.10.00 7215 7214 7216.33.00 7216.32.00 7216.31.00 7216.22.00 7217 7216.99.00 7216.50.00 7216.40.00 7221 7220 7219 7218 7225 7224 7223 7222 7229 7228 7227 7226 7302.90 7302.40.00 7302.10 7301.10.00 7306 7305 7304". Pre-fix rules[s232_steel_primary_membership].versions[0].values held exactly the 11 dotted 8-digit members of that list and nothing else; post-fix that rule is unchanged and the two new tables carry the missing 4- and 6-digit widths, so the union now equals the printed list. Note the resolver caveat: resolve_provision.py resolves the toolchain pin to release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, which contains only the Rev-3 notes file, so its page-236 is unrelated Rev-3 content; the Rev-3 prose form of the same note (pages 228/231/235) independently corroborates that the primary list is stated at heading level (7206-7229, 7304-7306) with 7302.10/7302.90 at 6-digit, and I read the Rev-15 file directly from the pinned corpus commit for the decisive check. Root cause is in the same commit's tools/generate_incidence_tables.py diff: the old HTS regex matched only dotted 8/10-digit atoms; the new PRINTED_WIDTH_HTS regex plus per-production widths=(4, 6, 8) preserves printed width. B16-BUILD-REPORT.md in the same commit states verbatim: "Round-2 section 232 primary-scope repair: the tokenizer and independent differential scanner now preserve the 4-, 6-, and 8-digit widths printed in notes 16(c)(iii) and 19(b)." (the build report is not an allowed quote_source value, so the commit subject is quoted in the field instead). The module diff is pure addition; nothing else in the module changed (module citation paths already listed page-236). The companion test file gained 20 lines of present/absent cases for the new tables. Alternative kind a reviewer may prefer: wrong_entity_or_scope, since what was wrong is the covered population of HTS lines; I chose unrepresented_clause per the instruction that adding coverage the source requires is unrepresented_clause. Caveat for corpus use: this module is generator-produced (tools/generate_incidence_tables.py), not encoder-produced, so the defect is a parser-width bug rather than an LLM encoding error.

modules.description_quote: b1.6: repair section 232 primary heading memberships
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The module encoded only the note 19(j) derivative-aluminum lists and contained no primary-aluminum membership table at all, so every article note 19(b) places in the Section 232 primary action list (headings 7601 and 7604-7609 and subheading 7616.99.51) was encoded as outside the action.
modules.triage_notes: Same root-cause pattern as index 0 (one tokenizer fix in tools/generate_incidence_tables.py covers both modules), but the aluminum loss was total: pre-fix rule names were only s232_aluminum_derivative_membership and s232_aluminum_derivative_membership_hts10. Provision read and confirmed: Rev-15 notes page-253 (pinned corpus commit 60de5efa) states "(b) The rates of duty set forth in heading 9903.85.01 and subheadings 9903.85.05 and 9903.85.06, inclusive, apply to all imported products of aluminum classifiable in the provisions enumerated in this subdivision: (i) unwrought aluminum provided for in heading 7601: (ii) bars, rods and profiles provided for in heading 7604; wire provided for in heading 7605; (iii) plates, sheets and strip provided for in heading 7606; foil provided for in heading 7607; (iv) tubes, pipes and tube or pipe fittings provided for in heading 7608 and 7609; (v) castings and forgings of aluminum provided for in subheading 7616.99.51." The post-fix values (7601, 7604, 7605, 7606, 7607, 7608, 7609 at 4-digit; 76169951 at 8-digit) reproduce that list exactly. Why even the 8-digit row was missing pre-fix: the old regex ended with a (?![\d.]) lookahead and 7616.99.51 is followed by the sentence-ending period, so the only dotted atom in the 19(b) segment was rejected too; the new lookahead (?!\d|\.\d) accepts it. The diff also adds us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-253 to module.source_verification.corpus_citation_paths, provenance bookkeeping riding along with the substantive fix. Diff is pure addition; the existing derivative tables are untouched; companion test file gained 20 lines. Same alternative-kind caveat as index 0 (wrong_entity_or_scope vs unrepresented_clause), and same caveat that this is a generator-produced module rather than encoder output.

verdict.justification: The cited source, note 16(c)(iii) "Articles of steel:", enumerates 39 provisions at three printed widths (26 bare 4-digit headings 7206-7215/7217-7229/7304-7306, two 6-digit subheadings 7302.10 and 7302.90, and 11 dotted 8-digit lines), and the pre-fix module encoded only the 11 dotted lines — no 7206-7229, 7302.10/.90, or 7304-7306 key appears anywhere in the parent revision of the file. The fix adds those 28 source-enumerated memberships, and the generator diff shows the cause was a tokenizer that only matched dotted 8/10-digit forms (`HTS` regex; the fix adds `PRINTED_WIDTH_HTS` and `widths=(4, 6, 8)` on the 16(c)(iii) production), so the encoded meaning — which goods are on the Section 232 primary-steel action list — disagreed with the cited text. I tried to refute this as "new output surface the module never claimed" since the fix adds two new rules rather than editing the existing table, but the module already split tables by printed width pre-fix (`s232_steel_derivative_legacy_membership_hts10`), the existing rule's `source:` and every proof atom claim subdivision 16(c)(iii) in full, and the author frames it as a "repair". Kind fits: the fix adds source-stated content that was absent from the encoding.
verdict.justification_quote_note: quote field holds verbatim added diff lines
verdict.quote:
+  - name: s232_steel_primary_heading_membership
+    kind: parameter
...
+    versions:
+      - effective_from: '2026-08-03'
+        values:
+          7206: 1
+          7207: 1
+          7208: 1
verdict.notes: Source verification: the Rev-15 notes ingest the generator pins (data/corpus/provisions/us/statute/2026-08-04-usitc-hts-2026-rev15-notes.jsonl, line 246, citation_path us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-236) reads verbatim "(iii) Articles of steel: 7209 7208 7207 7206 7213 7212 7211 7210 7216.21.00 7216.10.00 7215 7214 7216.33.00 7216.32.00 7216.31.00 7216.22.00 7217 7216.99.00 7216.50.00 7216.40.00 7221 7220 7219 7218 7225 7224 7223 7222 7229 7228 7227 7226 7302.90 7302.40.00 7302.10 7301.10.00 7306 7305 7304" — exactly the 26 + 2 entries the fix adds plus the 11 retained. Caveat for the reviewer: resolve_provision.py --citation us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-236 --rulespec-commit a70eb63414 resolves to the Rev-3 notes file (2026-08-01-usitc-hts-2026-rev3-notes.jsonl), whose page-236 is note 16(r)-(t) and does not contain 16(c)(iii); the resolver's release pin does not match the Rev-15 ingest the generator pins, so the resolver output alone would have been misleading here. Alternative kind worth a second look: wrong_entity_or_scope, since what was wrong is the covered population of HTS provisions (nearly all primary steel encoded as non-member) rather than a condition or exception; I kept unrepresented_clause because the omitted material is enumerated content of the cited clause that the fix adds back, which the rubric routes to unrepresented_clause. Corroborating (not quoted as module-diff text): B16-BUILD-REPORT.md in the same commit adds "Round-2 section 232 primary-scope repair: the tokenizer and independent differential scanner now preserve the 4-, 6-, and 8-digit widths printed in notes 16(c)(iii) and 19(b)" and states it adds 26 steel-heading, two steel-six-digit, and seven aluminum-heading rows while retaining 11 steel 8-digit rows. Module 1 (note19-232-aluminum.yaml) is the same defect in note 19(b) and should classify identically. Companion tests were added for both new tables (hts_line 7206 -> 1; 730210 -> 1).

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as "new coverage the module never claimed" and failed: at the parent commit the generator's own grammar already declared `Production("232-aluminum", "s232_aluminum_primary_membership", "19(b)", ...)` for this file, yet the emitted module contained only note 19(j) derivative tables and cited only page-255, so the entire note 19(b) primary-aluminum list the source enumerates was missing from a module that claimed it. The pinned Rev-15 corpus text at us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-253 reads "(b) The rates of duty set forth in heading 9903.85.01 ... apply to all imported products of aluminum classifiable in the provisions enumerated in this subdivision: (i) unwrought aluminum provided for in heading 7601 ... (v) castings and forgings of aluminum provided for in subheading 7616.99.51", exactly the seven headings plus 76169951 the fix adds with companion tests. This is not mechanical (new parameter rules with values, new proof atoms, new tests) and no other kind fits better: nothing numeric was wrong, no bound or boolean flipped, and no existing rule pointed at the wrong population — a clause the source states was simply absent and the fix adds it, which the taxonomy routes to unrepresented_clause.
verdict.notes: Root cause verified, not inferred: the pre-fix tokenizer `HTS = re.compile(r"(?<![\d.])(\d{4}\.\d{2}\.\d{2}(?:\d{2})?)(?![\d.])")` matched neither the bare 4-digit headings (7601, 7604-7609) nor the one dotted 8-digit code, because note 19(b) prints it sentence-final as "subheading 7616.99.51." and the trailing period trips the `(?![\d.])` lookahead — I ran both regexes over the corpus segment and the old one returns [] while the new PRINTED_WIDTH_HTS returns ['7616.99.51']. Two caveats for the reviewer. (1) The first reader's phrasing "encoded as outside the action" is slightly stronger than the artifact supports: the primary table was absent entirely rather than encoding an explicit 0, and the only consumer (tools/b16_entry_flags.py, mapping "s232_aluminum_primary" to both new tables) arrives in this same commit — the substantive omission stands, the false-negative framing is an extrapolation. (2) This is an intra-PR repair: commit a70eb63414 (2026-08-15) lands inside PR #1298, merged 2026-08-16, so the defective encoding never reached main; if the corpus is meant to hold post-merge defects, that is a selection question, not a classification one. The steel module (index 0) in the same commit carries the parallel defect at 4- and 6-digit widths in note 16(c)(iii) — 26 heading and 2 six-digit rows — so the two module files are one defect with one cause. Build report language for the same change: "the tokenizer and independent differential scanner now preserve the 4-, 6-, and 8-digit widths printed in notes 16(c)(iii) and 19(b)".

item.subject: Address sol audit: FRA-dated bound, exact quotations, scoped claims

triage.commit_summary: This commit revises the single California MPP 63-410.321 ABAWD age-exception module (an amendment inside PR #1223 addressing a "sol" cross-family audit) by moving the version's effective_to from 2025-06-30 back to 2023-08-31, because the pinned corpus's USLM amendment notes show P.L. 118-5 (Fiscal Responsibility Act) section 311(a)(1) struck the mirrored former federal text "under 18 or over 50 years of age;" applicable to certifications and recertifications received from September 1, 2023, so a June-2025 bound kept superseded criteria resolving across the whole FRA phase-in. It also rewrote the module summary, the upstream_source_check rationale, and the version comment so quotations carry their original terminal punctuation, the amendment-note quotes are attributed to the archived USLM source document, the pre-FRA band claim is scoped to what the FNS memo footnote supports, and the certification-keyed transition is documented as abstained-from; the companion cases moved from period 2026-05 to 2023-05 and the encoding manifest was re-signed.

modules.description_quote: keeping the version alive through June 2025 preserved a legally obsolete result across the FRA phase-in
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The module's only version ran through 2025-06-30, so every month from September 2023 (when P.L. 118-5 section 311(a)(1)'s strike of the mirrored federal "under 18 or over 50 years of age;" exception began applying to certifications and recertifications) through June 2025 still resolved to the superseded pre-FRA criteria that the source had already replaced.
modules.triage_notes: Decisive change is one line: versions[0].effective_to '2025-06-30' -> '2023-08-31'. The formula, rule name, inputs, outputs, and the MPP proof atom/excerpt are untouched. Everything else in this module diff is prose (module.summary, upstream_source_check.rationale, the version comment) rewritten for exact quotation punctuation, attribution of the amendment-note quotes to the archived USLM source document, and scoping of the pre-FRA band claim; those parts alone would be mechanical/provenance, so the fidelity call rests solely on the date bound. Confidence is not higher only because the pre-fix state is an earlier commit on the same PR branch (parent 7284408e, which itself introduced the 2025-06-30 bound over a previously timeless version), not a state that ever reached main - the wrong bound was caught by the audit before merge. Provision read: resolve_provision.py on us/statute/7/2015/o/3 at the pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, corpus commit d9d6fba0) returns current text "(A) under 18, or over 65, years of age;", confirming no 50-year exception survives today; the corpus provision rows do not carry the P.L. 118-5 amendment or effective-date notes, so the September 1, 2023 application date rests on the commit message and PR body, which quote the USLM note that the amended paragraph applies "to any application for initial certification or recertification received starting 90 days after the date of enactment" (enacted June 3, 2023). The PR calls the module out of FY2026 program scope with no consumers ("archival honesty, not a behavior fix"), so the defect is in asserted encoded meaning rather than in any computed output. Companion file us-ca/regulations/mpp/63-410/321.test.yaml moved its three cases from 2026-05 to 2023-05 and .axiom/encoding-manifests/us-ca/regulations/mpp/63-410/321.json was re-signed; neither is a separate module index. The bundle contains exactly the one module index expected for this chunk.

verdict.justification: The only encoded value the commit touches is the single version's `effective_to`, moved from 2025-06-30 to 2023-08-31, and the companion cases move from period 2025-06 to 2023-05 to stay inside the narrowed window — so encoded meaning (which months resolve to the pre-FRA "under 18 or 50 or over" criterion) really changed, which rules out mechanical/test_only, and no other kind fits a pure version-window change (it is not a comparison-strictness flip, a missing clause, or an entity/scope change). Reg. 55964), replacing the placeholder 2026-02-14/2026-02-15 "panel" dates and ch-82's premature 2025-08-07 start. It also retires the Japan 9903.02.30 module outright because the September 4, 2025 EO applies successors 9903.02.72/.73 retroactively to 2025-08-07 in lieu of the prior duties, leaving no operative window, and adds 44 companion-test cases (test files, not module files) so every Boolean input in the floor modules' OR exception judgments has a true witness.

Verification trail: pinned corpus release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union (corpus commit d9d6fba0b9), provision record a82a1c36-7b8b-5694-be12-83b6ce6a0b2b, text sha256 e39d2570a833228e5a65ede43c921b9eb9708ad1b9099b735ee5c3b799941ba0 — the compiler's-note excerpt in the new proof atoms is byte-exact against that text. One genuine caveat a reviewer should carry, which weakens the fix but not the defect: the corpus text states termination without a date, and the module comment concedes this verbatim — "no termination date in the corpus text); effective_to 2026-02-14 is a conservative no-later-than bound, the last day before the successor floor headings' 2026-02-15 panel domain." So the specific boundary 2026-02-14 is an inference from the successor heading's start date (and, per the note, from 90 Fed. Reg. 59281, which I did not read — no web access and it is not in the corpus), not a quoted source date. If one held the strict bar "the fix must be fully grounded in the cited text", one could argue the fix trades an unsourced unbounded window for an unsourced bounded one. That does not rescue the pre-fix state: unbounded directly contradicts "provision terminated", so the pre-fix encoding was wrong against the source either way, and the defect class is the period, not the branch. The date's own groundedness is a separate, lesser question for a source-fidelity reviewer.

Secondary note: the in-transit exception rule also gets the same 2026-02-14 bound; that rule was already inert after the 2025-10-05 transition deadline in its own formula, so bounding it is harmless and consistent rather than independently load-bearing. item.subject: fix: compute MFS increment from complete AMTI

triage.commit_summary: The commit repairs the bounded tax-year-2026 individual AMT module (us/statutes/26/55.yaml) so that the section 55(d)(2) married-filing-separately AMTI increment is computed from the complete pre-increment alternative minimum taxable income — adding the section 151 exemption and senior deduction addbacks and the adopted section 57(a)(5), 58(a), 58(b), 59(e), 59(g) and 59(h) adjustments to the base that previously held only taxable income plus the restored standard/itemized deductions. In the same commit it tightens the module's verified domain to fail closed for non-individual tax units and for filing-status codes outside 0..4, and adds three reviewer regression fixtures plus an extension of an existing MFS case through the final tax outputs.

modules.description_quote: compute MFS increment from complete AMTI
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The section 55(d)(2) married-filing-separately increment was taken on a base of `taxable_income + amt_excluded_deductions` only, omitting the section 151 exemption and senior deduction addbacks and the section 57(a)(5), 58(a), 58(b), 59(e), 59(g) and 59(h) amounts that the statute's "alternative minimum taxable income (determined without regard to this sentence)" includes, so the increment and the resulting AMTI were understated.
modules.triage_notes:
Provision read through the pinned corpus release: us/statute/26/55/d/2 flush text says the increment is "the lesser of (i) 25 percent of the excess of alternative minimum taxable income (determined without regard to this sentence) over the minimum amount of such income (as so determined) for which the exemption amount under paragraph (1)(C) is zero, or (ii) such exemption amount". The module's own `amt_income` rule (same file, unchanged here) already defines AMTI as taxable_income + amt_excluded_deductions + amt_separate_addition + section_151_exemption_deduction + senior_deduction + the 57/58/59 adjustments, so the pre-fix `amt_separate_addition` base was demonstrably a proper subset of the module's own AMTI, not the statute's. The added terms are exactly the AMTI components other than the increment itself, i.e. the correct "without regard to this sentence" base.

Two hunks in one module. Hunk 2 (amt_separate_addition) is the one the commit subject names and is the decisive change. Hunk 1 adds `taxpayer_is_individual and (filing_status == 0 or 1 or 2 or 3 or 4)` to `section_55_verified_domain_is_satisfied`; on its own that is a second fidelity defect of kind wrong_entity_or_scope (the domain rule already carried the proof atom excerpt "In the case of a taxpayer other than a corporation" from us/statute/26/55/b/1 but did not enforce it, and pre-fix it returned `holds` for a non-individual tax unit and for filing_status 9). If the corpus wants one defect per module, unrepresented_clause on the MFS base is the primary; a reviewer may want to split this commit into two labeled defects.

Kind doubt: I chose unrepresented_clause because the fix adds statutorily required AMTI components (deductions and section 57/58/59 adjustments) that were absent from this formula. An arguable alternative is `other` ("incomplete base quantity referenced"), since the clauses were represented elsewhere in the module (`amt_income`) and the error is that the 55(d)(2) formula reused a partial subtotal. It is not amount_mismatch — no numeric constant, rate, or threshold changed.

Corroborating evidence outside the allowed quote sources: PROGRESS.md in the same commit says "Changed the section 55(d)(2) base to complete pre-increment AMTI, including the section 151 exemption and senior adjustments and every adopted signed section 57, 58, and 59 amount" and "Reproduced the reviewer fixture before repair with exact pinned tools: separate addition `$0`, AMTI `$690,200`, and tentative minimum tax `$190,811`, plus `holds` for both invalid-status and nonindividual cases"; post-fix the same fixture yields increment $25,000, AMTI $715,200, TMT $197,811. PROGRESS.md is not one of the permitted quote_source values, so the commit subject is quoted instead.

Companion test file us/statutes/26/55.test.yaml gained three fixtures named `reviewer_mfs_private_activity_preference_affects_separate_addition`, `reviewer_invalid_filing_status_fails_closed`, and `reviewer_nonindividual_tax_unit_fails_closed`, indicating a reviewer-driven repair; the bundle's PR record (#1180) has empty reviews/review_comments/issue_comments, and the PR body covers the whole multi-commit spine PR rather than this commit.

Doubt worth flagging to a reviewer: the added `taxpayer_is_individual` symbol is not in the module's `imports:` list and gained no proof/import atom in this commit (it appears exactly once in the post-fix file, at line 202); the fixtures feed it as `us:statutes/26/151#input.taxpayer_is_individual`. That provenance gap is unrelated to the fidelity defect but may have been cleaned up in a later commit. Only `PROGRESS.md` and the companion test changed alongside the module; no unrelated formula, parameter, effective-date, or metadata edits ride along.

The fix adds exactly the AMTI components the module's own `amt_income` rule already carried — the section 151 exemption and senior deduction addbacks (disallowed by section 56(b)(1)) plus the section 57(a)(5), 58(a), 58(b), 59(e), 59(g) and 59(h) amounts — so the added terms are clauses of the AMTI definition that the encoding omitted, i.e. an understated increment and understated AMTI. This is encoded meaning changing in a formula against cited source text, not provenance or bookkeeping, and the added-clause kind fits better than amount_mismatch (no number moved), untraceable_branch (nothing was removed or re-grounded), or boundary/polarity (no comparison or logic flipped).

item.subject: fix: reject contradictory individual entity facts

triage.commit_summary: The commit hardened the federal individual taxable-income composition (us/policies/income_tax/taxable_income_pipeline.yaml) so its fail-closed verified-domain guard rejects a taxpayer who is simultaneously attested as an individual and as an estate, trust, common trust fund, or partnership, adding a matching 26 USC 63 proof atom ("an estate or trust, common trust fund, or partnership"). It was one of five blocker repairs on PR #1179; the companion fixture ti-entity-zeroes-standard was converted into an explicit contradictory-facts regression (ti-contradictory-individual-entity-facts-fail-closed) asserting the imported §63(c)(6) disqualifier still holds while the local guard, deduction total, and taxable income fail closed.

modules.description_quote: fix: reject contradictory individual entity facts
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The guard admitted a taxpayer attested as an estate, trust, common trust fund, or partnership into the 26 USC 63(b) individual taxable-income composition (it only required taxpayer_is_individual and not taxpayer_is_corporation), so the module produced an individual taxable-income figure, with §151 exemption, senior, tips, overtime and vehicle-interest deductions, for a population §63(b) and §63(c)(6)(D) treat as non-individual, instead of failing closed.
modules.triage_notes: Single module in the commit; the only substantive change is one conjunct added to the verified-domain formula (`and not estate_or_trust_common_trust_fund_or_partnership`) plus one new proof atom citing us/statute/26/63 with excerpt "an estate or trust, common trust fund, or partnership". Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus: §63(c)(6) reads "In the case of— ... (D) an estate or trust, common trust fund, or partnership, the standard deduction shall be zero", and §63(b) frames the nonitemizer computation as "In the case of an individual"; the added excerpt is a byte substring of that body. The flag is the shared input of the imported us:statutes/26/63/c/6#standard_deduction_ineligible module, so the §63(c)(6)(D) zeroing was already represented via that import — what was missing was entity-scope rejection in the individual composition itself, which is why I chose wrong_entity_or_scope over unrepresented_clause; a reviewer could reasonably prefer unrepresented_clause, or downgrade to `unclear` on the view that this is fail-closed hardening against contradictory caller facts rather than a mis-encoded formula (hence confidence 0.7). Companion test and PROGRESS.md changed in the same commit (PROGRESS: "Made the individual verified-domain guard reject a simultaneous estate/trust/common-trust-fund/partnership fact."); nothing unrelated changed, and proof/import hashes were deliberately NOT regenerated here (PROGRESS says mechanical regeneration and manifest re-signing remain for the main lane). PR #1179's bundle carries no reviews or review comments; the blocker list lives in a "frozen adversarial review" at commit f58fc22a6 that is not in the bundle, so the commit subject is the best available quote. Preceding repair commit on the same file: c3e2a54de "fix: align taxable-income proofs with current law".

verdict.justification: The pre-fix guard already required `taxpayer_is_individual`, so a well-formed estate/trust/partnership fact set was already excluded and fell to zero; the only fact sets the new conjunct changes are ones that simultaneously attest `taxpayer_is_individual: true` and `estate_or_trust_common_trust_fund_or_partnership: true`, which the commit itself calls "contradictory" and the new test comment says "must fail closed." That is a fail-open-to-fail-closed hardening of the verified-domain consistency check (the rubric's polarity_or_logic), not the admission of a genuinely wrong population, so "wrong_entity_or_scope" mis-describes the change. The refutation is reinforced by what the pre-fix behavior actually produced: the renamed test previously expected `*standard_ineligible_outputs` (`standard_deduction_ineligible: holds`, deductions `0`, taxable income `100000`), i.e. exactly the 26 USC 63(c)(6)(D) "the standard deduction shall be zero" outcome that the module already encoded through its `us:statutes/26/63/c/6#standard_deduction_ineligible` import — so the old encoding was not returning a figure that disagreed with the cited text for that fixture. It remains a real meaning change with a source-grounded proof atom (63(c)(6)(D)) and the module's unchanged summary already promised "consistent branch facts ... and an individual taxpayer," so I keep it as a fidelity defect rather than not_a_defect, but the kind should be the logic/fail-closed one.
verdict.quote: +          and not estate_or_trust_common_trust_fund_or_partnership
verdict.notes: Evidence chain for a reviewer. (1) Diff is 6 lines: one added proof atom (corpus_citation_path us/statute/26/63, excerpt "an estate or trust, common trust fund, or partnership") plus the one added conjunct in rules[taxable_income_pipeline_verified_domain_applies].versions[0].formula. (2) The first reader's justification is accurate that the pre guard had only `taxpayer_is_individual` and `not taxpayer_is_corporation` (pre.yaml lines 209, 213), but it overstates the consequence: a taxpayer honestly attested as an estate has taxpayer_is_individual false and already failed closed pre-fix. Only a self-contradictory attestation reaches the changed behavior. (3) Companion test diff is decisive on intent: the case is renamed `ti-entity-zeroes-standard` -> `ti-contradictory-individual-entity-facts-fail-closed` with the comment "The shared valid-domain facts attest that the taxpayer is an individual. Simultaneously claiming an estate, trust, common trust fund, or partnership is contradictory, so this individual compose must fail closed." item.subject: fix: correct section 55 AMT integration

modules.triage_notes: Multi-defect commit; one module, whole-file rewrite (250 -> 1044 lines), so only one defect_kind could be recorded and the choice among several real fidelity kinds is what holds confidence below 0.8. Other genuine fidelity defects in the same diff, each independently classifiable: (a) untraceable_branch — the pre-fix `alternative_minimum_tax` subtracted `form_4972_lumpsum_distributions` and subtracted `alternative_minimum_tax_foreign_tax_credit` from the REGULAR-tax side; I read 26 USC 55(c)(1) through the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, corpus commit 0fd35bfb), which says regular tax 'means the regular tax liability for the taxable year (as defined in section 26(b)) reduced by the foreign tax credit allowable under section 27(a)' — neither the AMTFTC nor a Form 4972 subtraction appears there; the fix splits this into `regular_tax_after_ordinary_ftc` (section 26(b) total less ordinary FTC) and `tentative_minimum_tax_after_amtftc` (AMTFTC on the TMT side only). (b) untraceable_branch / wrong_period_or_effective_date — the pre-fix `amt_exemption` and `amt_income_for_exemption_offset` branched on `amt_kiddie_tax_applies` and capped the exemption at `amt_kiddie_tax_exemption_limit`, but section 55(d)(4)(A)(iii) provides that 'subsection (j) of section 59 shall not apply' after 2017; the fix deletes rule `amt_kiddie_tax_exemption_limit` outright and removes both branches. (d) wrong_entity_or_scope-adjacent — `income_tax_before_credits` moved from `income_tax_main_rates + capital_gains_tax + alternative_minimum_tax` to one `section_26_b_regular_tax_liability_before_credits + alternative_minimum_tax` total. I read 26 USC 55(b)(1) and 55(c)(1) through the resolver; both resolved cleanly (fix_time_corpus_match: same_body). The commit body is empty (just a newline), so all narrative evidence is the PR body (#1180); there are no PR reviews or comments. The same diff also carries non-fidelity work that a reviewer should not count as the defect: a new private `section_55_verified_domain_is_satisfied` fail-closed gate wrapping every monetary output, full proof-atom metadata on every rule, an explicit `inputs:` block, pinned per-output imports replacing one whole-module import, and `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` added to every version (bounding the module to TY2026 rather than correcting a date defect). verdict.justification: The pinned release text of 26 USC 55(b)(1)(D) defines AMTI as taxable income "(i) determined with the adjustments provided in section 56 and section 58, and (ii) increased by the amount of the items of tax preference described in section 57", and 26 USC 56(b)(1)(D)–(E) disallow "the deduction for personal exemptions under section 151" and state "Section 68 shall not apply" — none of which the pre-fix `amt_income`/`amt_excluded_deductions` formulas represented (they were `taxable_income + amt_excluded_deductions + amt_separate_addition + exemptions` and `salt_deduction + misc_deduction`). I tried the two available refutations and both fail: it is not mechanical (formulas, sources, imports and outputs all change), and it is not mere new coverage, because the pre-fix module already claimed the AMTI base (source "26 USC 55(b)(2)(D), 26 USC 56") and shipped `alternative_minimum_tax` and `income_tax_before_credits`, so an AMTI lacking the §57 preference produced a wrong number rather than an absent one.

Verified through the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union (corpus commit 0fd35bfbda): 55(b)(1)(D) (AMTI = §§56/58 adjustments + §57 preferences), 56(b)(1)(D)/(E) (§151 exemptions disallowed; "Section 68 shall not apply"), 151(d)(5)(C) ("there shall be allowed a deduction in an amount equal to $6,000 for each qualified individual"), 55(c)(1) (regular tax = §26(b) liability reduced by the §27(a) FTC), 55(d)(4)(A)(iii) ("subsection (j) of section 59 shall not apply" after 2017).

Caveat for a reviewer: this single commit bundles at least three further, differently-kinded fidelity defects beyond the anchored one, so if the corpus wants one kind per defect it is a candidate to split:

3. unrepresented_clause — the §68 reversal, which lives in `amt_excluded_deductions`, not in the anchored `rules[amt_income].versions[0].formula`.

Also note the commit simultaneously restructures the module into a bounded, fail-closed form (new `section_55_verified_domain_is_satisfied` judgment gating every output, `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` on every version, hashed imports and ~114 proof atoms). item.subject: fix: preserve signed section 58 adjustments

triage.commit_summary: The commit reworks the bounded 26 USC 58 module so that the subsection (a) tax-shelter-farm and subsection (b) passive-activity AMTI adjustments are single signed completed after-insolvency amounts, replacing the pre-fix surface of four inputs (two nonnegative pre-insolvency loss adjustments plus two separate per-leg insolvency reductions) and the six numeric guard conditions (nonnegativity plus a per-leg reduction cap) inside the domain judgment. It did so because section 58(c)(1)(A) states one insolvency reduction against "the amount of losses to which subsection (a) or (b) applies" without stating any per-leg allocation or ordering, and because the pre-fix nonnegativity guards zeroed out every statutorily possible negative adjustment; the companion test file was rewritten accordingly (11 cases to 6) and PROGRESS.md updated.

modules.description_quote: fix: preserve signed section 58 adjustments
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module invented a per-leg split of the single section 58(c)(1)(A) insolvency amount into separate subsection (a) and (b) reductions, each capped by its own leg and forced nonnegative along with both pre-insolvency loss adjustments, conditions the statute never states, so any statutorily possible negative (allowed-loss) adjustment made the domain judgment not_holds and drove both public adjustments to zero.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release for us/statute/26/58/a, /b, /c/1 and /c/2. 58(c)(1)(A) reads 'The amount of losses to which subsection (a) or (b) applies shall be reduced by the amount (if any) by which the taxpayer is insolvent as of the close of the taxable year' - one amount, no allocation or ordering between the legs, which is exactly what the pre-fix formula and the two removed *_insolvency_reduction inputs imposed. 58(a)(1)(B) (disallowed loss deductible in the succeeding year) and 58(c)(2) (entire-interest disposition: the loss 'shall (to the extent otherwise allowable) be allowed') both make a negative net AMTI adjustment possible, so the removed '>= 0' guards were ungrounded too. The companion test diff is the clearest confirmation: the pre-fix case 'negative_pre_insolvency_loss_adjustment_fails_closed' (a = -1 -> all outputs zero) is deleted and replaced by 'signed_completed_adjustments_are_exposed' with b = -300 flowing through unchanged. PROGRESS.md in the same commit states the reason in the maintainers' words ('both downstream loss adjustments are signed completed after-insolvency aliases, and the module infers no allocation or ordering for the single subsection (c)(1) insolvency amount'), but PROGRESS.md is not one of the permitted quote sources so the commit subject is quoted instead; the PR body (#1180) only describes the post-fix state ('the two post-insolvency adjustments') and carries no review comments. Kind is a judgment call between untraceable_branch (chosen: the fix deletes conditions and input values with no basis in 58(c)(1), namely the invented per-leg allocation and the nonnegativity/cap guards) and polarity_or_logic (the same nonnegativity guards made the module fail closed and emit zero on a legitimate negative adjustment); hence confidence 0.62 rather than higher. Same-diff incidentals that are mechanical, not fidelity: one proof-atom excerpt reflowed from a block scalar to an inline string, two rule 'source:' strings reworded to 'guarded signed completed adjustment', and the module summary rewritten. A secondary doubt for the reviewer: the fix also narrows the module's attested input boundary (the caller now supplies the after-insolvency amount instead of the pre-insolvency amount and the reduction), which is partly a boundary re-scope; it still qualifies as fidelity because the pre-fix module produced wrong zeros on a case the statute permits.

verdict.justification: 26 USC 58(c)(1)(A) states one amount — "The amount of losses to which subsection (a) or (b) applies shall be reduced by the amount (if any) by which the taxpayer is insolvent as of the close of the taxable year" — with no per-subsection allocation, no nonnegativity floor, and no per-leg cap; the pre-fix module invented all three (two separate `completed_section_58_{a,b}_insolvency_reduction` inputs, four `>= 0` conjuncts, and two `<=` leg caps) and folded them into the domain judgment, so any statutorily reachable negative adjustment (e.g. the 58(c)(2) disposition-year allowance, or freed passive losses under 58(b)/469) forced `not_holds` and zeroed both public surfaces. The fix removes those unsourced conjuncts and inputs rather than adding any source clause, and its own summary replaces "Separate completed nonnegative reductions apply the insolvency rule to each leg" with "The module does not infer an allocation or ordering for the single statutory insolvency amount" — the removal-of-ungrounded-conditions signature of untraceable_branch, not unrepresented_clause. I tested the refutations: it is not a mere input-contract refactor, because the companion test flips from `negative_pre_insolvency_loss_adjustment_fails_closed` to `signed_completed_adjustments_are_exposed` returning -300, a reachable behavior change; and it is not polarity_or_logic, because the `and` chain was never inverted or mis-combined, it simply carried extra conjuncts the statute does not state.
verdict.justification_short: Statute states a single insolvency reduction; the encoding invented per-leg reductions, nonnegativity, and per-leg caps, which the fix removes.
verdict.quote:
-          completed_section_58_a_tax_shelter_farm_loss_adjustment_before_insolvency >= 0
-          and completed_section_58_a_insolvency_reduction >= 0
-          and completed_section_58_a_insolvency_reduction
-            <= completed_section_58_a_tax_shelter_farm_loss_adjustment_before_insolvency
verdict.notes: Source read through the pinned resolver: 58(c)(1)(A) = "The amount of losses to which subsection (a) or (b) applies shall be reduced by the amount (if any) by which the taxpayer is insolvent as of the close of the taxable year"; 58(c)(2) allows the disposition-year loss "(to the extent otherwise allowable) ... in computing alternative minimum taxable income", which is what makes a negative (allowance) adjustment reachable and the removed `>= 0` floors wrong. Resolver note: the fix-time provision file was absent at the toolchain corpus ref, so text came from release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union (expression_date 2026-07-12); section 58's text is long-stable, so this does not affect the reading. Confounds a reviewer should see: the same diff also restructures the input contract from four inputs to two (the arithmetic moves to the caller's attested post-insolvency amounts) and reflows two proof-atom excerpts and two `source:` strings — those parts alone would be mechanical/refactor, so the fidelity finding rests specifically on the six removed unsourced numeric conjuncts and the test flip (negative b-leg adjustment of -300 now exposed rather than zeroed). 58(c)(2) remains an attested Judgment input both before and after, so the fix adds no clause; it declines to infer one. Kinds rejected: unrepresented_clause (nothing source-required is added), polarity_or_logic (no inversion or mis-combination; the guard's fail-closed default is unchanged), boundary_direction (the defect is the existence of the cap, not its strictness). Confidence held at 0.78 rather than higher only because the commit body is empty and the PR body describes §58 at one line ("completed-loss domain judgment + the two post-insolvency adjustments"), so the meaning change is inferred from the diff and tests rather than stated.

item.subject: fix: fail closed on injected canonical SNAP members

triage.commit_summary: Round-2 repair on PR #1176 (CalFresh BBCE/MCE): it adds a private California integrity judgment `calfresh_mce_canonical_membership_integrity_verified` that compares the length of the CA-side canonical member projection with the trusted federal `snap_state_plan_member_of_household_count`, and wires that judgment into the two household MCE outputs so they fail closed (household exclusion `holds`, MCE status `not_holds`) whenever the two counts diverge. (PROGRESS.md is an other_file, not the commit message/PR/module comment, so it is not used as description_quote). modules.triage_notes: Diffed pre-fix (b197fb225) against post-fix directly: the only change is a seven-line `metadata.proof.atoms` block (corpus_citation_path us/guidance/usda/fns/snap-fy2026-cola/page-1, span 'Federal SNAP state-plan composition support') added to the already-existing private rule `snap_state_plan_member_of_household_count`; `formula: len(member_of_household)` and `effective_from: '2025-10-01'` are byte-identical before and after. No quotable sentence describes this specific change in the commit message (subject only, empty body), the PR body, or the file; the PR body's 'Proof validation: 28 MCE + 9 composition atoms.' is the closest but describes gate counts, not this fix, so quote_source is 'none'.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix formulas already encoded every clause of the cited source: 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii)'s four household bars (resolved through the pinned release) were all scanned over the household's member set, and nothing in (vii) or (ix) requires any membership-set integrity or count check. Verbatim from PROGRESS.md in this same commit (not from the commit message or PR body, so not offered as the decisive quote): "The round-2 blocker is the caller-injectable private derived relation `calfresh_mce_canonical_member_of_household`." and "Confirmed the reviewer reproduced a fail-open by directly supplying an eligible row under the private derived relation while the federal relation contained only an excluded member." item.subject: fix: bind MCE gates to canonical member projection

triage.commit_summary: The commit adds a private, tautological `derived_relation` (`calfresh_mce_canonical_member_of_household`) that projects the federal SNAP `member_of_household` relation from `us:policies/usda/snap/state-plan-composition` (Person at slot 0, Household at slot 1) and repoints both CalFresh MCE membership aggregations at it. It was the third repair in the PR #1176 chain: the predecessor commit had swapped a PR-new California-local membership relation for a bare `member_of_household` name, and the first full program compile showed that bare cross-module name never bound to the imported federal relation, so the household-bar and eligible-member gates were ranging over an unqualified implicit relation instead of the canonical household member set.

modules.description_quote: fix: bind MCE gates to canonical member projection
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Both MCE membership aggregations ranged over a bare `member_of_household` name that did not resolve to the imported federal state-plan relation and compiled as an unqualified implicit relation, so the 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii) household bars and the (ix) member exclusions/eligible-member test were not evaluated over the household's actual canonical member set.
modules.triage_notes: Read the diff, both pre- and post-fix module text, the federal `us/policies/usda/snap/state-plan-composition.yaml` relation definition (data_relation member_of_household, arguments Person, Household — consistent with the new projection's current_slot: 1 / related_slot: 0 for a Household-entity aggregation), and the cited provision via resolve_provision (us/regulation/7/273/2 resolved fine; the new proof atom's excerpt 'No person shall be included as a member in any household which is otherwise categorically eligible if that person is:' is byte-verbatim in paragraph (j)(2)(ix), and (vii)(D) reads 'Any member of that household is ineligible...', so both gates must range over the real household member set). The commit body is empty; the PR body describes the whole encoding, not this defect. The decisive prose evidence is the PROGRESS.md hunk in this same commit (not one of the allowed quote_source values, so the commit subject is quoted instead): 'The first full program compile exposed that a bare imported relation name with a local predicate remained an unqualified implicit relation. Replaced that alias with a private, tautological derived relation whose executable source is the fully qualified federal state-plan relation; both MCE aggregations now range over this complete canonical projection.' Repair chain context: c0487985b originally encoded a CA-local `calfresh_mce_member_of_household` data_relation; 2a0771d02 ('fix: close CalFresh MCE membership fail-open') deleted it and substituted the bare federal name; this commit completes the binding. REVIEWER CAVEAT: this is a borderline item. The intended meaning was already correct in words — the defect is a cross-module relation-resolution/binding failure whose consequence is a wrong member set (the household-bar aggregation silently fails open and the eligible-member test fails closed on an unpopulated relation). A judge comparing only module text to the statute could not detect it without knowing RuleSpec's relation-resolution rules, so if the corpus is restricted to source-text-detectable defects, prune this one; it is not mechanical under the stated definition, because formulas changed and the member set the gates evaluate over changed. The commit touched nothing else in the module (no parameter, version, effective-date, or scope changes beyond the two count_where arguments) and only PROGRESS.md besides.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical plumbing and could not: the diff rewrites two executable formulas' aggregation domain and adds an executable `derived_relation` rule, so nothing in the mechanical carve-out (hashes, pins, metadata, excerpts) applies. The same commit's PROGRESS.md states the pre-fix state verbatim — "The first full program compile exposed that a bare imported relation name with a local predicate remained an unqualified implicit relation" — so before the fix the `count_where` in `calfresh_mce_household_exclusion_applies` and in `calfresh_mce_status_conferred` did not range over the canonical federal `member_of_household` projection, and the engine's `infer_slots` shows the bare name lowers into an auto-emitted relation with `slot_entities: Vec::new(), derivation: None`. The corpus text of 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii)(A)/(D) ("Any member of that household is disqualified…") and (ix) ("No person shall be included as a member in any household which is otherwise categorically eligible if that person is:") are member-scoped tests, so aggregating them over an unbound relation instead of the household's actual member set is a member-set/scope divergence, not a polarity flip (the mis-binding fails open on the exclusion gate and fails closed on the eligible-member gate). wrong_entity_or_scope, which the taxonomy defines to cover "household member set," is the right kind.
verdict.quote:
-            member_of_household,
+            calfresh_mce_canonical_member_of_household,
verdict.notes:
Supporting evidence, verbatim from the same commit's PROGRESS.md hunk (not the module diff, so not used as the decisive quote): "The first full program compile exposed that a bare imported relation name with a local predicate remained an unqualified implicit relation. Replaced that alias with a private, tautological derived relation whose executable source is the fully qualified federal state-plan relation; both MCE aggregations now range over this complete canonical projection." The added rule binds `source_relation: us:policies/usda/snap/state-plan-composition#relation.member_of_household` with `current_slot: 1 / related_slot: 0`, which matches the engine's fixed `infer_slots` convention (axiom-rules-engine src/formula.rs: "Preserve the established runtime convention: current entity in slot 1, related entity in slot 0"), so the slot orientation is unchanged and the only semantic change is which relation is aggregated. `us/policies/usda/snap/state-plan-composition.yaml` declares `member_of_household` as a `kind: data_relation` over [Person, Household]; the engine docs note that repo-backed execution requests "reject bare output, input, and relation names" and key relation rows by durable id (`…#relation.member_of_household`), which is why the unqualified alias could not receive the canonical rows.

Two caveats a reviewer should weigh:
1. Provenance: bfadb95594 is an intra-PR repair commit inside PR #1176, the PR that first encodes this module (file history: c0487985b → a350ed6ba → 4ce32e959 → e4d561a24 → 2a0771d02 → bfadb95594, all pre-merge). The defective state never existed on main outside the PR branch. If the corpus is meant to capture defects in shipped encodings, this is a WIP repair round rather than a regression fix.
2. Near-duplicate with its parent: 2a0771d0 ("fix: close CalFresh MCE membership fail-open") changed the exact same two `count_where` lines, deleting a CA-local `calfresh_mce_member_of_household` data_relation that could diverge from the federal household. Parent and child are two passes at the same underlying member-set scope problem; scoring both as independent fidelity defects double-counts one issue, and the "fail-open/polarity" framing belongs to the parent, not to this commit.
3. Character of the bug: this is a DSL name-binding failure whose fidelity consequence is the aggregation domain. A stricter "encoded meaning vs. source text" reading could file it as a compile/binding defect rather than a misreading of the provision; under the supplied taxonomy (which lists "household member set" under wrong_entity_or_scope) it still lands as fidelity, but that is the main axis on which this could be argued down to unclear.

item.subject: fix: close CalFresh MCE membership fail-open

triage.commit_summary: This repair-round commit inside PR #1176 (CalFresh modified categorical eligibility) deleted the PR-new, module-local `calfresh_mce_member_of_household` data_relation and re-pointed both MCE member aggregations — the 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii) household-bar scan and the paragraph-(ix) eligible-member scan in `calfresh_mce_status_conferred` — at the canonical federal `member_of_household` relation already imported from `us:policies/usda/snap/state-plan-composition`. It did so because the separate California membership relation could diverge from (or be empty relative to) the household's real member set, letting a household with an IPV-disqualified, drug-felony, or probation/parole member still be conferred MCE, i.e. the mandatory "under no circumstances" bar failed open; the companion tests were migrated to the canonical relation and three new divergent-omission cases were added.

modules.description_quote: close CalFresh MCE membership fail-open
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The household categorical bar scanned a module-local `calfresh_mce_member_of_household` relation instead of the household's actual SNAP members, so a household whose real member was disqualified for an IPV, workfare/monthly-reporting failure, or a drug-felony/fleeing-felon/probation-violation could be omitted from that relation and still be conferred MCE, contrary to 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii)'s mandatory "Under no circumstances shall any household be considered categorically eligible if: (A) Any member of that household is disqualified...".
modules.triage_notes:
Read: the module diff, pre-fix module at e4d561a243, post-fix module at 2a0771d025, the companion-test diff, the PROGRESS.md diff, the PR #1176 body/comments, and the cited provision text (resolve_provision.py on us/regulation/7/273/2 succeeded; paragraph (j)(2)(vii)(A)-(D) and (ix)(A)-(E) confirmed verbatim as quoted in the module's proof atoms).

Evidence for the kind: the commit subject names a "fail-open", and the PROGRESS.md diff in the same commit states "Removed the PR-new California membership relation and ranged both MCE aggregations over the imported federal state-plan `member_of_household`" plus "Traced every MCE member scan. Only the household-bar and eligible-member aggregations scan members". The three added companion cases are named canonical_membership_closes_divergent_ipv_omission, ..._probation_omission, ..._eligible_member_omission, i.e. exactly the households that previously slipped past the bar. (PROGRESS.md is not one of the allowed quote_source values, so the quote above is the commit subject fragment.)

Kind is genuinely three-way and a reviewer may prefer a different label: (a) polarity_or_logic — chosen, because the stated reason literally says "fail-open", the only kind whose definition names that; (b) wrong_entity_or_scope — the count_where ranged over the wrong household member set, which that definition lists explicitly, and nothing about the boolean structure was inverted; (c) untraceable_branch — the deleted relation is a California-only "MCE member" concept with no basis in 273.2(j)(2), and the fix re-grounds the scan on the canonical relation. Confidence is 0.6 for classification+kind jointly; classification as fidelity is much firmer (~0.9) than the kind.

Scope of the change: the module hunks are only the relation deletion and two identical `calfresh_mce_member_of_household` -> `member_of_household` substitutions; no parameter, threshold, effective date, import, or proof atom changed, so nothing unrelated rides along. The two other files in the commit are companion tests (relation key migrated, California-only bar facts merged into the benefit companion's federal rows, three divergent cases added) and PROGRESS.md.

Direction of the defect is asymmetric and worth flagging: in `calfresh_mce_household_exclusion_applies` an under-populated relation suppresses the bar (fail-open, the named defect); in `calfresh_mce_status_conferred` the same under-population would zero the eligible-member count and deny MCE (fail-closed). The commit title describes the first.

Follow-ups on the same issue, both after this commit and before merge: bfadb9559 "fix: bind MCE gates to canonical member projection" re-wraps the same canonical relation in a private `calfresh_mce_canonical_member_of_household` derived_relation projection (binding/plumbing, same member set, no meaning change), and 5db993493 "fix: fail closed on injected canonical SNAP members" hardens against injected members. A corpus curator may want to treat 2a0771d025 as the fidelity-bearing commit of that trio and the other two as hardening. Caveat for the corpus: the pre-fix state is a within-PR-branch state (the module was introduced earlier on the same branch by c0487985b/a350ed6ba), so this defect was caught in review and never shipped on main.

verdict.justification: This is a real fidelity defect, but nothing boolean changed: the diff deletes the module-private `calfresh_mce_member_of_household` data_relation and swaps the scanned relation to the canonical `member_of_household` (defined in us/statutes/7/2012/j.yaml and used by the rest of the SNAP composition) in two `count_where` calls, leaving every operator, the `not`, the `> 0` thresholds and both predicates identical. The source, read through the pinned release, quantifies over "Any member of that household" (7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii)(A)), so the defect is that the bar ranged over a second, caller-supplied roster that could diverge from the household's actual SNAP member set — the taxonomy's "household member set" case, not inverted or mis-combined logic. The "fail-open" in the subject names the consequence, not the mechanism, and it does not hold uniformly: the same substitution at `calfresh_mce_status_conferred`'s `count_where(..., calfresh_mce_member_eligible) > 0` is a positive existence test that an omitted roster would fail *closed*, which a polarity defect would not do in both directions. The added test `canonical_membership_closes_divergent_ipv_omission` supplies two canonical rows where the second is IPV-disqualified, confirming the pre-fix hole was a divergent roster rather than a flipped branch.
verdict.quote:
-            calfresh_mce_member_of_household,
+            member_of_household,
verdict.notes: Kind is the only thing I dispute; fidelity and the defect's reality are solid. Evidence checked: (1) module diff removes the `kind: data_relation` rule `calfresh_mce_member_of_household` (arity 2, Person/Household) and rewires both scan sites; (2) `member_of_household` is the canonical arity-2 data_relation declared in us/statutes/7/2012/j.yaml at 2a0771d025 and consumed by the SNAP composition, so pre-fix the MCE module scored its categorical bar on a roster independent of the roster driving `snap_member_eligible` and benefit calculation; (3) the companion test diff replaces `us-ca:...#relation.calfresh_mce_member_of_household` with `us:policies/usda/snap/state-plan-composition#relation.member_of_household` in every existing case and adds two regressions (`canonical_membership_closes_divergent_ipv_omission`, `canonical_membership_closes_divergent_probation_omission`) expecting `calfresh_mce_household_exclusion_applies: holds` / `calfresh_mce_status_conferred: not_holds`; (4) provision text resolved at corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union (body sha256 5170032c722b16cdaec6ae942be6f7b5cb2bb18bfb564b2813551e940cc2dadc) reads "(vii) Under no circumstances shall any household be considered categorically eligible if: (A) Any member of that household is disqualified for an intentional Program violation in accordance with § 273.16 or for failure to comply with monthly reporting requirements..." and (D) covers drug-felony/fleeing-felon/probation-violator, matching the first reader's provision reading. A reviewer who treats the subject line's "fail-open" as dispositive would keep polarity_or_logic; I weight the diff (a member-set substitution with no logical-operator change) over the message word. Not mechanical: a rule was deleted and two formulas changed. Not not_a_defect: the fix is a repair round inside PR #1176, whose maintainer comment describes a fixture that "exercises the engine-only union path that the integrity guard defends," i.e. a real vulnerability that was reproduced and closed.

item.subject: fix(ca): validate CalFresh MCE source scope

triage.commit_summary: A repair round inside PR #1176 (the CalFresh BBCE/MCE encoding) that re-scoped the federal 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii) categorical-eligibility bars from Household-level existential facts to per-Person facts aggregated over the MCE household relation, leaving only the whole-household workfare bar as a direct household fact, and folded the WIC 18901.3 drug-felony opt-out directly into the per-member federal gate (deleting the household-level intermediate rule). It also added `upstream_source_check` provenance blocks to both changed modules and expanded the companion suites from 41 to 44 passing cases, including a new adversary asserting that one member's serious-crime conviction plus a different member's sentence noncompliance must not bar the household.

modules.description_quote: fix(ca): validate CalFresh MCE source scope
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing in the encoded meaning was wrong: the module previously lacked the required higher-authority provenance attestation, which the commit supplies.
modules.triage_notes: The entire 28-line diff for this composition module is a single added `module.source_verification.upstream_source_check` block (status: checked_higher_authority, checked_paths for WIC 18901.5 and 7 CFR 273.2/8/9/10, plus a prose rationale). No rule, formula, parameter, version, effective date, import, input, output, or scope changed; the imports list and all composition rules are byte-identical between 8122fdece and 4ce32e9598. PROGRESS.md in the same commit records this verbatim as 'Added the required higher-authority checks for the retained CDSS implementation letters.' The companion file fy-2026-benefit-calculation.test.yaml did change heavily (1112 lines), but that is downstream churn from the member-scope correction in index 1 (household-level exclusion inputs replaced by per-member inputs inside the relation rows) plus mechanical YAML-anchor expansion, not a change to this module.

modules.description_quote: fix(ca): validate CalFresh MCE source scope
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii)(D) bars a household when 'any member' is ineligible '[under] § 273.11(s) for having a conviction of certain crimes and not being in compliance with the sentence' — a conjunction predicated of one member — but the pre-fix module evaluated that conjunction at Household entity over two separate household-wide existential facts, so a conviction held by member A combined with sentence noncompliance by member B (a split witness) wrongly denied the whole household MCE.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read: I resolved us/regulation/7/273/2 through the pinned corpus and confirmed (vii)(A)/(D) are 'any member' tests, (B) is 'the entire household is disqualified ... workfare', and (C) is 'the head of the household'. The fix re-levels entity Household -> Person on calfresh_wic_18901_3_drug_felony_opt_out_applies, calfresh_mce_federal_drug_felony_exclusion_before_state_opt_out, and the renamed calfresh_mce_member_household_exclusion_applies, then aggregates with count_where(calfresh_mce_member_of_household, ...) > 0 in the household-level rule that takes over the old name calfresh_mce_household_exclusion_applies; note the rename shuffle (old calfresh_mce_drug_felony_exclusion_applies deleted, old calfresh_mce_household_exclusion_applies renamed to ..._member_household_...), so diff line matching is misleading without reading both file versions. Decisive evidence is the new companion case 'different_members_cannot_split_serious_crime_conviction_and_sentence_noncompliance' (member 1 has the conviction, member 2 is out of compliance, expected calfresh_mce_household_exclusion_applies: not_holds), which the pre-fix formula would have failed; two more new cases (federal_drug_felony_member_exclusion_exists_before_the_state_opt_out, member_ipv_bar_applies_before_household_aggregation) pin the member-level layer. PROGRESS.md in the same commit states verbatim: 'Moved all member-triggered paragraph-(vii) bars to `Person` scope and aggregates them through the MCE household relation; only the whole-household workfare bar remains a direct household fact. This both matches source scope and prevents split-witness false positives.' — I did not use it as description_quote because PROGRESS.md is not one of the allowed quote sources; the commit subject's 'source scope' is the in-scope paraphrase of the same thing. Secondary changes bundled here: the added upstream_source_check block (provenance, mechanical), one proof atom moved between rules, and removal of the intermediate calfresh_mce_drug_felony_exclusion_applies, described in PROGRESS.md as 'Removed the unreachable current-law effective drug-felony intermediate' — that removal is behaviour-neutral today because calfresh_wic_18901_3_drug_felony_opt_out_applies is the constant `true`, so the drug-felony branch was and remains dead under current California law; the live defect corrected is the serious-crime split witness. Single-predicate bars (IPV, monthly reporting, fleeing felon, probation/parole) and the head-of-household work bar are semantically unchanged by the re-leveling. item.subject: fix: order current SC utility setters after 2009 revision

triage.commit_summary: This repair-round commit inside PR #1139 makes South Carolina's current SNAP utility-standard setters (manual page 159: $388 MUA, $265 BUA, $27 telephone) take precedence over the pre-existing page-369 module, which unconditionally binds the federal individual-utility-allowance hook to the superseded September 2009 telephone standard of $33. It does so by adding `us-sc:policies/dss/snap-policy-manual/page-369` to page-159's imports (so page-369's rules are merged first and page-159's `sets` relation is applied last) plus a summary sentence recording the supersession, and by pinning the resulting federal-target values (27 / 0 while page-369's own value stays 33) in four companion test cases.

modules.description_quote: order current SC utility setters after 2009 revision
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Pre-fix, page-159 did not declare page-369 as a dependency, so when both SC manual pages were composed the superseded September 2009 telephone standard ($33, encoded on page-369 with effective_from 2009-09-01 and no end date, and set unconditionally) could bind the federal `snap_individual_utility_allowance_state_option` hook for current periods instead of the current manual's $27 conditional allowance stated on page 159.
modules.triage_notes: Module diff is only two things: the added import `us-sc:policies/dss/snap-policy-manual/page-369` and a summary sentence ('The current setters supersede page 369's historical September 2009 utility-standard setters when both pages are composed.'). No formula, parameter, version, effective date, input, output, or scope changed inside the module, so a reviewer could argue 'mechanical' on the module-local text alone; I classified fidelity because the import genuinely changes composed meaning and the companion test was updated to pin it. Mechanism verified in code, not assumed: axiom-rules-engine `src/rulespec.rs` `load_...` merges every import first and then `merge_rules_documents(combined, document.without_imports())` appends the local document last (~line 1008-1013), and `apply_source_relation_sets` (~line 2869+) walks rules in order overwriting `target_derived.versions` / `target_parameter.versions`, i.e. last setter wins — so importing page-369 forces page-159's setter to be applied after it. Pre-fix companion test (parent 991bfb2ace) contained no reference to page-369 or to `us:regulations/7-cfr/273/9#snap_individual_utility_allowance_state_option`; the fix adds `page-369#snap_individual_utility_allowance_state_value: 33` and `7-cfr/273/9#snap_individual_utility_allowance_state_option: 27|0` assertions to four cases, which is what pins the precedence. Provision read through the pinned corpus release: page 159 states '(F) $27 Telephone allowance' alongside '$388 Mandatory utility allowance (MUA)' and '$265 Basic utility allowance (BUA)', confirming $27 as the current standard; page-369's own summary is a 2009 change-log entry ('TE from 27 to 33'). Collision existed only on the individual/telephone target — page-369 has just one `sets` rule (sets_snap_individual_utility_allowance); its MU/BU parameters bind nothing. Defect was introduced and fixed within PR #1139 (module created in d5394fc03; repairs 991bfb2ace, this commit, 198f20b05, 48da39b87), never on main, and was caught by the maintainer's blind review. The reviewer text, verbatim from the PR issue comments (bundle field `issue_comments`, not the `reviews` array, which is why I used the commit message for description_quote): round 1 flagged 'page-369 $33 unconditional setter collision with the new $27 hook'; round 2 reported "page 159's current $27 telephone allowance takes precedence over page 369's 2009-era $33 via import-first ordering (369 untouched)". Kind choice: wrong_period_or_effective_date under the 'timeless encoding of superseded text' clause — page-369's open-ended 2009 setter governing current periods; an alternative reading is 'other: setter-precedence/composition collision', and a weaker one is amount_mismatch ($33 vs $27), which I rejected because no literal amount in either module is wrong. page-369 itself was deliberately left untouched. Follow-up commits 198f20b05 ('limit SC rent exclusion to basic allowance') and 48da39b87 ('preserve SC heating and cooling qualifications') are separate repair rounds on other pages/findings in the same PR.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical (only a summary sentence and one import line changed) and failed: engine code shows the import edge changes composed meaning. `load_rulespec_document_from_source` merges every import's rules before the module's own rules, and `apply_source_relation_sets` overwrites the target hook's versions/derivation for each `sets` rule in merged order, so the last setter wins — adding page-369 as an import forces page-159's conditional $27 setter to bind `us:regulations/7-cfr/273/9#snap_individual_utility_allowance_state_option` after page-369's. Page-369 is verifiably a superseded September 2009 change record ("TE from 27 to 33") whose setter is unconditional with a single version `effective_from: '2009-09-01'` and no end date, while the pinned corpus for page 159 (expression date 2026-01-01) reads "(F) $27 Telephone allowance" — so before the fix the 2009 vintage could bind current periods, which is the taxonomy's "timeless encoding of superseded text". The companion test in the same commit adds composed expectations (`snap_individual_utility_allowance_state_option: 27` / `0` while page-369's own value stays 33), confirming behavior, not bookkeeping, changed.
verdict.quote:
+    The current setters supersede page 369's historical September 2009
+  - us-sc:policies/dss/snap-policy-manual/page-369
verdict.notes: Verification trail: diff is 3 added lines in us-sc/policies/dss/snap-policy-manual/page-159.yaml (summary sentence + one import); no formula, parameter, version, or date inside page-159 changed. Mechanism verified in code, not from the PR comment: /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-rules-engine src/rulespec.rs — imports merged first in declared order then `document.without_imports()` appended last (~lines 1093-1100), and `apply_source_relation_sets` (~line 2869) assigns `target_derived`/`target_parameter` from each matching `sets` rule, so the final matching rule wins. page-369 (read at 116728773d) sets the same federal hook unconditionally from `telephone_standard_te = 33`, one version `effective_from: '2009-09-01'`, no effective_to; it was left untouched (PR issue comment: "369 untouched"). Corpus check via resolve_provision.py: release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, provision us-sc/manual/dss/snap-policy-manual/page-159, expression_date 2026-01-01, text contains "(D) $388 Mandatory utility allowance (MUA)", "(E) $265 Basic utility allowance (BUA)", "(F) $27 Telephone allowance". Alternative kind a reviewer might prefer: the fix mechanism is setter precedence/composition ordering rather than an effective_to edit, so "other (setter-precedence collision)" is arguable; I keep wrong_period_or_effective_date because the defect substance is superseded 2009 amounts binding current periods, and the commit subject names the revision date ("order current SC utility setters after 2009 revision"). Not amount_mismatch: each module's amount is correct for its own vintage. Residual caveats for the reviewer: (1) the root defect arguably lives in page-369's open-ended window, and this fix patches the downstream module instead; (2) programs/us-sc/snap/fy-2026.yaml lists page-369 but still does not list page-159 (lexically it would sort between page-158 and page-160, i.e. before 369), so the collision was latent at merge time and the fix is pre-emptive; (3) I did not verify that axiom-compose dedups a module already pulled in as an import when the program spec also lists it later — the import-first guarantee depends on that dedup, which I confirmed only for the atomic loader's SourceLoadContext.

item.subject: fix: require shared-residence utility agreement

triage.commit_summary: Repair-round commit on PR #1139 (SC SNAP utility allowances) that wires the previously orphaned rule `same_residence_utility_allowance_agreement_requirement_satisfied` into the MUA, BUA, and actual-cost entitlements on page-165, and re-points page-159's MUA dollar output from page-163's raw MUA entitlement to page-165's now-gated `multiple_utility_allowance_entitlement` so the gate reaches the money. It exists because blind review found the p.165 sentence "Multiple households living in the same residence must agree on the type of utility allowance, either MUA, BUA or actual" encoded as a dead rule that constrained no outcome; companion tests added adversarial shared-residence-disagreement cases that now return $0.

modules.description_quote: shared-residence agreement now gates MUA/BUA/actual/telephone outcomes (adversarial case returns $0)

Classified unclear rather than fidelity because no commit or PR text names a defect and an added guard can equally be read as new precision the module never claimed.
