That divergence exists identically before and after this commit, so it is not what the commit fixed, but it looks like a live MFS defect worth its own investigation (the (10)(D) capture may also be garbled - the blob repeats subdivisions and (10)(E) reads 6.70% for trusts where the adjacent subdivision reads 6.99%). Provision read via resolve_provision.py at release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union.

modules.description_quote: absorb and retire the overlapping pilot and hand-authored statute fragment through signed manifests
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the deleted pilot published a complete 'Connecticut 2026 resident individual income tax before refundable credits' output built from a 12-703 personal-credit rate, a 12-700a AMT addend, a 12-704c property-tax credit and a 12-704i stillborn credit that it took as caller inputs, and it applied the resident 12-700 schedule with no residency or filing-status-exclusivity condition, so it claimed a liability surface and a population wider than the cited 12-700(a)(10) text supports.
modules.triage_notes: Whole-file deletion; the file is a real RuleSpec v1 rule module. Evidence that it was not merely redundant: at the parent commit it sat in known-validation-gaps.yaml under `validate_failures` as a pending waiver (issue #782, expires 2026-10-08) with `passed: false` in .axiom/pending-validation-fingerprints.json, and this commit removes both rows. Its signed manifest is rewritten by `axiom-encode retire` with the reason 'Replace the broad Connecticut pilot and stale pre-supplement EITC duplicate with bounded source-backed canonical tax-year-2026 components' (manifest, not an allowed quote_source, so the quote above is from the PR body). I could not demonstrate a specific numeric or logical error in the retired credit chain: 12-745 'Order of credits' and the operative 12-700a/12-703/12-704c text are all present in the cited us-ct/statute/12-700/block-1 Chapter 229 blob, and since both 12-704c and 12-704i are nonrefundable and capped by remaining liability, the pilot's hard-coded property-then-stillborn ordering does not change the total. One proof atom is not findable in the cited capture at the pinned release: the AMT rule's excerpt 'shall pay, in addition to the tax imposed under section 12-700, the net Connecticut minimum tax' returns 0 hits, though the shorter 'shall pay, in addition to the tax imposed under section 12-700' returns 3. The pilot's summary also carried an oracle/PolicyEngine-parity claim ('PolicyEngine-US 1.752.2 exposes each boundary as a distinct ancestor...', max abs error $0.4592) that the replacement explicitly drops ('PolicyEngine parity is not claimed'). Kept as unclear because the maintainers frame this as consolidation, not as correcting a stated wrong meaning. All formulas carried forward into index 0 are byte-equivalent after name normalization, so this deletion loses only the credit/AMT/liability stages.

modules.description_quote: absorb and retire the overlapping pilot and hand-authored statute fragment through signed manifests
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The module added a $250 qualifying-child supplement to the Connecticut EITC, and asserted a proof excerpt for it, on the strength of corpus_citation_path us-ct/statute/12-704e, whose pinned text contains no qualifying-child provision at all - the $250 comes from P.A. 25-168, which exists only in the 2026-supplement capture and applies only to taxable years commencing on or after January 1, 2025, while this module dated it effective_from '0001-01-01'.
modules.triage_notes: This is the one index where I could verify a defect against the source. I resolved us-ct/statute/12-704e at the release pinned by this commit (us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union): the phrase 'qualifying child' does not occur anywhere in that 473k-character capture, and the operative Sec. 12-704e text there runs (a) applicable percentage 23/30.5/40 per cent, (b) refund of excess only, (c) the MFS proration fraction, (d) the need-based-benefits exclusion - no $250. The deleted module nonetheless encodes `qualifying_child_additional_credit_amount: 250` and `ct_eitc_credit_allowed = ct_eitc_credit_before_child_addition + (if has_at_least_one_qualifying_child...: 250 else: 0)` with a proof excerpt 'at least one qualifying child for federal income tax purposes... additional two hundred fifty dollars' that is not present in the cited capture, and its module summary states the $250 as fact. I separately resolved us-ct/statute/2026-supplement/12-704e/earned-income-tax-credit, which does carry the $250 in subsec. (b) and whose history note reads 'P.A. 25-168 amended Subsec. (b) by adding provision re additional $250 for certain taxpayers ... applicable to taxable years commencing on and after January 1, 2025'. The prior commit e1e7f0e80 'Encode Connecticut qualifying-child EITC addition' had already re-grounded that $250 on the supplement path inside us-ct/policies/income_tax/2026_resident_liability_source_hold.yaml, so this deletion removes the ungrounded copy; the retire manifest calls it the 'stale pre-supplement EITC duplicate'. A second, co-existing defect kind applies: even on the correct supplement source the $250 and the rest of the module carry effective_from '0001-01-01' with no effective_to, i.e. timeless encoding that back-applies the 2025 amendment (and the 23% pre-2021 rate) to all years - wrong_period_or_effective_date. I chose untraceable_branch because the cited-source check is the harder evidence; a reviewer may prefer the period kind. Caveat: the module was created in bulk-encode commit aba1dc8d1 against whatever corpus release was pinned then, which I did not resolve, so I cannot rule out that an older capture under that path contained the clause. After this commit no module maps to us-ct/statute/12-704e in .axiom/index/provisions_to_rules.json, and the source-hold encodes only the 40% + $250 branch, so the MFS proration of subsec. (c) and the pre-2023 percentages are no longer covered anywhere.

verdict.justification: The file under review is new (pre_lines 0), and every §12-700(a)(10) value and formula in it is identical to the retired pilot's — same seven rates, same single floors 10k/50k/100k/200k/250k/500k, same scale factors 1/1.6/2.0, same phaseout starts and increments, same three recapture tiers including the head-of-household middle-tier special case — all of which I checked against the pinned statute text, so the commit corrects no number, boundary, date, version window, or statutory condition. The only added behavior is a full-year-residency input and an exactly-one-of-four-status judgment used as an `else: 0` gate; the retired pilot exposed no residency variable at all and documented its status booleans as an exclusive caller contract ("True only for joint or surviving-spouse filing status"), so there was no encoded branch that disagreed with the source to repair — this is precision the predecessor never claimed. The commit's own retirement manifest gives breadth, not error, as the reason, and the PR presents the change as an add-and-retire; the quoted sentence the first reader relied on is a disclaimer about what the new module claims, not an admission that the old encoding misstated the source. The substantive module-level delta is in fact a reduction of scope (personal credit, AMT, property-tax credit, stillborn credit, credit ordering, and the PolicyEngine-parity claim are all dropped).
verdict.quote: - absorb and retire the overlapping pilot and hand-authored statute fragment through signed manifests
verdict.notes: Verification detail for the reviewer. (1) Arithmetic equivalence: `ct_pit_2026_ordinary_schedule_tax` is line-for-line the pilot's `ct_pit_pilot_schedule_tax` with renamed symbols; `ct_pit_2026_ordinary_low_rate_phaseout_addback` inlines the pilot's `ct_pit_pilot_phaseout_start`/`_increment` selectors verbatim; low/middle/high recapture match, including the HoH carve-out (statute (B)(iv) is $140 per $8,000 max $4,200, which is not 1.6x the single $90/$2,700, hence the special case present in BOTH files). (2) MFS check: statute (D)(i) brackets equal (A)(i), and (D)(iii)-(v) use the same $105,000/$200,000/$500,000 starts and $25/$90/$50 per $5,000 with $250/$2,700/$450 maxima, so `schedule_scale = 1` for married-separate is correct and unchanged — no latent amount fix hiding in the rewrite. (3) The retirement manifest states verbatim: "reason": "Replace the broad Connecticut pilot and stale pre-supplement EITC duplicate with bounded source-backed canonical tax-year-2026 components", tool "axiom-encode retire"; the new module's own manifest carries "manual_exception": "repair", which is an axiom-encode exception category and plausibly the source of the commit subject "Repair ...", so that subject word is weak evidence of a fidelity fix. (4) The PR recorded no review findings ("Fresh independent exact-head review ... found no actionable findings"). (5) Fallback framing if a reviewer disagrees with me: the statute does say "There is hereby imposed on the Connecticut taxable income of each resident of this state a tax", and (b) taxes nonresidents by a different apportioned formula, so someone could call the added residency gate the addition of a condition the source states — but that reading is unrepresented_clause, not wrong_entity_or_scope, and it still runs into the rubric's rule that scope a module never claimed is at most unclear. (6) If any fidelity story exists in this commit it lives in module index 1 (the deleted pilot), whose `ct_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` grounded a credit-ordering chain on an excerpt "Order of credits" cited to the broad us-ct/statute/12-700/block-1 recovery blob while the statute places order of credits at §12-745; that would be untraceable_branch on the deleted file, not on the added one. The commit also drops the pilot's pending-validation waiver from known-validation-gaps.yaml.

verdict.justification: The first reader's premise fails on the text: the pilot did not cite only 12-700(a)(10); its module header cited `us-ct/statute/12-700/block-1` (the full Chapter 229 recovery capture) plus `12-704i/block-1`, and that pinned block demonstrably contains "Sec. 12-700a", "Sec. 12-703", "Sec. 12-704c", "Sec. 12-704i" and "Order of credits" (grep counts 4/2/2/2/2 in the resolved provision), so the personal-credit, AMT, property-tax and stillborn rules were inside the cited scope rather than wider than it. Nothing in the deletion corrects encoded meaning: every numeric parameter in the pilot (0.02/0.045/0.055/0.06/0.065/0.069/0.0699; floors 10000-500000; ceilings 16000/20000; phaseout 56500/78500/100500/50250, 5000/4000/2500, 25/250; recapture 105000/200000/500000, 25/90/50, 250/2700/450, head 140/4200) reappears unchanged in the added `2026_resident_ordinary_tax_before_personal_credit.yaml`, the schedule-scale and band formulas carry over structurally identical, and every proof excerpt the pilot cited resolves verbatim in the pinned block. The commit is a retirement of an overlapping hand-authored composition in favor of a bounded encoder-generated module — the signed manifest records `"tool": "axiom-encode retire"` with reason "Replace the broad Connecticut pilot and stale pre-supplement EITC duplicate with bounded source-backed canonical tax-year-2026 components", and the PR frames the replacement as a deliberate narrowing of claimed coverage, not a repair of wrong meaning. The residency and filing-status-exclusivity guards the replacement adds are new validation the pilot never claimed to enforce (it declared its caller boundaries explicitly), which the rules classify as added precision, not a defect.
verdict.quote: This is intentionally not a claim of complete annual Connecticut liability. Credits, alternative minimum tax, payments, refunds, and filing administration remain outside this module.
verdict.notes: Refutation evidence a reviewer can re-run: (1) `git -C rulespec-us show 196492ee5d:us-ct/policies/income_tax/2026_resident_ordinary_tax_before_personal_credit.yaml | grep -n "formula: '[0-9]"` versus the deleted file's parameters — all 25+ mapped values are identical, so there is no amount_mismatch, boundary, or logic change in the overlap. (2) resolve_provision.py on `us-ct/statute/12-700/block-1` (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, provision sha 9e7533110625f2bf…) returns a ~470KB Chapter 229 capture containing 12-700a, 12-703, 12-704c, 12-704i and "Order of credits" — the pilot's broad-block citation covered its credit/AMT rules, so "wrong_entity_or_scope" and "untraceable_branch" both lack a basis. (3) `.axiom/encoding-manifests/us-ct/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.json` is rewritten to a retire record (`"tool": "axiom-encode retire"`, `"applied_files": [... "deleted": true]`), and `known-validation-gaps.yaml` merely drops the pilot's pending fingerprint — bookkeeping, not fidelity. Residual uncertainty (why I did not go above ~0.72): the commit subject says "Repair", and the retired pilot was a `manual_exception: composition` hand-authored module carrying a pending validation waiver, so a reviewer could read the retirement as governance-driven removal of an under-validated over-broad surface; however that is a regime/hygiene judgment, and the PR's only scope complaint — "cite the exact official §12-700(a)(10) corpus scope instead of the full Chapter 229 recovery blob" — is citation-precision (provenance), which the rubric classifies as mechanical rather than fidelity. Also note the pilot's PolicyEngine-US oracle numbers (max abs error $0.4592 over 951 CT units) are self-reported inside the deleted module's own summary, so I treat them as corroborating, not decisive.

verdict.justification: The $250 qualifying-child supplement is not a branch invented out of nothing: it is real section 12-704e law, carried in the same corpus release at us-ct/statute/2026-supplement/12-704e/earned-income-tax-credit with metadata "amendment: P.A. 25-168, Section 371" and "amendment_applicable_tax_year_start: 2025-01-01", whose text reads "has at least one qualifying child for federal income tax purposes, such taxpayer shall be allowed an additional two hundred fifty dollars". What the deleted module got wrong against the source is the window, not the existence or the value: it gave the supplement a single timeless version starting '0001-01-01', so pre-2025 taxable years receive $250 the statute grants only "to taxable years commencing on and after January 1, 2025", and it pinned the amended content to the superseded pre-supplement capture (which itself opens "Readers should refer to the 2026 Supplement ... for updated versions of statutes amended ... during the 2025 legislative sessions"). The retire manifest's own reason — "stale pre-supplement EITC duplicate" — names staleness of the source expression, i.e. a version/date problem, and the first reader's own reading already states the 2025-01-01 vs '0001-01-01' mismatch. Untraceable_branch only survives on the narrow reading that the branch is absent from the one capture the module cited; the substantive defect a downstream reader would reproduce is wrong years.
verdict.quote:
-      - effective_from: '0001-01-01'
-        formula: |-
-          250
verdict.notes: Verification performed: resolve_provision at both 196492ee5d and parent 8ed64067 resolves us-ct/statute/12-704e to data/corpus/provisions/us-ct/statute/2026-07-13-recovery.jsonl (body sha 14bf7431…), whose 12-704e text runs (a)-(d) with zero occurrences of "qualifying child" — so the proof-atom excerpt "at least one qualifying child for federal income tax purposes... additional two hundred fifty dollars" is not in the cited path. The same text IS in /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/data/corpus/provisions/us-ct/statute/2026-07-24-ct-income-tax-supplement.jsonl (citation_path us-ct/statute/2026-supplement/12-704e/earned-income-tax-credit, expression_date 2026-01-01), added to the corpus 2026-07-24, i.e. after the module was generated on 2026-07-08. Caveats a reviewer should weigh before keeping this case at all: (1) the change is a whole-module retirement, not a targeted fix — it also deletes rules that are verbatim faithful to the pinned source (23 / 30.5 / 40 per cent applicable percentages, the subsection (c) separate-return proration), and nothing in the commit, PR, or manifest identifies the $250 as wrong; (2) the PR bullet the first reader quoted calls this a "hand-authored statute fragment", but .axiom manifest us-ct/.axiom/encoding-manifests/statutes/12-704e.json at the parent shows "tool": "axiom-encode encode --apply", backend codex, model gpt-5.5, run 40b435d4 — encoder-generated, so that quote is factually wrong about this file and is weak support for any kind; (3) the "overlapping"/"duplicate" framing is also inaccurate for the EITC: grep of the deleted pilot_liability_pipeline diff finds no EITC rules, and the replacement module's own rationale says it "does not compute the ... earned income tax credit", so CT EITC coverage was dropped outright rather than re-grounded; (4) the commit also removed the module's known-validation-gaps.yaml validate_failures pending entry (fingerprint sha256:399540d2…), consistent with the module having failed deterministic validation — plausibly on exactly the unmatched excerpt. If the corpus wants only fixes that correct meaning in place, this is prunable as a consolidation/retirement (verdict would be unclear); if retirement of defective content counts, the kind should be wrong_period_or_effective_date, with untraceable_branch as the defensible runner-up.

item.subject: Canonicalize Mississippi 2026 tax schedule

triage.commit_summary: The commit retires the Mississippi pilot liability pipeline module (and its fixtures) and replaces it with a single canonical calendar-year-2026 section 27-7-5 schedule module that takes one supplied Person-grain taxable income, floors it at zero, and computes 4 percent of the excess over $10,000. The reason given is that the pilot's two-candidate separate-vs-joint comparison, TaxUnit aggregation, and TaxUnit "income tax liability" output were PolicyEngine oracle-integration mechanics rather than rules established by Miss. Code section 27-7-5, so the replacement exposes schedule tax only and makes no tax-before-credit or final-liability claim.

modules.description_quote: The former pilot compared two PolicyEngine-specific completed-return candidates and selected the lower computed amount. That comparison was oracle-integration mechanics, not a rule established by this source, and is intentionally absent here.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix encoding of this same provision (the pilot module deleted at index 1) computed a TaxUnit-level 'income tax liability' by comparing separate-return and joint-return candidate taxes and taking the lower, a selection rule that Miss. Code section 27-7-5 does not establish; this replacement keeps only the source-owned rate schedule (4 percent of taxable income above $10,000, floored at zero) at the Person grain.
modules.triage_notes: Indices 0 and 1 are one replacement pair: this file is added, index 1 is deleted, and the rules are renamed (ms_pit_pilot_* -> ms_pit_2026_*), so the 'pre-fix' state for this module is the deleted pilot file. A reviewer building a pre/post defect corpus may want to fold the pair into a single defect instance keyed on the deleted file. Provision read through the pinned corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union (data/corpus/provisions/us-ms/statute/2026-07-16-pit-central-us-ms-section-27-7-5.jsonl): section 27-7-5 contains only the levy, the rate schedule (no tax through $10,000; 4% above $10,000 for calendar year 2026), the S-corporation exclusion, the nonresident like-tax, and the subsection (4) fiscal-year proration - there is no separate-vs-joint filing election and no lower-of rule anywhere in it, confirming the removed branch was ungrounded. Rate ($10,000 ceiling, 0.04) and the 2026-01-01/2026-12-31 window are unchanged between pre and post, so no amount or period defect. The new module narrows scope (Person-grain schedule tax only, no TaxUnit liability output), which is a removal of unsupported claims rather than an addition of new scope. Confidence held at 0.7 only because the defect text lives in the deleted half of the pair, not because the kind is in doubt. Companion non-module changes in the commit: new fixtures, a retire manifest whose 'reason' field reads 'Replace PolicyEngine-specific candidate comparison with one canonical source-owned Mississippi 2026 section 27-7-5 schedule', the reverse index, and oracle-coverage-pending (11 legacy IDs out, 4 canonical IDs in, ceiling 2518 -> 2511).

modules.description_quote: replace the legacy PolicyEngine-oriented pilot candidate-selection pipeline with one canonical Mississippi Code § 27-7-5 schedule surface
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: This module branched on whether a separate-return candidate tax was strictly lower than a joint-return candidate tax and returned the lower as a TaxUnit 'income tax liability', but Miss. Code section 27-7-5 establishes only the levy and the rate schedule and creates no filing-method election or lower-of selection, so that branch and the liability output had no basis in the cited source.
modules.triage_notes: Deletion of the defective module is the fix; the corrected encoding lands at index 0. The defect has two facets: (a) the ungrounded strict-lower branch (ms_pit_pilot_separate_total_is_strictly_lower feeding ms_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability) - untraceable_branch, the kind chosen here because both the PR and the replacement module's own rationale name exactly this; and (b) the TaxUnit aggregation via ms_pit_pilot_person_of_tax_unit and the 'liability before credits' output surface, which would read as wrong_entity_or_scope if a reviewer prefers that facet. The independent-review comment on PR #1114 (an issue comment by PavelMakarchuk, not a formal GitHub review, so not quoted as pr_review) states: 'Confirmed the legacy pilot, PolicyEngine two-candidate comparison, TaxUnit aggregation, and misleading liability output are fully retired.' Commit message body is empty; PR body and that comment plus the replacement module's rationale are the evidence. Provision text read (see index 0 notes) and confirms no election or lower-of rule in section 27-7-5. Parameters that were NOT wrong: the $10,000 zero-tax ceiling and the 4% 2026 rate carry over unchanged into the replacement. Note the module's own excerpt for ms_pit_pilot_separate_total_is_strictly_lower cited only 'a tax at the following rates', which does not support a comparison branch - visible evidence of the ungrounding inside the deleted file itself.

verdict.justification: I read the pinned § 27-7-5 text and it establishes only rate brackets (no tax on the first $5,000; no tax $5,000–$10,000 from CY2023; 4% on taxable income in excess of $10,000 for CY2026), an S-corporation exclusion, a nonresident like-tax, and fiscal-year proration — nothing authorizing a comparison of separate-return versus joint-return candidate taxes or a selection of the lower amount. The deleted pilot nonetheless encoded `ms_pit_pilot_separate_total_is_strictly_lower` and a TaxUnit `ms_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` whose rule-level `source:` and proof atom attributed that selection branch to § 27-7-5(1), and the commit removes it while keeping the source-owned arithmetic `0.04 × max(0, TI − 10000)`, which I verified matches (a)(i)6, (b)(i) and (b)(ii)3 exactly. That is a branch with no basis in the cited source being removed — untraceable_branch — not an amount, boundary, period, or polarity error, and not a mere enhancement, since the PR calls it a repair and the review comment calls the retired output "misleading". The change is also not mechanical: formulas, rule set, output entity and public output surface all changed.
verdict.quote:
-    source: Miss. Code section 27-7-5(1), lower compared 2026 schedule amount before credits
-        formula: |-
-          if ms_pit_pilot_separate_total_is_strictly_lower:
-            ms_pit_pilot_separate_total_schedule_tax
-          else:
-            ms_pit_pilot_joint_total_schedule_tax
verdict.notes:
Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "the source actually provides a filing-method election" — verified false against the pinned provision (release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, body sha a0a11e16…, fix_time_corpus_match same_body); subsections (1)–(4) contain rates, the S-corp exclusion, the nonresident like-tax, and fiscal-year proration only. (2) "the replacement is itself defective" — the new module's 4% × max(0, TI − $10,000), effective 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, is faithful, so there is no competing amount_mismatch/boundary_direction/wrong_period kind. (3) "the pilot disclaimed statutory grounding, so it was known scaffolding, not a defect" — the pilot's module rationale did disclaim it in prose, but the rule-level `source:` field and the proof atom ("there is hereby assessed and levied, to be collected and paid") still attributed the selection branch and a TaxUnit liability output to § 27-7-5, which is what makes it untraceable rather than merely narrow.

Two caveats for the reviewer. First, the case is genuinely commit-level: module index 0 is a pure file addition with no pre-image, so all defect evidence lives in the paired deletion at index 1 (`us-ms/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml`). If the corpus is meant to be strictly per-file, this case should be anchored to index 1 or to the commit, not to the added file. Second, a defensible alternative kind is wrong_entity_or_scope: the fix also moves the public output from a TaxUnit "income tax liability" to a Person-grain schedule tax ("expose schedule tax only; make no annual tax-before-credit or final-liability claim"). I treat that as the downstream consequence of deleting the aggregation the comparison required — the untraceable selection branch is the primary defect — but a reviewer who weights the output-surface claim more heavily could reasonably relabel it. Confidence is 0.82 rather than higher only because of that kind overlap and the file-pairing question, not because the fidelity call is in doubt.

verdict.justification: The deleted module published a public TaxUnit rule `ms_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` whose formula branched on `ms_pit_pilot_separate_total_is_strictly_lower` and returned the lower of a separate-return and a joint-return candidate tax, and it grounded that branch in a proof atom citing us-ms/statute/27-7-5 with the excerpt "there is hereby assessed and levied, to be collected and paid" (the selector rule likewise cited "a tax at the following rates"). Reading § 27-7-5 through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, body sha a0a11e16…) shows subsections (1)-(4) contain only the levy, the graduated/flattening rate schedule, the S-corporation exclusion, the nonresident like-tax, and fiscal-year proration — no filing-method election and no lower-of-two-returns selection — so the branch and the liability output had no basis in the cited source. The fix removes that construct entirely and re-grounds the surface on the schedule alone (`ms_pit_2026_rate * max(0, taxable_income - 10000)` at Person grain), which is the removal/re-grounding pattern of untraceable_branch rather than a mere refactor. The tempting refutation — that the old module's rationale itself disclaimed the comparison as "target-integration mechanics" — fails because the encoded artifact still attributed the branch and the liability output to § 27-7-5 in its `source:` field and proof atoms, and the merge-time review calls that output "misleading".
verdict.quote:
-        formula: |-
-          if ms_pit_pilot_separate_total_is_strictly_lower:
-            ms_pit_pilot_separate_total_schedule_tax
-          else:
-            ms_pit_pilot_joint_total_schedule_tax
verdict.notes: Refutation attempts and why they fail: (1) "mechanical / pilot retirement" — no; formulas, a public output rule, the TaxUnit aggregation relation, and two candidate pipelines are deleted and replaced with a different arithmetic surface. (2) "not_a_defect, the pre-fix module disclaimed source grounding" — the prose rationale disclaimed it, but `source: Miss. Code section 27-7-5(1), lower compared 2026 schedule amount before credits` plus proof atoms citing corpus_citation_path us-ms/statute/27-7-5 on both the selector and the liability formula are exactly the encoded attribution the statute does not support; PR #1114 review comment: "Confirmed the legacy pilot, PolicyEngine two-candidate comparison, TaxUnit aggregation, and misleading liability output are fully retired." (3) Secondary kind worth noting for a reviewer: wrong_entity_or_scope is a real co-defect — the old surface emitted a TaxUnit-level "income tax liability" while § 27-7-5 levies on the individual's net income, and PR bullet "expose schedule tax only; make no annual tax-before-credit or final-liability claim while the TY2026 annual package is unavailable" is a scope/output-surface correction. I keep untraceable_branch as the primary because the flagged rule_path is the if/else formula itself and the TaxUnit scope existed only to host that ungrounded comparison. (4) boundary_direction does not fit: the strict `<` in `ms_pit_pilot_separate_total_is_strictly_lower` was not corrected to `<=`; the whole comparison was deleted, so the defect is the branch's existence, not its strictness. (5) amount_mismatch does not fit: the $10,000 ceiling and 0.04 rate are carried over unchanged and both match the statute ("For calendar year 2023 and all calendar years thereafter, there shall be no tax levied under subparagraph (ii) … in excess of Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000.00) up to and including Ten Thousand Dollars ($10,000.00)" plus "For calendar year 2026, on such taxable income, the rate shall be four percent (4%)"). Mild residual uncertainty: the commit is framed as canonicalization of a pilot rather than a bug fix, and its body is empty, so the fidelity reading rests on the PR body, the review comment, and the replacement module's own rationale ("That comparison was oracle-integration mechanics, not a rule established by this source, and is intentionally absent here") rather than on an explicit "this was wrong" statement.

item.subject: Repair NC TY2026 statute source backing

triage.commit_summary: The commit repointed the North Carolina TY2026 individual income-tax modules from a stale predecessor rendition of N.C. Gen. Stat. §105-153.5/.7/.9 to the pinned TY2026 successor corpus expression (axiom-corpus PR #539, commit b403bf49), and rewrote the encodings that the successor text contradicts. Substantively it replaced the superseded pre-2022 child-deduction table with the current seven-band $3,000 table, deleted standard-deduction and child-deduction versions that the current section no longer states, and added the §105-153.5(a)(2)e. section 165(d) wagering-loss itemized deduction to the resident core pipeline; the remaining edits are summaries, citation paths, proof excerpts, and a refreshed import hash.

modules.description_quote: repoint North Carolina resident income-tax modules from stale predecessor fragments to the official TY2026 temporal statute successor
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing computed was wrong: the only substantive edit is the refreshed import hash for us-nc:statutes/105/105-153/7#individual_income_tax_rate (whose proof excerpt changed in index 5) plus new module-level upstream_source_check metadata and a reworded summary.
modules.triage_notes: Diff touches only module.source_verification (new upstream_source_check block), module.summary prose, and the sha256 of the imported rate atom. Both rules keep effective_from 2026-01-01 / effective_to 2026-12-31 and identical formulas (max(0, nc_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income); nc_pit_pilot_taxable_income * individual_income_tax_rate); the imported rate is still 0.0399. Summary prose was corrected (pre-fix said subsection (a1) 'may change the rate beginning in 2027'; the pinned successor §105-153.7(a) actually schedules 3.49% in 2027-2029 and (a1) triggers start FY2033-34), but that is module-level metadata with no effect on the 2026-bounded output, so mechanical per the triage rules.

modules.description_quote: encode the current §105-153.5 child-deduction bands, TY2026 3.99% rate, post-2023 §105-153.9 rendition, and §165(d) wagering-loss itemized component
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The itemized-deduction sum omitted §105-153.5(a)(2)e., the deduction for wagering losses allowed under Code section 165(d) to the extent not deducted in arriving at adjusted gross income, so NC itemized deductions were understated for any taxpayer with such losses.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read: I resolved us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5 two ways. The resolver's default release (us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, expression 2026-07-13) has no wagering item, but the successor corpus commit b403bf49e3c9cf31f26f239f1e188683be1b9e65 that this PR pins (file data/corpus/provisions/us-nc/statute/2026-07-26-nc-ty2026-income-tax-core.jsonl, expression 2026-07-07) contains verbatim: 'e. The amount allowed as a deduction for wagering losses under section 165(d) of the Code, to the extent the losses are not deducted in arriving at adjusted gross income.' — exactly the new proof excerpt. Pre-fix the string 'wagering' appears nowhere under us-nc (git grep at parent 5c087fc8). The fix also adds input nc_pit_2026_wagering_loss_deduction_not_in_federal_agi (companion test file updated, outside this chunk), widens module.source_verification to four citation paths, refreshes the same imported rate hash as index 0, and rewrites the deferral rationale that had wrongly asserted 'the available section 105-153.9 provision is the pre-2023 version'; the final liability output stays deferred. PR body also says 'independent review fixed ... an incorrectly anchored wagering proof', i.e. the anchor landed on §105-153.5 in the final state. Max's later HOLD review (2026-07-27, after this commit) says other enacted S.L. 2026-31 modifications are still missing — not fixed here.

modules.description_quote: repoint North Carolina resident income-tax modules from stale predecessor fragments to the official TY2026 temporal statute successor
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The module carried historical versions and a whole rule (2019/2020 standard deduction columns of $20,000/$21,500, $15,000/$16,125, $10,000/$10,750 and a timeless pre-2022 $2,500 child amount) whose table columns and values do not exist anywhere in the cited §105-153.5 text, which states one current 'Standard Deduction' column and a $3,000 top child amount.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read: both the pinned successor (corpus b403bf49) and the earlier release's own §105-153.5/a fragment show a single column — 'Filing Status Standard Deduction Married, filing jointly/surviving spouse $25,500 Head of Household 19,125 Single 12,750 Married, filing separately 12,750' — with no 2019 or 2020-2021 columns, so the removed proof atoms cited columns ('2019 standard deduction', '2020-2021 standard deduction') that the source does not contain. Surviving 2022-01-01 amounts are unchanged; citation paths move from us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5/a to us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5; the summary adds a mention of the TY2025 wagering item but no rule for it (the input lives in the composed pipeline, index 1). Caveat for the reviewer: the deleted values are historically accurate NC amounts for those years, so this can also be read as a temporal-scope narrowing/provenance repair rather than a corrected meaning — hence the moderate confidence. The deleted timeless '0001-01-01: 2500' child version is the same defect family as index 3 and could alternatively be tagged wrong_period_or_effective_date.

modules.description_quote: independent review fixed two actionable findings: incomplete current child-deduction bands and an incorrectly anchored wagering proof
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The child-deduction table encoded the superseded pre-2022 schedule — six bands per filing status topping out at $2,500 — while the cited §105-153.5(a1) states seven bands per status topping out at $3,000 (MFJ bounds 40k/60k/80k/100k/120k/140k), so every child deduction came out $500 low and the top band was missing.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read and matched cell by cell against the pinned successor (corpus b403bf49, §105-153.5(a1)): 'Married, filing jointly/ Up to $40,000 $3,000 ... Over $120,000 Up to $140,000 500.00 Over $140,000 0', Head of Household to $105,000, Single and MFS to $70,000 — identical to the post-fix 28-entry tables. The same commit also fixes the version window from the timeless effective_from '0001-01-01' to '2022-01-01' and repoints the citation from the .../105-153.5/a1 fragment to the section, so this module carries a wrong_period_or_effective_date aspect as well; I tagged amount_mismatch because the decisive change is the replacement of every band bound and deduction amount. Pre-fix summary even self-described as 'Effective for taxable years beginning before January 1, 2022', yet the module fed the TY2026 resident pipeline.

modules.description_quote: repoint North Carolina resident income-tax modules from stale predecessor fragments to the official TY2026 temporal statute successor
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing in the encoded meaning was wrong; only the module's corpus citation string pointed at the predecessor fragment path us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5/b instead of the section path us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5.
modules.triage_notes: Single-line diff: corpus_citation_path only. Summary, deferred_outputs, rules, versions, formulas and inputs are untouched — citation-string-only correction, mechanical provenance per the triage rules.

modules.description_quote: The enacted subsection (a) schedule sets the rate at 3.99% in 2026 and changes the scheduled rate after 2026.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The encoded 2026 rate was already right (0.0399); what was wrong was the proof anchor and summary, which quoted a predecessor rendition row 'After 2025 3.99%' and claimed 3.99% applies to all years after 2025, whereas the successor §105-153.7(a) table reads 'In 2026 3.99%' and drops to 3.49% in 2027-2029.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read: pinned successor §105-153.7(a) table is 'In 2022 4.99% In 2023 4.75% In 2024 4.5% In 2025 4.25% In 2026 3.99% In 2027, 2028, and 2029 3.49% In 2030, 2031, and 2032 3.24% After 2032 2.99%', and the (a1) triggers start FY 2033-2034, so the post-fix row/excerpt are exact. I compared the full pre- and post-fix files: all four rules keep identical versions and formulas (rate 0.0399 bounded 2026-01-01..2026-12-31; month count 12; tax formula; withholding predicate), so only module.summary and one proof-atom table row/excerpt changed — mechanical per the rules. Reviewer note: the substantive misstatement was confined to prose, and index 0's import hash change is the downstream effect of this excerpt edit. Max's 2026-07-27 review says §105-153.7(b) is still too narrow ('statute excludes only a §443(a)(1) return that is ALSO under 12 months') — that logic defect is present both before and after this commit and is not fixed here.

modules.description_quote: encode the current §105-153.5 child-deduction bands, TY2026 3.99% rate, post-2023 §105-153.9 rendition, and §165(d) wagering-loss itemized component
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The encoded rule was unchanged and already correct; only the summary was restated to describe the current post-2023 rendition of §105-153.9 rather than quoting subsection (f) plus an 'Effect of Amendments' note.
modules.triage_notes: Byte-compared pre- and post-fix files: the only difference is module.summary. The rule keeps source 105-153.9(f), both proof atoms with identical excerpts, effective_from '2023-01-01', and formula 0. Provision read: the pinned successor §105-153.9 is headed '(Effective for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2023)', which is what the new summary asserts. The companion file 9.test.yaml also changed in this commit (outside this chunk). The related substantive correction — the resident pipeline's stale claim that §105-153.9 was the pre-2023 version — lives in index 1, not here.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix TY2026 itemized sum was charitable + mortgage/property + medical/dental + claim-of-right, while the cited provision at the pinned successor record (us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5, expression date 2026-07-07, in 2026-07-26-nc-ty2026-income-tax-core.jsonl) lists a fifth item, "e. The amount allowed as a deduction for wagering losses under section 165(d) of the Code, to the extent the losses are not deducted in arriving at adjusted gross income," and the rule's own proof atom claims to encode "An amount equal to the sum of the items listed in this subdivision," so the encoding disagreed with its cited source rather than merely under-claiming scope. The fix adds exactly that missing statutory deduction item (plus its input and an excerpt-matched proof atom), which is the definition of unrepresented_clause; no effective date, version window, entity, threshold, or boolean structure changed, so wrong_period_or_effective_date and the other kinds do not fit the semantic delta even though the commit's root cause was stale source backing. It is not mechanical or an unclaimed enhancement: the sum flows through nc_pit_2026_deduction_amount = max(standard, itemized) into the live, non-deferred nc_pit_2026_income_tax_before_credits, and the companion suite's expected outputs moved (itemized '26000' → '28000', tax before credits '2633.4' → '2553.6') for the case carrying 2000 of wagering losses. I tried and failed to refute on all three fronts — clause absent from source (it is present verbatim), scope never claimed (proof atom claims the statutory sum), and metadata-only (formula and expectations changed).
verdict.quote: +          + max(0, nc_pit_2026_wagering_loss_deduction_not_in_federal_agi)
verdict.notes: Verification trail: (1) The added proof excerpt is verbatim in the pinned corpus successor — git -C /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus show e07011cce174be6b4f6c6e132e66dc4e122565bd:data/corpus/provisions/us-nc/statute/2026-07-26-nc-ty2026-income-tax-core.jsonl, record 1, citation_path us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5, item e. appears immediately after item d. with no effective-year bracket excluding TY2026 (adjacent items that are time-limited do carry explicit brackets, e.g. the §105-153.11 donation carve-out "Effective for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025, and expiring ... January 1, 2027"). (2) resolve_provision.py --citation us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5 --rulespec-commit d1ed1b5949 resolves to the OLDER rendition (release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, file 2026-07-13-recovery.jsonl line 52) whose (a)(2) list ends at item d. and contains no "wagering" — so a reviewer running the resolver alone will wrongly conclude the clause is absent; the module's own pin (toolchain axiom_corpus_ref e07011cc, comment "NC TY2026 temporal successor from axiom-corpus PR #539") carries the successor row that does contain it. (3) The parent commit 5c087fc88 is "Pin NC TY2026 corpus successor", so the correct text was already available and cited when the omission stood — the disagreement with the cited source is real at the parent, not created by this commit. (4) Residual nuance a reviewer may weigh: the rule's source line ("supported North Carolina itemized deductions") and module summary ("selects the larger supported standard or itemized deduction") hedge with "supported" both before AND after the fix, so the hedge cannot be read as an intentional exclusion of item e.; and the commit-level framing ("Repair NC TY2026 statute source backing") is temporal, so someone could argue wrong_period_or_effective_date at commit granularity — but within this module no date/window/period field changed. (5) Out of scope but worth flagging: MaxGhenis's PR comment records a HOLD finding that the addition/deduction sums still omit S.L. 2026-31 items (§164 SALT addback, §105-153.6A R&E addback), so this module remains incomplete against TY2026 law even after the fix; that is a separate, unfixed gap and does not bear on this classification. Other module_files in the same commit are separate candidates: 002 (105-153.5/a.yaml) drops pre-2022 standard-deduction versions and repoints the fragment citation, 006 (105-153/9.yaml) swaps the pre-2023 rendition for the post-2023 one — those look like wrong_period_or_effective_date, not this kind.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as provenance-only (citation-string) or as a temporal re-pin, and it survives: alongside the citation-path edits the diff deletes real encoded meaning — two version rows from each of four standard-deduction rules ($20,000/$21,500, $15,000/$16,125, $10,000/$10,750), a timeless $2,500 child-deduction version, and the entire rule child_deduction_highest_amount_before_2022 — so the module's 2019–2021 answers change. I read the provision through the corpus commit pinned in .axiom/toolchain.toml (e07011cc, identical at parent 5c087fc8 and at the fix), and the TY2026 successor record for us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5 carries exactly one "Standard Deduction" column ($25,500 / 19,125 / 12,750 / 12,750) and a child table topping at $3,000: the strings 21,500, 16,125, 10,750 and $2,500 appear nowhere, and the successor file contains no .../105-153.5/a fragment record at all (only the superseded 2026-07-13-recovery rendition does, and that fragment likewise lacks the historical columns and contains no child-deduction table). So the deleted versions and the deleted rule were values and proof atoms with no basis in the cited provision — including child-deduction atoms grounded on subsection (a), which does not contain the child table — which is untraceable_branch ("the fix removes or re-grounds it, including formulas grounded on the wrong provision"), not a corrected date or number.
verdict.quote:
-            column: 2019 standard deduction
-  - effective_from: '2019-01-01'
-    formula: '20000'
-- name: child_deduction_highest_amount_before_2022
verdict.notes:
Verification trail: pinned corpus is axiom-corpus e07011cce174be6b4f6c6e132e66dc4e122565bd at BOTH the parent and the fix commit (.axiom/toolchain.toml is byte-identical), so the pre-fix atoms were already untraceable against the module's own pin — this is not a case where the source moved under the encoding. That file's us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5 body (2026-07-26-nc-ty2026-income-tax-core.jsonl, expression_date 2026-07-07) contains "Filing Status Standard Deduction Married, filing jointly/surviving spouse $25,500 Head of Household 19,125 Single 12,750 Married, filing separately 12,750" and a child table whose top amount is $3,000; counts of "21,500", "16,125", "10,750", "$2,500", "2,500.00" are all zero. The older 2026-07-13-recovery rendition holds the us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5/a fragment the module used to cite; its text also has only the single current column and zero occurrences of "Child Deduction".
Second-best kind considered and rejected: wrong_period_or_effective_date. Two of the removed items (the child_deduction version at effective_from '0001-01-01' formula '2500' and the whole child_deduction_highest_amount_before_2022 rule, also '0001-01-01') are literally "timeless encoding of superseded text". But the fix re-dates nothing — it deletes, and it leaves other timeless versions untouched (the repayment-threshold rule keeps effective_from '0001-01-01'; the $20,000 mortgage/property cap keeps '2014-01-01'), so this was not a date-correction pass. A reviewer who weights the '0001-01-01' deletions heavily could defensibly move this to wrong_period_or_effective_date; the kind is the softer part of my 0.82.
Honest caveat for the reviewer: the deleted numbers are historically accurate North Carolina law (2019 MFJ $20,000, 2020–21 $21,500, etc.), so under a "wrong versus real-world law" notion of fidelity this would look like scope narrowing rather than a correction. It is a defect under this taxonomy's definition (encoded meaning disagreeing with the CITED source text) because the module asserted table columns — "column: 2019 standard deduction", "column: 2020-2021 standard deduction", "column: deduction amount before 2022" — that its pinned provision does not contain.
Scope note: many hunks in this file are citation-path-only (us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5/a -> us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5) on rules whose values did not change (standard_deduction_ineligible_under_section_63, the $20,000 cap, the $3,000 repayment threshold, child_deduction_highest_amount_2022_and_later); taken alone those are mechanical provenance. The module summary also newly mentions the §165(d) wagering item, but no wagering rule is added in this file (the successor text does contain "165(d)"), so that line is metadata, not encoding. The classification rests solely on the deleted versions and the deleted rule.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix module was not a botched transcription of the current table: its own summary declared it encoded the schedule "Effective for taxable years beginning before January 1, 2022", and its six-band / $2,500-max values are a faithful encoding of that superseded pre-2022 §105-153.5(a1) text — but all three parameter tables carried `effective_from: '0001-01-01'` with no `effective_to`, so superseded text applied for all time, including the TY2026 pipeline that consumed it. The fix narrows the window to `effective_from: '2022-01-01'`, repoints `corpus_citation_path` from the stale `/a1` predecessor fragment to `us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5`, and swaps in the current seven-band / $3,000 schedule; the commit subject ("Repair NC TY2026 statute source backing") and PR bullets ("repoint … from stale predecessor fragments to the official TY2026 temporal statute successor"; "This is a legitimate temporal/source-structure repair") frame it the same way. The kind taxonomy assigns exactly this pattern — "timeless encoding of superseded text" — to wrong_period_or_effective_date, so the changed cell values are the symptom of a version-anchoring defect rather than an independent amount error. It is still a fidelity defect (the numbers really were wrong for TY2026), so only the kind changes, not the classification.
verdict.quote:
-    Effective for taxable years beginning before January 1, 2022, a taxpayer allowed a federal child tax credit under section 24 is allowed a North Carolina deduction for each qualifying child, with the per-child amount set by filing status and federal adjusted gross income.
-      - effective_from: '0001-01-01'
+      - effective_from: '2022-01-01'
verdict.notes:
Verified source text: the resolver (pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, corpus commit 0fd35bfbda, provision file data/corpus/provisions/us-nc/statute/2026-07-13-recovery.jsonl line 52, body sha256 f40ff33b90…) gives current §105-153.5(a1) as seven bands per filing status topping at $3,000 with MFJ bounds 40k/60k/80k/100k/120k/140k, HoH 30/45/60/75/90/105k, Single and MFS 20/30/40/50/60/70k. The post-fix tables match that exactly; the pre-fix tables match the pre-2022 statute exactly (same bounds minus the top band, every amount $500 lower, $2,500 max). So the pre-fix numbers were internally coherent law, just the wrong vintage — that is the reason I moved the kind.

Two honest counterweights for the reviewer, which is why confidence is 0.6 and not higher: (1) resolving the pre-fix citation path `us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5/a1` at the parent commit 5c087fc884 through the same pinned corpus returns the CURRENT text ($3,000, seven bands, sha256 2422c4d27b…) — the stale predecessor fragment is no longer reachable, so a reviewer who defines "the cited source" as what that path resolves to today would legitimately keep amount_mismatch, since the encoded cells disagree with the resolvable cited text. (2) The diff really does change ~60 table cells and add a band per status, and the PR bullet "encode the current §105-153.5 child-deduction bands" supports the numeric framing. If the corpus rubric prefers root cause, this is wrong_period_or_effective_date; if it prefers the surface of what the fix edited, amount_mismatch survives.

Separately, the first reader's justification quote ("independent review fixed two actionable findings: incomplete current child-deduction bands and an incorrectly anchored wagering proof") is weak evidence for the pre-fix defect: it describes findings raised and fixed inside PR #1106's own review cycle against an intermediate head, not the state of main before d1ed1b5949, and the "wagering proof" half belongs to a different module (the §165(d) itemized component, not a1.yaml). The decisive evidence for this module is the diff itself plus the old summary line.

Not mechanical: parameter values and version windows both changed. Not not_a_defect: the module fed us-nc/policies/income_tax/resident_core_liability_pipeline.yaml for TY2026, so the superseded schedule was live, producing child deductions $500 low per band with the >120k band wrongly zeroed at what the current law makes a $500 band.

item.subject: Add Colorado 2026 resident source-held boundary (#1104)

triage.commit_summary: The commit adds one entirely new Colorado module, us-co/policies/income_tax/2026_full_year_resident_source_hold.yaml, that encodes a tax-year-2026 full-year-resident "source-readiness boundary": it carries federal taxable income and federal AGI in from the aligned federal return per C.R.S. 39-22-104, and makes every downstream Colorado stage (modifications, taxable income, tax including the 39-22-627 annual rate adjustment, credits, and signed liability) a fail-closed zero sentinel gated by explicit source-hold judgments, because the pinned 2025 CRS Title 39 corpus does not resolve the 2026 conditional modification branches, the certified rate determination, or a complete credit surface. It also ships a four-case companion test suite, a signed encoding manifest, a reverse-index regeneration, and removes one now-obsolete known-validation-gaps waiver for us-co/statutes/39/39-22-627.yaml.

modules.description_quote: add a source-grounded Colorado TY2026 full-year-resident boundary from federal taxable income and federal AGI
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the module did not exist before this commit (status 'added', pre_lines 0), so no pre-fix encoding was wrong — the change adds brand-new TY2026 Colorado resident scope rather than correcting any encoded meaning against the source.
modules.triage_notes: RECOMMEND PRUNING from the defect corpus: there is no pre-fix module state for a fidelity judge to compare against. Verified with `git -C rulespec-us log --oneline a08cb62408 -- us-co/policies/income_tax/` that the only prior Colorado income-tax modules are pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml and eitc_pilot_pipeline.yaml, and `git show --stat` confirms neither was touched here; the PR body explicitly says "Merged PR #986 is the distinct narrow base-tax pilot. This PR does not alter that pipeline." So nothing was superseded or re-grounded. Classification is 'unclear' only because the triage taxonomy has no bucket for a pure new-module addition: 'mechanical' would be factually false (402 lines of new rules, formulas, versions, inputs and outputs), and 'fidelity' would assert a pre-fix defect that does not exist. The task guidance "A change that merely adds new outputs, precision, or scope the module never claimed is not a defect; classify unclear at most" is what drove the label; defect_kind is 'none' because no defect was identified, not because evidence was missing. Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus (resolve_provision.py, us-co/statute/39/39-22-104): the proof-atom excerpts are verbatim in the pinned 2025 CRS text — "a tax of four and forty one-hundredths percent is imposed on the federal taxable income" (§ 39-22-104(1)(c)), "Prior to the application of the rate of tax prescribed in subsection (1), (1.5), or (1.7) of this section, the federal taxable income shall be modified as provided in subsections (3) and (4) of this section" (§ 39-22-104(2)), and "Except as otherwise provided in section 39-22-627" — so the new encoding's grounding checks out. Other changes in the commit are non-module and mechanical: a 6-line deletion of the us-co/statutes/39/39-22-627.yaml pending waiver from known-validation-gaps.yaml ("Retire obsolete Colorado source validation waiver" in the commit body; PR body says the waiver "was removed by #986 and later mechanically reintroduced during protected-base approval migration"), the signed encoding manifest, and .axiom/index/provisions_to_rules.json regeneration. The PR has empty reviews, review_comments and issue_comments, so the only narrative evidence is the commit body and PR body. One intra-PR commit, "Clarify Colorado post-modification income stage", suggests a rename/rework of co_pit_2026_state_income_after_modifications during review, but the squashed merge collapses it so no pre/post pair survives in merged history.

verdict.justification: The diff is a whole-file creation ("new file mode 100644", "--- /dev/null", 402 added lines, zero removed), and `git ls-tree` on parent 5cca26e89d confirms the only pre-existing us-co/policies/income_tax modules are `eitc_pilot_pipeline.yaml` and `pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml`, neither of which this commit touches — so there is no prior encoded meaning that could disagree with the source. The module itself declares it is additive, not corrective: its summary says "The module is intentionally incomplete and makes no annual liability or oracle-parity claim," and every Colorado stage is an explicit fail-closed zero sentinel rather than a re-grounded formula. The only deletion in the commit is a `known-validation-gaps.yaml` waiver entry for `39-22-627` (ledger bookkeeping in a non-module file), which is mechanical provenance, not a fidelity fix. This is new TY2026 resident scope the repo never claimed before, so the first reader's hedge to "unclear" understates a settled negative: nothing was wrong pre-fix because nothing existed.

verdict.notes: Refutation target: the first reader's "unclear" hedge. The evidence is not ambiguous — it settles the question in the negative, so the case should be pruned from a real-defect corpus rather than kept for a second look. Supporting facts verified read-only: (1) `git show --stat a08cb62408` lists 5 files — the new module (402 lines added, 0 removed), its new companion test, a new encoding manifest under `.axiom/encoding-manifests/`, a `provisions_to_rules.json` index regeneration, and a 6-line deletion from `known-validation-gaps.yaml`; (2) `git log --follow` on the module path returns exactly one commit, a08cb6240, so there is no earlier version under any name; (3) the deleted waiver entry is the `us-co/statutes/39/39-22-627.yaml` pending fingerprint, which the PR body explains "was removed by #986 and later mechanically reintroduced during protected-base approval migration" — bookkeeping, not encoded meaning. If the corpus rubric insists on the "unclear at most" ceiling for purely additive changes, the fallback is unclear/none; the defect kind is "none" under either reading, and no kind is supportable from this diff. One latent oddity worth a reviewer's eye but NOT a defect fixed here: `co_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid` contains the tautologies "co_pit_2026_federal_taxable_income >= 0 or co_pit_2026_federal_taxable_income < 0" (and the same for federal AGI), which are unconditionally true and encode no real domain check — that is a weakness introduced by this commit, not corrected by it, so it cannot make this case a fidelity correction. If a later commit tightens those clauses, that commit is the defect-fix candidate.

item.subject: Add Maryland 2026 resident source-held boundary (#1103)

item.subject: fix: repair Medicaid MAGI household pipeline

triage.commit_summary: The commit repairs the 42 CFR 435.603 MAGI household-income composition in PR #1007 after a blind review returned six blocking findings, replacing the 816-line applicant-scoped pipeline with a 2,506-line fail-closed rewrite. It re-grounds household membership on a module-owned member-first relation (including the mandatory paragraph-(f)(5) fallback to (f)(3)), moves the paragraph-(d)(3) cash-support option from every member's contribution to the paragraph-(f)(2)(i) applicant only, splits current-month and projected-annual budget bases per paragraph (h), routes final eligibility through the paragraph-(c) exception gate for (i)/(j)/(k), and makes every public output gate on the runtime-validity rule that was previously computed but never consumed.

modules.description_quote: (d)(2)(ii) and (d)(3) are scoped to different applicants but applied per member
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module summed the wrong person set for the applicant: it iterated the imported paragraph-(d) relation with reversed argument orientation and added the paragraph-(d)(3) State-option cash support inside every member's contribution, although 42 CFR 435.603(d)(3) allows that support only 'In the case of individuals described in paragraph (f)(2)(i)' and (d)(2)(ii) excludes the dependent's income from the taxpayer's household, not the dependent's own.
modules.triage_notes: IMPORTANT for corpus use: the bundle shows this module as status 'added' with pre_lines 0 because the PR branch was force-pushed and the build+repair were folded into the branch's base commit. The true pre-fix module is the 816-line file at GitHub commit 593e0f945aa33f2abd7a7a626bdd73fa405f7839 (same path, blob dcc0dd3d78533e411b3983472d8b8680ee236231), the head the blind review (issue comment, 2026-07-26T01:18Z) targeted; it is not in the local clone but is fetchable with `gh api "repos/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/contents/us/policies/medicaid/magi_household_income_pipeline.yaml?ref=593e0f945a"`. I diffed that pre-fix version against 30e2327e4b:<path> to triage; a verifier item should be built from that pair, not from the commit diff alone. MULTI-DEFECT: the commit body names seven repairs spanning at least four kinds — wrong_entity_or_scope (per-member (d)(3)/(d)(2)(ii) application; reversed relation argument order, the review's headline B3, fixed by declaring a module-owned relation medicaid_household_member_of_applicant with household_member first), unrepresented_clause (missing mandatory (f)(5) fallback to (f)(3); final eligibility bypassing the paragraph-(c) router for (i)/(j)/(k) — the pre-fix module did not even cite /c, /i, /j, /k), wrong_period_or_effective_date (everything at period Year with Month-period public consumers, versus (h)(1)'s current-monthly requirement for applicants; post splits current-month and projected-annual surfaces), and polarity_or_logic (medicaid_magi_household_runtime_inputs_valid was defined but referenced nowhere in the pre-fix file, so invalid inputs still emitted affirmative results; post gates ~18 outputs on it). I chose wrong_entity_or_scope because the commit message leads with 'applicant scoping' and two of the seven repairs (scoping and relation order) are member-set defects, but unrepresented_clause is nearly as defensible — hence confidence 0.72. Provisions read through the pinned corpus (resolve_provision, us/regulation/42/435/603/c, /d, /f, /h; all resolved cleanly): (c) 'Except as specified in paragraph (i), (j), and (k)'; (d)(3) applicant scoping; (f)(5) mandatory fallback (the post file quotes it verbatim as a proof-atom excerpt); (h)(1) current-monthly requirement for applicants. The rewrite also adds scope the module never claimed (explicit State-election inputs, contract-validity rules, 435.119 age elections), so not every added line is a defect fix. Companion test file and tests/test_medicaid_magi_pipeline_contract.py changed alongside. Later commits in the same PR continue the repair: c3b9a2ea60 'Make Medicaid relation orientation executable', 455cfb4a8c 'Make Medicaid relation mutant expose sentinel', 3a3f3bf525 'Fail closed on Medicaid family size FPL mismatches', d15442b4fd 'Fail closed on contradictory Medicaid applicant ages'. Quote source note: the blind review lives in pr.issue_comments (a GitHub issue comment titled 'Blind review: REQUEST-CHANGES — 6 blocking'), not in the formal reviews array; I labeled it pr_review. Alternate verbatim quote from the commit message: 'Repair applicant scoping, household fallback, relation order, period algebra, exception routing, fail-closed validity, and explicit State elections.'

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this and could not: the pre-review module (recovered from the force-pushed PR head 593e0f945a, which is the blob the reviewer read at 2026-07-26T01:18Z) summed `sum_where(member_of_individuals_household, medicaid_magi_household_member_contribution, medicaid_household_member)` over an imported relation whose own declaration is `arguments: [individual, household_member]` (applicant-first), i.e. the opposite orientation from the member-first slot the compiled sum consumes, and its per-member contribution was `household_member_counted_magi_based_income + state_option_available_cash_support_included`, where the imported (d)(3) rule is gated on that *member's* `tax_dependent_described_in_paragraph_f_2_i`. The pinned corpus text (us/regulation/42/435/603/d, release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union) reads "(3) In the case of individuals described in paragraph (f)(2)(i) of this section, household income may, at State option, also include actually available cash support..." and "(ii) ...is not included in the household income of the taxpayer", so both clauses are scoped to a specific person (the applicant / the claiming taxpayer), not applied on every member row. The fix re-scopes exactly that: it declares its own relation `medicaid_household_member_of_applicant` with `arguments: [household_member, medicaid_applicant]`, adds cash support once at applicant level gated on `medicaid_applicant_is_described_in_paragraph_f_2_i`, and makes the (d)(2)(ii) exclusion applicant-relative via `household_row_applicant_expects_to_claim_candidate_as_tax_dependent`. That is an encoded-meaning correction about which person set/whose household a rule applies to — fidelity, wrong_entity_or_scope.

Paragraph (d)(2)(ii) is scoped to the claiming taxpayer's household,
while paragraph (d)(3) is scoped to the paragraph-(f)(2)(i)
applicant's household. Counted member MAGI is therefore summed
separately from applicant-level cash support.

Second caveat: this single commit repairs at least six review findings of different kinds — the reversed relation orientation and the (d)(2)(ii)/(d)(3) scoping (wrong_entity_or_scope), the missing mandatory (f)(5) fallback and the bypassed (c)/(i) exception router (unrepresented_clause), Month/Year budget-period mixing under (h) (wrong_period_or_effective_date), and diagnostic-only runtime validity that still emitted affirmative results (polarity_or_logic, fail-open). The chosen kind is correct for the quoted reason and the cited rule_path (`rules[medicaid_household_pre_disregard_magi].versions[0].formula`, which exists only in the pre-fix file), but this commit should probably be split into several corpus cases rather than carrying one label. Note also that "unrepresented_clause" does NOT fit the quoted finding: the (f)(2)(i) gate was present pre-fix, just evaluated on the wrong person.
