item.subject: Fix Head Start eligibility boundaries

triage.commit_summary: This is the repair round on PR #1010's Head Start / Early Head Start composition, answering the maintainer's blind-review REQUEST-CHANGES: it splits the single conflated paragraph-(b) age bridge into separate ordinary/Tribal and Migrant-or-Seasonal age rules, adds the statutory "pregnant woman or a child" subject predicate to the paragraph-(c), additional-allowance, and participation outputs, and re-grounds the (e) Tribal and (f) Migrant paths on explicit caller inputs (tribal program, approved service area, primary agricultural employment income) instead of the imported combined eligibility rules. It also adds a fail-closed domain contract (head_start_runtime_inputs_valid) gating every output on nonnegative income and age, a positive poverty line, and enrollment shares in [0,1], and expands the companion test file by ~306 lines.

modules.description_quote: the Head Start public age bridge is wrong for ordinary and dual program contexts; paragraph-(c)/participation outputs omit the statutory subject predicate; numeric runtime leaves fail OPEN with no domain contract
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The single public age bridge (participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b) was gated on `tribal_program or migrant_or_seasonal_program`, so it denied paragraph-(b) age satisfaction to ordinary Head Start participants and let one program's age test (e.g. the (b)(1)/(b)(2) branch) satisfy the other program's requirement in dual contexts, while the paragraph-(c) and participation outputs dropped the §1302.12(c)(1) subject predicate ("A pregnant woman or a child is eligible if") and so fired for persons who are neither a child nor a pregnant woman.
modules.triage_notes: Read the pinned provision (us/regulation/45/1302/12, corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union): (b) states age rules for Early Head Start, Head Start Preschool, and Migrant or Seasonal separately with no Tribal/Migrant gating on the ordinary case; (c)(1) reads "A pregnant woman or a child is eligible if"; (e) requires a Tribal program + approved service area + paragraph (b); (f) requires at least one family member with income primarily from agricultural employment + paragraph (b). Multi-defect repair in one module: (1) scope/contamination in the shared age bridge — pre-fix the local rule participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b also fed the imported us:regulations/45-cfr/1302/12#tribal_service_area_participant_eligible and #migrant_or_seasonal_participant_eligible, whose own formulas consume that same open name, so one bridge served both program scopes; the fix drops those two imports and composes (e)/(f) locally from three newly declared inputs (head_start_tribal_program, head_start_participant_in_approved_tribal_service_area, head_start_family_has_primary_agricultural_employment_income). (2) missing statutory subject predicate added to head_start_paragraph_c_path_satisfied, head_start_additional_allowance_path_satisfied, and head_start_participation_path_satisfied. (3) a secondary polarity_or_logic defect — fail-open numeric runtime leaves replaced by the fail-closed head_start_runtime_inputs_valid contract, now ANDed into every rule; if a reviewer prefers one kind per finding, this module supports both wrong_entity_or_scope (primary, 2 of 3 named findings) and polarity_or_logic (secondary). The quote is verbatim from MaxGhenis's blind-review comment on PR #1010, which the bundle stores under issue_comments rather than reviews (reviews/review_comments are empty); it is a review in substance. The commit body is empty, so all stated reasoning comes from that review. No effective dates, thresholds, or multipliers changed (all versions stay effective_from 2021-01-01); the 100%/130% logic is untouched. Note the public rule rename participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b -> head_start_ordinary_or_tribal_age_requirement_met, an interface-breaking rename bundled with the fidelity fix. Companion test file us/policies/hhs/head_start/eligibility_pipeline.test.yaml grew by 306 lines in the same commit. The review's top finding (WIC 185% federal maximum vs the operative State agency guideline) concerns a different module and is not in this commit.

verdict.justification: My refutation attempt fails on the core claim: the pre-fix module published a single `participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b` gated on `tribal_program ... or migrant_or_seasonal_program ...`, and the imported regulation rules `tribal_service_area_participant_eligible` (`tribal_program and participant_in_approved_service_area and participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b`) and `migrant_or_seasonal_participant_eligible` both bound that one contaminated predicate by name, so in a dual context one program's age test satisfied the other program's §1302.12(b) requirement — the companion test flips prove it (`-...participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b: holds` / `-...#migrant_or_seasonal_participant_eligible: holds` become `+...head_start_migrant_or_seasonal_age_requirement_met: not_holds` for a 2-year-old who fails (b)(3)), and in an ordinary (non-Tribal, non-MSHS) context the bridge returned false for a participant who does meet (b). Separately, §1302.12(c)(1) reads "A pregnant woman or a child is eligible if" (pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-24, body sha ec9bc785...), yet the pre-fix (c)/(d)/participation outputs were the bare imported family-level predicates, so they held for a person outside the statutory subject class; the fix adds `participant_is_child or participant_is_pregnant_woman` to exactly those outputs. Both corrections are about which program, which population, and which output surface the rule speaks for, so wrong_entity_or_scope fits better than polarity_or_logic (the OR is the mechanism, the scope conflation is the error) or unrepresented_clause (the added clause is a population restriction).
verdict.quote:
-  - name: participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b
+  - name: head_start_ordinary_or_tribal_age_requirement_met
[...]
-          paragraph_c_participant_eligible
+          head_start_runtime_inputs_valid
+          and (
+            participant_is_child
+            or participant_is_pregnant_woman
+          )
+          and paragraph_c_participant_eligible
verdict.notes: Three refutation angles I tested, two of which partly land and should temper the record. (1) The added `head_start_runtime_inputs_valid` fail-closed domain contract (`family_income >= 0`, `poverty_line_amount > 0`, shares in [0,1], `child_age_years >= 0`) has no basis in 45 CFR 1302.12 — the provision says nothing about negative income or a zero poverty line. That piece is defensive precision the module never claimed, i.e. not itself a fidelity defect, and it is the part of the reviewer's quote ("numeric runtime leaves fail OPEN with no domain contract") that would be polarity_or_logic if counted. It should not carry the kind; the age-bridge and subject-predicate defects do. (2) The new inputs `head_start_tribal_program` and `head_start_participant_in_approved_tribal_service_area` are NOT a missing-gate fix: the pre-fix import `us:regulations/45-cfr/1302/12#tribal_service_area_participant_eligible` already contained `tribal_program and participant_in_approved_service_area` (verified at parent fc95ef85, us/regulations/45-cfr/1302/12.yaml lines ~174-192). Those inputs are re-localization of the (e)/(f) conditions after the module stopped importing the two reg outputs, not new coverage. (3) The subject-predicate omission does not change the terminal answers: pre-fix `head_start_eligible` already required `participant_is_child` and `early_head_start_eligible` already required pregnant-or-child, so the (c)(1) subject fix corrects the published intermediate outputs (`head_start_paragraph_c_path_satisfied`, `head_start_additional_allowance_path_satisfied`, `head_start_participation_path_satisfied`) rather than eligibility results — an output-surface scope defect, still real, but narrower than "wrong eligibility answer". The dual-context contamination is the one piece that reaches a regulation-level eligibility output. Commit body is empty and the subject ("Fix Head Start eligibility boundaries") is generic; the evidence is the diff plus the PR #1010 issue comment. Files: /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us us/policies/hhs/head_start/eligibility_pipeline.yaml and .test.yaml at de7bc07dac vs fc95ef85; imported module us/regulations/45-cfr/1302/12.yaml (unchanged by this commit, so its own `tribal_service_area_participant_eligible` still references the now-removed bridge name — worth a follow-up check).

item.subject: Fix WIC State eligibility boundaries

triage.commit_summary: The commit repairs the WIC person-level eligibility pipeline (`us/policies/usda/wic/eligibility_pipeline.yaml`) after a blind review on PR #1010 found that it screened every applicant against a hard-coded 1.85 x Federal poverty guideline, although 7 CFR 246.7(d)(1) makes the State or local agency's own guideline (floor 100% FPG, ceiling the reduced-price-meal level) operative and treats 185% only as a Federal maximum. It deletes the `wic_income_limit_multiplier` parameter and derived `wic_income_limit` rule in favor of a caller-attested `wic_state_or_local_income_guideline` input, and in the same pass restores two omitted mandatory source clauses (the paragraph (d)(2)(ix) instream-migrant income-satisfaction route and the paragraph (e)(1)(v) presumptive pregnant-woman nutritional-risk window) plus a new fail-closed numeric domain contract.

modules.description_quote: WIC computes `1.85 × FPG` as every applicant's income limit, but 7 CFR 246.7(d)(1) makes the *State agency's* guideline operative (floor 100% FPG, ceiling the reduced-price-meal guideline); the 185% figure is a federal maximum.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module made `1.85 * wic_federal_poverty_guideline` the operative income limit for every applicant, grounding it on the 7 CFR 246.7(d)(2)(iii) sentence that merely caps eligibility at 185 percent, whereas 246.7(d)(1) delegates the operative guideline to the State or local agency (anywhere from 100 percent FPG up to the reduced-price-meal level), so an applicant above a State's lower guideline was wrongly reported income-eligible; the module also omitted the mandatory (d)(2)(ix) instream-migrant income-satisfaction route and the (e)(1)(v) presumptive pregnant-woman nutritional-risk window.
modules.triage_notes: Single module in the commit (plus its companion test file us/policies/usda/wic/eligibility_pipeline.test.yaml, not in this chunk). This is a repair commit on PR #1010 (merged 2026-07-26); the commit body is empty (a single newline), so the quote comes from the maintainer's 'Blind review: REQUEST-CHANGES' comment, which the bundle carries under issue_comments rather than reviews (quote_source recorded as pr_review). Three distinct fidelity corrections ride in one diff: (1) headline - the 1.85 parameter and derived wic_income_limit rule are deleted and the direct screen becomes `wic_family_income <= wic_state_or_local_income_guideline` against a positive caller-attested operative guideline; (2) the paragraph (d)(2)(ix) instream-migrant route is moved out of deferred_outputs into an import with a real sha256 and OR'd into wic_income_eligible (unrepresented_clause); (3) a new wic_nutritional_risk_eligibility_requirement_met rule adds the (e)(1)(v) presumptive pregnant-woman route gated on three fail-closed attestations (unrepresented_clause). A fourth change, the new wic_numeric_inputs_valid domain contract (`wic_family_income >= 0 and wic_state_or_local_income_guideline > 0`), closes a fail-open numeric leaf - runtime robustness rather than a clear source-fidelity defect on its own. Provisions were read through the pinned corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union (corpus commit 0fd35bfbda98): (d)(1) confirms the State-agency delegation with the 100% FPG floor and reduced-price-meal ceiling; the pre-fix proof-atom excerpt 'gross income in excess of 185 percent of the Federal income guidelines' sits in (d)(2)(iii) as a uniformity/ceiling sentence, not an operative-limit rule; (d)(2)(ix) says instream migrants 'shall be declared to satisfy the State agency's income standard'; (e)(1)(v) supplies the 60-day presumptive window matching the new proof excerpt. Kind call: wrong_entity_or_scope (Federal maximum standing in for the State agency's guideline) and amount_mismatch (the 1.85 threshold) are both defensible; I chose untraceable_branch because the fix removes the parameter and the derived limit rule outright and re-grounds the test on the operative guideline, which matches 'formulas grounded on the wrong provision'. Despite 'boundaries' in the subject, no comparison strictness changed - the direct screen stayed `<=` - so boundary_direction does not fit.

verdict.justification: The refutation attempt fails: the diff changes encoded meaning exactly as the review quote describes. Pre-fix, `wic_income_eligible` tested `wic_family_income <= wic_income_limit` where `wic_income_limit = wic_income_limit_multiplier * wic_federal_poverty_guideline` with the multiplier parameter `1.85` grounded on the proof excerpt "gross income in excess of 185 percent of the Federal income guidelines"; the fix deletes both the parameter and the derived limit rule and re-grounds the screen on a caller-supplied `wic_state_or_local_income_guideline`. Reading 7 CFR 246.7(d) through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union) confirms the mis-grounding: (d)(1) makes the State agency's prescribed guidelines operative (floor 100% of the HHS poverty guidelines, ceiling the reduced-price school meal guidelines), while the 185-percent sentence sits in (d)(2)(iii) as an assurance that the health-care-guideline option does not let households "in excess of 185 percent" qualify — a ceiling, not the operative threshold. That is a formula grounded on the wrong provision whose fix removes and re-grounds it, i.e. untraceable_branch; amount_mismatch fits worse because no corrected number replaces 1.85 (the parameter is deleted and the threshold delegated), and wrong_entity_or_scope fits worse because entity, period, and population are unchanged.
verdict.quote:
-          wic_income_limit_multiplier * wic_federal_poverty_guideline

item.subject: fix: require section 22 retirement permanence

triage.commit_summary: The commit adds a section 22(b)(2) at-retirement permanence gate to the elderly/disabled credit composition pipeline: whenever any under-65 taxpayer or spouse qualifies through the disability branch, the pipeline now imports `under_65_elderly_disabled_qualified_individual` and requires a new tax-unit attestation that every such individual was permanently and totally disabled when he retired, failing closed to zero otherwise. It was made because the upstream encoded section 22 module derives only annual impairment facts (22(e)(3) tests evaluated for the taxable year) and never establishes the statutory "when he retired, was permanently and totally disabled" condition, so the pipeline was publishing the credit for individuals the statute does not qualify; a new companion case proves the fail-closed behavior ($300 pre-fix vs 0 post-fix).

The commit also touched only the companion test (adds case eld-disabled-retirement-permanence-not-attested, which shows the upstream `elderly_disabled_credit` still returning '300' while the pipeline final goes to zero, plus expanding one anchor-merge into explicit inputs) and PROGRESS.md; no unrelated formula, parameter, version, or effective-date change. Commit body is empty, so the description quote is taken from the module summary text added in the diff; the PR body (#1004) independently names it: 'the disabled branch requires the at-retirement permanence attestation (§22(b)(2))'. Minor oddity, not a defect: the new import proof atom for `under_65_elderly_disabled_qualified_individual` carries the same sha256 b8f25c27... as the pre-existing `elderly_disabled_credit` import atom (looks like a module-level artifact hash). This file is a composition pipeline under us/policies, but it is a rulespec/v1 module with its own rule and formula, so it is triaged as a rule module.

The pinned corpus text of 26 USC 22(b)(2) reads "who retired on disability before the close of the taxable year and who, when he retired, was permanently and totally disabled," while the imported §22 module computes retired_on_permanent_total_disability as retired_on_disability_before_year_end and permanently_totally_disabled, both Year-period impairment facts — so the at-retirement permanence clause was absent and the pre-fix pipeline published the credit to under-65 individuals §22 does not qualify. The pre-fix summary still claimed "Every expected value is the statutory section 22 credit before section 26 applies," so this is a correction of encoded meaning, not optional new scope. item.subject: fix: defer section 22 payment adjustment

triage.commit_summary: The commit changed the IRC 22 elderly/disabled credit composition pipeline from a bare identity over the imported encoded final (`formula: elderly_disabled_credit`) to a guarded formula that publishes the credit only when the section 104(a)(4) payment relation is empty and otherwise returns zero, adding a proof atom quoting section 22(c)(3)(A)'s sentence "No reduction shall be made under clause (i)(III) for any amount described in section 104(a)(4)." It did so because the imported us/statutes/26/22 module subtracts section 104(a)(4) service-injury payments from its combined nontaxable-benefit reduction, whereas the statute limits that no-reduction exception to the clause (i)(III) veterans-benefit bucket alone, so the pipeline was publishing overstated credits for any unit with such payments.

modules.description_quote: The section 104(a)(4) exception applies only to the veterans-benefit bucket in section 22(c)(3)(A)(i)(III), while the imported module applies related payments against its combined benefit reduction.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pipeline published the imported section 22 credit unconditionally, so it never represented section 22(c)(3)(A)'s limitation that the section 104(a)(4) no-reduction exception applies only under clause (i)(III) (Department of Veterans Affairs benefits), and it therefore published credits computed with that exception netted against the entire combined benefit reduction.
modules.triage_notes: Single module in the commit; the only other changes are the companion test file and PROGRESS.md. Read the statute through the pinned corpus release (resolve_provision.py, us/statute/26/22): section 22(c)(3)(A) ends "No reduction shall be made under clause (i)(III) for any amount described in section 104(a)(4)." Verified the upstream defect by reading us/statutes/26/22.yaml at this commit: rule section_22_service_injury_payment_exclusion = sum(section_22_payment_of_tax_unit.service_injury_pension_excluded_amount), and section_22_nontaxable_pension_benefit_reduction subtracts it from the sum of ALL buckets (title II + RRA + VA + other + workers' comp), not just the VA bucket. The companion case added here is a concrete counterexample: $5,000 title II benefits, $0 VA benefits, and a $5,000 Foreign Service Act section 808 annuity produce $750 from the imported final where the statute gives $0. Diff is consistent with the commit subject and with the PR body line "104(a)(4) payment relation must be empty (over-application defect #1054)". Two caveats a reviewer should weigh. (1) The real over-application lives in the imported us/statutes/26/22 module, which this commit does NOT fix (git log shows that file was only ever moved afterward, in 86ec136fd); this pipeline defers/fails closed pending an "upstream bucket-specific correction", so a fidelity judge would have to follow the import to see the defect from the pre-fix pipeline alone. (2) Fail-closed-to-zero is the statutory answer in the added test case but is not the statutory answer generally: when VA benefits are nonzero the exception legitimately applies and the post-fix pipeline now under-credits, so the fix removes a wrong published number rather than encoding the correct bucket allocation. Kind is the main uncertainty: unrepresented_clause (the clause-(i)(III) limitation the source states was missing, and the fix adds a condition for it with a proof atom quoting exactly that sentence) versus wrong_entity_or_scope (the exception was applied to the wrong reduction bucket) versus polarity_or_logic (pre-fix fail-open, post-fix fail-closed). I chose unrepresented_clause because the pre-fix formula contained no boolean logic at all and the fix adds a source-grounded condition. Follow-up commit 58a81fbd0 "fix: require section 22 retirement permanence" touches the same pipeline for a different defect.

verdict.justification: The diff changes encoded meaning: the version formula goes from the bare identity `elderly_disabled_credit` to a conditional that publishes the imported credit only when the section 104(a)(4) payment relation is empty, and a new proof atom of `kind: condition` is grounded on the exact clause that was previously unrepresented ("No reduction shall be made under clause (i)(III) for any amount described in section 104(a)(4)."). The pinned corpus text of 26 USC 22(c)(3)(A) confirms that limiting sentence attaches only to clause (i)(III) (Department of Veterans Affairs benefits), and the companion case added in the same commit demonstrates the pre-fix module published $750 for a single aged-66 unit whose entire $5,000 reduction was title II social security while a $5,000 Foreign Service section 808 annuity wrongly cancelled it — the statutory section 22 amount there is $5,000 - $5,000 = $0, so the pre-fix surface disagreed with the source it cites. I tried to refute this as either an upstream-only defect or mere new coverage, but the pre-fix summary claimed the caller supplies "any section 104(a)(4) payment facts" and that "Every expected value is the statutory section 22 credit", so this module did claim the population it was getting wrong.

-        formula: elderly_disabled_credit
+        formula: |-
+          if len(section_22_payment_of_tax_unit) == 0:
+              elderly_disabled_credit
+          else:
+              0
verdict.notes: Strongest remaining objection for a reviewer, and the reason I stopped at 0.72 rather than higher: the fix does not actually represent the (i)(III) limitation — it defers it. The module comment says "Pending an upstream bucket-specific correction, this pipeline therefore fails closed to zero whenever `section_22_payment_of_tax_unit` is nonempty", and the commit subject is "fix: defer section 22 payment adjustment". Post-fix the module is still unfaithful for a unit that has both VA benefits under (i)(III) and a section 104(a)(4) payment: the statute allows a nonzero credit there, the pipeline now returns 0. So the remedy is a scope narrowing (publish only where the import is faithful), which is why a reviewer could argue for wrong_entity_or_scope instead. I kept unrepresented_clause because defect kinds should describe the defect, not the remedy style: the defect is the missing source-stated limitation on the no-reduction exception, and the repo itself grounds the added condition on that clause via the new `kind: condition` proof atom. Corroborating evidence outside the module diff (test file, not quotable as module-diff text): the new case eld-nonempty-section-104-payment-relation-fails-closed asserts `us:statutes/26/22#elderly_disabled_credit: '750'` alongside `...#federal_elderly_disabled_credit: '0'`, i.e. the import is known-wrong and the pipeline suppresses it. PR #1004 labels the root cause "over-application defect #1054" in the imported statute module; the import hash (sha256:b8f25c27...) is unchanged in this commit, so the correction is purely at the pipeline's published surface. Not mechanical (formula changed), not test_only, not not_a_defect.

item.subject: fix: source 2026 QBID policy values

triage.commit_summary: The commit stops the 2026 QBID pipeline from taking its statutory policy amounts from callers: the Rev. Proc. 2025-32 threshold moves from a runtime input (`qualified_business_income_threshold_amount_2026`) to an import of the encoded Rev. Proc. 2025-32 qualified-business-income module, and the §199A(i) minimum-deduction machinery moves from the statute's COLA-adjusted rules (driven by a caller-supplied `minimum_deduction_cost_of_living_adjustment`) to the unadjusted statutory bases `$1,000`/`$400`, with a new local applicability rule and effective-period proof atoms citing the "beginning after 2026" indexation clause. Companion fixtures were rewired to the new inputs but every expected output value is unchanged, so the change corrects how the 2026 amounts are grounded (and closes a fail-open COLA path inside the module's 2026-only window) rather than any computed number for a correctly-supplied caller.

modules.description_quote: The filing-status input selects the imported 2026 threshold; callers do not supply a policy amount.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Inside its declared tax-year-2026 window the pre-fix pipeline left the section 199A policy amounts caller-determined - the Rev. Proc. 2025-32 threshold as a free runtime input and the section 199A(i) $1,000/$400 minimums as the statute's COLA-scaled rules keyed to a caller-supplied `minimum_deduction_cost_of_living_adjustment` - although 199A(i)(3) allows that increase only "In the case of any taxable year beginning after 2026" and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.26 fixes the 2026 thresholds.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read: resolve_provision on us/statute/26/199A returned 199A(i) in full - (i)(1)(B) "$400", (i)(2)(A) "is at least $1,000", and (i)(3) "In the case of any taxable year beginning after 2026, the $400 amount in paragraph (1)(B) and the $1,000 amount in paragraph (2)(A) shall each be increased". Two distinct halves in one commit. (a) COLA half (durable): parent 26/199A.yaml exposes `active_qbi_minimum_threshold` and `minimum_active_qbi_deduction_amount` as base + floor(base*minimum_deduction_cost_of_living_adjustment/5 + 0.5)*5 with effective_from 2026-01-01 and no effective_to, so the pre-fix 2026 pipeline would silently return non-statutory 2026 minimums for any nonzero COLA input; the fix imports `active_qbi_minimum_threshold_base`/`minimum_active_qbi_deduction_base`, adds local rule `pipeline_applicable_taxpayer_for_minimum_active_qbi_deduction` (aggregate active QBI >= 1000), drops the COLA input, and adds `versions[0].effective_to` proof atoms quoting the after-2026 clause. This half survives unchanged on main (verified in main:...pipeline.yaml lines 98-99, 419-504). (b) Threshold half (transient): the import target `us:policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/qualified-business-income#qualified_business_income_threshold_amount` does not exist in the rev-proc module as of this commit - that file has only the nine per-category rules (`qualified_business_income_threshold_joint|separate|all_other`, range ends, widths); PROGRESS.md in this same commit says it was validated "In a temporary integration worktree containing cached `origin/fed-parity/revproc`". Same-day follow-up 652125375 ("fix: validate QBID threshold return category") reverts this import back to `qualified_business_income_threshold_amount_2026` plus a return-category attestation, and 7f2603e88 ("fix: import 2026 QBID threshold parameters") then imports the nine real parameters with a local filing-status selector, renamed by db9533dad. So if the corpus entry is keyed on the threshold half it captures a reverted intermediate state; keying on the COLA/effective-period half is safer. Alternative readings a reviewer may prefer: untraceable_branch (ungrounded caller-supplied policy values re-grounded on encoded sources) for the threshold half; or a mechanical/provenance reading, since no fixture expected output changed (the .test.yaml diff only rewires inputs: drops the threshold and COLA inputs, moves filing_status from the 199A namespace to the pipeline namespace) and the pre-fix module explicitly documented the threshold as a runtime input ("RuleSpec imports cannot substitute the official 2026 amount"), i.e. it never claimed to encode it. Commit body is empty; commit subject is "fix: source 2026 QBID policy values"; PROGRESS.md in the same commit states verbatim: "Replaced the QBID threshold runtime input with the PR #1009 Rev. Proc. module import and replaced the caller-supplied COLA with the unadjusted statutory $1,000/$400 bases for 2026." PR #1004 (no reviews or review comments captured) describes the head state, not this commit, and records the related review finding as "the 9th (threshold provenance) by the #1009 import at this head". The commit also reworded the module summary, source_verification rationale, and a waiver `reason`/`source_values` entry (metadata only). Note both new import proof atoms reuse hash sha256:caa63943...b816 for two different targets, which looks like a stale/duplicated hash but is outside fidelity scope.

verdict.justification: The diff changes no effective_from, effective_to, version window or period kind anywhere: every rule keeps '2026-01-01'/'2026-12-31' before and after, and the only period-flavored edits are two newly ADDED `kind: effective_period` proof atoms (metadata/provenance), plus the window on a brand-new rule that copies the module's existing 2026 window. What actually changed in meaning is grounding: the threshold formula stops reading a free caller input and reads an imported Rev. Proc. 2025-32 value, and the 199A(i) minimum stops flowing through the statute's COLA-escalated rules (base x caller-supplied `minimum_deduction_cost_of_living_adjustment`) and reads the unadjusted $400/$1,000 bases, with the caller COLA input deleted. Since 199A(i)(3) reads "In the case of any taxable year beginning after 2026, the $400 amount in paragraph (1)(B) and the $1,000 amount in paragraph (2)(A) shall each be increased" (verified through the pinned release), the pre-fix pipeline computed a 2026 result through a provision that does not apply to 2026 and left a source-fixed threshold caller-determined — a value/formula grounded on the wrong provision or on nothing, which the fix re-grounds. That is untraceable_branch, not wrong_period_or_effective_date; the first reader's quote (a summary sentence about filing-status selection of an imported threshold) carries no period content at all.

item.subject: fix: fail closed outside single QBID group

triage.commit_summary: The commit adds a required attestation input to the 2026 QBID pipeline and makes the final deduction rule fail closed to zero unless the caller attests that the supplied scalar QBI, W-2 wage, UBIA, and cooperative amounts constitute the taxpayer's only qualified-trade-or-business aggregation group, because the scalar leg cannot perform the 26 USC 199A(b)(1)(A) sum of per-business paragraph-(2) amounts. It also extracts the existing $75,000/$150,000 phase-in widths into two named parameter rules with Rev. Proc. 2025-32 / 199A(b)(3)(B) proof atoms (values unchanged) and adds a false-attestation companion case plus a PROGRESS.md note.

modules.description_quote: single-aggregation-group attestation fails closed (multi-business summation is upstream)
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix final rule returned the single-scalar trade-or-business result as the taxpayer's section 199A deduction for every non-corporate filer, failing open when the taxpayer carried another qualified trade or business, even though 199A(b)(1)(A) defines the combined amount as the sum of the paragraph-(2) amounts determined separately for each qualified trade or business.
modules.triage_notes: Provision was read through the pinned corpus release (us/statute/26/199A): 199A(b)(1)(A) reads 'the sum of the amounts determined under paragraph (2) for each qualified trade or business carried on by the taxpayer', and (b)(2) applies the 50%-of-W-2 / 25%+2.5%-UBIA limit per business, so a scalar single-business computation is not the statutory combined amount when another qualified business exists; the added proof-atom excerpt matches the corpus text verbatim. Decisive change is the guard on the final formula: pre-fix 'if taxpayer_is_corporation: 0' became 'if (taxpayer_is_corporation or not supplied_amounts_are_for_taxpayers_only_qualified_trade_or_business): 0', with a new required Boolean TaxUnit input and a new companion case 'qbid-multiple-business-boundary-fails-closed' proving the scalar leg still yields 20000 while the final yields 0. Kind chosen as polarity_or_logic because the task's kind list places fail-open vs fail-closed there and the commit subject is 'fix: fail closed outside single QBID group'; a defensible alternative is unrepresented_clause, since the unrepresented item is the (b)(1)(A) per-business sum, but the fix guards against that gap rather than implementing the sum (the PR says multi-business summation stays upstream). Second, non-decisive part of the same diff is mechanical/provenance: the pipeline_qbi_phasein_range match arms swap the literals 75000/150000 for two new parameter rules pipeline_qbi_phasein_range_other/_joint holding the identical values with Rev. Proc. 2025-32 page-22 and 199A(b)(3)(B) proof atoms; no value, scope, entity, or effective-date change (both new params are effective_from 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, matching the rest of the module). Commit body is empty (just a newline), so the quote comes from the body of merged PR #1004, which covers a larger multi-surface composition; this commit is one incremental commit in that PR, and the PR has no reviews or review comments in the bundle. The module summary added in this diff also states the reason verbatim: 'Because the scalar trade-or-business leg cannot perform the paragraph-(2) sum across nonaggregable businesses, the final output requires an attestation that the supplied amounts form the taxpayer's only qualified-trade-or-business aggregation group and that no other qualified business exists.' PROGRESS.md pre-fix listed 'Implement the remaining QBID one-group contract' as an open Next item, i.e. this was a known, tracked gap rather than an incidental hardening. Only this one module file changed; the other touched files are the companion test and PROGRESS.md.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as an added-precision guard and could not: pre-fix, `federal_qualified_business_income_deduction` zeroed only for corporations and otherwise returned the single-scalar trade-or-business leg as the taxpayer's whole deduction, while the pinned corpus text of 199A(b)(1)(A) reads "the sum of the amounts determined under paragraph (2) for each qualified trade or business carried on by the taxpayer" — so for a multi-business filer the encoding computed an unsound number instead of declining, a fail-open branch, and the commit subject is literally "fail closed outside single QBID group". The fix changes encoded meaning, not documentation: it adds a required Boolean input and disjoins `or not supplied_amounts_are_for_taxpayers_only_qualified_trade_or_business` into the zero branch, and the new companion case `qbid-multiple-business-boundary-fails-closed` pins `pipeline_qbi_deduction_before_minimum_active_qbi: '20000'` against `federal_qualified_business_income_deduction: '0'`, proving the branch flip. The taxonomy names "fail-open vs fail-closed" and "default value" under polarity_or_logic, and entity, period, output surface, and every parameter value are unchanged, so that kind fits better than wrong_entity_or_scope; unrepresented_clause does not fit because the fix deliberately does not add the paragraph-(2) summation ("multi-business summation is upstream").

+          if (
+              taxpayer_is_corporation
+              or not supplied_amounts_are_for_taxpayers_only_qualified_trade_or_business
+          ):

verdict.notes: Scope of the meaning change: only rules[federal_qualified_business_income_deduction].versions[0].formula plus its new required input changes behavior. The other rules in the reader's rule_names list (pipeline_qbi_phasein_range, ..._other, ..._joint) are a value-preserving refactor — the literals 75000/150000 in the filing-status match are replaced by two new parameter rules holding exactly 75000 and 150000, so that part is mechanical and should not be counted as a second defect. The strongest competing kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (the pre-fix rule answered for a broader population than its scalar inputs can support); I rejected it because nothing about entity, filing status, period, or output surface changed and the defect and fix are both boolean. A reviewer could also argue not_a_defect on the ground that the pre-fix input descriptions already said "the represented qualified trade or business" — but that assumption was unenforced and the final output was described as the "final tax-unit deduction", so the module did claim an answer for filers it could not correctly answer for. Grounding check: the added proof atom's excerpt "the sum of the amounts determined under paragraph (2) for each qualified trade or business carried on by the taxpayer" matches the pinned corpus text verbatim (release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, provision record 09e89e17-8e86-5caa-b36d-2de501af862d), so the guard is source-grounded rather than a bare policy choice. Caveat worth recording: returning 0 on a false attestation is itself not the statutory answer; the real safety comes from the input being required, so omission makes the output unevaluable.

item.subject: fix: key QBID phase-in width to return status

triage.commit_summary: The commit stops the QBID composition pipeline from importing the encoded statute module's `qbi_phasein_range` rule and replaces it with a locally proofed `pipeline_qbi_phasein_range` rule that maps all five filing-status codes explicitly, giving the $150,000 phase-in width only to joint returns (status 1) and $75,000 to everything else including surviving-spouse returns (status 4). The upstream rule had extended the joint width to surviving spouses via `filing_status == 1 or filing_status == 4`, which 26 USC 199A(b)(3)(B) ("$75,000 ($150,000 in the case of a joint return)") and the Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.26 three-row table do not support; a companion counterexample at the $276,750 "All Other Returns" band top was added with the fix.

modules.description_quote: local width mapping ($150k joint / $75k otherwise incl. surviving spouse — upstream width defect #1053)
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pipeline consumed the imported statute rule `qbi_phasein_range`, whose formula `if filing_status == 1 or filing_status == 4: qbi_phasein_range_joint else: qbi_phasein_range_other` handed surviving-spouse returns (status 4) the $150,000 joint phase-in width, but 26 USC 199A(b)(3)(B) allows the $150,000 width only "in the case of a joint return" and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.26 places surviving-spouse returns in the "All Other Returns" band ($201,750 threshold / $276,750 top = a $75,000 width).
modules.triage_notes: Single rule-module commit; the only behavioral change is filing_status 4 (150000 -> 75000). Statuses 0, 2 and 3 already resolved to 75000 under the imported rule and status 1 stays at 150000, so the new five-arm match is meaning-changing for exactly one status. The commit also drops the `us:statutes/26/199A#qbi_phasein_range` import line and its two import proof atoms (in pipeline_trade_or_business_phasein_reduction and pipeline_trade_or_business_deductible_amount) and repoints both formulas to the local rule — bookkeeping consequent to the fix, not separate changes. The commit message body is empty; the quote comes from the composing PR #1004 body, which names it "upstream width defect #1053". The companion test file (not a module, so not quotable here) adds case `qbid-surviving-spouse-uses-all-other-width` with the comment "Status 4 is a surviving-spouse return, not a joint return" and asserts pipeline_qbi_phasein_range = 75000 at taxable income $276,750; PROGRESS.md records "Replaced the imported `{1,4}` QBID width selector with a local five-status rule". I read the provision through the pinned corpus release (us/statute/26/199A resolved cleanly): the text says "threshold amount plus $75,000 ($150,000 in the case of a joint return)" at (b)(3)(B)(i)(I), (b)(3)(B)(ii)(II) and (d)(3), with no surviving-spouse extension; (e)(2) likewise doubles the threshold only "in the case of a joint return". The upstream statute module us/statutes/26/199A.yaml still carries `if filing_status == 1 or filing_status == 4` at repo HEAD, so this fix is a local override in the pipeline rather than an upstream repair — a reviewer may want the sibling upstream commit if one ever lands. Kind could alternatively be read as amount_mismatch (150000 where 75000 belongs), but the taxonomy lists filing status under wrong_entity_or_scope and the fix is precisely a re-keying of which return statuses fall in which branch.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this and could not: the diff drops the import `us:statutes/26/199A#qbi_phasein_range`, whose formula at the parent commit (598e55889e, us/statutes/26/199A.yaml line 288) reads `if filing_status == 1 or filing_status == 4: qbi_phasein_range_joint else: qbi_phasein_range_other`, and replaces it with a local rule that gives filing_status 4 the $75,000 width — the only substantive value change (0/2/3 keep $75,000, 1 keeps $150,000), so the change is about which filing-status population gets the joint width, not about a number being wrong. Read through the pinned release, 26 USC 199A grants $150,000 only "in the case of a joint return" and never mentions surviving spouses, section 2(a), 6013 or 7703 anywhere in its text, and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.26 has exactly three bands ("Married Individuals Filing Joint Returns $403,500 $553,500 ... All Other Returns $201,750 $276,750", a $75,000 width), so a surviving-spouse return had no source basis for the joint width. The module's own input description ("0 single/other, 1 joint, 2 married filing separately, 3 head of household, 4 surviving spouse", threshold "$201,750 otherwise") shows the pipeline already claimed status-4 coverage and was internally inconsistent pre-fix, which rules out "new coverage the module never claimed" and rules out mechanical, since a formula's value changed for a real population.
verdict.notes: Corroboration beyond the module diff: commit subject "fix: key QBID phase-in width to return status", and the companion case added in the same commit, whose comment reads "Status 4 is a surviving-spouse return, not a joint return." (test file, asserting pipeline_qbi_phasein_range: '75000' at the $276,750 all-other band top). Competing kind considered and rejected: untraceable_branch (the `or filing_status == 4` disjunct has no basis in the cited text) is defensible, but the branch it re-grounds lives in the upstream statute module, not in this diff, and "filing status" is named explicitly in wrong_entity_or_scope, so that kind is the more specific fit. amount_mismatch does not fit: both $75,000 and $150,000 are correct source amounts; only the population assignment was wrong. item.subject: fix: exclude corporations from final QBID

triage.commit_summary: The commit wraps the final QBID pipeline output (`federal_qualified_business_income_deduction`) in a `if taxpayer_is_corporation: 0` guard, adds a proof atom quoting 26 USC 199A(a)'s "In the case of a taxpayer other than a corporation" clause, and adds a companion test case (`qbid-corporation-cannot-receive-active-minimum`) proving a corporation gets $0. modules.description_quote: exclude corporations from final QBID
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The final rule took max(pipeline_qbi_deduction_before_minimum_active_qbi, minimum_active_qbi_deduction_amount) whenever the taxpayer was an applicable taxpayer under 199A(i), so a corporation with at least $1,000 of active QBI still received the $400 floor even though 199A(a) allows the deduction only "In the case of a taxpayer other than a corporation" (the corporation guard existed only on the intermediate pre-minimum rule).
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release: 199A(a) reads "In the case of a taxpayer other than a corporation, except as provided in subsection (i), there shall be allowed as a deduction...", and 199A(i)(1) only re-sizes "the deduction allowed under subsection (a)" to the greater of that amount or $400 for an applicable taxpayer (aggregate active QBI >= $1,000) -- so a corporation, which gets no subsection (a) deduction at all, cannot receive the floor. Pre-fix file line 266 shows the corporation guard present on pipeline_qbi_deduction_before_minimum_active_qbi but absent from the final rule, and the companion test added in this same commit (qbid-corporation-cannot-receive-active-minimum, taxpayer_is_corporation: true, aggregate active QBI 1000) asserts final = '0' with before_minimum = '0', which is exactly the value that would have been $400 pre-fix. taxpayer_is_corporation was already a declared Boolean input pre-fix (no input/scope additions). Kind ambiguity worth a reviewer's eye: this is equally describable as unrepresented_clause (the 199A(a) "other than a corporation" carve-out missing from the final rule); I chose wrong_entity_or_scope because the commit subject and PR body frame it as an entity exclusion on the module's output surface ("corporation guard on the final (§199A(a))"). One quirk: the new condition proof atom with excerpt "In the case of a taxpayer other than a corporation" was inserted into the atoms block of pipeline_trade_or_business_phasein_reduction (post lines 112-117), not into federal_qualified_business_income_deduction whose formula actually gained the guard; a later commit 598e55889 "fix: attach corporation proof to final QBID" moved it, so that follow-up is provenance-only (mechanical). No unrelated formula, parameter, version, or effective-date changes in this diff; PROGRESS.md was the only other file. PR #1004 has no reviews or review comments; its body covers the whole composition campaign, not just this commit.

verdict.justification: The diff changes the final output rule's formula, wrapping it in `if taxpayer_is_corporation: 0`, so this is an encoded-meaning change, not bookkeeping. The pre-fix path was genuinely reachable and wrong: the imported gate `applicable_taxpayer_for_minimum_active_qbi_deduction` is defined in us/statutes/26/199A.yaml purely as `aggregate_qualified_business_income_from_active_qualified_trades_or_businesses >= active_qbi_minimum_threshold` with no corporation test, so a corporation with $1,000 of active QBI took `max(0, $400) = $400` even though the pinned corpus text of 199A(a) reads "In the case of a taxpayer other than a corporation ... there shall be allowed as a deduction", and 199A(i)(1) only re-sizes "the deduction allowed under subsection (a)". The module already declared the input `taxpayer_is_corporation` ("whether the taxpayer is a corporation and therefore outside section 199A(a)") and already guarded the intermediate `pipeline_qbi_deduction_before_minimum_active_qbi`, so the final rule contradicted the module's own claimed scope rather than adding coverage it never claimed. The added companion fixture `qbid-corporation-cannot-receive-active-minimum` pins the $400 → $0 behavior change, and the defect is an entity-class scope error (the deduction reaching corporations), which fits wrong_entity_or_scope.

+          if taxpayer_is_corporation:
+              0

-              pipeline_qbi_deduction_before_minimum_active_qbi
+              if applicable_taxpayer_for_minimum_active_qbi_deduction:
verdict.notes: Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "the guard was already upstream" — false at the final rule; the corporation guard sat only on pipeline_qbi_deduction_before_minimum_active_qbi, and the 199A(i) floor branch bypassed it entirely. (2) "the imported applicable-taxpayer gate already excludes corporations" — false; us/statutes/26/199A.yaml line ~589 defines it solely as active QBI >= threshold. (3) "new coverage, not a defect" — false; `taxpayer_is_corporation` is an existing declared input and the rule's own `source:` says "26 USC 199A(a), (i)". (4) "mechanical" — false; the versions[0].formula body changed. Residual textual ambiguity, the only real counterargument: 199A(a) says "except as provided in subsection (i)", which a hostile reader could stretch to let (i) override the corporation exclusion; the natural reading is that (i) modifies only the lesser-of amount, since (i)(1) speaks of "the deduction allowed under subsection (a)" and no such deduction is allowed to a corporation. Alternate kind worth a reviewer's eye: unrepresented_clause also fits mechanically (the fix adds a source-stated carve-out), but the carve-out is an entity-class limitation, so wrong_entity_or_scope is the more specific label. Separate minor issue in the same commit, not affecting this verdict: the new proof atom with excerpt "In the case of a taxpayer other than a corporation" was inserted into the atoms list of `pipeline_trade_or_business_phasein_reduction` (diff hunk at pre-line 100-111), not into `federal_qualified_business_income_deduction`, whose atoms are unchanged in the post file — a misplaced provenance atom for the very guard being added.

item.subject: fix: fail close additional Medicare SE leg

triage.commit_summary: The commit withdraws the locally authored section 1401(b)(2)(B) wage-coordination and self-employment legs of the federal Additional Medicare Tax pipeline, restricting the self-employment domain judgment to tax units with zero imported self-employment income so the coordination helper, the public SE leg, and the combined output fail closed to zero, while the imported section 3101(b)(2) wage leg stays observable. The stated reason is that the pinned corpus record for section 1401(b)(2)(B) carries the enacted scrivener's cross-reference to section 3121(b)(2) rather than 3101(b)(2), so the excerpt the pre-fix proof atoms quoted does not exist in the cited provision and the coordination arithmetic is unsupported until the axiom-corpus#514 re-ingest is pinned.

modules.description_quote: The lawful coordination sentence is absent from the current corpus pin: the record names section 3121(b)(2), not section 3101(b)(2).
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module reduced the section 1401(b)(2)(A) filing-status threshold by tax-unit wages and published a positive self-employment Additional Medicare tax on the strength of a §1401(b)(2)(B) proof excerpt that the cited corpus record does not contain — the pinned record's coordination sentence names "the tax imposed under section 3121(b)(2)" and omits the "(as defined in section 3121(a))" clause — so the wage-coordination formula (and the SE leg built on it) had no basis in the cited provision.
modules.triage_notes: Provision was read through the pinned release: us/statute/26/1401 resolves to "The amounts under clause (i), (ii), or (iii) (whichever is applicable) of subparagraph (A) shall be reduced (but not below zero) by the amount of wages taken into account in determining the tax imposed under section 3121(b)(2) with respect to the taxpayer." — confirming the pre-fix excerpt in rules[wages_taken_into_account_for_additional_medicare_tax] and rules[pipeline_reduced_additional_medicare_self_employment_threshold] was a non-verbatim, substituted quotation (3101(b)(2) for 3121(b)(2)). Two decisive formula changes: the domain Judgment gains "and federal_self_employment_income == 0", and wages_taken_into_account_for_additional_medicare_tax goes from bare `wages` to a guarded conditional returning 0 outside that domain; federal_additional_medicare_self_employment_tax itself changed only its `source:` string because its fail-closed guard already keyed off the Judgment. Competing kind: the subject line "fail close additional Medicare SE leg" supports reading this as polarity_or_logic (fail-open vs fail-closed default); I chose untraceable_branch because the stated reason in the module comment, the deferred-output reasons, and the PR body all locate the defect in a formula grounded on source text the cited record does not contain, which the fix removes rather than re-polarizes. A third, weaker reading is mechanical/provenance (the pre-fix arithmetic matches Form 8959 / 26 CFR 1.1401-1(d)(2) as administered), but this is not excerpt-only: formulas, version windows, and published values all changed, so it is not mechanical. Collateral changes in the same diff: two rules' version windows narrowed from open-ended effective_from '2013-01-01' to '2026-01-01'..'2026-12-31'; two proof atoms swapped from kind: formula (excerpt) to kind: import (one with hash sha256:local); two new deferred_outputs entries added; module summary/rationale rewritten. PR body (#1003) quote for the same defect: "the pinned §1401 record faithfully carries the enacted scrivener's error (cross-reference printed as 3121(b)(2); Treasury administers as 3101(b)(2) per 26 CFR 1.1401-1(d)(2) and Form 8959 — see TD 9645)". PR had no reviews or review comments attached. Companion test us/policies/income_tax/additional_medicare_tax_pipeline.test.yaml changed alongside (fail-closed fixtures). Follow-ups on this module after the corpus repair: a0a2ec594 "feat: restore additional Medicare self-employment tax" and a374b52a1 "fix: keep Medicare coordination proof regulatory" — a reviewer may prefer the restore commit as the positive-direction benchmark item.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical (the diff's bulk is proof-atom excerpt→import swaps, comments, summaries, and deferral entries) and as not_a_defect (the pre-fix arithmetic matches how Treasury administers the Additional Medicare Tax), but both fail: the diff changes executable meaning — the domain Judgment gains `and federal_self_employment_income == 0`, the wage-coordination helper drops `formula: wages` for a conditional zero, and the published SE and combined outputs therefore go from a positive §1401(b)(2) tax to zero for any tax unit with self-employment income. Resolving the citation through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, record sha256 38a25e0d…) shows the cited record's subparagraph (B) reads "by the amount of wages taken into account in determining the tax imposed under section 3121(b)(2) with respect to the taxpayer" — so the pre-fix proof excerpt (which inserted "(as defined in section 3121(a))" and "imposed by section 3101(b)(2)") is not verbatim in the source, and the wage-reduction formula plus the SE leg built on it rested on a provision the cited record does not contain. That is untraceable_branch on its stated definition ("formulas grounded on the wrong provision"; the fix removes or re-grounds them), not merely an excerpt/citation-string correction. The nearest competing kind is polarity_or_logic, since the subject line is "fail close additional Medicare SE leg" and the rubric lists fail-open vs fail-closed there, but fail-closing is the remedy here, not the defect — the pre-fix guard was correctly polarized for §1401(c) and only the missing grounding forced the new condition.

-            kind: formula
-            source:
-              corpus_citation_path: us/statute/26/1401
-              excerpt: "The amounts under clause (i), (ii), or (iii) (whichever is applicable) of subparagraph (A) shall be reduced (but not below zero) by the amount of wages (as defined in section 3121(a)) taken into account in determining the tax imposed by section 3101(b)(2) with respect to the taxpayer."
     versions:
-      - effective_from: '2013-01-01'
-        formula: wages
verdict.notes:
Source verification (decisive): resolve_provision for us/statute/26/1401 at rulespec commit 08e2874132 returns corpus_release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, record_id 28922e55-97ac-5e80-82dd-759fcf156217, resolved_text_sha256 38a25e0db79501f48205f05a735ee97cd663d622044f1de9747d015482dd2e65, fix_time_corpus_match "same_body". Its (B) reads verbatim: "(B) Coordination with FICA The amounts under clause (i), (ii), or (iii) (whichever is applicable) of subparagraph (A) shall be reduced (but not below zero) by the amount of wages taken into account in determining the tax imposed under section 3121(b)(2) with respect to the taxpayer." Two divergences from the pre-fix excerpt: the record has no "(as defined in section 3121(a))" clause, and it says "imposed under section 3121(b)(2)" not "imposed by section 3101(b)(2)". So the pre-fix proof atom quoted text that is not in the cited record.

Meaning changes in the diff (why mechanical is refuted): (1) additional_medicare_tax_pipeline_self_employment_domain_is_valid formula `no_foreign_system_exclusive_se_income` → `no_foreign_system_exclusive_se_income and federal_self_employment_income == 0`; (2) wages_taken_into_account_for_additional_medicare_tax formula `wages` → `if ...domain_is_valid: wages else: 0`, with its window narrowed from open-ended effective_from '2013-01-01' to 2026-01-01..2026-12-31; (3) pipeline_reduced_additional_medicare_self_employment_threshold window likewise narrowed to 2026 only. Net effect on published outputs: federal_additional_medicare_self_employment_tax and federal_additional_medicare_tax go to zero whenever imported SE income is nonzero (pre-fix they published a positive 0.9% tax on SE income above the wage-reduced threshold).

Residual uncertainty a reviewer should weigh: this is a defect against the *cited corpus record*, not against real-world administered law. The PR body states the pinned §1401 record "faithfully carries the enacted scrivener's error" and that Treasury administers the cross-reference as 3101(b)(2) per 26 CFR 1.1401-1(d)(2) / Form 8959 / TD 9645 — I did not verify those regulatory citations and they are not needed for the verdict, but they are the basis of a not_a_defect argument (the old output was arguably closer to operative law). Under the rubric's definition of fidelity as agreement with the cited source text, the pre-fix module encoded a coordination rule the pinned record does not state and claimed a verbatim excerpt it does not contain, so I confirm. Also worth noting: the diff's own new module comment ("The lawful coordination sentence is absent from the current corpus pin: the record names section 3121(b)(2), not section 3101(b)(2).") is verbatim accurate against the resolved text, so the first reader's quote checks out. Version-window narrowing is collateral to the fail-close scoping, not a wrong_period_or_effective_date defect. Commit body is empty; the PR (#1003) has no reviews or comments, so the module comments and deferral reasons are the only narrative evidence.

modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module computed and published the full section 1401(a) and 1401(b)(1) self-employment taxes for every taxpayer with no representation of section 1401(c), which exempts self-employment income that is subject exclusively to a foreign social-security system under a section 233 agreement, so an in-scope exempt taxpayer received a positive SECA tax the statute says is exempt.
modules.triage_notes: Provision was read through the pinned corpus release (resolve_provision.py, us/statute/26/1401): subsection (c) 'Relief from taxes in cases covered by certain international agreements' is present and the module's new proof-atom excerpt is verbatim from it. Pre-fix evidence that the clause was unrepresented rather than merely undocumented: at parent f2aea3b2dc the only mentions of 1401(c) were (a) the module summary saying the executable slice 'assumes ... no section 1401(c) foreign-exclusive social security coverage' and (b) a deferred_outputs entry for us:statutes/26/1401#self_employment_tax_after_international_agreement_exemption; the three public tax formulas were unconditional sum_where/addition expressions. The fix is a single coherent change (one new Judgment rule, one new required Boolean input, three formula gates, summary rewrite) with no unrelated formula, parameter, rate, base, or effective-date changes — the $184,500 base, 0.9235 factor, 12.4%/2.9% rates and 2026-01-01/2026-12-31 windows are untouched. Caveat for a reviewer: the remedy is a conservative fail-closed zero for the whole tax unit, whereas 1401(c) exempts only 'to the extent' the income is subject exclusively to the foreign system; the commit's own summary and the PR body acknowledge the actual foreign-agreement relief calculation remains a deferred boundary, so this corrects a fail-open defect without fully encoding the clause's partial-exemption arithmetic. Commit message is terse ('fix: gate ordinary SECA tax outputs') but PROGRESS.md in the same commit states 'Gated the existing OASDI, hospital-insurance, and combined ordinary SECA tax outputs behind that Judgment without renaming any existing surface', and the PR body (#1003) says '§1401(c) attestation gates the public outputs'. The companion test file adds `seca-foreign-system-boundary-fails-closed` asserting domain_is_valid: not_holds, federal_self_employment_income '46175' still observable, and all three taxes '0'. The new import proof atoms carry hash: sha256:local, and PROGRESS.md lists 'Refresh the downstream SE import hash' as remaining work, so a follow-up commit on the same branch likely rewrites those hashes (mechanical).

verdict.justification: The first reader's premise — "no representation of section 1401(c)" — is factually wrong: the pre-fix module already carried a structured `deferred_outputs` entry `us:statutes/26/1401#self_employment_tax_after_international_agreement_exemption` whose reason names section 1401(c) and states the submodules "do not encode that exemption," and that entry survives this commit verbatim. The fix does not encode the exemption either; it adds a required TaxUnit attestation plus a fail-closed gate, and its own added comment still calls the relief calculation a deferred boundary, so the in-domain encoded meaning is unchanged and the out-of-domain output (zero for the whole tax unit) is not the statutory result for the "to the extent that" partial-exemption case the pinned §1401(c) text actually states. Against that, the pre-fix module did publish a positive `federal_self_employment_tax` for a population the statute exempts with no input by which a caller could express the fact, and the commit adds a breaking required input and a companion showing 7,064.775 → 0, which reads as a genuine fail-open correction. The message is generic ("fix: gate ordinary SECA tax outputs") and the diff is a domain guard rather than a clause encoding, so the evidence does not settle fidelity-correction versus enforcement of an already-declared deferred boundary.
verdict.quote: When that Judgment is `not_holds`, all three public tax outputs fail closed to zero while the pre-relief income outputs remain observable. The unresolved foreign-agreement relief calculation, full upstream section 1402(a) completed-return construction, and the complete cross-referenced wage definition remain explicit deferred boundaries below.
verdict.notes:
Refutation attempt on the KIND failed: if this is kept as fidelity, `unrepresented_clause` is still the best fit. `polarity_or_logic` is tempting because its definition names "fail-open vs fail-closed" and PROGRESS.md calls this "the ordinary SECA fail-closed foreign-coverage boundary," but there was no prior boolean or branch on this condition to invert — the fix creates the branch — so "clause missing, fix adds it" describes it better.

Refutation on the CLASSIFICATION has real force, which is why I land on unclear rather than confirmed:
1. Pre-declared boundary. Pre-fix `deferred_outputs` (unchanged by this commit) reads: "Section 1401(c) exempts income subject exclusively to a foreign social security system under a section 233 agreement. The cap-aware, Person-level section 1401(a) and (b)(1) submodules do not encode that exemption..." Pre-fix summary prose: "The executable slice assumes ... no section 1401(c) foreign-exclusive social security coverage. Those mechanisms ... remain explicit deferred boundaries below." This is scope the module explicitly disclaimed, in machine-readable metadata, not a silent omission.
2. The fix adds no statutory computation. The 1401(c) deferred_outputs entry is byte-identical post-fix; the new rule is a Judgment over a caller attestation, not the exemption.
3. Post-fix is also not source-faithful for the partial case. Pinned §1401(c) (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, provision sha256 38a25e0d...) exempts SE income "to the extent that" it is subject exclusively to the foreign system. The new input `no_foreign_system_exclusive_se_income` is Boolean and TaxUnit-level, while the statutory exemption is per-individual and proportional, so a partially-covered filer now gets zero for the whole unit — wrong in the opposite direction. Zero here is a refusal sentinel, not a computed result.

Counterweights a reviewer should hold against the above, if they want to keep it as confirmed/unrepresented_clause: the pre-fix public output was unconditional over all TaxUnits, `us/statute/26/1401` was a claimed `corpus_citation_paths` entry, the new proof atom is `kind: exception` quoting the §1401(c) text verbatim from the pinned corpus (verified — the excerpt matches the release text exactly), the commit is labeled "fix:", and it adds a *required* input (a breaking caller-contract change), which implies the authors judged the prior surface wrong rather than merely incomplete. New companion `seca-foreign-system-boundary-fails-closed` pins the behavior change: pre-fix would have produced 5,725.70 + 1,339.075 = 7,064.775; post-fix all three tax outputs are '0' with `federal_self_employment_income` still '46175'.

PR #1003 body describes this as the house pattern rather than a one-off correction ("valid ONLY in its verified domain ... out-of-domain fails closed"), applied to the NIIT pipeline in the same PR; if the benchmark wants genuine statutory-meaning defects rather than domain-guard hardening, this case and its NIIT sibling should be judged the same way.
