item.subject: test: characterize exact SE floor boundary

triage.commit_summary: The commit adds a dedicated, source-backed non-tax Judgment rule (plus a new Person input and a new import of us:statutes/26/1402/b#self_employment_income_inclusion_threshold) to the federal self-employment-tax pipeline so a companion test can assert the section 1402(b)(2) $400 floor at exactly $400. It exists because that exact boundary is otherwise unreachable through the module's public path (the pre-paragraph-(12) input times the 0.9235 paragraph-(12) factor yields the repeating amount 800000/1847), so no existing formula, parameter, version, effective date, or public tax output was changed.

modules.description_quote: It permits exact-boundary observability without replacing the principal pre-paragraph-(12) input or changing any public tax output.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: nothing in the pre-fix module disagreed with the source — the section 1402(b)(2) floor was already carried correctly by the imported us:statutes/26/1402/b#self_employment_income (formula 'if ... < self_employment_income_inclusion_threshold: 0 else: net_earnings_from_self_employment', i.e. inclusive at exactly $400, matching the statute's 'less than $400'); the module merely lacked a surface on which a test could land exactly on that boundary.
modules.triage_notes: Recommend PRUNING from the defect corpus. This is additive test instrumentation, not a fidelity correction. The diff (1) adds one import, (2) adds one new derived rule of dtype Judgment (completed_post_paragraph_12_net_earnings_meet_section_1402_b_floor, formula 'completed_post_paragraph_12_net_earnings_for_floor_boundary >= self_employment_income_inclusion_threshold'), (3) adds one new Person input consumed only by that Judgment, and (4) extends the module summary. No existing rule formula, parameter, version, effective date, entity, or public output changed. Commit subject is 'test: characterize exact SE floor boundary' and the commit body is empty; PROGRESS.md in the same commit says the new Judgment's 'exact-$400 case proves that the imported section 1402(b)(2) threshold is inclusive without approximating the repeating pre-adjustment amount or changing any public tax output'. The PR body (#1003) likewise frames it as coverage, not repair: 'floor fixtures assert the imported 1402(b)(2) branch at both straddle points (exact N=400 unreachable via the 0.9235 factor — documented)'. Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus release (us/statute/26/1402): subsection (b)(2) excludes net earnings 'if such net earnings for the taxable year are less than $400', so the inclusive-at-$400 reading the new Judgment characterizes is correct, and the imported 1402(b) encoding already implemented it correctly at this commit (verified via git grep of us/statutes/26/1402/b.yaml at 183573f2d6, line 116). defect_kind is boundary_direction only because floor inclusivity is the property being characterized; no boundary was actually wrong before the change. PR #1003 has no reviews, review comments, or issue comments. Companion file us/policies/income_tax/self_employment_tax_pipeline.test.yaml gained one case, seca-floor-exact-post-adjustment-400, in the same commit; PROGRESS.md also changed.

verdict.justification: The module diff is entirely additive — a new import, a new `Judgment` rule, a new caller-supplied input, and a summary paragraph — with no pre-existing formula, parameter, version, effective date, output, or comparison operator changed, so no encoded meaning was corrected. The section 1402(b)(2) floor was already faithful before the commit: the untouched imported module `us/statutes/26/1402/b.yaml` reads `if net_earnings_from_self_employment_for_paragraph_2_threshold_test < self_employment_income_inclusion_threshold: 0 else: net_earnings_from_self_employment`, which excludes strictly below and includes at exactly $400, matching the pinned corpus text "(2) the net earnings from self-employment, if such net earnings for the taxable year are less than $400." The added rule's `>= self_employment_income_inclusion_threshold` restates that same boundary on a new surface rather than flipping any strictness, so `boundary_direction` has no referent: no operator was wrong and none was fixed. This is added test observability the module never claimed — the new input is, by its own description, "never substituted into the public tax calculation" — introduced only because the exact boundary was unreachable through the principal input (400 / 0.9235 = 800000/1847, non-terminating).
verdict.quote: +    description: Completed section 1402(a) net earnings after paragraph (12), consumed only by the exact section 1402(b)(2) floor-characterization Judgment and never substituted into the public tax calculation.
verdict.notes: Refutation of the first reader: the reader's narrative ("nothing in the pre-fix module disagreed with the source") is correct, but it cannot coexist with defect kind boundary_direction, which requires a wrong strictness somewhere in the pre-fix text; there is none, and the diff changes no operator. Verified read-only: `git show --stat 183573f2d6` touches only PROGRESS.md, self_employment_tax_pipeline.test.yaml, and the module; every module hunk is `+` lines (one comment-block hunk, one imports hunk, one new-rule hunk, one new-input hunk). Imported boundary verified at the commit's own tree: `git show 183573f2d6:us/statutes/26/1402/b.yaml` line 116. Source verified through the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union (corpus commit 0fd35bfbda), provision us/statute/26/1402, body sha256 b21f64df69cb...: "less than $400". Corroborating in-repo evidence that this is a characterization test, not a fix: the new test case comment "This dedicated boundary Judgment avoids approximating the repeating pre-adjustment amount 800000 / 1847", and PR #1003's line "floor fixtures assert the imported 1402(b)(2) branch at both straddle points (exact N=400 unreachable via the 0.9235 factor — documented)". Not classified mechanical because the change does add a rule, an import, and an input (the module's input contract changed), which exceeds the metadata/provenance-only definition — but nothing it adds feeds a public tax output. Residual uncertainty (why 0.86 and not higher): the new input lets a caller supply a post-paragraph-(12) amount inconsistent with the principal pre-(12) input, which is a new risk surface introduced here, not a defect repaired here; a reviewer who counts "missing exact-boundary observability" as coverage the source requires could argue unclear, but the source requires a result, not a probe.

item.subject: fix: gate additional Medicare SE domain

triage.commit_summary: The commit adds a required section 1401(c) applicability boundary to the federal Additional Medicare Tax composition pipeline: a new TaxUnit Judgment rule (`additional_medicare_tax_pipeline_self_employment_domain_is_valid`) driven by a new `no_foreign_system_exclusive_se_income` attestation input, and it gates both the public self-employment leg and the public combined tax on that Judgment so they fail closed to zero outside the ordinary (no foreign totalization-agreement relief) domain, while the independently grounded imported wage leg stays observable. It also expands two truncated section 1401(b)(2)(B) coordination proof excerpts to the full served sentence, notes an upstream corpus `source_url` metadata defect in a comment, and adds two companion cases (a 1401(c) fail-closed case and a joint two-positive-SE-earner single-threshold case) plus a PROGRESS.md log entry.

modules.description_quote: Required attestation that no self-employment income of the tax unit is exempt from section 1401 under subsection (c) because it is subject exclusively to a foreign social-security system under a section 233 agreement.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module computed and published the section 1401(b)(2) self-employment additional Medicare leg (and the combined tax) unconditionally for every tax unit, with no representation of the section 1401(c) exemption for self-employment income that a section 233 totalization agreement subjects exclusively to a foreign social-security system, so it asserted positive tax for taxpayers the cited source exempts.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us/statute/26/1401 resolved; 1,924 chars): subsection (c) states 'During any period in which there is in effect an agreement entered into pursuant to section 233 of the Social Security Act with any foreign country, the self-employment income of an individual shall be exempt from the taxes imposed by this section to the extent that such self-employment income is subject under such agreement exclusively to the laws applicable to the social security system of such foreign country.' The pre-fix summary already disclosed that the executable surfaces 'cover the ordinary case in which section 1401(c) foreign-system relief is not implicated', but nothing enforced that domain, so the encoding silently produced out-of-domain numbers; the fix does not model the relief computation (still deferred upstream) but fails closed, which is the represented-clause repair rather than added scope. Single-module commit, so no repeated pattern. Mechanical/provenance changes ride along in the same diff and are not the defect: both 1401(b)(2)(B) proof-atom excerpts are expanded from the truncated 'shall be reduced (but not below zero) by the amount of wages taken into account' to the full served sentence (which exposes the enacted '3121(b)(2)' scrivener's cross-reference discussed in the PR body), and a new comment records that the corpus record's source_url wrongly points at 26 USC 45A (no corpus edit here). The commit message body is empty and there are no PR reviews or review comments; the PR body's 'FAIL CLOSED' language concerns a different fail-closed condition (the pinned corpus record's 1401 cross-reference), so the quote was taken from the module diff instead. Companion tests added in the same commit: amt-foreign-system-boundary-fails-closed asserts wage leg 450 with SE leg and combined both 0 when the attestation is false, plus a joint two-earner threshold case; every pre-existing case gained the attestation input via a YAML anchor.

verdict.justification: The refutation attempts fail: the pinned corpus record for us/statute/26/1401 carries subsection (c) verbatim ("the self-employment income of an individual shall be exempt from the taxes imposed by this section to the extent that such self-employment income is subject under such agreement exclusively to the laws applicable to the social security system of such foreign country"), and "this section" is §1401, which contains the (b)(2) additional-Medicare leg this module encodes, so the exception is on-point for the encoded rules. Pre-fix, both public outputs computed unconditionally (`pipeline_additional_medicare_self_employment_tax_base * pipeline_additional_medicare_self_employment_tax_rate`) with no applicability condition anywhere in the chain — I checked the sibling `self_employment_tax_pipeline.yaml` at parent 791ff29eb5 and it had no §1401(c) attestation or gate either, so nothing upstream represented the exemption; the only representation was prose in the module summary, which does not constrain encoded meaning. The fix adds a new Judgment rule whose proof atom is `kind: exception` quoting §1401(c) verbatim, a new required Boolean input, and rewrites two previously unconditional public formulas into gated ones, which is a change in encoded meaning plus input scope, not bookkeeping. That is exactly the rubric's "adds a missing exception the source states" case, so unrepresented_clause fits better than boundary/polarity (there was no prior condition to invert) or wrong_entity_or_scope (the narrowing derives from a statutory exception clause, not an entity/population mis-assignment).
verdict.quote:
+          if additional_medicare_tax_pipeline_self_employment_domain_is_valid:
+            pipeline_additional_medicare_self_employment_tax_base
+            * pipeline_additional_medicare_self_employment_tax_rate
+          else:
+            0
verdict.notes: Caveats a reviewer should keep with this case. (1) The fix is a partial representation: §1401(c) exempts SE income "to the extent that" it is foreign-exclusive, while the encoding uses a Boolean attestation and fails closed to zero for the whole leg; the deferred outputs `pipeline_additional_medicare_self_employment_income_exempt_under_international_agreement` and `pipeline_taxable_self_employment_income_for_additional_medicare_tax` remain blocked on upstream `us:statutes/26/1401#self_employment_tax_after_international_agreement_exemption`. So the defect is corrected in the direction of removing a false positive assertion, not by implementing the relief arithmetic. (2) Possible residual fidelity issue introduced by the same fix: `federal_additional_medicare_tax` (combined) also returns 0 when the attestation fails, which zeroes the §3101(b)(2) wage leg — a tax §1401(c) does not exempt (it is imposed by §3101, not "this section"). The new companion `amt-foreign-system-boundary-fails-closed` asserts wage leg 450 but combined 0, i.e. combined ≠ sum of legs out of domain. (3) The diff also contains genuinely mechanical content — two proof-atom excerpts expanded from "shall be reduced (but not below zero) by the amount of wages taken into account" to the full 1401(b)(2)(B) sentence, plus a comment about the corpus record's wrong `source_url`. Those alone would be provenance-only; they ride along with the meaning change and should not be scored as the defect. (4) Pre-fix PROGRESS.md listed "Add the section 1401(c) boundary gate and companion case" under Next, i.e. the gap was identified in review before this commit; the commit is labeled "fix:". PR #1003's separate scrivener's-error/corpus-pin fail-closed discussion (3121(b)(2) vs 3101(b)(2)) is a different matter and is not what this commit changes.

item.subject: fix: constrain NIIT to verified input domain

triage.commit_summary: The commit narrows the federal NIIT composition pipeline (26 USC 1411, TY2026) to the input domain in which its imported §1411 encoding is actually faithful: it adds a Judgment rule `niit_verified_domain_applies` requiring zero qualified-plan distributions, zero §1401(b)-taxed income, zero §911-derived MAGI adjustments, a zero separate working-capital slot, and a caller attestation that the supplied §1411(c)(1) income categories are disjoint post-classification amounts, and gates the public `federal_net_investment_income_tax` output to return the imported tax only when that Judgment holds and zero otherwise. It does this because the imported `us/statutes/26/1411` module subtracts the §1411(c)(5)-(6) exclusion categories from unrelated included income instead of leaving them out of net investment income, separately adds a working-capital slot on top of the named categories, and cannot enforce the §1411(d)(2) "allocable to the §911(a)(1) exclusion" filter, so the pipeline previously published §1411-inconsistent tax amounts for those inputs (upstream defects tracked as rulespec-us #1052); three unrestricted surfaces are declared deferred and six fail-closed companion cases were added.

modules.description_quote: thin wiring over encoded §1411, valid ONLY in its verified domain (qualified-plan distributions = 0, §1401(b)-income-for-NII = 0, §911 amounts = 0, disjoint-categories attestation); out-of-domain fails closed (companions prove each guard)
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix pipeline failed open — it published an imported §1411 tax amount across a declared input domain (nonzero qualified-plan distributions, §1401(b)-taxed items, §911 exclusion/disallowance amounts, a separate working-capital slot) in which the imported encoding contradicts the statute, so it returned §1411-inconsistent tax for those taxpayers; but this file's own formula was a faithful pass-through and the fix substitutes a refusal (zero) rather than the statutory answer.
modules.triage_notes: Decisive diff: `formula: net_investment_income_tax` becomes `if niit_verified_domain_applies: net_investment_income_tax else: 0`, plus a new derived Judgment rule `niit_verified_domain_applies` (conjunction of the disjointness attestation and five ==0 checks), two new §911 imports so the domain rule can test the imported §911(a)(1)/§911(d)(6) amounts, one new Boolean input, three `deferred_outputs` entries, and rewritten input descriptions. Verified the underlying source and the upstream defect directly: through the pinned corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, §1411(c)(5) reads "The term “net investment income” shall not include any distribution from a plan or arrangement described in section 401(a), 403(a), 403(b), 408, 408A, or 457(b)" and (c)(6) "Net investment income shall not include any item taken into account in determining self-employment income ... on which a tax is imposed by section 1401(b)" — category exclusions, not offsets; the imported us/statutes/26/1411.yaml at this commit computes `net_investment_income = max(0, net_investment_income_gross_items - allocable_investment_deductions - net_investment_income_excluded_items)` where `net_investment_income_excluded_items = qualified_plan_distributions + self_employment_income_subject_to_1401_b`, i.e. it subtracts excluded categories from unrelated included income (understating NII), and `net_investment_income_gross_items` adds `investment_of_working_capital_income` on top of the named §1411(c)(1)(A) categories (double-count risk given §1411(c)(3)'s §469(e)(1)(B) rule). Why unclear rather than fidelity: the real fidelity defect lives in the imported statute module (PR body: "Upstream encode defects: #1052"), not in this composition, whose own pre-fix formula faithfully re-exposed the import; and the fix does not restore the statutory answer for the excluded domain — it returns zero, which §1411 also does not prescribe. A judge shown only this module plus §1411 could not detect a contradiction with the source text in the pre-fix file, which makes this a weak benchmark item; a reviewer may prefer to keep only the upstream #1052 fix commit. Kind choice: polarity_or_logic because the enumerated "fail-open vs fail-closed / default value" shape matches the decisive edit exactly; the alternative reading is wrong_entity_or_scope (the declared output surface covered a wider input domain than the encoding supports). Supporting module-diff text added by this commit, more specific than the PR quote: "The imported section 1411(c)(5)-(6) encoding subtracts excluded items from unrelated included income instead of keeping the categories out of net investment income." Commit message body is empty (subject only); PR #1003 has no reviews or review comments in the bundle. The commit also touched the companion test file (six new fail-closed cases, anchor split into common vs verified-domain inputs) and PROGRESS.md, and it incidentally re-labeled the passive-activity and financial-trading inputs from §1411(c)(2)(A)/(B) to §1411(c)(1)(A)(ii) — a citation-string (mechanical/provenance) correction unrelated to the guard.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as a mere containment enhancement and could not: the pre-fix surface was demonstrably wrong against the pinned source over a domain it expressly declared. The pinned §1411 text reads "(5) ... The term 'net investment income' shall not include any distribution from a plan ... (6) ... shall not include any item taken into account in determining self-employment income ...", while the imported module computes net_investment_income = max(0, gross_items − allocable_deductions − (qualified_plan_distributions + self_employment_income_subject_to_1401_b)), i.e. it offsets excluded categories against unrelated included income; the pre-fix pipeline declared those very inputs ("Section 1411(c)(5) qualified-plan distribution exclusion") and published that contradicting number, and the same mismatch exists for §1411(d)(2)'s "(taken into account in computing adjusted gross income) ... with respect to the amounts described in paragraph (1)" filter, which the imported §911(d)(6) aggregate does not apply. The diff changes encoded meaning exactly as the quoted reason describes — it adds a conjunctive guard rule and converts the public output from an unconditional pass-through to a guarded branch defaulting to zero, with six new companions asserting not_holds/0 — and "fail-open vs fail-closed, default value" is the named archetype of polarity_or_logic, so the kind fits and the evidence settles it beyond "unclear".
verdict.quote:
-        formula: net_investment_income_tax
+        formula: |-
+          if niit_verified_domain_applies:
+            net_investment_income_tax
+          else:
+            0
verdict.notes: Verification trail: statute text via resolve_provision (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, body sha256 b5f89c82...), imported formulas at `git -C /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us show 791ff29eb5:us/statutes/26/1411.yaml` lines 123-240 (niit_modified_adjusted_gross_income, net_investment_income_excluded_items, net_investment_income). Worked example from the new fixture niit-qualified-plan-input-fails-closed (AGI 250,000, interest 10,000, plan distributions 5,000, single): statute = .038 × min(10,000, 50,000) = $380; pre-fix module = .038 × min(5,000, 50,000) = $190; post-fix = $0. Two caveats a reviewer should weigh and that keep me at 0.7 rather than higher. (1) The remedy is a refusal, not the statutory answer — the arithmetic defect stays in us/statutes/26/1411.yaml (upstream issue #1052, unfixed here), so this module change removes a wrong nonzero and substitutes a wrong zero plus three deferred_outputs blocked-surface records; if the corpus wants only fixes that move a value toward the source amount, this one is a containment fix and belongs in a separate bucket. (2) A defensible alternative kind is wrong_entity_or_scope, since the substance of the defect is an over-claimed input domain (the pre-fix summary invited "qualified-plan distributions, self-employment income already taxed under section 1401(b) ... section 911 facts") and the boolean is only the mechanism; I kept polarity_or_logic because the kind list assigns fail-open/fail-closed and default-value changes to it explicitly. Also note a second, independent statutory basis the diff relies on: §1411(c)(3) makes working-capital income a rule-similar-to-469(e)(1)(B) reclassification, not an additive tenth category, yet the imported gross-items formula adds investment_of_working_capital_income alongside the named categories — double-count risk, which the fix addresses by requiring that slot to be zero. The module change is not mechanical: formula, inputs, input semantics, imports and the published output surface all changed.

item.subject: fix: express ACA PTC grid guard as judgment logic

triage.commit_summary: The commit rewrites the on-grid rounding guard inside the ACA PTC pipeline's `aca_ptc_full_year_runtime_inputs_valid` Judgment rule from a pair of nested scalar `if/else` expressions compared against their own `floor()` into an equivalent three-way boolean disjunction (band-below-zero, flat-band, interpolated-band), and updates PROGRESS.md accordingly. The reason was tooling, not law: the deterministic validator rejected nested scalar `if` expressions inside a `Judgment` formula even though the engine executed them, so the same condition was re-expressed in boolean-only syntax.

modules.description_quote: fix: express ACA PTC grid guard as judgment logic
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing was wrong relative to the source: the pre-fix formula encoded the same on-grid rounding guard, but in scalar if/else form that the deterministic validator rejected inside a Judgment dtype, so the fix only re-expresses it as boolean branches.
modules.triage_notes: Verified semantic equivalence branch by branch against the pre-fix file (git show 3457540fd:us/policies/aca/ptc_pipeline.yaml, lines ~563-600). Pre-fix: band < 0 fed numerator 0, so 0/grid == floor(0/grid) evaluated true; post-fix that case becomes the literal disjunct `aca_ptc_applicable_percentage_band < 0`. Pre-fix band>=0 with applicable_initial_percentage == applicable_final_percentage compared init/grid to floor(init/grid); post-fix keeps exactly that as the second disjunct. Pre-fix band>=0 with init != final compared the linear-interpolation expression /grid to its floor; post-fix keeps exactly that expression as the third disjunct. No parameters, effective dates (2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31), imports, proof atoms, inputs, outputs, or entity/period changed; the module diff is a single hunk and the only other file touched is PROGRESS.md. The stated reason is in that PROGRESS.md hunk, not in the commit body (body is empty) and not in the PR body, so the quote above is the commit subject; the PROGRESS.md text reads: "Deterministic validation rejected nested scalar `if` expressions inside the `Judgment` formula even though the engine executed them, so the on-grid check was rewritten as equivalent boolean branches." That is validator-syntax normalization, i.e. provenance/tooling, not encoded meaning. PR #1002 is the composition PR for the whole 2026 PTC pipeline; the substantive fidelity work on the fail-closed grid gate landed in the immediately preceding commits 2d032aa87 ("fix: gate ACA PTC public arithmetic off grid") and 3457540fd ("test: assert ACA PTC intermediates fail closed"), so a fidelity-defect corpus should look there, not here. item.subject: fix: gate ACA PTC public arithmetic off grid

triage.commit_summary: The commit extends the ACA premium tax credit pipeline's fail-closed "on-grid" guard from the final annual credit to every public output on the operative chain (applicable percentage, the 36B(b)(2)(B)(ii) rate bridge, the monthly enrolled/SLCSP premium operands, required monthly contribution, and monthly/annual premium assistance), so off-grid income ratios now yield zero on all of them instead of emitting the raw unrounded interpolation chain. It was made because 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g)'s nearest-0.01-percentage-point rounding of the interpolated applicable percentage is not in the pinned corpus, and the pre-fix module gated only the annual credit, leaving legally operative public intermediates fail-open; the validity rule was rewritten to compute the raw interpolation candidate internally (from the imported Rev. Proc. 2025-25 endpoints) to avoid a dependency cycle with the now-gated public percentage.

modules.description_quote: the round-2 residual (ungated public intermediates) are all addressed at this head
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Pre-fix only the annual credit was gated on the on-grid validity judgment, so for off-grid income ratios the module still published an applicable percentage, required monthly contribution, and monthly/annual premium assistance computed from the raw unrounded 36B(b)(3)(A)(i) interpolation - values that are not the lawful applicable percentage, which 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g) (cross-referenced by Rev. Proc. 2025-25 sec. 3.01) requires rounded to the nearest 0.01 percentage point.
modules.triage_notes: Single-module commit (PROGRESS.md also changed; no companion test file in this commit - PROGRESS's 'Next' shows companion expectations for the gated surfaces landed in a later commit of PR #1002). Commit body is empty, so evidence is the PR body plus the module's own summary/deferred_outputs prose changed in the diff ('every public percentage, contribution, and assistance output fails closed unless that candidate already equals its nearest-0.01-percentage-point value'). PROGRESS.md in the same commit states the pre-fix defect most plainly (removed line): 'public legally operative ACA PTC intermediates still emit the unrounded calculation chain when `aca_ptc_full_year_runtime_inputs_valid` is `not_holds`' - not quoted in description_quote because PROGRESS.md is not one of the allowed quote sources. I read us/guidance/irs/rev-proc-2025-25 through the pinned corpus resolver (release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union): sec. 3.01 gives the 2026 table 'for purposes of § 36B(b)(3)(A)(i) and § 1.36B-3(g)' but the corpus contains no 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g) text, so the rounding requirement itself is only cross-referenced, not readable in the pinned corpus - the module documents it as a deferred output. Kind is arguable: I chose polarity_or_logic because the rubric puts 'fail-open vs fail-closed' there and the pre-fix formulas fired the computing branch where they should have defaulted to zero; wrong_entity_or_scope ('output surface') is the plausible alternative, since the delta is which public output surfaces the existing guard covers. Confidence held below 0.8 because the fix suppresses the unlawful values rather than computing the lawful rounded ones (a conservative fail-closed narrowing rather than a value correction), which leaves room to call this defensive hygiene instead of a meaning correction. The rest of the diff is consequential, not unrelated: aca_ptc_full_year_runtime_inputs_valid inlines the raw interpolation candidate (and swaps its proof-atom import from #aca_ptc_applicable_percentage to the Rev. Proc. initial/final percentage imports) purely to break the cycle created by gating the public percentage; no parameter values, effective dates, entities, or module scope changed.

verdict.justification: The diff does change encoded meaning — five public outputs go from unconditional formulas to `if aca_ptc_full_year_runtime_inputs_valid: ... else: 0` — but it is doubtful that this corrects a disagreement with the cited source text. The rounding requirement driving the gate lives in 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g), which the resolver confirms is absent from the pinned corpus (Rev. Proc. 2025-25 sec. 3.01 only cross-references "§ 36B(b)(3)(A)(i) and § 1.36B-3(g)" for the table and states no rounding rule; 36B(b)(3)(A)(i) itself prescribes only that the percentage "increase, on a sliding scale in a linear manner"), and the module declares that surface a deferred output both before and after the fix, with the guard parameter labeled "Guard-only ... not a general rounded-rate output" and the judgment sourced as a "fail-closed computability boundary pending ingestion of 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g)". Post-fix the off-grid outputs are 0, which is not the lawful applicable percentage either, so the change withdraws an assertion rather than bringing the encoding into agreement with the source; it even gates the monthly enrolled-premium and adjusted monthly SLCSP outputs, whose statutory definitions (36B(b)(2)(A), (b)(2)(B)(i)) do not depend on the applicable percentage at all, to 0 for off-grid ratios. If a reviewer counts "published a value the module disclaimed the ability to compute" as fidelity, polarity_or_logic (fail-open → fail-closed default) is the right kind; on the pinned source text alone this reads as declared-boundary hygiene, not a fidelity correction.
verdict.quote:
-        formula: aca_ptc_annual_slcsp_benchmark_premium / required_contribution_annual_to_monthly_divisor
+        formula: |-
+          if aca_ptc_full_year_runtime_inputs_valid:
+            aca_ptc_annual_slcsp_benchmark_premium / required_contribution_annual_to_monthly_divisor
+          else:
+            0
verdict.notes: Facts a reviewer should weigh. (1) Provenance of the "quote" the first reader used: PR #1002 has `reviews: []` and `review_comments: []` in the bundle, so "the round-2 residual (ungated public intermediates) are all addressed at this head" is the PR author's own body text summarizing a blind-review finding, not an independent reviewer statement. (2) Commit 2d032aa87a is a within-PR review round on the same PR (#1002, merged 2026-07-24) that introduced `us/policies/aca/ptc_pipeline.yaml`; the pre-fix state was never merged or live. (3) The annual credit was already gated pre-fix (`if aca_ptc_full_year_runtime_inputs_valid and aca_ptc_applicable_taxpayer:` at pre-file line 661, unchanged by this commit), so the fix extends an existing convention to intermediates rather than adding a missing source clause. (4) Pre-fix deferred_outputs already said the module "does not claim to compute the general rounded rate ... every other interpolation fails closed before the annual premium tax credit is exported" — literally true pre-fix; the fix widens that sentence to "across the public applicable-percentage, contribution, assistance, and annual-credit surfaces." (5) Source check via the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union (corpus commit 0fd35bfbda): Rev. Proc. 2025-25 sec. 3.01 reads "the Applicable Percentage Table for purposes of § 36B(b)(3)(A)(i) and § 1.36B-3(g) is:" with no rounding language; 36B(b)(3)(A)(i) has no rounding language. So no pinned, cited text makes the pre-fix raw interpolation wrong. (6) The large `aca_ptc_full_year_runtime_inputs_valid` hunk that inlines the interpolation is a circularity consequence of gating `aca_ptc_applicable_percentage` on the judgment (it could no longer import it), not an independent meaning change; the two new import atoms for applicable_initial/final_percentage follow from that inlining. (7) Under the task's own rule that scope/precision a module never claimed is not a defect, this is the mirror case: the module explicitly deferred the rounded general surface, and the fix suppresses output inside that deferred region. Keep as unclear; if the corpus convention treats "publishes a value it cannot show lawful" as fidelity, keep polarity_or_logic and lower confidence, rather than reclassifying to unrepresented_clause (the fix does not add the rounding the source states) or untraceable_branch (the pre-fix formula was grounded in 36B(b)(3)(A)(i)).

item.subject: fix: fail closed on unrounded ACA percentages

triage.commit_summary: The commit hardened the 2026 ACA premium tax credit composition (`us/policies/aca/ptc_pipeline.yaml`) so it no longer exports a credit built on a raw, unrounded section 36B(b)(3)(A)(i) interpolated applicable percentage: it adds a private 0.01-percentage-point grid parameter and extends the module's runtime-validity judgment with an on-grid test, so any household-income/FPL ratio whose interpolation lands off the nearest-0.01-percentage-point grid fails closed to a zero credit. The stated reason is that 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g) requires the interpolated percentage to be rounded to the nearest 0.01 percentage point but that regulation is absent from the pinned corpus, so rather than emit a chain that contradicts the regulation, the module restricts itself to inputs whose raw interpolation already equals its lawful rounded value.

modules.description_quote: 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g) requires the interpolated percentage rounded to the nearest 0.01 percentage point; that regulation is NOT in the pinned corpus, so instead of emitting an unrounded chain, EVERY public output carrying the operative percentage/contribution/assistance chain is gated on an on-grid validity judgment — off-grid ratios fail closed to zero/not_holds
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix validity judgment held (fail-open) for every household-income/FPL ratio, so for ratios whose 36B(b)(3)(A)(i) linear interpolation lands off the 0.01-percentage-point grid the module exported an annual premium tax credit computed from a raw unrounded applicable percentage, a rate that disagrees with the rounded percentage 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g) requires.
modules.triage_notes: Read the whole diff plus pre-fix (46ddf937a) and post-fix module bodies; also resolved us/guidance/irs/rev-proc-2025-25 through the pinned corpus, which confirms the new parameter's proof excerpt verbatim ('the Applicable Percentage Table for purposes of § 36B(b)(3)(A)(i) and § 1.36B-3(g) is') and that the 2026 table endpoints (2.10/3.14/4.19/6.60/8.44/9.96%) are stated to 0.01 percentage point, supporting the 0.0001 grid increment. 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g) itself is NOT in the pinned corpus (the module says the resolver finds no provision for it), so the rounding requirement itself could not be read directly — evidence for it is the commit/PR text plus the rev proc's cross-reference. Kind is genuinely contestable: I chose polarity_or_logic because the commit subject ('fail closed on unrounded ACA percentages') and PR body ('off-grid ratios fail closed to zero/not_holds') name the fail-open→fail-closed change, the taxonomy lists fail-open vs fail-closed under polarity_or_logic, and the decisive diff is an added and-clause in a boolean Judgment formula. The strong alternative is unrepresented_clause: the underlying disagreement with the source is the missing 1.36B-3(g) rounding operation, which the pre-fix module disclosed only as a deferred output ('Required fixtures use table endpoints, constant bands, or an exact midpoint, so this missing operation does not change their rates') while still exporting an operative unrounded chain; note the fix does not add the rounding, it narrows the domain. Alternative quotable line from inside the module diff (quote_source module_comment): 'The pinned corpus resolver finds no provision for 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g), so this module does not claim to compute the general rounded rate.' Scope caveat: the PR body describes head ce08e342a and claims EVERY public output is gated, but at THIS commit only rules[aca_ptc_annual_premium_tax_credit] consumes the validity judgment; the public intermediates were gated in follow-up 2d032aa87 ('fix: gate ACA PTC public arithmetic off grid') and the guard expression was restructured in 3a7b27612 ('fix: express ACA PTC grid guard as judgment logic'), both same-day commits in PR #1002. The commit also touched only prose/deferral metadata otherwise (module summary, deferred_outputs reason plus new source_values, and the rule's `source` string) — no other formula, parameter, effective date, input, output, or entity changed. The PR has no reviews or review comments in the bundle.

verdict.justification: Both cited corpus sources are silent on rounding: the pinned 26 USC 36B text states only that the applicable percentage "shall increase, on a sliding scale in a linear manner, from the initial premium percentage to the final premium percentage", and Rev. Proc. 2025-25 contains zero occurrences of "round"/"nearest"/"hundredth" — so the pre-fix raw linear interpolation matched the cited source text exactly, and the module had already declared the rounded rate a deferred output. The fix does not encode the source rule it invokes; by its own words the regulation is un-ingested ("The pinned corpus resolver finds no provision for 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g)"), the deferral stays in place, and the module instead refuses to answer off-grid, which its own companion documents as moving the exported credit from $5,209.9668 (raw rate, 66 cents from the lawful $5,209.3095) to $0 — further from the lawful amount, not closer. That is a provenance/conservatism policy choice about what the module may claim, not an encoded meaning corrected against a cited source, so neither polarity_or_logic nor any fidelity kind fits cleanly. Separately, the quoted PR-body evidence describes the merged head, not this commit: "EVERY public output" only became gated two commits later in 2d032aa87 "fix: gate ACA PTC public arithmetic off grid", which had to inline the interpolation to undo the self-referential `hash: sha256:local` import this commit introduced.
verdict.quote: +    source: Guard-only 0.01-percentage-point increment required by un-ingested 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g); not a general rounded-rate output
verdict.notes:
Strongest counterargument to my verdict (a reviewer may prefer "unclear"): the pre-fix module did export a PTC amount that disagrees with real-world law, and the framework lists "fail-open vs fail-closed" under polarity_or_logic. But the missing thing is the rounding operation of 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g), which is still unrepresented after the fix — the fix quarantines the gap rather than curing it — so if anyone insists on a fidelity label, unrepresented_clause fits the underlying gap better than polarity_or_logic, and neither is satisfied by this diff.

Evidence chain, all read-only: (1) pinned corpus us/statute/26/36B (release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, corpus commit 0fd35bfbda) contains no rounding language for 36B(b)(3)(A)(i); us/guidance/irs/rev-proc-2025-25 has 0 hits for round/nearest/hundredth/0.01 and mentions § 1.36B-3 only in its header cross-reference line — which is also the excerpt the new guard parameter's proof atom leans on ("the Applicable Percentage Table for purposes of § 36B(b)(3)(A)(i) and § 1.36B-3(g) is"). (2) Pre-fix 46ddf937a0 already deferred us:regulations/26-cfr/1.36B-3/g#rounded_applicable_percentage and already gated aca_ptc_annual_premium_tax_credit on aca_ptc_full_year_runtime_inputs_valid; the only computational change in this commit is one added conjunct plus the 0.0001 grid parameter. (3) The companion case added here, off-grid-210fpl-fails-closed-pending-regulatory-rounding, states the lawful rounded chain ($2,290.6905 contribution, $5,209.3095 credit), the raw-rate credit ($5,209.9668) and the new output ($0).

Context a reviewer should weigh: us/policies/aca/ptc_pipeline.yaml was created two days earlier in the same PR (#1002) at 72058b2b0 and iterated five times (44a871f06, 52224b0513, 8e72ccd28, 2d032aa87, 3a7b27612). This candidate is an intermediate blind-review round on unmerged new code, not a fix to a shipped module, and the next two commits had to rework the very formula it added (inlining the interpolation to break the cycle it created, then re-expressing the guard "as judgment logic").

item.subject: Correct Kansas 2026 resident income tax core

triage.commit_summary: The commit re-grounds the Kansas tax-year-2026 full-year-resident income tax module on signed 2026 House Bill 2029: it adds hb-2029 pages 60-62 to the module's corpus citation and upstream-check path lists, repoints the rate-schedule, bracket-threshold, personal-exemption, and imposition proof atoms from K.S.A. 79-32,110 / 79-32,121 / 79-32,121b to the reconciled bill pages, and rewrites the rationale and the taxable-income deferred-output reason to say the parallel-amendment conflict is now resolved and the remaining holds are TaxUnit-interface limits rather than source conflicts — with every encoded rate, bracket, and exemption amount and every effective window unchanged. In the same commit it also drops the state-and-local-income-tax term from the Kansas itemized deduction formula and from the input-domain guard, removing that input from the module interface and moving the companion test's supported deductions from 19,480 to 20,980 and net liability from 2,173.616 to 2,089.916.

modules.description_quote: Signed 2026 House Bill 2029 reconciles the parallel 79-32,110 and 79-32,121 amendments, preserves the individual rate schedule and contingent-rate reference, combines the head-of-household and permanently disabled-veteran exemption amendments, and repeals 79-32,110b and 79-32,121b. This module follows that reconciled text.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix itemized deduction reduced the four K.S.A. 79-32,120(a)(5) components (charitable, medical, qualified residence interest, real and personal property taxes) by state and local income taxes deducted in federal itemized deductions — an amount those four enumerated components never contain, so the (b) reduction had no base to apply to and the deduction was understated — but 79-32,120(b) states that reduction on its face, so the removal could equally be a dropped clause rather than a correction.
modules.triage_notes: Two distinct things happen in this one-module commit. (1) Provenance/prose: three hb-2029 pages are added to module.source_verification.corpus_citation_paths and to upstream_source_check.checked_paths; ten proof-atom corpus_citation_path strings move from us-ks/statute/2026/79-32-110, 79-32-121, 79-32-121b to us-ks/statute/session-2026/hb-2029/page-60|61|62; four rule `source:` prose lines change from 'Shared/Intersection of K.S.A. 79-32,121 and 79-32,121b' to 'Reconciled ... in 2026 H.B. 2029'; and the rationale plus the complete_taxable_income deferred reason are rewritten. I read HB 2029 pages 61-62 through the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, corpus commit d9d6fba0): the bill carries exactly the amounts already encoded (5.2% / 5.58%, $46,000 joint and $23,000 other brackets, $18,320 / $9,160 / $2,320 exemptions), and `git diff` shows no `effective_from`, `effective_to`, or `formula:` header line changed anywhere in the file. So that half is excerpt/citation-string provenance = mechanical on the rubric, and the held-output set is identical. (2) The only encoded-meaning change: `- ks_pit_2026_state_local_income_tax_in_itemized_deductions` is removed from rules[ks_pit_2026_itemized_deduction].versions[0].formula and the two corresponding clauses (`>= 0` and the cap inequality) are removed from rules[ks_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid].versions[0].formula; after the commit the identifier appears nowhere in the file (it was never a declared rule, only a referenced raw input), and the companion test drops it from all four cases and updates deductions 19480 -> 20980, taxable income 40520 -> 39020, and tax 2173.616 -> 2089.916. I read K.S.A. 79-32,120/block-1 through the resolver: (a)(5) defines the Kansas itemized deduction as exactly four components at 100% (no income-tax component), while (b) says 'The total amount of deductions from federal adjusted gross income shall be reduced by the total amount of income taxes imposed by or paid to this state or any other taxing jurisdiction to the extent that the same are deducted in determining the federal itemized deductions and by the amount of all depreciation deductions ...'. That cuts both ways, which is why I did not mark this fidelity: the fix is defensible (reducing an enumerated four-category base by an item the base never includes is a phantom reduction that overstates tax), but a literal reading of (b) is exactly what the pre-fix encoded, and the post-fix module keeps the other half of the same sentence (the depreciation reduction) and keeps the proof atom whose excerpt is 'total amount of deductions from federal adjusted gross income shall be reduced', so it now applies half of (b) with no recorded rationale. Evidence gap: the commit body is empty, the commit subject is the generic 'Correct Kansas 2026 resident income tax core', and nothing in the diff, the PR body, or any review mentions the itemized-deduction change — the added rationale I quoted describes only the HB 2029 re-grounding. The bundled PR (#1083, 'Encode Kansas 2026 resident income tax core') is the encoding PR this mid-branch correction commit lives in, not a separate fix PR; `gh api commits/<sha>/pulls` confirms #1083 is the only PR, and it has zero reviews, review comments, issue comments, and commit comments. The change stuck: the last commit touching the file (a9fad7642) still has no SALT-in-itemized term; the separate `ks_pit_2026_income_taxes_deducted_in_federal_agi` addback in the Kansas AGI formula is a different, above-the-line 79-32,117 modification and is untouched. Leftover inconsistency a reviewer may want: module.summary still says the module 'computes ... the exemption amount on which both official amendment versions agree', which the rewritten rationale contradicts. HB 2029 pages 60-62 do not amend 79-32,120, so the re-grounding is not what motivated the itemized change. If a reviewer decides the removal is source-correct, this is untraceable_branch (formula term with no supporting base under the cited provision); if they decide (b) applies literally, the commit is a regression and the entry should be dropped rather than relabeled.

verdict.justification: The removed term is not an untraceable branch: K.S.A. 79-32,120(b), read through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union), states verbatim "The total amount of deductions from federal adjusted gross income shall be reduced by the total amount of income taxes imposed by or paid to this state or any other taxing jurisdiction to the extent that the same are deducted in determining the federal itemized deductions and by the amount of all depreciation deductions claimed..." — so the pre-fix subtraction tracked the cited provision word for word, and the fix drops the first half of that single sentence while keeping the depreciation half and keeping the rule's `source: K.S.A. 79-32,120(a)(5)-(b), current allowed components and reductions` label plus the surviving proof atom excerpt "total amount of deductions from federal adjusted gross income shall be reduced". Nothing in the commit (message is the bare subject "Correct Kansas 2026 resident income tax core", empty body), PR #1083, or the newly added sources justifies the removal: HB 2029 pages 60-62 amend only 79-32,110 (Sec. 23), 79-32,121 (Sec. 24) and 82a-955 (Sec. 25), never 79-32,120, so the quoted HB 2029 rationale the first reader relied on is about a different section entirely. The rest of the diff is provenance (citation paths re-grounded from 79-32,110/121/121b to hb-2029 pages, `source:` strings, rationale prose), which the rubric calls mechanical. With the source text stating the reduction and no evidence offered that it was wrong, the pre-fix content was not wrong against the source; the removal is an interpretive/modeling choice (and an internally inconsistent one), not a demonstrated fidelity correction.
verdict.quote: -            - ks_pit_2026_state_local_income_tax_in_itemized_deductions
verdict.notes: Refutation of the kind is the stronger half and should stand regardless: the branch is traceable, so untraceable_branch does not fit. Facts for the reviewer: (1) the change is a real meaning change, not cosmetic — the input `ks_pit_2026_state_local_income_tax_in_itemized_deductions` disappears from the module's entire input surface (formula, the `>= 0` domain check, and the `SALT + depreciation <= sum of the four components` guard), and the companion test moves supported_deductions_and_exemptions 19480 -> 20980 and net liability 2173.616 -> 2089.916. (2) History: the term was present from the original encoding 8ba6de05e, removed here, and is still absent on main (no later revert re-adding it). (3) The best argument FOR the fix is interpretive — the (a)(5) base is only charitable / medical / qualified residence interest / real and personal property taxes, none of which contains state income taxes, so applying (b)'s income-tax reduction to that base is arguably a double disallowance. But that same argument applies equally to the depreciation half of the identical sentence (79-32,221/227/232/... depreciation is likewise not among the four components), and the fix kept that half, which is why I read the removal as unprincipled rather than source-grounded. (4) No K-40 / Schedule A instruction source could have grounded the removal: the module itself holds branches because "the tax-year-2026 Form K-40 and credit ordering instructions are not yet available." (5) If a reviewer disagrees with not_a_defect, the fallback is unclear, not confirmed-untraceable_branch; a reviewer might also flag the post-fix module as a new defect (unrepresented_clause: half of 79-32,120(b) is now unimplemented while still cited).

item.subject: Correct South Dakota source provenance

triage.commit_summary: The commit repoints the South Dakota 2026 resident income-tax module's citation of SDCL 10-43-2 from the non-existent leaf `us-sd/statute/10/43/2/block-1` to the real leaf `us-sd/statute/10/43/2/operative-text` (in the module's `source_verification.corpus_citation_paths` and in the proof atom of `sd_pit_2026_business_and_entity_taxes_outside_scope`), and un-swaps two human-readable rule-level `source:` provenance labels that had been attached to the wrong rules. It also bumps `.axiom/toolchain.toml`'s `axiom_corpus_ref` to a release that contains the corrected leaf and regenerates the encoding manifest and the reverse index accordingly; no formula, parameter, version, effective date, input, output, or scope changed.

modules.description_quote: Correct South Dakota source provenance
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module cited SDCL 10-43-2 through a corpus leaf id that does not exist (`us-sd/statute/10/43/2/block-1`) and carried two rule-level prose `source:` labels on the wrong rules, but the encoded meaning (the quoted excerpt, the boundary rule's `formula: false`, and both money rules' `formula: 0`) already matched the source and was unchanged by the fix.

item.subject: Fix Illinois resident tax profile review findings

triage.commit_summary: The commit applies review findings to the single Illinois TY2026 full-year-resident income-tax core module from PR 1074, re-basing the section 203 United States obligation subtraction on the section 203 modified total (so federally exempt obligation interest added back under paragraph (A) is subtractable), adding the federal qualifying-surviving-spouse branch to the exactly-one-filing-status guard, and adding an integrality guard on dependent count. It also pins two additional Public Act 104-0468 corpus pages, adds a proof atom grounding the existing pass-through-entity refundable-credit hold branch, rewrites the source-verification rationale, and adds three companion tests covering each behavioral change.

modules.description_quote: United States obligation income included in the section 203 modified total, including federal-tax-exempt amounts first added under paragraph (A).
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix subtraction term used il_pit_2026_federally_included_united_states_obligation_income, so US-obligation interest that is excluded from federal AGI but added back to Illinois base income under 35 ILCS 5/203(a)(2)(A) was never subtracted, although 203(a)(2)(N) deducts "all amounts included in such total which are exempt from taxation by this State ... by reason of the Constitution, treaties or statutes of the United States" and "such total" is the total after the paragraph (A) additions.
modules.triage_notes: Multi-fix commit on one module; the decisive fidelity change is the US-obligation subtraction base (input renamed to il_pit_2026_united_states_obligation_income_in_section_203_modified_total in both il_pit_2026_directly_encoded_subtractions and the input-domain guard). Provision was read: resolve_provision on us-il/statute/35/5/203-current/block-1 confirms the individual chain "and by deducting from the total so obtained the sum of the following amounts" with subparagraph (N) "An amount equal to all amounts included in such total which are exempt from taxation by this State either by reason of its statutes or Constitution or by reason of the Constitution, treaties or statutes of the United States", so the pre-fix 'federally included' restriction narrowed the statutory deduction. New companion test 'federal-tax-exempt United States obligation interest is added then subtracted' (500 added under (A), 500 subtracted, base income back to 10000) proves the behavior change, so this is not a rename-only edit. Two secondary changes ride along: (a) adding il_pit_2026_filing_status_qualifying_surviving_spouse as a fifth mutually exclusive branch in il_pit_2026_filing_status_is_valid, which previously fail-closed every federal qualifying-surviving-spouse filer out of the supported profile even though 35 ILCS 5/204 grants the exemption to such individuals - a separate defect best read as wrong_entity_or_scope (new test 'qualifying surviving spouse uses the supported nonjoint branch'); (b) adding il_pit_2026_dependent_count == floor(il_pit_2026_dependent_count) to the input-domain guard, which is input-domain hygiene rather than a clear source-disagreement (new test 'fractional dependent count fails closed'). Purely provenance/mechanical parts of the same commit: two added corpus_citation_paths (PA 104-0468 page-1290, page-1333), the rewritten upstream_source_check rationale, and a new proof atom on il_pit_2026_credit_source_hold_applies whose formula already contained il_pit_2026_has_pass_through_entity_refundable_credit (grounding only, no meaning change). Commit body is empty and PR 1074 records no reviews or review comments (its body describes an earlier corpus-pin correction, not these findings), so the only quotable description of the defect is the module's own rationale text in the diff; if the kind is contested, the runner-up for the decisive change is wrong_entity_or_scope (scope of the amounts eligible for the (N) subtraction).

verdict.justification: The subtraction rule il_pit_2026_directly_encoded_subtractions is proof-anchored to 35 ILCS 5/203(a)(2)(N), whose text I read through the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, provision us-il/statute/35/5/203-current/block-1): "(N) An amount equal to all amounts included in such total which are exempt from taxation by this State ... by reason of the Constitution, treaties or statutes of the United States", where "such total" is federal AGI after the (A)-(D-26) additions ("and by deducting from the total so obtained"). Pre-fix the term operated on an input whose name confined it to federally included amounts, while the module's own (A) addition input (il_pit_2026_federal_tax_exempt_interest_and_dividends_other_than_section_305_e_utility_stock_dividends) accepts federally excluded interest with no typed hold, so US-obligation interest excluded from federal AGI was added under (A) and never subtracted under (N) — part of the cited deduction was simply unrepresentable, overstating Illinois base income. The fix swaps the operand to il_pit_2026_united_states_obligation_income_in_section_203_modified_total and rewrites the rationale to say the input now covers "federal-tax-exempt amounts first added under paragraph (A)", which is the missing-clause coverage the source requires, so fidelity/unrepresented_clause fits.
verdict.quote:
-          + il_pit_2026_federally_included_united_states_obligation_income
+          + il_pit_2026_united_states_obligation_income_in_section_203_modified_total
verdict.notes: Refutation attempts and residual doubt, for the reviewer: (1) Mechanically this is an identifier rename plus prose — no operator, coefficient, parameter, version window, effective date, entity or output changed, the (N) proof-atom excerpt ("all amounts included in such total which are exempt from taxation by this State") is identical pre and post, and the companion test kept the same values (0 and 1000) under the new input name, so no computed test expectation moved. The meaning change lives entirely in the input's name/contract; the module has no separate inputs block (the identifier appears only twice in the pre file, lines 270 and 508), so the name is the only carrier of the input's semantics, and the rationale edit states the broadening explicitly. I judged that a meaning change rather than a cosmetic rename, but a reviewer applying "renames are mechanical" strictly could land on mechanical/unclear — this is the main reason I capped confidence at 0.7. (2) A "not_a_defect / disclosed scope" reading exists: the pre-fix rationale already said the encoded profile was "limited to ... federally included United States obligation income", and the module carries a caller-asserted hold il_pit_2026_has_other_section_203_addition_or_subtraction. I discounted it because the module claims to encode (N) itself, the matching (A) addition is accepted without a hold, and a caller would not naturally flag the (N) subtraction of its own (A)-added dollars as an "other" section 203 modification — so the pre-fix module could silently overstate base income for an in-domain filer. (3) The commit body is empty and the PR body (#1074) describes only a corpus-pin correction, so there is no review text naming this finding; the only textual support is the module rationale. (4) The same diff contains a cleaner, separately classifiable meaning change the first reader folded in via rule_names: il_pit_2026_filing_status_is_valid gains il_pit_2026_filing_status_qualifying_surviving_spouse as a fifth exclusive status (a filing status the encoding omitted — that one would be wrong_entity_or_scope), plus a new integrality constraint "and il_pit_2026_dependent_count == floor(il_pit_2026_dependent_count)" and a new PTE refundable-credit exception proof atom. If the corpus is being deduplicated per defect, consider splitting the filing-status change out as its own case.

item.subject: Harden benefit eligibility boundaries

triage.commit_summary: This repair commit on PR #1010's composition branch tightened the two eligibility pipelines that the two preceding commits had just composed: the Head Start Tribal (45 CFR 1302.12(e)) and Migrant/Seasonal (1302.12(f)) path rules gained the "pregnant woman or age-qualifying child" predicate that both paragraphs require through their "if they meet the requirements of paragraph (b) of this section" condition, and the WIC income test gained the mandatory 7 CFR 246.7(d)(2)(vii) unborn-child family-size adjustment plus explicit deferral declarations for (d)(2)(i) and (d)(2)(ix). Both pre-fix modules were fail-open on those source clauses — a tribal-service-area participant who met no paragraph-(b) age requirement still satisfied the Head Start path, and a pregnant applicant whose income exceeded 185 percent FPG for her unadjusted family size was denied income eligibility — and the companion test files added the matching negative and positive cases (e.g. WIC income 20000 vs limit 18500 now holds; dual-context tribal/migrant contamination negatives now fail).

modules.description_quote: Tribal + Migrant/Seasonal routes with dual-context contamination negatives
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Both special-population paths omitted the source's subject-and-age condition — 45 CFR 1302.12(e)(1) and (f) extend eligibility only to "pregnant women or children ... if they meet the requirements of paragraph (b) of this section" — so the pre-fix formulas (`tribal_service_area_participant_eligible` alone, and `migrant_or_seasonal_program and migrant_or_seasonal_participant_eligible`) fired for a participant who was neither a pregnant woman nor a child meeting any paragraph-(b) age requirement.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-cms-435-correction-immutable-scopes (us/regulation/45/1302/12): (e)(1) "a Tribal program may determine any pregnant women or children in the approved service area to be eligible for services regardless of income, if they meet the requirements of paragraph (b) of this section"; (f) "...and if they meet the requirements of paragraph (b) of this section." The pre-fix module summary already CLAIMED "the Tribal and Migrant or Seasonal paths with the paragraph-(b) age predicates" and the pre-fix proof atom quoted the (e)(1) sentence truncated just before the paragraph-(b) clause, so the encoding asserted a gate it did not implement. The module also carries an unused standalone rule participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b (defined at line 89, referenced nowhere pre- or post-fix); the fix inlined equivalent logic into the two path rules rather than consuming it. Companion test adds two negatives named migrant_age_fact_cannot_activate_tribal_path_in_dual_context and tribal_age_fact_cannot_activate_migrant_path_in_dual_context, which would have failed pre-fix — direct behavior evidence. Commit message is a bare generic subject ("Harden benefit eligibility boundaries", empty body), so the quote comes from the PR body; hence confidence 0.8 rather than higher. The diff changed nothing else in this module (only the two formulas and their supporting import proof atoms). Follow-up: de7bc07da "Fix Head Start eligibility boundaries" later repaired a separate defect flagged in MaxGhenis's blind-review comment on PR #1010 ("the Head Start public age bridge is wrong for ordinary and dual program contexts") — that is a different defect from this one and is NOT fixed here.

modules.description_quote: The paragraph-(d)(2)(vii) unborn-child adjustment is an explicit imported income path; the caller supplies its pregnancy, income-only failure, fetus-adjusted-guideline, and waiver facts.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: wic_income_eligible tested only adjunctive eligibility or `wic_family_income <= wic_income_limit`, omitting 7 CFR 246.7(d)(2)(vii), which mandates that a pregnant woman who fails the income guidelines "shall be considered to have satisfied the income guidelines" if they would be met by increasing her family size by the number of embryos or fetuses in utero, so pregnant applicants entitled to that adjustment were wrongly found income-ineligible.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us/regulation/7/246/7/d): "(vii) Income eligibility of pregnant women. A pregnant woman who is ineligible for participation in the program because she does not meet income guidelines shall be considered to have satisfied the income guidelines if the guidelines would be met by increasing the number of individuals in her family by the number of embryos or fetuses in utero... The State agency shall allow applicants to waive this increase in family size." Mandatory ("shall"), so its absence is a fidelity gap, not optional added scope. Companion test case pregnant_unborn_child_adjustment_overrides_direct_income_ceiling (income 20000, limit 18500) now expects wic_income_eligible: holds — pre-fix it would have been not_holds. The commit also added two deferred_outputs entries for (d)(2)(i) and (d)(2)(ix) plus rewordings of the module summary, the `source:` string, and two input descriptions; those are scope/provenance bookkeeping, and the decisive meaning change is the single `or pregnant_applicant_income_guidelines_satisfied_with_unborn_children` disjunct in wic_income_eligible. Note the new disjunct is ungated at the pipeline level in THIS commit (the imported rule carries its own applicant_is_pregnant input); the later commit 2cf80aa97 "Guard WIC pregnancy income adjustment" added the pipeline-level pregnant-woman gate, which is why the PR body's "gated to the pregnant-woman category" describes the post-review end state rather than this commit. The biggest WIC defect in MaxGhenis's blind-review comment — using 1.85 x FPG as the operative limit when 7 CFR 246.7(d)(1) makes the State agency's guideline operative — is NOT touched here; it was fixed later in fc95ef853 "Fix WIC State eligibility boundaries".

verdict.justification: The first reader's failure scenario is refuted by the composed semantics: pre-fix, both path rules consumed regulation outputs whose formulas are `tribal_program and participant_in_approved_service_area and participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b` and `at_least_one_family_member_income_comes_primarily_from_agricultural_employment and participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b`, and that bridge (defined in this same pipeline pre-fix) already required `participant_is_pregnant_woman or (participant_is_child and <an age requirement>)`, so a participant who was neither a pregnant woman nor an age-qualifying child could never fire either path. The clause "if they meet the requirements of paragraph (b) of this section" was therefore represented, not absent; what was wrong is that the bridge ORs the three program-context branches, so in a dual-context program (tribal_program and migrant_or_seasonal_program both true) the Migrant/Seasonal age branch satisfied the Tribal route and the Early Head Start age branch satisfied the Migrant route — the wrong branch firing, which the fix closes by pinning each route to its own context's age predicate. The companion tests added in the same commit are named exactly that (`migrant_age_fact_cannot_activate_tribal_path_in_dual_context`, `tribal_age_fact_cannot_activate_migrant_path_in_dual_context`) and only the dual-context case changes any terminal output (`early_head_start_eligible` flips holds → not_holds). It is a genuine fidelity correction against 45 CFR 1302.12(b)(3)/(f), but the kind is a mis-combined boolean route gate, not an unrepresented clause.

verdict.notes: Key files: diff /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/diffs/us/044fe328f2/000.diff; pre-fix module `git -C /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us show 2343854f88:us/policies/hhs/head_start/eligibility_pipeline.yaml`; the shared bridge is the pipeline rule `participant_meets_age_requirements_under_paragraph_b` (pre-fix lines ~126-150), whose formula is `(tribal_program and (pregnant or (child and (EHS or HS-preschool age)))) or (migrant_or_seasonal_program and (pregnant or (child and MSHS age)))`, and it feeds the undeclared name of the same spelling inside us/regulations/45-cfr/1302/12.yaml (that module has no inputs: section; the new tests confirm the binding by asserting `#tribal_service_area_participant_eligible: holds` without supplying the age fact). Reachability: in a pure tribal or pure migrant context the pre-fix formulas are already equivalent to the post-fix ones, so the only defective inputs are dual-context ones. The migrant-route hardening is squarely source-grounded ((f) plus (b)(3) "For Migrant or Seasonal Head Start, a child must be younger than compulsory school age"); the tribal-route hardening (requiring (b)(1)/(b)(2) even when the same program is Migrant/Seasonal) is a defensible but less clearly compelled reading of (e)(1), and it changes no terminal output — only the intermediate `head_start_tribal_service_area_path_satisfied` / `head_start_participation_path_satisfied` outputs. Runner-up kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (a route accepting the other program scope's age requirement); unrepresented_clause is the weakest fit because the paragraph-(b) condition and the pregnant-woman/child subject predicate were both already in the composed pre-fix logic. The first reader's cited quote ("Tribal + Migrant/Seasonal routes with dual-context contamination negatives") is verbatim PR-body text, but it describes the original composition PR's test coverage, not this hardening commit; the PR review comment's Head Start finding is about the "public age bridge" and participation outputs, which is consistent with the contamination reading.

verdict.justification: The diff changes encoded meaning in exactly the way described: `wic_income_eligible`'s formula gains a third disjunct importing `pregnant_applicant_income_guidelines_satisfied_with_unborn_children`, and the rule's `source:` line is extended to add `(d)(2)(vii)`. The pinned release text of 7 CFR 246.7(d)(2)(vii) is mandatory ("A pregnant woman who is ineligible ... shall be considered to have satisfied the income guidelines if the guidelines would be met by increasing the number of individuals in her family by the number of embryos or fetuses in utero"), and the target rule already existed in the encoded source module `us/regulations/7-cfr/246/7/d.yaml` at the parent commit — the pipeline neither imported it nor listed it under `deferred_outputs` (only the (e) nutritional-risk output was deferred pre-fix), so this is an omitted mandatory clause, not scope the module disclaimed or new coverage it never claimed. item.subject: Clarify Alabama 2026 amendment source hold

triage.commit_summary: The commit repairs the Alabama tax-year-2026 full-year-resident income-tax source-hold module by adding a dedicated typed hold rule, al_pit_2026_october_amendments_source_hold_applies, grounded in the pinned 40-18-15 and 40-18-19 pages' notices that Acts 2026-604 and 2026-603 amend those sections effective October 1, 2026 with revised language available only in the (absent) Acts. modules.description_quote: the pinned 40-18-15 and 40-18-19 pages identify Acts 2026-604 and 2026-603 as effective October 1, 2026 without supplying the revised operative text; that full-year authority gap is modeled by a dedicated typed hold and propagated through the chain

(Amended by Act 2026-604) AMENDED BY ACT 2026-604, EFFECTIVE OCTOBER 1, 2026. SEE ACT FOR REVISED LANGUAGE."; 40-18-19 header carries the identical notice for Act 2026-603. This commit is a repair round inside merged PR #1045, whose body names the repaired item as "the unmodeled October 2026 amendments". No PR reviews or review comments exist in the bundle; the two issue comments are the author's own refresh/CI notes and do not discuss this defect.

verdict.justification: The first reader's premise fails on the pre-fix file: `al_pit_2026_income_base_source_hold_applies` is `formula: true` (unchanged in both revisions, versions[0], 2026-01-01..2026-12-31), and the pre-fix deduction/exemption hold was exactly `formula: al_pit_2026_income_base_source_hold_applies`, so the deduction/exemption, tax/surtax and complete-liability holds were already unconditionally true for the entire 2026 year and every downstream Money stage was already a fail-closed zero sentinel — the module never asserted the full-year deduction/exemption coverage the reading attributes to it. The added `or al_pit_2026_october_amendments_source_hold_applies` disjuncts are therefore logically inert (true or true), which the companion test confirms: the only test change is one added expectation line for the new rule, and every pre-existing hold expectation stays `holds` with no Money value touched. Nothing in the diff changes an effective_from, effective_to, period kind or version window (14 identical 2026-01-01/2026-12-31 windows become 15, the extra one belonging to the new always-true rule), so `wrong_period_or_effective_date` has no textual support at all. What actually changed is the module-level `source_verification.rationale`, the `deferred_outputs` reasons, two `source:` description strings, and a newly named typed hold that attributes an already-active hold to a second, independently real source gap — added traceability the module never previously claimed to compute, not a correction of encoded meaning.

-        formula: al_pit_2026_income_base_source_hold_applies
+        formula: |-
+          al_pit_2026_income_base_source_hold_applies
+          or al_pit_2026_october_amendments_source_hold_applies
verdict.notes: Evidence trail for a reviewer: (1) pre-fix parent 69a966bc08 and post 5ab50dfa39 both contain `al_pit_2026_income_base_source_hold_applies` with `formula: true` and a single version window `effective_from: '2026-01-01'` / `effective_to: '2026-12-31'`; the diff does not touch that rule, so all three ORed holds evaluate identically before and after. (2) `git show --stat` on the commit: module +80/-27 lines, test file exactly one added line (`...#al_pit_2026_october_amendments_source_hold_applies: holds`); no existing expectation flipped, no Money sentinel changed. (3) The new proof-atom excerpts are genuine, not fabricated: the pinned corpus release `us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix` text for us-al/statute/40-18-15 contains verbatim "AMENDED BY ACT 2026-604, EFFECTIVE OCTOBER 1, 2026. SEE ACT FOR REVISED LANGUAGE." So the amendment gap is real — it just was not being mis-encoded before, because everything downstream was already held closed. (4) The quoted PR-body sentence the first reader relied on is PR #1045's description of the whole new module's design (PR title: "Add Alabama 2026 resident income-tax source-hold surface"), not a statement that this intermediate commit repaired a wrong year window; the PR narrates it as a review repair of an "unmodeled" amendment, i.e. an unattributed reason for an existing hold.
