item.subject: Repair Oregon 2026 resident income tax core

triage.commit_summary: This is the second commit of PR #1038 (TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us), a repair round on the Oregon tax-year-2026 full-year-resident income-tax core that had just been encoded in parent dc9e9924: it re-grounds the module on the operative chaptered 2026 session laws (SB 1507, HB 4084, SB 1510), raising the refundable Oregon EITC from 9%/12% to 14%/17%, adding the SB 1507 passenger-vehicle-loan-interest, section 1202 and bonus-depreciation additions, encoding the ORS 316.698 film labor rebate directly, and deleting the ORS 316.078 dependent-care, 316.079 limb-loss and 316.087 elderly/disabled credits that the encoder had allowed for 2026 despite their post-2015 claim bar. It also adds an input-domain validity guard, new source holds for the certified new-jobs credit, the SB 1510 pass-through-entity member credit and dependent exemptions, splits the ORS 316.792 military-pay subtraction into per-service-member $6,000 caps for taxpayer and spouse, and adds the ORS 316.695 rule zeroing the standard deduction for a married-separate filer whose spouse itemizes.

modules.description_quote: The official chaptered 2026 SB 1507 supplies the operative passenger-vehicle-interest, qualified-small-business-stock, bonus-depreciation, earned-income-credit, and new-jobs provisions.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module encoded a tax-year-2026 version window (2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31) carrying the superseded pre-amendment ORS 315.266 rates of 9% and 12%, although Oregon Laws 2026 chapter 142 section 3 (SB 1507) amended those rates to 14% and 17% and section 10 makes that amendment apply to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026; the same wrong-vintage grounding also let the module allow the ORS 316.078, 316.079 and 316.087 credits for 2026.
modules.triage_notes: Multi-defect repair round; this is commit 2 of 4 in PR #1038 and the module file changed in only these two commits (dc9e9924 encode, c8e871b0 repair). The PR body's 'Review-fix cycle' paragraph ('The repair gates EITC on the bounded profile...') describes the LATER commit 2e82126b ('Fail close Oregon 2026 held tax outputs'), not this one - this commit moves the public EITC gate the other way, from `if or_pit_2026_bounded_profile_applies` to `if or_pit_2026_is_full_year_resident and or_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid`, and the next commit reverses that. So the PR text is NOT evidence for this commit; the only quotable prose is the module's own summary/rationale added in the diff. Provision read: yes. Resolved us-or/statute/session-laws/2026/sb1507/document-1 through the pinned corpus - SECTION 3 reads 'an amount equal to [nine] 14 percent of the earned income credit allowable' and '[12] 17 percent', and SECTION 10 reads 'the amendments to ORS 315.266 by sec-tion 3 of this 2026 Act apply to tax years begin-ning on or after January 1, 2026', so the 9%/12% pre-fix values are confirmed superseded for the encoded period. Also resolved us-or/statute/316.078, 316.079, 316.087: their section bodies in the pinned release (release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix) contain the 30%/15%/8%/6%/5%/4% dependent-care table, the '$50 credit' and the '40 percent of the credit for the elderly', and contain NO sunset note - so the module's added claim 'Credits under ORS 316.078, 316.079, and 316.087 are excluded because their statutory notes prohibit claims for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2016.' rests on statutory notes not retrievable through the resolver; a reviewer should confirm that bar independently before using this as the anchor. Other real fidelity defects bundled in the same diff, any of which could be split out as separate corpus items: (a) unrepresented_clause - ORS 316.695's 'standard deduction referred to in subparagraph (A) of this paragraph shall be zero' for a married-separate filer whose spouse itemizes was missing and is added to rules[or_pit_2026_profile_candidate_standard_deduction] and [..._additional_standard_deduction]; (b) unrepresented_clause - the SB 1507 sections 2, 5, 7/9 additions (qualified passenger-vehicle loan interest, section 1202 excluded gain, section 168(k) bonus-depreciation difference) added to or_pit_2026_profile_candidate_supported_additions, and ORS 316.698 film labor rebate moved from a hold to a direct subtraction; (c) wrong_entity_or_scope - the ORS 316.792 military subtraction was one household-level cap over pooled 'specifically qualified' pay and is rewritten as separate taxpayer and spouse computations each with its own $6,000 other-pay cap (spouse leg only on a joint return); (d) wrong_entity_or_scope/unrepresented_clause - the personal exemption credit stops using the federal section 151 exemption count and derives 1 or 2 units from filing status, with dependents moved to a new hold. Provenance-only (mechanical) parts of the same diff: or_pit_2026_personal_exemption_single_agi_limit and _joint_agi_limit keep formulas 100000/200000 while only source and proof excerpt move from ORS 316.085 to the 2026 OR-ESTIMATE; or_pit_2026_profile_candidate_basic_standard_deduction gains a proof atom with no formula change. Companion test file grew by ~6300 lines and oracle-coverage-pending dropped the nine dependent-care/disability legal_ids (ceiling 2237 -> 2230), consistent with the module change. Confidence is 0.6 because the fidelity classification is near-certain but the single 'kind' is genuinely mixed: the EITC anchor could equally be labeled amount_mismatch (0.09 -> 0.14, 0.12 -> 0.17) rather than wrong_period_or_effective_date, since the effective_from/effective_to window itself was already correct and only the source vintage inside it was wrong.

verdict.justification: The change at the anchored path is a real fidelity correction, but not a period/date one: the version window is byte-identical before and after (`effective_from: '2026-01-01', effective_to: '2026-12-31'`) and only the rate literal moves, 0.09 → 0.14 (and 0.12 → 0.17 on the companion young-dependent rule). I checked every `effective_from`/`effective_to`/`period:` line in the 874-line diff: not one date, window, or period kind value is changed anywhere in the module — the `+/-` window lines are only whole-rule insertions and deletions, all carrying the same 2026-01-01→2026-12-31 window. Reading SB 1507 through the pinned release (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, commit d9d6fba0b9) confirms section 3 amends ORS 315.266(1)(a) to read "[nine] 14 percent" and (1)(b) to "[12] 17 percent", and section 10(1) makes it apply to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026 — so the pre-fix encoding was wrong against the operative source, but the way it was wrong is a superseded numeric rate, which the taxonomy calls amount_mismatch. The added `kind: effective_period` proof atom is provenance for the already-correct window, not a date correction.
verdict.quote:
-    versions: [{effective_from: '2026-01-01', effective_to: '2026-12-31', formula: '0.09'}]
+    versions: [{effective_from: '2026-01-01', effective_to: '2026-12-31', formula: '0.14'}]
verdict.notes:
Source check (read this session, not recalled): SB 1507 text via resolve_provision on us-or/statute/session-laws/2026/sb1507/document-1 at rulespec commit c8e871b0fe — "SECTION 3. ORS 315.266 is amended to read: 315.266. (1)(a) ... an amount equal to [nine] 14 percent of the earned income credit allowable"; "(b) ... equal to [12] 17 percent"; "SECTION 10. (1) Sections 2 and 5 of this 2026 Act and the amendments to ORS 315.266 by section 3 of this 2026 Act apply to tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2026." So fidelity (not mechanical, not an enhancement) is solid; only the kind is wrong.

The first reader's quote came from the module-level `rationale:` comment, not from the anchored rule, which is likely what pulled it toward a period reading. If a "wrong vintage of the source" framing is preferred over the plain numeric one, the better alternative kind is untraceable_branch ("formulas grounded on the wrong provision") — the rule was grounded on the pre-amendment ORS 315.266 in the pinned 2025 ORS snapshot. I still prefer amount_mismatch because the anchored path is `versions[0].formula` holding a bare numeric literal whose value changed; a citation-only swap with 0.09 retained would have been mechanical provenance.

This commit bundles several independent fidelity defects beyond the anchored one; a reviewer may want to split them into separate cases rather than let this one case absorb them:
- Removal of the ORS 316.078 dependent-care table, 316.079 $50 limb-loss credit, and the 316.087 40% elderly/disabled rate, with the summary line "Credits under ORS 316.078, 316.079, and 316.087 are excluded because their statutory notes prohibit claims for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2016." That sub-defect IS period-flavored (a sunset the encoding ignored) and is the closest thing in this commit to wrong_period_or_effective_date, though the fix deletes the rules outright, which also reads as untraceable_branch. It is not the rule the case is anchored to.
- Military subtraction re-scoped from a single household aggregate to per-spouse caps with a joint-only spouse leg (wrong_entity_or_scope).
- Standard deduction and additional standard deduction now forced to 0 when married-separate and the spouse itemizes (unrepresented_clause, ORS 316.695).
- EITC gate changed from `or_pit_2026_bounded_profile_applies` to `or_pit_2026_is_full_year_resident and or_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid`, plus a new `or_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid` guard and three new source holds folded into the bounded profile — scope/logic changes, not amounts.

Read-only throughout: only `cat`, `sed`, `grep` on the diff bundle and the resolve_provision script; nothing in rulespec-us or the corpus was modified.

The commit subject "Complete New Jersey credit boundary coverage" refers to the companion test file, which gains 99 lines and removes 0 (numstat 99/0): new boundary cases cdcc_and_child_credit_exact_30000, cdcc_and_child_credit_immediately_above_30000, child_credit_exact_40000, cdcc_exact_90000, one added selector assertion on an existing case, and ~36 direct parameter-value assertions. No existing expected output was modified, so the module's behavior is unchanged by this commit. The third file, .axiom/encoding-manifests/.../2026_resident_ordinary_core.json, is pure signing bookkeeping (sha256s, generated_at, HMAC signature, nested supersedes chain; "manual_exception": "repair"). The PR body carries no reviews, review_comments, or issue_comments in the bundle, and the commit body is empty, so the PR summary is the only stated reason. I did not run resolve_provision.py: the classification does not depend on what any NJ provision says, since no encoded meaning changed. Note for corpus use: this commit is a poor fidelity-judge item -- the interesting content (the credit boundary cases) is entirely in the .test.yaml, and the module change is provenance/formatting only.

item.subject: Repair New Jersey 2026 resident income tax core

triage.commit_summary: This commit applies the independent-review repair round to the New Jersey TY2026 full-year-resident ordinary income tax core added in PR #1036, rewriting the single module's gross-income, deduction, property-benefit, and credit rules. It removes branches whose encoded meaning did not match Title 54A (gross gambling winnings with no N.J.S.54A:6-11 lottery exclusion or same-year wagering-loss netting, caller-completed exempt-interest/qualified-fund/alimony/medical classifications, and a caller-completed homestead ownership share), encodes the clauses the statute states (54A:3-3(c) medical disallowances, 54A:3A-17(c)/(d) title-interest and MFS half shares, 54A:3A-20(b) half credit, 54A:4-17(c) CDCC married-living-apart exception, 54A:4-17.1 joint-return requirement), and adds the 54A:11-3/11-4 State shared responsibility tax as an explicit typed hold and deferred output so the net output is an income-tax-only candidate.

modules.description_quote: Independent review required repairs for gambling/lottery losses and thresholds, valid MFS credit/property paths, caller-completed legal-result inputs, the shared-responsibility boundary, blanket-oracle claims, material threshold coverage, service/housing overlap, direct credit assertions, and malformed YAML descriptions.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Inside the profile it claimed to support, the module added raw `nj_pit_2026_gambling_winnings` straight into New Jersey gross income with no representation of N.J.S.54A:6-11 (which excludes New Jersey Lottery winnings except from a single prize exceeding $10,000) and no within-category offset of same-year wagering losses that 54A:5-2 permits, so a resident with, say, a $5,000 New Jersey Lottery prize was taxed on an amount the statute excludes from gross income.
modules.triage_notes: Read the provisions through the pinned corpus: 54A:6-11 is verbatim "Gross income shall not include lottery winnings from the New Jersey Lottery, except that New Jersey Lottery winnings from a prize in an amount exceeding $10,000 shall be included in gross income"; 54A:5-1(g) is bare "Gambling winnings" and 54A:5-2 allows within-category loss offsets; 54A:3-3(c) lists the three disallowances (household/dependent care, excluded MSA distributions, self-employed health insurance) the fix now encodes; 54A:3A-17(c)/(d) give the title-interest proportion and the MFS tenants-by-entirety one-half share; 54A:4-17(c) reads "Married couples shall file a joint return in order to claim the credit" with the section 21(e)(3)/(4) exception the fix adds. Pre-fix citation list did not even contain 54a:6-11, 54a:11-3, or 54a:11-4. This is a multi-defect repair round and one kind had to be chosen: unrepresented_clause covers the largest group (missing lottery exclusion and loss netting, missing 54A:3-3(c) disallowances, missing MFS half-share and title-interest proportion, missing CDCC married-living-apart exception, missing 54A:4-17.1 joint-return bar). Two other findings arguably fall elsewhere: the new `nj_pit_2026_service_remuneration_excludes_employer_housing_value` guard fixes a double-count (employer-furnished housing was both inside total service remuneration and added again as its own gross-income term), and the new 54A:11-3/11-4 typed hold plus `nj_pit_2026_total_return_tax_liability` deferred output is a wrong_entity_or_scope-style correction (the net output was presented as a return-level candidate without the separate State shared responsibility tax). Note the remedy for gambling/alimony/exempt-interest/qualified-fund facts is removal plus a typed hold rather than encoding the clause, so the post-fix module is narrower; the pre-fix defect is still real because those facts were inside the claimed supported profile and produced a wrong number. The commit body is empty, so the quote is from the PR body. The five-way split of `nj_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid` into filing/income/deferred-income/deduction/property sub-rules is structural, not itself a defect. Follow-up commit 15f982991 "Complete New Jersey credit boundary coverage" in the same PR also touches this file; the PR records the final reviewed head as 15f982991ad36e24a6472d1a03c9ce0a640d5d4c. PR has no review or comment records in the bundle (reviews/review_comments/issue_comments all empty), so the findings list in the PR body is the only reviewer evidence.

verdict.justification: The refutation attempts fail: the pre-fix formula really did add the input `nj_pit_2026_gambling_winnings` (declared as "Gross gambling winnings in the supported profile") straight into `nj_pit_2026_profile_candidate_gross_income`, its only exception proof atom was 54A:6-14 (interest on obligations), and 54A:6-11 appeared in the pre-fix header only under `upstream_source_check.checked_paths`, never in `corpus_citation_paths` or any rule — so the exclusion was demonstrably unrepresented, and the pre-fix `supported_profile_applies` gate contained no gambling or lottery condition. Read through the pinned release, 54A:6-11 says "Gross income shall not include lottery winnings from the New Jersey Lottery, except that New Jersey Lottery winnings from a prize in an amount exceeding $10,000 shall be included in gross income", and 54A:5-2 permits same-category offsets, while 54A:5-1(g) makes "Gambling winnings" a category of its own — so gross receipts with no exclusion and no same-year wagering-loss offset overstated gross income against the source. The one real counter-argument, that the pre-fix caller flag `nj_pit_2026_has_specialty_income_exclusion_or_deduction` ("any unencoded Title 54A chapter 3 or 6 specialty exclusion or deduction") might already have held lottery cases, does not survive: it is a caller-completed legal conclusion the module's own header disclaims, it is limited to chapters 3 and 6 so it cannot reach the chapter-5 loss netting, and no wagering-loss input existed at all. The kind holds because the term removed is grounded in 54A:5-1(g) (so not untraceable) and the repair adds the missing exception's machinery — the `nj_pit_2026_new_jersey_lottery_prize_exclusion_limit` parameter at 10000 with the 54A:6-11 excerpt, a per-prize judgment input, and a gross-receipts/losses split.
verdict.quote: -          + nj_pit_2026_gambling_winnings
verdict.notes: Decisive evidence spans three places in the diff: the removal `-          + nj_pit_2026_gambling_winnings` from rules[nj_pit_2026_profile_candidate_gross_income].versions[0].formula; the new parameter `+  - name: nj_pit_2026_new_jersey_lottery_prize_exclusion_limit` with `+      - {effective_from: '2026-01-01', effective_to: '2026-12-31', formula: '10000'}` and excerpt "New Jersey Lottery winnings from a prize in an amount exceeding $10,000 shall be included in gross income"; and the new gate line `+          and not nj_pit_2026_has_gambling_or_new_jersey_lottery_activity` in nj_pit_2026_no_deferred_income_branch_applies. Two caveats for a reviewer. (1) The remedy is a typed hold (deferral) plus a threshold parameter rather than encoding the exclusion arithmetic, so a reviewer who reads "the fix adds it" strictly could prefer wrong_entity_or_scope (the supported population was re-scoped); I judge unrepresented_clause better because the pre-fix output disagreed with 54A:6-11/54A:5-2 for taxpayers the module claimed to support, and the fix does add representation of the $10,000 boundary. (2) This commit is a bundle: the same formula also lost `- nj_pit_2026_exempt_us_or_nj_obligation_interest`, `- nj_pit_2026_exempt_qualified_investment_fund_dividends`, and `+ nj_pit_2026_alimony_received` (removal of caller-completed legal classifications), and the commit separately repairs MFS property/credit halving (new nj_pit_2026_mfs_property_benefit_share = 0.5 citing "shall each be entitled to one-half of the deduction"), medical-expense disallowances (new nj_pit_2026_profile_candidate_allowable_medical_expenses), and the 54A:11-3 shared-responsibility-tax boundary. If the corpus wants one defect per module change, this file supports several distinct fidelity entries; the gambling/lottery one is the best evidenced. Statutes read through the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix (corpus commit 01e00777cb), fix_time_corpus_match=same_body. Incidental tooling note: two sequential `git show` redirects chained with && into the scratchpad produced truncated/mixed files on the first attempt; re-running each show separately gave the correct 1654-line pre-image.

item.subject: Repair Hawaii resident liability contract

triage.commit_summary: This is the first repair round on the Hawaii TY2026 full-year-resident income tax pipeline (created one commit earlier in PR #1035), fixing a batch of independent review findings in the single module file plus its companion tests, manifest, reverse index, and oracle-pending ledger. It adds the previously unrepresented HRS 235-53 Director-prescribed tax-table substitution (as a new ceiling parameter, a source-hold judgment, a waiver, and a new supported-profile gate), corrects the CDCC dollar-limit/section-129 exclusion ordering and the surviving-spouse earned-income limitation, adds the 235-55.7(d) pro-rata rent test, derives the food/renter qualified-exemption counts and CDCC qualifying-individual count from raw facts instead of caller-completed legal conclusions, converts the Hawaii capital-gain adjustment and Form N-158 amounts into typed holds, makes the supported-profile net liability signed, and opens married-filing-separately as a supported filing status.

modules.description_quote: HRS §235-53 requires the Director-prescribed tax table for nonitemizers up to a Director-determined ceiling that is not less than $20,000.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module never represented HRS 235-53, so it published section 235-51 schedule tax for every nonitemizer, including those whose taxable income does not exceed the Director's ceiling (statutorily at least $20,000), for whom the statute imposes the Director-prescribed table tax "in lieu of the tax imposed by section 235-51".
modules.triage_notes: Read the provisions through the pinned corpus: us-hi/statute/235-53 (confirms "In lieu of the tax imposed by section 235-51" for nonitemizers whose taxable income "does not exceed the ceiling amount", ceiling "not less than $20,000"), us-hi/statute/235-55.7 (confirms (d) "If a rental unit is occupied by two or more individuals, and more than one individual is able to qualify as a claimant, the claim for credit shall be based upon a pro rata share of the rent paid"), and us-hi/statute/235-55.6 (confirms (c) the dollar limit "shall be reduced by the aggregate amount excludable from gross income under section 129", and (d)(1)(A)/(B) earned-income limit keyed to being married at the close of the year). This is a MULTI-DEFECT single-module commit; I picked the 235-53 hold as decisive because the PR body devotes its whole "Source boundary" section to it and the diff adds the citation path, the $20,000 ceiling parameter, the hold judgment, the waiver entry, and the profile gate. Other independent fidelity corrections in the same diff, any of which a reviewer could split out: (1) hi_pit_2026_cdcc_creditable_expenses changed from max(0, min(expenses, cap) - assistance_exclusion) to min(expenses, max(0, cap - assistance_exclusion), earned-income limit) — the pre-fix form reduced the expenses rather than the 235-55.6(c) dollar limit and understated the credit whenever expenses were below the cap (amount_mismatch); (2) the same rule's earned-income limit now applies the two-earner minimum only when joint AND not a surviving spouse, since a surviving spouse is not married at the close of the year under 235-55.6(d)(1) (wrong_entity_or_scope); (3) hi_pit_2026_refundable_low_income_renter_credit now divides cash rent by the qualified-claimant count before the $1,000 test, encoding 235-55.7(d), which was absent (unrepresented_clause); (4) hi_pit_2026_capital_gains_worksheet_line_10 dropped the Hawaii long/short-term gain adjustments and the Form N-158 line 4e subtraction, which had been caller-completed amounts with no in-module grounding, replacing them with boolean holds (untraceable_branch / completed-result inputs); (5) hi_pit_2026_supported_profile_net_income_tax_liability dropped the max(0, ...) floor so refundable credits can drive liability negative — note the pre-fix module did publish a separate refundable-excess output (now made private), so the floor was arguably a presentation choice rather than lost information; (6) new domain bound age_65_exemption_count <= 2 from 235-54(a). Changes that are NOT defects: married-filing-separately moved from a hold to a supported filing status (added scope, plus the matching filing-status exclusivity logic), the decomposition of composite caller judgments into granular raw facts (CDCC conditions, EITC status/dependents match, renter occupancy/property-tax conditions, food/renter exemption presence-failure counts), and the new public hi_pit_2026_supported_profile_tax_after_nonrefundable_credits stage. Follow-ups in the same PR: 26ebd1a18 "Tighten Hawaii tax-table and MFS holds" later REMOVED the `taxable_income <= ceiling` condition from hi_pit_2026_tax_table_source_hold_applies (because only the statutory minimum of the Director's ceiling is known, so all nonitemizers must fail closed) and moved the hold out of supported_profile_applies into the public tax/liability stages, and also re-held MFS food/renter claims; 249e8e6f6 "Prevent Hawaii food credit child overlap" followed. So this commit's 235-53 fix was correct in kind but too narrow, and was widened one commit later. Commit message body is empty; the PR body is the whole-PR body, which is why confidence is 0.75 rather than higher.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute the label and could not: the pre-fix file at e97d5848 contains no mention of "235-53" or any tax table (verified by grep over the full 2261-line pre file), yet its supported profile already required `not hi_pit_2026_elects_itemized_deductions`, so every publicly published taxpayer was a nonitemizer and the public `hi_pit_2026_supported_profile_tax_before_credits` returned the §235-51 schedule/alt-tax `hi_pit_2026_income_tax_liability` for all of them. The pinned corpus text of HRS 235-53(a)(1) reads "In lieu of the tax imposed by section 235-51, there is hereby imposed ... (A) Who does not itemize ... and (B) Whose taxable income for such taxable year does not exceed the ceiling amount, a tax determined under tables ... prescribed by the director", with (a)(2) fixing the ceiling at "the amount (not less than $20,000) determined by the director" — a mandatory substitution, not an election, so the pre-fix published amount disagrees with the source for that population. The fix adds the missing clause (new §235-53 citation path, `hi_pit_2026_statutory_minimum_tax_table_ceiling` = 20000, the `hi_pit_2026_tax_table_source_hold_applies` condition, and the gate in `supported_profile_applies`), which is exactly unrepresented_clause; "mechanical" and "not_a_defect" both fail because formulas, inputs, outputs and the profile gate all changed and the module previously claimed this population rather than disclaiming it.
verdict.quote: +          and not hi_pit_2026_tax_table_source_hold_applies
verdict.notes: Cross-checks a reviewer should know. (1) Boundary strictness of the new hold is right, not a second defect: the statute says "does not exceed the ceiling amount" and the added rule uses `hi_pit_2026_taxable_income <= hi_pit_2026_statutory_minimum_tax_table_ceiling`. But the ceiling parameter is pinned at the statutory *minimum* ($20,000) while §235-53(a)(2) lets the director set any amount "not less than $20,000"; taxpayers between $20,000 and the director's actual ceiling are therefore still published under §235-51, so the fix only partially represents the clause — a residual, not a reason to downgrade the label. (2) This is a multi-defect repair commit, so the corpus entry is not one-defect-per-module-change. Other independent fidelity fixes in the same diff, each a different kind: capital-gain worksheet line 10 drops the Hawaii long/short-term adjustments and the `- hi_pit_2026_form_n_158_line_4e` subtraction (re-grounding, untraceable_branch); `hi_pit_2026_supported_profile_net_income_tax_liability` loses its `max(0, ...)` floor so the signed liability can go negative (boundary/polarity); CDCC creditable expenses re-nest min/max so the assistance exclusion no longer reduces the already-capped expense (polarity_or_logic); the renter credit gains the statutory "pro rata share of the rent paid" divisor (another unrepresented_clause); MFS is added to the supported scope by deleting `and not hi_pit_2026_is_married_filing_separately` (wrong_entity_or_scope); and a new age-65 exemption cap of 2 bounds the input domain (amount/domain). If the corpus wants a single canonical kind per entry, the §235-53 hold is a defensible pick (it is the PR body's headline "Source boundary" and matches the supplied rule_path), but the entry should be flagged as bundled. (3) Provenance caveat: commit a8ca13eee7 is an intra-PR repair inside PR #1035 "Add Hawaii 2026 resident tax bounded core" (merged 2026-07-24), so the defective state existed only on the unmerged branch and was caught by the review-fix cycle — never in merged rulespec-us content. If the corpus is meant to hold defects that reached main, this case is branch-internal. (4) Weakest alternative kind considered: untraceable_branch ("formulas grounded on the wrong provision"), on the theory that nonitemizer tax was grounded on §235-51 instead of §235-53. I rejected it because the §235-51 branch is genuinely grounded and is left intact for its correct population; nothing is removed or re-grounded, a condition is added. wrong_entity_or_scope is the second-best alternative (the published population was too broad), but scope narrowing is the remedy here, not the defect.

item.subject: Repair North Dakota 2026 annual tax source holds

triage.commit_summary: This is the single repair commit on PR #1034 ("Add North Dakota 2026 resident tax bounded core"), applied to the initial encode 49059168a after an independent review found that the module published annual North Dakota income tax computed from the continuous 2026 ND-1ES estimated-payment schedule even though N.D.C.C. 57-38-30.3(10) makes the Commissioner's prescribed annual tax table controlling and no 2026 annual table is pinned. It demotes the ND-1ES computation to a private diagnostic and forces every public annual-tax output to fail closed (new constant-false `nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies` plus a `nd_pit_2026_annual_tax_table_authority_is_complete` hold), and in the same pass repairs the subsection 2(d)(1) capital-gain sequencing, removes the single-annual-cap organ-donation reduction and the planned-gift addback in favor of typed holds, and removes the other-state-credit chain pending Schedule ND-1CR.

modules.description_quote: Section 57-38-30.3(10) requires the prescribed annual tax table, and the latest annual instructions use tables below $100,000 rather than the continuous estimated-payment schedule.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module published a public annual North Dakota tax (e.g. 3916.0875, 1638, 1958.2875 in its own companion tests) computed from the continuous 2026 ND-1ES estimated-payment schedule, which is not the annual tax the cited statute requires because 57-38-30.3(10) provides that any tax tables prescribed by the commissioner "must be followed by every individual, estate, or trust determining a tax under this section" and no 2026 annual table is in the pinned corpus.
modules.triage_notes: Multi-defect repair in one module; I chose the annual-table substitution as decisive because it matches the commit subject ("Repair North Dakota 2026 annual tax source holds") and it is the change that flips every public money output. Mechanics of the fix: the old profile gate was renamed `nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies` -> `nd_pit_2026_base_profile_applies` (still gating the upstream income outputs) and a NEW `nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies` with formula 'false' was added, so `nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_tax_before_credits` and `nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_candidate_tax_after_nonrefundable_credits` now return 0 in all 22 companion cases (verified by diffing the .test.yaml expectations across 49059168a..34c7fec48b); `nd_pit_2026_profile_candidate_tax_before_credits`'s source string was re-grounded from "N.D.C.C. section 57-38-30.3(1), applicable official 2026 schedule" to "Private reference calculation from the official 2026 estimated-tax schedule". Note the rate parameters themselves were NOT changed and their values (49575/250400/3916.09, 82800/304850/4329.98, 41400/152425/2164.99, 66400/277600/4118.40) match the schedules in the pinned 57-38-30.3(1)(a)-(d) verbatim, so this is not amount_mismatch; the defect is that a continuous-schedule result was published as annual liability when the statute subordinates it to the unpinned prescribed table. A reviewer could reasonably re-label this one unrepresented_clause instead, since the fix literally adds a rule representing subsection (10) (excerpt "tax commissioner may prescribe tax tables") -- that ambiguity is why confidence is 0.72 rather than higher. THREE further independent fidelity repairs ride in the same module diff and may be worth splitting into separate corpus entries: (1) capital-gain sequencing, `nd_pit_2026_profile_candidate_capital_and_dividend_reduction` went from max(0, allocated_LTCG - allocated_STCL) to max(0, min(federal_LTCG - federal_STCL, LTCG_allocated_to_nd)); I read 57-38-30.3(2)(d)(1) through the pinned corpus and it says "The excess of the taxpayer's net long-term capital gain for the taxable year over the net short-term capital loss for that year, as computed for purposes of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. The adjustment provided by this subdivision is allowed only to the extent the net long-term capital gain is allocated to this state" -- so the pre-fix encoding netted on ND-allocated figures instead of computing the federal excess and then applying the allocation as a ceiling (a clean source-verifiable defect, kind unrepresented_clause or wrong_entity_or_scope; the post-fix suite adds the case "federal capital loss offset precedes north dakota allocation cap"). (2) organ-donation grain: the pre-fix `nd_pit_2026_profile_candidate_organ_donation_reduction` = min(expenses, 10000) applied one annual $10,000 cap, but 2(i) allows the reduction "only once for each instance of organ donation" by the taxpayer or a dependent, so multiple instances were understated; the rule, its cap parameter and its input were deleted in favor of the `nd_pit_2026_has_living_organ_donation_expense_claim` hold. (3) other-state credit: the 4(a)-(b) credit chain and the planned-gift 2(j) addback were removed in favor of holds (`nd_pit_2026_has_other_state_income_tax_credit`, `nd_pit_2026_has_planned_gift_credit_or_addback`), so the commit also withdraws coverage rather than only correcting it. The provision was read (corpus release resolved via resolve_provision.py; subsections 1, 2(d), 2(i), 9, 10 inspected); the commit body itself is empty (just a newline), all quotable evidence is in the PR body; PR has no review or issue comments in the bundle. Companion files changed alongside: the test suite (212+/240-), the encoding manifest, and oracle-coverage-pending.yaml -- consistent bookkeeping, no unrelated module edits. No follow-up repair commits touch us-nd between this commit and the merge.

verdict.justification: The quoted rationale does not survive the pinned source: 57-38-30.3(10) reads "The tax commissioner may prescribe tax tables, to be used in computing the tax according to subsection 1, if the amounts of the tax tables are based on the tax rates set forth in subsection 1. If prescribed by the tax commissioner, the tables must be followed" — permissive and conditional, while subsection 1 itself supplies the operative filing-status schedules, and every pre-fix bracket parameter quotes those schedules verbatim from the same provision ("$0 | $49,575", "$49,575 | $250,400", "$3,916.09 + 2.50%", "$0 | $41,400"), so the pre-fix annual-tax branch was traceable to the cited source, not ungrounded. The commit changes no rate, threshold, or computed amount for that branch at all: 3916.0875 merely moves from the public nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_tax_before_credits to the private nd_pit_2026_profile_candidate_single_tax in the companion tests, i.e. the annual-tax part is an output-surface hold driven by source-boundary conservatism. The same diff does, however, carry a source-provable fidelity correction: 57-38-30.3(2)(d)(1) allows forty percent of the excess of net long-term capital gain over net short-term capital loss "as computed for purposes of the Internal Revenue Code" and "only to the extent the net long-term capital gain is allocated to this state", and the fix replaces the pre-fix allocated-minus-allocated excess with the federal excess capped by the ND allocation — the statutory limitation clause that the encoding omitted (as with 2(i)'s "only once for each instance of organ donation" grain). That makes the module change a fidelity defect of kind unrepresented_clause rather than untraceable_branch.
verdict.quote:
+              min(
+                nd_pit_2026_federal_net_long_term_capital_gain
+                  - nd_pit_2026_federal_net_short_term_capital_loss,
+                nd_pit_2026_net_long_term_capital_gain_allocated_to_nd
+              )
verdict.notes:
Multi-defect repair commit; the PR body itself lists the bundle: "Independent review found and required repairs for annual-table substitution, capital-gain sequencing, organ-donation grain, caller-completed classifications, other-state-credit mechanics, and filing-status threshold coverage."

Refutation detail on the first reader's anchor (rules[nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies].versions[0].formula -> 'false'):
- Resolved provision us-nd/statute/57/57-38-30.3 (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, expression date 2026-07-16, body sha d06df87b...) contains the full subsection 1(a)-(e) rate schedules with exactly the amounts the pre-fix module encoded, and subsection 1 says the tax "is equal to North Dakota taxable income multiplied by the rates in the applicable rate schedule in subdivisions a through d". Subsection 10 is permissive ("may prescribe"; "If prescribed ... must be followed") and constrains any table to be "based on the tax rates set forth in subsection 1". So the premise "57-38-30.3(10) requires the prescribed annual tax table" is a misreading of the cited text, and "no basis in the cited source" is false for that branch — the pre-fix parameters' proof atoms quote the statute, not ND-1ES, even though their `source:` labels say ND-1ES.
- If a reviewer insists on anchoring the classification to the annual-tax gate, the honest labels there are wrong_entity_or_scope (public output surface narrowed) or not_a_defect (fail-closed project policy about unpinned annual-return material), not untraceable_branch; no number, rate, window, or boolean in the tax computation changed.
- Other removals in this diff (other-state credit under 4(a)-(b), planned-gift addback under 2(j)) look source-faithful pre-fix and were withdrawn to holds for missing ND-1CR / credit-recomputation material, i.e. conservatism rather than demonstrated error. One genuinely ungrounded pre-fix condition was also dropped: the input-domain constraint "nd_pit_2026_other_state_source_federal_adjusted_gross_income <= nd_pit_2026_other_state_credit_denominator", which has no statutory basis — a reviewer who wants to keep untraceable_branch could anchor there instead, but it is incidental to the commit's subject.
- Strongest fidelity anchors, both verifiable against the pinned text: (1) capital-gain sequencing per 2(d)(1) (quote above); (2) organ donation, where the pre-fix flat unit-level min(expenses, 10000) ignored "A taxpayer may claim the reduction in this subdivision only once for each instance of organ donation during the taxable year", and the fix withdraws the branch to the new nd_pit_2026_has_living_organ_donation_expense_claim hold.

item.subject: Address Rhode Island resident core review findings

triage.commit_summary: This commit applies the independent-review repairs to the Rhode Island TY2026 full-year-resident income-tax core (PR #1032), touching one rule module plus its companion test suite, encoding manifest, and the oracle-pending ledger. It removes an ungrounded ordering between the section 44-30-18 other-state credit and the section 44-30-2.6 child/dependent-care credit (now a typed hold when both are positive), splits the organ-donation subtraction into per-donor primary/spouse facts with a per-individual $10,000 cap, replaces the single collapsed "special tax computation" flag with the six separately enumerated section 44-30-2.6(G)/(H)/(I) Rhode Island taxes, and re-derives the forty-percent phaseout step from the grounded twenty-percentage-point reduction instead of asserting 0.4 directly.

modules.description_quote: When both nonrefundable credits are positive, their tax-year-2026 ordering is a typed hold because the pinned corpus lacks the 2026 return and instructions.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: When both the section 44-30-18 other-state credit and the section 44-30-2.6 child/dependent-care credit were positive, the pre-fix module computed a result under a specific application order (other-state credit first, then CDCC capped against the tax remaining after it) that the pinned Rhode Island corpus nowhere establishes, instead of holding; secondarily it capped the organ-donation subtraction once per tax unit although the statute grants the $10,000 subtraction per individual donor, collapsed the statute's six separately enumerated 'other Rhode Island taxes' into one composite flag, and asserted the 40% phaseout step as a bare 0.4 rather than deriving it from the grounded twenty-percentage-point reductions.
modules.triage_notes: Multi-defect repair commit; I read every hunk. (1) DECISIVE: ri_pit_2026_bounded_credit_chain_applies gains 'and ri_pit_2026_nonrefundable_credit_order_is_unambiguous', and the new judgment rule holds unless one of the two nonrefundable candidates is zero. Verified the CDCC formula body itself is byte-identical pre/post (git show of both revisions); only the gate and the source: string changed, so the behavior change is entirely the new hold. Classified untraceable_branch because the fix removes a computed ordering with no basis in the pinned authority rather than correcting a value. (2) A second, independently classifiable defect in the same diff is wrong_entity_or_scope / amount_mismatch on the organ-donation subtraction: ri_pit_2026_unreimbursed_organ_donation_expenses and its two history flags are split into primary_taxpayer_* and spouse_* inputs, and ri_pit_2026_profile_candidate_organ_donation_subtraction now applies min(cap, expenses) separately per donor with the spouse leg gated on ri_pit_2026_is_married_filing_jointly. I read us-ri/statute/44-30-12 through the pinned release: '(7) Modification for organ transplantation. (i) An individual may subtract up to ten thousand dollars ($10,000) ... (ii) An individual may claim that subtract modification hereunder only once, and the subtract modification may be claimed for only the following unreimbursed expenses that are incurred by the claimant and related to the claimant's organ donation' — per individual donor, so the pre-fix single tax-unit cap and single lifetime-claim flag were wrong for a joint return with two donors. ri_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies also gains a guard forcing spouse organ facts to be absent on non-joint returns. (3) A third: unrepresented_clause on the specialty taxes — ri_pit_2026_has_special_tax_computation (described as 'lump-sum child-investment recapture or farm-averaging tax') is replaced by six inputs matching us-ri/statute/44-30-2.6 subsections (G)(1)(a)-(c), (H)(1)(a) and (I)(1)(a), which I read in the pinned release; the pre-fix composite silently folded the parent-election and fishing-averaging items into one flag and the proof atom cited only the heading excerpt 'Other Rhode Island taxes'. (4) ri_pit_2026_forty_percent_allowed goes from kind: parameter with formula '0.4' to kind: derived, entity: TaxUnit, formula full - twenty - twenty - twenty; with full=1 and twenty=0.2 in the same module this is numerically the same 0.4, so it is a grounding/derivation repair ('direct assertions' finding), not an amount change — note eighty_percent_allowed and sixty_percent_allowed were left as literal parameters, so the repair is inconsistent. (5) Genuinely mechanical bits mixed in: several proof atoms flip kind: ordering -> kind: exception and excerpt strings are swapped for more specific statutory text; module doc comment and deferred_outputs reason text updated. Commit body is empty (just a newline); the PR has no reviews or review comments, so the stated reason lives in the PR body's review-fix-cycle paragraph, which lists 'source-derived percentages, direct assertions, caller-result shortcuts, input grain, organ-donation caps/history, specialty-tax inventory, OOS/CDCC ordering, taxable-income floors, duplicate fixture keys, and opportunity-zone per-investment eligibility' — the first six of those map onto this diff; taxable-income floors and opportunity-zone grain do not appear here. Follow-up commits on the same module: cfdc84cf7 'Satisfy Rhode Island deterministic validation' and bdf6b6965 'Constrain Rhode Island opportunity-zone investment grain'. Companion test file and .axiom encoding manifest changed alongside, as expected. If the corpus wants one defect per row, this module could reasonably be split into three fidelity rows (untraceable_branch, wrong_entity_or_scope, unrepresented_clause).

verdict.justification: The pre-fix module computed `ri_pit_2026_bounded_child_and_dependent_care_credit_applied` as `min(cdcc_candidate, max(0, schedule_tax - ordinary_aggregate_other_state_credit_candidate))`, i.e. it asserted that the § 44-30-18 other-state credit is applied first and the § 44-30-2.6 CDCC is capped against the remainder; I read both provisions plus ADV 2025-22 pages 1-2 through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix) and neither contains any ordering language — § 44-30-18(b) caps the other-state credit at a proportion of RI tax and § 44-30-2.6(c)(3)(F)(g) caps the CDCC at "the Rhode Island tax liability," each independently, and the guidance pages contain no occurrence of "credit" at all. The fix adds `ri_pit_2026_nonrefundable_credit_order_is_unambiguous` and gates the chain on it, so the ungrounded ordering branch is removed and both-positive returns now hold, which changes public outputs (the chain gate and every bounded money rule are non-private). That is exactly "a branch, condition, or value with no basis in the cited source (the fix removes or re-grounds it)," so fidelity/untraceable_branch stands; I could not refute it.
verdict.quote:
+          and ri_pit_2026_nonrefundable_credit_order_is_unambiguous
-    source: Supported CDCC capped against tax remaining after ordinary other-state credit
+    source: Supported CDCC capped only on the unambiguous branch where the other-state candidate is zero
verdict.notes: Two caveats for the reviewer. (1) The ordering is arguably numerically inert for the terminal figure: `ri_pit_2026_bounded_tax_before_eitc` is `max(0, schedule_tax - oos - cdcc_applied)`, and min(cdcc, max(0,tax-oos)) and min(cdcc, tax) both collapse to max(0, tax-oos-cdcc) there, so the pre-fix error is observable in the public intermediate output `ri_pit_2026_bounded_child_and_dependent_care_credit_applied` and in the population that now fails closed, not in the net-liability number. That is why I set confidence at 0.75 rather than higher; it does not rescue the pre-fix text, which still capped the CDCC on a base the cited excerpt ("such credit shall not exceed the Rhode Island tax liability") does not support. (2) The same commit carries a second, separately classifiable fidelity defect that a reviewer may want split out or preferred as the anchor: the organ-donation subtraction was computed once per tax unit from a single `ri_pit_2026_unreimbursed_organ_donation_expenses` input, while § 44-30-12(c)(7)(i) reads "An individual may subtract up to ten thousand dollars ($10,000)... for only the following unreimbursed expenses that are incurred by the claimant"; the fix splits primary/spouse inputs and sums two separately capped amounts on joint returns — that one is wrong_entity_or_scope (household member set). The remaining changes are weaker: splitting `ri_pit_2026_has_special_tax_computation` into six named specialty-tax flags is grain, not meaning (the catch-all already gated them), and re-deriving `ri_pit_2026_forty_percent_allowed` from full minus three twenty-point reductions yields the identical 0.4, so that part is grounding/provenance only.

item.subject: Address Montana resident core review

triage.commit_summary: This is the review-fix commit on PR #1031 (the Montana TY2026 full-year-resident income-tax core was first encoded in parent 34b60479e), rewriting one module and its 3,181-line companion suite to answer independent-review findings. It adds the MCA 15-30-2120(5)(a) family-education contribution deduction with its $4,500/$9,000 caps and account-owner constraints, adds the MCA 15-30-2321 eligible-child/one-credit-per-child conditions to the refundable adoption credit, adds raw applicability holds requiring the absence of the separate taxes and recaptures under 15-30-2105, 15-30-3005, 15-62-208, 53-25-118, 15-30-2328(3) and 15-30-2359(6) plus the refundable 15-30-3328 pass-through-entity credit, removes the ungrounded nonnegative floor on Montana taxable income (flooring only the 15-30-2103 schedule base), and makes the refundable-credit rules fail closed outside the supported profile.

modules.description_quote: Separate taxes and recoveries under sections 15-30-2105, 15-30-3005, 15-62-208, 53-25-118, 15-30-2328(3), and 15-30-2359(6), plus the refundable pass-through-entity-tax credit under 15-30-3328, are represented by distinct raw applicability facts and must be absent.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module returned a full-year-resident net liability that silently omitted clauses the cited Montana statutes state: the separate lump-sum/farm-ranch/recapture taxes and credit recoveries under 15-30-2105, 15-30-3005, 15-62-208, 53-25-118, 15-30-2328(3) and 15-30-2359(6) and the refundable 15-30-3328 pass-through-entity credit had no representation at all, the 15-30-2120(5)(a) family-education deduction was parked as a typed hold even though its $4,500/$9,000 caps and account-owner relationship test are in the pinned corpus, and the adoption credit multiplied per-adoption amounts by unbounded counts with none of 15-30-2321's eligible-child (under 18 or incapable of self-care), adoption-final-in-year, or "Only one credit is allowed for each eligible child" conditions.
modules.triage_notes: Single module file, but this is a multi-defect review-fix commit; at least four distinct fidelity corrections land in the same diff and I had to pick one kind. (1) unrepresented_clause, the dominant pattern: missing separate taxes/recaptures and the PTE credit (now fail-closed applicability holds in mt_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies), the missing 15-30-2120(5)(a) family-education deduction (new caps 4500/9000, child/stepchild Montana-residency test, added into mt_pit_2026_profile_candidate_subtractions and the corresponding hold input mt_pit_2026_has_family_education_contribution_deduction deleted), and the missing 15-30-2321 eligible-child/one-credit conditions on mt_pit_2026_refundable_adoption_credit. (2) untraceable_branch: the pre-fix mt_pit_2026_profile_candidate_montana_taxable_income wrapped fed TI + additions - subtractions in max(0, ...) with no basis in 15-30-2101; the fix renames it to mt_pit_2026_profile_candidate_signed_section_2101_amount without the floor and introduces mt_pit_2026_profile_candidate_schedule_tax_base = max(0, ...) so only the 15-30-2103 schedule base is floored (module summary: "computes Montana taxable income without forcing a nonnegative floor, floors only the schedule base"). (3) polarity_or_logic / fail-open: the refundable adoption, EITC, and public-access credit rules previously computed unconditionally and now return 0 when mt_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies is false (PR body: "transitive fail-closed gates"). (4) capital character: a new gate requires section_1222_net_long_term_capital_gain == 0 or both additions and subtractions == 0, because Montana modifications can change income character. Also in scope but not a defect: the public-access hold was renamed and NARROWED (mt_pit_2026_has_shared_or_duplicate_public_access_claim -> mt_pit_2026_has_shared_ownership_or_same_property_public_access_allocation, so separate properties under 15-30-2380(4) no longer set the hold), and ~25 cross-title modification inputs gained `== 0` requirements in the profile gate (PR body finding "caller-completed legal results"). Provisions read through the pinned release: MCA 15-30-2120(5)(a) confirms the $4,500/$9,000 caps, the taxpayer/spouse/child-or-stepchild account-owner constraint with the Montana-residency condition, and (5)(b) the 15-62-208 recapture tax; MCA 15-30-2321 confirms the $7,500/$5,000 amounts, subsection (5) "Only one credit is allowed for each eligible child." and subsection (7) "eligible child" = under 18 or incapable of self-care. MCA 15-30-2105 could NOT be resolved: the resolver reported "Active corpus source 'us-mt/statute/15-30-2105' is repealed" for every candidate release, so the lump-sum-distribution excerpt is taken from the module's own proof atom, not independently verified. Commit message body is empty; PR body is the best commit-level evidence ("Findings covering specialty taxes and recaptures, capital character, transitive fail-closed gates, caller-completed legal results, public-output gating, federal-EITC domain consistency, adoption proof completeness, and generated-artifact minimality were fixed and revalidated."). Follow-up: 915fc7cc8 "Tighten Montana resident core domain" touches this same module after this commit; a PR comment says that rebase carried no substantive Montana changes, so reviewers should check whether 915fc7cc8 contains further fidelity fixes. Companion test file changed by +3,181 lines in the same commit.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix module (34b60479:us-mt/.../resident_core_liability_pipeline.yaml, rule mt_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies, lines 414-465) emitted mt_pit_2026_supported_profile_candidate_net_income_tax_liability = "Net Montana income-tax liability before payments" for a gate that had no conjunct, input, or hold for the separate taxes and recaptures MCA 15-30-3005, 15-62-208, 15-30-2328(3), 15-30-2359(6) and 15-30-2120(6)(b)/53-25-118 impose, or for the refundable 15-30-3328 pass-through-entity credit, so a resident with any of them silently got an understated liability; the fix adds the raw facts and gate conjuncts, i.e. it adds representation of clauses the source states. I read those provisions in the release the commit's toolchain pins (us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current) and every added proof excerpt is verbatim in the corpus body ("There is a recapture tax at a rate equal to the highest rate of tax provided in 15-30-2103"; "increase the amount of tax due under 15-30-2103 or 15-31-101 by the amount of the credit allowed"; "may claim the distributive share of the owner's entity tax paid by an electing pass-through entity as a refundable credit"). The "new coverage it never claimed" defense fails because the pre-fix gate affirmatively admitted those taxpayers, and it also fails for the family-education deduction: the pre-fix hold rationale called it "indexed", but 15-30-2120(7)(a) indexes only subsections (3)(g) and (3)(o), so the fixed $4,500/$9,000 caps in (5)(a) were a source-stated deduction left unrepresented. The one weak item is 15-30-2105, which the pinned corpus row marks metadata.status "repealed".
verdict.quote:
+          and not mt_pit_2026_has_lump_sum_distribution_tax
+          and not mt_pit_2026_has_farm_ranch_risk_account_distribution
+          and not mt_pit_2026_has_farm_ranch_risk_account_penalty
+          and not mt_pit_2026_has_529_recapture_tax
+          and not mt_pit_2026_has_able_recapture_tax
+          and not mt_pit_2026_has_endowment_recovery_or_credit_recapture
+          and not mt_pit_2026_has_trades_training_recovery_or_credit_recapture
+          and not mt_pit_2026_has_refundable_pass_through_entity_tax_credit
verdict.notes: Reviewer caveats. (1) Multi-defect commit: besides the quoted unrepresented clauses it also (a) rewrites the refundable adoption credit from an ungated count product (`mt_pit_2026_foster_care_adoption_amount * ..._count + ...`) to a single child-level claim conditioned on 15-30-2321's "eligible child" age-18/self-care test, 2026 finality and "Only one credit is allowed for each eligible child." (all three excerpts verified verbatim) — also unrepresented_clause; (b) gates mt_pit_2026_refundable_earned_income_credit and mt_pit_2026_refundable_public_access_credit on the profile, which is a fail-open→fail-closed fix (polarity_or_logic); (c) splits mt_pit_2026_profile_candidate_montana_taxable_income into a signed 15-30-2101 amount plus a floored 15-30-2103 schedule base, removing an ungrounded max(0) on Montana taxable income (arguably untraceable_branch). If the corpus wants one kind per case, unrepresented_clause is the dominant and the one the quoted comment supports; wrong_entity_or_scope is an adjacent reading (the supported population was too broad) but the cause is the missing clauses. (2) Partial weakness in the first reader's quote: MCA 15-30-2105 (lump-sum distribution tax) carries metadata.status "repealed" in the pinned release row (656 of the MT Title-15 rows carry that status, so the flag is meaningful), and `resolve_provision.py` refuses it as "Active corpus source ... is repealed" — the lump-sum hold added for it is conservative rather than source-required. The other six items are active sections and carry the fidelity finding on their own. (3) Provenance: this is a review-fix commit inside PR #1031, the PR that first introduced the module, so the defective state never reached main; that is a corpus-curation question (does the corpus admit intra-PR fixes?), not a classification one. (4) Verified read-only via git show, the scratchpad release JSONL, and resolve_provision.py; no repo state touched.

item.subject: Address West Virginia resident core review

triage.commit_summary: This commit applied the independent-review fixes to the newly encoded West Virginia TY2026 resident income-tax core pipeline (PR #1029), the only module file being us-wv/policies/income_tax/resident_core_liability_pipeline.yaml. It gated the §11-21-10 low-income earned-income exclusion on a full taxable year, restricted the increasing-modification withdrawal inputs to amounts not already included in federal AGI, marked every ungated intermediate rule `private: true` so only `wv_pit_2026_supported_profile_*` outputs leave the module, and added supporting proof atoms for the social-security, gambling, exemption, and full-year clauses.

modules.description_quote: Independent review found unsupported-profile intermediate exposure, incomplete SS/exemption/gambling/full-year proofs, withdrawal addback semantics, and missing boundary/branch tests.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The low-income earned-income exclusion returned a nonzero deduction for any return meeting the AGI thresholds, omitting W. Va. Code 11-21-10(d), which bars the exclusion for a taxable year covering a period of less than twelve months; the fix wraps the whole formula in `if wv_pit_2026_is_full_year_resident_return: ... else: 0`.
modules.triage_notes: Provision WAS read: resolve_provision.py on us-wv/statute/11-21-10 returns subsection (d) verbatim -- 'Taxable year must be full taxable year. -- Except in the case of a taxable year closed by reason of the death of the taxpayer, no credit shall be allowed under this section in the case of a taxable year covering a period of less than twelve months.' Pre-fix, `wv_pit_2026_is_full_year_resident_return` appeared ONLY in the wv_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies gate (parent line 220), never in the exclusion rule's own formula, and the exclusion rule was not private, so reading it directly for a short taxable year produced a wrong nonzero amount. Caveat on the fix: it does not implement the (d) death-of-taxpayer carve-out (a short year closed by death still gets zero); the module fails closed outside the full-year profile, so this is under- rather than over-claiming. The commit consists of four distinct change classes bundled together -- (1) the full-year gate above (fidelity); (2) renaming four increasing-modification withdrawal inputs to `..._not_in_federal_adjusted_gross_income` with matching descriptions and a new module-description sentence 'Increasing-modification withdrawal inputs are expressly limited to amounts not already included in federal adjusted gross income.', which aligns the inputs with the 11-21-12(b) lead-in 'There shall be added to federal adjusted gross income, unless already included therein' already cited as a pre-existing proof atom -- a second, weaker unrepresented_clause signal implemented only as input rename/description, with formulas otherwise unchanged; (3) adding `private: true` to eight intermediate rules, an output-surface narrowing that removes exposure the module arguably never intended to claim (not itself a defect under the task's 'added scope' rule, and it removes rather than adds surface); (4) five added proof-atom excerpts (social security pre/post-2026 AGI conditions, 11-21-9 gambling and personal-exemption definitions, 11-21-10 full-year condition on the profile gate) -- pure provenance, mechanical. Confidence held below 0.8 because the commit body is empty and the PR body names the finding set generically ('full-year proofs', 'withdrawal addback semantics') rather than stating the formula defect; the diff plus the resolved statute make the kind clear. Also changed outside this module index: the companion test file and the encoding manifest. No follow-up commits inspected.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as mere hardening and could not: the pinned corpus text of W. Va. Code §11-21-10(d) reads "Taxable year must be full taxable year. -- Except in the case of a taxable year closed by reason of the death of the taxpayer, no credit shall be allowed under this section in the case of a taxable year covering a period of less than twelve months", and the pre-fix `wv_pit_2026_low_income_earned_income_exclusion` formula tested only filing status and the AGI thresholds, so it returned a nonzero deduction on a short taxable year. The fix wraps the entire formula in `if wv_pit_2026_is_full_year_resident_return: ... else: 0` and adds a proof atom quoting that subsection, i.e. it adds a source-stated clause the encoding omitted. The rule was public before this commit (`private: true` is added in the same hunk) and the companion test now asserts `is_full_year_resident_return: false` → exclusion `'0'`, so the omission was observable at the module's output surface rather than masked by the `wv_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies` gate. Kind unrepresented_clause fits better than wrong_entity_or_scope because the decisive change at the cited rule_path is a missing statutory condition added to the formula, not a re-scoping of the population.
verdict.quote:
+          - path: versions[0].formula
+            kind: exception
+            source: {corpus_citation_path: us-wv/statute/11-21-10, excerpt: "Except in the case of a taxable year closed by reason of the death of the taxpayer, no credit shall be allowed under this section in the case of a taxable year covering a period of less than twelve months"}
...
+          if wv_pit_2026_is_full_year_resident_return:
verdict.notes:
Verification path: corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, provision us-wv/statute/11-21-10, body sha256 9dd6bea…858fbe; the added proof-atom excerpt is verbatim from subsection (d).

Three caveats for the reviewer, none of which overturn the verdict:
1. The fix over-corrects relative to the source. §11-21-10(d) excepts "a taxable year closed by reason of the death of the taxpayer", but the new gate denies the exclusion for every non-full-year return with no death carve-out. The module fails closed in a case the statute allows; that is a residual (opposite-direction) fidelity gap in the post state, not a reason to reject the pre-state as wrong.
2. The gate input `wv_pit_2026_is_full_year_resident_return` is described as "Whether the return covers a full taxable year for West Virginia full-year residents", conflating residency status with the twelve-month period test that (d) actually states.
3. The commit is mixed, so the other rule_names in this candidate carry changes of different character: `wv_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid`, `wv_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies`, and `wv_pit_2026_profile_candidate_additions` change only through the rename of four withdrawal inputs to `..._not_in_federal_adjusted_gross_income` (a separate narrowing of increasing-modification semantics that would need its own §11-21-12(b) check), plus `private: true` metadata on intermediates and added proof atoms (provenance/scope hardening). The first reader's quote is the PR's generic laundry-list review sentence and does not by itself evidence this kind; the diff line and the §11-21-10(d) text do.

Pre/post copies written to the scratchpad at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/pre.yaml and post.yaml. No repository state was modified.

item.subject: Pin corrected Oklahoma corpus status

triage.commit_summary: The commit re-pins `.axiom/toolchain.toml`'s `axiom_corpus_ref` from `dc965655…` to the companion axiom-corpus merge `4f0c9557…`, which corrected Oklahoma §2358 version status so v1/v2 are marked superseded and v3 operative, and rewrites the corresponding provenance rationale inside the single Oklahoma module so it no longer claims a "verified extraction-status exception" for corpus metadata that used to say v3 was repealed. No encoded meaning changed: the module already cited and used `us-ok/statute/68-2358v3` as operative before the fix, and every rule, formula, version, effective date, parameter, input, and output is byte-identical across the commit; the encoding manifest hash/signature and toolchain pin were regenerated to match.

modules.description_quote: The RuleSpec then pinned that merge, removed the obsolete extraction-status exception, re-signed its manifest, and passed final independent re-review of exact head `6e45a2cfbbc8f5f535db44c370695a69d6e0519a` with no findings.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing in the encoded meaning was wrong: the pre-fix module already cited and applied §2358v3 as the operative text, and only its provenance note was stale, asserting a corpus extraction-status exception (metadata saying the section was "repealed") that the companion corpus correction removed.
modules.triage_notes: Verified mechanically: I dumped the full parent and commit versions of the module and diffed everything after the rationale block (pre lines 44-1492 vs post lines 45-1493) — byte-identical, so no rule name, formula, version, effective_from/to, parameter, input, output, or scope changed. The only YAML hunk rewrites five lines of free-text inside module.source_verification.upstream_source_check.rationale, replacing 'Its generated corpus metadata incorrectly says "repealed" because the Oklahoma extractor scans historical repeal notes inside the section body; that verified extraction-status exception does not alter the official text.' with a statement that the pinned corpus now classifies 2358v1/v2 superseded and v3 operative. corpus_citation_paths and checked_paths are unchanged and already included us-ok/statute/68-2358v3 pre-fix. The other two files in the commit are also bookkeeping: .axiom/toolchain.toml bumps axiom_corpus_ref dc965655→4f0c9557, and the encoding manifest updates sha256/signature/generated_at plus flips manual_exception from "composition" to "repair" and nests the prior supersedes chain. I did NOT run resolve_provision.py because no encoded meaning is in dispute — the substantive fidelity work (EITC ratio caps, per-person retirement caps, civil-service branch, 529/ABLE windows) described in the PR's review-fix cycle happened in earlier commits on PR #1028, not in this one; those are candidates for separate triage. The PR body notes this exact head b4e4a4077a is the post-rebase integration head onto rulespec-us main cb4e24b5, so the commit is the rebased tail of that PR. Per the stated rule that provenance/citation-string-only corrections are mechanical, this is mechanical, not fidelity.

item.subject: Address Oklahoma resident core review findings

triage.commit_summary: This commit is the review-repair round inside PR #1028 ("Encode Oklahoma 2026 resident income-tax core"), applying an independent reviewer's six findings to the single TY2026 Oklahoma full-year-resident core module plus its companion fixtures and re-signed apply manifest. It adds the missing 68 O.S. § 2358(E)(18) full exemption for federal civil-service retirement/survivor benefits paid in lieu of Social Security, moves the § 2358(E)(8)/(13) $10,000 retirement cap from TaxUnit grain to per-individual (taxpayer plus, on a joint return, spouse) grain, extends the § 2358(E)(16)/(E)(24) 529 and ABLE deductions to contributions made through the April 15 succeeding-year statutory deadline, and caps the § 2357.43 EITC proration ratio at one (returning full ratio instead of zero when federal AGI is not positive).

modules.description_quote: Independent review found six issues: EITC proration could exceed one or divide by zero; retirement caps were applied at TaxUnit rather than individual grain; the civil-service-in-lieu-of-Social-Security full exemption was missing; 529/ABLE deadline windows were ambiguous
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module had no representation of 68 O.S. § 2358(E)(18), which exempts 100% of federal civil-service retirement and survivor benefits paid in lieu of Social Security for tax years beginning after 2010, so a supported full-year resident with those benefits got no exemption (or at best the capped § 2358(E)(8) $10,000 treatment) and an overstated Oklahoma taxable income; the same commit also fixed three further source disagreements (per-individual retirement cap grain, the 529/ABLE succeeding-year contribution window, and the uncapped EITC proration ratio).
modules.triage_notes: Multi-defect repair commit on ONE module; a judge could legitimately name a different kind, hence confidence capped at 0.8. The four distinct fidelity defects, all verified against the pinned corpus text of us-ok/statute/68-2358v3 and us-ok/statute/68-2357-43 (provisions read via resolve_provision.py, both resolved successfully): (1) unrepresented_clause [chosen as primary] - § 2358(E)(18) reads 'retirement benefits received by federal civil service retirees, including survivor annuities, paid in lieu of Social Security benefits shall be exempt ... e. in the taxable year beginning January 1, 2011, and subsequent taxable years, one hundred percent (100%) of such benefits shall be exempt'; the pre-fix module had no such rule and no such input, and the fix adds rule ok_2026_resident_federal_civil_service_in_lieu_social_security_deduction, a new input, and a new subtraction line in ok_2026_resident_taxable_income_before_unpinned_return_floor_core. The pre-fix module's declared supported boundary did NOT exclude civil-service retirees, so this is a missing clause inside claimed scope, not new scope. (2) wrong_entity_or_scope - § 2358(E)(8) exempts up to '$10,000.00 ... received by an individual'; the pre-fix formula applied one TaxUnit-level cap across combined (E)(8)+(E)(13) amounts, so a joint return with two retirees was capped at $10,000 total instead of $10,000 each. Fix splits inputs into taxpayer/spouse and adds the filing-status-indexed parameter ok_2026_spouse_retirement_exemption_eligibility. (3) unrepresented_clause / period - § 2358(E)(16) ('deductions may be taken for contributions and rollovers made during a taxable year and up to April 15 of the succeeding year, or the due date of a taxpayer's state income tax return, excluding extensions, whichever is later') and § 2358(E)(24) (same window for ABLE) were not represented; pre-fix accepted only current-year contributions. (4) amount/boundary - § 2357.43 says the maximum EITC 'shall be prorated on the ratio that Oklahoma adjusted gross income bears to the federal adjusted gross income', i.e. a proration that cannot exceed the full credit; pre-fix ratio was uncapped (Oklahoma AGI can exceed federal AGI via § 2358 additions such as the state/local tax add-back) and returned 0 when federal AGI was not positive, denying the credit entirely. Fix adds parameter ok_2026_full_credit_proration_ratio = 1 and uses min(1, ratio) with 1 as the non-positive-AGI branch. Bundled non-fidelity changes in the same diff: the module rationale/summary prose was rewritten (including a new note that the corpus's generated 'repealed' extraction status for § 2358v3 is an extractor artifact) and the module summary line was updated - provenance/metadata, mechanical. Also in the commit but outside this module: 1,449 added lines of fixtures in 2026_resident_ordinary_core.test.yaml and a re-signed .axiom/encoding-manifests entry. Caveat for the corpus: this is an intra-PR repair round (pre-fix state was a branch head reviewed before merge, never on main), so the defective version was caught pre-merge rather than in production.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix file (parent 578c39059) contains no token matching "civil", "in_lieu" or "2358(E)(18)" anywhere, while the pinned corpus text of us-ok/statute/68-2358v3 states at paragraph 18 that "retirement benefits received by federal civil service retirees, including survivor annuities, paid in lieu of Social Security benefits shall be exempt from taxable income ... e. in the taxable year beginning January 1, 2011, and subsequent taxable years, one hundred percent (100%) of such benefits shall be exempt". This is not merely absent coverage: the same statute's paragraph 8 enumerates "the civil service of the United States" under the $10,000 cap, and the pre-fix input ok_2026_enumerated_public_retirement_benefits_in_federal_agi swept those benefits into that capped branch (the fix re-scopes it "excluding any amount separately qualifying under section 2358(E)(18)"), so a supported full-year resident with such benefits received a $10,000-capped exemption instead of 100% and an overstated Oklahoma taxable income within the module's own claimed taxable-income-before-floor output. The fix adds a rule for the missing clause and subtracts it in that output, which is the definition of unrepresented_clause; the module's generic disclaimer of "a complete section 2358 adjustment inventory" does not exclude civil-service retirees from the supported boundary, so the not-a-defect ("new coverage never claimed") reading fails.
verdict.quote:
+  - name: ok_2026_resident_federal_civil_service_in_lieu_social_security_deduction
+        formula: max(0, ok_2026_federal_civil_service_retirement_and_survivor_benefits_paid_in_lieu_of_social_security_in_federal_agi)
+          - ok_2026_resident_federal_civil_service_in_lieu_social_security_deduction
verdict.notes:
Provenance caveat for the corpus curator: this is an intra-PR repair round, not a post-merge fix. `git log a5f26f045c -- us-ok/policies/income_tax/2026_resident_ordinary_core.yaml` shows exactly two commits — the parent 578c39059 "Encode Oklahoma 2026 resident income tax core" that created the 1,372-line file, and this commit. Both are on PR #1028, merged together 2026-07-24, so the defective version never existed on main. If the corpus is meant to hold defects that shipped, flag it; if it holds encoder-produced defects caught by review, it belongs.

The commit bundles at least four distinct fidelity fixes, so the case is multi-kind and the anchor decides it: (a) the missing §2358(E)(18) clause — the anchored rule_path, unrepresented_clause; (b) retirement cap grain, TaxUnit-wide cap split into taxpayer/spouse inputs gated by ok_2026_spouse_retirement_exemption_eligibility[filing_status] — that alone would read as wrong_entity_or_scope; (c) 529/ABLE contribution window extended to the April 15 succeeding-year deadline (new inputs ..._made_by_statutory_succeeding_year_deadline_for_tax_year) — unrepresented_clause or wrong_period_or_effective_date; (d) EITC proration min-capped at 1 with the zero-AGI branch changed from `0` to the full ratio. If the corpus wants one kind per case, the anchored rule_path (the civil-service formula) makes unrepresented_clause correct; a second row could be split out for (b).

Alternative kind I considered and rejected: amount_mismatch, on the theory that the exemption for civil-service benefits was $10,000 instead of 100%. Rejected because no parameter value or table cell was corrected — the fix adds a whole rule for a clause the encoding never represented, and the $10,000 cap in ok_2026_retirement_exemption_cap remains correct for §2358(E)(8).

The first reader's quote is verbatim from the PR #1028 body ("Review-fix cycle" section). Also note the header rationale change in this diff documents a corpus extraction-status exception ("Its generated corpus metadata incorrectly says 'repealed'"); that part is provenance/metadata, not the fidelity defect.

item.subject: Fix Louisiana EITC rate validation

triage.commit_summary: The commit is the last repair round of PR #1026 (Louisiana TY2026 resident income-tax core): exact-head CI rejected the module for using the imported La. R.S. 47:297.8 composite EITC rate as a flat multiplier, so the branch dropped the `us-la:statutes/47:297/8#earned_income_tax_credit_rate` import and added a locally proved TY2026 parameter `la_2026_earned_income_tax_credit_rate` = 0.05 (effective 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31) with proof atoms for the "five percent" amount and the 2019-2030 effective window. It also re-pointed the nominal EITC formula at the new local parameter, re-signed the apply manifest as a "repair", and ratcheted `oracle-coverage-pending.yaml` by one entry for the newly declared parameter output; the companion fixture file was not touched.

modules.description_quote: Exact-head CI then found that the imported EITC rate was flattened outside its source mechanics. The repair replaced that import with a local TY2026 rate parameter directly proving both the five-percent amount and the 2019–2030 effective period.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing was wrong relative to the source: the pre-fix formula multiplied the federal EITC by the imported 47:297.8 composite rate, which resolves to the same statutory five percent for TY2026, so only the provenance path (import vs. locally proved parameter) changed.
modules.triage_notes: Read the diff, both file versions, the imported module, the companion test file, the provision, and the CI check that drove the change. (1) Numeric meaning is provably unchanged: the companion fixture `2026_resident_core.test.yaml` is byte-identical across the fix (no entry in test_files; `git diff 8d3d0f5e30 bee5412e8b -- ...test.yaml` is empty) and asserts `la_2026_resident_nominal_earned_income_tax_credit: 250` on `federal_earned_income_tax_credit: 5000`, i.e. 5% both before and after. (2) The imported `us-la/statutes/47:297/8.yaml#earned_income_tax_credit_rate` is a three-version chain (0.035 from 0001-01-01, temporary 0.05 from 2019-01-01, 0.035 from 2031-01-01), so at the consuming rule's 2026-only window it already yielded 0.05.
