(3) Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, corpus commit 01e00777cb, fix_time_corpus_match: same_body): 47:297.8(A)(2) gives five percent for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2030, so 5% is correct for TY2026 under both encodings. (4) The driver was the encoder's `_check_flattened_thresholded_imported_rates` gate in axiom-encode (`src/axiom_encode/harness/validator_pipeline.py:37477`), whose `_imported_rate_source_is_thresholded` heuristic fires because the imported 47:297.8 module text contains "excess" (the (B) overpayment mechanics) while the consuming formula applies the rate flat — a provenance/architecture gate, not a source disagreement. (5) Caveat on the label: this is not literally metadata-only — an import was removed, a new parameter rule/output was added, and the formula now names a local symbol — so it does not fit the narrow 'mechanical' wording; I chose mechanical because the encoded meaning, versions, effective dates, scope, and fixture results are identical and the fix only re-grounds provenance. If a reviewer insists that added-output changes cannot be mechanical, the fallback label is 'unclear' with defect_kind none/other — but it should be pruned from a fidelity-defect corpus either way. (6) Non-module files in the same commit: the re-signed apply manifest (manual_exception flipped composition -> repair) and the oracle-pending ceiling bump 1856 -> 1857; both bookkeeping.

item.subject: Fix Louisiana resident core review findings

triage.commit_summary: The commit applies the independent-review findings on the newly encoded Louisiana TY2026 full-year resident income-tax module (PR #1026), gating every spouse-level exemption/deduction on joint filing status, making filing-status selection fail closed via a new selection-count/validity pair, and re-ordering the R.S. 47:293 construction-code retrofit arithmetic so the sponsored-incentive value is subtracted after the fifty-percent rate rather than before it. It also narrows the module's claims by renaming the aggregates to explicitly partial/pre-held names, removing the retrofit amount from aggregate deductions, and deferring tax-table income, tax-before-credits, and the retrofit amount because LAC 61:I.1937 is not in the pinned corpus.

modules.description_quote: Independent review found four initial issues: unqualified aggregate names, spouse items applied outside joint returns, incorrect retrofit operator ordering/unpinned regulatory eligibility, and filing-status fallback.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module added the spouse's disability-income exemption, active-duty-outside-Louisiana exclusion, and volunteer deduction for any taxpayer regardless of filing status, so a single, head-of-household, or married-filing-separately return picked up spouse-level amounts that only exist on a joint return (and, separately, it computed the 47:293 retrofit amount as fifty percent of cost minus incentives and fell back to the single/separate standard deduction when no recognized status was selected).
modules.triage_notes: Single-module commit with three distinct fidelity defects fixed at once, plus a scope-honesty renaming pass; I labeled the kind by the broadest-footprint defect. (1) wrong_entity_or_scope: three spouse branches gained 'la_2026_resident_filing_status_joint and ...' guards. (2) amount_mismatch: retrofit formula changed from rate * max(0, cost - incentives) to max(0, rate*max(0,cost) - max(0,incentives)); I read us-la/statute/47:293 through the pinned corpus release and it reads 'an amount equal to fifty percent of the cost paid or incurred ... less the value of any municipally sponsored, state-sponsored, or federally sponsored financial incentives', i.e. the incentive offset applies after the fifty percent, so the pre-fix ordering overstated the deduction whenever incentives were nonzero; the commit also adds a second proof atom quoting that 'less the value of...' clause. (3) polarity_or_logic: the pre-fix standard deduction had a fail-open else-branch returning the single/separate amount for any unrecognized or empty filing status; the fix adds selection_count/selection_valid rules and returns 0 (and zero partial tax-table income) unless exactly one status is set. The renames (positive_exempt_income -> encoded_positive_exempt_income, tax_table_income -> partial_tax_table_income_before_held_adjustments, etc.) plus the new deferred_outputs entries are scope-labeling/claim-narrowing, not meaning changes by themselves; but dropping the retrofit amount out of la_2026_resident_encoded_direct_deductions_before_held_adjustments does change the aggregate, and the retrofit rule also lost its 'if la_2026_resident_qualifying_retrofit_completed_in_tax_year' gate (which is itself grounded in 47:293(2)(b) 'claimed on the return for the taxable year in which the work is completed') because the rule is now nominal-only and excluded from aggregates - a reviewer may want to flag that as a coverage loss rather than a gain. Follow-up commits in the same PR: 8d3d0f5e3 'Fail closed Louisiana spouse components' (re-review found the spouse branches needed valid-status AND joint, not just joint) and bee5412e8 'Fix Louisiana EITC rate validation'. No PR reviews or review comments were captured in the bundle; the commit body is empty, so the quote comes from the PR body.

verdict.justification: The anchored rule's formula changed meaning exactly as described: each spouse-level branch in la_2026_resident_disability_income_exemption, la_2026_resident_active_duty_outside_louisiana_exclusion, and la_2026_resident_volunteer_deduction gained an `la_2026_resident_filing_status_joint and ...` conjunct, narrowing the population from any return to joint returns only. The companion fixture proves the pre-fix behavior was live and wrong, not defensive: the old case `disability_and_active_duty_caps_apply_per_spouse_at_and_above_boundary` set `filing_status_single: true` with spouse flags true and expected `disability_income_exemption: 12000` / `active_duty_outside_louisiana_exclusion: 100000`, and it was rewritten to `married_separate_ignores_spouse_disability_active_duty_and_volunteer_amounts` expecting 6000 / 50000 / volunteer 0. The pinned source supports the narrowing: 47:44.1(B) exempts disability income "received by an individual," and 47:293(6) defines "Individual" as a natural person who reaches the return only via the joint-return option ("a husband and wife may file a joint income tax return"), so a single/HOH/MFS return cannot carry a spouse's individual amount. Filing status and household member set are precisely wrong_entity_or_scope, and no other listed kind fits the anchored formula change better.
verdict.quote:
+            if la_2026_resident_filing_status_joint
+               and la_2026_resident_spouse_has_qualifying_permanent_total_disability_income:
verdict.notes:
Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "the gate is defensive, spouse inputs would be zero anyway" — refuted by the rewritten fixture, which had a single filer receiving 12000/100000 pre-fix; spouse flags are raw undeclared inputs with no zeroing rule in the module. (2) "renames only" — refuted; the renames (positive_exempt_income -> encoded_positive_exempt_income, tax_table_income -> partial_..._before_held_adjustments) are mechanical, but they sit alongside three formula changes with changed fixture values. (3) "new coverage never claimed" — refuted; the module claimed a filing-status-aware resident core and mis-scoped spouse items within it.

Reviewer caveats worth carrying: this commit bundles at least two ADDITIONAL, distinct fidelity defects that are not wrong_entity_or_scope, and if the corpus wants one kind per item they should probably be split out. (a) amount_mismatch in the retrofit rule: `la_2026_retrofit_deduction_rate * max(0, cost - incentives)` became `max(0, rate * max(0, cost) - max(0, incentives))`; the added proof atom excerpt is "less the value of any municipally sponsored, state-sponsored, or federally sponsored financial incentives for the retrofitting cost paid", and 47:293(2)(a)(i) reads "an amount equal to fifty percent of the cost paid or incurred" — the new fixture `retrofit_incentive_is_subtracted_after_half_of_cost_before_cap` gives 3000 where the old ordering gave 4000 (cost 10000, incentives 2000). (b) polarity_or_logic in la_2026_resident_standard_deduction: the old `else` fell open to `la_2026_standard_deduction_single_or_separate` when no status was selected; it now returns 0 unless la_2026_resident_filing_status_selection_valid holds (new fixtures all_filing_statuses_false_fails_closed and conflicting_filing_statuses_fail_closed, plus two existing fixtures that had to flip `filing_status_single: false` -> `true` to keep their old outputs). The retrofit change also dropped the `la_2026_resident_qualifying_retrofit_completed_in_tax_year` input branch and removed retrofit from the aggregate because LAC 61:I.1937 is absent from the pinned corpus — that piece reads as untraceable_branch / deferral rather than wrong scope.

Provenance caveat: f1ed255931 is a pre-merge review-fix commit inside PR #1026, the PR that ADDS this module (merged 2026-07-23). The defect was caught in review and never existed in a released module. It is still a real encoding defect with a real formula correction, but if the corpus is meant to hold post-release regressions only, this item is in scope by accident.

item.subject: Address Missouri resident core review findings

triage.commit_summary: This is the review-fix commit on PR #1025 (branch = encode commit 02b1ead1 plus this one) for the TY2026 Missouri noncombined full-year resident income-tax core: it rewrites the module's rationale/summary/deferred-output prose, renames five consumed inputs from raw-fact names to explicit `mo_2026_completed_partial_*` names and declares them in a new top-level `inputs:` block, adds a new deferred output stating the module supports only nonnegative federal AGI, and adds three proof atoms (§§143.113, 143.118, 143.174) to the taxable-income rule. Its stated purpose is to answer independent-review findings that completed boundaries were mislabeled as raw facts, that negative-FAGI treatment was unsupported, that the 143.022/143.177 "revenue-trigger" hold wording was stale (the real hold is missing pinned corpus evidence), and that proof atoms were missing — none of which changed any formula arithmetic, parameter, version, or effective date.

modules.description_quote: Independent review found incomplete branch coverage, completed boundaries mislabeled as raw, unsupported negative-FAGI treatment, stale trigger-hold wording, and missing proof atoms.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix module declared a scope it did not have — it asserted it 'never accepts completed Missouri ... amounts' while in fact consuming five caller-completed partial amounts (Missouri-benefit portion of a prior-year federal refund, Missouri-disallowed federal NOL, created-work appraisal itemized increase, other-jurisdiction Missouri-AGI numerator, reciprocal-credit-eligible other-jurisdiction tax) under raw-fact names, and implied coverage of returns with negative federal AGI that the pinned authority does not establish; but no encoded number disagreed with the statute, since the fix changed only names, declarations, prose, and proof atoms.
modules.triage_notes: Read the whole 225-line diff plus both full file versions (git show of parent 02b1ead118 and of 53b40448c3). Every formula change in the diff is a pure identifier rename (2 in the AGI core, 1 in the itemized deduction, 2 in the other-state credit); no parameter value, bracket, rate, cap, comparison operator, version window, or effective date changed, so outputs are numerically identical pre and post for the same input values. The other changes are: module.source_verification.rationale and module.summary rewritten (recasting the 143.022 business-income-subtraction and 143.177 working-family-credit hold from 'revenue-triggered percentages undetermined' to 'no pinned current-year corpus evidence'); a new deferred output mo_2026_resident_core_for_negative_federal_adjusted_gross_income whose reason states 'The pinned authority establishes Missouri modifications to federal adjusted gross income but does not establish a zero floor for negative federal adjusted gross income'; a new top-level inputs: block declaring the five renamed completed-partial inputs (the pre-fix file had no inputs: block at all); and three added proof atoms on rules[mo_2026_noncombined_resident_taxable_income_core] for us-mo/statute/143.113, 143.118 and 143.174 covering formula terms that were already present unchanged. Important caveat for the reviewer: the pre-fix AGI formula had NO max(0, ...) floor on federal AGI either, so the 'unsupported negative-FAGI treatment' finding was resolved by narrowing the declared scope (deferred output + 'nonnegative federal adjusted gross income' wording) rather than by removing an ungrounded branch; the pre-fix fixture named zero_income_floors_tax_and_credit used FAGI = 0, not a negative value, and was renamed zero_federal_agi_is_supported_without_negative_income_normalization. A strong case exists for pruning this to 'mechanical' (renames + module-level metadata + proof-atom provenance, with formulas/parameters/versions/outputs unchanged); I kept it 'unclear' only because the declared input contract and the declared scope did change and the PR names substantive-sounding findings. Companion test file changed in the same commit (renamed input keys, dropped YAML anchors, added the zero-FAGI branch fixture and more edge fixtures); the encoding manifest change is hash/signature/supersedes bookkeeping only. Provision read was attempted per step 4: resolve_provision.py for us-mo/statute/143.121 returned {"error": "unresolved"} — every candidate release reports "Active corpus source 'us-mo/statute/143.121' is repealed" — so the statute text was not read; it would not change the call, since no formula semantics changed.

verdict.justification: I normalized the five renamed variables and diffed the pre/post `rules:` sections: they are byte-identical except three added proof atoms (143.113, 143.118, 143.174 excerpts), so no formula, parameter, version window, effective date, or output changed — the module computes exactly the same numbers before and after (every retained fixture expectation, e.g. '1899.258', '313.008', '994.508', is unchanged; the 1,414 test-line growth is new fixtures plus the same renames). What actually changed is module-level prose (notes, summary, deferred_outputs), five pure input renames to `completed_partial_*` with a new declaration block describing the same quantities, and proof-atom excerpt/citation strings — every one of these is in the rubric's mechanical list. The "wrong_entity_or_scope" reading fails because no entity, population, filing status, or output surface changed: the "nonnegative federal AGI" restriction is a disclosure only, with no zero floor added or removed (the AGI formula is `mo_2026_federal_adjusted_gross_income + max(0, ...)` terms in both versions), and §143.081's reciprocal-benefit definition is unencoded before and after — the fix relabels who supplies the number, it does not correct encoded meaning against the source.
verdict.quote:
-          + max(0, mo_2026_prior_year_federal_income_tax_refund_with_missouri_benefit)
+          + max(0, mo_2026_completed_partial_prior_year_federal_refund_missouri_benefit_addition)
verdict.notes: Evidence trail for a reviewer: (1) Normalization test — mapping the 5 old names to the 5 new names and diffing `sed -n '99,$p' pre.yaml` vs `sed -n '126,818p' post.yaml` yields only the three added proof-atom blocks plus one blank line. No arithmetic, threshold, bracket, version, or effective-date change exists in this commit. (2) Negative-FAGI finding: pre and post both compute `mo_2026_federal_adjusted_gross_income + max(0, additions) - max(0, subtractions)` with no outer floor; the fix only adds a `deferred_outputs` entry (`mo_2026_resident_core_for_negative_federal_adjusted_gross_income`) and the words "nonnegative federal adjusted gross income" to the notes. A negative-FAGI return gets the identical answer from both versions, so nothing was corrected — coverage was disclaimed. (3) §143.081 check via the pinned resolver (release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, body sha 0f031f8c...): the statute does define "income tax imposed" subject to the other state authorizing "a reciprocal benefit for residents of this state", and neither version encodes that test — the pre input was literally named after the statutory phrase (`..._income_tax_imposed`), the post renames it and pushes the determination to the caller in prose. If a reviewer insists the input-contract rename plus its description ("after applying its reciprocal-benefit definition") counts as a meaning change, the next-best verdict is not_a_defect (a disclosure/boundary-honesty change with no source basis for calling the old encoding wrong), not wrong_entity_or_scope. (4) The first reader's quote is PR-level narrative for the whole branch ("incomplete branch coverage ... missing proof atoms"); branch coverage was addressed in the companion test file, proof atoms are provenance, and "stale trigger-hold wording" is prose — none of it is a module-formula correction. Files: /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us us-mo/policies/income_tax/2026_noncombined_resident_core.yaml at 02b1ead118 vs 53b40448c3.

item.subject: Encode Missouri 2026 noncombined resident core

triage.commit_summary: Commit 02b1ead118 adds a brand-new RuleSpec module, us-mo/policies/income_tax/2026_noncombined_resident_core.yaml (775 lines, 23 rules), encoding an explicitly partial Missouri tax-year-2026 noncombined full-year-resident income tax core that runs from federal AGI through Chapter 143 modifications, the standard/itemized deduction election, zero §151-conditioned exemptions, the surviving/head-of-household deduction, the income-tiered §143.171 federal-tax deduction, the eight-bracket §143.011 2026 schedule, and the §143.081 other-state tax credit. It is purely additive — the parent tree contains no Missouri 2026 income-tax core module and no existing rule, formula, parameter, version, or effective date was touched — and it ships alongside a 40-fixture companion test file, an encoding manifest, a regenerated reverse index, and 23 new oracle-coverage-pending declarations.

modules.description_quote: adds a source-certified, explicitly partial TY2026 Missouri noncombined full-year resident core
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: nothing was wrong pre-fix, because there was no pre-fix encoding — the parent commit 437399dc contains no Missouri 2026 income-tax core module, so this diff creates meaning rather than correcting it.
modules.triage_notes: RECOMMEND PRUNE from the defect corpus. Verified with `git ls-tree -r --name-only <parent|commit> -- us-mo/`: the only us-mo/policies/income_tax file in the parent is the untouched `pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml`; `2026_noncombined_resident_core.yaml` appears only in the post tree. The diff is a `new file mode` hunk with 775 added lines and zero removed lines (`grep -c '^-[^-]' 000.diff` returns 0), so no formula, parameter, version, effective date, input, output, or scope was changed relative to any prior encoding. Classified 'unclear' rather than 'mechanical' because 'mechanical' asserts that formulas/parameters stayed the same, which is factually false for a greenfield file, and rather than 'fidelity' because no encoded meaning was corrected; the taxonomy has no bucket for a new encoding, so 'unclear' is used per the instruction that additive changes are 'unclear at most'. The commit message body is empty (subject only: 'Encode Missouri 2026 noncombined resident core'); the only quotable prose is the PR body, and it describes an addition, not a defect. The PR body does reference defects — 'Independent review found incomplete branch coverage, completed boundaries mislabeled as raw, unsupported negative-FAGI treatment, stale trigger-hold wording, and missing proof atoms' — but those were fixed in intermediate branch commits before merge, so their pre-fix states are NOT reachable from this commit's parent; a harvester wanting real MO defects should mine the branch's intermediate commits (PR #1025) instead of this squashed/merged result. Step 4 (corpus provision read) was intentionally skipped: with no pre-fix encoding there is no encoded-vs-source disagreement to adjudicate, and reading §§143.011/143.121/143.171 would only audit the new encoding's correctness, which is outside this triage. Other files in the commit (encoding manifest, provisions_to_rules.json reverse index, oracle-coverage-pending.yaml +23 MO declarations, and the 180-line 40-fixture companion test) are all consistent with a first-time encoding. Module carries module.deferred_outputs for three outputs and an upstream_source_check rationale disclosing the partial boundary, reinforcing that it never claimed the deferred scope.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute the "unclear" call and instead found the evidence decisive in the other direction: the module file is a pure addition (`new file mode 100644`, `@@ -0,0 +1,775 @@`, zero removed content lines — the only `-` line in the diff is the `--- /dev/null` header), and `git show 437399dc:us-mo/policies/income_tax/2026_noncombined_resident_core.yaml` fails with "exists on disk, but not in '437399dc...'". item.subject: Clarify Pennsylvania core boundary

triage.commit_summary: The commit is the review-fix commit on PR #1024 (Pennsylvania TY2026 resident income-tax core): it rewrites the module summary and deferred-output reason to narrow the claimed input surface, and it changes the Pennsylvania income base so each of the eight section 303 income classes is floored at zero before summation, with a new proof atom grounding that formula in section 302. The companion test file gains a regression named loss_in_one_income_class_does_not_offset_another_class, so the substantive effect is that a loss in one statutory class can no longer offset income in another class, matching section 302's per-class imposition of tax on each dollar of income received in each class.

modules.description_quote: Independent review found six source/scope/test issues; the branch fixed them, including per-class nonnegative treatment and a negative-class regression.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix formula summed the eight section 303 class totals raw, so a net loss in one class (e.g. net gains from property) reduced taxable income from other classes, contrary to section 302(a), which imposes the tax on each dollar of income received in each of the classes enumerated in section 303.
modules.triage_notes: Single-module commit, second commit of PR #1024 (parent 3ce0238b adds the module; this commit is the review-fix/boundary-clarification pass). The only meaning-changing hunk is the formula, which becomes max(0, <class>) for all eight class inputs; everything else in the diff is provenance/metadata: module summary rewrite, deferred_output reason rewrite, eight input `description` rewrites (Raw -> Caller-computed), and one added proof atom (path versions[0].formula citing us-pa/statute/act-1971-2/article-3/section-302, excerpt 'a tax upon each dollar of income received by that resident'). Companion test adds case loss_in_one_income_class_does_not_offset_another_class with pa_pit_net_gains_from_property: -5000 and pa_pit_compensation: 10000 expecting base 10000 and tax 307, which pins the behavior change. Provisions read through the pinned corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix: section 302(a) does say tax is imposed 'for the privilege of receiving each of the classes of income hereinafter enumerated in section 303, a tax upon each dollar of income received'; section 303 as stored contains no explicit 'a loss in one class may not offset another class' sentence (PA's explicit no-offset statement lives in regulation/case law, not in this Article III text), so the grounding for the fix is section 302's per-class imposition plus section 303's class enumeration. That is why kind could alternatively be argued as 'other: cross-class loss offset'; I kept unrepresented_clause because the fix adds a per-class limitation the source structure requires and the encoding omitted. The commit message body is empty and the subject ('Clarify Pennsylvania core boundary') is generic, so the quote is from the PR body; the PR body's phrase 'per-class nonnegative treatment' names exactly this fix. No PR reviews or review comments were captured in the bundle.

verdict.justification: The diff changes encoded meaning exactly as the first reader described: the `pa_pit_resident_income_before_annual_deductions` formula went from a raw sum of the eight section 303 class totals to a per-class `max(0, ...)` sum, and the commit adds a new proof atom on `versions[0].formula` grounded in section 302 with the excerpt "a tax upon each dollar of income received by that resident", which the pinned corpus text of section 302(a) carries verbatim ("shall pay for the privilege of receiving each of the classes of income hereinafter enumerated in section 303, a tax upon each dollar of income received by that resident"). The pre-fix encoding therefore let a net loss in one class (its own input description said "Raw section 303(a)(3) net gains less net losses from dispositions", i.e. possibly negative) cancel income received in another class, taxing less than each dollar received in the profitable classes; the companion test added in the same commit pins the corrected behavior (compensation 10000 with net gains −5000 now yields income 10000 and tax 307, versus 5000/153 before). This is a required condition the source imposes that the encoding omitted and the fix adds, so unrepresented_clause fits better than boundary_direction (no pre-existing bound had the wrong side — no class-level floor existed at all) or untraceable_branch (nothing was removed or re-grounded).
verdict.quote:
-          pa_pit_compensation
+          max(0, pa_pit_compensation)
verdict.notes: Scope of the change: the rest of the commit (module summary rewrite, deferred_outputs reasons, and the eight input descriptions "Raw section 303(a)(N)..." -> "Caller-computed section 303(a)(N) ... class total") is prose/boundary metadata and would be mechanical on its own; the one substantive meaning change is the per-class floor, plus the new section 302 proof atom. Provenance caveat for a reviewer: this is an in-branch review fix — parent 3ce0238b3 "Add Pennsylvania resident income-tax core" added the module in the same PR #1024, so the defect never reached main; PR body's "Independent review found six source/scope/test issues ... including per-class nonnegative treatment and a negative-class regression" is the review evidence, matched line-for-line by this diff and the added test `loss_in_one_income_class_does_not_offset_another_class`. Source caveat: the pinned section 303 text contains no explicit "a loss in one class may not offset another class" clause (grepped for offset/other class/net loss); the grounding rests on section 302(a)'s per-class imposition language, which is what the new proof atom cites. If a reviewer insists a defect kind requires a literally stated clause, "other (per-class loss-offset prohibition implied by the imposition provision)" would be the fallback label, but the encoded meaning is still wrong against the source either way.

item.subject: Fix NC resident core tax boundaries

triage.commit_summary: The commit repaired the not-yet-merged North Carolina TY2026 resident core pipeline (added in the immediately preceding commit cf02b47e8) by adding the two §105-153.5(a)(2) clauses the encoding had omitted: the carve-out excluding a credit-backed qualified real-property donation from the charitable deduction, and the married-filing-separately combined $20,000 mortgage-interest/property-tax cap with its paid-percentage proration, each split into its own new derived rule with new inputs. It also stopped flooring "North Carolina taxable income" at zero, renaming that rule to nc_pit_2026_modified_income_before_tax_base (signed) and introducing a separate nc_pit_2026_tax_base = max(0, ...) that the 3.99% rate is applied to, plus 416 lines of added companion tests.

modules.description_quote: The independent cycle found and fixed signed-income flooring, MFS cap handling, the current charitable-deduction exclusion, incomplete boundary/status coverage, deduction-attribution semantics for credit-backed property, and an untested MFS under-cap branch.

Multi-part fix in one module: (1) charitable carve-out (unrepresented_clause), (2) MFS combined cap + proration (unrepresented_clause, with a scope flavor since the cap applies to both spouses combined), and (3) a restructuring that removes the max(0, ...) floor from the rule that claimed to encode 'North Carolina taxable income' and moves it into a separate nonnegative nc_pit_2026_tax_base; part (3) is value-neutral for tax before credits and reads more like untraceable_branch/naming hygiene, which is why confidence is 0.85 rather than higher. The commit message body is empty, so the quote comes from the PR body's review-fix-cycle paragraph, which describes the cycle for PR #1023 as a whole rather than this commit alone. The commit also rewrote the companion test file (+416 lines) and the encoding manifest. Follow-up commit c294a83ec 'Clarify NC charitable and MFS deductions' (same day, same PR branch) refines the carve-out input from the donation's value to the section 170 deduction amount attributable to it, i.e. the 'deduction-attribution semantics' finding named in the same PR sentence was only fully resolved there; later commits d1ed1b594 and 450ca0144 touched source locators for this file.

(Effective for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025, and expiring for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2027 ...) Certain Real Property Donations. - A qualified donation that is the basis for an allocated credit under G.S. 105-153.11 is not eligible for a deduction under this subdivision." and "For spouses filing as married filing separately or married filing jointly, the total mortgage interest and real estate taxes claimed by both spouses combined may not exceed twenty thousand dollars ($20,000). ... these deductions must be prorated based on the percentage paid by each spouse." The pre-fix itemized formula deducted `max(0, charitable_contributions)` with no §105-153.11 carve-out and applied `min(cap, interest + taxes)` per return with no MFS combined-cap or proration branch, so for TY2026 (inside the clause's 2025–2026 window) both branches overstate the deduction against the cited text. This is not new scope the module never claimed: the pre-fix module already ran the married-separate schedule (rule `nc_pit_2026_narrow_status_index`, "single or married-separate statutory row") and already computed a charitable itemized deduction, so the fix adds statutorily required conditions to claimed outputs rather than extending coverage. unrepresented_clause is the right kind for both changes — no comparison strictness was flipped (the new `<=` correctly mirrors "if the amount ... exceeds $20,000"), no number changed (the $20,000 cap parameter is untouched), and nothing untraceable was removed.

item.subject: Fix Georgia low-income credit semantics

triage.commit_summary: This commit is the review-fix round inside PR #1022 (Georgia TY2026 resident household tax core): it corrects the O.C.G.A. 48-7A-3 low-income credit so the schedule band is selected on federal adjusted gross income rather than the module's post-adjustment Georgia AGI, and so the credit multiplier counts the statutory/IT-511 credit units (self, spouse on a joint return, natural or legally adopted children excluding unborn dependents) plus the age-65 units, instead of reusing the caller-classified Georgia dependent count used for the $5,000 exemption deduction. It also re-points the 50 percent child/dependent-care proof atom at the 2025 HB 136 session law, adds the IT-511 and HB 136 corpus citations with an upstream_source_check status of checked_higher_authority, and expands the companion fixtures with band-boundary and unit cases.

modules.description_quote: Independent review found and the branch fixed: use of Georgia instead of federal AGI for low-income bands; missing self/spouse/age units and unborn-dependent exclusion; stale proof for the 50% care credit; and insufficient boundary/status/disqualifier fixtures.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix credit multiplied the schedule amount by the caller-classified Georgia dependent count (plus age-65 adders), so it never represented 48-7A-3(a)(1)'s clause deeming each spouse on a joint return a dependent nor the taxpayer's own credit unit, and it never excluded unborn dependents that the IT-511 low-income worksheet carves out of the exemption count, understating (and for a single filer with no dependents zeroing) the credit.
modules.triage_notes: Read the module diff, the pre-fix and post-fix YAML, the companion test diff, and the pinned corpus text of O.C.G.A. 48-7A-3 (resolve_provision.py succeeded; 48-7A-1 resolved but is a repealed definitions section, so the statute alone does not say whether 'adjusted gross income' means federal AGI - the fix leans on the 2025 IT-511 worksheet for that). This commit fixes TWO co-equal fidelity defects in one module and I had to pick one kind: (1) the unrepresented clause coded above, and (2) the band selector reading ga_2026_resident_adjusted_gross_income (federal AGI plus completed Georgia additions minus subtractions) instead of ga_2026_resident_federal_adjusted_gross_income, best read as untraceable_branch / formula grounded on the wrong basis, with the proof atom re-grounded from us-ga/statute/48/48-7A-3 to us-ga/form/it-511/2025/document-1 (rules[ga_2026_resident_low_income_credit_band].versions[0].formula). A reviewer who prefers that framing should reclassify the kind; the classification 'fidelity' is not in doubt either way. Both behavior changes are pinned by new fixtures: federal_agi_controls_band_when_georgia_agi_differs (federal 5999 with 25000 of Georgia additions still lands in band 0) and low_income_units_include_self_spouse_and_age_but_exclude_unborn (joint, 3 children of which 1 unborn, both spouses 65 -> 4 exemption units + 2 age units = $156), and two pre-existing fixtures' expected credits moved from $5 to $10. Not every change in the module is fidelity: the child/dependent-care rule's formula and percentage import are byte-identical and only its source string and one proof-atom corpus_citation_path moved to us-ga/statute/session-laws/2025/hb136/document-1 (the 'stale proof' item, provenance-only/mechanical), and the module rationale prose plus the upstream_source_check status change from composed_from_supplied_current_authority to checked_higher_authority are metadata. Two new caller inputs were introduced (low_income_natural_or_legally_adopted_child_count_including_unborn, low_income_unborn_dependent_count). No boundary strictness changed - the band comparisons keep < 6000 and the >= / <= pairs matching the statute's 'but not more than' schedule rows. No follow-up commits inspected; the PR states the exact-head re-review at this SHA returned no actionable findings.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute the reading and could not: at the anchored rule the pre-fix formula multiplied the schedule amount by `max(0, ga_2026_resident_georgia_dependent_count)` plus age indicators, and the fix replaces that count with `ga_2026_resident_low_income_exemption_units` = 1 (self) + 1 if joint + natural/adopted children minus unborn, so the change adds clauses the cited sources state and the encoding omitted. Both clauses are verbatim in the pinned corpus: O.C.G.A. 48-7A-3(a)(1) "A husband and wife filing a joint return shall each be deemed a dependent for purposes of such joint return", and 2025 IT-511 worksheet line 2 "Enter the number of exemptions. Exemptions are self, spouse and natural or legally adopted children.......... Note: For purposes of the low income credit, dependents do not include those unborn with a detectable heartbeat" — and the fix adds a proof atom of `kind: exception` for exactly that carve-out. The module already claimed this surface (pre-fix rule `source: O.C.G.A. § 48-7A-3(b), low-income schedule amount before liability cap`), so this is a correction, not new coverage, and the companion fixture flips from `low_income_credit: '5'` to `'10'`, confirming an encoded-meaning change in the understatement direction described.
verdict.quote:
-                max(0, ga_2026_resident_georgia_dependent_count)
-                + (if ga_2026_resident_taxpayer_age_65_or_older: 1 else: 0)
-                + (if ga_2026_resident_spouse_age_65_or_older: 1 else: 0)
+                ga_2026_resident_low_income_exemption_units
+                + ga_2026_resident_low_income_age_units
verdict.notes:
Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "new coverage, not a defect" — no; the pre-fix rule already carried `source: O.C.G.A. § 48-7A-3(b)` and computed the credit, it just used the wrong unit set (the caller-classified Georgia dependent count that Form 500 line 7a explicitly excludes self and spouse from, and that includes unborn dependents via line 7b). (2) "mechanical/provenance" — no; formulas changed and two new derived rules were added, with fixtures changing value (5 → 10). (3) "the self unit has no source basis" — the statute alone says "multiplied by the number of dependents", but the module now cites the official 2025 IT-511 worksheet, which is in the pinned corpus and says exemptions are self, spouse and children; that is the cited source the fidelity test runs against.

One real caveat for the reviewer: this commit bundles more than one defect kind. The second change, `ga_2026_resident_adjusted_gross_income` → `ga_2026_resident_federal_adjusted_gross_income` in `ga_2026_resident_low_income_credit_band`, is a different flavor — the band was grounded on Georgia AGI with no basis in the source table, which reads "Credit Table: Federal Adjusted Gross Income Credit" (and "You may claim the Low Income Credit if your Federal adjusted gross income is less than $20,000"); scored on its own that one is closer to untraceable_branch (formula grounded on the wrong quantity/provision). Note also 48-7A-1, the chapter's definitions section, is repealed in the corpus, so the federal-AGI base is settled by IT-511, not by statute. A third, minor change is provenance-only and correctly not the anchor: the care-credit proof atom's citation path moved from `us-ga/statute/48/48-7-29.10` to `us-ga/statute/session-laws/2025/hb136/document-1` with the same excerpt, which is mechanical.

Context: this is an intra-PR review-fix commit on PR #1022 (a module addition), so the defect never reached main; if the corpus is meant to hold defects that shipped, that is a selection question, not a classification one. Corpus release used for verification: us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, `fix_time_corpus_match: same_body` for both 48-7A-3 and the IT-511 document.

item.subject: Correct Idaho projected subtraction sourcing

triage.commit_summary: The commit strips an unsupported Idaho Code 63-3022D attribution from the composed Idaho income-tax pilot liability pipeline: it removes 63-3022D from the module's corpus_citation_paths/checked_paths, deletes the proof atom that grounded the taxable-income subtraction on that provision (excerpt "deduction from taxable income"), flips proof_validation.required from true to false, rewrites the rationale/summary/source prose to declare the entire AGI-to-taxable-income subtraction a caller-supplied, unverified projection, and drops the corresponding edge from .axiom/index/provisions_to_rules.json. It did this because 63-3022D is Idaho's $12,000-capped employment-related (dependent-care) expense deduction and does not authorize the general standard-deduction-style subtraction the pipeline applies; no formula, parameter, version, effective date, input, output, or test fixture value changed (the PR states it closes truthfulness gaps "without changing the underlying tax formulas").

THE COUNTERARGUMENT for reclassifying as fidelity/untraceable_branch: the defect-kind list says untraceable_branch includes 'formulas grounded on the wrong provision', and a fidelity judge shown the PRE-fix module plus its cited sources could legitimately flag that id_pit_pilot_taxable_income's subtraction has no basis in 63-3022D. item.subject: Encode Missouri 2026 individual tax schedule

triage.commit_summary: The commit rewrites the Missouri income-tax pilot module so that the full official 2026 eight-bracket schedule of Mo. Rev. Stat. 143.011 (upper bounds, floors, cumulative bases, marginal rates) is encoded as parameter tables with an explicit bracket-selection rule, instead of the prior design in which the active bracket's base, floor, and rate were supplied by the caller as inputs. It also moves the rules from TaxUnit to Person grain, bounds every version to tax year 2026 with effective_to '2026-12-31', renames the output from mo_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability to mo_pit_pilot_income_tax_before_credits_indiv, and rewrites the companion tests to hit every bracket boundary (plus oracle-pending ledger and signed-manifest bookkeeping).

modules.description_quote: replace caller-supplied active-bracket inputs with the complete official 2026 Missouri eight-bracket schedule
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module claimed to implement the section 143.011 schedule and cited its bracket rows as proof atoms, but encoded none of the statute's eight brackets or their selection conditions: it applied one caller-supplied base/floor/rate linear piece to any taxable income, so for income outside the supplied bracket it returned a figure the statute's table does not produce (e.g. $263 rather than $89.68 on $5,000 of taxable income).
modules.triage_notes: Read the cited provisions through the pinned corpus release: us-mo/statute/143.011 subsection 1 lists exactly the eight rows the fix adds (0/1,348/2,696/4,044/5,392/6,740/8,088/9,436 with bases 0,0,27,61,101,148,202,263 and rates 0,2.0,2.5,3.0,3.5,4.0,4.5,4.7%), so every added parameter value matches the source, and the new bracket selection uses 'ti <= upper[k]', matching the source's 'Over $X but not over $Y' inclusive-upper phrasing. The commit bundles several other changes that each have an independent fidelity flavor and could support a different kind label: entity moves TaxUnit -> Person (143.011 'imposed ... on the Missouri taxable income of every resident' and 143.021 'Every resident having a taxable income shall determine his or her tax' are per-individual, so the old TaxUnit grain was wrong_entity_or_scope); every version gains effective_to '2026-12-31' where the pre-fix versions were open-ended even though 143.011 subsection 5 inflation-adjusts the brackets annually (wrong_period_or_effective_date); and the output rule is renamed from '..._income_tax_liability' to '..._income_tax_before_credits_indiv', dropping an over-claimed 'liability' surface. I chose unrepresented_clause because the PR's lead bullet and the bulk of the diff are about the missing statutory schedule. Counter-argument a reviewer should weigh: the pre-fix module's own rationale openly declared the bracket values 'caller-supplied current-authority inputs' (status composed_from_supplied_current_authority), so this can be read as a pilot being upgraded in scope rather than a targeted defect fix; the commit subject is 'Encode Missouri 2026 individual tax schedule', the commit body is empty, and the PR has zero reviews/comments (its own text says 'Draft only. Independent review-fix cycle is pending and required before readiness.') yet it was merged 2026-07-22. Hence confidence held at 0.6. No follow-up commits touch this file; its only prior commit is 699cc028f which created the pilot. Non-module changes in the commit: oracle-coverage-pending.yaml ledger entries (ceiling 1699 -> 1703, renamed legal_ids) and the signed encoding manifest, both bookkeeping.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix module did not silently omit the eight brackets: its header declared `status: composed_from_supplied_current_authority` and its rationale said it "accepts completed-return Missouri taxable income and the active bracket's cumulative base tax, floor, and marginal rate as caller-supplied current-authority inputs", the same sanctioned pilot pattern the sibling us-dc module uses at the same parent commit, so internalizing the schedule is largely coverage the module expressly declared out of scope (and the reader's $5,000 → $263 example requires a caller to supply a non-active bracket, violating that stated contract). What the diff changes that the source does contradict is grain and output surface: every rule moves from `entity: TaxUnit` to `entity: Person` and the output is renamed from `mo_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` to `mo_pit_pilot_income_tax_before_credits_indiv`, while the pinned corpus text of Mo. Rev. Stat. 143.011 imposes the tax "on the Missouri taxable income of every resident" and 143.021 says "Every resident having a taxable income shall determine his or her tax from the rates provided in section 143.011". Applying a per-resident graduated schedule to a TaxUnit aggregate mis-states the tax for any multi-earner unit (the pre-fix grid used only one-earner joint cases, which masked it; the fix adds `dual_person_y_companion_9100` / `dual_person_s_companion_3900`), and "liability" over-claimed an output that excludes credits. So it is a fidelity defect, but wrong_entity_or_scope is the kind that survives the module's own scope disclaimer.
verdict.quote:
-  - name: mo_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability
+  - name: mo_pit_pilot_income_tax_before_credits_indiv
     kind: derived
-    entity: TaxUnit
+    entity: Person
verdict.notes:
Both kinds are genuinely present in this one commit; the reviewer should decide which the corpus item is meant to capture.

Case for keeping the first reader's unrepresented_clause (the strongest counter to my reclassify): the pinned corpus record for us-mo/statute/143.011 (release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, body sha d6a5131…) contains all eight rows verbatim ("$0 to $1,348: $0" … "Over $9,436: $263 plus 4.7% of excess over $9,436"), and the pre-fix rule `mo_pit_pilot_schedule_tax` cited four of those rows as `kind: formula` proof atoms on `versions[0].formula` under `proof_validation: required: true`, while that formula was only `mo_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_base + mo_pit_pilot_supplied_marginal_rate * max(0, mo_pit_pilot_taxable_income - mo_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_floor)` — i.e. it asserted formula-level evidence from bracket rows it did not encode, and 143.021.2(1)'s zero-tax band was likewise unrepresented. If the reviewer holds that formula proof atoms citing a row constitute a claim to implement that row, unrepresented_clause stands and the verdict should be confirmed.

Case against: the disclaimer is explicit and repo-wide, not an oversight. us-dc/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml at the parent commit e9b82eac uses the identical status and says "All tax-law amounts are inputs so the composition is source-grounded without embedding an unencoded annual schedule". The commit subject is "Encode Missouri 2026 individual tax schedule" and the PR says "replace … with …"; no message, review, or comment anywhere calls the prior state wrong (PR #994 has zero reviews and was merged as a same-day draft-cycle PR). Post-fix values match the source table exactly, so nothing numeric was corrected — amount_mismatch is ruled out.

Two further meaning changes the reader did not cite, both secondary: every version gains `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` where the pre-fix versions were open-ended (143.011.5 requires annual bracket adjustment, so a timeless 2026 schedule would be wrong_period_or_effective_date — but pre-fix the values lived outside the module, so this mostly follows from the new parameter tables); and the caller input is renamed `mo_pit_pilot_supplied_taxable_income` → `mo_pit_pilot_individual_taxable_income` with a real `inputs:` block added (pre-fix the module declared no inputs at all; the supplied symbols existed only in test fixtures).

If the harness wants one label per commit and prefers the largest edit, unrepresented_clause is defensible at ~0.5; I put wrong_entity_or_scope slightly ahead because it needs no assumption about caller misuse and no contested reading of what the module claimed. Not mechanical and not not_a_defect under any reading: formulas, entities, versions and the output surface all changed.

PR #990 records two review rounds, the second CLEAN on this exact head, with reviews/review_comments empty in the bundle (the review history is summarized in the PR body only).

item.subject: Promote Mississippi 2026 income tax schedule

triage.commit_summary: The commit rewrites the single Mississippi pilot income-tax module from a "composed_from_supplied_current_authority" shell — which took the active bracket's cumulative base, floor, and marginal rate as caller-supplied inputs and applied them at the TaxUnit grain — into an "official_parameter_source" module that owns the section 27-7-5(1) calendar-year-2026 schedule itself ($10,000 zero-tax ceiling and a 4% rate above it) as two new parameter rules, moves the schedule to the Person grain, bounds every version with effective_to 2026-12-31, and aggregates to the TaxUnit through a new Person→TaxUnit data_relation. It additionally adds a separate-vs-joint candidate comparison that selects the separate total only when strictly lower, which the module's own rationale describes as target-integration mechanics rather than a section 27-7-5 rule; the companion test file, encoding manifest, and oracle-coverage-pending ledger were updated to match.

modules.description_quote: promote the source-backed Mississippi schedule-before-credits pipeline
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix schedule formula computed tax as ms_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_base + ms_pit_pilot_supplied_marginal_rate * max(0, taxable_income - ms_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_floor), so the three numbers the statute actually fixes for 2026 (the $10,000 zero-tax amount and the 4% rate) carried no basis in the cited source even though the rule's proof atoms quoted those very amounts from 27-7-5 — but the module had explicitly declared that boundary via upstream_source_check.status: composed_from_supplied_current_authority, so the promotion may be planned scope expansion rather than a correction.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, provision file 2026-07-16-pit-central-us-ms-section-27-7-5.jsonl). The source confirms the post-fix numbers: 27-7-5(1)(a)(i)(6) plus (1)(b)(i) give a $10,000 zero-tax amount for 2026, and (1)(b)(ii)(3) gives 4% above $10,000 for calendar year 2026 only (2027 is 3.75%). Four distinct changes are bundled in this one module: (a) re-grounding the supplied bracket base/floor/rate into source-owned parameter rules ms_pit_pilot_zero_tax_ceiling=10000 and ms_pit_pilot_2026_rate=0.04, with status moving from composed_from_supplied_current_authority to official_parameter_source; (b) moving the taxable-income and schedule-tax rules from entity TaxUnit to entity Person (the statute levies 'upon the entire net income of every resident individual'), with a new ms_pit_pilot_person_of_tax_unit data_relation and sum_where aggregation; (c) adding effective_to: '2026-12-31' to every version where the pre-fix versions were open-ended despite the schedule being calendar-year-2026-specific ('All executable versions fail closed outside tax year 2026'); (d) adding a separate-vs-joint lower-of comparison. I classify unclear rather than fidelity because the commit body is empty, the subject and PR body frame the change purely as a promotion ('Promote', 'promote the source-backed ... pipeline') with no defect, error, or correction language anywhere, and the pre-fix module had honestly declared its supplied-parameter boundary in its own status field and rationale — which puts it close to the rubric's carve-out for scope the module never claimed. Decisive counter-evidence for change (d): the follow-up commit 26565db8a 'Canonicalize Mississippi 2026 tax schedule' (2026-07-26) deletes this pilot module entirely and replaces it with us-ms/policies/income_tax/2026_section_27_7_5_schedule.yaml, whose rationale states 'The former pilot compared two PolicyEngine-specific completed-return candidates and selected the lower computed amount. That comparison was oracle-integration mechanics, not a rule established by this source, and is intentionally absent here.' So the largest structural addition in this commit was itself ungrounded and removed four days later; the successor keeps only changes (a), (b) and (c). If a reviewer keeps this row, untraceable_branch is the kind that fits the durable core (values with no basis in the cited source, re-grounded by the fix); wrong_entity_or_scope (TaxUnit -> Person) and wrong_period_or_effective_date (unbounded versions -> effective_to 2026-12-31) are the alternate kinds also present, which is a further reason this is a mixed, non-clean benchmark row. The PR body line 'independent review found and fixed the relation-argument order' refers to a fix made inside the PR to its own new code, not to a pre-existing defect on main, so it is not usable as defect evidence. Also changed outside the module: the companion test file (10 -> 16 fixtures), the encoding manifest, and oracle-coverage-pending.yaml (ceiling 1664 -> 1672, new rule ids registered as manual/unmapped).

verdict.justification: The pre-fix module did not contain an untraceable branch: it declared the bracket base, floor, and rate as caller-supplied current-authority inputs (`status: composed_from_supplied_current_authority`), and its own fixtures fed exactly the statutory 2026 values (base 0, floor 10000, rate 0.04), producing 4% of taxable income above $10,000 — which is what 27-7-5(1)(a)(i)6, (1)(b)(i), and (1)(b)(ii)3 require, as confirmed against the pinned corpus release. The commit therefore promotes a declared composition boundary to `official_parameter_source` (internalizing $10,000 and 4% as parameters, which is why `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` windows appear) and adds scope the module never claimed: Person grain, a Person→TaxUnit relation, and separate-vs-joint candidate aggregation for the pinned PolicyEngine target. If anything the direction of "untraceable_branch" is inverted — the change ADDS the strict-lower selector, whose own rationale concedes "The relation and strict-lower comparison are target-integration mechanics, not a claim that section 27-7-5 creates a filing election," and 27-7-5 contains no filing election. Every new rule, including the promoted parameters, was added to `oracle-coverage-pending.yaml` as newly pending, consistent with a rewrite/promotion rather than a correction of encoded meaning that disagreed with the source.
verdict.quote:
-      status: composed_from_supplied_current_authority
+      status: official_parameter_source
verdict.notes: Decisive corroboration beyond the module diff: (1) the parent-commit fixture `single_30000` supplies `ms_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_base: 0`, `..._bracket_floor: 10000`, `..._marginal_rate: 0.04` and expects `ms_pit_pilot_schedule_tax: '468'` = 4% * (21,700 - 10,000) — the identical arithmetic the post-fix module now performs internally, so no output for the pre-fix module's declared slice was wrong against 27-7-5. (2) Statute read through the pinned release (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, provision body sha a0a11e16...) confirms 2026 = 4% on taxable income over $10,000 with no tax through $10,000, and contains no separate/joint comparison anywhere in 27-7-5. (3) The post-fix `ms_pit_pilot_separate_total_is_strictly_lower` rule is proof-anchored only on the excerpt "a tax at the following rates", which does not support a lower-of-two-methods election — a reviewer may want to flag this new rule as a forward-looking grounding weakness, but it is introduced by this commit, not removed by it. (4) All ten new/renamed rule ids land in `oracle-coverage-pending.yaml` with `since: '2026-07-22'`; the commit/PR language is uniformly "promote", with no statement that anything was wrong. Residual uncertainty: if the program's policy is that a rate-section module may never delegate its own statutory rate/threshold to a caller, someone could read the old `composed_from_supplied_current_authority` status as itself a fidelity gap; even then the honest label would be the first reader's "unclear", never "confirmed", since the declared boundary and the matching fixture values show the pre-fix encoding asserted nothing contrary to the source.

item.subject: Address Vermont PIT validation review

Minor note: the two new parameter versions carry effective_to '2026-12-31' while the consuming derived rule has no effective_to, which bounds the pilot parameters to 2026 but does not change 2026 behavior. Companion changes outside this module (oracle-coverage-pending.yaml ceiling 1609->1611 plus the two new legal_ids; regenerated .axiom encoding manifest) are ledger/manifest bookkeeping. No PR reviews or review comments exist in the bundle; the only issue comment is a clean post-merge-cycle attestation. Chunk contained the single expected module index [0].

item.subject: Tighten Oklahoma taxable-income boundary proof

triage.commit_summary: The commit removes an ungrounded zero floor from the Oklahoma 2026 pilot income-tax pipeline: final liability becomes a direct alias of the statutory schedule instead of max(0, schedule_tax), the caller-supplied taxable-income input is redeclared as nonnegative, and the remaining max(0, ...) on the taxable-income rule is re-described as a defensive identity over that boundary rather than a statutory transformation. modules.description_quote: Initial independent review found an unsupported caller-boundary floor claim. The input is now explicitly nonnegative, the validator-required defensive floor is documented as an identity over that boundary, the unsupported negative fixture was removed, and final liability is a direct schedule alias.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module computed final liability as max(0, ok_pit_pilot_schedule_tax) and described the upstream taxable-income max(0, ...) as a statutory flooring of Oklahoma taxable income, attributing to 68 O.S. section 2355(D) a zero-floor/negative-income normalization rule that the cited provision does not state.
modules.triage_notes: Single module in the commit. item.subject: Draft North Carolina PIT taxable-income boundary

triage.commit_summary: The commit rewrites the North Carolina personal income tax encoding for tax year 2026: the section 105-153.7 statute module drops its multi-version rate schedule (which had 4.6% for 2024, 4.5% for 2025, 4.25% for 2026 and 3.99% only after 2026) and keeps a single TY2026 version at 3.99%, matching the corpus table row "After 2025 3.99%", while bounding the individual-tax rule to 2026 because subsection (a1) can retrigger the rate from 2027. The composed pilot pipeline is simultaneously re-cut from an AGI-minus-supplied-standard-deduction, bracket-base/bracket-floor/credit construction citing 105-153.5(a) to a one-input contract that takes completed-return North Carolina taxable income, floors it at zero, and multiplies by the rate imported from the encoded 105-153.7 module; both modules' pending validate_failures waivers (issue 782) are removed in the same commit.

modules.description_quote: promotes North Carolina 2026 personal income tax to the exact taxable-income boundary
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix pipeline computed liability from structure the cited sections do not contain -- a bracket base plus a caller-supplied marginal rate above a bracket floor and a subtracted nonrefundable credit under 105-153.7, which imposes a single flat percentage on North Carolina taxable income and says nothing about brackets or credits -- and derived 'North Carolina taxable income' as AGI minus a supplied standard deduction while its own proof excerpt from 105-153.5(a) says the taxpayer may deduct 'either the standard deduction amount or the itemized deduction amount'.
modules.triage_notes: Read the pinned corpus text of us-nc/statute/105/105-153.7 (release us-rulespec-2026-07-19-dedup, provision sha e174d86f...): subsection (a) is a flat percentage table with no bracket base/floor, and credits live outside 105-153.7, so the pre-fix bracket-base + supplied-marginal-rate + supplied-credit construction and its 105-153.5(a) grounding had no basis in the cited provisions; the fix removes nc_pit_pilot_schedule_tax entirely, re-grounds nc_pit_pilot_taxable_income on a supplied completed-return boundary, and pins the rate by importing us-nc:statutes/105/105-153/7#individual_income_tax_rate instead of accepting it from the caller. Kind is the uncertain part, not whether meaning changed: unrepresented_clause is defensible for the omitted itemized/child-deduction alternative (the fix retracts the derivation rather than adding the clause), and wrong_entity_or_scope is defensible because the output surface moves from post-nonrefundable-credit liability to a before-credits target. A reviewer could also argue this is a deliberate pilot-contract redesign (the old rationale explicitly wired 'the same supplied-schedule form as the Arizona and Kentucky flat pilots') rather than a defect -- hence confidence 0.5. Corroborating evidence that it was treated as broken: known-validation-gaps.yaml drops this module's pending validate_failures waiver (issue 782) in this same commit. The commit body is empty; the PR body is generic ('Draft until required CI is green and current'). Follow-up commit d1ed1b594 'Repair NC TY2026 statute source backing' (2026-07-26) touches this pipeline again.

modules.description_quote: The fixed subsection (a) schedule sets the rate at 3.99% after 2025.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix rate schedule was shifted one row off the statutory table -- it encoded 0.046 from 2024, 0.045 from 2025, 0.0425 from 2026 and 0.0399 only from 2027, so the operative TY2026 rate was 4.25% -- while the cited provision's table reads 'In 2024 4.5% In 2025 4.25% After 2025 3.99%', making 3.99% the 2026 rate.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned resolver (us-nc/statute/105/105-153.7, corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-19-dedup, resolved_text_sha256 e174d86f38..., fix_time_corpus_match same_body): the table is 'In 2022 4.99% In 2023 4.75% In 2024 4.5% In 2025 4.25% After 2025 3.99%'. The pre-fix proof atoms quoted excerpts that do not appear in that text at all ('In 2024 4.6%', 'In 2025 4.5%', 'In 2026 4.25%', 'After 2026 3.99%') -- i.e. the superseded pre-2023-134 schedule -- and the deleted companion test asserted $4,600 tax on $100,000 for TY2024 (4.6%), confirming the encoded cells disagreed with the source. Competing kind: wrong_period_or_effective_date, since the defect can be read as version windows carrying superseded text; I chose amount_mismatch because the decisive consequence is that the value applied in the module's own target year changed from 0.0425 to 0.0399. Other changes in this module are collateral: individual_income_tax's window narrowed from effective_from 2014-01-01 to 2026-01-01/2026-12-31 (deferring subsection (a1) trigger years), and short_period_return_month_threshold was renamed to short_period_return_month_count with its value of 12 and its predicate logic unchanged (mechanical). Waiver for this file removed from known-validation-gaps.yaml in the same commit. Follow-up d1ed1b594 (2026-07-26) later re-labeled the proof atom row/excerpt from 'After 2025 3.99%' to 'In 2026 3.99%' without changing the 0.0399 value -- provenance only.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix pipeline claimed N.C. Gen. Stat. 105-153.7 as the source for a bracket-base-plus-marginal-rate-above-a-floor formula and a subtracted nonrefundable credit, but the pinned corpus text of 105-153.7 imposes only "a percentage of the taxpayer's North Carolina taxable income computed as follows" with a year table (After 2025 3.99%) and contains no bracket base, no bracket floor, and no credit; the statutory rate itself was a caller-supplied variable, so the module encoded none of the operative law it cited. The fix deletes the entire nc_pit_pilot_schedule_tax rule, drops the credit subtraction, and re-grounds liability as taxable income times the rate imported from the encoded 105-153.7 module under a pinned proof hash, which is exactly the untraceable_branch pattern (remove or re-ground structure with no basis in the cited source). I tried wrong_period_or_effective_date (the fix does add effective_to 2026-12-31 because subsection (a1) can change the rate in 2027) and unrepresented_clause (the pre-fix taxable-income rule hard-wired the standard deduction although its own 105-153.5(a) excerpt allows "either the standard deduction amount ... or the itemized deduction amount"), but both are secondary: the period bound is a consequence of baking in the imported rate, and the fix removes the deduction step rather than adding the missing alternative. Mechanical is ruled out because a rule is deleted, both surviving formulas change, and the input set collapses from five supplied values to one.

-          max(0, nc_pit_pilot_schedule_tax - nc_pit_pilot_supplied_nonrefundable_credit)
+          nc_pit_pilot_taxable_income * individual_income_tax_rate
