Nothing in the section mentions brackets or credits, and the removed formula "nc_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_base + nc_pit_pilot_supplied_marginal_rate * max(0, nc_pit_pilot_taxable_income - nc_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_floor)" carried a proof atom whose 105-153.7 excerpt ("A tax is imposed for each taxable year on the North Carolina taxable income of every individual") does not support bracket mechanics. This change is multi-kind: alongside the untraceable structure it also (a) bounds both versions with effective_to 2026-12-31 for the (a1) 2027 trigger (wrong_period_or_effective_date flavor, but only because the rate is now baked in via import) and (b) retires an AGI-minus-standard-deduction derivation whose own 105-153.5(a) excerpt offered an either/or the encoding ignored (unrepresented_clause flavor, though the fix deletes rather than completes it). Confidence is 0.68 rather than higher because a substantial part of the change is architectural (moving the upstream boundary to caller-supplied state taxable income, importing rather than accepting the rate) and the PR reports population parity with a maximum absolute difference under one dollar, so a reviewer could read it as a precision/scope promotion; what defeats that reading is that the module already asserted 105-153.7 as the source for a credit and bracket structure the section does not contain. Second module in the commit (us-nc/statutes/105/105-153/7.yaml) was not assessed here.

verdict.justification: The pinned corpus text of N.C. Gen. Stat. § 105-153.7(a) reads "Taxable Years Beginning Tax In 2022 4.99% In 2023 4.75% In 2024 4.5% In 2025 4.25% After 2025 3.99%", while the pre-fix module encoded 0.046 from 2024-01-01, 0.045 from 2025-01-01, 0.0425 from 2026-01-01 and 0.0399 only from 2027-01-01 — the superseded pre-S.L. 2023-134 schedule, one row late — so the operative TY2026 rate was 4.25% instead of the source's 3.99%. The fix changes the 2026-01-01 version's formula to 0.0399 and replaces the proof atom's fabricated row "In 2026 4.25%" (no such row exists in the provision) with the real row "After 2025 3.99%", which is a change to encoded meaning, not provenance alone. I tried the competing kind wrong_period_or_effective_date and it fits worse: the 2024 and 2025 versions carry effective dates that match the source's own rows while holding wrong values, so most of the defect is wrong table cells rather than wrong windows, and the kind's parenthetical covers timeless encoding of superseded text whereas this encoding was dated. Subsection (a1) cannot rescue the old value, since its trigger table's earliest affected year is "In 2027", leaving subsection (a) governing TY2026.
verdict.quote:
-              excerpt: "In 2026 4.25%"
+              excerpt: "After 2025 3.99%"
verdict.notes:
Decisive evidence is threefold. (1) Source, read through resolve_provision.py at corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-19-dedup (provision file data/corpus/provisions/us-nc/statute/2026-07-13-recovery.jsonl line 53, body sha256 e174d86f...), with fix_time_corpus_match "same_body", so the pre-fix module cannot be excused by a corpus that changed: "In 2024 4.5% In 2025 4.25% After 2025 3.99%". (2) The formula change itself is split across the diff hunk because the line "- effective_from: '2026-01-01'" survives as context; the net effect is that the 2026-01-01 version's body goes from "0.0425" to "0.0399" (verbatim removed lines: "-        formula: |-" / "-          0.0425" and "-      - effective_from: '2027-01-01'"). (3) The pre-fix proof atoms quoted rows that do not appear in the cited provision at all ("In 2026 4.25%", "After 2026 3.99%", and the pre-2022 excerpts "before January 1, 2019 ... five and four hundred ninety-nine thousandths percent (5.499%)"), corroborating that the encoding tracked a superseded version of the table.

Two secondary observations for the reviewer, neither of which changes the primary kind. First, the same commit deletes every pre-2026 version and bounds individual_income_tax_rate and individual_income_tax to effective_from 2026-01-01 / effective_to 2026-12-31; the module summary explains this as deliberate deferral because subsection (a1) can reduce the rate beginning in 2027. That is pilot scope-bounding, not a scope correction, so wrong_entity_or_scope is not the right kind. Second, the removed pre-2022 versions (5.499%, 5.25%) are ungrounded in the current cited text and could read as untraceable_branch, but they are removed as part of the blanket scope narrowing rather than because they were ungrounded, and the reader's cited reading is about the operative TY2026 rate.

Also cosmetic in this diff: short_period_return_month_threshold renamed to short_period_return_month_count, with the import target and the consuming formula updated consistently; no meaning change there.

item.subject: Promote Illinois PIT to exact taxable-income boundary

triage.commit_summary: The commit rewrote the composed Illinois PIT pilot pipeline so that it no longer reconstructs the 35 ILCS 5/204 standard-exemption chain from caller-supplied per-person amounts, instead accepting completed-return Illinois taxable income (floored at zero) and investment-credit recapture as its two TaxUnit boundaries, importing the 4.95% rate from the encoded 35 ILCS 5/201 module and adding the recapture amount to liability. Its stated purpose was to promote the Illinois 2026 encoding to an exact before-nonrefundable-credits comparison boundary against PolicyEngine's il_income_tax_before_non_refundable_credits (PR reports max absolute difference $0.504 over 2,332 certified TaxUnits), and it correspondingly rewrote the fixtures and dropped the 35 ILCS 5/204 citation and imports.

modules.description_quote: promotes Illinois 2026 personal income tax to an exact taxable-income plus investment-credit-recapture boundary
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix liability rule was sourced to "35 ILCS 5/201(b) ... before section 201/212 credits" but computed only rate x net income, omitting the section 201(f)/(h) investment-credit recapture increase the statute states ("the tax imposed under subsections (a) and (b) of this Section for such taxable year shall be increased"), so it understated the before-credits tax for any unit with a recapture, and it applied a caller-supplied rate and a $2,925 per-person exemption figure that the cited sections do not state.
modules.triage_notes: Whole 133-line module was replaced by a 72-line one, so several things moved at once and the recapture omission cannot be isolated as the sole intent. (1) Input boundary changed: supplied base income + reconstructed 35 ILCS 5/204 standard-exemption stage (with the 204(g) AGI cutoff, strictness '>' which matches "exceeds") was dropped for a supplied il_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income floored at zero; rules il_pit_pilot_standard_exemption and il_pit_pilot_net_income_after_exemption were deleted and il_pit_pilot_taxable_income added. (2) Rate changed from the caller-supplied input il_pit_pilot_supplied_income_tax_rate to the import us-il:statutes/35/5/201#individual_trust_or_estate_current_income_tax_rate - same 4.95%, so this is grounding/provenance strengthening rather than a numeric change. (3) The only genuinely new statutory content is the added '+ il_pit_pilot_recapture_of_investment_credit' term with a new proof atom quoting the recapture increase clause; that reads as unrepresented_clause, but the pre-fix summary had explicitly declared it "deliberately excludes the section 201 investment ... credits", so a reviewer could also read the addition as new scope the module never claimed (which the triage guidance says is not a defect) - hence unclear. (4) effective_to: '2026-12-31' was added to both versions; this is pilot-year scoping with no statutory sunset (the 4.95% rate applies to taxable years beginning on or after July 1, 2017), so it is not the defect being fixed but is a scope narrowing worth noting. (5) Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus release (us-il/statute/35/5/201, resolver exit 0): it confirms "(5.4) In the case of an individual, trust, or estate, for taxable years beginning on or after July 1, 2017, an amount equal to 4.95% of the taxpayer's net income" and four "shall be increased" recapture clauses, including the (h) paragraph (6) text the post-fix atom quotes. (6) Commit body is empty (just a newline); the PR (TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us#958) has no reviews, review comments, or issue comments, so the only narrative evidence is the PR summary bullets. (7) Follow-up commit 4652444ae "Address Illinois PIT review findings" touched this same module but only changed the source string '(h)(6)' to '(h)(7)' plus the apply manifest and a waiver removal - mechanical citation bookkeeping, no formula change. (8) Companion test file was rewritten from seven exemption-chain fixtures to four boundary fixtures, and .axiom/index/provisions_to_rules.json lost the 35 ILCS 5/204 entries (index regeneration, consistent with dropping that citation).

verdict.justification: I could not refute the kind, but I also could not lift this to confirmed: the commit is dominated by an input-boundary re-scoping (the 204 standard-exemption stage and both 204 imports are deleted, the module drops to a single us-il/statute/35/5/201 citation, and the caller now supplies Illinois taxable income directly) plus a provenance upgrade (the caller-supplied rate becomes a hashed import of a rate rule that already existed at the parent commit, with the same 4.95% value), neither of which is an encoded meaning that disagreed with the source. The one element that does look like fidelity is the recapture increase: I confirmed through the pinned release that 35 ILCS 5/201(f)(6) states verbatim "the tax imposed under subsections (a) and (b) of this Section for such taxable year shall be increased", so a rule whose source line claimed "before section 201/212 credits" understated before-credits tax for any unit with a recapture, and the fix adds a proof atom quoting exactly that clause. It weighs against calling it a defect that the pre-fix summary explicitly scoped the module to "the ordinary wage-earner slice" and said it "deliberately excludes the section 201 investment ... credits", and that the recapture enters post-fix as a new caller-supplied input (il_pit_pilot_recapture_of_investment_credit) rather than as an encoded statutory computation — i.e. new boundary coverage, not a corrected formula. The message text ("Promote ... to an exact taxable-income boundary", parity statistics) describes a boundary promotion, never a correction, so the evidence does not settle it.
verdict.quote:
-          il_pit_pilot_net_income_after_exemption * il_pit_pilot_supplied_income_tax_rate
+          il_pit_pilot_taxable_income * individual_trust_or_estate_current_income_tax_rate + il_pit_pilot_recapture_of_investment_credit
verdict.notes: Evidence read: bundle JSON, full diff, pre file at fd918bb79f (133 lines) and post at 2f99fc5a02 (72 lines), and 35 ILCS 5/201 resolved through corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-19-dedup (text sha256 067d9252f0a3...). Three distinguishable changes are bundled: (1) recapture added — the only meaning-vs-source candidate; (2) rate re-grounded from il_pit_pilot_supplied_income_tax_rate to the import us-il:statutes/35/5/201#individual_trust_or_estate_current_income_tax_rate, which already existed at the parent commit (us-il/statutes/35/5/201.yaml:48) and carries the same 4.95%, so this is provenance, not a corrected number; (3) the whole 204 exemption stage deleted, which REMOVES represented statutory coverage (the 204(g) AGI cutoff branch and its two hashed imports) and moves the caller boundary upstream — a scope move, not a correction, and evidence against reading the commit as a fidelity fix. Also note the pre-fix module's own rationale conceded its $2,925 per-person figure came from IDOR Informational Bulletin FY 2026-15 rather than the statute, and it was a declared input, never a hardcoded formula value, so amount_mismatch does not apply. Two smaller things for the reviewer: the deleted il_pit_pilot_net_income_after_exemption carried source "35 ILCS 5/203" while proving against us-il/statute/35/5/204 (net income is 35 ILCS 5/202), a grounding mismatch on a rule the fix deletes rather than repairs; and the fix's new source line cites "(h)(6)", but the resolved text limits (h)(6) recapture to "any taxable year ending on or before December 31, 1996", so for the 2026 window only (f)(6) (and (h)(7) relocation) can apply — a mis-citation introduced BY the fix. If a reviewer keeps this case, the honest framing is unrepresented_clause on the recapture alone; if the corpus wants only isolated fidelity corrections, this is a mixed boundary-promotion commit and is a reasonable prune.

item.subject: Promote Georgia PIT to taxable-income boundary

triage.commit_summary: The commit rewrites the Georgia 2026 personal-income-tax pilot pipeline so that it stops deriving Georgia taxable net income from a supplied AGI minus a supplied standard deduction and instead accepts the completed-return Georgia taxable-income amount as its explicit upstream boundary, floors it at zero, and multiplies it by a rate imported from a newly added encoded O.C.G.A. § 48-7-20 module (4.99 per cent for tax year 2026 under HB463 / 2026 Ga. Laws Act 465). It also drops the ungrounded caller-supplied bracket-base/bracket-floor/marginal-rate/nonrefundable-credit schedule mechanics, corrects the § 48-7-20 proof excerpts to verbatim corpus text, and removes the module's `validate_failures` waiver from known-validation-gaps.yaml.

modules.description_quote: The caller supplies that completed-return Georgia taxable-income amount as the explicit upstream boundary; this module does not claim to reconstruct federal adjusted gross income or the deductions, exemptions, exclusions, and adjustments that produce the boundary under section 48-7-27.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module encoded Georgia taxable net income as `max(0, ga_pit_pilot_adjusted_gross_income - ga_pit_pilot_supplied_standard_deduction)` and grounded it on O.C.G.A. § 48-7-27, but § 48-7-27(a) defines that boundary as federal AGI less the itemized-or-standard deduction *plus* the age-65 and blind additional deductions, the § 48-7-26 exemptions together with the subsection (b) adjustments, and the retirement-income and other exclusions, so the encoded equation states a relation the cited provision does not support; the § 48-7-20 flat rate and bracket mechanics were likewise carried as caller-supplied inputs with no statutory grounding at all.

item.subject: Promote Pennsylvania PIT to taxable-income boundary

triage.commit_summary: The commit rewrites the Pennsylvania 2026 personal-income-tax pilot so that the only caller-supplied quantity is completed-return Pennsylvania adjusted taxable income, replacing the previous formula that took the bracket base, bracket floor, and marginal rate from the caller as a cumulative-base-plus-marginal schedule. modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus resolver (release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current, corpus commit c5af541326e0, provision line 4): section 302(a) says "a tax upon each dollar of income received by that resident during that resident's taxable year at the rate of three and seven hundredths per cent" -- a flat rate, with no bracket base, floor, or marginal-rate schedule anywhere in subsections (a)-(c). Pre-fix rule pa_pit_pilot_schedule_tax had formula 'pa_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_base + pa_pit_pilot_supplied_marginal_rate * max(0, pa_pit_pilot_taxable_income - pa_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_floor)' while its proof atom quoted the excerpt "at the rate of three and seven hundredths per cent." -- the cited text supports a fixed 3.07 percent multiplication, not three caller-supplied schedule parameters, which is why I read this as untraceable_branch (ungrounded structure removed and re-grounded) rather than amount_mismatch: no number in the pre-fix file was numerically wrong, the statutory number was simply absent. The pre-fix test file had to feed base=0, floor=0, marginal_rate=0.0307 to obtain the statutory answer, confirming the statute's own rate lived outside the encoding. The fix deletes pa_pit_pilot_schedule_tax entirely, makes pa_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability = pa_pit_pilot_taxable_income * personal_income_tax_rate with an import proof atom (hash sha256:326e196b...) pointing at the new index-0 module, renames the single remaining input to pa_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income with an explicit inputs: block, and rewrites the module summary and rationale. The commit also touches the two companion test files, two encoding manifests, and .axiom/index/provisions_to_rules.json (outside this chunk). The commit body is empty; all quotable evidence is the PR body (PR #961) and the bundle has no reviews, review comments, or issue comments, which is why confidence is 0.72: the PR names the fix (importing the statute-backed rate, promoting to a single taxable-income boundary) but never explicitly calls the removed bracket structure ungrounded.

verdict.justification: Module index 0 is a pure file addition: the diff has a zero-line pre-image, and `git ls-tree` on parent fd918bb7 shows `us-pa/policies/income_tax/` contained only the pipeline module and its test, with no rename or deletion in the commit, so no prior encoding of a Pennsylvania rate existed anywhere that this file could be correcting. Its single encoded value, `0.0307` for 2026, matches both cited sources read through the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current: §302(a) says "at the rate of three and seven hundredths per cent" and the DOR table says "2004 – Present 3.07%". The first reader's supporting quote ("imports the statute-backed 3.07% rate from Tax Reform Code §302") describes what the *pipeline* module now does, not a correction inside this file. This is new parameter coverage the module never previously claimed, which the task rules place outside fidelity defects, and the evidence settles that cleanly rather than leaving it open, so "unclear" understates what the diff shows.

item.subject: Promote Michigan PIT to taxable-income boundary

triage.commit_summary: The commit promotes the Michigan 2026 personal income tax pilot from a fully caller-supplied flat-tax composition to a source-grounded encoding: it adds a new parameter module encoding the Michigan Treasury's 2026 determination that the MCL 206.51 rate remains 4.25%, and rewrites the liability pipeline so it takes completed-return Michigan taxable income as an explicit caller boundary and multiplies it by the imported determined rate. In doing so it deletes the pre-fix pipeline's ungrounded bracket-base/bracket-floor/marginal-rate/nonrefundable-credit wiring and its AGI-minus-personal-exemption reconstruction of "taxable income", closes both rule versions at 2026-12-31 so 2025 and 2027 fail closed, and removes the module's pending entry from known-validation-gaps.yaml.

modules.triage_notes: Provision read: MCL 206.51(1) resolves through the pinned release and says '(b) Except as otherwise provided under subdivision (c), on and after October 1, 2012, 4.25%' with the (1)(c) annual formulary redetermination - there is no bracket base, bracket floor, or credit subtraction in it, and the rate is supplied by law rather than by a caller, which is what makes the pre-fix wiring untraceable. Numbers do not move: the same taxable income (24050) still yields 1022.125, so this is a grounding/scope correction, not an amount_mismatch. Secondary fidelity fix in the same diff: both versions gain effective_to '2026-12-31' where the pre-fix versions were open-ended even though 206.51(1)(c) redetermines the rate each year - a reviewer could reasonably tag that as wrong_period_or_effective_date, and the PR notes '2025 and 2027 fail closed with no applicable formula version'. Alternative kind reading is wrong_entity_or_scope, since the subject line frames it as moving the module's claimed boundary; I chose untraceable_branch because the decisive edits remove ungrounded values/structure and re-ground the rate on a real source. The real evidence is the diff plus the source text, so the confidence is justified on different grounds than the reader gave.

Strongest surviving counter-argument for a reviewer (why this is 0.7 and not 0.85): every removed policy-bearing element was a declared caller input set to zero, so with base=0/floor=0/credit=0 the pre-fix pipeline is arithmetically identical to the post-fix one at the same taxable income — the unchanged fixtures prove it. A reviewer could read this as a provenance/architecture "promotion" (caller-supplied parameters → imported official rate; AGI boundary → completed-return taxable-income boundary) rather than a meaning correction. What defeats that: the formula *shape* and its proof atoms are themselves encoded assertions about 206.51(1), and the pre-fix rationale admits the shape had no Michigan basis — the removed line reads "Michigan imposes the flat rate from the first dollar of taxable income and allows no per-exemption tax credit for these cases, so the supplied bracket floor, bracket base, and nonrefundable credit are zero."

Provenance of the defect: it is a template artifact, not a Michigan-specific misreading. The module was created in ebb7afef4 "Compose AZ/GA/MI/NC income-tax liability pipelines (flat) (#794)", and the AZ sibling at the same parent carries the identical `source: 43-1011, flat tax as the supplied bracket base plus the supplied marginal rate on income above the supplied bracket floor` and the same `- az_pit_pilot_supplied_nonrefundable_credit` line. So the same untraceable structure exists across AZ/GA/MI/NC and was corrected state by state (see a76b6afda "Tighten Arizona taxable-income boundary proof", 02f5ae9e6 "Promote Indiana PIT to 2026 AGI boundary", branch `pit-2026-boundary-truthfulness-closeout`). If the corpus wants independent cases, these siblings are near-duplicates of this one and should be deduped or sampled, not counted as distinct defects.

Secondary aspects present in the same commit but not the primary kind: (a) the pre-fix liability was an after-credit amount (`schedule_tax - supplied_nonrefundable_credit`) while the summary targeted `mi_income_tax_before_non_refundable_credits`, a scope/output-surface mismatch (wrong_entity_or_scope) papered over by "the credit is zero for the childless wage-earner grid"; (b) the removed proof excerpt "the tax imposed ... upon the taxable income of every person other than a corporation" is not verbatim — the statute reads "there is levied and imposed under this part upon the taxable income of every person other than a corporation a tax at the following rates." On its own (b) would be mechanical (provenance), but formulas changed here too.

Not a bookkeeping-only change, so `mechanical` is excluded: formulas, the input set, the output set (`mi_pit_pilot_schedule_tax` removed), and the version windows all changed. `not_a_rule_module` is excluded: it is a rulespec/v1 module with rules, versions, formulas and required proof validation, though its manifest carries `"manual_exception": "composition"` (assembled, not encoder-generated), which is worth knowing if the corpus is meant to sample encoder output specifically.

module_files[0], `us-mi/policies/income_tax/2026_rate_determination.yaml`, is a newly added parameter module in the same commit and needs its own classification; as pure new coverage it is most likely not_a_defect.

item.subject: Promote Utah PIT to full-Populace taxable-income boundary (#955)

triage.commit_summary: The commit rewrote the composed Utah individual income-tax pilot pipeline (us-ut/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml) so that it takes a single caller-supplied completed-return Utah state taxable-income boundary floored at zero, and applies the 4.45% rate imported (with an exact proof hash) from the encoded us-ut/statutes/59-10-104 module, instead of deriving the taxable base as caller-supplied federal AGI minus caller-supplied subtractions and multiplying by a caller-supplied rate. It also replaced the fixture inputs accordingly, added zero and negative-boundary fixtures, re-signed the apply manifest, and retired the module's known-validation-gaps waiver, which the PR reports now passes pinned axiom-encode validate over the full certified US Populace.

modules.description_quote: replace Utah PIT caller-supplied AGI, subtraction, and rate slots with one completed-return Utah taxable-income boundary
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module asserted that Utah state taxable income equals caller-supplied federal AGI less caller-supplied subtractions and multiplied that base by a caller-supplied rate, but the cited provision (Utah Code 59-10-104, whose proof-atom excerpt is 'a tax on the state taxable income of a resident individual') neither defines the base that way (Utah's state taxable income also carries additions) nor leaves the rate free — it fixes the tax at 4.45% of state taxable income — so both the base derivation and the rate had no grounding in the cited source.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus (us-rulespec-2026-07-19-dedup, release sha 5b52bfb3…): 59-10-104 says only '(1) A tax is imposed on the state taxable income of a resident individual… (2) …the tax is an amount equal to the product of: (a) the resident individual's state taxable income…; and (b) 4.45%.' Nothing there supports the pre-fix 'max(0, ut_pit_pilot_adjusted_gross_income - ut_pit_pilot_supplied_subtractions)' base, and the pre-fix module rationale made the unsupported claim that 'Utah taxable income for the resident wage earner is federal adjusted gross income'; the fix deletes that derivation and the caller-supplied rate slot and re-grounds the rate via 'imports: us-ut:statutes/59-10-104#resident_individual_income_tax_rate' with an import proof atom (hash sha256:a6a9d878…). Two changes in one module (base re-grounded, rate re-grounded); I chose the base formula as the decisive path because the commit title centers on the taxable-income boundary. Counter-reading a reviewer should weigh (why confidence is 0.6, not higher): the commit body and PR describe this as a promotion from a narrow 'resident wage-earner slice' to a full-Populace boundary and never say the prior encoding contradicted the source; for the six retained positive fixtures the expected outputs are unchanged (30k→1335 etc.), so no computed value moved inside the old declared scope, and part of the change is scope/provenance hardening rather than a value correction. Supporting evidence that the repo itself treated the pre-fix module as failing its own gate: the commit removes the module's 'validate_failures' pending waiver in known-validation-gaps.yaml (second commit-body bullet: 'Retire obsolete Utah validation waiver'); that waiver class is the merge-bypass allowlist described in rulespec-us issue 782. Other files in the commit are the companion test fixtures, the re-signed .axiom encoding manifest (adds a 'supersedes' block), and the waiver file — no unrelated rule changes. Follow-up noticed: commit 4bca2b9f3 ('Bound RI and UT 2026 tax pilots', 2026-07-23) later added effective_to: '2026-12-31' to both versions of this module, a separate period-bounding fix not part of this commit. No PR reviews or review comments exist on #955.

verdict.justification: The diff changes encoded meaning in both rules, not just scope or provenance: the taxable-income formula stops asserting that Utah state taxable income equals caller AGI minus caller subtractions (an arithmetic the cited 59-10-104 never states — the pinned corpus text only says "A tax is imposed on the state taxable income of a resident individual"), and the liability formula stops multiplying by a free caller-supplied rate slot. The pinned provision fixes the rate — "the tax is an amount equal to the product of: (a) the resident individual's state taxable income for that taxable year; and (b) 4.45%" — and the already-encoded us-ut/statutes/59-10-104 module carried 0.0445 grounded to the excerpt "4.45%", so the pre-fix module left ungrounded a value its own cited section specifies; the fix re-grounds it through an import with an exact sha256 proof atom. Both edits are removals/re-groundings of values with no basis in the cited source rather than added clauses, so untraceable_branch fits better than unrepresented_clause or amount_mismatch (no wrong number was ever written; the tests supplied 0.0445 correctly). Corroboration: the same commit retires this module's entry from known-validation-gaps.yaml, whose header reads "Modules failing encode validate (source grounding etc.)".
verdict.quote:
-          ut_pit_pilot_taxable_income * ut_pit_pilot_supplied_rate
+          ut_pit_pilot_taxable_income * resident_individual_income_tax_rate
verdict.notes: Strongest refutation available, and I considered it seriously: the commit is framed as a promotion ("Promote Utah PIT to full-Populace taxable-income boundary"), and part of it really is coverage expansion (wage-earner slice -> all full-year resident tax units, plus new zero/negative fixtures), which the rubric says is not a defect on its own. The pre-fix rationale also openly declared the rate as "a declared caller-supplied current-authority input", so one could call the old state an honest boundary rather than a misencoding. I still land on confirmed because a boundary is defensible for state taxable income (defined outside 59-10-104 via the additions/subtractions chain) but not for the rate, which 59-10-104(2)(b) fixes in the very provision the rule's proof atom cites, and because the old base formula operationalized a claim ("Utah taxable income for the resident wage earner is federal adjusted gross income") that the source does not support and the fix explicitly retracts ("this module does not claim to reconstruct the federal and Utah adjustments"). Second-best kind if a reviewer disagrees: unrepresented_clause, on the reading that the fix adds the statutory 4.45% the encoding never represented. Not mechanical under any reading — formulas, inputs, and the imports block all changed. Confidence held at 0.72 because the defect is entangled with a genuine scope expansion in the same commit, and there are no PR review comments naming a defect.

Supporting evidence from the PR's author-posted cycle notes (bundle field is issue_comments, not reviews/review_comments, so I did not tag it as quote_source 'pr_review'): 'corrected the Washington RCW proof excerpt to match the canonical text and re-attested the module' and 'One exact-source correction remains locally in `us-wa/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml` (1 line changed). modules.triage_notes:
Module status is 'added' (0 pre-lines, 422 post-lines); the diff is a pure file creation, so there is no pre-fix/post-fix module pair in this commit for a fidelity judge to score. Classified unclear rather than mechanical (the whole module - formulas, parameters, versions, effective dates, scope - is new, so 'mechanical' would wrongly tell a reviewer nothing substantive is here) and rather than fidelity (no encoded meaning was corrected relative to the parent). Confidence is set below 0.5 per the band convention for 'unclear'; the underlying facts (file absent at parent, squash merge) are certain.

The real defects are recoverable from the unsquashed branch commits, still fetchable via gh api repos/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/commits/<sha> (branch bulk/us-mo-manual-...-block-1); each is a genuine pre-fix -> post-fix pair on this same module file, and a corpus builder should harvest these instead of this merge commit:
- add5a433d8 'Apply current Missouri SNAP income limits' (+49/-15): the 165% table had a single version at effective_from '0001-01-01' carrying FY2025 values; the fix bounds it to '2024-10-01' and adds a versions[1] at '2025-10-01' with the FY2026 USDA values (2071->2152 ... 7249->7446; additional member 740->757). Kind: wrong_period_or_effective_date (timeless encoding of superseded values), with an amount_mismatch component for current periods.
- 75e613a439 'Fix Missouri individual household authority' (+63/-22): the module treated the Missouri administrative evidence list (SSDI or SSI or MRT determination) as the qualifying-disability test; the fix renames that rule to individual_has_missouri_administrative_disability_evidence and adds individual_has_qualifying_disability_basis grounded on 7 USC 2012(m)(3), requiring 'as certified by a licensed physician' AND (Social Security Act permanent disability OR severe non-disease-related permanent infirmity). Kind: unrepresented_clause / untraceable_branch (encoding grounded on the wrong authority).
- f353e97a50 'Enforce federal Missouri individual household bars' (+55/-9): adds the full 7 USC 2012(m)(4) institution / boarding-house / pays-compensation-for-meals bars. Kind: unrepresented_clause.
- a3c0aa201a 'Exclude spouses from Missouri individual income test' (+17/-11): the 165% test used other_residents_household_size and other_residents_countable_gross_income; the fix switches both to the *_excluding_spouse inputs, per 7 USC 2012(m)(3) ('of the others, excluding the spouse, does not exceed the poverty line'). Kind: wrong_entity_or_scope (household member set).

item.subject: Encode the whole-dollar rounding the FNS SNAP computation applies (#826)

triage.commit_summary: The commit adds whole-dollar rounding at three steps of the 7 CFR 273.10(e)(1) SNAP net-income chain in us/regulations/7-cfr/273/10.yaml: the earned income deduction now floors (drops cents), and the excess shelter cost and the applied homeless shelter deduction now round to the nearest whole dollar (floor(x + 0.5)), with a new proof atom quoting the (e)(1)(ii)(A) rounding election plus updated summary and rationale text. It was made because the encoding carried cents end to end while FNS computes in whole dollars at defined steps, causing 33 of 856 Colorado FY 2024 SNAP QC replays to differ by exactly one dollar (rulespec-us#762 / axiom-oracles#244).

modules.description_quote: Fixes #762 — the last residual class in the SNAP QC administrative-data oracle (TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-oracles#244): 33 of 856 Colorado FY 2024 replays differed by exactly $1 because the encoded chain carried cents where FNS computes in whole dollars.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module carried cents through the entire net-income chain and so represented neither procedure of the 273.10(e)(1)(ii) rounding election the source says the State agency shall use — in particular the (e)(1)(ii)(A) round-down-1-to-49-cents / round-up-50-to-99-cents step on the excess shelter calculation — producing benefits a dollar off from the FNS computation.
modules.triage_notes: Single rule module in the commit (plus its companion test file and the encoding manifest). Read the cited provision through the pinned corpus release (us-sc-snap-2026-07-15, corpus commit 3932af44) and confirmed the source text verbatim: '(ii) In calculating net monthly income, the State agency shall use one of the following two procedures: (A) Round down each income and allotment calculation that ends in 1 through 49 cents and round up each calculation that ends in 50 through 99 cents; or (B) ...' — so the rounding clause is in the source and was absent from the pre-fix encoding. Three formulas changed inside this one module: snap_earned_income_deduction_for_net_income gained floor(...), and snap_homeless_shelter_deduction_for_net_income and snap_excess_shelter_cost gained floor(... + 0.5) (half-up nearest dollar). I picked snap_excess_shelter_cost for rule_path because it is the only one that also gained a new proof atom whose excerpt quotes the (e)(1)(ii)(A) election, making the source linkage decisive; the other two are equally part of the same defect. Caveat for a reviewer: the earned-income-deduction change is floor (drop cents), which is NOT literally the (e)(1)(ii)(A) half-up election — the commit and PR ground it empirically on the QC file's constructed FSERNDED values (earned 432 -> 86, 424 -> 84) and on the newly added checked_path us/guidance/usda/fns/snap-qc-fy2024-technical-documentation/page-84, i.e. on the computation FNS applies rather than on the (A) text alone. An alternative kind of amount_mismatch is defensible because the observable symptom was $1 benefit differences, but the fix adds a source-stated clause that was missing, so unrepresented_clause fits better. Non-fidelity changes ride along in the same diff and are mechanical: module rationale/summary prose, the source string on snap_earned_income_deduction_for_net_income ('7 CFR 273.10(e)(1)(i)(B) with the (e)(1)(ii) rounding election'), and the added checked_path. PR #826 has no reviews and no review or issue comments. The PR notes companion work #765 and a verification rerun landing on axiom-oracles#244, and states two pre-existing New York composition test failures are unrelated.

verdict.justification: The pinned corpus release (us-sc-snap-2026-07-15) carries a mandatory rounding step inside the very paragraph the module encodes: "(ii) In calculating net monthly income, the State agency shall use one of the following two procedures: (A) Round down each income and allotment calculation that ends in 1 through 49 cents and round up each calculation that ends in 50 through 99 cents". The pre-fix module contained no rounding anywhere in the (e)(1) chain — grep of the parent blob shows rounding only at the (e)(2)(ii) 30-percent reduction and the minimum benefit — so the (e)(1)(ii) election was simply absent, and the fix adds it as a half-up step on the flagged rule plus a new proof atom at versions[0].formula bound to the verbatim (A) excerpt. This changes computed meaning, not presentation (33 of 856 Colorado replays moved by $1), which rules out mechanical, and it is a clause the source states rather than new coverage the module never claimed, which rules out not_a_defect. boundary_direction does not fit better because there was no rounding operator whose side was wrong, and amount_mismatch does not fit because no numeric value, rate, or threshold changed.
verdict.quote: +          if snap_homeless_shelter_deduction_for_net_income > 0: 0 else: max(0, floor(snap_total_allowable_shelter_expenses - (snap_net_income_before_shelter * snap_excess_shelter_income_share) + 0.5))
verdict.notes: Two caveats a reviewer should see, neither of which overturns the verdict on the flagged rule_path. (1) The commit changes three formulas, and only two of them follow the (A) text. snap_earned_income_deduction_for_net_income becomes floor(...) (drop cents), which contradicts (A): the commit's own example, earned income 424 -> deduction 84, is 84.80, which (A) would round UP to 85. Its basis is the QC file's constructed FSERNDED ("empirically decisive over nearest-dollar"), i.e. agency practice, not the cited (A) election — closer to untraceable_branch/other if that sibling rule were the one being scored. The flagged rule (snap_excess_shelter_cost) is the well-grounded one: the commit says the regulation text "fixes the shelter direction the data alone cannot distinguish," and the added proof atom excerpt is verbatim (A). (2) Procedure (B) lets a State include cents in income calculations where its TANF program does, so a cents-carrying chain is not literally forbidden for every State; I considered this as grounds for not_a_defect and rejected it, because (B) itself ends "...and round the final shelter deduction amount," so the shelter deduction is rounded under either procedure, and because the module is a single national encoding with no State-election input for (e)(1)(ii). Worth noting the asymmetry: the module does parameterize the (e)(2)(ii) election via state_agency_rounds_thirty_percent_net_income_up but hardcodes (A) here. item.subject: Repair Massachusetts TAFDC nonnegative floor

triage.commit_summary: A deterministic `axiom-encode repair-nonnegative-floors` pass (manifest `tool: axiom-encode repair-nonnegative-floors`, `model: nonnegative-floor-v1`, `runner: deterministic-repair`) rewrote one line of the Massachusetts TAFDC 106 CMR 704.230 child-support deduction formula so the disregard parameter operand is wrapped in `max(0, ...)`, satisfying the encoder's nonnegative-floor validator. Since the disregard parameter is the fixed literal `50`, the rewrite is semantically a no-op; the accompanying manifest change is bookkeeping (new encoder version 0.2.1000 -> 0.2.1046, new content hash and HMAC signature, and dropping the companion `.test.yaml` entry from `applied_files`).

modules.description_quote: Repair Massachusetts TAFDC nonnegative floor
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing was wrong relative to the source: the pre-fix formula already disregarded the first $50 of absent-parent income exactly as 106 CMR 704.230(B)(1) states, and wrapping the constant-50 disregard parameter in max(0, ...) cannot change any computed value.
modules.triage_notes: Single-line diff: `min(max(0, absent_parent_income_for_child_in_assistance_unit), ma_tafdc_monthly_absent_parent_income_disregard)` becomes `min(max(0, absent_parent_income_for_child_in_assistance_unit), max(0, ma_tafdc_monthly_absent_parent_income_disregard))`. The second operand is the sibling rule ma_tafdc_monthly_absent_parent_income_disregard, a `kind: parameter` with exactly one version (effective_from '0001-01-01', formula '50'), so max(0, 50) == 50 and the encoded meaning, amount, boundary, scope, entity, period, effective dates, inputs and outputs are all unchanged. I did not read the provision through the corpus resolver because the classification does not turn on what 704.230 says: no amount, comparison, clause, branch, date or scope changed, and the $50 proof-atom excerpt ('except for the first $50 received in any month') is untouched. Evidence it is validator conformance rather than fidelity: the sibling manifest .axiom/encoding-manifests/us-ma/regulations/106-cmr/704/230/block-1.json flips `tool` from `axiom-encode repair-oracle-parameter-tests` to `axiom-encode repair-nonnegative-floors` and `model` from `oracle-parameter-test-v1` to `nonnegative-floor-v1`, both with runner `deterministic-repair`; the PR body independently confirms the validator exists and blocks generated artifacts ('the encoder-generated artifact was blocked by the nonnegative-floor validator'). Note the PR (#505, 'Add Alaska ATAP RuleSpec') is about Alaska and does not discuss this Massachusetts module at all, so the commit message is the only direct evidence for this change. Also note the manifest silently drops the block-1.test.yaml entry from applied_files, though that test file still exists in the tree at this commit; that is manifest bookkeeping, not a module change. No follow-up commit has touched this module since (git log 9d4ff7ef3a..HEAD on the path is empty), which is consistent with the formula having been correct both before and after. Borderline only in that the strict 'mechanical' definition says formulas stay the same; here the formula string changed but its value is provably identical, so a reviewer wanting a stricter reading could downgrade to unclear rather than promote to fidelity.

item.subject: Repair Medicaid community engagement timing (#500)

triage.commit_summary: The commit split the `is_medicaid_eligible` rule in us/statutes/42/1396a/a/10.yaml into two versions so that the 42 USC 1396a(xx) community engagement (work requirement) condition gates adult-group eligibility only from 2026-12-31 forward, leaving the 2014-01-01 version ungated. It also bumped the rules-engine and encoder pins in .axiom/toolchain.toml to versions supporting versioned formulas and regenerated the encoding manifest.

modules.description_quote: keep adult-group Medicaid ungated before the 2026-12-31 community engagement effective date
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The single 2014-01-01 version of `is_medicaid_eligible` applied the 42 USC 1396a(xx) community engagement condition (`adult_group_eligible and demonstrated_community_engagement_for_month`) to every month back to 2014, although the source makes that requirement effective no earlier than the first quarter after December 31, 2026, so adult-group Medicaid was wrongly gated in all pre-2027 periods.
modules.triage_notes: Only one rule module changed; the commit's other files (.axiom/toolchain.toml engine/encoder pins and us/.axiom/encoding-manifests/statutes/42/1396a/a/10.json) are mechanical. The fix removes `and demonstrated_community_engagement_for_month` from the 2014-01-01 formula and adds an otherwise identical formula carrying that gate as a new version effective_from '2026-12-31'; the community-engagement import proof atom moves from versions[0] to versions[1], and the remaining proof atoms are duplicated for versions[1] (mechanical provenance mirroring). No parameters, entities, scope, or other rules changed. Effective date verified against the imported module us/statutes/42/1396a/xx.yaml at this same commit, where `demonstrated_community_engagement_for_month` and every other community-engagement rule/parameter carry effective_from '2026-12-31' and the module summary reads "beginning not later than the first quarter after December 31, 2026". resolve_provision was not run because this module's own corpus citation (us/statute/42/1396a/a/10) does not contain the (xx) timing language; evidence is the PR body plus the imported (xx) module. No test files in the commit. PR body notes full Populace parity additionally depends on axiom-encode#919 (Medicaid oracle pregnancy input projection), an unrelated follow-up.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical or as merely-added coverage and could not: the pre-fix file had a single `is_medicaid_eligible` version at `effective_from: '2014-01-01'` whose formula read `or (adult_group_eligible and demonstrated_community_engagement_for_month)`, so the gate fired in every month from 2014 onward, and the fix rewrites that 2014 version to plain `or adult_group_eligible` and adds a second version at 2026-12-31 carrying the gate — a change in encoded meaning for all pre-2027 periods, not bookkeeping. The pinned corpus confirms the source basis: 42 USC 1396a(a)(10)(A)(i)(VIII) is "subject to subsections (k) and (xx)", and 1396a(xx)(1) says the requirement applies "beginning not later than the first day of the first quarter that begins after December 31, 2026", so the old timeless encoding disagreed with the source on timing, not on the clause's content, its logic, or its population. Alternative kinds fail: the clause itself was present (not unrepresented_clause), it has a real statutory basis (not untraceable_branch), and the boolean combination `adult_group_eligible and demonstrated_community_engagement_for_month` is unchanged in the post-2026 version (not polarity_or_logic). The only residual doubt is the fix's own boundary choice, which does not change the kind of the defect being corrected.
verdict.quote: +      - effective_from: '2026-12-31'
verdict.notes: Second decisive diff line: `+          or adult_group_eligible` (diff line 130) replacing the pre-fix `or (adult_group_eligible and demonstrated_community_engagement_for_month)` in the 2014-01-01 version; the community-engagement proof atom is re-pathed from `versions[0].formula` to `versions[1].formula`, so the import now grounds only the post-2026 formula. Everything else in the diff (duplicated import proof atoms at versions[1]) is mechanical fallout of the version split. Reviewer flag, not a reason to change this classification: the new window starts at `2026-12-31`, while 1396a(xx)(1) says "beginning not later than the first day of the first quarter that begins after December 31, 2026" — i.e. 2027-01-01 — so the repaired version is arguably one day (and, for a monthly period kind, potentially the whole December 2026 month) early; 1396a(xx)(1) also permits a State to elect an earlier date by waiver/State plan, which this module does not represent at all. Both are candidate follow-on defects in the fix itself (boundary_direction / unrepresented_clause), not defects in the pre-fix text this commit repaired. Corpus evidence read through the pinned resolver: release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, provision file sha256 78e603358d..., 1396a(xx) expression_date 2025-07-04.

item.subject: Repair SNAP income eligibility backbone

triage.commit_summary: The commit rewires the federal SNAP income-eligibility backbone so that 7 CFR 273.9(a)'s gross and net income tests consume the canonical income and deduction outputs computed in 7 CFR 273.10(e) (snap_total_gross_income, snap_net_monthly_income) instead of ungrounded free input leaves (snap_gross_monthly_income, snap_net_income) that no module in the corpus produced. To make 273.9 able to import 273.10 without creating a dependency cycle, 273.10's uncapped-excess-shelter condition was re-pointed from the 273.9 rule snap_full_excess_shelter_deduction_applies to the definitionally identical snap_household_has_elderly_or_disabled_member in 7 USC 2012(j), and the 273.9 companion tests plus both signed encoding manifests were refreshed.

modules.description_quote: Refactor 7 CFR 273.10 to import the elderly/disabled household fact directly from 7 USC 2012(j), removing the 273.10 -> 273.9 dependency edge.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing in the pre-fix module disagreed with the source: the condition it tested (us:regulations/7-cfr/273/9#snap_full_excess_shelter_deduction_applies) had the literal formula 'snap_household_has_elderly_or_disabled_member' with the same effective_from, so swapping it for the direct 7 USC 2012(j) import leaves the encoded meaning identical.
modules.triage_notes: Verified semantics-preserving by reading the parent version of regulations/7-cfr/273/9.yaml: its rule snap_full_excess_shelter_deduction_applies (source 7 CFR 273.9(d)(6)(ii), effective_from 2025-10-01) is defined as exactly 'snap_household_has_elderly_or_disabled_member', itself imported from us:statutes/7/2012/j, so both the pre- and post-fix branch conditions evaluate the same fact and the capped/uncapped shelter branch is unchanged. The whole diff is three things: the imports list (drop us:regulations/7-cfr/273/9, add us:statutes/7/2012/j), the matching proof-atom import target/output/sha256 (provenance bookkeeping), and the one variable name inside the formula. This edit exists only to break the 273.10 -> 273.9 edge so that index 1 can add the reverse edge 273.9 -> 273.10 without a cycle; it is the enabling counterpart to the real repair, not itself a meaning correction. Confirmed via git grep that no reference to 273/9 or snap_full_excess_shelter_deduction_applies remains in the post-fix 273.10. No effective dates, parameters, amounts, entities, or outputs changed. Commit message body is empty; the only prose evidence is the PR body (no reviews or review comments on PR #392).

modules.description_quote: Refactor 7 CFR 273.9 income eligibility to consume the canonical 273.10 gross and net income calculation outputs instead of stale free gross/net input leaves.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix eligibility tests compared ungrounded free input leaves (snap_net_income, snap_gross_monthly_income) that no module in the corpus computes, so 273.9(a)(1)-(2) was applied to values with no basis in the regulation's own income definition (273.9(b)-(c) gross income net of exclusions) or its deduction-based net income (273.9(d), computed in 273.10(e)(1)) rather than to the amounts the source prescribes.
modules.triage_notes: Read the cited provision through resolve_provision.py for us/regulation/7/273/9: (a) sets the gross and net standards, (b) defines household income as 'all income from whatever source excluding only items specified in paragraph (c)', and (d) supplies the deductions that produce net income. Post-fix the module imports us:regulations/7-cfr/273/10 and uses snap_total_gross_income (7 CFR 273.10(e)(1)(i)(A): earned + unearned - exclusions) and snap_net_monthly_income (7 CFR 273.10(e)(1)(i): max(0, net income before shelter - excess shelter deduction)), both verified in the post-fix 273.10 file. That the pre-fix names were unbound leaves is confirmed by the companion test diff, which previously seeded 'us:regulations/7-cfr/273/9#input.snap_gross_monthly_income' and '#input.snap_net_income' and now seeds the 273.10 calculation inputs instead. Caveat a reviewer should weigh: the module's unchanged deferred_outputs prose says the module 'applies income eligibility standards to resolved gross and net income amounts', so the free leaves could be read as an intentional interface and the change as integration plumbing rather than a meaning correction; I call it fidelity because the leaves were never produced anywhere (the PR calls them 'stale'), leaving the net-income test ungrounded, but confidence is held below 0.8 for that reason. untraceable_branch is chosen for the 'value with no basis in the cited source ... the fix re-grounds it' sense; no listed kind fits a mis-wired variable more exactly. Index 0 is the enabling cycle-breaking edit for this change; the commit also refreshed the signed manifests under .axiom/encoding-manifests/ for both modules. Commit body empty; PR #392 has no reviews or comments.

verdict.justification: The diff changes only which symbol supplies each operand (free leaves `snap_gross_monthly_income`/`snap_net_income` become the 273.10 outputs `snap_total_gross_income`/`snap_net_monthly_income`, plus one added import); the comparison direction, the 130%/100% FPL standards, the elderly/disabled carve-out, entity, period, effective_from and the module's declared scope are byte-identical pre and post, and the unchanged `deferred_outputs` block still says the module "applies income eligibility standards to resolved gross and net income amounts" with 273.9(b) and (c) composition deferred both before and after the fix. The companion test diff re-seeds inputs but leaves every expected `holds`/`not_holds` output untouched, so no answer the pre-fix encoding produced was wrong against 7 CFR 273.9(a)(1)-(2), and free input leaves are a sanctioned pattern in this corpus (273.10 still takes `snap_total_medical_expenses`, `snap_total_allowable_shelter_expenses`, etc. as leaves). Against that, the first reader's point has real force: net income is a quantity the cited section itself defines via (d) deductions, so binding it to an arbitrary caller-supplied number does leave (a)(2) applied to an amount with no derivation in the corpus, which fits the "re-grounds it" half of untraceable_branch. The evidence does not settle which reading governs, so I neither confirm nor clear it.
verdict.quote:
-        formula: snap_net_income <= snap_net_income_limit_100_percent_fpl_48_states_dc
+        formula: snap_net_monthly_income <= snap_net_income_limit_100_percent_fpl_48_states_dc
verdict.notes: Refutation evidence a reviewer should weigh. (1) The PR's other module half is provably semantics-preserving: 273.10 swapped `us:regulations/7-cfr/273/9#snap_full_excess_shelter_deduction_applies` for `us:statutes/7/2012/j#snap_household_has_elderly_or_disabled_member`, and 273.9's rule for the former is literally `formula: snap_household_has_elderly_or_disabled_member` — identical value, so that half is pure dependency-edge removal ("removing the 273.10 -> 273.9 dependency edge", PR body). The 273.9 half is the mirror image of the same graph refactor. (2) The PR body's own words are "stale free gross/net input leaves" — superseded plumbing, not a contradiction with the CFR. (3) The fix adds no source coverage: the 273.9(b) and (c) deferral entries are identical in the parent and the commit, so the regulation's income-composition clauses are still unrepresented after the fix; it only points the operands at 273.10(e)(1)'s computation. (4) Verified via `git grep` at parent 6321354: `snap_gross_monthly_income` and `snap_net_income` appear in 273.9 only in the formulas and as `#input.` seeds in 273.9.test.yaml — genuinely unbound leaves, but the engine treats unbound names as module inputs by design, so this is a graph-completeness property, not a mis-encoded rule. (5) Rubric-relevant: the module never claimed to derive income, so under "a change that merely adds new outputs, precision, or scope the module never claimed is not a defect; classify unclear at most", the leading alternative verdict is not_a_defect (integration/grounding enhancement), and I put roughly 55/45 on not_a_defect versus fidelity/untraceable_branch. (6) Weak counter-evidence for the defect reading: the commit subject is "Repair SNAP income eligibility backbone" and axiom-encode shipped a bespoke `repair-snap-273-9-income-eligibility` command, and the pre-fix test 4 asserted an internally impossible state (gross 1000 with net 1306), which only an ungrounded leaf permits. If the corpus's convention is that a regulation-derived quantity may never be a free leaf, this is fidelity/untraceable_branch; if free leaves plus explicit deferrals are an accepted encoding contract, it is not a defect. I could not settle that convention from the commit, PR, or module text.

item.subject: Refresh payroll generated repairs

triage.commit_summary: Commit 792270d54b, part of merged PR #328 "Refresh generated payroll and tax rules", re-ran the signed encoder over railroad payroll (Chapter 22) modules: statutes/26/3231/d.yaml gained a verbatim statutory module summary, normalized source citation strings, many added proof-atom excerpts, and one restructured formula, while statutes/26/3241/a.yaml took only refreshed proof-import hashes pointing at the regenerated 3241(b) rate table. Most of the churn is provenance bookkeeping from a generated-artifact refresh, but one real meaning change rides along: the 26 USC 3231(d)(7) general-chairman compensation formula was re-nested and its fall-through default changed from returning the full remuneration to returning zero.

modules.description_quote: apply signed encoder output/repairs only; no generated RuleSpec files were hand-edited
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix formula flattened paragraph (7)'s three conditions into a single `and`, so whenever the individual was NOT acting as a general chairman or assistant general chairman the single `else` branch fell through to `remuneration_for_general_chairman_service` and treated the entire remuneration as compensation, although 26 USC 3231(d)(7) attaches its compensation treatment only "in such case", i.e. when he acts in that capacity; the fix nests the office/headquarters and non-US-employer conditions inside the general-chairman test and defaults the outer else to 0.
modules.triage_notes: Bundle contains exactly 2 module files, matching chunk indices [0,1]; nothing missing. Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us/statute/26/3231 resolved cleanly): (7) reads "he acts in the capacity of a general chairman or an assistant general chairman of a general committee which represents individuals rendering service in the United States to an employer, but in such case if his office or headquarters is not located in the United States and the individuals represented by such general committee are employees of an employer not conducting the principal part of its business in the United States, only such proportion of the remuneration ... shall be regarded as compensation ...", which grounds both the nesting and the zero default. Pre- and post-fix agree on every input combination where the general-chairman flag is true; the only behavioral delta is that flag false, where pre-fix returned full remuneration and post-fix returns 0 (a fail-open default corrected to fail-closed). Everything else in this 164-line diff is mechanical: module summary replaced with a verbatim statutory excerpt, source strings normalized (e.g. "26 USC 3231(d), paragraphs (1) and (2)" -> "26 USC 3231(d)(1)-(2)"), one proof atom's kind: amount -> kind: parameter, and about ten added proof-atom excerpt strings; no other formula, version, effective date, input, output, entity or scope changed. The companion statutes/26/3231/d.test.yaml was rewritten in the same commit (cases renamed/reordered, a new general_chairman_mileage_proration_below_minimum_is_zero_compensation case asserting 0, the old auto_zero case replaced by auto_positive cases), but no test pins the decisive not-a-general-chairman -> 0 behavior, so the formula change is not test-forced. Alternative kind considered: wrong_entity_or_scope (paragraph (7) treatment applied to individuals outside (7)'s scope); I chose polarity_or_logic because the defect mechanism is the mis-combined `and` and the wrong default value in the else branch. Confidence held at 0.62 because the commit message body is empty and the PR body is generic about "signed encoder output/repairs" and never mentions 3231(d); the diff plus the source text carry the classification.

modules.description_quote: refresh dependent payroll proof-import hashes in `26 USC 3201`, `3221`, `3241(a)`, `3131(f)`, `3132(f)`, `3133(a)`, and `3134(c)` using signed deterministic encoder repairs
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing relative to the source: the 22-line diff changes only two sha256 proof-import hashes (b56dc9d5... -> 6023ccf3...) after 26 USC 3241(b) was regenerated elsewhere in the same PR; formulas, effective_from dates, import targets and outputs, entity, dtype, period and scope are byte-identical.
modules.triage_notes: Pure provenance bookkeeping - the PR body explicitly lists 3241(a) among the modules whose dependent proof-import hashes were refreshed because 3241(b)'s rate schedule was regenerated with "band thresholds externalized into indexed parameters". Both import atoms carried the identical old hash and take the identical new hash even though they name different outputs (applicable_percentage_for_section_3201_b vs applicable_percentage_for_sections_3211_b_and_3221_b), which suggests the recorded hash is module-level rather than per-output; that is an encoder/proof-format observation, not a fidelity issue, and it does not change the classification. Provision text not needed for this module; no formula or version line appears in the diff.

verdict.justification: The diff really does restructure the boolean nesting, but the only input state where pre and post disagree is `acts_as_general_chairman... == false` combined with a nonzero `remuneration_for_general_chairman_service`: with A true the two formulas are identical (A∧B∧C → proration, otherwise full remuneration), and with A false and the general-chairman remuneration at its only coherent value (0) both return 0. The pinned text of 26 USC 3231(d)(7) ("he acts in the capacity of a general chairman ... but in such case if his office or headquarters is not located in the United States and the individuals represented ... only such proportion of the remuneration for such service shall be regarded as compensation") gates the proration exactly as the old formula already did, and says nothing at all about a non-chairman, so the fix swaps one ungrounded default (full) for another (0) rather than aligning a reachable outcome with the source. Provenance points the same way: the manifest shows a wholesale re-encode (openai/0.2.279 → codex/0.2.529, new run_id and signature), the commit says only "Refresh payroll generated repairs", the PR body describes refreshing generated artifacts and proof-import hashes, and no test was added pinning the changed branch. If it is a defect the first reader's kind is the right one (a mis-nested `and` firing the wrong default branch = polarity_or_logic), but the evidence does not settle that it was wrong against the source.
verdict.notes: Refutation targets the verdict, not the kind. (1) The first reader's quote — "apply signed encoder output/repairs only; no generated RuleSpec files were hand-edited" — is generic PR boilerplate about the apply pipeline and carries zero evidence of a corrected meaning; the only real evidence is the diff. (2) Behavioral delta is confined to a self-contradictory input (not acting as general chairman, yet nonzero remuneration *for general chairman service*); on every coherent input pre == post. (3) `general_chairman_service_remuneration_regarded_as_compensation` has no consumer anywhere in the repo at this commit (`git grep` at 792270d54b over statutes/26 hits only d.yaml and d.test.yaml), so the old fail-open default could not propagate. (4) The companion test file was rewritten in the same commit, and the removed case `auto_zero_general_chairman_service_remuneration_regarded_as_compensation` (A=false, remuneration=0 → 0) passed under BOTH formulas; the replacement case `general_chairman_mileage_proration_below_minimum_is_zero_compensation` exercises A=true/B=true/C=true only. Nothing pins the corrected branch — not what you'd expect from a diagnosed repair. (5) Everything else in this module diff is provenance: summary rewritten to a source excerpt, proof-atom `kind: amount` → `kind: parameter`, added `excerpt` strings, and source-string normalizations ("26 USC 3231(d), paragraphs (1) and (2)" → "26 USC 3231(d)(1)-(2)") — mechanical on their own. (6) Corpus read: us-rulespec-2026-07-13, provision text sha256 2701fa1c5ee0…, resolver reported `fix_time_corpus_match: provision_file_absent_at_corpus_ref`, so the text read is a later release than the toolchain corpus ref — noted for completeness; (d)(7)'s wording is not in dispute. Recommend keeping as a borderline/weak corpus member or dropping it; a stronger reading would be "defensive scoping added during a backend re-encode", i.e. closer to not_a_defect than to a confirmed polarity defect.

item.subject: Fix SNAP minimum benefit allotment source

triage.commit_summary: The commit repairs the `snap_minimum_benefit` formula in `regulations/7-cfr/273/10.yaml` so that 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(C)'s "8 percent of the maximum allotment for a household of one" is computed from the canonical corpus-grounded one-person allotment rule (`snap_one_person_thrifty_food_plan_cost`, i.e. `snap_maximum_allotment_table[1]` in the FY 2026 COLA module) instead of the free symbol `snap_maximum_allotment_for_one_person_household`, which no rule module in the repo ever defined and which only the test fixtures supplied. It also deletes that orphan input from the five 273.10 test cases and refreshes the signed axiom-encode apply manifest (0.2.457 to 0.2.503); the PR reports the NY SNAP ECPS minimum-benefit mismatch disappeared as a result.

modules.description_quote: repair 7 CFR 273.10 minimum-benefit formula to use the canonical one-person thrifty food plan cost
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The minimum benefit was computed as 8 percent of `snap_maximum_allotment_for_one_person_household`, a symbol defined by no rule module anywhere in the corpus and supplied only by test fixtures, so the encoding did not actually ground the base on the source's "maximum allotment for a household of one" and produced a wrong minimum benefit outside the fixtures.
modules.triage_notes: Single-module commit; the only module hunk is the one-symbol operand swap at rules[snap_minimum_benefit].versions[0].formula (line 410): `floor((snap_maximum_allotment_for_one_person_household * snap_minimum_benefit_rate) + 0.5)` -> `floor((snap_one_person_thrifty_food_plan_cost * snap_minimum_benefit_rate) + 0.5)`. Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus release (us/regulation/7/273/10): 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(C) reads "The minimum benefit is 8 percent of the maximum allotment for a household of one, rounded to the nearest whole dollar." item.subject: Repair standard deduction status component

triage.commit_summary: The commit repaired the 2026 standard deduction policy module (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 .14) by replacing the ungrounded local boolean input `individual_is_unmarried_and_not_surviving_spouse`, which gated the higher $2,050 aged/blind additional amount, with the filing-status enum predicate `filing_status == 0 or filing_status == 3` (single or head of household), and it dropped the now-stale input from the four companion test cases. It was applied by the deterministic `axiom-encode repair-tax-status-components` tool (model `tax-status-component-v1`, encoder 0.2.93), which enforces that a tax filing-status classification must be derived from the filing-status source rather than accepted as a caller-supplied fact; the commit also carried a repository-layout test allowance for explicitly non-executable modules.

(3) Aged or blind. For taxable years beginning in 2026, the additional standard deduction amount under Sec. 63(f) for the aged or the blind is $1,650. The additional standard deduction amount is increased to $2,050 if the individual is also unmarried and not a surviving spouse.' The module's own enum (from rules[basic_standard_deduction_by_filing_status].versions[0].formula) is 1=joint, 4=surviving spouse, 3=head of household, 2=MFS, 0=unmarried, so the post-fix predicate (0 or 3) matches 'unmarried and not a surviving spouse' and excludes joint, MFS, and surviving spouse. Kind is a judgment call between untraceable_branch (chosen: the branch condition had no grounded derivation in the encoding and the fix re-grounds it on the filing-status table the source states) and 'other' (ungrounded free input for a derived legal classification); the classification 'fidelity' itself is well supported. Caveat a reviewer should weigh: the four companion test cases only lost the removed input line, no expected output changed, so the repair is behavior-preserving on the shipped tests and a reviewer could read it as structural rather than a wrong-answer defect. Corroborating mechanism read in axiom-encode src/axiom_encode/harness/validator_pipeline.py (find_tax_status_component_local_input_issues, ~line 23871): 'Tax filing-status component is a derived legal classification, not a local factual input'. The commit also touched non-module files (.axiom/encoding-manifests/.../standard-deduction.json re-signed under backend 'deterministic', tool 'axiom-encode repair-tax-status-components'; tests/test_repository_layout.py). Later commits 095d680d4 (refresh) and 86ec136fd (move under us/) did not revisit the predicate: the fix is still present at HEAD in us/policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/standard-deduction.yaml:281. PR #47 has no reviews or review comments.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as a mere modeling preference and could not: the pre-fix branch gating the higher aged/blind amount was an undefined, free boolean input (`individual_is_unmarried_and_not_surviving_spouse`) that no rule in the module defined and no import supplied, so the encoding did not itself determine the source's condition and could pay $2,050 to a joint filer or $1,650 to a single filer depending on an exogenous flag. The pinned corpus text ("The additional standard deduction amount is increased to $2,050 if the individual is also unmarried and not a surviving spouse.", us/guidance/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/page-18) ties the increase to the same marital/surviving-spouse status the module already encodes as `filing_status`, and the fix re-grounds the gate on that enum (0 unmarried, 3 head of household; excluding 1 joint, 2 MFS, 4 surviving spouse, which the module's own basic-deduction `match` and companion tests fix as the mapping), so the new predicate is itself faithful and the change is a correction rather than a lateral rewrite. This is not mechanical (a derived rule's formula and the module's input surface both changed), and the alternative kinds fit worse: no amount, boundary, date, or polarity changed, no source clause was added, and pre-fix there was no wrong population stated — only an ungrounded one — so untraceable_branch ("the fix removes or re-grounds it") is the right kind.

-          additional_standard_deduction_entitlement_count_under_subsection_f * (if individual_is_unmarried_and_not_surviving_spouse: additional_standard_deduction_amount_unmarried_not_surviving_spouse else: additional_standard_deduction_amount)
+          additional_standard_deduction_entitlement_count_under_subsection_f * (if filing_status == 0 or filing_status == 3: additional_standard_deduction_amount_unmarried_not_surviving_spouse else: additional_standard_deduction_amount)
verdict.notes:
Evidence trail: bundle diff 000.diff (one formula line in rules[additional_standard_deduction_for_aged_or_blind].versions[0].formula); post file `git -C /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us show 5cdc45e555:policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/standard-deduction.yaml`; provision resolved through us-rulespec-2026-07-13 (corpus commit 612d20ca43, record 229d5117-ab80-57cd-973e-a0cd3f467b93).

Enum grounding is internal to the module and unambiguous: `basic_standard_deduction_by_filing_status` maps 1/4 => joint_or_surviving_spouse, 3 => head_of_household, 2 => married_filing_separately, 0 => unmarried, and the four companion test cases use 1 (joint), 3 (HoH), 0 (single dependent), 2 (MFS). So `filing_status == 0 or filing_status == 3` is exactly "unmarried and not a surviving spouse" (MFS filers are married, correctly excluded; test 4 expects 2 x 1650 = 3300).

Caveat a reviewer should weigh: the defect was latent under the committed tests. The companion test diff only deletes the now-unused `#input.individual_is_unmarried_and_not_surviving_spouse` lines; not a single expected output changed, because every test set the flag consistently with its filing_status. The behavioral divergence only appears on flag/filing-status combinations the source forbids, which is why this is "encoding does not determine the condition" rather than "encoding computes a wrong number".

Corroborating (tooling, not source): axiom-encode's own validator treats this exact pattern as an error — src/axiom_encode/harness/validator_pipeline.py:23871 `find_tax_status_component_local_input_issues`, message "Tax filing-status component is a derived legal classification, not a local factual input", and src/axiom_encode/prompts/encoder.py:1326 prohibits "compound status predicates such as `individual_is_not_married_and_is_not_surviving_spouse`" and prescribes the structural enum. That is repo-tooling evidence for the defect class, not source evidence; the source basis is the sentence quoted above.

No PR reviews or comments exist on rulespec-us#47, so the only narrative evidence is the PR body line the first reader quoted, which is verbatim and accurate.

Residual uncertainty (why 0.82, not higher): one could argue the module legitimately takes other status-ish facts as free inputs (`may_be_claimed_as_dependent_by_another_taxpayer`, `additional_standard_deduction_entitlement_count_under_subsection_f` remain free), so "free input" alone is not automatically a fidelity defect. The distinguishing fact I relied on is that this particular predicate was redundant with, and could contradict, a source-backed determinant already present in the same module.
