item.subject: Repair capital gains taxable income floor

triage.commit_summary: The commit re-applied statutes/26/1/h.yaml through `axiom-encode repair-nonnegative-floors` (manifest: backend "deterministic", runner "deterministic-repair", model "nonnegative-floor-v1"), which turned on module-level `proof_validation.required` and added a `metadata.proof.atoms` block to all 16 rules, and wrapped exactly one formula — `capital_gains_excluded_from_taxable_income` — in `max(0, ...)`. It is the second of a pair of automated floor sweeps (the parent commit 9203ca050 did the same for `taxable_income` in statutes/26/63.yaml); no tests were added and no other formula, parameter, version, effective date, input, output, or scope changed.

modules.other_kind: missing nonnegative floor on a derived money amount, with no corresponding not-below-zero clause in the cited provision
modules.description_quote: Repair capital gains taxable income floor
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix formula computed `taxable_income - max(taxable_income - net_capital_gain, min(min(max(taxable_income, 0), capital_gains_zero_rate_threshold), taxable_income - adjusted_net_capital_gain))` with no zero floor, but 26 USC 1(h)(1)(A) states no 'not below zero' limit for this (encoder-invented) intermediate, and the module's own definitions make a negative result unreachable, so it is not clear the pre-fix encoding disagreed with the source at all.
modules.triage_notes: Read the provision through the pinned corpus release (us/statute/26/1 resolved successfully; 1(h)(1)(A) = tax on 'the greater of (i) taxable income reduced by the net capital gain; or (ii) the lesser of (I) the amount of taxable income taxed at a rate below 25 percent; or (II) taxable income reduced by the adjusted net capital gain'). Notably 1(h)(2) and 1(h)(3) DO use the explicit idiom 'reduced (but not below zero)' and (h)(1)(B),(E),(F) use 'excess (if any)' — the statute has no such floor language for the (h)(1)(A)-derived quantity this rule encodes, so there is no source clause the pre-fix module failed to represent. Evidence that this is an automated lint-style hardening rather than a source-fidelity correction: (a) the commit body is empty; (b) the encoding manifest .axiom/encoding-manifests/statutes/26/1/h.json changed tool from 'axiom-encode encode --apply' to 'axiom-encode repair-nonnegative-floors', backend 'codex'->'deterministic', model 'gpt-5.5'->'nonnegative-floor-v1', run_id 'deterministic-repair'; (c) in axiom-encode, validator_pipeline.repair_nonnegative_amount_reductions selects rules purely by name regex _NONNEGATIVE_TAXABLE_INCOME_NAME_PATTERN = ^(?:[A-Za-z0-9_]+_)?taxable_income$ and then unconditionally emits `max(0, <expr>)` — `capital_gains_excluded_from_taxable_income` matched only because its name ends in _taxable_income, not because of anything in 26 USC 1(h). Behaviorally the wrap appears to be a no-op: within this module net_capital_gain and adjusted_net_capital_gain are both floored at 0 and adjusted_net_capital_gain <= net_capital_gain, so for taxable_income >= 0 the subtracted max(...) is always <= taxable_income (result >= 0), and for taxable_income < 0 the expression evaluates to adjusted_net_capital_gain (>= 0); taxable_income itself was floored at 0 by the immediately preceding commit 9203ca050 (statutes/26/63.yaml). The rest of the 158-line diff is pure provenance/metadata (module.proof_validation.required plus one metadata.proof.atoms block per rule) and is mechanical. I did not classify this 'mechanical' only because a formula string did change, which the mechanical definition excludes. No tests accompany the change (test_files empty); the repair manifest also narrowed applied_files from [h.yaml, h.test.yaml] to [h.yaml] only, dropping the companion test file from the manifest binding — worth a reviewer's attention. The PR the bundle attached (rulespec-us#25, 'Encode 26 USC 63(c) standard deduction') has no reviews or comments and its body does not mention capital gains or floors, so it supplies no evidence about this commit; the only quotable text is the commit subject. Recommend a reviewer prune this from a fidelity-defect corpus unless they can exhibit an input where the pre-fix formula returns a negative value.

verdict.justification: The only meaning-bearing hunk wraps `capital_gains_excluded_from_taxable_income` in `max(0, ...)`, and the commit's own manifest shows it was produced by a source-blind mechanical sweep ("tool": "axiom-encode repair-nonnegative-floors", "runner": "deterministic-repair", "model": "nonnegative-floor-v1"), whose selector in axiom-encode (`_NONNEGATIVE_TAXABLE_INCOME_NAME_PATTERN = r"^(?:[A-Za-z0-9_]+_)?taxable_income$"`, validator_pipeline.py:1596) matched this rule solely because its NAME ends in "taxable_income" — the rule is not a taxable-income quantity at all. The pinned corpus text of 26 USC 1(h)(1)(A) has no "not below zero" or "excess (if any)" limit for this quantity (the statute's "(but not below zero)" appears only in 1(h)(2) and 1(h)(3)(A), which the module already floors), and the later regeneration 3320c8e1d anchors this formula to the excerpt "a tax computed at the rates and in the same manner as if this subsection had not been enacted on the greater of—…" with no floor language. I also proved the floor is unreachable: with net_capital_gain and adjusted_net_capital_gain both nonnegative (each is `max(0, ...) + qualified_dividend_income` with QDI >= 0), `max(TI - NCG, min(min(max(TI,0), thr), TI - ANCG)) <= TI` always, so a 400k-draw sweep found the pre-fix minimum to be exactly 0.0 — the change is a no-op defensive floor with no source basis for calling the old text wrong.
verdict.quote: +          max(0, taxable_income
verdict.notes: Refutes the first reader's "unclear/other" and strengthens it to not_a_defect on three independent grounds. (1) Provenance: the commit's companion manifest .axiom/encoding-manifests/statutes/26/1/h.json flips backend "codex"/model "gpt-5.5" to backend "deterministic", "run_id": "deterministic-repair", "tool": "axiom-encode repair-nonnegative-floors", "model": "nonnegative-floor-v1" — an automated lint sweep, not a source-driven repair. (2) Selector: axiom-encode/src/axiom_encode/harness/validator_pipeline.py:1596 and repair_nonnegative_amount_reductions (line 25247) floor any derived Money rule whose name matches `^(?:[A-Za-z0-9_]+_)?taxable_income$` or contains allotment|benefit|credit|deduction|allowance|subsidy|phased_in; the lint message itself states a house convention ("Benefit, allotment, credit, deduction, allowance, and subsidy outputs must use `max(0, ...)`"), not a statutory clause. (3) Unreachability: proved algebraically and by 400k random draws over realistic inputs that the pre-fix expression's minimum is 0.0; it only goes negative if qualified_dividend_income is fed a negative value, which is not a statutory case. All remaining hunks in the diff are proof-atom metadata blocks plus `proof_validation: required: true` — pure provenance. No test file changed in the commit (the manifest actually DROPS statutes/26/1/h.test.yaml from applied_files), consistent with a behavior-preserving edit. Caveat for the reviewer: the commit subject says "Repair", and the verb plus the ~155-line diff is what makes this look like a fidelity fix at a glance; the PR it landed under (#25) is titled "Encode 26 USC 63(c) standard deduction" and its body never mentions 1(h), so PR text gives no independent support. If the corpus builds a set of "real defects", this commit and any sibling `repair-nonnegative-floors` commits should be excluded as a class — they are name-regex transforms that never consult the provision text.

item.subject: Repair taxable income nonnegative floor

triage.commit_summary: The commit wrapped both branches of the top-level `taxable_income` rule in `statutes/26/63.yaml` in `max(0, ...)` so that the computed taxable income cannot go negative, and added one companion test (`low_income_nonitemizer_zero_taxable_income`) asserting a taxable income of 0 for a non-itemizer whose deductions exceed AGI. The apply manifest records the change as a deterministic sweep (`tool: axiom-encode repair-nonnegative-floors`, `model: nonnegative-floor-v1`, `backend: deterministic`) rather than a re-encode, and no new proof atom was added to cite source language for the floor.

modules.description_quote: Repair taxable income nonnegative floor
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix formula let taxable income be negative whenever deductions exceeded gross income or AGI (the added test's non-itemizer would have returned about -2000 instead of 0), which the maintainers call a defect, but 26 USC 63 as cited states no nonnegative floor, so the pre-fix encoding does not visibly disagree with the source text it cites.
modules.triage_notes: Single-line formula change: `if individual_who_does_not_elect_to_itemize_deductions_for_taxable_year: taxable_income_for_individual_who_does_not_itemize else: taxable_income_general_rule` became the same expression with each branch wrapped in `max(0, ...)`. Provision WAS read: resolve_provision.py on us/statute/26/63 against corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-13 (expression_date 2025-12-03) returns 8017 chars with no floor language for taxable income - 63(a) is 'gross income minus the deductions allowed by this chapter', 63(b) is 'adjusted gross income, minus-' and the only occurrence of 'zero' is 63(c)(6) ('the standard deduction shall be zero'), which is a different rule. Evidence that this is a convention sweep rather than a source-fidelity repair: the manifest switched backend from openai/gpt-5.5 to `deterministic` with `tool: axiom-encode repair-nonnegative-floors`, `run_id: deterministic-repair`, `model: nonnegative-floor-v1`; no proof atom was added or changed to cite floor language (the three existing atoms are untouched); and the floor was applied only to the top-level output rule, not to the upstream `taxable_income_general_rule` or `taxable_income_for_individual_who_does_not_itemize`, which is the signature of an output-surface convention. The same module already used an ungrounded `max(0, ...)` on `itemized_deductions` before this commit. The zero floor on taxable income comes from Form 1040 line instructions rather than section 63, and negative results are meaningful elsewhere in the Code (NOL under section 172), so a judge reading only section 63 could not derive the floor. Commit also touched statutes/26/63.test.yaml (one added case) and .axiom/encoding-manifests/statutes/26/63.json (hashes and provenance only); nothing unrelated changed. PR #25 ('Encode 26 USC 63(c) standard deduction', merged 19:57Z, 18 minutes after this commit) has an empty reviews/review_comments/issue_comments set and its body describes the 63(c) encoding, not the floor, so the commit subject is the only quotable description. Follow-up: the May 16 re-encode dbd9933f6 ('Encode section 63 taxable income') kept `max(0, ...)` in the same rule and still added no atom citing a floor; by 095d680d4 the top-level 26/63 module carries `rules: []` with deferral reasons. Recommend a reviewer prune this unless the corpus intends to count modeling-convention floors as fidelity defects.

verdict.justification: The sole module change wraps both branches of `taxable_income` in `max(0, ...)`, but the pinned corpus text of 26 USC 63 (resolved via us-rulespec-2026-07-13, record 7acfd1b0, body sha256 7fa5f5d7) contains no nonnegative floor on taxable income anywhere — the only "shall be zero" in the section is 63(c)(6), which zeroes the *standard deduction* for certain filers and is encoded in a different module. The pre-fix formula therefore tracked the cited text literally, so nothing in the encoding disagreed with the source; the floor is added convention, not corrected meaning, and no proof atom was added or changed to cite any floor language. The commit's own manifest records the change as a name-pattern sweep ("backend": "deterministic", "model": "nonnegative-floor-v1", "tool": "axiom-encode repair-nonnegative-floors"), and I read that tool in axiom-encode this session: `repair_nonnegative_amount_reductions` in `src/axiom_encode/harness/validator_pipeline.py:25247` selects rules only by `kind: derived`, dtype in {money, currency, decimal, integer, number} and a rule-name regex, never consulting the source text — its docstring is "Mechanically floor supported nonnegative amount reduction formulas." This is the taxonomy's "policy choice with no source basis for calling the old text wrong," so it refutes both the "unclear" hold and the "other / missing_nonnegative_floor_on_computed_amount" kind.
verdict.quote: +          if individual_who_does_not_elect_to_itemize_deductions_for_taxable_year: max(0, taxable_income_for_individual_who_does_not_itemize) else: max(0, taxable_income_general_rule)
verdict.notes:
Refutation of the first reader: the reader had the right observation (63 "states no nonnegative floor") but stopped at "unclear"; the added evidence settles it as not_a_defect rather than leaving it in the corpus.

Decisive supporting evidence, all verbatim:
1. Module diff is exactly one line (statutes/26/63.yaml, rules[taxable_income].versions[0].formula). Nothing else in the module changed — proof atoms for `taxable_income` are byte-identical pre and post, and they cite only "Except as provided in subsection (b)", "In the case of an individual who does not elect to itemize his deductions for the taxable year", and "the term “taxable income” means gross income minus the deductions allowed by this chapter (other than the standard deduction)." No excerpt citing a floor exists, because none exists in the section.
2. Source read through the pinned release (resolve_provision.py, us/statute/26/63, corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, corpus_commit 612d20ca, resolved_text_sha256 7fa5f5d7...): subsections (a)-(g) in full. The only zero-flooring language is 63(c)(6) "...the standard deduction shall be zero." — a different quantity, already encoded in statutes/26/63/c.yaml. 63(a) and 63(b) are bare subtractions.
3. The commit's non-module files show the provenance. `.axiom/encoding-manifests/statutes/26/63.json` flips from the encoder run to a sweep: `-  "backend": "openai",` / `+  "backend": "deterministic",`; `-  "model": "gpt-5.5",` / `+  "model": "nonnegative-floor-v1",`; `-  "tool": "axiom-encode encode --apply",` / `+  "tool": "axiom-encode repair-nonnegative-floors",`, with `context_manifest_file`, `generation_prompt_sha256`, `trace_file` all set to null. There is no re-grounding against the corpus.
4. Mechanism read from code this session (not from a message): `src/axiom_encode/harness/validator_pipeline.py:25247` `repair_nonnegative_amount_reductions(content)` filters on `rule.get("kind") == "derived"`, dtype in {"money","currency","decimal","integer","number"}, and `_NONNEGATIVE_TAXABLE_INCOME_NAME_PATTERN.fullmatch(name)` / `_NONNEGATIVE_REDUCTION_AMOUNT_NAME_PATTERN.search(name)`, then `_repair_nonnegative_taxable_income_expression` recurses into if/else branches and returns `f"max(0, {expression})"`. No corpus, citation, or excerpt is consulted at any point. A sibling commit 9d4ff7ef3 "Repair Massachusetts TAFDC nonnegative floor" is the same sweep applied elsewhere — corroborating that this is a repo-wide convention pass, not a per-provision fidelity finding.

Why not "mechanical": the verdict taxonomy reserves mechanical for changes where "formulas, parameters, versions, dates, inputs, outputs, and scope stay the same." A formula changed here, so mechanical does not apply despite the tool's own docstring calling the transform "mechanical." The semantics did change (the added test asserts `us:statutes/26/63#taxable_income: 0` where the pre-fix module returned -19000 for that fixture: AGI 1000 minus standard deduction 20000 with all other subsection-(b) deductions zero); it just changed away from the cited text rather than toward it.

Residual tension a reviewer should weigh (the reason I did not go above ~0.8): Form 1040's taxable-income line carries "If zero or less, enter -0-", and downstream rate schedules in §1 assume a nonnegative base, so a practitioner would call the floored value the correct real-world answer. But that instruction is IRS form guidance, not the text of §63, and this module's `source_verification.corpus_citation_path` is `us/statute/26/63` alone. Cutting the other way, §172(c) defines an NOL as the excess of deductions over gross income, which presupposes the unfloored quantity is meaningful. Either way, the floor's basis lies outside the provision the module cites, so the pre-fix encoding was not wrong against its own source.

If a reviewer disagrees with not_a_defect, the next-best label is unclear (as the first reader had it), not a confirmed fidelity kind — there is no diff line or message text anywhere in this commit or PR #25 asserting that §63 requires a floor. PR #25 ("Encode 26 USC 63(c) standard deduction") never mentions the floor; it has zero reviews and zero review comments, and the commit body is empty (just a newline), so "Repair taxable income nonnegative floor" is the entire maintainer rationale.

item.subject: Repair generated RuleSpec validation coverage

triage.commit_summary: This commit (part of merged PR #25, whose body describes an unrelated 26 USC 63(c) encoding) repairs proof/validation coverage across seven generated modules: it adds `proof_validation: required` plus per-rule proof atoms to the §3101(b)(2) module, re-pins stale import hashes in two modules (self-imports to the `sha256:local` sentinel, one cross-module hash to the target's current digest), and adds companion tests to six modules. Two of the four module files in this chunk also change encoded meaning: the SNAP allotment formula is floored at zero, and the additional-Medicare-tax threshold match gains branches for head-of-household and surviving-spouse filing statuses.

modules.description_quote: Repair generated RuleSpec validation coverage
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix formula subtracted 30 percent of net monthly income from the maximum allotment with no lower bound, so a household whose 30-percent reduction exceeded the maximum allotment received a negative allotment, whereas 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2) contemplates at worst a household 'entitled to no benefits' (zero), never a negative benefit.
modules.triage_notes: Sole change to this module is wrapping both branches of the rounding conditional in max(0, ...). The companion test added in the same commit (initial_month_high_income_zero_allotment: 1-person household, $1,200 unearned income, $298 max allotment) asserts snap_calculated_monthly_allotment_before_minimums = 0; pre-fix that expression evaluates to 298 - ceil(0.3 * net) = -1, so the change is behavioral, not cosmetic. Downstream snap_monthly_allotment masks the negative for initial months (<$10 rule) and for 1-2 person non-initial months (minimum benefit), but a 3+ person non-initial-month household would have emitted a negative allotment. Provision read through the pinned corpus release: 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(A) states the allotment 'shall be equal to the maximum SNAP allotment for the household's size reduced by 30 percent of the household's net monthly income' and (e)(2)(iii) refers to 'an eligible household with three or more members which is entitled to no benefits'; the zero floor is implied by that language rather than stated as an explicit clause, so an 'other: missing zero floor' kind is a defensible alternative. Commit message is generic (subject only, empty body) and the attached PR body describes a different module, hence confidence below 0.8.

modules.description_quote: Repair generated RuleSpec validation coverage
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing in the encoded meaning was wrong: two proof-atom import hashes for same-module targets carried a stale digest and were replaced with the 'sha256:local' sentinel used for intra-module imports.
modules.triage_notes: Diff is exactly two lines, both metadata.proof.atoms[*].import.hash, on imports whose target is this same module (us:statutes/26/22#section_22_age_threshold and #permanent_total_disability_minimum_duration_months). Formulas, versions, effective dates, parameters, entities and outputs are untouched (verified against the post-fix file around lines 195-255). Provenance bookkeeping only; a companion test file statutes/26/22.test.yaml was added in the same commit but the module file's meaning is unchanged.

modules.description_quote: Repair generated RuleSpec validation coverage
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix match on filing_status enumerated only joint (1), married-filing-separately (2) and single (0), so head-of-household and surviving-spouse taxpayers got no threshold at all, leaving 26 USC 3101(b)(2)(C)'s catch-all ('in any other case, $200,000') unrepresented for those statuses.
modules.triage_notes: MIXED MODULE - read carefully before using as a benchmark item. The rest of the diff (module.proof_validation.required plus metadata.proof.atoms blocks on all six rules) is mechanical provenance; only the match arms are meaning-bearing. The fix adds '4 => additional_medicare_wage_tax_joint_threshold' and '3 => additional_medicare_wage_tax_other_threshold'. Branch 3 (head of household) at $200,000 matches the statute's clause (C), which I read through the pinned corpus release: '(A) in the case of a joint return, $250,000, (B) in the case of a married taxpayer (as defined in section 7703) filing a separate return, 1/2 of the dollar amount determined under subparagraph (A), and (C) in any other case, $200,000.' Branch 4 (surviving spouse) at $250,000 is itself unsupported by (C) - a qualifying surviving spouse does not file a joint return - and follow-up commit 1e0518cbf 'Repair generated section 3101(b)(2) filing status threshold (#311)' flips '4 => additional_medicare_wage_tax_joint_threshold' to '...other_threshold' and rewrites the module summary's filing-status convention. So this commit fixes one missing branch correctly and introduces a second defect that a later commit repairs; that later commit is the cleaner amount/scope instance. The companion test added here (surviving_spouse_uses_joint_threshold, filing_status 4 -> 250000) encodes the wrong expectation. Confidence held at 0.6: the diff and test show the missing-coverage defect but the commit message is generic and the PR body describes an unrelated module.

modules.description_quote: Repair generated RuleSpec validation coverage
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing in the encoded meaning was wrong: a single proof-atom import hash pinning us:statutes/7/2015/d/2/C#bona_fide_student_half_time_enrollment_exemption_applies was stale and was re-pinned to the target's current digest.
modules.triage_notes: One-line change (sha256:d94b2a33... -> sha256:9545ebb8...) inside metadata.proof.atoms of the composed exemption rule; the sibling import hashes for subparagraphs A, B, D, E and the rule's formula, versions, entity, period and outputs are unchanged. Import-hash bookkeeping only. Note this module file got no companion test in this commit (only its encoding manifest was updated).

verdict.justification: The single hunk in regulations/7-cfr/273/10.yaml changes the formula of a derived Money rule, wrapping both rounding branches in max(0, ...), so it changes encoded meaning and cannot be mechanical. The pre-fix value propagated: snap_monthly_allotment returns snap_calculated_monthly_allotment_before_minimums unchanged for a non-initial-month household above snap_minimum_benefit_household_size_limit, so a three-or-more-person household whose 30 percent net-income reduction exceeded its maximum allotment received a negative benefit, while 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(A) opens "Except as provided in paragraphs (a)(1), (e)(2)(iii) and (e)(2)(vi) of this section" and (e)(2)(iii) governs "an eligible household with three or more members which is entitled to no benefits" — the source floor is no benefits, never a negative allotment. The encoder already applied max(0, ...) to snap_net_monthly_income in the same module, so the omission here was a missing carve-out rather than a design choice, and the companion test added in the same commit pins the calculated allotment at 0. The missing element is the source's "entitled to no benefits" carve-out that (e)(2)(ii)(A) expressly excepts, which the fix adds, so unrepresented_clause fits better than boundary_direction (no existing bound had its side or strictness flipped).
verdict.quote: +          if state_agency_rounds_thirty_percent_net_income_up: max(0, snap_maximum_allotment_for_household_size - ceil(snap_net_monthly_income * snap_allotment_net_income_reduction_rate)) else: max(0, floor(snap_maximum_allotment_for_household_size - (snap_net_monthly_income * snap_allotment_net_income_reduction_rate)))
verdict.notes: Refutation attempts and why they fail: (1) Mechanical — no: the formula text changed, not just proof atoms/manifests (the manifest and .test.yaml churn in this commit is separate). (2) No output effect — no: only the initial-month (<$10 -> 0) and one/two-person minimum-benefit branches masked the negative; for household_size > snap_minimum_benefit_household_size_limit outside an initial month the negative reaches snap_monthly_allotment directly. (3) New coverage never claimed — no: the rule claims to encode 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(A) and emits dtype Money / unit USD allotments; a negative allotment contradicts the cited source rather than extending it. (4) Wrong kind — boundary_direction is the closest rival, since a reviewer could read an absent lower clamp as a floor/ceiling-side error; I rejected it because no comparison strictness or bound side was flipped, a max(0, ...) clamp was added where none existed. Caveats a reviewer should weigh: the commit message ("Repair generated RuleSpec validation coverage") is generic and the PR (#25, "Encode 26 USC 63(c) standard deduction") never mentions this module, so the fidelity reading comes from the diff plus the source, not from any authored statement; and the zero floor is implied by (e)(2)(iii)/(e)(2)(ii)(B) ("no benefits shall be issued") rather than stated verbatim as "not less than zero" — the regulation's own remedy for that case is denial or suspension, which max(0, ...) approximates numerically but does not model. Provision read through the pinned release us-sc-snap-2026-07-15 (corpus commit 3932af44ea0fb6dd5a7432959a4396356ef8e6ae), citation us/regulation/7/273/10. The new test initial_month_high_income_zero_allotment (household_size 1, unearned 1200, max allotment 298, initial month) exercises the clamp on the intermediate rule but its final allotment would be 0 either way, so the test alone is not the evidence — the 3+ person propagation path is.

But the defect is filing-status coverage of the derived rule, not a missing clause: 3101(b)(2)(C)'s catch-all and its $200,000 were already encoded (`additional_medicare_wage_tax_other_threshold` = '200000', applied to status 0), so nothing about the clause was unrepresented — the rule simply applied to the wrong population, which the kind list assigns to wrong_entity_or_scope. The first reader's rationale is also partly contradicted by the fix itself: it maps status 4 to the $250,000 joint threshold, not to the catch-all, and the pinned corpus text reads "(A) in the case of a joint return, $250,000 ... (C) in any other case, $200,000" with no surviving-spouse language, which is why the later commit 1e0518cbf re-repaired `4 => additional_medicare_wage_tax_other_threshold`.

verdict.notes: Bundle path statutes/26/3101/b/2.yaml, module index 2; commit ee7f9bc09a, parent 86e2549dc7. item.subject: Remove ungrounded derived tax amounts

triage.commit_summary: The commit re-grounds the additional Medicare tax thresholds in the two §1401 and §3101(b)(2) statute modules: the pre-fix encodings carried a filing-status-indexed parameter table with a hard-coded $125,000 married-filing-separately cell, an amount that appears nowhere in the statutes, which instead define that threshold as "½ of the dollar amount" of the joint figure. The fix splits the table into a joint ($250,000) and an other-case ($200,000) parameter and computes the separate-return threshold as joint/2 in a match on filing_status, and it separately adds a provenance-only source_verification block to the SNAP FY2026 income-eligibility module (plus one added expected output in an unrelated standard-deduction test file).

modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing was wrong in the encoded meaning; the module only lacked a source_verification provenance block, and every parameter value it now asserts was already present unchanged in the rules.
modules.triage_notes: The entire 33-line diff is an addition of module.source_verification (source_url plus a values map). I read the post-fix rules section: snap_net_income_limit_100_percent_fpl_48_states_dc_table (1305/1763/2221/2680/3138/3596/4055/4513), the 459/596/757 additional-member parameters and the 130%/165% tables are byte-identical to the pre-fix versions, and the added source_verification values mirror them exactly. Provision not read (SNAP FNS PDF, not a corpus statute citation) because nothing turned on the source text.

modules.description_quote: Remove ungrounded derived tax amounts
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module stated the married-filing-separately threshold as a hard-coded $125,000 literal, a figure that appears nowhere in 26 USC 1401(b)(2)(A), whose clause (ii) instead defines that threshold as one-half of the clause (i) joint amount, so the encoding asserted a derived number in place of the derivation the statute actually enacts.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus (us-rulespec-2026-07-13, us/statute/26/1401): 26 USC 1401(b)(2)(A) reads '(i) in the case of a joint return, $250,000, (ii) in the case of a married taxpayer (as defined in section 7703) filing a separate return, 1/2 of the dollar amount determined under clause (i), and (iii) in any other case, $200,000.' No literal 125000 in the source, confirming the commit subject. The fix is value-preserving arithmetically (250000/2 = 125000) but changes the encoded structure so the MFS threshold tracks the joint parameter, which is what the statute says; classification is fidelity rather than mechanical because parameters, rule names and the derived formula all changed. Note a side effect: the post-fix match drops the explicit filing_status 3 arm that the old table carried (3: 200000). I read axiom-rules-engine src/formula.rs (lower_to_scalar, Expr::Match): a match with no '_' arm falls back to the last arm's result, here '0 => other_threshold' (200000), so head-of-household still resolves to 200000 and the unchanged companion tests still pass; the arm is non-exhaustive rather than wrong. Commit body is empty and there is no PR in the bundle (pr: null), so the subject line is the only quotable evidence. Later commit 3f609bb66 'Regenerate self-employment tax RuleSpec' touched this file.

modules.description_quote: Remove ungrounded derived tax amounts
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module encoded the married-filing-separately additional Medicare wage tax threshold as a literal $125,000, which 26 USC 3101(b)(2)(B) never states; the statute defines it as one-half of the subparagraph (A) joint amount, so the encoding carried a derived number with no basis in the cited text.
modules.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 1, on the wage side. Provision read through the pinned corpus (us-rulespec-2026-07-13, us/statute/26/3101): '(A) in the case of a joint return, $250,000, (B) in the case of a married taxpayer (as defined in section 7703) filing a separate return, 1/2 of the dollar amount determined under subparagraph (A), and (C) in any other case, $200,000.' Same non-exhaustive-match side effect as index 1 (filing_status 3 arm dropped; falls back to the final '0 => other_threshold' = 200000, so the unchanged companion test case head_of_household_above_threshold still expects and gets 200000). Follow-up commit 1e0518cbf 'Repair generated section 3101(b)(2) filing status threshold (#311)' later restored explicit 3 and 4 arms and fixed a separate, genuine defect this commit did not touch: the module summary/convention here still says '1 = joint / surviving spouse', and that commit re-mapped surviving spouse (status 4) from the joint $250,000 to the other-case $200,000. That is a distinct wrong_entity_or_scope defect belonging to 1e0518cbf, not to this commit. Commit body is empty and pr is null in the bundle.

verdict.justification: The pinned corpus text of 26 USC 1401(b)(2)(A) reads "(i) in the case of a joint return, $250,000, (ii) in the case of a married taxpayer ... filing a separate return, ½ of the dollar amount determined under clause (i), and (iii) in any other case, $200,000", and ½ × 250,000 = 125,000 exactly, so the pre-fix table cell `2: 125000` encoded precisely the amount the statute determines — no number, boundary, date, scope, or logic disagreed with the source. The fix replaces the literal with the statutory derivation `joint_threshold / 2`, which changes representation and provenance (the commit's "ungrounded" concern) while leaving every computed threshold identical for filing statuses 0, 1, and 2, so it does not correct an encoded meaning. It is also not true that the fix removed an ungrounded branch: the only branch actually deleted is `3: 200000`, which clause (iii) ("in any other case, $200,000") plainly grounds, and the post-fix `match` covers only 1, 2, 0 — the later regeneration 3f609bb66 had to restore `3 => ..._other_threshold` (and add 4). Because nothing the fix changed brought the encoding into agreement with the source, "untraceable_branch" is not supported and no fidelity kind fits.
verdict.quote:
-          2: 125000
+              2 => additional_medicare_self_employment_joint_threshold / 2
verdict.notes:
Evidence trail: bundle module index 1, diff /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/diffs/us/429c02408a/001.diff; pre file 34ad1467701d956dbacca81e4a9971467ff4b154:statutes/26/1401.yaml, post 429c02408a:statutes/26/1401.yaml; provision resolved through release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, corpus_commit 612d20ca4325a9f27ccfe33482b5ea5d1ef89e4e, citation us/statute/26/1401, resolved_text_sha256 38a25e0db79501f48205f05a735ee97cd663d622044f1de9747d015482dd2e65.

Three points a reviewer should weigh before keeping this case:
1. Value-preserving. Pre-fix threshold by filing status: {0: 200000, 1: 250000, 2: 125000, 3: 200000}. Post-fix: {1: 250000, 2: 250000/2 = 125000, 0: 200000}. Statuses 0/1/2 are numerically unchanged; a companion test would pass identically against both versions. A defect corpus built for fidelity verification would be teaching a verifier to flag a correct amount.
2. The fix lost coverage rather than removing an ungrounded branch. `-          3: 200000` is deleted with no replacement arm and no default, although the module's own summary (unchanged by the commit) still states "3 head of household/other case", and clause (iii) grounds $200,000 for that case. Commit 3f609bb66 ("Regenerate self-employment tax RuleSpec") later restores `3 => additional_medicare_self_employment_other_threshold` and adds `4 => ...`, plus an explicit `additional_medicare_self_employment_separate_threshold` built from a `separate_threshold_fraction` parameter of `1 / 2`. If anything is the defect here, it is the arm dropped by 429c02408a, not anything present before it.
3. Steelman for the original reading, and why I still refute it: the taxonomy's parenthetical "(the fix removes or re-grounds it)" does describe re-grounding a literal, and $125,000 appears nowhere in the enacted text, so under Axiom's groundedness doctrine the literal is untraceable as written. But the same taxonomy defines a fidelity defect as "an encoded meaning that disagrees with the cited source text", and this meaning agrees. The change is closest in kind to the excerpt/citation-string corrections the instructions classify as provenance rather than fidelity; it is not strictly "mechanical" only because rule names, parameter structure, and the formula body changed. A reviewer who treats ungrounded-but-correct literals as in-scope for this corpus should reclassify to untraceable_branch rather than confirm; my confidence is 0.62 because that policy call, not the facts, is what separates the two answers.
4. The sibling file statutes/26/3101/b/2.yaml (module index 2) in the same commit received the identical edit with the identical properties (125000 → joint/2, branch 3 dropped), so whatever the reviewer decides here should apply to that case too.

verdict.justification: The corpus text of 26 USC 3101(b)(2)(B) resolved through release us-rulespec-2026-07-13 reads "in the case of a married taxpayer (as defined in section 7703) filing a separate return, ½ of the dollar amount determined under subparagraph (A)", and ½ × $250,000 is exactly $125,000 — so the pre-fix literal did not disagree with the source, and the post-fix `joint_threshold / 2` computes the identical number. The commit is a derivation/provenance refactor (stop hard-coding an amount the statute states as a formula), which the rubric puts outside fidelity: no threshold, rate, comparison, scope, or effective date changed for any filing status the new match still covers. It is not "mechanical" either, since rule names, parameters, and formulas were rewritten, but no encoded meaning was corrected. Notably the change moves in the wrong direction for coverage: the pre-fix table carried `3: 200000` (correct under (C)), the post-fix match has no `3` arm at all, while the untouched companion test at the same commit still asserts 200000 for filing_status 3.
verdict.quote:
-          2: 125000
+              2 => additional_medicare_wage_tax_joint_threshold / 2
verdict.notes:
Statute text verified via resolve_provision.py (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, corpus commit 612d20ca43, provision record a0e0112b-9ca1-57e0-9a5d-7c9062cb1eeb): "(B) in the case of a married taxpayer (as defined in section 7703) filing a separate return, ½ of the dollar amount determined under subparagraph (A)". 125000 is that half exactly, so the first reader's premise ("carried a derived number with no basis in the cited text") is true about provenance but false about meaning — the number is grounded, just computed rather than quoted.

Evidence the change is behavior-neutral-or-worse, not a correction:
1. statutes/26/3101/b/2.test.yaml is NOT in this commit's file list (`git show 429c02408a --stat`: only standard-deduction.test.yaml, the SNAP policy file, 26/1401.yaml, 26/3101/b/2.yaml). Its `separate_above_threshold` case still expects `additional_medicare_wage_tax_threshold: 125000` before and after — the fix changed no expected value.
2. The post-fix match covers only 1, 2, 0. The pre-fix table covered 0,1,2,3 with `3: 200000`, correct under (C) "in any other case", while the module summary still declares "3 = head of household" and the unchanged test's `head_of_household_above_threshold` case asserts 200000 for filing_status 3. So this commit deleted a correctly-grounded branch.
3. Commit 1e0518cbf (2026-05-28) "Repair generated section 3101(b)(2) filing status threshold (#311)" later re-adds `3 => additional_medicare_wage_tax_other_threshold` and fixes `4 => ...other_threshold` — i.e. the (A)-(C) filing-status mapping needed repair after this commit, not because of what this commit fixed.
4. The sibling file 26/1401.yaml in the same commit makes the identical edit and its summary change only deletes the parenthetical "($125,000)" from prose that already said "one-half of that amount" — confirming the commit's intent is "don't restate a derived amount", i.e. provenance.

If a reviewer wants to keep this case rather than prune it, the honest label is a provenance/derivation cleanup (mechanical-adjacent), not untraceable_branch: nothing computed changes, and "untraceable_branch" as defined requires a branch or value with no basis in the source, whereas (B) supplies the basis arithmetically. There is a defensible opposite reading — that this commit INTRODUCED a wrong_entity_or_scope defect by dropping filing_status 3 — but that is a defect in the post state, so it cannot make 429c02408a a fidelity fix. Recommend dropping this from the real-defect corpus, or re-targeting the corpus entry at 1e0518cbf, which does change encoded meaning for filing statuses 3 and 4.

item.subject: Address sol round-1: add paragraph-8 override and edge coverage

triage.commit_summary: Responding to a sol round-1 review on PR #307 (wave-11 Middlesbrough working-age CTR encode), the commit adds a new derived rule for Schedule 1 paragraph 8 and wires it as the first branch of the banded-discount selector so that a passported applicant with adverse income/capital evidence (or a failure to respond to an evidence request) drops to the zero-discount band instead of Band 1. It also adds an unused `per_cent_unit` (0.01) parameter, two new pending-oracle ledger entries, and roughly 1,600 lines of companion tests covering the paragraph-8 classifier and the per-family band income edges.

modules.description_quote: Address sol round-1: add paragraph-8 override and edge coverage
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix selected_band_index awarded Band 1 to every passported applicant with no path to zero discount, omitting the Schedule 1 paragraph 8 carve-out that denies any discount where the authority holds adverse income/capital evidence or the applicant failed to respond to an evidence request — an exception the rule's own paragraph-7 proof excerpt already flagged ('except where the authority determines that 8 below applies').
modules.triage_notes: Provision read via resolve_provision on uk-middlesbrough/.../page-65 (pinned release): paragraph 7 awards Band 1 to IS/IR-ESA/IB-JSA recipients 'except where the authority determines that 8 below applies', and paragraph 8 states the no-discount override verbatim as quoted in the new rule's proof excerpt. Decisive evidence that this is a missing-clause defect rather than added scope: the pre-fix selected_band_index proof atom ALREADY cited the paragraph-7 sentence containing 'except where the authority determines that 8 below applies', while its formula encoded no such exception; the only change to that rule is the single formula line prepending 'if ..._paragraph_8_adverse_evidence_or_failure_applies: ..._zero_band_index else: <old formula>'. The new derived rule gates on passported_to_band_1, which is consistent with paragraph 8's scope ('bands 1 to 4, where that band is determined as a result of state benefit entitlement') because in this scheme benefit entitlement only ever determines Band 1 (paragraph 7); paragraph 4's separate capital>£10,000 disentitlement is untouched and already encoded. Secondary, non-defect change in the same module: a new parameter middlesbrough_council_tax_reduction_per_cent_unit = 0.01 with a page-70 excerpt ('100 per cent. of such payments', Schedule 1 para 25 board-and-lodging disregard). I confirmed via `git show 97c58907b2:<path> | grep -n per_cent_unit` that nothing references it, and `git log 97c58907b2..HEAD -- <path>` shows no later commits on the file, so it stays dangling — it changes no computed meaning and is at most added precision, not a correction; it does not alter the module-level classification. Also in the commit but outside this module: one new input (authority_has_paragraph_8_adverse_evidence_or_evidence_response_failure, Boolean/Household/Week), two oracle-coverage-pending entries with ceiling 3056 -> 3058, and ~1,600 lines of companion tests (a paragraph_8_classifier case plus single/couple band edge cases at 126.77/126.78, 228.17, etc.). Caveat on quote provenance: the bundle's PR record for #307 has empty reviews/review_comments/issue_comments, so the named 'sol round-1' review itself is not retrievable here; the commit subject is the only maintainer statement naming the fix, and the paragraph-8 excerpt inside the module diff corroborates it.

verdict.justification: Every refutation route fails. The pinned-release resolver (uk-rulespec-2026-09-05, corpus commit 019e8600f6, page-65) returns Schedule 1 paragraph 8 verbatim as quoted in the fix, and paragraph 7 in that same page reads "discount will be awarded at Band 1 level except where the authority determines that 8 below applies" — a sentence the PRE-fix module already carried as the proof excerpt on the very rule being fixed (pre.yaml line 677, rules[...selected_band_index].versions[0].formula), so the omission is a gap against the encoding's own cited text, not uncovered scope. It is also not an enhancement the module never claimed: Schedule 1 paragraph 8 appears nowhere in module.deferred_outputs (the only deferred "paragraph 8" is Schedule 3 paragraph 8 joint-claim-couple status, a different provision), and the module summary claims the Schedule 1 banded grid. The diff changes encoded meaning — a passported household with authority adverse evidence moves from band_1_index (90 per cent) to zero_band_index (0 per cent) — which is the addition of a source-stated carve-out, i.e. unrepresented_clause, not polarity inversion, boundary strictness, or an untraceable branch.
verdict.quote: if middlesbrough_council_tax_reduction_paragraph_8_adverse_evidence_or_failure_applies: middlesbrough_council_tax_reduction_zero_band_index else: if middlesbrough_council_tax_reduction_passported_to_band_1: middlesbrough_council_tax_reduction_band_1_index
verdict.notes: Verified source text (resolver, page-65, resolved_text_sha256 ebe639685556e906862d625225d8bedfd3d3115035e8b15c743a4a8c1c5e44be): "8. Where an applicant is otherwise entitled to discount in bands 1 to 4, where that band is determined as a result of state benefit entitlement, but the authority has evidence or there has been a failure to respond to a request for evidence concerning income or capital that would otherwise mean no discount then no discount may be granted." Matches the added proof excerpt exactly. Two side observations for the reviewer, neither of which alters the verdict: (1) the same commit adds a parameter middlesbrough_council_tax_reduction_per_cent_unit = 0.01 that no formula in the post-fix module references (grep of post.yaml shows only its definition) — dead additive metadata asserted by a companion-test expectation, not part of the defect; (2) the new paragraph-8 rule fires only when passported_to_band_1, narrowing the source's "bands 1 to 4, where that band is determined as a result of state benefit entitlement" — defensible because paragraph 7 makes Band 1 the only benefit-determined band in this scheme, but a residual fidelity question if any other band can be benefit-determined. Paragraph 4's capital cliff ("including where the authority determines that 8 below applies") is handled upstream in award_conditions_met, so there is no ordering conflict with the new first branch. Companion tests added: middlesbrough_paragraph_8_classifier plus band-edge cases.

item.subject: Address sol round-1: preserve classes and link deductions

triage.commit_summary: Responding to sol's round-1 review of PR #305 (East Hertfordshire working-age CTR, wave 11), the commit rewrites the award-eligibility condition so the scheme's distinct Class D (income less than applicable amount) and Class E (income more than applicable amount plus the amount A > amount B test) routes are each represented, and re-points the maximum-reduction formula at the module's own printed paragraph 58.1-58.2 non-dependant deduction table indexed by the selected band instead of an ungrounded aggregate input. It also drops the now-unused `..._non_dependant_deductions_weekly` input, moves the band input from Person to Household entity, restates the deferred-output entry as the upstream "resolved_non_dependant_deduction_band" determination, and rewrites the companion test file (5 → 33 cases, including income below/equal/above applicable amount and a maximum-after-selected-deduction case).

modules.description_quote: Address sol round-1: preserve classes and link deductions
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix award condition encoded only the Class E 'amount A exceeds amount B' test and left out both class income tests the scheme states — Class D's 'the person's income is less than their applicable amount' route and Class E's 'income is more than their applicable amount' qualifier — and the maximum-reduction formula subtracted an ungrounded aggregate input instead of applying the module's own printed paragraph 58.1-58.2 deduction table at the selected band.
modules.triage_notes: Two distinct fidelity fixes in one module, both named in the subject. (1) 'preserve classes': pre-fix `award_conditions_met` was `... and maximum_weekly > taper_deduction_weekly`; post-fix it is `... and (income + tariff < applicable_amount or (income + tariff > applicable_amount and maximum_weekly > taper_deduction_weekly))`, with two new proof atoms quoting page-8 "person’s income4 is less than their applicable amount5" (Class D) and page-9 "person’s income10 is more than their applicable amount11;" (Class E). I read both provisions through the pinned corpus release (resolve_provision.py, pages 8 and 9): page 8 lists Class D condition (h) income less than applicable amount with no taper test; page 9 lists Class E conditions (i) income more than applicable amount and (k) amount A exceeds amount B. Behavioral delta is real but narrow: a household whose income exactly equals its applicable amount previously passed (excess = 0, taper = 0, so maximum > 0 held) and now correctly falls in neither class — the new companion case `east_hertfordshire_ctr_income_equal_applicable` asserts weekly_amount 0. That equal-income effect could alternatively be read as boundary_direction, but the root cause and the fix are the missing class clauses, so unrepresented_clause. (2) 'link deductions': `maximum_weekly` changed from `- ..._non_dependant_deductions_weekly` (an opaque Household input) to `- ..._non_dependant_deduction_weekly[..._non_dependant_deduction_band]`, i.e. the already-encoded printed table (values {0:0, 1:5.20, 2:10.60, 3:13.30, 4:15.95}, grounded on page-71 paragraphs 58.1-58.2, which I also read and which prescribes exactly those amounts) was dead before this commit; the new case `east_hertfordshire_ctr_maximum_after_selected_deduction` checks 100 * 0.915 - 15.95 = 75.55 at band 4. Taken alone that second fix reads as untraceable_branch (a subtrahend with no grounding in the cited source, re-grounded by the fix); I picked the class fix as decisive because it is named first and the source reading settles it. Collateral non-defect changes: the removed `..._non_dependant_deductions_weekly` input, the band input's entity moved Person -> Household (needed for the Household-level indexed lookup), and the deferred_outputs entry restated from `non_dependant_exemption_classifier` to `resolved_non_dependant_deduction_band`. No formulas outside these two rules changed; parameter values, effective dates (all '2026-04-01') and units are untouched. The bundle's PR record for #305 has empty reviews/review_comments/issue_comments, so the sol round-1 review text itself was not available — the subject line is the only quotable statement of the defect. Sibling commit 1641f4c "Ground Worthing taper and preserve strict classes" applies the same class-preservation pattern to another authority, and no later commit touches this module file.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as a traceability-only refactor and could not: the pinned corpus confirms the scheme prints two working-age income tests the pre-fix encoding simply did not contain — Class D h "the person's income4 is less than their applicable amount5" (page-8) and Class E i "the person's income10 is more than their applicable amount11" (page-9) — while the pre-fix award condition carried only Class E k's "amount A exceeds amount B" comparison. The fix adds both as a disjunction with matching new proof atoms, and the change is behavioral, not cosmetic: the companion suite's new `east_hertfordshire_ctr_income_equal_applicable` case (income 100, applicable 100, liability 100, band 0) now expects weekly_amount 0, where the pre-fix formula (taper = 0, maximum = 91.5 > 0) would have awarded 91.5. A source-stated condition was missing and the fix supplies it, so fidelity / unrepresented_clause holds on the rule_path given (award_conditions_met.versions[0].formula).
verdict.quote: (east_hertfordshire_council_tax_reduction_assessed_income_weekly + east_hertfordshire_council_tax_reduction_tariff_income_weekly < east_hertfordshire_council_tax_reduction_applicable_amount_weekly or (east_hertfordshire_council_tax_reduction_assessed_income_weekly + east_hertfordshire_council_tax_reduction_tariff_income_weekly > east_hertfordshire_council_tax_reduction_applicable_amount_weekly and east_hertfordshire_council_tax_reduction_maximum_weekly > east_hertfordshire_council_tax_reduction_taper_deduction_weekly))
verdict.notes: Caveats a reviewer should carry forward. (1) The second half of the first reader's reading — that maximum_weekly "subtracted an ungrounded aggregate input" — is the weak half and should not be what the kind rests on. Paragraph 57.1(b) on page-71 expressly says the maximum is computed "less any deductions in respect of non-dependants which fall to be made under section 58", so the pre-fix input `east_hertfordshire_council_tax_reduction_non_dependant_deductions_weekly` was a grounded delegation, not an invented value; what was actually wrong is that the module declared the printed 58.1-58.2 table with proof atoms and never referenced it (dead parameter, dead Person-entity band input). Linking it is a wiring/coverage fix, and arguably narrows coverage: 58.1 gives a deduction per non-dependant, while the post-fix single Household-entity band lookup can express only one selected band (58.3's one-deduction-per-couple rule does not merge two unrelated non-dependants). On its own that half would be "unclear". (2) The class-test half is nearly behavior-preserving away from the boundary: when income <= applicable, excess income is floored at 0 so taper = 0 and the old test reduces to maximum_weekly > 0. The demonstrable outcome flips are income exactly equal to the applicable amount (pre awarded, post denies, matching the source's literal strict "less than"/"more than" pair) and Class D households with maximum_weekly <= 0 (pre denied, post grants). So this is a genuine but corner-case meaning change, which is why I sit at 0.8 rather than higher. (3) The fix is partial and the module still under-represents the source: Class D h's alternative route "or the applicant or partner is in receipt of income support, jobseekers' allowance (income based) or employment and support allowance (income related)" is still unencoded, and the rule's `source:` field still reads "East Hertfordshire Council Tax Reduction Scheme 2026/27 Class E" although the formula now encodes Class D as well. (4) Not mechanical under any reading: formulas, an input's entity (Person -> Household), the input list, and a deferred_outputs target all changed. (5) Corpus resolution used release uk-rulespec-2026-09-05, corpus commit 019e8600f6, provision file sha256 60cd0071c5961fee22b048f3d19aa937c188588076abf5e323a7128d2f9a2445. (6) Scratchpad hygiene note: generic filenames pre.yaml/post.yaml in the shared scratchpad were overwritten mid-session by a concurrent worker's Middlesbrough content; I re-extracted under a unique name (eherts_post_a55b.yaml). Other verifier workers on this corpus may hit the same collision.

item.subject: Convert Worthing taper per-cent ground to oldham per_cent_unit parity

triage.commit_summary: The commit rewrites the Worthing CTR taper's percent conversion from a `percent_divisor` parameter of 100 divided into the mixed-number taper to a `per_cent_unit` Rate of 0.01 multiplied by it, re-grounding the proof atom from the page-25 taper sentence to the page-40 maximum provision's printed "100 per cent of the amount A/B" notation, exactly mirroring the already-merged uk-oldham precedent. It was an intra-PR fixup on PR #267 made because the validator would not ground a bare literal 100 against either cited provision; the arithmetic is unchanged (the companion's weekly_taper_rate expectation stays 0.2, and only the renamed parameter's own expectation moves from 100 to 0.01), with the oracle-coverage ledger legal_id and the module summary sentence updated to match.

modules.description_quote: The percent-divisor form (/100) cannot ground: the validator rejects the literal 100 against both the taper sentence and the page-40 maximum provision.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing in the encoded meaning was wrong — (2 + 6/7)/100 equals (2 + 6/7)*0.01, so the daily and weekly taper rates are identical before and after; the pre-fix parameter's literal 100 simply had no printed basis in its cited page-25 taper sentence, a provenance/grounding defect rather than a disagreement with the source.
modules.triage_notes: Verified arithmetic neutrality three ways: (1) the parameter has exactly one consumer, worthing_council_tax_reduction_daily_taper_rate (git grep of the pre-fix file at parent 95b5a8df shows only line 130 referencing percent_divisor); (2) the companion test diff leaves worthing_council_tax_reduction_weekly_taper_rate at 0.2 and changes only the renamed parameter's own expectation 100 -> 0.01; (3) downstream income_taper_deduction_weekly and weekly_amount formulas are untouched. Read the cited provision through the pinned release (resolve_provision.py, uk-worthing/.../page-40): para 29.0(1) does print "that person's maximum council tax reduction amount in respect of a day is 100 per cent of the amount A/B", so the new excerpt is verbatim and the per-cent-unit grounding is genuine. Confirmed the parity claim against uk-oldham/policies/oldham/council-tax-reduction.yaml at this commit: oldham_council_tax_reduction_per_cent_unit is dtype Rate, formula 0.01, atom excerpt "100 per cent of the amount A/B less C" — Worthing now mirrors it (Worthing's copy omits oldham's `period: Year`, which is the one non-identical detail). Classified mechanical under the rule that excerpt/citation-path provenance corrections are provenance, not fidelity; the counter-argument a reviewer should weigh is that the diff does change a parameter value (100 -> 0.01), its dtype (Number -> Rate) and the consuming operator (/ -> *), and one could read the pre-fix literal 100 as an untraceable value that the fix re-grounds (untraceable_branch) — hence confidence 0.72 rather than higher. Do not conflate with the immediately preceding commit on the same branch, 1641f4c "Ground Worthing taper and preserve strict classes", which contains a genuine boundary_direction fidelity fix (award_conditions_met changed income <= applicable_amount to income < applicable_amount) and first moved this same parameter's atom to page-25; this commit only finishes the grounding. PR #267 has no reviews or review comments ("Sol batch review to follow on this head"), so the commit message is the only stated reason. Non-module files in the commit: oracle-coverage-pending.yaml legal_id rename and the companion test.

item.subject: Ground Worthing taper and preserve strict classes

triage.commit_summary: The commit re-grounds Worthing's council tax reduction percent divisor from the 100%-maximum paragraph (29.0(1), page-40) and a stray section heading (page-83 "100.0 Extended reductions") onto the operative taper sentence at paragraph 14.0(f)(ii) ("amount B is 2 6/7 per cent…", page-25), leaving the value 100 unchanged, and it tightens the award-conditions formula from `income <= applicable_amount` to `income < applicable_amount`. The second change is the substantive one: paragraph 13.0 Class D covers income strictly "less than" the applicable amount and paragraph 14.0 Class E strictly "greater than" it, so the scheme assigns no class at equality; the encoding had swept equality into Class D and paid a full award, and the companion case at equality flips from holds/£100 to not_holds/£0.

modules.description_quote: Class D strictly requires income less than the applicable amount and Class E strictly requires income greater than it; the corpus assigns no class at equality, so this module preserves that drafting gap rather than extending either class.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The award-conditions formula used a non-strict `income_including_tariff_weekly <= applicable_amount_weekly` for the Class D branch, so an applicant whose income exactly equals the applicable amount received a full award, whereas paragraph 13.0 Class D requires income "less than his applicable amount" and paragraph 14.0 Class E requires income "greater than his applicable amount", leaving equality in no class at all.
modules.triage_notes: Two-part change in one module. (1) Decisive fidelity change: `<=` -> `<` in worthing_council_tax_reduction_award_conditions_met.versions[0].formula. Provision read through the pinned release (corpus_release uk-rulespec-2026-08-10, corpus_commit f398953a) at uk-worthing/manual/council-tax-reduction-scheme-2026-2027/page-25: para 13.0 Class D (e) "whose income (if any) for the relevant week is less than his applicable amount" and para 14.0 Class E (e) "whose income for the relevant week is greater than his applicable amount" - both strict, no equality branch, so the pre-fix inclusive bound invented entitlement at the boundary. The companion test in the same commit confirms the behavior change: case worthing_ctr_income_including_tariff_equals_applicable_amount (income 99 + tariff 1 = 100 vs applicable 100) flips award_conditions_met holds->not_holds and weekly_amount 100->0. (2) Secondary, non-decisive: worthing_council_tax_reduction_percent_divisor had its `source:` string and proof atoms re-grounded from page-40 para 29.0(1) plus a page-83 section heading ("100.0 Extended reductions (qualifying contributory benefits).", which never supported a percent divisor) onto the operative taper sentence on page-25; the formula stays `100`, so per the triage rules that half is provenance/mechanical, not fidelity - worth flagging to a reviewer as a formula-grounded-on-wrong-provision repair that happens to leave the value intact. The module summary sentence quoted above was added in this same diff and is the only prose describing the defect (commit body is empty; PR #267 body predates this re-land and has no reviews or review comments). Only this module plus its .test.yaml changed; no unrelated edits.

verdict.justification: The diff flips the Class D branch of the award-conditions formula from a non-strict `<=` to a strict `<` against the applicable amount, and the pinned corpus page-25 confirms the strictness verbatim: ¶13.0(e) "whose income (if any) for the relevant week is less than his applicable amount," and ¶14.0(e) "whose income for the relevant week is greater than his applicable amount". Pre-fix the module encoded `<=` while its own unchanged proof atom already quoted the "less than" excerpt, so the encoding contradicted its cited source and granted a full award to an applicant whose income equals the applicable amount, a case neither class reaches. The companion case `worthing_ctr_income_including_tariff_equals_applicable_amount` flips from `award_conditions_met: holds` / `weekly_amount: 100` to `not_holds` / `0`, proving a real meaning change at the boundary rather than bookkeeping. The commit's other change (percent_divisor re-grounded from ¶29.0(1)/page-40 and a page-83 atom to ¶14.0(f)(ii)/page-25) leaves the value `100` unchanged and is provenance-only, so it does not displace boundary_direction as the kind.
verdict.quote: (worthing_council_tax_reduction_income_including_tariff_weekly < worthing_council_tax_reduction_applicable_amount_weekly or (worthing_council_tax_reduction_income_including_tariff_weekly > worthing_council_tax_reduction_applicable_amount_weekly and worthing_council_tax_reduction_maximum_weekly_amount > worthing_council_tax_reduction_income_taper_deduction_weekly))
verdict.notes: Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "source is silent at equality, so the old text was a policy choice" — no, ¶13.0(e) states an affirmative requirement that equality fails, so awarding at equality asserts entitlement under a class whose printed condition is unmet; the fix preserves the gap the drafter left. (2) "Class F covers equality" — ¶15.0 Class F is the alternative-maximum (second-adult) route keyed to other residents' income and never references the applicable amount, so it supplies no basis for `<=`. (3) "the real change is the taper re-grounding (untraceable_branch)" — the percent_divisor formula value stays `100`; only the rule `source:` string and proof-atom citation/excerpt changed, which the rubric classes as mechanical provenance. (4) "mechanical overall" — ruled out by the formula operator change and the companion-case output flip. Provision verified through the pinned release: corpus_release uk-rulespec-2026-08-10, corpus_commit f398953ab9, provision_file_sha256 2aaaedc1..., stored_body_sha256 ca8cab09..., record 3e92afdd-a41d-53db-a179-0a62f50986c1. Note for the reviewer: this commit bundles one fidelity change and one provenance change; if the corpus wants single-kind cases, the divisor re-grounding is the mechanical half.

item.subject: Fix Worthing CTR taper and boundary coverage

triage.commit_summary: The commit reworked the Worthing 2026/27 working-age CTR module in two ways: it replaced the hard-coded 28-digit decimal daily taper literal (0.0285714285714285714285714286) with four new printed-component parameters (2, 6, 7, 100) so the daily rate is computed as (2 + 6/7)/100 and the derived weekly taper becomes exactly 0.2 instead of 0.2000000000000000000000000002, and it loosened the Class D branch of worthing_council_tax_reduction_award_conditions_met from income < applicable amount to income <= applicable amount, adding a companion case asserting an award at exact equality (plus two tariff-income boundary cases). The stated motive is the encoding-discipline rule that the printed mixed number, not a decimal literal, grounds the taper; the boundary half was reverted five days later by 1641f4c "Ground Worthing taper and preserve strict classes", whose summary records that the corpus assigns no class at equality and the module must preserve that drafting gap.

modules.description_quote: taper decomposed from the printed mixed number by the printed 7-day denominator (oldham 4-param precedent), never a decimal literal
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix daily taper was a rounded 28-digit decimal literal instead of the printed "2 6/7 per cent", so the derived weekly taper evaluated to 0.2000000000000000000000000002 rather than exactly 20 percent - a genuine but de-minimis (2e-28) numeric departure from the source, while the commit's other change (Class D "<" to "<=") was not source-supported and was later reverted.
modules.triage_notes: Two-part commit, and only one part survives as a candidate defect. (1) Taper: pre-fix rules[worthing_council_tax_reduction_daily_taper_rate].versions[0].formula was the literal 0.0285714285714285714285714286, cited to the page-25 excerpt "amount B is 2 6/7 per cent..."; the fix adds four printed-component parameters and computes (2 + 6/7)/100. Observable effect is confined to exactness: the companion expectation for daily_taper_rate is unchanged ('0.0285714285714285714285714286'), and only weekly_taper_rate moves from '0.2000000000000000000000000002' to 0.2. A fidelity judge reading the pre-fix module would have to apply a strict exactness/no-decimal-literal norm to flag it, which is why I did not mark this fidelity. (2) Boundary: the fix changed award_conditions_met from income_including_tariff_weekly < applicable_amount_weekly to <=, adding a companion case (worthing_ctr_income_including_tariff_equals_applicable_amount) asserting award_conditions_met: holds and weekly_amount: 100 at equality. I read page-25 through the pinned corpus release (resolve_provision.py, release resolved cleanly): para 13.0(e) Class D reads "whose income (if any) for the relevant week is less than his applicable amount" and para 14.0(e) Class E reads "whose income for the relevant week is greater than his applicable amount" - strict on both sides, so the source assigns no class at equality and the pre-fix "<" matched the printed text. Follow-up commit 1641f4c (2026-08-19, on origin/main) reverts <= back to < and flips that companion case to not_holds / 0, with the module summary stating "Class D strictly requires income less than the applicable amount and Class E strictly requires income greater than it; the corpus assigns no class at equality, so this module preserves that drafting gap rather than extending either class." So this commit's boundary_direction half introduced a defect rather than fixing one; do NOT harvest it as a boundary_direction specimen. (3) This commit also grounded the new percent_divisor parameter partly on an irrelevant excerpt (page-83 "100.0 Extended reductions (qualifying contributory benefits).", a paragraph-number coincidence); 1641f4c dropped it and b12f2ca replaced the whole parameter with a per_cent_unit Rate of 0.01 grounded on page-40 "100 per cent of the amount A/B" because the validator rejected the literal 100. Non-module changes in the commit: the companion test file (new parameter expectations, two tariff-income boundary cases at 6250 and 6250.01, the equality case) and oracle-coverage-pending.yaml (four new legal_ids, ceiling 2984 -> 2988) - bookkeeping. Recommend pruning this commit from the corpus, or keeping it only as a negative/near-miss example.

verdict.justification: The commit has exactly two meaning-level changes and neither survives as a fidelity correction. The taper change replaces the literal 0.0285714285714285714285714286 with a 4-parameter decomposition of the same printed "2 6/7 per cent"; the pre-fix literal is already the correctly-rounded 28-decimal value of 20/700 and already carried the correct proof atom citing that exact sentence, so the only change in encoded meaning is the derived weekly rate moving from 0.2000000000000000000000000002 to 0.2 — a 2e-28 artifact of representing a repeating fraction in the engine's 28-digit decimal type (2e-26 GBP on £100 of excess income), i.e. added precision the module never misstated, which the task rules cap at "not a defect / unclear at most". The Class D/E boundary change is affirmatively wrong, not a fix: the pinned corpus prints "whose income (if any) for the relevant week is less than his applicable amount" (Class D) and "whose income for the relevant week is greater than his applicable amount" (Class E), and commit 1641f4c reverted the "<=" five days later with the rationale that "the corpus assigns no class at equality, so this module preserves that drafting gap". The kind label amount_mismatch is therefore unsupported at any material level, and untraceable_branch does not fit either because the pre-fix value was traceable to the right sentence.
verdict.quote:
-          0.0285714285714285714285714286
+          (worthing_council_tax_reduction_taper_whole_percentage_points + worthing_council_tax_reduction_taper_fraction_numerator / worthing_council_tax_reduction_taper_fraction_denominator) / worthing_council_tax_reduction_percent_divisor
verdict.notes:
New evidence the first reader did not have, all read-only:
1. The boundary half is definitively refuted. Source text resolved through the pinned release (uk-rulespec-2026-08-10, corpus commit f398953a, provision uk-worthing/manual/council-tax-reduction-scheme-2026-2027/page-25) prints Class D as "whose income (if any) for the relevant week is less than his applicable amount" and Class E as "whose income for the relevant week is greater than his applicable amount" — strict on both sides, no class at equality. Follow-up commit 1641f4c (2026-08-19, "Ground Worthing taper and preserve strict classes") restores "<" and adds to the module summary: "Class D strictly requires income less than the applicable amount and Class E strictly requires income greater than it; the corpus assigns no class at equality, so this module preserves that drafting gap rather than extending either class." The companion test worthing_ctr_income_including_tariff_equals_applicable_amount added in this commit asserted award_conditions_met: holds at equality, which the source does not support.
2. The taper half is a 1-ulp decimal refinement, verified numerically at 28-digit precision: literal 0.0285714285714285714285714286 x 7 = 0.2000000000000000000000000002; the decomposition x 7 = 0.2000000000000000000000000000; delta 2E-28 (2.00E-26 GBP on £100 of excess income, i.e. never a penny of award). The test diff corroborates that the engine really carries this (weekly_taper_rate expectation '0.2000000000000000000000000002' -> 0.2), so the departure is real but de minimis and is a representation artifact, not a misreading — the pre-fix atom already cited "amount B is 2 6/7 per cent of the difference between his income for the relevant week and his applicable amount".
3. This commit is a poor fidelity exemplar for a third reason: the percent_divisor it adds is itself grounded on unrelated excerpts (page-40 "100 per cent of the amount A/B" plus page-83 "100.0 Extended reductions (qualifying contributory benefits)." — a paragraph heading number). 1641f4c re-grounds it onto the page-25 taper sentence, and b12f2ca (2026-09-05) then removes the divisor entirely: "The percent-divisor form (/100) cannot ground: the validator rejects the literal 100 against both the taper sentence and the page-40 maximum provision."
Recommendation: prune from the real-defects corpus. If a reviewer prefers to keep it, keep it as unclear/amount_mismatch but record the magnitude (2e-28, no monetary effect), record that the pre-fix value was correctly cited and correctly rounded, and record that the commit's other change was source-contradicting and reverted — otherwise the case teaches a detector that a house-style decomposition ("never a decimal literal") is an amount defect.
