item.subject: Kingston #46 closeout: encoder pin + re-emitted module + waiver removal (atomic) (#158)

triage.commit_summary: The commit is the atomic closeout of rulespec-uk issue #46: it re-emits the Kingston upon Thames council-tax-reduction module so the 20 percent excess-income taper is derived from the grounded daily rate ("amount B is 2 6/7 per cent", manual page 28) times the seven-day conversion (page 40), deleting the fabricated `annual_taper_denominator = 5` parameter that the old `withdrawal_rate` divided into 1. Because a fixed module under an active waiver cannot be green, the same PR also bumps the pinned AXIOM_ENCODE_REF in both workflows, removes the Kingston record from known-validation-gaps.yaml, recomputes validation_waiver_set_sha256 (13 -> 12 records), and refreshes the release fingerprint file.

modules.description_quote: drop the ungrounded annual_taper_denominator (5); derive withdrawal_rate = daily_taper_rate * days_per_week (2 6/7 per cent x 7 = 20 per cent, manual pages 28/40)
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module computed the class E taper as 1 divided by an invented parameter `annual_taper_denominator = 5` whose proof atom cited page-28 text ('amount B is 2 6/7 per cent') that states no denominator of 5 and no annualization, so the taper rate rested on a value with no basis in the cited provision instead of on the source's daily 2 6/7 per cent rate converted over seven days.
modules.triage_notes: Single module in the commit; the module diff is only two hunks (39 lines). Hunk 1 deletes the entire `annual_taper_denominator` parameter rule (value 5, source line 'annualized class E amount B percentage', proof excerpt 'amount B is 2 6/7 per cent' at page-28) and extends the `daily_taper_rate` literal from 0.02857142857142857 to 0.02857142857142857142857142857; hunk 2 rewrites `withdrawal_rate` from `1 / ..._annual_taper_denominator` to `..._daily_taper_rate * ..._days_per_week`. Provision WAS read through the pinned release: page-28 says '(ii) amount B is 2 6/7 per cent of the difference between his income for the relevant week and his applicable amount' within class E ('On any day class E consists of...'), and contains no 5 and no annualization — confirming the deleted parameter was ungrounded. Important caveat for a reviewer: the numeric outcome is unchanged (1/5 = 0.2 and the 28-digit daily literal x 7 = exactly 0.2, which is why all 7 companion tests hold unchanged), so this is a grounding/derivation defect rather than a value defect; if the corpus wants only behavior-changing defects this one is a boundary case, but the maintainers tracked it as a real defect (issue #46 with an active validation waiver) and the PR body calls the deleted parameter 'fabricated'. The module header (singular source_verification with the page-38 locator) is byte-identical to the parent because PR commits 2 and 3 undid the re-emitter's plural corpus_citation_paths/upstream_source_check shape, so none of that contract churn appears in the net diff. Other files in the commit (.axiom/toolchain.toml, both workflow YAMLs, known-validation-gaps.yaml, the release fingerprint JSON) are pin/waiver bookkeeping, not rule content. Corroborating quotes: PR body — 'fabricated `annual_taper_denominator=5` deleted'; PR issue comment (Sol verdict) — 'the withdrawal rate is transparently derived as daily rate x 7 rather than through the erroneous denominator.'

verdict.justification: The pre-fix module carried a source-attributed parameter rule (`kind: parameter`, `source: "... annualized class E amount B percentage"`) whose value was `5` and whose only proof atom cited page-28 with the excerpt "amount B is 2 6/7 per cent"; I resolved page-28 through the pinned release (uk-rulespec-2026-07-14, corpus 592ac643) and its class E text states only "amount B is 2 6/7 per cent of the difference between his income for the relevant week and his applicable amount" — no denominator of 5, no annualization, no 20 per cent — so the module's class E taper rested on a value the cited provision does not state, and the fix deletes that parameter and re-grounds `withdrawal_rate` on the source's own daily rate times the manual's daily conversion (page-40: "£17.31 x 1/7"). That is exactly "a value with no basis in the cited source (the fix removes or re-grounds it)". I tried the two available refutations and both fail: mechanical is excluded because a parameter rule is deleted and a formula rewritten (parameters/formulas did not stay the same), and amount_mismatch fits worse because the taper is 20 per cent before and after — the 17→28 digit extension of `daily_taper_rate` is a representation device so the engine product is exactly 0.2, not a correction of a wrong rate. The only real weakness is that no computed output changes (companions stay 7/7), but the taxonomy's untraceable_branch is precisely the grounding-level kind, and the repo treated it as a live validation gap (waiver #46, removed by this same commit).
verdict.quote: -  - name: kingston_upon_thames_council_tax_reduction_annual_taper_denominator … -              excerpt: "amount B is 2 6/7 per cent" … -          5 … -          1 / kingston_upon_thames_council_tax_reduction_annual_taper_denominator … +          kingston_upon_thames_council_tax_reduction_daily_taper_rate * kingston_upon_thames_council_tax_reduction_days_per_week
verdict.notes: Diff is 2 insertions / 19 deletions in the module, all inside the taper chain. Pre-fix: `daily_taper_rate` (0.02857142857142857) and `days_per_week` (7) existed but were dead — nothing referenced them; `withdrawal_rate = 1 / annual_taper_denominator` = 0.2. Post-fix: the denominator rule is gone, `withdrawal_rate = daily_taper_rate * days_per_week`, and the daily literal is widened to 28 digits (0.02857142857142857142857142857, a truncation of 1/35 = 2 6/7%) so the engine product is exactly 0.2. The single consumer (line 484/501, `excess_income_for_year * withdrawal_rate`) is untouched, so behavior is numerically unchanged — a reviewer who requires an output-visible delta for "fidelity" could push this to unclear/mechanical, but "mechanical" as defined here is unavailable because a parameter rule and a formula changed. Source verification: page-28 (class E, para 17(f)(ii)) grounds 2 6/7 per cent of the weekly excess and nothing else; page-40 (para 30A) grounds the manual's weekly→daily "x 1/7" convention behind days_per_week = 7. Commit message and PR body corroborate ("drop the ungrounded annual_taper_denominator (5)"; "fabricated `annual_taper_denominator=5` deleted"). Note the commit is a 4-part stack that also touches waivers, toolchain pins and the release manifest, but those live in other_files; the module file itself changed only as described. Also note the module header locator moved to page-38 in this commit (module-level metadata, not part of the defect).

item.subject: ground policy surfaces in ingested sources

triage.commit_summary: The commit rewrites the seven remaining UK "PolicyEngine-alignment surface" policy modules (carer support payment, carer's allowance, council tax reduction, DLA, pension credit, Scottish child payment, state pension) so their formulas come from ingested gov.uk / mygov.scot / legislation.gov.uk slices instead of PolicyEngine reported-receipt inputs, takeup gates and dataset-year prorating, and it vendors those provision slices under data/corpus. It also adds a new module for the SI 2015/621 reg 4 national living wage rate, rewords one statute module's summary, and pins the toolchain to axiom-encode 0.2.648.

modules.description_quote: carer's allowance and carer support payment with the 35-hour and £204 earnings conditions
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module paid carer support payment on a PolicyEngine-shaped gate (in Scotland AND a rollout switch AND (35 care hours OR a reported carer's allowance amount)) and never applied the mygov.scot conditions that the carer be aged 16 or over, not in full-time education, caring for someone who gets a qualifying disability benefit, and have take-home pay of no more than £204 a week.
modules.triage_notes: Read the vendored source slices added in this commit (data/corpus/provisions/uk/guidance/2026-06-10-uk-mygovscot-carer-support-payment-{who-can-apply,if-you-work}.jsonl): they state "You can apply for Carer Support Payment if you provide unpaid care for 35 hours or more a week and you must be aged 16 or over", "The person you care for must get a qualifying disability benefit" and "Your 'take home pay' cannot be more than £204 a week", so the added conditions are source-required clauses that were missing. Two defects co-occur in the same module: besides the missing clauses, the pre-fix formula's `or reported_carers_allowance_for_year > 0` disjunct and the `carer_support_payment_in_effect` switch are untraceable branches (PolicyEngine reported receipt / rollout switch, no basis in the cited regulations) that the fix removes; a reviewer who prefers that framing should re-kind this as untraceable_branch. Module was also restructured into weekly + annual rules and the citation set moved from SSI 2023/302 regs 5/16 to mygov.scot guidance (the SSI rate/hours imports are kept). Boundary check: source says pay "cannot be more than £204", encoding uses <= 204 - consistent. Same commit-wide pattern as indices 1-6.

modules.description_quote: carer's allowance and carer support payment with the 35-hour and £204 earnings conditions
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module paid carer's allowance whenever the person met the 35-hour test or had a reported carer's allowance amount, omitting the GOV.UK eligibility conditions that the carer be 16 or over, not in full-time education, caring for someone who gets a qualifying disability benefit, and earning £204 or less a week after tax, National Insurance and expenses.

You're not studying for 21 hours a week or more. Your earnings are £204 or less a week after tax, National Insurance and expenses." - so the added conditions are source-required. Same pattern as index 0, including the co-occurring untraceable `or reported_carers_allowance_for_year > 0` disjunct that the fix removes. Boundary: source "£204 or less" vs encoded <= 204 - consistent.

modules.description_quote: council tax reduction on the SI 2012/2885 prescribed requirements with the 2 6/7 per cent taper encoded exactly (2×7+6 per cent-days)
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module computed the award from PolicyEngine's national CTR framework - an undefined `council_tax_reduction_withdrawal_rate` taper input, a `council_tax_reduction_scheme_supported` / `would_claim_council_tax_reduction` gate, and a fallback to `reported_council_tax_reduction_for_year` for "unsupported" schemes - none of which exists in the SI 2012/2885 prescribed requirements, where amount B is fixed at 2 6/7 per cent of the weekly excess of income over the applicable amount.

Secondary changes worth a reviewer's eye: the module is re-scoped in its summary to "pension-age applicants in England" (narrower than the pre-fix national framework), the reported-CTB fallback for local schemes is dropped entirely, `council_tax_reduction_maximum_support_rate` (=1) is replaced by a per-cent unit parameter, the capital gate now reads `household_capital` instead of `council_tax_reduction_assessed_capital`, and all effective_from values move from 0001-01-01 to 2013-04-01. Provision text not read for this module (no vendored slice for SI 2012/2885 in this commit); judgement rests on the diff plus the commit/PR wording.

Source verified through the pinned release (corpus_release uk-rulespec-2026-07-12, commit 3cc9219ac4): uk/guidance/mygovscot/carer-support-payment/who-can-apply = "You can apply for Carer Support Payment if you provide unpaid care for 35 hours or more a week and you must be aged 16 or over. You must usually live in Scotland. The person you care for must get a qualifying disability benefit."; .../if-you-work = "Your 'take home pay' cannot be more than £204 a week." The diff's new parameter carries the excerpt "take home pay' cannot be more than £204 a week" and formula 204.

Reviewer decision point on kind. This one module change carries two defect kinds at once:
(1) unrepresented_clause — four source-stated conditions added (age, qualifying disability benefit, £204 earnings cap, full-time education);
(2) untraceable_branch — the pre-fix formula's `carer_support_payment_in_effect` rollout switch and `or reported_carers_allowance_for_year > 0` proxy are removed, and the rule's `source:` changes from "PolicyEngine UK carer_support_payment final receipt wrapper over Carer Support Payment Regulations 2023 regs. 5 and 16" to mygov.scot guidance. The commit subject ("ground policy surfaces in ingested sources") and the maintainer comment ("those surfaces are the old pattern this PR removes (\"PolicyEngine-alignment surface… used by PolicyEngine UK and HBAI\", `reported_*` inputs)") both frame the fix as de-grounding a model-derived surface, which favors untraceable_branch. If the corpus wants one label per case and prefers the kind the commit message emphasizes, reclassify to untraceable_branch; if it prefers the kind with the most added source-traceable meaning, keep unrepresented_clause.

Note also that the 35-hour condition quoted in the first reader's PR-body quote was ALREADY present pre-fix (`weekly_care_hours >= carer_support_payment_minimum_weekly_care_hours`); only the £204 half of that quote is new, so the quote overstates the delta slightly.

Two side changes that are not defect fixes and should not drive the kind: effective_from moves from '2026-04-06' to '0001-01-01' (less precise, not a wrong_period correction), and the main derived rule's period changes from Year to Week with a new annualising wrapper. Also, the added `not person_is_in_full_time_education` term has no basis in the resolved who-can-apply slice I read (its proof atoms cite only the 35-hour and age-16 excerpts) — that is a possible post-fix grounding gap, not evidence about the pre-fix defect.

verdict.justification: The pinned-release text of the cited provision (uk/guidance/govuk/carers-allowance/eligibility) states "All of the following must apply: You're 16 or over. You're not in full-time education. ... item.subject: Fix student loan source grounding

triage.commit_summary: The commit re-grounded the GOV.UK student-loan-repayments module's provenance: it repointed the module-level and every proof-atom `corpus_citation_path` from the non-resolving `uk/guidance/govuk/student-loan-repayments` to the real corpus provision `uk/guidance/govuk/student-loan-repayments/what-you-pay`, and rewrote six proof-atom excerpts from paraphrased ASCII ("Plan 1, GBP 26900") to the source's verbatim wording ("Plan 1, £26,900"), with the corpus toolchain pin bumped to the release that carries that provision. No encoded meaning changed: all thresholds (26900 / 29385 / 33795 / 25000 / 21000), the 9% and 6% rates, plan selection, effective dates, inputs and outputs are byte-identical before and after; the only side changes are the encoding manifest, the toolchain corpus ref, and one added test assertion.

modules.description_quote: Fix student loan source grounding
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module's provenance was wrong, not its meaning: every proof atom cited `uk/guidance/govuk/student-loan-repayments`, a path that resolves to no active corpus source in any release, and six excerpts were ASCII paraphrases ("Plan 1, GBP 26900") that do not appear verbatim in the cited GOV.UK text, while the encoded thresholds, rates and formulas already matched the source.
modules.triage_notes: Single-module commit. I diffed the parent and commit versions of the whole file and classified every changed line by YAML key: 28 `corpus_citation_path` lines (14 pairs) and 12 `excerpt` lines (6 pairs), and nothing else — file length is 304 lines both before and after, and formulas, parameters, `effective_from` dates, dtypes, periods, units, inputs and outputs are byte-identical. That is squarely the task's mechanical rule: proof-atom excerpt/citation-path strings only, so provenance, not fidelity. Provision WAS read via resolve_provision.py: `uk/guidance/govuk/student-loan-repayments/what-you-pay` resolves (release uk-rulespec-2026-07-12, record 9227075c-eb47-51fa-8288-4be864a0cace) and its text contains verbatim "The yearly income thresholds are: Plan 1, £26,900; Plan 2, £29,385; Plan 4, £33,795; Plan 5, £25,000; Postgraduate Loan, £21,000." plus the 9%/6% sentences, confirming the post-fix excerpts are exact quotes and the pre-fix numbers were already correct. I also tried resolving the pre-fix path `uk/guidance/govuk/student-loan-repayments`: it errors with "No active corpus source found" in every release tried, so the old citation was dangling. Tempting near-miss for `untraceable_branch` given the subject line "Fix student loan source grounding" and the dangling path, but no formula was re-grounded onto different substance — the numbers and logic never moved — so the explicit "citation-string-only corrections are mechanical" instruction governs. Side files (not modules): `.axiom/toolchain.toml` bumped `axiom_corpus_ref` 96bc4867 -> e5f07c38 (the corpus PR that added the /what-you-pay provision; note that ref is not present in the local corpus checkout, so the resolver fell back to the earliest release after it), `.axiom/encoding-manifests/policies/govuk/student-loan-repayments.json` re-signed (8 lines), and the companion test gained one assertion line `student_loan_annual_income_threshold: 0` for the no-listed-plan case — added coverage, not a meaning change. PR #28 had no reviews, review comments, or issue comments, and the commit body is empty, so the subject line is the only quotable text. If a reviewer wants this commit in the corpus as a provenance-repair negative example, it is a clean one; it should not be scored as a fidelity defect.

triage.commit_summary: The commit re-emits all 100 generated us-tariff-schedule composition modules so the Brazil IEEPA carve-out is gated on the membership-semantic caller input `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` instead of the witness composition's per-line exemplar flag `entry_is_line_b`, and re-grounds the Section 232 steel rate parameter's proof from the stale HTS 9903.81.87/.88 headings to the consolidated 9903.82.02 heading (rate value 0.50 unchanged). It also adds the B1.6-C certification evidence (`.b16-evidence/`, B16-C-REPORT.md, B16-C-LOG.md) and the one-line generator change that produced the new steel citation, because the generated artifacts committed in the parent were still carrying the exemplar-flag gate that the generator's replacement table already specified.

modules.description_quote: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The Brazil IEEPA exception was conditioned on the witness's exemplar line identity `entry_is_line_b`, a flag with no basis in the cited HTS text, so at schedule scale the 40% Brazil surcharge was added to Section 232 aluminum entries that the module's own cited exception ('The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02.') exempts.
modules.triage_notes: Two distinct change classes in one diff, identical in all 12 modules of this chunk (and, per the PR, all 100 generated modules). (1) Brazil gate `not entry_is_line_b` -> `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` in rules ieepa_component_rate and ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions (both versions[0].formula, from 2026-02-15); this is the fidelity change, since entry_is_line_b remains a live input elsewhere in the module (it is still the formula of entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded), so this is a substitution of one input for another, not a rename. (2) Steel parameter proof re-grounding 9903.81.87/.88 -> 9903.82.02 plus the rule-level `source:` string; the rate stays '0.50', so on its own that part is provenance/mechanical. Provisions read through the pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap): us/statute/hts/9903.81.87 is UNRESOLVED in this vintage, confirming the report line 'The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage'; 9903.82.02 resolves with the exact excerpt 'Rates of duty (1-General): The duty provided in the applicable subheading + 50%'. 9903.01.77 resolves as the Brazil +40% heading with exclusions in 9903.01.78-9903.01.83, and 9903.01.83 covers 'Articles of iron or steel; derivative articles of iron or steel; articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum; wood products; passenger vehicles ...' -- so a residual gap remains post-fix: the gate excludes only aluminum, not the steel/wood/vehicle classes the exclusion heading also names (the module's own cited excerpt is aluminum-specific, so this is arguably out of scope for this fix). Alternative kind: wrong_entity_or_scope (the carve-out population was one exemplar line rather than the aluminum-covered article class); I chose untraceable_branch because the fix re-grounds a condition that had no source basis. These are generated modules with module.kind: composition emitted by tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py, whose COMPONENT_FORMULA_REPLACEMENTS table already contained the ieepa substitution at the parent a9562cfd4 -- the parent's committed artifacts were stale relative to the generator. Commit message is bare ('b1.6: certify generalized component gates'); evidence comes from the PR body and .b16-evidence/c-structural-note.md ('Direct component-formula exemplar references are gone except the intentionally retained beer/section-338 `entry_is_line_d` slots.'). Follow-up commit a14f43975 ('b1.6: repair the steel proof chain per review finding') unwrapped the double-nested metadata.proof.proof on section_232_steel_component_rate and added us/statute/hts/9903.82.02 to module.source_verification.corpus_citation_paths, neither of which is present at this commit, so the steel proof here was not yet containment-gate visible.

verdict.justification: I tried three refutations and all fail. The diff is not provenance-only: alongside the steel-parameter re-grounding (9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02, where the formula stays '0.50', i.e. genuinely mechanical), two formula lines change the IEEPA gate condition from `not entry_is_line_b` to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, which is encoded meaning. It is also not "new scope the module never claimed": the pre-fix `ieepa_component_rate` rule carries its own proof atom `kind: exception` citing "The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02.", and the pre-fix module summary already asserts that "section-232 aluminum ... identifiers are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation" — so the gate keyed on the five-line witness's exemplar identity `entry_is_line_b` contradicted both the cited source and the module's own declared surface. The resolver confirms 9903.01.77 is the Brazil IEEPA "+ 40%" heading whose exceptions are defined by product headings (9903.01.78–.83, .90), never by a line identity, so the old condition had no basis in the cited text and the fix re-grounds it — untraceable_branch, not polarity (the negation is preserved) and not wrong_entity_or_scope (entity, geography and rate are unchanged).

Only the two IEEPA gate lines carry the fidelity finding, so if the corpus keys the case on rule_names it should key on rules[ieepa_component_rate] / [ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions], not on the steel rules.

Duplicate-coverage risk for the reviewer: the generator already contained the substitution pair `"ieepa_component_rate": (("not entry_is_line_b", "not entry_is_section_232_aluminum"),)` at the PARENT commit a9562cfd ("b1.6: generalize generated component surfaces"); only the emitted YAML lagged, and this commit regenerates. `git -C rulespec-us show a9562cfd -- tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py` shows it. If a9562cfd (or 2a6bdb01d) is also screened into the corpus, the same underlying defect may appear twice — this commit is the emission, that one is the intent.

Not intra-PR scaffolding: the generated file was first added in aa44a141b ("Generated tariff-schedule compositions, batch 1 of the B1.3 series"), which is an ancestor of origin/main, so the exemplar-flag gate shipped at schedule scale before PR #1300.

Two caveats on the first reader's stated consequence, neither changing the verdict: (1) the "40% added to aluminum entries" incidence claim depends on `entry_is_line_b` evaluating FALSE for real aluminum lines at schedule scale — the natural reading of a caller-supplied exemplar flag, but I did not execute the module to confirm; (2) the affected version window is narrow — the branch runs `from: '2026-02-15'` and is superseded at `from: '2026-02-20'` by `terminated_ieepa_additional_ad_valorem_duty_rate`, so the mis-grounded gate is live for roughly five days of encoded time. Also note the new gate is a close but not exact match to the source: `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` covers the module's whole §232 aluminum membership (9903.85.08 content-basis, 9903.85.67 Russia, etc.) while the cited carve-out names products "provided for in heading 9903.85.02" — an approximation in the right direction, not a reason to reject.

Corpus-vintage note: resolving us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219 through the pinned release returns a Rev. 3 note page (a subheading list), not the aluminum carve-out sentence — page numbering differs from the Rev. 15 vintage the module is grounded on, so the excerpt is not independently verifiable through the pinned resolver. 9903.01.77 itself resolves and confirms Brazil +40% with heading-defined exceptions.

verdict.justification: The refutation attempts fail: the diff changes a formula condition in two rules (ieepa_component_rate and ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions), so it is not mechanical, and the file is a rulespec/v1 module with rules, formulas and proof atoms, so it is not a non-module. (g)", so the source class is aluminum membership, exactly what the fix substitutes using the module's already-present `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` input. That is a condition with no grounding in the cited provision being re-grounded, which is untraceable_branch rather than a missing clause (the clause was present but wrongly grounded) or a mere scope tweak. The steel half of the diff (9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02) is citation/excerpt-only with the rate unchanged at '0.50', i.e. mechanical provenance, but it does not displace the substantive Brazil-gate change.

verdict.notes: Caveats a reviewer should weigh. (1) Numerically inert in this module: ch02 is meat and edible meat offal, so for any real ch02 line both `entry_is_line_b` (the witness's 7601.10.30.00 aluminum exemplar) and `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` are false; the defect is in encoded meaning and in the generated template shared across ~100 chapters, not in ch02's computed rate. (2) Intra-PR self-repair: the parent a9562cfd ("b1.6: generalize generated component surfaces") is the immediately preceding commit on PR #1300's own branch, so the wrong gate never reached main — it is the generalization pass missing one gate, which this "certify" commit closes. Supporting evidence that it is a genuine miss rather than a design choice: the module summary is byte-identical in pre and post and already states that section-232 aluminum identifiers "are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation" and that only "Beer/section-338 keeps entry_is_line_d because no membership module exists" — the pre file contradicted its own contract. (3) Residual, worth flagging separately: `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` still has `formula: entry_is_line_b` post-fix (line 1925) with a 9903.01.33 "articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum" atom, so the same exemplar coupling survives in that rule. (4) Source verification limit: the pinned corpus is 2026 Rev 3 (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap) while the module claims Rev 15 vintage, so `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219` resolves to an unrelated derivative-list page and the quoted aluminum carve-out sentence could not be re-read at that locator; 9903.01.77 and 9903.85.02 resolve cleanly and corroborate the semantics. (5) A defensible alternative kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (exception scoped to one exemplar line instead of the aluminum class); untraceable_branch is preferred because the pre condition is a scaffold identity with no source basis at all and the fix re-grounds it.

verdict.justification: The ch03 diff changes encoded meaning in exactly the way described: in both `ieepa_component_rate` and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions`, the Brazil IEEPA carve-out flips from the witness's exemplar-line flag `entry_is_line_b` to the membership predicate `entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, while the rule's own (unchanged) exception proof atom cites "The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02." I verified against the pinned corpus that 9903.01.77 is the Brazil +40% IEEPA heading and 9903.85.02 is the §232 aluminum heading (note 19(g) aluminum products), so the source criterion is aluminum membership, not a single line; `entry_is_line_b` is the witness's aluminum exemplar HTS 7601.10.30.00 (`entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` has `formula: entry_is_line_b`), a fixture identifier with no basis in the cited text, and the fix re-grounds it — the textbook untraceable_branch, not merely a scope widening, since the clause was already encoded and only its grounding was wrong. The rest of the diff (steel `source:` string and 9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02 proof atoms, formula still '0.50') is provenance-only and mechanical, so the fidelity finding rests solely on the gate lines, which is where the reader anchored it.

verdict.notes: Refutations tried and rejected: (1) "mechanical" fails — the steel half of the diff is citation/excerpt-only, but two formula gates changed; (2) "not_a_defect / new scope never claimed" fails — the parent module already declares chapter-scale coverage and says "Membership-semantic ... section-232 aluminum/steel ... are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation", and `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` already existed as an input in the parent (used by the §232 aluminum component at pre-file lines 2744/2751), so the Brazil gate was a straggler inconsistent with both the module's own prose and its cited exception; (3) "tolerated placeholder" (cf. the deliberately retained beer/§338 `entry_is_line_d`, kept only "because no membership module exists") fails for the same reason — the aluminum membership input did exist. Residual doubt driving confidence below 0.9: this is an in-branch repair of the immediately preceding commit a9562cfd on PR #1300 rather than a fix to long-lived shipped content, and the commit subject ("b1.6: certify generalized component gates") never names the Brazil gate; the PR body explicitly calls only the §122 exemplar coupling "unlawfully suppressed". Also worth flagging for the reviewer: chapter 3 is fish/crustaceans, so no real ch03 line is §232 aluminum — the runtime bite of this identical generated edit lives in metal chapters (ch76 etc.), and all 100 generated chapter modules carry the same two lines, so this commit will present as ~100 near-identical candidates. Competing kind considered: wrong_entity_or_scope (the carve-out reached the wrong population); I rejected it because the entity (CustomsEntry) is unchanged and the rubric's untraceable_branch explicitly covers a condition "re-grounded" off a basis absent from the source.

Two residual issues for a reviewer, neither changing this verdict: (1) the post-fix gate excludes only 232 aluminum, while 9903.01.77's exclusion set (9903.01.78-.83 and .90) also covers steel, wood, vehicles, semiconductors, copper and civil aircraft — a residual unrepresented_clause in the encoding after this fix; (2) the exclusion proof atom cites us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219, which in the resolver's corpus vintage returns a page of derivative-article HTS numbers, not the quoted exclusion sentence — the page locator looks vintage-stale even though the substance is confirmed via 9903.01.77/.83 and 9903.85.02.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as a mere input-surface generalization and could not: the diff changes the operative gate of `ieepa_component_rate` and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions` from `not entry_is_line_b` — the witness harness's identity flag for the single exemplar line 7601.10.30.00, a caller input with no definition or meaning inside a generated chapter-27 module — to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, a membership predicate. Read through the pinned release, HTS 9903.01.77 states "Except for products described in headings 9903.01.78-9903.01.83 and 9903.01.90, articles the product of Brazil…", and 9903.01.83 carves out "Articles of iron or steel; derivative articles of iron or steel; articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum…", i.e. a class membership, never a per-line identity; the module's own proof atom for this rule is a `kind: exception` atom quoting that the 9903.01.77 duties "shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02". So the pre-fix condition had no basis in the cited source and the fix re-grounds it on the class the source actually uses — untraceable_branch, not amount, boundary, polarity, or a missing clause. The other half of the diff (steel citation 9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02) is provenance-only and does not carry the verdict.

verdict.notes: (1) The first reader's quote is the PR body's lede and describes PR #1300 as a whole, most of which landed in the PARENT commit a9562cfd ("b1.6: generalize generated component surfaces") — that commit already swapped entry_is_line_b → entry_is_section_232_aluminum in section_232_aluminum_component_rate and added the steel component with the 9903.81.87/.88 citations. This commit is the leftover: the generator's substitution map (tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py lines 99-100) already contained the ieepa_component_rate entries at the parent, but the parent's emitted YAML was stale for those two rules; the certify re-emit applied them. A commit-scoped quote is the diff line, not the PR lede. (2) The steel hunks (source string + proof-atom corpus_citation_path/excerpt 9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02, two atoms collapsed to one) are mechanical provenance: `formula: '0.50'` is byte-identical, and B16-C-REPORT.md says "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage: Rev. 15 contains no operative 9903.81.x row and consolidates the charge at 9903.82.02." If this case is later split per-hunk, that half is mechanical. (3) Residual issues a reviewer may want: the post-fix predicate is still under-inclusive versus 9903.01.83, which also excludes iron/steel and derivatives, wood products, vehicles and parts, semiconductor articles and copper — only aluminum is gated; and `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` still carries `formula: entry_is_line_b` in the post file (line 1924), a surviving exemplar coupling under a rule sourced to "HTS 9903.01.33 section 232 metals article scope". (4) Runtime impact within ch27 itself is probably nil (mineral fuels; no §232 aluminum lines, and entry_is_line_b would default false), so the correction is to encoded meaning rather than to any ch27 number — this is the main reason I held confidence at 0.75 rather than higher; the same generated formula in ch76 is where the carve-out would actually misfire. (5) The module's proof-atom excerpt is cited to us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219, which in the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, HTS 2026 Rev 3 notes) resolves to a list of derivative HTS numbers, not that sentence — page numbering differs from the Rev. 15 vintage the module claims. The substance is independently confirmed by 9903.01.77 and 9903.01.83 themselves, but the page-level locator does not verify.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as a mere generalization/refactor and could not: the module's own proof atom for `ieepa_component_rate` cites the Brazil IEEPA exclusion ("The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02."), and the pinned corpus confirms 9903.01.77 excepts "products described in headings 9903.01.78-9903.01.83", with 9903.01.83 reading "articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum; ..." — a class/heading membership, never a single line. 1. I verified the substance directly from 9903.01.77 and 9903.01.83 instead.
3. The first reader's justification names 9903.01.83 as "the source's excluded heading" while the module's atom cites 9903.85.02; both are consistent (9903.01.83 is the Brazil-side exception heading, 9903.85.02 the §232 aluminum heading it points into), so the reader's reading survives despite the mismatched citation.

If the corpus policy is "no meaning change without a runtime delta in this module", that is the one lever that would push this to unclear.

triage.commit_summary: The commit re-emits all 100 generated chapter compositions so the Brazil IEEPA carve-out stops keying on the hand-built witness's exemplar flag `entry_is_line_b` and keys on the membership-semantic caller input `entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, and re-grounds the Section 232 steel rate parameter's source string and proof atoms from the stale locators 9903.81.87/.88 to the consolidated HTS 9903.82.02 (the 0.50 rate itself is unchanged). It also lands the B1.6-C certification evidence (`.b16-evidence/`, B16-C-REPORT.md, B16-C-LOG.md) for determinism, witness-slice equivalence, certified oracle replay and validate, plus the one four-line generator change in `tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py` that produced the steel re-grounding.

modules.description_quote: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The Brazil IEEPA exception was gated on `not entry_is_line_b`, a positional flag for the witness's single aluminum exemplar line that the cited source never mentions, instead of the aluminum-article membership the heading 9903.01.77 carve-out actually names, so the surcharge was suppressed for one exemplar line rather than for §232 aluminum articles.
modules.triage_notes: Two changes per module. (a) Formula: the Brazil term in `ieepa_component_rate` and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions` (both versions[0].formula) goes from `not entry_is_line_b` to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` — this is what drives the classification. (b) Provenance only: the steel parameter's `source:` string and the proof atoms of `ch49_s232_steel_heading_rate` / `section_232_steel_component_rate` are re-grounded from us/statute/hts/9903.81.87 + .88 to us/statute/hts/9903.82.02; the excerpt text and the '0.50' formula are unchanged, so that half is mechanical on its own. Provisions read through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, HTS 2026 Rev. 3 vintage): 9903.81.87 fails to resolve (resolver exit 1), confirming B16-C-REPORT.md's line "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage"; 9903.82.02 resolves as "articles of aluminum, of steel or of copper and derivative aluminum or steel articles ... Rates of duty (1-General): The duty provided in the applicable subheading + 50%", matching the 0.50 rate. 9903.01.77 (Brazil, +40%) excepts headings 9903.01.78-9903.01.83 and 9903.01.90, and 9903.01.83 covers iron/steel, aluminum, wood products and vehicles — so the post-fix aluminum-only gate is still narrower than the full source exception (it matches the module's own unchanged proof atom, "The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02."); that residual is not the defect fixed here. These are generator-emitted compositions (hand edits prohibited): the parent commit a9562cfd4 already carried the ieepa entry in COMPONENT_FORMULA_REPLACEMENTS but shipped stale module bytes, and this commit's generator diff touches only steel_parameter_rule, so the module change is a re-emission that brings the bytes to the intended grounding. Alternative kind reading: wrong_entity_or_scope (exclusion scoped to one exemplar line instead of the aluminum class). Follow-up noted: the steel atoms here sit under a non-canonical `metadata.proof.proof.atoms` key in section_232_steel_component_rate, which a later PR #1300 review flagged and a subsequent commit repaired (see the PR issue comment).

verdict.justification: The refutation attempt fails on the meaning-bearing half of the diff: both IEEPA component formulas in this generated chapter-49 composition gated the Brazil 9903.01.77 carve-out on `not entry_is_line_b`, and the branch's own proof atom in the pre file cites a membership proposition ("The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02"), while the commit's own `flag-action-map.md` states "`entry_is_line_b` — HTS 7601.10.30.00", i.e. the condition was the identity of one witness exemplar line, a concept the source never states. Resolving the source through the pinned release confirms the carve-out is by article class (9903.01.83: "Articles of iron or steel; derivative articles of iron or steel; articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum; ..."), so the fix re-grounds a source-less condition onto the membership the provision names — untraceable_branch, not amount, boundary, polarity, or a missing clause. The pre-fix state was merged content on main (the generated module came from 1bc7292f, "Generated tariff-schedule compositions, batch 2"), not an intra-PR staging artifact, so "enhancement the module never claimed" does not hold; the module always claimed to encode this exception. The steel half of the diff (9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02, rate unchanged at 0.50) is mechanical provenance only, so the first reader's PR-body quote is not the decisive evidence — the Brazil gate line is.

verdict.notes: Strongest surviving counter-arguments, for the reviewer: (1) For chapter 49 specifically the change is output-neutral — no printed-matter line is either the 7601.10.30.00 exemplar or a §232 aluminum article, so the Brazil surcharge applies either way; what is corrected is the encoded condition and the caller input contract, not a computed duty for this chapter. (2) The PR frames it as decoupling, and the generator applies it as a blind substring substitution across 100 chapters ("Exact witness substrings: every other gate and effective window is preserved" in tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py), with certified witness-slice equivalence under the input mapping — so this is a generated-artifact regeneration, not a targeted repair on ch49. I still call it fidelity because the pre-fix encoded condition disagreed with the cited source and the module already used the correct membership flag `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` for its own §232 aluminum component (pre lines 2744/2751) while using the positional flag for this carve-out. Two caveats: the fix is partial — 9903.01.83 also carves out steel, wood, vehicles, semiconductors and copper, and the post formula still excludes only aluminum; and `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` still reads `formula: entry_is_line_b` at post line 1924, so an exemplar-flag gate remains in the same file. If a reviewer prefers a scope framing (exception applied to one exemplar line instead of the aluminum-article population), wrong_entity_or_scope is the runner-up kind; untraceable_branch fits better because the fix re-grounds a condition that had no counterpart in the source at all. verdict.notes: Four things a reviewer should weigh. I checked the pinned corpus: 9903.81.87 and 9903.81.88 have no rate rows in 2026-08-03-rulespec-hts-current-with-legacy-aluminum.jsonl while 9903.82.02 does, carrying exactly "Rates of duty (1-General): The duty provided in the applicable subheading + 50%", so the report's "the task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage" holds and this is provenance, not fidelity. (2) Strongest argument against confirming: in chapter 50 (silk) both predicates are extensionally empty — no silk line is the witness's line b (7601.10.30.00, ch76) and none is §232 aluminum — so no ch50 output value changes; the correction is textual/structural here and materially behavioral only in metals chapters. (3) Alternate kind: wrong_entity_or_scope is arguable (the carve-out covered the wrong population), but untraceable_branch is tighter — the predicate itself was a witness artifact re-grounded on the heading the source names. Note also that `entry_is_line_b` survives post-fix as the body of `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` (line 1925), so the exemplar-flag problem is only partly swept — a related, still-open issue, not part of this diff.

I resolved the provisions through the pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap): 9903.01.77 is the Brazil IEEPA +40% heading and 9903.85.02 is "products of aluminum provided for in the tariff headings or subheadings enumerated in subdivision (g) of note 19" +50%, so `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` is the source-grounded operand and `entry_is_line_b` is not. Alternative kind worth a reviewer's eye: wrong_entity_or_scope (the carve-out covered one exemplar line rather than the whole 9903.85.02 aluminum population); I chose untraceable_branch because the discarded operand itself has no source referent. (2) Mechanical (provenance) half of the same diff: `ch61_s232_steel_heading_rate`'s `source:` string and its two proof atoms (us/statute/hts/9903.81.87 and .88) collapse to one atom on us/statute/hts/9903.82.02, with the excerpt and the value '0.50' unchanged; `section_232_steel_component_rate`'s nested atom changes the same way. I confirmed 9903.81.87/.88 do not resolve in the pinned corpus while 9903.82.02 does ("articles of aluminum, of steel or of copper and derivative aluminum or steel articles ... note 16 (c)(i)-(v)", + 50%), matching the in-commit report line "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage". Caveats: the generator diff in this commit (tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py) only changes the steel heading tuple — the ieepa exemplar-flag mapping already existed at the parent a9562cfd, so the parent's committed YAML was stale relative to its own generator and this certify commit is where the corrected bytes actually land. `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` is still defined as `entry_is_line_b` in both pre and post, i.e. not every exemplar proxy was removed. modules.triage_notes: Two distinct changes in this module diff. (1) SUBSTANTIVE: in both `ieepa_component_rate` (versions[0].formula, effective_from 2026-02-15) and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions`, `+ (if origin_is_brazil and not entry_is_line_b: brazil_ieepa_additional_duty_rate else: 0)` becomes `... and not entry_is_section_232_aluminum ...`. The unchanged proof atom on that formula is `corpus_citation_path: us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219`, `kind: exception`, excerpt 'The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02.' I read the corpus through resolve_provision.py: 9903.01.77 is the Brazil +40% IEEPA heading, 'Except for products described in headings 9903.01.78-9903.01.83 and 9903.01.90'; 9903.01.83 is the class-wide carve-out 'Articles of iron or steel; derivative articles of iron or steel; articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum; ...'; 9903.85.02 is 'products of aluminum provided for in the tariff headings or subheadings enumerated in subdivision (g) of note 19'. So the exception is defined by article class, not by one exemplar entry - the pre-fix condition is ungrounded and the fix re-grounds it. Kind is genuinely between untraceable_branch (condition with no source basis, re-grounded - matches the taxonomy's 'the fix removes or re-grounds it' and the PR's 'move from ... exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs') and wrong_entity_or_scope (the carve-out covers the wrong set of entries); I chose untraceable_branch, a reviewer may prefer the other. NOTE the post-fix gate excepts only aluminum, while 9903.01.83 also lists iron/steel and several other classes - a residual under-representation this commit does not address. (2) MECHANICAL: `ch98_s232_steel_heading_rate` and `section_232_steel_component_rate` only change the `source:` string and the proof atoms' corpus_citation_path from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02; I compared parent and commit text - the rate stays '0.50', effective_from stays 2026-02-15, and the component formula is byte-identical. Provenance only, and it is corroborated: `us/statute/hts/9903.81.87` does not resolve in the pinned corpus at all (empty result) while `us/statute/hts/9903.82.02` resolves with exactly the recorded excerpt 'Rates of duty (1-General): The duty provided in the applicable subheading + 50%'. Classification for the module is driven by (1). Provenance/mechanism caveat for the corpus builder: these are generator-emitted `module.kind: composition` files - all 100 module diffs in this commit carry the identical pair of changes, and tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py at the PARENT commit already contained `"ieepa_component_rate": (("not entry_is_line_b", "not entry_is_section_232_aluminum"),)`, so the parent's committed YAML lagged its own generator and this commit is a regeneration sweep; only the steel citation was a fresh generator edit here. The committed pre-fix module content was still wrong against the source, so it is a usable fidelity item, but 100 near-identical copies should be deduped before benchmarking.

(2) The source text could not be independently verified through the pinned release: `resolve_provision.py --rulespec-commit a9562cfd44` selects release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap (HTS 2026 Rev. 3 notes), where chapter-99/page-221 resolves to note subdivisions (x)-(z) on heading 9903.01.77 and page-230 to §232 steel quota notes — neither contains the §122 (aa)(ii) text or the 9903.82.02/.04 excerpt the atoms quote (page drift across revisions). verdict.justification: The change is a genuine fidelity correction — the §122 surcharge version in force 2026-02-24 to 2026-07-23 is re-gated, and the PR states the old coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins" — so "not_a_defect"/"mechanical" are refuted. But the kind is mis-labeled: entity (CustomsEntry), period, origin tests and output surface are identical pre and post; what was wrong is that the §122 exemption branch was keyed to predicates carrying a different provision's meaning. The same module defines `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_a` and `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_b` (post lines 1907/1924, unchanged), while §122's own proof atoms cite entirely different exceptions (the "exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03" and "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper ... provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04"), and entry_is_line_a simultaneously gated `list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate` for China-301. That is a branch grounded on the wrong provision, which the fix re-grounds — the untraceable_branch definition — rather than a wrong entity, population or scope.

Evidence trail: diff /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/diffs/us/a9562cfd44/002.diff; pre/post windows saved at .../scratchpad/pre_ch03.yaml and post_ch03.yaml.

Why untraceable_branch over wrong_entity_or_scope: the decisive defect is flag conflation, not mis-targeting. Pre-fix, one caller input carried three unrelated statutory meanings — entry_is_line_a was the reciprocal-annex exclusion flag (9903.01.32), the China-301 list-1 gate, and a §122 exemption trigger; entry_is_line_b was the reciprocal-metals flag (9903.01.33, aluminum only), the China-301 2024-action gate, the §232-aluminum gate and the second §122 exemption trigger. Outside the five witness exemplar lines no consistent assignment exists, so the generated chapter-wide module encoded a §122 exemption the cited provision does not state. Note also that pre-fix §122 keyed the metals exemption to an aluminum-only flag while its atom cites aluminum, steel and copper — a secondary under-representation of the same exception.

The commit bundles three different things; only the first is the defect the classification rests on:
1. Re-grounding of §122, §232-aluminum, §201 and the four China-301 slots onto membership-semantic inputs (the defect; untraceable_branch).
2. Brazil/forced-labor: pre-fix `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0 elif origin_is_brazil: ...` becomes `if entry_is_brazil_301_listed and origin_is_brazil: ...`. This removes an ungrounded suppression but converts an exclusion-structured rule into an inclusion-list rule, and the module's own summary says these inputs "currently default to the declared-boolean FALSE pattern because entry preparation cannot yet populate those lists" — so the component is effectively zero everywhere post-fix, while the Brazil atoms cite 9903.05.01 "articles the product of Brazil" with named exclusions. A reviewer may want to treat this half as a separate, opposite-direction item (possible fail-closed regression) rather than part of the same finding; the PR excuses it as outside the April-June evaluation window.
3. The brand-new `section_232_steel_component_rate` + `ch03_s232_steel_heading_rate` and the new `+ section_232_steel_component_rate` stack term. The PR frames this as coverage "the witness never had" and the module previously claimed only the witness's component set, so per the task rule this is added coverage, not a defect.

Provenance caveats for the reviewer (not part of the verdict): the new steel rule is emitted with a double-nested `metadata: proof: proof: atoms:`, which the PR's own issue comment confirms was repaired later ("steel atoms unwrapped to canonical `metadata.proof.atoms`"); the PR body says the steel rate is "grounded on the consolidated HTS 9903.82.02 provision" while the atoms cite 9903.81.87/.88; and under the pinned corpus (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, Rev 3 notes) `us/statute/hts/9903.81.87` does not resolve at all and `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-221` returns IEEPA reciprocal notes containing neither "9903.03.03" nor "surcharge", so the §122 exception excerpts could not be verified against source at their cited paths (those atoms are unchanged by this commit, so the mismatch predates it).

verdict.justification: The §122 version[1] formula changes its exemption gate from `entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b` to `entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered`, while the rule's proof atoms are untouched — so the source ground is constant and only the population the exemption covers changed, which is scope, not groundedness. The cited proclamation (resolved through the pinned release) defines that population as "articles listed in paragraph 2 of Annex I ... and as enumerated in Annex II" plus "shall not apply in addition to tariffs imposed under section 232"; the pre-fix gate instead used the module's own exemplar flags, which the same file reads as reciprocal-annex/China-301-list-1 membership (`entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_a`, and `if entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate`) and as aluminum-only metals membership (`entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_b`). That is both over-inclusive (any §301-list line exempted, for every origin) and under-inclusive (§232 steel/copper articles not exempted), exactly the "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins" the PR body describes. It is not a rename or mechanical churn: entry_is_line_a/b survive post-fix as separate live inputs, so the §122 gate now takes genuinely different caller inputs, and the PR reports 18 witness-slice cells changing value.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as a rename or a generator-level refactor and could not: `entry_is_line_a` maps to two different semantic inputs in two different rules (`entry_is_section_122_exempt` in §122, `entry_is_china_301_list123` in §301), so it is a semantic split of an overloaded proxy flag, not a one-to-one rename, and encoded outputs change (the PR enumerates 18 witness-slice cells that changed because "the witness's own coupling was the unlawful part"). The rule's own proof atoms are byte-identical pre and post and already ground versions[1] on "subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03" plus "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04" — so the encoding claimed one exemption scope and implemented a different predicate. Reading the cited provision through the pinned release (Proclamation 11012, FR 2026-03824 ¶14) confirms the surcharge "shall not apply to the following products, as further detailed in Annexes I and II", items (a)–(m) including (k) articles "subject to additional import restrictions imposed pursuant to section 232" — nothing in the source makes §301 list membership or a specific exemplar HTS row the exemption trigger. That is a branch condition with no basis in the cited source which the fix re-grounds, i.e. untraceable_branch, not unrepresented_clause (the exemption branch already existed) and not wrong_entity_or_scope (entity, period, dtype and output surface are unchanged).

Bundle: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/inputs/us/a9562cfd44.json; diff: .../scratchpad/diffs/us/a9562cfd44/012.diff.

One caveat a reviewer should see: the first reader's stated mechanism ("zeroed the surcharge for every China-301-listed line regardless of origin") matches the PR body and the pre-fix module summary ("entry_is_line_a ... are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification"), but the shipped parent-commit entry-prep tool populates those flags as literal exemplar rows: `git -C /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us show 29dbbdac05:tools/b16_entry_flags.py` has `WITNESS_LINES = {"entry_is_line_a": "7202111000", "entry_is_line_b": "7601103000", ...}` and `result = {name: hts == digits for name, digits in WITNESS_LINES.items()}`. Under that literal wiring the ch13 defect is the mirror image — neither witness row occurs in chapter 13, so the §122 exemption never fired there and every Annex I/II and §232-covered ch13 line was charged the full 10%. Either wiring makes the pre-fix condition an ungrounded proxy for the proclamation's stated exclusion scope, so the kind is unchanged, but the reader's specific over-suppression narrative is the PR's account, not something I could reproduce from the parent-commit tool.

The diff is multi-defect and the reader picked the strongest anchor. Two other rules in the same file carry a different kind: `brazil_section_301_component_rate` and `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate` previously applied their rates to every entry of the listed origins with no listedness gate (`elif origin_is_brazil: brazil_section_301_additional_duty_rate`), and the fix adds `entry_is_brazil_301_listed and` / `entry_is_forced_labor_301_listed and` — that slice reads as unrepresented_clause. The new `section_232_steel_component_rate` + `ch13_s232_steel_heading_rate` and the extra `+ section_232_steel_component_rate` term in `schedule_statutory_stack` are new coverage the module never claimed (PR: "a Section 232 steel component the witness never had"), so they are an enhancement, not a defect, and should not be counted as a second finding. item.subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 generalize (PR #1300): decouples component gates from exemplar flags; PR body says the witness's exemplar coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins" — logic/scope correction to 100 merged generated modules.
item.screen_reason: b1.6 generalize (PR #1300): decouples component gates from exemplar flags; PR body says the witness's exemplar coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins" — logic/scope correction to 100 merged generated modules.

triage.commit_summary: The commit regenerates 100 merged tariff-schedule composition modules with generator b1.6-schedule-compositions-3, replacing the hand-built witness's five exemplar flags (entry_is_line_a..e) that gated the authority components with membership-semantic caller inputs (entry_is_section_122_exempt, entry_is_section_232_covered, entry_is_section_232_aluminum/steel, entry_is_china_301_list123/list4a/2024_action/solar, entry_is_section_201_cspv, entry_is_brazil_301_listed, entry_is_forced_labor_301_listed). The stated reason is that the exemplar coupling generalized incorrectly to whole chapters - most concretely the section 122 temporary import surcharge was zeroed for any China-301 list member or aluminum member line for all origins, which the source's exemption (the 9903.03.03 exclusion list plus section 232-covered metals) does not support - and the same regeneration adds a new section_232_steel_component_rate (+50%) into the statutory stack that the witness never had.

modules.description_quote: the witness's exemplar coupling, which round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix section 122 surcharge returned 0 whenever the entry carried exemplar flags entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b - which at chapter scale mean China-301 list-1 membership and section-232-aluminum membership - while the cited source exempts only the 9903.03.03 subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion-list articles and section-232-covered aluminum/steel/copper articles, so the 10 percent surcharge was suppressed on every 301-listed line of every origin.
modules.triage_notes: Generated composition module (module.kind: composition, 'hand edits prohibited'); the fix is a regeneration, and the identical hunk shape lands in all 100 chapter files, so this is one defect replicated 100x rather than 100 independent encodings - a benchmark builder should probably keep only a few. Verified in pre/post files: rules[section_122_component_rate].versions[1] (from 2026-02-24, effective_to 2026-07-23) goes from 'if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0' to 'if entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered: 0'; that rule's own proof atoms cite the 9903.03.03 exclusion list and 'articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04' as the exceptions, confirming the exemption is list/metal based, not 301 based. Kind could also be argued untraceable_branch (the exemplar flags have no source basis and the fix re-grounds them); I chose wrong_entity_or_scope because the PR frames the harm as the wrong population (301-member lines) being exempted. Same commit also re-grounds section_201_component_rate (line_e -> entry_is_section_201_cspv; both branches return 0, no runtime change), section_232_aluminum_component_rate (line_b -> entry_is_section_232_aluminum), china_section_301_component_rate (line_a/b/c/e -> list123/2024_action/list4a/solar, line_d retained), brazil_section_301_component_rate and forced_labor_section_301_component_rate (drops the line_a/line_b zero-gate, adds a listed-membership conjunct), and ADDS section_232_steel_component_rate + ch25_s232_steel_heading_rate (0.50) to schedule_statutory_stack - arguably a separate unrepresented_clause correction but also new scope the pilot surface never claimed, so not made the primary kind. Caveats: the added steel rule ships here with malformed nested metadata.proof.proof.atoms and cites 9903.81.87/.88 although the PR body cites 9903.82.02; follow-up commit a14f43975 'b1.6: repair the steel proof chain per review finding' (same PR, before merge) unwraps the atoms, adds 9903.82.02 to source_verification, and fixes companion test inputs. Residual exemplar coupling remains post-fix: entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded = entry_is_line_a, entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded = entry_is_line_b, the Brazil IEEPA term 'not entry_is_line_b', and section 338/beer still on entry_is_line_d. Provision read attempted: resolve_provision for us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-230 succeeded but returned section 232 steel quota notes rather than the section 122 exclusion language (pagination drift in the pinned release), so I relied on the module's proof-atom excerpts plus the PR statement.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix `section_122_component_rate` version-2 formula zeroed the 10 percent surcharge on the union of two witness exemplar flags, and the same module simultaneously uses `entry_is_line_a` as the China-301 list-1 gate (`if entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate`) and `entry_is_line_b` as the section-232-aluminum / China-301 2024-action gate, so no caller assignment can make both rules match the source — the §122 exemption necessarily captured the wrong population of entries. Read through the pinned release, the cited source (Proclamation 11012, FR 2026-03824) exempts only "articles listed in paragraph 2 of Annex I ... and as enumerated in Annex II" and "all articles and parts of articles currently or that later become subject to additional import restrictions imposed pursuant to section 232", and expressly says the surcharge "is in addition to any other duties" — there is no §301-membership exemption, and the §232 carve-out covers steel and copper, not aluminum alone. The fix repoints the gate to `entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered` while leaving the rule's proof atoms, versions, dates and stack position identical, which is a pure change of the exempted population rather than a provenance or serialization edit, so it is fidelity and not mechanical. I considered reclassifying to untraceable_branch (the §301-keyed condition has no basis in the §122 proclamation) but the branch itself is source-grounded — the exemption exists and the atoms already cited it — and what changed is which articles it captures, which is squarely wrong_entity_or_scope.

+      (((((((((((((if entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered: 0
verdict.notes: Refutation attempts and what survived. (1) "Mechanical rename": refuted — one old flag maps to several distinct new flags (`entry_is_line_b` becomes `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` in the aluminum component but `entry_is_china_301_2024_action` in the 301 component), and the §122 gate moves to a different population entirely; the summary's boilerplate "changes no formula tokens ... or runtime values" is contradicted by the diff itself. (2) "Enhancement / new scope the module never claimed": refuted — the generated ch25 composition already claims chapter-wide scope (it stacks components over `chNN_general_rate[hts_line]` for any chapter-25 line), and the PR's own gate evidence enumerates "18 explained" witness-slice cells "where the witness's own coupling was the unlawful part", i.e. wrong outputs, not absent coverage. (3) "Pre-fix was correct": on the witness's five exemplar lines it was — `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: entry_is_line_a` is atom-cited to 7202.11.10 (a §122-exempt line) and `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded: entry_is_line_b` to 9903.01.33 aluminum scope — but that correctness cannot survive chapter-scale reuse of the same flags as 301-list gates. Residual uncertainty a reviewer should weigh: the module text alone is ambiguous about which direction entry preparation populated `entry_is_line_a` (annex-exclusion membership vs. 301 list-1 membership); the PR body settles it ("unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins"), so my confidence rests partly on the PR message rather than on the diff alone. Two further observations: the pre-fix gate also under-exempted, since `entry_is_line_b` covered aluminum only while the source exempts §232-covered steel and copper too; and the fix is partial — `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded` and `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` still ride on `entry_is_line_a`/`entry_is_line_b` in the post file (post lines 1907, 1924). This is a `module.kind: composition` file produced by generator b1.6 rather than encoder output; it is still a RuleSpec v1 rule module with formulas and versions, so not_a_rule_module does not apply, but the upstream defect lives in the hand-built witness the generator copied. Source pages cited by the atoms (us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-221/226/230) do not resolve to the surcharge text in the pinned corpus release (rev 3, us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap) — the exemption text was verified instead through us/rulemaking/federal-register/2026-02-25/2026-03824, which the rule also cites. Other components in the same commit carry different kinds (Brazil/forced-labor 301 gain a missing listed-membership condition; the added `section_232_steel_component_rate` is new coverage) and should be judged separately.

So the encoding's exemption population disagreed with the population its own cited source defines, which is a scope error, and the PR body calls the old behavior "unlawfully suppressed" — a correction, not an enhancement. The §122 proof atoms are byte-identical pre and post, so nothing here is excerpt/provenance bookkeeping; the encoded meaning changed.

The rule's own unchanged proof atoms confine the §122 exceptions to "subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03", "7202.11.10", and "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04"; an exemplar-line identity flag is not one of them, so the branch condition had no source basis and the fix re-grounds it on `entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered` — untraceable_branch, not a rename, a policy choice, or added scope.
verdict.notes: Kind runner-up is wrong_entity_or_scope (the condition selects the wrong population of lines), but the taxonomy puts "a condition with no basis in the cited source (the fix removes or re-grounds it)" under untraceable_branch, which is the better fit here: the source states no exception keyed to exemplar-line identity at all. Reviewer cautions on the rest of this same module diff, which is multi-kind and should not be folded into this finding: (1) `section_232_steel_component_rate` + `ch86_s232_steel_heading_rate` are NEW coverage the module never claimed (the pre-fix summary scopes the stack to "the same panel-projection component sequence as the witness total", and the witness's 7202.11.10.00 ferroalloy exemplar sits outside note 16(c)), so that addition alone would be not_a_defect / unclear, not a fidelity fix; (2) the `brazil_section_301_component_rate` and `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate` edits ADD a previously-missing listed-line membership condition (pre-fix they applied the §301 rate to every Brazil-origin / listed-country entry in the chapter), which reads as unrepresented_clause — a separate defect from the pinned §122 one; (3) the decoupling is only partial — post-fix lines 1908, 1925, 2693, 2817, 2873 and 2998 still ride `entry_is_line_a/b/d`, so residual exemplar coupling survives this commit (the summary admits "Beer/section-338 keeps entry_is_line_d because no membership module exists"). I also resolved us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-221 through the pinned release (corpus us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, provision sha 818d993e…); the resolved page under HTS 2026 Rev. 3 covers note subdivisions (x)–(z) rather than the (aa)(ii) list the atom spans, i.e. the atom's page anchor does not reproduce under the pinned release — that is a provenance wrinkle worth a separate look, but it does not bear on this kind, which turns on the branch condition rather than on the exclusion list's contents. The same module simultaneously uses `entry_is_line_a`/`entry_is_line_b` as the China §301 list-1/2/3 and 2024-action gates in `china_section_301_component_rate`, so no binding of those inputs can satisfy both provisions: the §122 branch had no source basis and the fix re-grounds it on `entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered`, with the PR reporting the evaluated wrong output. verdict.notes: Bundled change, so a reviewer should know what else is inside it. verdict.justification: I tried to refute the reading and could not: the diff deletes five derived rules whose formulas are equality tests against statistical reporting numbers belonging to chapters 72, 76, 95, 22 and 85 (`(hts_number == "7202.11.10.00")` … `(hts_number == "8541.42.00.10")`), each carrying its own proof atoms citing those out-of-chapter provisions, from a chapter-01 composition. This is not mechanical: formulas, proof atoms and the module's input/output surface changed (the PR ledger records "−500 removed exemplar-flag outputs"), and it is the removal arm of untraceable_branch (a condition with no basis in the cited source / grounded on the wrong provision), not a boundary, amount, period or polarity error.

Since every line this module covers is 03xx (the companion test keys on `hts_number: 0301.11.00.00`), those conditions were structurally false for the module's entire population — branches grounded on provisions outside the cited chapter that could never fire, which is exactly "formulas grounded on the wrong provision," and the fix removes that grounding and makes the flags caller inputs. verdict.notes: Attempted refutations and why they fail: (1) "Mechanical / generator-version bump b1.3 -> b1.6" — refuted: five `kind: derived` rules with formulas and proof atoms are deleted and the module's input surface grows by five slots (the post-fix ch03.test.yaml feeds `input.entry_is_line_a..e: false`, which the pre-fix test could not have done since they were derived). (3) "not_a_rule_module (module.kind: composition)" — the file is rulespec/v1 with rules and formulas, and the harness passed it as a module file; composed modules are assembled rather than encoder-generated but are still rule modules. Residual uncertainty (why 0.74, not higher): this commit is only stage 2 of PR #1300 — it removes the ungrounded exemplar tests but does not yet install the source-grounded membership predicates described in the PR body (`entry_is_section_122_exempt`, per-list China-301 membership); in this commit the downstream gates still read `entry_is_line_a..e`, now unbound caller inputs whose proof atoms still cite exemplar excerpts (e.g. `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded` cites chapter-99 page-182 excerpt "7202.11.10"). A reviewer could argue the fidelity correction lands in the later commit and this one is the decoupling half. Alternative kind if the panel prefers it: wrong_entity_or_scope (chapter-03 gating scoped to chapters 22/72/76/85/95 lines); I chose untraceable_branch because the rubric names "formulas grounded on the wrong provision" under that kind. The PR issue comment notes later repairs (steel atoms unwrapped, 9903.82.02 added to source verification, tests feeding only a/b/d), so the merged end state differs from this commit.

triage.commit_summary: The commit bumps the schedule-composition generator to b1.6 and deletes the five hard-coded `entry_is_line_a..e` derived rules from all 100 generated HTS chapter compositions (plus their companion tests), re-declaring the identifiers as caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification. Those rules had been deep-copied from the hand-built five-line CBP witness, so every chapter carried identity tests (`hts_number == "7202.11.10.00"` etc.) and proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS statistical reporting numbers, and those flags gated the §301/§232/§201/§338/§122 components of each chapter's statutory stack; the generator diff states that "generated compositions must not derive them from the five hand-built witness HTS exemplars."

modules.description_quote: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Chapter 13 (lac, gums, resins) derived entry_is_line_a..e as identity tests against five HTS statistical reporting numbers belonging to other chapters (7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 9506.62.40.40, 2203.00.00.30, 8541.42.00.10), with proof atoms citing those other chapters' provisions, so the §301/§232/§201/§338/§122 components the chapter's stack gates on those flags were keyed to lines a chapter 13 entry can never have — conditions with no basis in this chapter's own cited source.
modules.triage_notes: Diff read in full (124 lines): only the module `summary` string and the five removed derived rules change; no other formula, parameter, version, date, input or output is touched. Provision read through the pinned corpus release: us/statute/hts/7202.11.10.00 resolves to a chapter 72 ferromanganese line ('Containing by weight more than 2 percent but not more than 4 percent of carbon', unit 'kg, Mn kg'), confirming the exemplar is out-of-chapter. Companion test diff (ch13.test.yaml) shows pre-fix cases like "positive coverage: entry_is_line_a" feeding hts_number 7202.11.10.00 into the chapter 13 module. Generator rationale in tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py (an 'other file', not quotable as a module comment): 'Entry preparation now supplies the five witness-compatible incidence flags; generated compositions must not derive them from the five hand-built witness HTS exemplars.' PR issue comment notes a follow-up round where flags c and e were 'fully replaced and no longer valid input slots'.

modules.triage_notes: Diff has exactly two hunks: the module summary (metadata) and removal of the five derived rules; no other formula, parameter, date, or citation-path change. Alternative kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (classification scoped to other chapters' lines); I chose untraceable_branch because the defining fault is a condition grounded on the wrong provision that the fix deletes. Provision text not resolved through the corpus — the chapter mismatch is evident from HTS numbering and from the removed rules' own `source:` fields. Part of the PR #1300 stack; a sibling commit re-gates the components on membership-semantic inputs (entry_is_section_122_exempt / entry_is_section_232_covered) and adds the §232 steel component, so this commit is the removal half of that repair.
