verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as a pure architectural decoupling and could not: the ch37 diff deletes five derived rules whose formulas are literal equalities against 10-digit statistical reporting numbers in chapters 22, 72, 76, 85 and 95 (e.g. `hts_number == "7202.11.10.00"`), conditions that can never be true for an entry routed to a chapter-37 composition, and the surviving consumers then read them as caller inputs. Those flags carry substantive branches in this module (`entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: entry_is_line_a`, `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded: entry_is_line_b`, the five-slot `china_301_component_rate` sum, the §201 CSPV and §338/beer slots), whose own proof atoms cite list-membership provisions ("Heading 9903.88.03 applies to all products of China that are classified in the following 8-digit subheadings"), so grounding incidence on one out-of-chapter exemplar line is a formula grounded on the wrong provision, not a missing clause or a scope/entity slip. It is not mechanical: formulas, proof atoms and the input surface all change (the PR comment notes "c and e are fully replaced and no longer valid input slots"), and the next commit in the same PR, a9562cfd4, re-grounds those same references on membership-semantic inputs (`entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, `entry_is_section_201_cspv`, §301 list slots) — removal plus re-grounding, exactly the untraceable_branch pattern. The first reader's kind and reading survive; I would keep confidence just under 0.8 only because this commit performs the removal half and the re-grounding half lands one commit later.

The pre-state conditions were unsatisfiable inside this module: the ch49 line table holds only 49xx keys and `schedule_base_general_rate` raises on a missing key, so a chapter 49 entry's `hts_number` can never equal a chapter 22/72/76/85/95 line — and the module's `source_verification` citation list contains no chapter 49 provision at all, only the five foreign exemplar lines plus chapter 99 overlays. That is exactly "a condition with no basis in the cited source / grounded on the wrong provision," and the fix removes it; the hand-built witness at us/policies/cbp/us-tariff-duty/composition.yaml keeps the five flags (line 691), confirming they were legitimate only for the five-line oracle and were wrongly copied into 100 generated chapters.
verdict.notes: Three caveats for the reviewer, none of which overturn the verdict. (1) The first reader's quote is from the PR body and describes more than this commit: the membership-semantic re-gating of `section_122_component_rate` and the new `section_232_steel_component_rate` are NOT in the ch49 diff for 2a6bdb01de — this commit is only the removal half (subject: "b1.6: make generated entry flags caller inputs"). The kind still holds on this commit's own content. (2) The reader's reading ("every component gated on them ... could never fire") is directionally imprecise: several gates put the flags in negative/carve-out position — `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0 else: ...` (lines 2571/3038/3196 post) and `if origin_is_brazil and not entry_is_line_b: brazil_ieepa_additional_duty_rate else: 0` — so with the flags permanently false the exemptions never fired and the duty always applied, while the §301 stack (post lines 2993-2997) was identically 0. Wrong in both directions, untraceable in all. (3) The sharpest single instance is `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded`, whose declared source is "Chapter 99 U.S. note reciprocal annex exclusion list under heading 9903.01.32" but whose formula is `entry_is_line_a` — i.e. pre-fix, "excluded from the reciprocal tariff iff the entry is ferromanganese." The strongest not_a_defect argument (generated chapters are declared deterministic copies of the witness pilot surface, so the flags are scaffolding rather than a chapter 49 claim) fails because the module still emits chapter-49 §301/§232/§338/reciprocal-exclusion component outputs whose values those flags decided, and the maintainers themselves call the pre-state unlawful in the PR body ("the witness's exemplar coupling, which round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins"). The runner-up kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (the flags scope the ch49 stack to five foreign-chapter lines); untraceable_branch fits better because the fix removes the conditions and their proof atoms cite provisions outside the module's subject chapter. triage.commit_summary: Across all 100 generated tariff-schedule chapter compositions (12 in this chunk, ch73-ch85), the commit deletes the five hard-coded exemplar predicates entry_is_line_a..e - each of which defined an authority-membership flag as identity with one HTS statistical reporting number copied wholesale from the five-line hand-built CBP witness (7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 9506.62.40.40, 2203.00.00.30, 8541.42.00.10) - and leaves those identifiers as caller inputs supplied by entry preparation, with companion tests switched from asserting them as outputs to feeding them as inputs. Because every downstream section 301 / section 232 / section 201 / section 338 / reciprocal-exclusion gate in each chapter's statutory stack keys off those flags, the pre-fix generated chapters held those components at zero for every line in the chapter that was not the copied exemplar; PR #1300 frames the removal as the decoupling repair that stops the witness's exemplar coupling from suppressing lawful surcharges.

modules.description_quote: The identifiers entry_is_line_a, entry_is_line_b, entry_is_line_c, entry_is_line_d, and entry_is_line_e are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Chapter 73's section 301-list, reciprocal-annex-exclusion, section 232 aluminum, section 201 solar and section 338 beer membership predicates were encoded as identity with five single exemplar HTS lines copied from the witness (7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 9506.62.40.40, 2203.00.00.30, 8541.42.00.10), none of which is a chapter 73 line, so those authority components evaluated to zero for every chapter 73 entry even though the cited Chapter 99 notes define membership by long enumerated line lists that include chapter 73 lines.
modules.triage_notes: Read the full diff plus pre/post files. Two hunks only: module summary rewrite (generator b1.3 -> b1.6, new caller-input sentence) and deletion of the five derived rules with their proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines. The flags remain referenced ~20 times in the post-fix file (china_section_301_component_rate lines 2994-2998, section_122/201/232/338 gates, entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded = entry_is_line_a, entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded = entry_is_line_b), so the removal is load-bearing, not dead-code deletion; the companion ch73.test.yaml in the same commit moves them from expected outputs to #input.* facts and drops the 'positive coverage: entry_is_line_a' cases that fed a chapter-72 HTS number to a chapter-73 module. Doubt to flag: the summary still carries the serialization boilerplate 'Values, dates, dtypes, proof atoms, and runtime semantics are unchanged', and the commit is one step of a multi-commit decoupling repair (follow-up c27e3d99f 'b1.6: generalize generated component surfaces' replaces flags c and e with membership-semantic inputs; 606300042 adds the caller-side incidence flag classifier), so a reviewer could read this single commit as a plumbing refactor rather than a fidelity fix - hence confidence 0.65. Provision check: resolved us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-182 against pinned release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap; it returns an enumerated list of ~198 HTS line numbers (chemical chapters), not the '7202.11.10' excerpt the removed atom cited, so page numbering differs from the encode-time vintage, but the chapter-99 page-219 text already in the scratchpad shows the same notes enumerate many chapter-73 lines (7304.x, 7306.x), confirming membership is list-based rather than single-line. Bundle has 100 modules; all 12 chunk indices exist.

verdict.justification: I tried to reduce this to mechanical or not_a_defect and could not: the diff deletes five whole derived rules (formulas plus proof atoms) from ch73.yaml and converts their identifiers into implicit caller inputs, so formulas, rule set, and input surface all change. The deleted rules pinned chapter 73's membership predicates to single HTS lines from other chapters (7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 9506.62.40.40, 2203.00.00.30, 8541.42.00.10), none of which exists in the ch73 rate table this module imports (us/policies/usitc/us-tariff-duty/lines/generated/ch73.yaml contains only 73xx lines, and a missing key deliberately raises), so entry_is_line_a..e were identically false and every component gated on them (china_section_301_component_rate, section_201/232-aluminum/338, entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded, entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded) was inert for every chapter 73 entry. The pinned release confirms the disagreement with the cited source: 9903.01.33 reads "Articles of iron or steel; derivative articles of iron or steel; articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum; ...", yet the module encoded that exclusion as one aluminum line (its own proof excerpt truncates to "articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum"). That is a condition grounded on the wrong provision that the fix removes, which is untraceable_branch as defined.
verdict.notes: Kept the first reader's classification and kind, with caveats a reviewer should see. (1) This commit only deletes the definitions; every consuming formula in ch73 is byte-identical (section_122_component_rate still reads "if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0" at post line 2572, and china_section_301_component_rate still has five exemplar slots), so the repair is delegation to entry preparation, not in-module re-grounding — the PR body's §122 regating and the steel component land in later commits of PR #1300. (2) The exemplar-copy pattern survives this commit: entry_is_energy_resource is still hard-coded as hts_number == "7202.11.10.00" in the post file (line 1951), so ch73 still carries a chapter-72 ferroalloy grounding for an IEEPA energy-scope predicate — a live follow-on defect worth filing separately. (3) The retained summary sentence "Values, dates, dtypes, proof atoms, and runtime semantics are unchanged" is scoped to the sibling-distinctness serialization device (redundant parens and ch73_ scalar prefixes), not to the flag change; read against the flag change it is false, since derived rules became caller inputs. (4) The first reader's quote is from the new module comment, which is not itself the defect evidence; the decisive evidence is the deleted formula lines plus PR #1300's statement that the witness's exemplar coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins". (5) Closest alternative kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (a witness five-line panel population copied onto chapter 73's population); I did not reclassify because the taxonomy puts "formulas grounded on the wrong provision" and fixes that remove the branch under untraceable_branch. (6) The file is module.kind: composition — generator output from tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py (in other_files), regenerated across 100 chapters — so the defect is one generator bug replicated per chapter, not 100 independent findings; corpus de-duplication should account for that.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as bookkeeping or as a pure architectural decoupling and could not: the diff deletes five derived rules whose formulas were literal identity tests against HTS lines in other chapters (7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 9506.62.40.40, 2203.00.00.30, 8541.42.00.10), each carrying proof atoms citing those other chapters' provisions, inside a chapter 74 copper module whose base rates come from ch74_general_rate[hts_line], so every one of them was statically false for any entry this module can price. Those flags are the sole gates on china_section_301_component_rate (all five terms), section_201_component_rate, section_232_aluminum_component_rate, and the annex/metals exclusion in section_122_component_rate, so chapter 74's authority stack was a constant fixed by other chapters' line identities rather than by the chapter 99 notes the module cites. Resolving the module's own cited provision us/statute/hts/9903.01.33 through the pinned release returns "articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum; ... semi-finished copper; and intensive copper derivative products" — copper is named in the cited text, yet the copper chapter's metals-exclusion predicate was `entry_is_line_b` (an aluminum wire line), which is exactly a formula grounded on the wrong provision. The fix removes those ungrounded predicates and makes the identifiers caller inputs "supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification," i.e. re-grounding, which is the untraceable_branch pattern and not a scope enhancement the module never claimed.
verdict.notes:
Evidence trail: diff /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/diffs/us/2a6bdb01de/073.diff (124 lines: summary paragraph + removal of the five derived rules, nothing else); pre/post of us/policies/cbp/us-tariff-schedule/generated/ch74/ch74.yaml at 956a5474 and 2a6bdb01de.

Refutations I tested and rejected: (1) "mechanical" — the module summary's boilerplate "Values, dates, dtypes, proof atoms, and runtime semantics are unchanged" is contradicted by the diff, which deletes five derived outputs with formulas and proof atoms and moves them to the implicit caller-input surface; PR #1300 counts this as "-500 removed exemplar-flag outputs" across 100 chapters and its ledger ceiling moves 15770 -> 15470, so inputs and outputs changed. (2) "not_a_defect / new coverage" — the pre-state disagreed with a provision already in this module's own source_verification set (9903.01.33 names semi-finished copper), so the old text was wrong, not merely narrower. (3) "not_a_rule_module" — it is module.kind: composition, but it is a format: rulespec/v1 file with rules and formulas in a rulespec-us jurisdiction repo, not a compose spec/registry/ledger.

Closest alternative kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (a chapter 74 predicate keyed to chapter 72/76/95/22/85 line identities), but untraceable_branch explicitly covers formulas grounded on the wrong provision and is the better fit for a fix that deletes the ungrounded predicates.

Two caveats for the reviewer. (a) Direction is not uniform: for section 301 / 201 / 232-aluminum the flags being false zeroed the components, while for section_122 the false flags meant the annex and metals exclusions never fired, so the reciprocal component over-applied to copper; the candidate quote's phrase "reciprocal-exclusion components were zero" is accurate only in the sense that the exclusion predicate was false. (b) This commit is one half of PR #1300's repair — it removes the exemplar derivations while leaving the identifier names in the formulas; the sibling work in the same PR re-gates components on membership-semantic inputs ("never again zeroed by China-list or aluminum membership (the witness's exemplar coupling, which round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on 301-member lines for all origins)"). If the corpus policy is one defect per repair rather than per commit, this commit and the component-decoupling commit should be deduplicated into a single untraceable_branch defect rather than counted twice, and the same removal is replicated verbatim across all 100 generated chapter modules in this commit.

Reading the cited Chapter 99 notes through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, corpus commit e79781bd) shows the source disagrees in both directions: the 9903.01.32 annex exclusion list announced at chapter-99 page-178 continues onto page-184, which lists 7501.10.00, 7502.10.00, 7502.20.00, 7503.00.00, 7504.00.00 and 7508.90.50 (so the exclusion should fire for nickel lines and never could), and the 9903.88.03 List 3 enumeration announced at page-264 runs through page-283, which lists 28 chapter 75 subheadings (7501.10 through 7507.12 and more) at the 25% action that the module could never apply. The fix deletes those five ungrounded identity conditions and their foreign-chapter proof atoms, making membership caller-supplied — exactly the "condition with no basis in the cited source / formula grounded on the wrong provision, removed or re-grounded" shape, not a mechanical or bookkeeping change (five rule formulas, their proof atoms, and the module's input surface all change).
verdict.notes: Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "mechanical" is excluded because the diff removes five derived rules with formulas and proof atoms and converts them to inputs, so inputs/outputs and runtime values for chapter-75 entries change; (2) "not_a_defect / new coverage never claimed" is excluded because the consuming rules advertise chapter-99 grounding in their own `source` and proof atoms (`source: Chapter 99 U.S. note reciprocal annex exclusion list under heading 9903.01.32`, atoms citing chapter-99 page-177/page-182 and page-273) while implementing the predicate as a foreign-chapter line identity, and the PR body itself calls the prior coupling one that "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins". Competing kind worth a reviewer's eye: wrong_entity_or_scope (the predicate ranged over the wrong HTS line population); I kept untraceable_branch because the kind definition explicitly covers "formulas grounded on the wrong provision" and the fix's operative act is removal, not re-scoping. Caveats: this commit only removes the definitions — the membership-semantic re-gating (`entry_is_section_122_exempt` / `entry_is_section_232_covered`) and the §232 steel component described in PR #1300 are not in this module's diff at this SHA, where the §301 component still reads `if entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate ...`; and the module summary's retained boilerplate "changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values" is false for this commit (it removes proof atoms and adds five input slots), which is why the screener flagged it. The maintainer's later PR comment notes flags c and e were subsequently "fully replaced and no longer valid input slots", so the final merged state differs from this commit.

verdict.justification: The ch76 diff contains nothing but the summary rewrite and the deletion of the five `entry_is_line_a..e` derived rules; every meaning-bearing consumer is byte-identical after the commit (`entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` is still `formula: entry_is_line_b`, `section_232_aluminum_component_rate` still branches `elif entry_is_line_b:`, and the five-term §301 sum is unchanged), so this commit relocates where a flag is defined rather than re-grounding any duty predicate on the 9903.01.33 membership. Two pieces of evidence cut against the "fidelity correction" reading: the identical exemplar proxy `entry_is_energy_resource` = `hts_number == "7202.11.10.00"` (a chapter 72 ferroalloy line cited to the 9903.01.13 energy scope) survives untouched at post-commit line 1986, and the maintainer's own PR comment says flags a/b/d were *retained* as exemplar input slots, so the aluminum/metals predicate the first reader's reading turns on was never moved to membership semantics by this PR. The pre state was genuinely narrower than the resolved 9903.01.33 text ("articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum … as provided in subdivisions (v)(vi) through (v)(xvi) of U.S. note 2"), and removing four out-of-chapter line bindings (footballs, beer, PV cells, ferroalloy) from an aluminum module does unfreeze branches that were dead-false for every real chapter-76 entry — which is why I do not call it mechanical or not_a_defect. But with a generic structural commit subject, PR gates certifying byte-exact determinism and witness-slice equivalence "exact under input mapping", and no consumer formula touched, the evidence does not settle that this module change corrects encoded meaning rather than plumbing it out to a caller.

verdict.notes:
Refutation attempts and why they failed. (1) "Summary says runtime semantics unchanged" — that sentence ("This deterministic RuleSpec serialization changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values ... Values, dates, dtypes, proof atoms, and runtime semantics are unchanged") is generator boilerplate about the parenthesization/scalar-rename serialization and appears verbatim in the PRE file too, so it is no evidence that this change is inert. (2) "Enhancement / new coverage the module never claimed" — the module is a chapter-wide composition (schedule_base_general_rate does ch85_general_rate[hts_line] over the whole chapter table) and it emitted the five flags as outputs, so it made a false chapter-85 claim rather than declining to claim. (3) "Defined elsewhere via import" — checked: no import defines entry_is_line_*; only the untouched hand-built witness composition (us/policies/cbp/us-tariff-duty/composition.yaml) does, and generated chapters do not import it.

Caveats a reviewer should weigh. This commit is one step of the PR #1300 stack: after it, ch85 still carries the exemplar coupling (`section_122_component_rate`: "if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0" at post line 2571, same at brazil/forced-labor §301 3038/3196, and `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded` still `formula: entry_is_line_a`). The membership re-grounding the PR body describes ("gated on `entry_is_section_122_exempt` / `entry_is_section_232_covered`", "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins") landed in later commits, so this commit removes the mis-grounded definitions and defers the correct membership to the caller rather than fixing the incidence inside the module. Kind is a near-tie for entry_is_line_e alone — 8541.42.00.10 is a genuine chapter-85 PV line standing in for the whole 9903.91.02 / note 31(c) membership, which reads as wrong_entity_or_scope — but a through d are grounded on other chapters entirely and the fix shape is removal, which is the untraceable_branch signature, so the kind holds for the change as a whole. I did not run resolve_provision: the defect does not hinge on a number, boundary or clause in the source text, only on the module's own proof atoms citing corpus paths for other chapters' lines, which the diff shows directly.

triage.commit_summary: Across all 100 generated chapter tariff-schedule compositions the commit deletes the five hard-coded `entry_is_line_a`..`entry_is_line_e` derived rules — predicates of the form `hts_number == "<exemplar line>"` copied verbatim from the hand-built five-line CBP witness (7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 9506.62.40.40, 2203.00.00.30, 8541.42.00.10), whose proof atoms cite HTS lines belonging to other chapters — and re-declares those identifiers as caller inputs supplied by entry preparation under the repository's referenced-implies-input convention, bumping the generator tag from b1.3-schedule-compositions-1 to b1.6-schedule-compositions-2. It is the first of PR #1300's four b1.6 commits, which go on to re-ground the §301/§232/§201 component gates on membership-semantic inputs and add a §232 steel component; the generator change is explicit that "generated compositions must not derive them from the five hand-built witness HTS exemplars".

modules.description_quote: The identifiers entry_is_line_a, entry_is_line_b, entry_is_line_c, entry_is_line_d, and entry_is_line_e are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Chapter 86's composition derived its five action-incidence gates as equality against single HTS lines from other chapters (7202.11.10.00 ferroalloys, 7601.10.30.00 aluminum, 9506.62.40.40 footballs, 2203.00.00.30 beer, 8541.42.00.10 PV cells), with proof atoms citing those out-of-chapter provisions, so for any chapter-86 entry all five were constant false and the §301/§201/§232-aluminum/§338 components were identically zero — a condition with no basis in the provisions this module encodes.
modules.triage_notes: Verified the grounding claim: the imported chapter-86 base table (us/policies/usitc/us-tariff-duty/lines/generated/ch86.yaml) lists only 86xx lines in source_verification, and schedule_base_general_rate does ch86_general_rate[hts_line] with a missing key raising a lookup error, so an entry routed to this module can never have hts_number 7202.11.10.00 etc.; pre-fix section_301_component_rate in this file (`if entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate ...`) was therefore dead. Corroborating evidence outside the module diff: the same commit's tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py adds the comment "Entry preparation now supplies the five witness-compatible incidence flags; generated compositions must not derive them from the five hand-built witness HTS exemplars." Two caveats that keep confidence below 0.8: the commit body is empty and the module summary retains the boilerplate sentence "This deterministic RuleSpec serialization changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values", which is inconsistent with the input-surface change this commit makes; and this commit only removes the wrong derivation — the membership-semantic re-grounding lands in follow-up commits a9562cfd4, 198bee703, a14f43975 of the same PR. wrong_entity_or_scope is a defensible alternative kind (the gate selected one out-of-chapter line as the population). Leftover: module.source_verification still lists us/statute/hts/9506.62.40.40, 2203.00.00.30 and 8541.42.00.10 although no proof atom cites them any more post-fix. Provision text was not fetched through resolve_provision.py — the defect is structural (wrong-chapter grounding) and does not turn on what 9903.88.03 etc. say.

verdict.justification: The ch86 diff deletes five derived rules whose formulas were equality against single out-of-chapter statistical reporting numbers (7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 9506.62.40.40, 2203.00.00.30, 8541.42.00.10), each with proof atoms citing those other chapters' provisions, and makes the identifiers caller inputs — so this is a change to the module's computed values and input surface, not proof/metadata bookkeeping. Because an hts_number classified in chapter 86 can never equal any of those five lines, every gate was constant false pre-fix, which forced china_section_301_component_rate (`if entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: list_1_... + ... + if entry_is_line_e ...`), section_201_component_rate, the §232 aluminum/beer chain and the §338 gate to zero for all chapter-86 entries. I checked the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap) and HTS chapter 99 U.S. note 20(b) and 20(d) — the enumerations for headings 9903.88.01/9903.88.02 — do list chapter-86 subheadings (8601.10.00, 8601.20.00, 8602.10.00, 8603.x, 8604.00.00, 8605.00.00, 8606.x, 8607.x), so the identically-zero §301 output contradicted the source rather than harmlessly matching it. The branch condition had no basis in the provisions this module encodes and the fix removes it, which is untraceable_branch (a formula grounded on the wrong provision); alternatives fail — nothing is inverted (polarity_or_logic), no clause is added (unrepresented_clause), and no amount or window moved.
verdict.notes: Refutation attempts and what survived: (1) "mechanical" fails — five rules with formulas, dtypes, effective windows and proof atoms are deleted and the identifiers become caller inputs; the post summary itself says they "are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification." (2) "not_a_defect / new coverage never claimed" fails — the module is the chapter-86 statutory stack (it imports ch86's own rate table and does `ch86_general_rate[hts_line]`), so it claims to serve chapter-86 entries, and its §301/§201/§232/§338 components were live outputs that could only ever fire on other chapters' lines. (3) The generator boilerplate "Values, dates, dtypes, proof atoms, and runtime semantics are unchanged" is stale text describing the sibling-distinctness serialization (redundant parens, chapter-prefixed scalars) relative to the witness, not this change; the screener was right to be unsure of it. Caveats for the reviewer: this identical repair lands in ~100 generated chapter modules in one commit (tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py is the real edit), so the corpus will hold ~100 near-duplicate instances of this one defect — dedupe to one representative. The repair is also partial at this commit: post-fix, china_section_301_component_rate still carries proof atoms citing 7202.11.10.00 / 9506.62.40 / 7601.10.30.00 / 2203.00.00 / 8541.42.00, section_122 still reads `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0`, and module source_verification still lists the five out-of-chapter citation paths; the §122 decoupling and the steel component described in the PR body are in other commits of PR #1300. PR body language supporting fidelity (not this file's diff): "the witness's exemplar coupling, which round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins".

verdict.justification: I tried to knock this down to mechanical or not_a_defect and could not: the diff deletes five whole derived rules (formula, dtype, effective `from: '2026-02-15'`, proof atoms) from the chapter-87 module, so formulas and the module's input/output surface changed (the PR's own ledger records "−500 removed exemplar-flag outputs"), which is outside the mechanical list. Each deleted rule asserted, inside a ch87 composition, that a gate fires iff `hts_number` equals a statistical reporting number from another chapter (7202.11.10.00 ferrosilicon, 7601.10.30.00 aluminum wire, 9506.62.40.40 footballs, 2203.00.00.30 beer, 8541.42.00.10 PV cells), with proof atoms citing those out-of-chapter provisions; since `schedule_base_general_rate` is `ch87_general_rate[hts_line]` and raises on a missing key, those conditions were constant-false in any evaluable ch87 entry, leaving `china_section_301_component_rate` (post lines 2993–2997), the §201 and §338 gates, and the reciprocal annex/metals exclusions dead or never excluded — a condition with no basis in this module's cited source, which is exactly untraceable_branch ("formulas grounded on the wrong provision", fix removes or re-grounds). The "not a defect, just architecture" reading fails because the pre summary already promised "Chapter and rate-line routing occur in entry preparation, never through cross-chapter RuleSpec dispatch" while the module did that routing locally, and the PR calls the same exemplar coupling one that "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins."
verdict.notes:
Evidence checked: diff 085.diff (two hunks only — summary rewrite plus removal of entry_is_line_a..e), plus full pre (956a5474, 3471 lines) and post (2a6bdb01de, 3371 lines) files.

Caveats a reviewer should weigh:
1. This commit is stage one of PR #1300. The references keep the old names and the old gating: post line 2571 still has `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0 else: temporary_import_surcharge_rate`, i.e. the §122 re-gating the PR body describes ("gated on entry_is_section_122_exempt / entry_is_section_232_covered") is NOT in this module diff. So the PR's "unlawfully suppressed" line is context, not the decisive evidence for this file; the decisive evidence is the removed formulas themselves.
2. Re-grounding here is partial. The components retain out-of-chapter grounding in their own metadata, e.g. post `source: Flat ad-valorem section 232 aluminum overlay composition for HTS 7601.10.30.00` and china_301 atoms citing us/statute/hts/7202.11.10.00, and the module's source_verification still lists 2203.00.00, 7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 8541.42.00.10, 9506.62.40.40 after the fix. A reviewer could reasonably say the untraceable grounding is only half removed at this commit.
3. The screen note's worry ("summary claims runtime semantics unchanged") is a false alarm: that sentence ("This deterministic RuleSpec serialization changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values") is boilerplate about the sibling-chapter parenthesization step and is carried verbatim from the pre summary; it is not a claim about the b1.6 flag change, which the new summary sentence describes explicitly.
4. Second-best kind considered and rejected: wrong_entity_or_scope (the gates selected the wrong population of entries). It fits loosely, but the rubric puts wrong-provision grounding and removal-type fixes under untraceable_branch, and the removed rules' proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines is the cleanest evidence available.
5. Confidence held at 0.7 rather than higher because the diff alone is a derived→input boundary move with byte-identical referencing formulas; the meaning change is real but its correctness depends on the caller contract stated only in the module comment ("caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification").

verdict.justification: The diff for ch88.yaml is 104 deleted lines and 4 added (summary only): it removes five derived rules whose formulas were bare equality tests against statistical reporting numbers in chapters 72, 76, 95, 22 and 85, each with proof atoms citing those out-of-chapter provisions, inside a chapter-88 module. Those flags are the gates for this chapter's §301, §122 temporary-import-surcharge, §201, §232-aluminum and §338 components, and for semantic rules such as entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded (source: "Chapter 99 U.S. note reciprocal annex exclusion list under heading 9903.01.32", formula: entry_is_line_a) and entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded (source: "HTS 9903.01.33 section 232 metals article scope", formula: entry_is_line_b) — so the module asserted a chapter-99 class membership while implementing "hts_number == 7202.11.10.00", a condition with no basis in the cited source for any 88xx entry. Removing those derivations and making the identifiers caller inputs re-grounds branches that were grounded on the wrong provision, which is untraceable_branch, not a provenance-only edit; the summary's boilerplate "runtime semantics are unchanged" is contradicted by the PR's own removal-aware ledger (−500 removed exemplar-flag outputs) and by its statement that the exemplar coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins".
verdict.notes: Refutation attempts and why they fail. (1) Mechanical: rejected — whole rules with formulas and proof atoms are deleted, the module's declared input surface gains five caller inputs and loses five derived outputs (PR: "removal-aware pending ledger — −500 removed exemplar-flag outputs", i.e. 5 per chapter over 100 chapters), so formulas/inputs/outputs did not stay the same. (2) not_a_defect (pilot-scope enhancement): rejected — the module does not disclaim these gates; it affirmatively names the semantics (entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded / entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded / china_section_301_component_rate) with chapter-99 proof atoms while implementing single foreign-chapter line equality, so the pre-fix encoded meaning disagreed with the cited source rather than merely omitting coverage. (3) Alternative kind wrong_entity_or_scope is arguable (a single exemplar line standing in for a whole covered class), but the kind rubric puts "formulas grounded on the wrong provision" under untraceable_branch, and the fix's action is removal/re-grounding, not a scope re-targeting. Caveats for a reviewer: this commit does not re-gate any component formula in ch88 — the §301/§122/§201/§338 formulas still reference entry_is_line_a..e verbatim (post lines 2572, 2648, 2816, 2994-2998); the "membership-semantic" re-gating described in the PR body happens elsewhere in the stack. Also, if the engine defaults an unsupplied input to false, evaluated values for a caller that supplies nothing would be identical to pre-fix; the meaning change is that the module stops asserting a false grounding and hands class membership to entry preparation. Verified read-only via git show of parent 956a547418 and 2a6bdb01de.

verdict.justification: The ch95 diff deletes five hard-coded `derived` rules (formulas, `from: '2026-02-15'` windows, proof atoms, and the five flag outputs) and turns the identifiers into caller inputs, so this is not a metadata/serialization change: the module's input and output surface changes. Pre-fix, every chapter-95 entry hit four gates testing HTS numbers from other chapters (7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 2203.00.00.30, 8541.42.00.10 — identically false for a 95xx line) plus `entry_is_line_c = (hts_number == "9506.62.40.40")`, and those flags drive `china_section_301_component_rate` (`+ (if entry_is_line_c and origin_is_china: list_4a_additional_ad_valorem_rate else: 0)`), so the module determined that within all of chapter 95 only one football statistical reporting number bears §301 list-4A duty. Resolving the cited provisions at the pinned release refutes that grounding: the list-4A footnote sits on the 8-digit 9506.62.40 ("Footballs and soccer balls") and 9903.88.15 applies to "articles the product of China, as provided for in U.S. note 20(r) ... and as provided for in the subheadings enumerated in U.S. note 20(s)" — membership by enumerated subheading, not by one 10-digit SRN. Removing conditions whose proof atoms ("Footballs", "Containing by weight more than 2 percent but not more than 4 percent of carbon") cannot support the §301/§232/§201 incidence they gate is exactly untraceable_branch (a branch grounded on the wrong provision, removed by the fix), so the first reader's classification and kind survive.
verdict.notes: Refutations I tried and why they failed: (1) "mechanical" — no: five derived rules with formulas, effective dates and declared outputs are deleted (PR ceremony records "−500 removed exemplar-flag outputs" across 100 chapters = 5 each), and inputs/outputs are explicitly disqualifying changes. (2) "not_a_defect / pure interface refactor" — this is the real residual risk and the reason I hold confidence at 0.7 rather than higher: in ch95 the *referencing* formulas are byte-identical pre and post (lines 2993-2997 post vs 3093-3097 pre; the §122 `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0` coupling is also unchanged here), so this commit relocates the determination to the caller rather than re-grounding it in-file, and the module still carries the arbitrary five-slot structure with the names `entry_is_line_a..e`. The PR's own gate language ("Witness-slice equivalence: exact under input mapping") is consistent with a semantics-preserving-under-mapping refactor. (3) Alternative kind wrong_entity_or_scope is arguable (gates keyed to out-of-chapter lines inside a chapter-wide composition), but the operative mechanism is removal of ungrounded/misgrounded conditions, which the taxonomy assigns to untraceable_branch; unrepresented_clause is wrong because nothing is added here. Corroborating non-diff evidence a reviewer may want: PR #1300 body calls the pre-state "the witness's exemplar coupling, which round-2 evaluation showed unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins", reports "the same 9 explained ch95 cells" of changed behavior, and the maintainer comment records that "c and e are fully replaced and no longer valid input slots" — i.e., the re-grounding for ch95's list-4A and solar slots completes in later commits of the same PR, so this commit is one step of a multi-commit fidelity repair, not the whole of it. The file is `module.kind: composition` but is a rulespec/v1 module carrying real rules, versions and formulas (the commit itself calls it the "merged composition"), so I treated it as a rule module rather than not_a_rule_module. The diff also changes a rationale comment block and adds one condition proof atom (verbatim note 2(u) entry-date clause) on ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions; those are provenance/documentation, mechanical alongside the substantive scope fix. Non-module files in the commit (composition.test.yaml with 3 new HK cases, the encoding manifest, oracle-coverage-pending.yaml ledger +1 for the new judgment output) are consistent with the stated fix and change nothing else. Kind alternative: this could also be read as unrepresented_clause (the HK half of the source clause was missing and the fix adds it); I chose wrong_entity_or_scope because the commit and PR both describe it as a scope/geography defect ("Scope defect in merged composition") and the correction is to the geographic population the branch fires for. The diff changes encoded meaning in exactly the way the first reader described: both `ieepa_component_rate` and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions` fentanyl branches go from `(if origin_is_china: ...` to `(if origin_is_china or origin_is_hong_kong: ...`, plus a new `origin_is_hong_kong` derived judgment (`country_of_origin == "HK"`) — formulas and origin scope, not bookkeeping. imed new coverage: the pre-fix composition already priced HK entries through its general origin cascade (reciprocal/baseline `else` branches, no `HK` string anywhere in the pre file), so an HK entry got a computed fentanyl component of 0 — a wrong value for an in-scope population. Kind holds: the defect is an under-inclusive geographic population, which is wrong_entity_or_scope; unrepresented_clause fits worse because the added disjunct is the second half of the provision's scope phrase rather than a separate exception or carve-out, and polarity_or_logic fits worse because no boolean was inverted or mis-combined.

triage.commit_summary: Round-2 repair commit on rulespec-us PR #1196 (forced-labor section 301 country overlays, HTS 9903.05.20-9903.05.84): it encoded five deferred column-1 floor headings (9903.05.39/.49/.71/.74/.76) with boundary and exception tests, split the CBP tariff composition into an explicitly non-exempt panel projection (`forced_labor_section_301_component_rate`) plus a new legally complete entry-level rate (`forced_labor_section_301_entry_component_rate`) that applies the 9903.05.85 in-transit safe harbor, the U.S. note 52(g)/(h) USMCA relief, the note 52(a) chapter-98 exclusion and personal-use accompanied baggage, and added a Japan 9903.05.48 country-FALSE test case. It also repaired 54 modules' heading-range proof excerpts and module summaries from ASCII hyphens to the Rev14 en-dash and re-signed every changed file with fresh encoding manifests, so most touched overlay modules changed only provenance strings.

modules.description_quote: split the composition into a non-exempt panel projection plus a legally complete entry-level rate applying the 9903.05.85 in-transit safe harbor, note 52(g)/(h) USMCA exception, note 52(a) chapter-98 exclusion, and personal-use baggage
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The composition's forced-labor section 301 component encoded the country tiers and line A/B carve-outs but represented none of the exceptions the source states for headings 9903.05.20-9903.05.84 - the 9903.05.85 in-transit safe harbor, the note 52(g)/(h) USMCA relief for Canada and Mexico, the note 52(a) chapter-98 exclusion, and the personal-use accompanied-baggage carve-out - so duty was computed as if those exempt entries were dutiable.
modules.triage_notes: Verified against the parent: `git show 4dfebb74...:us/policies/cbp/us-tariff-duty/composition.yaml` has zero matches for 9903.05.85, USMCA, chapter 98, baggage or in-transit, so the four exception clauses were entirely absent pre-fix; the fix adds three new Judgment rules plus the entry-level rate. Provision read: the resolver returned HTS 9903.05.85 verbatim ('loaded onto a vessel ... before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026' and 'entered for consumption ... before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 28, 2026'), which matches both the new excerpts and the new version windows (2026-07-24 to 2026-07-27, then false). Caveat on the note 52(a) grounding: `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-553` resolves through the pinned release to `2026-08-01-usitc-hts-2026-rev3-notes.jsonl` (Rev3), whose text is the 2025 note 2(v) reciprocal table and contains no '9903.05' string, so I could NOT confirm the note 52(a) chapter-98/baggage excerpts against the corpus - the Rev14 text the module quotes is not reachable at that citation path in this resolver. Partial correction only: `us_tariff_total_ad_valorem_rate` still consumes the non-exempt `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate` (line ~1650 post-fix); the new legally complete rate is deliberately unconsumed by panel-facing rules, and the module note says so. The commit also makes non-fidelity changes in this same file: 7 added corpus_citation_paths in module.source_verification (twice), a longer module note/summary, an added proof atom on `origin_is_korea` citing 9903.05.71, and 14 added proof atoms on `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate` grounding the existing MFN-floor branches in 9903.05.38/.48/.70/.73/.75 and 7601.10.30.00 - that rule's formula itself is byte-identical pre and post. Module is `kind: composition`; I classified it as a rule module because it carries rules with formulas and versions, not as a compose spec. No PR reviews or review comments exist on #1196 (reviews/review_comments/issue_comments all empty), so the commit message is the only stated reason.

verdict.justification: The cited source really does state the exceptions and the pre-fix module represented none of them: `9903.05.85` resolves through the pinned release to the in-transit safe harbor verbatim and `9903.05.93` to the note 52(g) Canada USMCA heading, while pre-fix `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate` (entity CustomsEntry, entry-date version windows, source string claiming "Forced labor section 301 overlay composition under headings 9903.05.20 through 9903.05.84") branched only on country tier and line A/B and already carried an `exception` atom for heading 9903.05.86 from the same exception family, so it claimed exception coverage and omitted four of them. The fix adds three new Judgment rules plus an entry-level rate that applies them, along with six new module inputs, which is an encoded-meaning change of exactly the kind the reason describes. I tried to refute this as mere added scope and could not: the rule declared entry-level scope, so an entry inside the 9903.05.85 window was given the full additional duty against the source text. The caveat that keeps confidence at 0.7 rather than higher is that the fix is purely additive — the defective formula and `us_tariff_total_ad_valorem_rate` are byte-identical post-fix, and the corrected rate is consumed by nothing.
verdict.quote:
+          if forced_labor_in_transit_safe_harbor_applies
+             or forced_labor_usmca_exception_applies
+             or forced_labor_chapter_98_exclusion_applies
+             or entry_is_personal_use_accompanied_baggage: 0
+          else: forced_labor_section_301_component_rate
verdict.notes: Verification detail for a reviewer. (1) Source grounding checked through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union): `us/statute/hts/9903.05.85` -> "Articles that (1) were loaded onto a vessel at the port of loading and in transit on the final mode of transit prior to entry into the United States before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 24, 2026; and (2) are entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, before 12:01 a.m. eastern time on July 28, 2026"; `us/statute/hts/9903.05.93` -> "Articles the product of Canada, as provided for in subdivision (g) of U.S. note 52 to this subchapter". The encoded version window (effective_from 2026-07-24, effective_to 2026-07-27) matches the "before July 28" cutoff. Note: `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-553` (the note 52(a) chapter-98/baggage excerpt) does NOT resolve to that text in this release — it resolves to a Revision 3 page covering headings 9903.02.02-9903.02.05 (Afghanistan/Algeria/Angola/Bangladesh reciprocal). That looks like a Rev3-vs-Rev14 page-numbering artifact (the same commit repairs "54 modules' heading-range excerpts to the Rev14 en-dash"), not a fabricated excerpt, but the note 52(a) excerpts are unverified against the resolvable corpus and someone should re-check them against Rev14. (2) The fix does not cure the computed duty. `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate`'s `versions:` block and the whole `us_tariff_total_ad_valorem_rate` rule are byte-identical between 4dfebb74e4 and 65997b4e49; the total still sums the non-exempt projection, and the new `forced_labor_section_301_entry_component_rate` is consumed by nothing (its own source says "not consumed by the panel total"). The added tests pin this explicitly: for an in-transit Canadian entry on 2026-07-25 they assert `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate: 0.10` and `forced_labor_section_301_entry_component_rate: 0`. So the first reader's tail clause "duty was computed as if those exempt entries were dutiable" remains true of the module's headline output after the fix. (3) The first reader's rule_names list mixes real and provenance-only items: `origin_is_korea` and `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate` changed only in `source:` string and proof atoms (including new atoms for 9903.05.38/.48/.70/.73/.75), which is mechanical; the meaning change is confined to the four newly added rules. (4) Related context: the per-country overlays (e.g. forced-labor-algeria-9903-05-20.yaml) already encoded the exception at Asset level as `and not article_described_in_headings_9903_05_85_through_9903_05_92`, but the composition re-derived the rate independently and did not inherit it — which is why the omission was composition-local.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix file encoded nothing at all — it was a machine-declared stub (`rules: []`, `module.status: deferred`) whose three `deferred_outputs` entries each name the missing output and state the reason, the first being an encoder namespace problem ("Generated rule used a local name that collides with a sibling RuleSpec export"), with the other two deferred only as dependents of it. Under the rubric a fidelity defect is "an encoded meaning that disagrees with the cited source text"; here no formula, parameter, version, date, input/output or scope asserted anything that the source contradicts, so the fix supplies coverage the module explicitly disclaimed rather than repairing a clause missing from a working encoding. That the repair renames the blocked output to the collision-free `forced_labor_eu_floor_heading_applies` confirms the gap's cause was a pipeline/naming block, not a misreading of HTS 9903.05.39. Git history also shows the stub was created by the immediate parent commit 4dfebb74e in the same PR (#1196) and drained in this intra-PR repair round, so no incorrect encoded meaning ever existed as a shipped state.

This output is deferred until it can be encoded with a semantic branch-specific" / "-      name without creating ambiguous sibling imports." PR #1196 carries zero reviews, review comments, or issue comments in the bundle, so the only "review blocker" evidence is the commit author's own summary line, which is self-reported. Residual uncertainty for the curator: if this corpus's policy is that a declared deferral leaving a cited provision unrepresented counts as a fidelity gap, then the first reader's kind (unrepresented_clause) is the right fallback and the verdict would be confirmed; I read the rubric's carve-out ("new outputs... or scope the module never claimed is not a defect") as controlling because `deferred_outputs` enumerates precisely the outputs never claimed. Secondary changes in the same diff are provenance-only: hyphen→en-dash in the summary heading range, `corpus_citation_path` → `corpus_citation_paths` (adding us/statute/hts/9903.05.38 for the complement branch), and removal of an empty `imports:` key.

modules.description_quote: the energy overlay judgment now carries the full U.S. note 2(j) scope: Canada-product gate, the 9903.01.11-.15 exception carve-outs, and accompanied-baggage exclusion
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix judgment fired on the bare article list alone (crude oil, natural gas, ... critical minerals), so it held for energy articles of any origin and ignored U.S. note 2(j)'s limitation to "the covered products of Canada" and its carve-outs for donations, informational materials, USMCA duty-free goods, potash, and personal-use goods in accompanied baggage.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus: `us/statute/hts/9903.01.13` is only the article list plus rates (477 chars, no origin or exception language), and `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-174` carries U.S. note 2(j) verbatim: "For the purposes of heading 9903.01.10, products of Canada, other than products described in headings 9903.01.11, 9903.01.12, 9903.01.13, 9903.01.14, 9903.01.15, 9903.01.16, 9903.76.01, 9903.76.02 and 9903.76.03 and other than products for personal use included in accompanied baggage of persons arriving in the United States, shall be subject to an additional 35% ad valorem rate of duty. For the purposes of heading 9903.01.13, the covered products of Canada shall be subject to an additional 10% ad valorem rate of duty." That confirms both the Canada-product gate and the accompanied-baggage exclusion. `wrong_entity_or_scope` is an equally defensible kind here: the single most consequential omission is the missing geography gate (`article_is_product_of_canada`), while four of the six added conjuncts are explicit carve-outs, which is why I chose unrepresented_clause; a judge that answers either should count. Caveat for the reviewer: headings 9903.01.11/.12/.14/.15 are textually exceptions to 9903.01.10, not to .13, so making .13 disjoint from them (and extending the accompanied-baggage exclusion to .13) is an encoder reading of the note's structure rather than literal .13 text - defensible but interpretive. The diff also widens `module.source_verification` from a single `corpus_citation_path` to seven `corpus_citation_paths`, rewrites the module summary, and retitles the rule's `source` string; those are provenance/mechanical and ride along with the formula fix. Companion test `fentanyl-energy-9903-01-13.test.yaml` changed in the same commit (new bare-fact inputs).

verdict.justification: The pre-fix `ieepa_component_rate` formula already encoded the 9903.01.11–.15 / 9903.01.02–.05 exception carve-outs and the potash branches faithfully; this commit deletes them from that rule and clones the identical pre-fix formula into a new `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions`, so no encoded meaning was corrected against the source — it was relocated. The commit's own rationale states the driver is engine plumbing, not a source disagreement: the five-input panel cannot demand a rule whose bare facts lower to required inputs. The companion-test diff settles it in the other direction: the excepted-entry cases now assert `ieepa_component_rate: 0.35` (was `0`) and their `us_tariff_total_ad_valorem_rate` / `us_tariff_duty` assertions were deleted, while `us_tariff_total_ad_valorem_rate` still sums the narrowed `ieepa_component_rate` — so the panel/total-duty path is strictly *less* faithful after the change. A change that makes the panel-demanded output diverge from the source for exception entries is not a fidelity correction, and `wrong_entity_or_scope` mislabels a deliberate, engine-forced narrowing as a scope fix.
verdict.quote:
+        The engine lowers every bare fact a demanded rule consumes to a
+        required input, so those facts cannot appear on the rate the
+        five-input panel demands: ieepa_component_rate therefore consumes
+        only facts derivable from the panel inputs
verdict.notes:
Refutation of the "unclear / wrong_entity_or_scope" reading, with the evidence the first reader did not cite.

1. Formula relocation, not correction. Pre (`426f1a72`:composition.yaml L783-798) `ieepa_component_rate` versions[0].formula contained `(if entry_is_fentanyl_canada_excepted: 0 / elif entry_is_energy_resource: ... / elif entry_is_potash_article: ...)`. Post, that exact block is byte-identical inside the new `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions` (post L845-858), and `ieepa_component_rate` keeps only `(if entry_is_energy_resource: ... else: fentanyl_canada_note_j_additional_duty_rate)` (post L785-788). Nothing was made to agree with the source that previously disagreed.

2. The change is a net fidelity *regression* on the demanded path. `us_tariff_total_ad_valorem_rate` (post L1083-1091) still sums `+ ieepa_component_rate`, the narrowed rule. The test diff for `composition.test.yaml` flips the four exception/potash cases from
   `-    ...#ieepa_component_rate: 0` / `-    ...#us_tariff_total_ad_valorem_rate: 0` / `-    ...#us_tariff_duty: 0`
   to
   `+    ...#ieepa_component_rate: 0.35` / `+    ...#ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions: 0`
   with the total-duty assertions dropped entirely. The commit rationale concedes this: "so no total-duty output is asserted for USMCA entries."

3. Driver is the harness, not the statute. The parent commit had added four bare-fact bindings (`entry_is_humanitarian_donation_article`, `entry_is_informational_material_article`, `entry_is_usmca_duty_free_entry`, `article_is_potash`) to all ~20 panel test cases; this commit reverts every one of them. That is the "five-input panel" revert the commit body advertises — an input-demand accommodation.

4. Not mechanical either: formulas changed and a rule was added, so the mechanical category (formulas/inputs/outputs/scope unchanged) does not apply. The proof-atom movement (9903.01.26/.27 staying on `ieepa_component_rate`; the .10/.01/.15/.05 exception atoms moving to the new rule) is pure provenance re-anchoring that follows the formula split.

5. Where the real fidelity defect in this commit lives: module_files[1], `us/policies/usitc/us-tariff-duty/overlays/ieepa/fentanyl-energy-9903-01-13.yaml` — the commit body's third clause ("the energy overlay judgment now carries the full U.S. note 2(j) scope: Canada-product gate, the 9903.01.11-.15 exception carve-outs, and accompanied-baggage exclusion") describes adding clauses the source states that the encoding lacked. If the corpus wants a keeper from 62833ba10c, that module index is the candidate (likely `unrepresented_clause`), not composition.yaml.

Residual uncertainty (why not 0.95): a reviewer could argue the pre-fix module over-claimed by exposing a panel-demanded rate that silently required undeclared entry facts, making the split a "scope of the output surface" correction. But that is an engine-contract complaint, not a disagreement with HTS chapter 99 text, and the defect taxonomy here is explicitly fidelity-to-source.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as an enhancement (the composition already gates energy on `origin_is_canada`, so the module's judgment might have been deliberately origin-agnostic "article scope"), but the module is a standalone overlay whose judgment feeds `fentanyl_energy_additional_duty` -> `fentanyl_energy_general_duty_rate`/`_special_duty_rate`, so pre-fix it asserted heading 9903.01.13's +10% on energy articles of any origin. The pinned release settles the source: U.S. note 2(j) says "For the purposes of heading 9903.01.13, the covered products of Canada shall be subject to an additional 10% ad valorem rate of duty," and the pre-fix summary ("Energy articles including crude oil ... are subject to the applicable subheading duty plus 10%") carried no Canada limitation — so the encoded meaning disagreed with the cited source and the fix adds the missing condition. The added `and article_is_product_of_canada` conjunct is a required clause the source states and the encoding omitted, which is unrepresented_clause; the change is a formula change, not metadata, so it is not mechanical.
verdict.quote: +          and article_is_product_of_canada
verdict.notes: Two caveats a reviewer should weigh. (1) Kind is arguably contestable: the decisive, source-mandated conjunct is an origin gate, so wrong_entity_or_scope (geography) is a live alternative; I kept unrepresented_clause because five of the six added conjuncts are exception carve-outs and the fix's mechanism is adding conditions the source states, not retargeting the entity (entity stays Asset, heading stays 9903.01.13). (2) The carve-outs the fix adds over-reach their cited source. Read in the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, corpus commit d9d6fba), note 2(j) attaches "other than products described in headings 9903.01.11, 9903.01.12, 9903.01.13, 9903.01.14, 9903.01.15 ... and other than products for personal use included in accompanied baggage" to heading 9903.01.10, not to 9903.01.13; the 9903.01.13 sentence says only "the covered products of Canada shall be subject to an additional 10% ad valorem rate of duty." Likewise the atom citing us/statute/hts/9903.01.10 ("Except for products described in headings 9903.01.11, 9903.01.12, 9903.01.13, 9903.01.14 or 9903.01.15") states that .13 is an exception FROM .10, i.e. the inverse of the relation the fix uses it for, and the "accompanied baggage" atom cites the same page-174 text that governs .10/.05. So `not article_is_humanitarian_donation / _informational_material / _usmca_duty_free_good / _potash / _personal_use_accompanied_baggage` is a defensible practical reading of the Canada fentanyl heading stack but is not stated for 9903.01.13 in the cited text — potentially a new untraceable_branch introduced by the fix. That does not disturb the verdict on the pre-fix defect (the Canada gate is squarely required), but if a reviewer wants the corpus text for the carve-out portion to be the defect evidence, the grounding is weaker than the commit message implies. The corpus record for us/statute/hts/9903.01.13 itself is only the article list ("Crude oil, natural gas, lease condensates, ... critical minerals, as defined by 30 U.S.C. 1606(a)(3)" plus the rate lines) — no Canada prefix — so the Canada gate is evidenced solely through note 2(j) on us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-174, which the fix correctly added to corpus_citation_paths.

modules.description_quote: re-encode the module so its scope predicate follows the current heading disjunction of note 19(a)(vii)(A) and note 19(m)(A) terms instead of requiring note 19(b) enumerated-heading coverage
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix applicability formula AND-ed two extra conjuncts onto the Russia-origin disjunction -- aluminum_article_under_note_19_a_vii_A and aluminum_article_provided_for_in_headings_or_subheadings_enumerated_in_note_19_b -- but heading 9903.85.67 conditions coverage only on 'the foregoing under the terms of note 19(a)(vii)(A) ... or note 19(m)(A) ..., as applicable per the date of entry', so the encoding invented a note 19(b) enumerated-heading requirement the cited text never imposes and dropped the note 19(m)(A) alternative, making covered Russian aluminum articles fail the gate and escape the +200% duty.
modules.triage_notes: Provision was read through the pinned corpus release (resolve_provision.py, us/statute/hts/9903.85.67): text confirms the disjunctive scope, the 19(a)(vii)(A) / 19(m)(A) date-dependent alternative, the Commerce-exclusion carve-out, and 'The duty provided in the applicable subheading + 200%'. No note 19(b) appears anywhere in the heading text, which is what makes the removed conjunct untraceable. The single fix bundles several changes: (a) the named scope-predicate defect (decisive); (b) the note 19(m)(A) alternative, previously absent, now folded into the '_under_applicable_note_19_terms' input names -- a reviewer could reasonably also tag that sub-defect unrepresented_clause or wrong_period_or_effective_date, since the heading makes the note choice depend on the date of entry and the module still has a single 2026-02-15 version with no window split; (c) entity changed Asset -> AluminumArticle on both derived rules, a genuine wrong_entity_or_scope element I judged secondary to the stated predicate defect; (d) the redundant rule section_232_aluminum_russia_total_duty_rate (applicable_subheading_duty_rate + additional) was deleted and the remaining derived rate rule renamed, so the module now exposes only the additional-duty rate and the composition adds the base -- an output-surface reduction, not a meaning error I could ground in the source; (e) rule renames plus proof-atom excerpt additions (the three scope excerpts and the exception excerpt) are provenance-only. This is an intra-PR repair: the module was added earlier in PR #1194 and no review bodies or review comments were captured in the bundle (reviews, review_comments, issue_comments all empty), so the commit message is the only statement of the finding; the PR body's unchecked 'sol cross-review before merge' box is consistent with the fix landing from that cross-review. Rate value 2.00 and effective_from 2026-02-15 were not changed.

verdict.justification: The diff does change encoded meaning in the way the commit message describes: the pre-fix applicability formula AND-ed `aluminum_article_under_note_19_a_vii_A` and `aluminum_article_provided_for_in_headings_or_subheadings_enumerated_in_note_19_b` onto the Russia-origin disjunction, and the fix removes both and re-grounds each limb on "applicable note 19 terms". But the first reader's rationale is factually wrong and must not be carried forward: note 19(a)(vii)(A) itself says heading 9903.85.67 covers Russia aluminum articles "as enumerated in subdivision (b) of this note", so the 19(b) rider was imposed by the cited heading through that cross-reference, not invented. The real defect is that note 19(a)(vii)(A) is expressly limited to goods entered "prior to 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on March 12, 2025", while the module's single version starts 2026-02-15, a window governed instead by note 19(m)(A) (which enumerates through subdivision (g) and puts no enumeration rider on the smelted-in-Russia or cast-in-Russia limbs) — so the conjuncts were grounded on the wrong provision, which untraceable_branch explicitly covers.

-          and aluminum_article_under_note_19_a_vii_A
-          and aluminum_article_provided_for_in_headings_or_subheadings_enumerated_in_note_19_b
verdict.notes: Source evidence (pinned release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, corpus commit d9d6fba0, provision line 1560 + chapter-99 pages 247/248/249/251): heading 9903.85.67 reads "the foregoing under the terms of note 19(a)(vii)(A) to this subchapter, or note 19(m)(A) to this subchapter, as applicable per the date of entry for consumption or withdrawal from warehouse for consumption"; note 19(a)(vii)(A) = entries "prior to ... March 12, 2025", "as enumerated in subdivision (b) of this note"; note 19(m)(A) = entries "on or after ... March 12, 2025", "as enumerated in subdivision (g) of this note". Subdivisions (b) and (g) list the same chapter-76 article set (7601, 7604, 7605, 7606, 7607, 7608/7609, 7616.99.51), so the practical scope error is not the (b)-vs-(g) list but (1) requiring a subdivision that cannot apply to any entry in the module's own 2026-02-15+ window (the overlay would fail closed) and (2) attaching an enumeration requirement to the smelted/cast limbs that 19(m)(A) does not impose on them. Competing kinds a reviewer should consider: wrong_period_or_effective_date ("timeless encoding of superseded text" fits the root cause exactly, though the diff changes no effective_from/effective_to or version window), and unrepresented_clause (the omitted "or note 19(m)(A) ..., as applicable per the date of entry" limb, which the fix restores only implicitly by renaming inputs to *_under_applicable_note_19_terms rather than as an explicit clause). Caveat on the fix itself: the post state still carries one timeless version effective_from 2026-02-15 and delegates the date-of-entry selection entirely to input semantics, so the date logic is not visible in the formula. Ancillary changes in the same module diff, outside the quoted reason: all three rules renamed; entity changed Asset -> AluminumArticle; the `section_232_aluminum_russia_total_duty_rate` rule (applicable_subheading_duty_rate + additional rate) was dropped, an output-surface removal that a reviewer may want scored separately. This is an intra-PR review fix (PR #1194, same PR that added the module), so the defect never shipped to main on its own.

item.screen_reason: PR #1143 "Restores the SE leg deliberately withheld from #1003": merged additional Medicare tax pipeline lacked the §1401(b)(2) self-employment leg; a deliberate deferral rather than an error, flagged for the diff stage.

triage.commit_summary: The commit restores the self-employment leg of the additional Medicare tax pipeline: it drops the `federal_self_employment_income == 0` fail-closed gate from the domain-validity Judgment, re-grounds the wage-coordination helper and the reduced threshold on 26 CFR 1.1401-1(d)(2)(i) (adding that citation path to the module's corpus_citation_paths and widening those two rules from a 2026-only window to effective_from 2013-01-01), and deletes the two waivers that had declared the coordination helper and the public SE-leg output deferred. The stated reason is that the operative coordination authority (the regulation, whose text the statute's §1401(b)(2)(B) scrivener's error had made unusable) is now in the pinned corpus chain, so a deferral deliberately taken in the earlier PR #1003 could be lifted; downstream rate, threshold, base, and combined formulas are unchanged.

modules.description_quote: Restores the SE leg deliberately withheld from #1003, now that the operative coordination authority is in the pinned corpus chain (axiom-corpus#523 → pin PR #1140).
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix module published $0 for the §1401(b)(2) self-employment leg (and $0 for the combined tax) for any tax unit with positive self-employment income, which disagrees with 26 USC 1401(b)(2) and 26 CFR 1.1401-1(d)(2)(i), but the module declared that restriction openly (waivers, domain-validity Judgment, summary) as a deliberate deferral rather than mis-reading the source.
modules.triage_notes: Screen flag is correct: this is a documented deliberate deferral being lifted, not an encoder misreading. Pre-fix evidence that the gap was declared, not accidental: (a) two waiver entries named `wages_taken_into_account_for_additional_medicare_tax` and `federal_additional_medicare_self_employment_tax` as fail-closed pending axiom-corpus#514; (b) the module summary said the combined surface is 'valid only for tax units whose imported federal self-employment income is zero'; (c) a public `additional_medicare_tax_pipeline_self_employment_domain_is_valid` Judgment exposed the invalid domain. Substantive changes in this diff: domain gate loses `and federal_self_employment_income == 0`; `wages_taken_into_account_for_additional_medicare_tax` goes from guarded (wages if valid else 0) to plain `wages` with effective_from 2026-01-01 -> 2013-01-01 and effective_to dropped; `pipeline_reduced_additional_medicare_self_employment_threshold` keeps its max(0, threshold - wages) formula but its proof atom changes from a local import to a formula atom grounded on us/regulation/26/1/1401-1/d/2/i, same window widening. Rate, filing-status thresholds, tax base, SE-leg and combined formulas are byte-identical pre/post; the SE-leg and combined public outputs stay 2026-only. I read the provision: resolve_provision could not isolate us/regulation/26/1/1401-1/d/2/i (missing structural marker in the resolvable releases), but the parent us/regulation/26/1/1401-1 resolved and contains the quoted sentence verbatim ('the applicable threshold specified under section 1401(b)(2)(A) is reduced (but not below zero) by the amount of wages (as defined in section 3121(a)) taken into account in determining Additional Medicare Tax under section 3101(b)(2)'), plus Example 3/4 confirming the wage-reduced threshold, so the post-fix encoding matches the source. The only reason to keep this at 'unclear' rather than 'not a defect' is that the pre-fix combined output `federal_additional_medicare_tax` returned 0 (dropping even the independently valid wage leg) for SE taxpayers, which a fidelity judge could read as an unrepresented §1401(b)(2)/1.1401-1(d)(2)(i) clause; recommend pruning from a real-defect corpus. Companion test file `additional_medicare_tax_pipeline.test.yaml` also changed (adds the $346.725 SE-leg case per the PR body). PR #1143 had no reviews or review comments; the sole issue comment is a CI/oracle-coverage-gate diagnosis unrelated to encoded meaning, and the PR depended on pin-only PR #1140.

verdict.justification: Every piece of SE machinery the fix "adds" (0.9% rate, filing-status thresholds, the reduced-threshold max(0, ...) formula, the base, the leg, the combined sum) already existed verbatim in the pre-fix module; the only encoded-meaning change is dropping the `and federal_self_employment_income == 0` conjunct from the domain-validity Judgment, un-gating the wages helper, and re-grounding the coordination proof atoms on 26 CFR 1.1401-1(d)(2)(i) — i.e. lifting a guard the module had declared in machine-readable `deferred_outputs` waivers naming exactly the two withheld outputs, plus the summary and a consumer-facing Judgment. I verified the deferral's cause was a genuine corpus gap, not a misreading: at commit a0a2ec5940's toolchain corpus ref (bf97b17b, release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union) the resolver returns "No active corpus source found for 'us/regulation/26/1/1401-1/d/2/i'" for that release and every earlier one, the reg only appears in a later ingest file named `2026-07-24-1401-coordination-repair-title-26-part-1.jsonl`, and the pinned statute row is byte-faithful to the enacted scrivener's error ("reduced ... by the amount of wages taken into account in determining the tax imposed under section 3121(b)(2)"), so under `proof_validation: required` there was no operative authority to encode the reduction from. Nothing in the commit subject, PR title, PR body, or the maintainer comment uses error/mistake/correction language — the PR says "deliberately withheld" and "Restores", and the enabling event is a dependency (axiom-corpus#523 → pin PR #1140), which is coverage the module expressly disclaimed rather than encoded meaning that disagreed with its cited source.
verdict.quote:
-    - output: us:policies/income_tax/additional_medicare_tax_pipeline#federal_additional_medicare_self_employment_tax
-      reason: |-
-        A positive section 1401(b)(2) tax requires the unsupported
-        section 1401(b)(2)(B) wage coordination. The current pinned record
-        incorrectly names section 3121(b)(2) instead of section 3101(b)(2);
-        axiom-corpus#514 and its pending targeted re-ingest track the repair.
-        The stable public output therefore fails closed to zero until the
-        repaired corpus release is pinned.
verdict.notes: Dissent a reviewer should weigh before dropping this case. (1) The strongest argument for keeping it: the pre-fix module did not merely omit the SE leg — it published `federal_additional_medicare_self_employment_tax` and the combined `federal_additional_medicare_tax` as stable public outputs and the companion tests ENFORCED $0 for positive-SE tax units. The fix flips those enforced expectations: `federal_additional_medicare_tax: '0'` → `'346.725'` (138,525 SE income, 100,000 wages), `'0'` → `'762.3'`, `'0'` → `'243.45'`. A consumer who read the public output without checking the Judgment got a number the law contradicts, so "published wrong meaning" is defensible. If a reviewer overrides me, `unrepresented_clause` is the right kind (the 1401(b)(2)(B)/1.1401-1(d)(2)(i) wage-coordination reduction was present but inert), not `wrong_period_or_effective_date`. (2) Against keeping it, and why I landed where I did: the restriction was declared three ways (deferred_outputs waivers on exactly those two outputs, the summary "the public self-employment leg is a fail-closed zero and the combined surface is valid only for tax units whose imported federal self-employment income is zero", and the domain-validity Judgment the consumer contract requires checking), and the removed waiver entries are the bulk of the diff's deletions. This is a declared-deferral lift gated on a dependency, so admitting it would teach a verifier that expanding openly-deferred coverage is an encoding defect. (3) Source verification performed: 26 USC 1401 resolved at the fix commit's pin (fix_time_corpus_match: same_body) confirms the enacted "section 3121(b)(2)" text; 26 CFR 1.1401-1 read from us-rulespec-2026-08-09-cutover-surface-union matches the fix's proof excerpt verbatim, including the Example 3 arithmetic the new test case reproduces. (4) One genuine sub-correction that is metadata only, not formula: the pre-fix rationale asserted the corpus record was "corrupted" pending re-ingest under axiom-corpus#514, which was itself wrong — the enacted statute really says 3121(b)(2); the post-fix rationale corrects this to "byte-faithful ... retains its enacted section 3121(b)(2) scrivener's error and is documentary only, never operative proof". That is a provenance/metadata fix, mechanical under the rubric.
