verdict.justification: Under rename detection the "added" file is `pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml` renamed (R054): every rate (0.02/0.04/0.05), every ceiling (500/3000/1000/6000), the zero floor, the joint/nonjoint branch, the TaxUnit entity, the Year period, both inputs, and the 2026-01-01/2026-12-31 window are carried over verbatim under new identifiers, and the retained public formula is byte-for-byte the old `al_pit_pilot_schedule_tax`. The one rule dropped, `al_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability`, was `max(0, al_pit_pilot_schedule_tax)` and its old companion test asserts exactly the same nine values as the schedule rule (0, 10, 10.04, 110, 110.05, 20, 20.04, 220, 220.05), so no input yields a different number before or after and no other module referenced it. What actually changed is naming, `private: true` on seven rules, rewritten summary/rationale, and consolidation of a duplicate statute module — the signed retire manifest's own reason is structural ("explicit typed inputs, private implementation rules, and one public result"). The scope reading is still defensible, since § 40-18-5 says only "The tax levied and imposed by Section 40-18-2 shall be computed as follows" and publishing a Money output named `..._income_tax_liability` from it outruns the section, but that overclaim lives in an identifier string and a label, which this taxonomy treats as a rename; strict "mechanical" also fails because the published output set did shrink, so the evidence does not settle it.
verdict.quote: - replace the broad Alabama pilot/statute overlap with one canonical tax-year-2026 section 40-18-5 schedule-before-credits module
verdict.notes: Bundle mis-labels module_files[1] as "added"; `git show --name-status -M 1f9e440d5a` reports `R054 us-al/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml -> us-al/policies/income_tax/2026_section_40_18_5_schedule_before_credits.yaml`, so read it as a rename+edit, not a new module. The deleted rule in full: `- name: al_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` / `source: Ala. Code § 40-18-5, income tax before nonrefundable credits` / `formula: max(0, al_pit_pilot_schedule_tax)` — note its own `source:` caption already bounded it to "before nonrefundable credits", so only the identifier says "liability". Pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, provision sha256 fc4478ba…) confirms § 40-18-5 contains only the lead-in plus the two schedules, and that the pre-fix rates/ceilings already matched it exactly — i.e. nothing numeric was wrong against the source. Both retired modules sat in `known-validation-gaps.yaml` as pending `validate_failures` with `passed: false`, and the commit clears those waivers, which supports a hygiene/dedup motive alongside the scope-narrowing one. New test file adds boundary cases (9.98, 109.96, 19.98, 219.96, fractional 110.0005/220.0005) but repeats the old values where they overlap — added coverage, not corrected behavior. A reviewer deciding this case is really deciding one policy question: does deleting a published output whose name overclaimed, with zero change to any computed value, count as fidelity (output surface) or as a rename/metadata change? If fidelity, `wrong_entity_or_scope` is the right kind; `untraceable_branch` fits worse because the removed rule's value was fully grounded in the cited section. Separately, module index 2 (deleted `us-al/statutes/40-18-5.yaml`) encoded the same schedule with timeless `effective_from: '0001-01-01'` versions — if any case in this corpus targets that file, it is a stronger fidelity candidate (wrong_period_or_effective_date) than this one.

verdict.justification: Module 2 is a whole-file retirement of a duplicate encoding, not a date correction: resolving `us-al/statute/40-18-5` through the pinned release shows the deleted module's 2/4/5 percent rates and $500/$3,000/$1,000/$6,000 ceilings, its inclusive "not in excess of" boundaries, and its two filing-status branches all match the source verbatim, and its own companion tests compute the schedule correctly (2500 -> 90, 4000 -> 160, joint 5000 -> 180). The 2026 window that the reader treats as the correction was not authored by this commit — the surviving file is a rename of `pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml`, which already carried `effective_from: '2026-01-01' / effective_to: '2026-12-31'` at the parent commit — and the source text contains no effective-date clause at all, only an acts credit line, so there is no source basis for calling `'0001-01-01'` a disagreement with the cited text. The kind's "timeless encoding of superseded text" case also does not apply: the retired module encoded the current 2026-07-13 expression, not superseded text. The signed retirement record gives the actual reason as structural — "Replaced by the canonical tax-year-2026 Alabama Code section 40-18-5 schedule-before-credits module with explicit typed inputs, private implementation rules, and one public result."
verdict.quote: replace the broad Alabama pilot/statute overlap with one canonical tax-year-2026 section 40-18-5 schedule-before-credits module
verdict.notes: Evidence trail for a reviewer: (1) `git show 1f9e440d5a --stat -M` shows `us-al/policies/income_tax/{pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml => 2026_section_40_18_5_schedule_before_credits.yaml}`, i.e. the canonical module is the pre-existing pilot renamed; `us-al/statutes/40-18-5.yaml` is the second, redundant encoding of the same provision and is deleted outright. (2) The pilot at parent `4d4a199705` already had 2026-bounded versions and the same min/max bracket arithmetic, so repo-level computed meaning for 2026 is unchanged by the deletion. (3) `.axiom/encoding-manifests/us-al/statutes/40-18-5.json` records `"tool": "axiom-encode retire"` with the reason quoted in the justification — typed inputs / private rules / one public result, nothing about dates. (4) Both the retired statute module and the pilot were rows in `known-validation-gaps.yaml` `validate_failures` (removed by this commit); the retired module declared no `inputs:` block and referenced `taxable_income` / `married_persons_filing_joint_return`, which its test file supplied as module-scoped `#input.` symbols — an implicit-input/structural problem, not a wrong entity binding (no repo-wide `taxable_income` rule binds them). (5) Genuine residue, offered as the strongest counter to my verdict: `effective_from: '0001-01-01'` with no `effective_to` on all 15 rules is an over-broad claim given the section's amendment credits (Acts 1935/1982, Act 98-502), and the retirement narrows it. But nothing in the commit, PR body, manifest, or comments treats that as the reason, no corrected date is derived from the source here, and the retired schedule was correct for every year its tests exercised — so this reads as structural deduplication rather than a fidelity correction. If the corpus curator wants a bucket for "overbroad/unsourced version window removed as a side effect of consolidation", that would be a new kind, not wrong_period_or_effective_date as defined.

The signed retirement manifests give the reason as "the pilot name and broader resident household core overstated the certified source boundary", so this is a scope/output-surface correction: the arithmetic and all eight fixture amounts are unchanged from the retired pilot, while the claimed surface narrows to annual § 48-7-20 tax before nonrefundable credits with taxable-income construction, filing mechanics, deductions, exemptions, credits, Form 500 ordering, and estimated tax made explicit deferred boundaries.

Numerically it is identical to the retired pilot: same imported rate atom (sha256:3b14bace271098396b2e7f91054f8f5453fdd291c7ba60a776f47b1f55d5fd02 for us-ga:statutes/48/48-7-20#individual_income_tax_rate), same effective window 2026-01-01..2026-12-31, and the six positive companion fixtures reproduce the pilot's exact expected values (748.5, 2245.5, 6736.5, 1497, 4491, 13473). Provision read: resolve_provision.py returned us-ga/statute/48/48-7-20 at expression_date 2022-11-01 (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union); that text has the pre-flat graduated tables and contains neither '(a.1)' nor '4.99 percent' nor '5.39 percent', and § 48-7-20(a) defines Georgia taxable net income only 'as defined in Code Section 48-7-27' — so the 4.99% rate legitimately comes from the imported 48-7-20 rate module plus the 2026 HB 463 session law, and § 48-7-20 itself constructs no taxable income. Because this index is an addition rather than a correction of its own prior meaning, a fidelity judge shown only this file has nothing to flag; a reviewer may prefer to keep only indices 1 and 2 as the benchmark entries.

modules.description_quote: replace the retired Georgia pilot and over-broad resident-core modules with one canonical tax-year-2026 annual O.C.G.A. § 48-7-20 tax-before-nonrefundable-credits surface
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The module published a tax-year-2026 after-credit Georgia income-tax surface (filing-status standard deduction selection, dependent exemptions, NOL, low-income credit bands/units, child-and-dependent-care credit) whose scope exceeded what the pinned official sources certify for 2026 — the corpus has no TY2026 Form 500/IT-511 package and the credit-schedule mechanics were taken from the 2025 IT-511 worksheet — so its terminal output claimed a certified boundary the cited authorities do not establish.
modules.triage_notes: Pure deletion (601 lines) plus deletion of its 353-line companion test; the signed retirement manifest at .axiom/encoding-manifests/us-ga/policies/income_tax/2026_resident_household_core.json states the reason verbatim as 'Superseded by one narrow canonical tax-year-2026 annual O.C.G.A. 48-7-20 tax-before-nonrefundable-credits surface; the pilot name and broader resident household core overstated the certified source boundary.' (I did not use that as description_quote because the manifest is not one of the allowed quote sources; the PR-body quote carries the same 'over-broad' finding, and the maintainer's review comment adds 'scope is truthfully limited to TY2026 O.C.G.A. §48-7-20 tax on caller-completed Georgia taxable net income at 4.99%, before nonrefundable credits—not final Form 500 liability or estimated tax'.) Concrete source-relative weaknesses a fidelity judge could detect in the pre-fix file: the 2026 low-income-credit exemption-unit and band structure is grounded on us-ga/form/it-511/2025/document-1 (a 2025 form) — arguably wrong_period_or_effective_date; `ga_2026_resident_low_income_last_band_index` is a synthesized parameter ('4') with only a table-row proof, not a statutory value — arguably untraceable_branch; and `ga_2026_resident_income_before_nol` floors at zero before the NOL deduction, which § 48-7-27 does not state. Caveat for the reviewer: the module was internally candid about its boundaries (summary and deferred_outputs both disclaim final liability), so the retirement is a certification-boundary judgment by the maintainers rather than a demonstrated disagreement with one specific clause; that is why confidence is mid-range. The retirement also removes genuinely encoded 48-7-27 / 48-7-26 / 48-7A-3 / 48-7-29.10 coverage, i.e. coverage loss rather than coverage gain.

modules.description_quote: replace the retired Georgia pilot and over-broad resident-core modules with one canonical tax-year-2026 annual O.C.G.A. § 48-7-20 tax-before-nonrefundable-credits surface
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The module published its § 48-7-20 rate computation as `ga_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` — an 'income tax liability' output that is only tax before nonrefundable credits (and before the withholding/estimated-payment credits § 48-7-20(c) allows) — and published a second output `ga_pit_pilot_taxable_income` that floors supplied income at zero under § 48-7-20 authority, although § 48-7-20(a) defines Georgia taxable net income only by reference to § 48-7-27 and states no floor.
modules.triage_notes: Pure deletion (68 lines) plus its 89-line companion test; same retirement manifest reason string as index 1, which specifically names 'the pilot name ... overstated the certified source boundary'. Verified against the pinned corpus that § 48-7-20(a) says Georgia taxable net income is 'as defined in Code Section 48-7-27', so the pilot's max(0, ga_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income) rule with a § 48-7-20 imposition-sentence proof atom is grounded on the wrong provision — an alternative defect_kind of untraceable_branch is defensible for that rule; I chose wrong_entity_or_scope because the maintainers' stated reason is the overstated name/boundary. Important caveat: the replacement (index 0) computes identical amounts for every fixture, so nothing numeric, no threshold, and no effective date changed — the pre-fix file is wrong only in its declared output surface, and the pilot's own `source:` field already said 'before nonrefundable credits', which weakens the case that the pre-fix meaning was detectably wrong from the source text alone. Same pattern as index 1 (both retired by one `axiom-encode retire` operation with one shared reason).

verdict.justification: This file is `new file mode 100644` / `--- /dev/null`, so it has no pre-fix encoded meaning that could disagree with the source, and its one public output is arithmetically identical to the module it replaces: the retired pilot computed `max(0, ga_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income)` then `ga_pit_pilot_taxable_income * individual_income_tax_rate`, while the added module computes `x * individual_income_tax_rate` when `x >= 0` and `0` otherwise — same imported rate, the same import hash `sha256:3b14bace271098396b2e7f91054f8f5453fdd291c7ba60a776f47b1f55d5fd02`, and the same `2026-01-01`/`2026-12-31` window, so the advertised "fail closed at the negative-input boundary" changes no computed value. Nor does the source support a narrowing of entity/population here: O.C.G.A. § 48-7-20(a) as resolved through the pinned release imposes the tax on "every resident of this state" *and* "every nonresident", so the unrestricted TaxUnit surface is not a correction of a wrong entity. Whatever fidelity correction this commit records lives in the two deletions — the retirement manifest's own stated reason is that "the pilot name and broader resident household core overstated the certified source boundary" — not in this added replacement file, which is the narrowed surface rather than a corrected encoding.
verdict.quote:
+        formula: |-
+          if ga_pit_2026_annual_input_is_nonnegative:
+            ga_pit_2026_completed_georgia_taxable_net_income
+            * individual_income_tax_rate
+          else:
+            0
verdict.notes: Refutes both the kind and the case placement, not the existence of a correction in the commit. (1) Kind: `wrong_entity_or_scope` is not supported for this file — § 48-7-20(a) covers residents and nonresidents alike, so dropping the retired module's full-year-resident limitation is a broadening consistent with the source, not a corrected entity scope. (2) Placement: if the corpus wants a defect record from commit 6ff6a4a8b3, it belongs on module index 1 (`2026_resident_household_core.yaml`, deleted, 601 lines) — that module built AGI, standard deduction, dependent exemption, NOL, low-income credit and care credit from caller boundaries the pinned corpus could not certify (no TY2026 Form 500/IT-511), which reads as `untraceable_branch` or `wrong_entity_or_scope` on the *deleted* file. (3) A secondary, weaker candidate is module index 2: the retired pilot published `ga_pit_pilot_taxable_income` with `source: O.C.G.A. § 48-7-20, supplied completed-return Georgia taxable net income floored at zero`, but § 48-7-20(a) defines Georgia taxable net income only by reference ("as defined in Code Section 48-7-27"); the replacement demotes that to a `private: true` guard and a declared caller input described "under O.C.G.A. § 48-7-27". That is a grounding fix (`untraceable_branch`, wrong provision), and it is realized by the deletion plus the re-declaration — it is the one reading under which a reviewer could keep this pair, and it is why I did not push confidence higher. (4) Unrelated observation for the corpus, not this case: the pinned-release text for `us-ga/statute/48/48-7-20` is the pre-2024 graduated-table version (1%–5.75%, `expression_date 2022-11-01`, "This version is effective until January 1, 2024"); the flat 4.99% enters only through the imported `us-ga:statutes/48/48-7-20#individual_income_tax_rate` module and the hb463 session law, so any downstream check of the rate must go through the import, not this provision record.

verdict.justification: The first reader's reading — that the module's "terminal output claimed a certified boundary the cited authorities do not establish" — is contradicted by the deleted file itself, which names its terminal rule ga_2026_resident_income_tax_after_household_core_credits, states in its own summary that "The result is not complete annual liability", records in its upstream_source_check rationale that "Georgia DOR has not published the tax-year-2026 Form 500 and IT-511 annual-return package in the pinned official corpus", and carries a deferred_outputs entry for the final-before-payments surface. Reading the pinned sources, every substantive branch it encoded checks out: the 48-7A-3 schedule bands (Under $6,000 / 6,000–7,999 / 8,000–9,999 / 10,000–14,999 / 15,000–19,999), the dependency, food-stamp (e) and incarceration (e.1) bars, the (a)(2) married-separate joint-equivalent rule, the (c) liability cap and (d) timeliness waiver, and HB 463's 4.99 percent rate, $30,000/$15,000 standard deductions and $5,000 dependent exemption. The fix therefore corrects no encoded meaning: it deletes 17 rules wholesale and replaces them with rate × caller-supplied taxable net income, and the retirement manifest's stated reason ("overstated the certified source boundary") is a provenance/certification policy about what the pinned corpus package licenses, not a demonstrated disagreement with any cited provision's text. Entity, population (full-year GA residents under 48-7-20), filing-status handling and the 2026 period window were all correct both before and after, so wrong_entity_or_scope has no supporting diff line.
verdict.quote:
-    The result is not complete annual liability. Other-state, eligible-itemizer,
-    IND-CR, Schedule 2, and refundable Schedule 2B credits remain outside this
-    source-certified core pending the official 2026 Form 500/IT-511 package and
-    separate encoding of their eligibility and amount surfaces. The pipeline is
-    limited to full-year resident individual returns and tax year 2026.
verdict.notes:
Evidence trail: module 1 is a pure deletion (601 → 0 lines); module 0 is a new 112-line surface; module 2 (the pilot) is also deleted. The encoding manifest is an `axiom-encode retire` record whose reason is "Superseded by one narrow canonical tax-year-2026 annual O.C.G.A. 48-7-20 tax-before-nonrefundable-credits surface; the pilot name and broader resident household core overstated the certified source boundary." — a scope/certification statement, not a source-disagreement claim. The PR's own review comment says the outcome was "no actionable findings" and that scope is "truthfully limited", i.e. no reviewer identified a wrong encoded meaning.

If a reviewer nonetheless wants to keep this as fidelity, the kind should be untraceable_branch, not wrong_entity_or_scope: the only grounding weakness I could find is that the low-income-credit unit machinery (ga_2026_resident_low_income_exemption_units, ga_2026_resident_low_income_age_units) is grounded on us-ga/form/it-511/2025/document-1 — a TY2025 worksheet — while the resolved statute says "multiplied by the number of dependents which the taxpayer is entitled to claim. Each taxpayer 65 years of age or over may claim double the tax credit." The module adds age units instead of doubling (single 65+ with 2 children: 3 exemption + 1 age = 4 units, where literal doubling gives 6). That divergence is real but (a) it is DOR's own official worksheet reading, authorized by 48-7A-3(f), (b) it is never mentioned in the commit, PR body, or review, and (c) the fix removes rather than re-grounds it, so it cannot be scored as the corrected defect. Not a wrong_period case either: the effective windows are 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31 and the cited codified sections are in force for 2026.

I also checked HB 463 for a missing-clause angle: it adds 48-7-27(a)(16) qualified overtime up to $1,750 and (a)(17) cash tips up to $1,750 for tax years beginning on or after 2026-01-01, and the replacement module's rationale calls out "overtime or tip exclusions". But the deleted module took ga_2026_resident_completed_georgia_subtractions as a caller boundary that absorbs Schedule 1 subtractions, so it did not misencode those exclusions — no unrepresented_clause either. Net: this entry is a scope retirement/consolidation, best pruned from a corpus of real fidelity defects.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as a mechanical rename/retirement and failed: the deleted module published two public Money outputs and the replacement publishes one while demoting the nonnegativity to a `private: true` Judgment, so the published output set and scope changed, not just names. Reading O.C.G.A. § 48-7-20 through the pinned release confirms both overclaims the fix removes: subsection (a) defines the base "as defined in Code Section 48-7-27" and states no floor, yet the module published `ga_pit_pilot_taxable_income` as `max(0, ga_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income)` sourced to § 48-7-20 "floored at zero"; and subsection (c) allows withholding and estimated payments "as a credit against the tax imposed by this Code section," so a bare rate×base figure named `ga_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` misstates the section's own liability concept. The commit's signed retirement manifest says so in its own words — the pilot name "overstated the certified source boundary" — which is a published-output-surface error, i.e. wrong_entity_or_scope, rather than untraceable_branch, since the fix retains the nonnegativity semantics and re-grounds it on the identical § 48-7-20 excerpt instead of removing an unfounded branch.
verdict.quote: -  - name: ga_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability
verdict.notes: Second decisive diff line (verbatim, same deleted module): "-    source: O.C.G.A. § 48-7-20, supplied completed-return Georgia taxable net income floored at zero" on the removed `ga_pit_pilot_taxable_income` output, whose formula was "-          max(0, ga_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income)". Surviving caveat a reviewer should weigh: the arithmetic is unchanged — `max(0,x) * rate` equals the new `if x >= 0: x * rate else: 0` for every input, and all 8 old fixtures would produce identical tax values, so a reviewer who weights only numeric behavior could push this toward mechanical; the substantive anchor is the dropped public `ga_pit_pilot_taxable_income` Money output, which asserted "Georgia taxable net income = max(0, supplied)" on § 48-7-20 authority even though § 48-7-20(a) defers the definition to § 48-7-27. Note the PR-body quote used by the first reader is weak support for THIS file: "over-broad" attaches to the resident-core module (index 1), while the pilot is described only as "retired." The stronger, file-specific evidence is the signed retirement manifest at .axiom/encoding-manifests/us-ga/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.json, reason field: "Superseded by one narrow canonical tax-year-2026 annual O.C.G.A. 48-7-20 tax-before-nonrefundable-credits surface; the pilot name and broader resident household core overstated the certified source boundary." (That file is part of the same commit but outside the module diff, so it is cited here rather than as the quote.) Runner-up kind is untraceable_branch (zero floor grounded on § 48-7-20 rather than § 48-7-27); I rejected it because the fix preserves the nonnegativity and reuses the same § 48-7-20 excerpt as a condition atom. Provision resolution artifact worth knowing: the pinned corpus record for us-ga/statute/48/48-7-20 (expression_date 2022-11-01, fallback_index 0) is the pre-2024 graduated-table version, so subsection "(a.1)" cited by both modules is not in the resolved body; the 4.99% rate comes from the imported module plus us-ga/statute/session-laws/2026/hb463/document-1. That does not affect this verdict but would matter to anyone auditing the rate grounding. Also note the deleted module declared no `inputs:` block while referencing `ga_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income` (tests address it as `#input.ga_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income`); the replacement declares it explicitly. That is a separate hygiene improvement, not the defect classified here.

triage.commit_summary: The commit retires the Kentucky pilot module `us-ky/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml` with a signed tombstone manifest and re-lands it (git records a 63% rename) as one canonically named module, `2026_krs_141_020_schedule_before_credits.yaml`, whose three rules and input are renamed to KRS 141.020 / TY2026 names, whose summary and source-verification rationale are rewritten to disclaim any final-return or after-credits liability claim, and whose caller-supplied net-income boundary rule is now marked `private: true` so a single public schedule-before-credits output remains. No rate, formula, effective date, entity, period, unit, or companion-test expectation changed: both versions encode 0.035 for 2026-01-01..2026-12-31, `max(0, <caller net income>)`, and boundary × rate, and the ledger/index/waiver files were regenerated to follow the rename.

modules.description_quote: The module accepts completed Kentucky net income, applies the 3.5% statutory rate, and exposes one public schedule-before-credits output.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix module (named pilot_liability_pipeline, rules ky_pit_pilot_*) published the caller-supplied, zero-floored pass-through as a public output called 'net income' and named itself a liability pipeline, claiming a KRS 141.020 net-income/liability surface it never computes (it constructs no additions, subtractions, deductions, exemptions, or credits), while every computed value it produced already matched the statute.
modules.triage_notes: Read the full rename-aware diff (git shows R063 pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml -> 2026_krs_141_020_schedule_before_credits.yaml; the bundle presents it as 'added' because renames were not detected, so pre_lines is 0 and the 000.diff shows only the post file). Entire semantic delta: (a) rule/input/file renames ky_pit_pilot_* -> ky_pit_2026_krs_141_020_*, (b) `metadata.private: true` added to the net-income boundary rule, shrinking the public output set from two to one, (c) rewritten module summary and upstream_source_check rationale (drops the Form 740-ES $3,360 discussion, adds 'does not claim a complete annual return, tax after credits, or final liability'), (d) one `source:` string reworded. Unchanged: rate formula '0.035', boundary formula max(0, input), schedule formula boundary * rate, effective_from 2026-01-01 / effective_to 2026-12-31 on all three versions, entity TaxUnit, period Year, unit USD, dtypes, proof-atom excerpts and citation paths. The deleted and re-added companion test has byte-different names/anchors but numerically identical expectations (-100 -> 0; 3360 -> 117.6; 3360.01 -> 117.60035; 12345.67 -> 432.09845), so no arithmetic claim moved. Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus release: KRS 141.020(2)(f) reads 'For taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026, the tax shall be three and one-half percent (3.5%) of net income' and (1) 'applying the rates in subsection (2) of this section to net income and subtracting allowable tax credits' -- both pre- and post-fix encodings agree with this, so no amount, boundary, clause, date, or logic defect exists. The only argument for fidelity is the output-surface/scope narrowing, which the task rubric's mirror case ('a change that merely adds new outputs, precision, or scope the module never claimed is not a defect') suggests should not count; I kept it as unclear per the 'a reviewer prunes' instruction, but a reviewer will most likely reclassify this to mechanical (rename + module metadata + summaries). Contrary evidence for fidelity: the PR's own independent review said 'All RuleSpec/legal/arithmetic/manifests/source-hold checks were otherwise clean', and the PR's only blocking finding was oracle-comparator mapping in axiom-oracles/axiom-encode (legacy `ky_income_tax_before_refundable_credits` vs `ky_income_tax_before_non_refundable_credits_unit`), not encoding fidelity; the tombstone manifest reason is 'Replace the legacy Kentucky pilot with one canonical tax-year-2026 KRS 141.020 schedule-before-credits module'. Commit 4d10a73d is an intermediate head of PR #1117 (final merged head 5d5c8ed4); the module YAML was never touched again after this commit, only its test file (347b37c06, 'Test Kentucky rate oracle mapping', which added the 0.035 rate assertion to the 10 fixtures). Chunk covers the only module file in the commit; other changed files are manifests, .axiom index/fingerprints, known-validation-gaps.yaml, oracle-coverage-pending.yaml, and the two test files.

verdict.justification: Rendered with -M the change is a 63%-similarity rename of pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml, and the only line in it that touches encoded meaning is `+      private: true` on the net-income boundary rule: the rate (0.035), both formulas, the entity/dtype/period/unit, the 2026-01-01/2026-12-31 windows, the input, and every proof atom and excerpt are byte-identical, and all ten companion fixtures assert the same numbers before and after (0.01 -> 0.00035, 3360 -> 117.6, 100000 -> 3500). Against KRS 141.020 itself there is nothing to correct — the statute supplies only "applying the rates in subsection (2) ... to net income" and "(f) For taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026, the tax shall be three and one-half percent (3.5%) of net income", both already encoded correctly pre-fix, and the first reader concedes "every computed value it produced already matched the statute." The "named itself a liability pipeline" reading is refuted by the pre-fix module text, which already disclaimed liability in the same words the post-fix text uses, and `pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml` was a generic scaffold filename shared by ~20 states (us-al, us-az, us-ca, us-ct ... in the same fingerprint ledger), so retiring it is a rename, which the rubric classes as mechanical. The private flag is a cross-engine comparability disposition, not a source repair: the merged mapping records it as `mapping_type: not_comparable` with "Axiom exposes its nonnegative caller-supplied completed-net-income boundary as a private diagnostic. PolicyEngine ... does not expose this selected TaxUnit boundary as one standalone variable", and the module keeps the same "entire net income as defined in this chapter" proof atom on that rule, so no overclaimed grounding was actually removed.
verdict.quote:
+      private: true
-    credits, nonresident allocation, and final-return liability are outside
-    this narrow schedule.
verdict.notes: Full semantic delta, from `git show 4d10a73d4a -M`: one added line (`private: true`), three rule renames (ky_pit_pilot_* -> ky_pit_2026_krs_141_020_*), one input rename, one file rename, and reworded rationale/summary. No formula, parameter, version window, effective date, entity, dtype, unit, or proof excerpt changed. Companion fixtures are the same ten cases with the same expected values, only the legal_id prefixes rewritten. `git grep ky_pit_pilot` at the parent over us-ky/ returns nothing outside the pilot module and its own test, and the PR body states the full-year-resident source hold "remain byte-identical to main", so no consumer's meaning moved. The one live counterargument for keeping this in the corpus: `metadata.private` is part of the enforced surface contract (validator_pipeline.py builds ExistingTargetSurfaceContract with `private=(... metadata.get("private") is True)` and errors with "[existing-target-oracle-contract] ... metadata.private/public contract"), so the module's public output surface did go from two outputs to one, and the PR body frames that as "exposes one public schedule-before-credits output". If the project counts a public/private visibility narrowing as an output-scope defect even when no computed value or citation changes, this would be unclear/wrong_entity_or_scope at low confidence — never confirmed, since KRS 141.020 says nothing about which intermediates a module may publish and the driver is documented in axiom-oracles as a PolicyEngine comparability disposition. Also note the PR's own review thread frames the entire blocker as oracle plumbing ("The corrected comparator is `ky_income_tax_before_non_refundable_credits_unit` ... not the legacy `ky_income_tax_before_refundable_credits` target, which subtracts nonrefundable credits") — that comparator defect lives in axiom-oracles, not in this module, so it should not be scored against this file.

triage.commit_summary: The commit consolidates Oregon's tax-year-2026 rate-schedule encoding: it retires the duplicate, ambiguously named `pilot_liability_pipeline` module, adds one canonical, explicitly estimated-only Publication OR-ESTIMATE Chart S/J module, and strips the duplicated Chart S/J parameters plus the annual tax-before-credits, tax-after-nonrefundable-credits, and net-liability rules out of the resident core. The stated reason is an authority boundary: the final tax-year-2026 Form OR-40 and instructions are absent from the pinned corpus, and Publication OR-ESTIMATE ("Rate charts for estimating 2026 Oregon tax") supports only an estimated ordinary schedule amount, so the resident core must stop before annual tax and liability rather than deriving them from the estimated-tax chart.

modules.description_quote: establish one canonical, explicitly estimated-only 2026 Publication OR-ESTIMATE Chart S/J module
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: this file is newly added in this commit, so it has no pre-fix state of its own; it is the corrected replacement surface for the retired pilot module (index 1), not a module whose encoded meaning was fixed in place.
modules.triage_notes: Added file (349 lines, status=added). All Chart S/J numbers are byte-identical to the retired pilot and to the block removed from the resident core: Chart S bounds 4550/11400/125000, bases 216/678/10618; Chart J 9100/22800/250000, bases 432/1357/21237; rates .0475/.0675/.0875/.099. I read the pinned corpus text of us-or/form/individual-income-tax/2026/or-estimate/document-1 and confirmed every one of those values verbatim against page 3 ('Chart S: Single or Married filing separately ... Not over $4,550 4.75% of taxable income ... Over $125,000 $10,618 plus 9.9% of excess over $125,000'), so there is no amount_mismatch here. Relative to the retired pilot the new module (a) renames the public output from or_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability to or_pit_2026_or_estimate_schedule_tax_amount, (b) replaces the single Bool input or_pit_pilot_uses_chart_j with five filing-status flags plus a strict or_pit_2026_or_estimate_input_domain_is_valid gate that fails closed (returns 0) on an invalid status or negative income, and (c) declares four deferred_outputs (complete annual taxable income, tax before credits, tax after credits, net liability). Those are added precision/scope the file never previously claimed, which the rubric says is not a defect, so I classify unclear with kind none rather than inventing a pre-fix defect. NOT RECOMMENDED as a defect-corpus item: a fidelity judge cannot be shown a pre-fix version of this path. The signing manifest for this file records manual_exception 'repair'. Provision was read via resolve_provision.py (corpus release resolved cleanly).

modules.description_quote: retire the ambiguous Oregon `pilot_liability_pipeline` through the signed retirement path
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The module published a public output named or_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability whose value is only the Publication OR-ESTIMATE ordinary schedule amount before any credits, so the declared output surface asserted a final annual income-tax liability that the cited estimated-tax publication does not establish.
modules.triage_notes: Whole-module deletion (363 lines). The arithmetic and every parameter value in the retired module are correct against the pinned OR-ESTIMATE text I read, so this is not an amount or boundary defect; the only meaning issue is the output surface. Strongest evidence is NOT in an allowed quote source: the retirement manifest .axiom/encoding-manifests/us-or/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.json (rewritten by 'axiom-encode retire' in this commit) carries reason: 'Superseded by one explicitly estimated-tax-only 2026 Publication OR-ESTIMATE schedule surface; the prior pilot name ambiguously implied final annual liability.' That names an output-surface/scope overclaim exactly. I held this at unclear rather than fidelity for two reasons: (1) the commit subject frames the change as consolidation/dedup ('Consolidate Oregon 2026 estimated tax schedule'), and the module genuinely was a duplicate of the Chart S/J block also present in the resident core, which is repo hygiene rather than a source disagreement; (2) the retired module already self-disclosed the boundary in its own summary ('It stops before credits and all other final-return adjustments and makes no PolicyEngine-parity claim'), which weakens the claim that a judge reading it cold should flag it. A reviewer could reasonably promote this to fidelity/wrong_entity_or_scope on the manifest reason. The pre-fix file is recoverable at parent 59a10dab866e5359c21b98d0df270ac81d60f22f, so it is usable as a corpus item if promoted. Companion test file pilot_liability_pipeline.test.yaml (170 lines) was deleted in the same commit.

modules.description_quote: Publication OR-ESTIMATE supports an estimated ordinary schedule amount only. This change therefore does not claim completed annual taxable income, tax before/after credits, net liability, or PolicyEngine parity.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The annual resident core derived and published tax before credits, tax after nonrefundable credits, and a net income-tax-liability candidate by applying Publication OR-ESTIMATE's estimated-tax Chart S/J, a source that supplies only 'Rate charts for estimating 2026 Oregon tax' and expressly is not a complete statement of law, so those annual-return branches had no authority in the cited sources.
modules.triage_notes: Modification (320 lines net removed). Removed rules: or_pit_2026_profile_candidate_schedule_tax, or_pit_2026_bounded_tax_after_nonrefundable_credits, or_pit_2026_bounded_net_income_tax_liability_candidate (all three were PUBLIC outputs -- confirmed at parent lines 1090, 1263, 1307 and referenced as deferred-output source_values at lines 128, 137, 144), plus the private Chart S/J parameter block (chart_s/chart_j ceilings, schedule_selector, schedule_floor/base/rate) and the eight or_pit_2026_table_index_* constants. The module also drops us-or/statute/316.042 from corpus_citation_paths. I read ORS 316.042 through the pinned corpus: it says the joint tax 'shall be twice the tax which would be imposed if the taxable income were cut in half', yet the removed or_pit_2026_profile_candidate_schedule_tax formula implemented no income-splitting branch at all -- it indexed the printed Chart J directly while carrying a 316.042 proof atom. That is a second, independent instance of a formula grounded on a provision it does not implement, reinforcing untraceable_branch. I also read the OR-ESTIMATE text and confirmed it is estimated-only ('Rate charts for estimating 2026 Oregon tax'; 'These instructions aren't a complete statement of laws and Department of Revenue rules'), which is the crux of the authority-boundary claim. ALTERNATIVE KIND: wrong_entity_or_scope (output surface) is defensible, since the correction can be read as the module claiming annual outputs it was not sourced for; I chose untraceable_branch because the rubric explicitly covers 'formulas grounded on the wrong provision' and the fix removes rather than re-parameterizes the branches. UNRELATED MECHANICAL CHANGES IN THE SAME DIFF: or_pit_2026_filing_status_count, the additional-standard-deduction rules, and the personal-exemption/severe-disability credit rules were rewritten to use literals 1/0 in place of or_pit_2026_table_index_one/_zero -- identical values, no meaning change. Prose in summary/rationale/deferred_outputs was also rewritten, and the deferred_outputs source_values were repointed away from the removed rules. Companion test file lost 1689 lines. Signing manifest flipped manual_exception from 'composition' to 'repair'. No follow-up commit touches us-or/policies/income_tax/ after this one; the post-fix state is still HEAD.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute the "unclear/none" reading and could not: the file is newly added (verified absent at parent 59a10dab), and every source-derived value it carries is byte-identical to the retired pilot module it replaces — the same Chart S/J upper bounds (4550/11400/125000, 9100/22800/250000), the same floors, the same base amounts {0: 0, 1: 216, 2: 678, 3: 10618, 4: 0, 5: 432, 6: 1357, 7: 21237}, the same rates, the same 2026-01-01/2026-12-31 windows, and the same `<=` bracket comparisons. So this file corrects no amount, no boundary direction, no effective window, and no branch grounding relative to the retired encoding. Its only meaning deltas are additive: five validated filing-status flags with a fail-closed `input_domain_is_valid` gate replacing the caller-asserted `or_pit_pilot_uses_chart_j` boolean, and a narrowed public output surface (`..._schedule_tax_amount` plus explicit `deferred_outputs` for annual taxable income, tax before/after credits, and net liability) — added precision and declared scope the module never previously claimed, which the harness rules say is at most "unclear". The genuine scope overclaim (a public `or_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` and a public passthrough `or_pit_pilot_taxable_income` grounded on the ORS 316.037 imposition clause, from an estimated-tax-only publication) lives in the deleted file at module index 1, not here.
verdict.notes: Refutation attempted in both directions and neither lands cleanly on this file. Toward "confirmed": the commit as a whole is a real fidelity/scope correction, but the wrong-scope encoding is in module index 1 (`pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml`), whose retired rules `or_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` (formula `or_pit_pilot_schedule_tax`) and public `or_pit_pilot_taxable_income` (formula `max(0, or_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income)` with proof excerpt "A tax is imposed for each taxable year on the entire taxable income of every resident of this state.") presented an estimated-schedule amount as annual liability and a caller passthrough as statutory taxable income. If a reviewer wants to keep one case from this commit, attach it to index 1 as wrong_entity_or_scope (output surface / authority scope), with the PR's "Authority boundary" paragraph as corroboration: "Publication OR-ESTIMATE supports an estimated ordinary schedule amount only. This change therefore does not claim completed annual taxable income, tax before/after credits, net liability, or PolicyEngine parity." Toward "not_a_defect": defensible for this file alone (identical parameters, purely additive validation), but I stopped short of that verdict because the added module is the corrective surface for a real overclaim elsewhere in the same commit, and a file-boundary technicality should not be recorded as "the old text was fine". One arguable fidelity angle I considered and rejected: the retired module delegated the Chart S vs Chart J status mapping to a caller boolean while citing the chart-heading excerpts in its proof atoms, and the new module encodes that mapping (MFJ/HOH/QSS -> Chart J). That is not unrepresented_clause, because the retired module declared the mapping as an explicit input boundary in its input description and summary ("the caller supplies ... whether Chart J applies"); encoding it now widens scope rather than repairing a claim that disagreed with the source. No resolve_provision lookup was needed: nothing in the verdict turns on the printed chart values, since the added and retired modules carry identical numbers and identical inclusive ("not over" -> `<=`) boundaries.

verdict.justification: The candidate reading says the retired module "asserted a final annual income-tax liability," but the module's own text for that exact rule disclaims it: the deleted `or_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` carries `source: 2026 Publication OR-ESTIMATE ordinary schedule amount before credits and other final-return adjustments`, the summary says "It stops before credits and all other final-return adjustments," and four `deferred_outputs` explicitly hand off taxable-income construction, specialty rates, and final-return adjustments. Nothing encoded disagreed with the source: the replacement `2026_or_estimate_schedule.yaml` reproduces every bracket floor `{0: 0, 1: 4550, 2: 11400, 3: 125000, 4: 0, 5: 9100, 6: 22800, 7: 250000}`, base `{0: 0, 1: 216, 2: 678, 3: 10618, 4: 0, 5: 432, 6: 1357, 7: 21237}`, rate `{0: 0.0475, ... 7: 0.099}`, chart bound (4550/11400/125000, 9100/22800/250000), `<=` selector strictness, entity, period, and 2026-01-01→2026-12-31 window byte-identically. The commit's own retirement record states the motive as a naming ambiguity and supersession, not a mis-encoding, and the only other post-fix differences (five explicit filing-status flags plus a fail-closed `input_domain_is_valid` guard) are added precision the pilot never claimed, which the rubric says is not a defect. This is a consolidation/rename retirement, so it does not support wrong_entity_or_scope as a fidelity correction.
verdict.quote: -    source: 2026 Publication OR-ESTIMATE ordinary schedule amount before credits and other final-return adjustments
verdict.notes:
Decisive corroboration outside the module diff: the commit also rewrites `.axiom/encoding-manifests/us-or/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.json` into an `"tool": "axiom-encode retire"` record whose `"reason"` field reads verbatim: "Superseded by one explicitly estimated-tax-only 2026 Publication OR-ESTIMATE schedule surface; the prior pilot name ambiguously implied final annual liability." Note "name ambiguously implied," not "encoding asserted" — the maintainer's recorded ground is identifier clarity plus deduplication, which the rubric lists under renames/mechanical rather than fidelity.

Strongest surviving counterargument for a reviewer who wants to keep this: in a rules engine the public output name is the binding contract, and `or_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` was a non-private terminal output that aliased `or_pit_pilot_schedule_tax` one-to-one (`formula: or_pit_pilot_schedule_tax`); dropping it does narrow the repo's published output surface, which the wrong_entity_or_scope definition covers ("output surface"). That is why I am at 0.68 rather than higher. But the pre-fix value under that name was exactly what Chart S/J prints, so there is no source text the old module disagreed with — the test for a fidelity defect.

Also note the diff is a whole-file deletion, which structurally cannot distinguish "removed because the name overclaimed" from "removed because it duplicated the canonical module"; the PR's third bullet ("remove duplicate Chart S/J and annual tax/liability ownership from the resident core") shows deduplication was the PR's organizing action. If the screen wants the Oregon annual-liability theme captured as a fidelity item, the better candidate is module index 2 (`resident_core_liability_pipeline.yaml`, 465-line modification removing annual tax/liability ownership and adding explicit deferrals), not this deletion.

Commands were read-only (`git show`, `sed`, `grep` on scratchpad diff files only).

verdict.justification: The removed branch was not untraceable: I read the pinned provisions, and ORS 316.037(1)(a) itself imposes the annual tax on "the entire taxable income of every resident" with a rate table, (1)(b) directs the Department to adopt an indexed table "that shall apply in lieu of" it, and ORS 316.042 supplies the joint/head-of-household doubling that Chart J's exactly-2x brackets embody — all three were already the removed rule's cited sources. Nor did the pre-fix module publish a completed annual amount: its pre-fix `deferred_outputs` already deferred complete_tax_before_credits, complete_tax_after_nonrefundable_credits, and net_income_tax_liability, and already recorded that "Publication OR-ESTIMATE labels its indexed values as estimates," so the deleted rules were candidate signals, not annual-return claims. The identical Chart S/J values and the identical base + rate x excess formula survive unchanged in the new 2026_or_estimate_schedule.yaml added by the same commit, and the annual core keeps consuming the same estimated publication for standard deductions, the $8,750 subtraction ceiling, and the $260 exemption credit — so no encoded value, bound, or logic was corrected against any source. This is the PR's stated de-duplication of Chart S/J ownership after retiring the pilot pipeline plus a conservative narrowing of candidate outputs, not a fidelity correction.
verdict.quote: -    source: ORS 316.037, 316.042, and 2026 Publication OR-ESTIMATE charts
verdict.notes:
Refutation evidence a reviewer can re-check quickly:
1. Source text (pinned release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, via resolve_provision at 0d0ab42ada): us-or/statute/316.037 = "(1)(a) A tax is imposed for each taxable year on the entire taxable income of every resident of this state. The amount of the tax shall be determined in accordance with the following table" ... "(b) For tax years beginning in each calendar year, the Department of Revenue shall adopt a table that shall apply in lieu of the table contained in paragraph (a)". us-or/statute/316.042 = "the tax imposed by ORS 316.037 shall be twice the tax which would be imposed if the taxable income were cut in half ... a return of a head of household or a surviving spouse ... shall be treated as a joint return". Chart J is exactly 2x Chart S (9,100/22,800/250,000 vs 4,550/11,400/125,000), i.e. the statute's doubling rule. So the deleted annual branch had statutory authority; it was not a branch "with no basis in the cited source".
2. Pre-fix file (git show 59a10dab:...resident_core_liability_pipeline.yaml, lines 99-146) already lists complete_tax_before_credits, complete_tax_after_nonrefundable_credits and net_income_tax_liability under `deferred_outputs`, with the taxable-income deferral reason stating "Publication OR-ESTIMATE labels its indexed values as estimates". The screening reading that the core "derived and published tax before credits ... net liability" overstates the pre-state: those were deferred, and the removed rules only appeared as `source_values` candidates.
3. Same-commit module 0 (2026_or_estimate_schedule.yaml) re-creates the identical chart values and identical formula shape, so no number, bound, rate, or comparison changed anywhere in the repo.
4. Selectivity: diff line 28/29 shows the core still draws the standard deductions, the $8,750 federal-tax-subtraction ceiling and the $260 exemption credit from the same "estimated" publication ("-        subtraction ceiling, $260 exemption-credit unit, and Chart S/J rates." / "+        subtraction ceiling and $260 exemption-credit unit."), so the "estimated source cannot support annual amounts" principle is not applied as a fidelity rule — only Chart S/J ownership moved.
5. PR body frames it as ownership/dedup: "remove duplicate Chart S/J and annual tax/liability ownership from the resident core while preserving independently sourced upstream candidates and explicit annual deferrals". The commit also converted private table-index parameters to literals 0/1 (pure refactor, no meaning change).
If a reviewer still wants to keep this case, the only defensible kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (estimated-tax chart exposed on an annual-return output surface), not untraceable_branch — but I would not keep it, because the complete annual surfaces were deferred both before and after, and the post-fix rationale even withdraws the (accurate) claim that the pinned ORS 316 snapshot supplies "ordinary and specialty rate authority" although 316.037(1)(a) plainly does.

triage.commit_summary: The commit retires Nebraska's ambiguous `pilot_liability_pipeline` module and replaces it with one canonical `2026_1040n_es_estimated_schedule` module in a `ne_pit_2026_estimated_*` namespace, renaming the misleading public `income_tax_liability` output to `ne_pit_2026_estimated_schedule_tax` while preserving every Form 1040N-ES threshold, printed cent base, rate, and filing-status schedule unchanged. The one behavioral change is a new private Judgment rule `ne_pit_2026_estimated_filing_status_selectors_valid` that gates the public output, so contradictory joint-or-surviving-spouse plus head-of-household selectors now fail closed to zero instead of silently returning the married-filing-jointly schedule amount.

modules.description_quote: add a private selector-validity invariant so overlapping joint/surviving-spouse and head-of-household inputs fail the public output closed to zero
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Pre-fix the public output (then named `ne_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability`) resolved a contradictory filing-status input by silently returning the married-filing-jointly/surviving-spouse schedule amount whenever the joint selector was true even if the head-of-household selector was also true, producing a number for a filing-status combination that 2026 Form 1040N-ES has no schedule for, and its name asserted full income tax liability rather than the worksheet line-11 estimated schedule amount.
modules.triage_notes: Git records this as a rename (74% similarity) from `us-ne/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml`; the prepared bundle lists it as 'added' because rename detection was off, so the meaningful diff is `git -C <repo> show -M --find-renames=30% 54ef0d6fe3 -- us-ne/policies/income_tax/2026_1040n_es_estimated_schedule.yaml us-ne/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml`. Almost all 155 changed lines are the `ne_pit_pilot_*` -> `ne_pit_2026_estimated_*` namespace rename plus a summary-prose rewrite, which on its own is mechanical: every rate (0.0246/0.0351/0.0455/0.0455), floor (4130/24760/39900; 7700/39620/59160; 8250/49530/79800), printed cent base (101.60/825.71/1514.58; 189.42/1309.81/2198.88; 202.95/1651.88/3029.16), effective window (2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31), entity (TaxUnit), period, the max(0, ...) floor, and the `<=` boundary direction are byte-identical. The single behavioral delta is the new private `ne_pit_2026_estimated_filing_status_selectors_valid` (dtype Judgment, formula `not (joint and head)`) and the public output changing from `formula: ne_pit_pilot_bracket_tax` to an `if selectors_valid: ... else: 0` gate; rules go 28 -> 29, matching the PR's stated count. Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus (us-ne/form/individual-income-tax/2026/1040n-es/document-1): the form prints four mutually exclusive schedules headed 'Single Taxpayer', 'Head of Household', 'Married, Filing Separately', 'Married, Filing Jointly and Surviving Spouses', with no schedule for a taxpayer who is both, and the encoded thresholds/bases match the printed table; 'but not over' also confirms the unchanged inclusive `<=` bounds. Companion test adds `overlapping_filing_status_selectors_fail_closed` asserting `not_holds` and output '0'. Doubts a reviewer should weigh: (a) an alternative kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (the defect is about filing-status selection and about the public output surface claiming 'income_tax_liability'), or untraceable_branch (the pre-fix joint-wins precedence has no basis in the form); I chose polarity_or_logic because 'fail-open vs fail-closed' is the enumerated match and the decisive changed line is the boolean gate; (b) fail-closed-to-zero is itself a convention the form does not state, so one could argue this is defensive hardening rather than a source disagreement -- against that, the module's own input descriptions already claimed the selectors are 'mutually exclusive with head-of-household' without enforcing it; (c) all PR 'independent review' comments are posted by the same account as the author (PavelMakarchuk), so the review text is self-reported rather than a second reviewer; (d) the commit also touches non-module files (oracle-coverage-pending.yaml, known-validation-gaps.yaml, .axiom/pending-validation-fingerprints.json, the reverse index, and two manifests), all bookkeeping for the retirement, and deletes the legacy test file -- none of which affect this classification.

verdict.justification: A name-normalized diff of the pre file (us-ne/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml at 8ed6406784) against the post file shows that apart from renames and summary prose, the ONLY change is the new private Judgment `not (…joint_or_surviving_spouse and …head_of_household)` plus the wrapper `if …selectors_valid: …filing_status_schedule_tax else: 0` — every rate, floor, printed cent base, effective window, entity, period, and the joint→HOH→single selection order is byte-identical, so for every filing-status combination the 1040N-ES can actually produce the output is unchanged. The behavior that changed applies only to joint=true AND head-of-household=true, a state the module's own input contract already excluded verbatim ("mutually exclusive with head-of-household", identical text pre-fix), and the resolved form text prescribes no schedule and no zero for such a combination — so the new 0 has no more source grounding than the old joint amount; it is defensive enforcement of a documented precondition, a policy choice, not an encoded meaning that disagreed with the source. The other half of the change, renaming `ne_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` to `ne_pit_2026_estimated_schedule_tax`, is a rename (explicitly mechanical) whose pre-fix `source:` field already read "2026 Form 1040N-ES worksheet line 11 estimated schedule amount, not final-return liability", so the encoded scope never disagreed with the form either. Per the rubric's guard, hardening an input state the module never claimed to cover is at most unclear, and here the evidence is complete enough to call it an enhancement.
verdict.quote: description: True for married filing jointly or surviving-spouse status; mutually exclusive with head-of-household.
verdict.notes: Evidence trail: (1) Normalized diff (renames mapped: ne_pit_pilot_* -> ne_pit_2026_estimated_*, taxable_income -> taxable_income_boundary, supplied_taxable_income -> worksheet_line_10_taxable_income, bracket_tax -> filing_status_schedule_tax, income_tax_liability -> schedule_tax) yields exactly three hunks: summary prose, the added private rule, and `formula: X_status_sched` -> `if X_filing_status_selectors_valid: X_status_sched else: 0`. No parameter, threshold, rate, date, entity, period, or input/output type changed. (2) The pinned-release form text (corpus_release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, provision us-ne/form/individual-income-tax/2026/1040n-es/document-1) prints three status-keyed schedules and contains no instruction for a taxpayer who is both joint and head of household, and no fallback-to-zero rule. (3) The pre-fix fixture file had no overlapping-selector case; the new fixture adds `overlapping_filing_status_selectors_fail_closed`. So the old behavior was incidental precedence on an out-of-contract input, not an asserted encoding. (4) The added line, verbatim: `formula: not (ne_pit_2026_estimated_filing_status_joint_or_surviving_spouse and ne_pit_2026_estimated_filing_status_head_of_household)`. Where a reviewer could legitimately disagree with me: this repo's independent reviewer treated the missing invariant as an actionable finding, and the task's own kind list names "fail-open vs fail-closed, default value" under polarity_or_logic. If this corpus's definition of fidelity is widened to include silently producing a number for an impossible input state (a robustness/fail-closed defect rather than a disagreement with cited text), then the first reader's polarity_or_logic call stands and the verdict flips to confirmed; the decisive quote in that case is the added `not (... and ...)` formula line. I would keep this case as a borderline example rather than a clean positive: it changes no output for any source-realizable fact pattern. If the corpus needs a single fallback classification rather than a drop, `unclear` is more defensible than `confirmed`, because the rename half is unambiguously mechanical and the invariant half has no source text behind either the old or new value.

In the annual full-year-resident core it deletes the duplicated ND-1ES parameters and the schedule-based "candidate" annual tax-before-credits, tax-after-nonrefundable-credits, and net-liability rules, replacing the always-zero public annual tax output with structured deferrals whose stated reason is that N.D.C.C. 57-38-30.3(10) requires the Commissioner's prescribed annual Tax Table, which is not in the pinned corpus, and that the estimated-tax schedules cannot substitute for it.

modules.description_quote: consolidate North Dakota’s 2026 Form ND-1ES rate schedules into one explicitly estimated-only module
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: this path has no pre-image (the bundle records it as added), but its predecessor us-nd/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml exposed the ND-1ES worksheet schedule result as a public rule named nd_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability, sourced 'N.D.C.C. section 57-38-30.3(1)(a)-(d), applicable official 2026 individual schedule before credits' with proof excerpt 'A tax is hereby imposed for each taxable year upon income earned or received in that', i.e. an estimated-tax schedule figure fed by 'completed-return North Dakota taxable income' and labeled as liability even though subsection 7 credits and any prescribed subsection 10 table are excluded.
modules.triage_notes: File-level status in the bundle is 'added', but `git show -M --find-renames=30%` detects it as a rename of us-nd/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml (similarity 59%), and the pilot's apply manifest is rewritten by `axiom-encode retire` marking pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml and its .test.yaml deleted. Against that pre-image the only two meaning changes are (1) scope/output-surface: public output renamed nd_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability -> nd_pit_2026_nd1es_estimated_schedule_tax, source re-labeled to 'Official 2026 Form ND-1ES applicable estimated-tax schedule before credits', caller input re-described from 'Completed-return North Dakota taxable income' to 'Estimated North Dakota taxable income ... for Form ND-1ES', and the summary now states 'It is not annual Form ND-1 tax, an annual Tax Table result, estimated payments, or final liability'; and (2) fail-closed logic: a new nd_pit_2026_nd1es_filing_status_is_valid rule plus a new nd_pit_2026_nd1es_filing_status_single input make the selector return 0 when zero or more than one status holds, where the pilot defaulted to the single schedule ('when all three are false, the single schedule applies'). Every threshold, cumulative base, and rate is byte-identical to the pilot (49575/250400/3916.09; 82800/304850/4329.98; 41400/152425/2164.99; 66400/277600/4118.40; 1.95%/2.50%), so no amount change. Kept as unclear because as an added path there is nothing for a judge to correct in-place, the maintainers framed the change as dedup/consolidation rather than a defect fix, and 'preserve strict filing-status validation' in the PR body suggests they view the fail-closed logic as carried over rather than repaired. Runner-up kind: polarity_or_logic (default-to-single fail-open replaced by fail-closed zero) — N.D.C.C. 57-38-30.3(1) keys the schedule to 'an individual's filing status used for federal income tax purposes' and states no default-to-single rule. Provision was read through the pinned corpus release: the corpus text of 57-38-30.3(1)(a)-(d) already carries the 2026 indexed bracket tables matching the ND-1ES values, and (10) says the Commissioner 'may prescribe tax tables ... If prescribed ... the tables must be followed', which is the maintainers' basis for refusing an annual-tax claim. Reviewer comments are PR issue comments from PavelMakarchuk (self-reported independent review cycles); there are no formal PR reviews or inline review comments.

modules.description_quote: remove estimated schedules and misleading tax/liability candidates from the annual resident core
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The annual-return core computed annual tax before credits, tax after nonrefundable credits, and net income tax liability from a private copy of the Form ND-1ES estimated-tax schedules (proof-grounded on 57-38-30.3 excerpts such as 'The tax for individuals is equal to North Dakota taxable income multiplied by the rates' and 'A tax is hereby imposed for each taxable year'), which is not the prescribed annual computation the source requires, and it published a public annual tax-before-credits output that was hard-gated to zero instead of being declared deferred.
modules.triage_notes: Whole diff is deletions plus header/summary/deferred_outputs edits; the additions, reductions, and taxable-income formulas (57-38-30.3(2)) are untouched, so this is not a rewrite of the income chain. Removed: 14 ND-1ES parameters, the four per-status candidate tax formulas, nd_pit_2026_profile_candidate_tax_before_credits, and three supported-profile rules including the public nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_tax_before_credits. Note that nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies was hard-coded 'false' pre-fix, so all three public outputs already evaluated to 0 for every taxpayer; the observable change is therefore from 'public annual tax outputs return zero' to declared structured deferrals, and the module summary edit says exactly that. deferred_outputs additionally gains nd_pit_2026_complete_tax_before_credits with reason 'Section 57-38-30.3(10) requires use of the Commissioner's prescribed annual Tax Table ... The separate Form ND-1ES schedules are estimated-tax parameters and cannot substitute for that annual table', and the two existing deferrals' source_values are repointed off the deleted candidates onto nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies and nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_taxable_income. Runner-up kind: wrong_entity_or_scope (estimated-tax material and tax/liability outputs owned by an annual-return module; the screen flag calls the commit a scope correction). Caveat a reviewer should weigh: the pinned corpus text of 57-38-30.3(1)(a)-(d) already embeds the 2026 indexed schedules and says the tax equals ND taxable income times the applicable schedule, while (10) only says the Commissioner 'may prescribe tax tables', so the maintainers' 'cannot substitute' rationale is partly a conservatism/deferral judgment rather than a flat contradiction with the statute text; the untraceable-branch reading rests on the candidates claiming annual-return tax and liability (credits under subsection 7 excluded) from estimated-tax worksheet parameters. Companion test file lost 485 lines (fixtures for the removed rules) and a new 304-line fixture file was added for index 0; oracle-coverage-pending.yaml drops ND entries accordingly. Provision read via resolve_provision.py against the pinned release (succeeded).

verdict.justification: The bundle records this path as "added", but a rename-aware diff (`git show -M 6e0b21e114`) shows it is a 59%-similarity rename of `us-nd/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml` in which every rate, zero-tax ceiling, top threshold, cumulative base, `<=` boundary and 2026-01-01/2026-12-31 window is unchanged; the only computed-value change is a new exactly-one filing-status guard that fails closed to 0 where the pilot fell through to the single schedule, which mirrors the statute's own residual subdivision (a) ("Single, other than head of household or surviving spouse") and so is added defensiveness, not a corrected disagreement with the source. The pinned corpus record for `us-nd/statute/57/57-38-30.3` composes the Century Code with the 2026 Form ND-1ES tables under `source_components` role `operative_2026_individual_rate_schedules` and `rate_schedule_overlay.authority: "N.D.C.C. § 57-38-30.3(1)(g)"`, so the pre-fix grounding of those tables on 57-38-30.3(1)(a)-(d) was faithful — the "estimated-only" reframing narrows what the module claims (it will not stand in for the Commissioner's unpinned annual Tax Table under subsection 10) rather than fixing an encoded meaning that disagreed with the cited text. Everything else in the change is rule renames, `source:`/proof-excerpt strings, and prose rationale, which the rubric puts on the mechanical/provenance side. The "misleading tax/liability candidates" the PR body describes are removed in the other module of this commit (`resident_core_liability_pipeline.yaml`), not here, so no wrong_entity_or_scope defect is demonstrated for module index 0.
verdict.quote:
-  - name: nd_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability
+  - name: nd_pit_2026_nd1es_estimated_schedule_tax
     kind: derived
     entity: TaxUnit
     dtype: Money
     period: Year
     unit: USD
-    source: N.D.C.C. section 57-38-30.3(1)(a)-(d), applicable official 2026 individual schedule before credits
+    source: Official 2026 Form ND-1ES applicable estimated-tax schedule before credits
verdict.notes:
Key refutation of the first reader's premise: the reader treated the ND-1ES figures as estimated-tax-only material wrongly published as annual liability. The pinned corpus record (line 88 of /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-corpus/data/corpus/provisions/us-nd/statute/2026-07-16-pit-central-us-nd-title-57-38.jsonl) shows the opposite: the ND-1ES PDF is pinned as role "operative_2026_individual_rate_schedules" under the (1)(g) indexed-replacement authority, i.e. the operative 2026 subsection-1 schedules for the section, not an estimated-only artifact. The resolved provision text contains no "estimated"/"ND-1ES" language at all; its schedule rows ($49,575 | $250,400 | $0.00 + 1.95% | $49,575, etc.) match the module's parameters exactly both before and after the fix.

Fallback for a reviewer who disagrees: the only encoded-meaning change in this module is the new `nd_pit_2026_nd1es_filing_status_is_valid` rule plus `if not nd_pit_2026_nd1es_filing_status_is_valid: 0` in the public output (with a fourth input `nd_pit_2026_nd1es_filing_status_single`). If that fail-open-to-single -> fail-closed-to-zero default is judged a source-mandated correction, the kind is polarity_or_logic (default value / fail-open vs fail-closed), NOT wrong_entity_or_scope. It is not amount_mismatch or boundary_direction: no number or comparison operator moved.

Weakest point of my verdict: the pilot's public rule name `nd_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability` did overclaim ("liability") for a figure that excludes the subsection 4 other-jurisdiction credit and the twenty-one subsection 7 credits, and the PR body calls such names "misleading tax/liability candidates". But the pilot's own `source:` line and summary already said "before credits", so the mismatch was identifier-vs-prose; per the rubric renames and metadata are mechanical. That is why I landed on not_a_defect rather than confirmed, and only at 0.6.

Scope note for the corpus build: module index 1 (`resident_core_liability_pipeline.yaml`) is where the real surface removal happens — it drops `nd_pit_2026_profile_candidate_tax_before_credits`, `nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_candidate_tax_after_nonrefundable_credits`, and `nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_candidate_net_income_tax_liability` along with a duplicate copy of all twelve schedule parameters. If any case in this commit deserves a wrong_entity_or_scope look, it is that file, not this one.

Commands used were read-only: `git -C /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us show --stat 6e0b21e114`, `git show -M 6e0b21e114 -- <two paths>`, `sed -n` on the bundle diff and the corpus JSONL, and the pinned resolve_provision.py (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, provision sha256 d06df87b…, fix_time_corpus_match "same_body").

verdict.justification: The "untraceable_branch" reading is refuted on both of its premises: the removed rate parameters are verbatim in the cited provision (the resolved 57-38-30.3 text contains "$49,575 | $250,400 | $0.00 + 1.95%", "$3,916.09 + 2.50%", "$4,118.40 + 2.50%" in subsection 1(a)-(d) under "multiplied by the rates in the applicable rate schedule in subdivisions a through d"), and the receiving module keeps the identical corpus_citation_path and excerpts, so nothing was re-grounded to a different provision. The core also never published schedule-based annual tax: the gate rule nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies had formula 'false', so the removed public output was unconditionally 0 and the whole ND-1ES candidate chain was unreachable, exactly as the pre-fix summary already said ("Public annual tax outputs return zero"). What the diff actually does is de-duplicate ownership (pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml was renamed into 2026_nd1es_estimated_schedule.yaml per git show --stat) and retire three always-zero public annual tax/liability outputs into structured deferred_outputs, changing no number, boundary, date, or logic branch. That leaves a genuine but unsettled question - withdrawing a public annual-tax surface fixed at 0 (which subsection 1 contradicts above the zero bracket) is an output-surface/scope correction at most, and competes with reading the change as convention plus dedup hygiene.
verdict.quote: -        formula: "if nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies: nd_pit_2026_profile_candidate_tax_before_credits else: 0"
verdict.notes: Evidence trail for the reviewer. (1) Pre-file gate: rules[nd_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies].versions[0].formula is 'false' (pre blob 11ba9aba90, lines 208-224), so all three removed public rules (supported_profile_tax_before_credits, supported_profile_candidate_tax_after_nonrefundable_credits, supported_profile_candidate_net_income_tax_liability) returned 0 for every input; the ND-1ES candidate chain fed nothing reachable. (2) Provision resolution (release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, corpus commit 0fd35bfbda, provision file .../2026-07-16-pit-central-us-nd-title-57-38.jsonl line 88, body sha256 d06df87b32...) shows the cited statute itself carries the 2026 indexed filing-status schedules, so the deleted parameters were source-traceable, not inventions. (3) The new module (module index 0, a rename of the retired pilot) re-hosts the same values under the same corpus_citation_path us-nd/statute/57/57-38-30.3 with the same excerpt strings - grounding unchanged, only ownership moved. (4) The fix's own new deferral reason states "Section 57-38-30.3(10) requires use of the Commissioner's prescribed annual Tax Table", but the provision reads "The tax commissioner may prescribe tax tables, to be used in computing the tax according to subsection 1, if the amounts of the tax tables are based on the tax rates set forth in subsection 1" - permissive, and derived from the subsection-1 rates the module already encoded. So the post-fix rationale overstates the source rather than correcting a source disagreement. (5) If the case is kept, the only defensible kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (output surface: an annual-return core publishing annual tax/liability outputs pinned at zero, plus estimated-schedule ownership), never untraceable_branch or amount_mismatch. A reviewer who requires an observable meaning error against the source should prune this case; a reviewer who counts withdrawal of an unsupported public output surface as fidelity should keep it as wrong_entity_or_scope.
