item.subject: (screen-flagged) Fail-closed guard on contradictory Medicaid applicant ages added to magi_household_income_pipeline; landed inside PR #1007 which introduced the module, so possibly a pre-merge repair.
item.screen_reason: Fail-closed guard on contradictory Medicaid applicant ages added to magi_household_income_pipeline; landed inside PR #1007 which introduced the module, so possibly a pre-merge repair.

triage.commit_summary: The commit appends two equality conjuncts to the Medicaid MAGI household pipeline's applicant-facts-consistency contract so that the canonical scalar `medicaid_applicant_age` must equal the applicant-age and candidate-age fields duplicated on the applicant's own candidate row. It also adds a companion case (`contradictory_canonical_and_self_row_ages_fail_closed`) and a pytest contract assertion showing that before the change a household row could say the applicant is 65 while the canonical fact said 19, and the pipeline would still emit an affirmative adult-group eligibility result.

modules.description_quote: Fail closed on contradictory Medicaid applicant ages
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The applicant-facts-consistency contract (sourced to 42 CFR 435.603(f), "one applicant classification across all candidate rows") cross-checked every applicant-level boolean against its row-duplicated copy but omitted the applicant's age, so an input where the canonical applicant age was 19 and the self row's applicant/candidate age was 65 passed the contract and the module still asserted eligibility while composing the (f)(2)/(f)(3) household from one age and applying the 435.119 adult-group band to the other.
modules.triage_notes: Purely additive change: two `sum_where(...) == medicaid_applicant_age * count_where(...)` conjuncts appended to the end of one formula; nothing else in the module (parameters, versions, effective dates, other rules' formulas, metadata) changed. Pre-fix the module did check row-internal coherence (`household_row_candidate_age == household_row_applicant_age` when `household_row_candidate_is_the_applicant`, inside household_row_inputs_valid) but never tied either row field to the canonical scalar, which separately drives medicaid_applicant_under_state_plan_age (f)(3)(iv) and the 435.119 adult-group bounds. Provision was read through the pinned corpus (us/regulation/42/435/603/f resolved cleanly): (f)(2)(ii)/(iii) and (f)(3)(ii)/(iii) key household composition off "the age specified by the State under paragraph (f)(3)(iv)", so the source treats the applicant's age as a single fact and the pre-fix encoding could use two contradictory values for it in one determination. Caveat on classification: this is an input-coherence guard on a duplicated-input surface that is an artifact of the encoding, not a clause the regulation states, so a stricter judge could call it defensive hygiene rather than source fidelity; I classified it fidelity because the rule itself claims to verify applicant-fact consistency under (f) and the fail-open path produced an affirmative eligibility answer on facts that cannot both hold. Kind chosen as polarity_or_logic per the 'fail-open vs fail-closed' clause, matching the commit subject. Provenance: this is the last commit on PR #1007's branch (https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/pull/1007), which also introduced the module (30e2327e4) and carried sibling repair commits (3a3f3bf52 'Fail closed on Medicaid family size FPL mismatches', c3b9a2ea6, 455cfb4a8c), so this is a pre-merge repair, not a post-merge defect fix. No inline PR review comment names this specific hole; the closest reviewer text is the blind-review issue comment: "runtime validity is diagnostic only, so structurally invalid inputs still emit affirmative results." No later commit touches the module file.

verdict.justification: The added conjuncts compare two copies of the same input field (the canonical `medicaid_applicant_age` against the row-duplicated `household_row_applicant_age` / `household_row_candidate_age` on the self row), so they only bite on inputs that are self-contradictory — a state 42 CFR 435.603(f) never describes; read through the pinned release, (f) is pure household-composition text (filer/dependent/non-filer rules and the (f)(3)(iv) age election) and states no consistency requirement over duplicated applicant facts. For every coherent fact pattern the regulation actually determines, the pre- and post-fix modules return identical results, so no encoded meaning was corrected; by the corpus's own symmetry an added branch with no hook in the cited source is not a fidelity correction. The claimed kind is also unsupported on its face: nothing was inverted or mis-combined, a new conjunct was appended to an existing conjunction, and the source states no clause for `unrepresented_clause` to have omitted either. Context reinforces the reading — the commit sits inside PR #1007, which introduced the module, in a burst of pre-merge mutation-hardening commits, and the reviewer frames fail-closed inputs as "the campaign-wide lesson from the sibling benefit reviews," i.e. a house design standard rather than a reading of 435.603.
verdict.quote:
+          and sum_where(
+            medicaid_household_member_of_applicant,
+            household_row_applicant_age,
+            household_row_candidate_is_the_applicant
+          ) == medicaid_applicant_age
verdict.notes: Not mechanical — the change is real and behavior-altering: at the parent commit the runtime-validity gate was already wired, so pre-fix an input with canonical age 19 and self-row ages 65 passed `medicaid_household_relation_applicant_facts_consistent`, passed `medicaid_magi_household_runtime_inputs_valid`, and emitted `medicaid_adult_group_eligible: holds`. The companion case added in the same commit (`contradictory_canonical_and_self_row_ages_fail_closed`) pins exactly that: `internal_eligible_under_highest_applicable_magi_income_standard: holds` but gated `eligible_under_highest_applicable_magi_income_standard: not_holds`. So a reviewer who counts fail-open input-validation gaps as in-scope defects should retain the case; my objection is scope, not substance. Two further details for that reviewer. (1) The pre-fix module already enforced `household_row_candidate_age == household_row_applicant_age` on the self row (rows_valid, pre-fix line 522) and already cross-checked the derived boolean `medicaid_applicant_under_state_plan_age` against its row copy — the hole was only that 19 and 65 both sit above the (f)(3)(iv) threshold, so the boolean cross-check agreed while the raw scalars did not. That makes the gap a derived-vs-raw surface omission, not inverted logic. (2) If the case is kept, `polarity_or_logic` is the wrong kind: nothing was negated, re-ordered, or defaulted; the closest shape is a missing validity conjunct, which fits `unrepresented_clause` in form but fails its definition ("a clause the source states") because 435.603(f) states no such clause. Also note the first reader's quote, "Fail closed on contradictory Medicaid applicant ages," is the commit subject only — the commit body is empty, there are no PR reviews or review comments on the diff, and the single issue comment's fail-open bullet ("runtime validity is diagnostic only, so structurally invalid inputs still emit affirmative results") describes a different repair, since gating was already present at parent 455cfb4a8c.

item.subject: (screen-flagged) Fail-closed guard on Medicaid family size / FPL mismatches added to magi_household_income_pipeline; landed inside PR #1007 which introduced the module, so possibly a pre-merge repair.
item.screen_reason: Fail-closed guard on Medicaid family size / FPL mismatches added to magi_household_income_pipeline; landed inside PR #1007 which introduced the module, so possibly a pre-merge repair.

triage.commit_summary: The commit hardens the Medicaid MAGI household income pipeline so that a supplied annual FPL amount must match an independent authoritative HHS poverty-guideline lookup keyed to the same applicable family size, adding two new inputs and five conjuncts to the `medicaid_scalar_contract_valid` judgment. It also adds a 34th companion fixture and a pytest contract test proving that a mismatched family-size/FPL pair now fails closed even when the caller's correspondence attestation boolean is true, where previously the attestation alone let an affirmative eligibility result through on a wrong FPL denominator.

modules.description_quote: Fail closed on Medicaid family size FPL mismatches
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The scalar contract accepted any positive annual FPL amount on the caller's self-asserted correspondence attestation, so an FPL guideline belonging to a different family size could drive the %FPL comparison and still yield an affirmative eligibility result, contradicting 42 CFR 435.603(d)(4)'s 'Federal poverty level for the applicable family size'.
modules.triage_notes: Single-module commit; the only module change is +5 conjuncts in rules[medicaid_scalar_contract_valid].versions[0].formula and +2 new inputs (authoritative_fpl_lookup_family_size, authoritative_fpl_lookup_annual_guideline_amount). No other rule, version, effective date, parameter, or output changed. Provision was read through the pinned corpus release (us/regulation/42/435/603/d resolved, 1828 chars) and does contain 'Federal poverty level for the applicable family size', so the source does tie the FPL denominator to the applicable family size. Evidence that the pre-fix behavior was fail-open and not merely missing precision: the new companion case 'family_size_fpl_amount_mismatch_with_true_attestation_fails_closed' (applicable_family_size 1, supplied FPL 21640, authoritative lookup 1/15960, attestation true) asserts internal_eligible_under_highest_applicable_magi_income_standard: holds while the gated eligible_under_highest_applicable_magi_income_standard: not_holds -- i.e. before the guard the module emitted an affirmative result off the family-2 denominator; its yaml comment states 'The true attestation cannot override the structural lookup mismatch.' Kind judgment: 'fail-open vs fail-closed' is enumerated under polarity_or_logic and the commit subject names exactly that; an alternative reading is unrepresented_clause (the source's family-size correspondence requirement was not enforced), which is why confidence is 0.75 rather than higher. Counter-consideration for the reviewer: the fix also widens the input surface with two inputs the module never previously claimed, so part of this is validation hardening rather than a corrected formula value; the pre-existing attestation input shows the module did already claim the correspondence, which is what tips it to fidelity. Context: this commit landed inside PR #1007, the PR that introduced the module, so it is a pre-merge repair -- the defect never shipped on main. The PR's blind review (issue comment) listed six blocking findings including 'runtime validity is diagnostic only, so structurally invalid inputs still emit affirmative results', which is the same fail-open family but does not name the FPL/family-size mismatch specifically; there are no PR reviews or review comments in the bundle. Sibling repair commits in the same series: c3b9a2ea6 'Make Medicaid relation orientation executable' (parent) and 30e2327e4 'fix: repair Medicaid MAGI household pipeline'.

verdict.justification: The diff changes no policy formula: it appends two conjuncts and two new caller-supplied inputs to the `medicaid_scalar_contract_valid` input contract, while the %FPL denominator, the (d)(4) 5-point disregard, membership, and standards logic are untouched, and the fail-closed gating (`medicaid_magi_household_runtime_inputs_valid` → `eligible_under_highest_applicable_magi_income_standard`) already existed in parent c3b9a2ea60. The correspondence requirement the reader calls unrepresented was already encoded pre-fix as the conjunct `applicable_family_size_fpl_year_region_and_budget_correspondence_attested` ("Required attestation that family size and annual FPL correspond to each other…"), on a formula proof atom already citing us/regulation/42/435/603/d with the excerpt "Federal poverty level for the applicable family size". The pinned provision text of (d)(4) says only "subtract an amount equivalent to 5 percentage points of the Federal poverty level for the applicable family size" — it states no lookup-key verification duty, and the added `authoritative_fpl_lookup_*` values are themselves inputs, so a self-consistent but wrong pair (declared size 1, FPL 21,640, lookup 1 / 21,640) still passes post-fix. That is added input-integrity precision the module never claimed, not an encoded meaning that disagreed with the source, so neither polarity_or_logic nor unrepresented_clause holds.
verdict.quote: +          and authoritative_fpl_lookup_family_size == applicable_family_size
verdict.notes: Refutation evidence a reviewer can re-check quickly: (1) `git -C /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us show c3b9a2ea6039f05f27e2c4550d3cdbfbb2ee9372:us/policies/medicaid/magi_household_income_pipeline.yaml | sed -n '926,965p'` shows the pre-fix rule already contains both the (d) proof atom excerpt "Federal poverty level for the applicable family size" and the attestation conjunct, so the source clause was represented before the change. (2) The added inputs are declared under `inputs:`, e.g. the diff's own description line "Family-size key returned by the authoritative HHS poverty-guideline lookup for the determination year and region; it must equal the applicable family size." — the module still never reads an HHS table, so the guard only catches contradiction between two caller declarations. (3) Same-commit test `family_size_fpl_amount_mismatch_with_true_attestation_fails_closed` frames the target as a caller whose attestation is untrue ("The true attestation cannot override the structural lookup mismatch"), i.e. a trust-boundary hardening; the honest-mismatch path was already covered pre-fix by the `unattested_family_size_fpl_scalars` case. (4) The commit landed inside PR #1007 which introduced the module, after MaxGhenis's blind review whose campaign-wide lesson was architectural — "State elections under 435.603 … get explicit election inputs that fail closed — no assumed defaults" — a repo design standard, not a provision of 42 CFR 435.603. Residual doubt (why 0.62, not higher): the reviewer's blocking finding "runtime validity is diagnostic only, so structurally invalid inputs still emit affirmative results" is genuinely a fail-open complaint, and one could argue applying a non-corresponding guideline to the (d)(4) comparison contradicts the provision's "for the applicable family size" wording; if the corpus counts review-driven fail-closed hardening of an already-attested precondition as fidelity, this would be polarity_or_logic, and "unclear" would be the fallback rather than confirmed.

item.subject: (screen-flagged) Makes the Medicaid MAGI pipeline's relation orientation executable: a polarity/direction fix to an existing module (34-line module diff plus test changes).
item.screen_reason: Makes the Medicaid MAGI pipeline's relation orientation executable: a polarity/direction fix to an existing module (34-line module diff plus test changes).

triage.commit_summary: The commit reworks how the Medicaid MAGI household pipeline declares its applicant-to-member relation: the raw two-slot data relation is renamed to medicaid_household_candidate_row_for_applicant, and the name the formulas consume, medicaid_household_member_of_applicant, becomes a derived_relation wrapper that explicitly declares current_slot 1 (applicant) and related_slot 0 (candidate member) with a tautological filter formula. It also adds a companion probe fixture and Python contract assertions so a slot reversal would fail a test, replacing an inert documentary `arguments:` list that the compiler was silently discarding.

modules.description_quote: The raw candidate-row relation is therefore wrapped by an executable derived relation with current_slot 1 (the applicant) and related_slot 0 (the candidate member), matching both the compiled sums and runtime tuples.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: nothing in the pre-fix encoding disagreed with 42 CFR 435.603(d)(1) — the pinned engine already traversed the relation member-first (current_slot 1, related_slot 0), so the pre-fix module summed the same member-side MAGI; the only defect was that the orientation declaration was inert and therefore unverifiable, not that it computed the wrong side.
modules.triage_notes: Recommend EXCLUDING from the fidelity corpus despite the polarity/direction screen flag; this is executability/mutation-observability hardening, not a meaning change. Evidence: (1) The pinned engine ref ffd8213271947b0189a9dd61a055c1e0e78908a0 (from .axiom/toolchain.toml at this commit) hard-codes the slot convention in src/formula.rs `fn infer_slots(_relation: &str) -> (usize, usize) { (1, 0) }` — 'Default slot convention: current entity is slot 1, related item is slot 0' — for every relation referenced from len/sum_where/count_where, and src/rulespec.rs uses derived_relation.current_slot/related_slot only as an override of that same inferred (1,0). Pre-fix and post-fix orientation are therefore identical. (2) The removed `arguments: [household_member, medicaid_applicant]` was never executable: src/rulespec.rs `is_relation_entity_kind_label` requires an ASCII-uppercase first byte, so those lowercase labels hit InvalidRelationArgumentEntityShape, whose message says the declaration 'is treated as undeclared and `slot_entities` is left empty'. (3) The new derived_relation's version formula is a tautology — `household_row_candidate_is_the_applicant or not household_row_candidate_is_the_applicant` — so it filters nothing. (4) A full pre-vs-post diff of the module (ignoring the renamed predicate lines) shows ONLY the rationale prose and this one relation block changed: all 20 sum_where/count_where formulas, every version, effective_from, parameter, input and output are byte-identical. (5) In the companion magi_household_income_pipeline.test.yaml, every pre-existing case keeps identical expected outputs and only has the relation input key renamed; the asymmetric orientation case still expects internal_current_month_household_pre_disregard_magi == 1330 before and after. The commit adds one new case, executable_relation_slot_reversal_surfaces_nonzero_opposite_side_value, which is purely a mutation probe. CAVEAT for a reviewer: PR #1007's maintainer review comment does contain a quotable direction finding — 'B3 — the declared relation argument order is reversed by the compiled sum, and the fixture harness masks it' — but that review targeted the pre-repair state; the earlier commit 30e2327e4 ('fix: repair Medicaid MAGI household pipeline', the only prior commit touching this file) is where the declared order was changed, and this commit only makes the already-correct orientation executable and testable. If the corpus wants the B3 orientation defect, screen 30e2327e4, not this commit. Its purpose is source-boundary hygiene rather than repair: because the pinned corpus's provision layer for the five cited Idaho Title 63 sections contains only site-navigation wrapper text and no substantive statutory body, the module accepts only federal AGI and raw residency/filing-unit facts, holds every Idaho stage (income after modifications, taxable income, tax before credits, tax after nonrefundable credits, refundable credits, net liability) under typed source holds, and emits fail-closed zero sentinels that are explicitly disclaimed as non-legal-claims.

modules.description_quote: fail closed with typed source holds where the retained official corpus does not establish an operative complete current-year chain
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: there is no pre-fix module to be wrong — the file is net-new in this commit (status 'added', pre_lines 0), so no previously encoded meaning was corrected against the source.
modules.triage_notes: NOT A PRE/POST FIDELITY PAIR. `git show --name-status` confirms the commit's full scope is four paths, three of them additions (the module, its .test.yaml, its .axiom/encoding-manifests JSON) plus the regenerated .axiom/index/provisions_to_rules.json; nothing existing was modified or deleted. The screen's description ('re-grounding of an existing module') is inaccurate for this commit: the entire module, all 15 rules, and all 3 inputs arrive at once with no prior version. I used 'mechanical' as the non-fidelity exclusion bucket rather than 'unclear', because the evidence settles the question (a net-new file cannot correct encoded meaning); the taxonomy has no 'net-new module' class, so treat 'mechanical' here as 'exclude from the defect corpus', not as 'only hashes changed'. Under the stated rubric this is at worst the 'adds new outputs/scope the module never claimed' case, which is explicitly not a defect. Possible source of the screen's 'existing module' framing: a separate, older Idaho income-tax module `us-id/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml` already existed at the parent commit (8b5e7a18, 97 lines) and encodes a caller-supplied flat-rate 63-3024 slice with proof_validation.required: false. This commit leaves that pilot module completely untouched — the new source-hold module sits beside it, so any 're-grounding' of the pilot would have to happen in a later commit, not here. Provision WAS read (step 4) to check the module's own rationale: resolve_provision.py for us-id/statute/63-3024 at this rulespec commit returns 955 chars that are entirely Idaho Legislature site chrome ('Senate Senate Leadership ... How current is this law?') with no statutory text, corroborating the module's claim that 'the corpus provision layer failed to extract the substantive provisions' and that fail-closed holds, not encoded amounts, are the honest output. All Money rules are literal '0' sentinels and all hold Judgments are literal 'true'; the module itself disclaims that these are legal claims. No maintainer or reviewer text anywhere in the commit message, PR body, or the two issue comments describes a defect being corrected — the commit message is a bare one-line subject with an empty body, PR reviews and review_comments arrays are both empty, and the two PavelMakarchuk issue comments are CI/merge-gate status only (one notes an unrelated repository baseline guard mismatch on us-co/regulations/9-ccr-2503-6/3.606.1/E.yaml, issue #782). A fidelity judge benchmarked on this pair would have no wrong-to-right transition to detect.

item.subject: (screen-flagged) Pins the Kansas 2026 rate determination: adds effective_period proof atoms citing Notice 25-06 and changes upstream_source_check status from checked_higher_authority_with_typed_holds to checked_higher_authority (effective-period grounding of rates).
item.screen_reason: Pins the Kansas 2026 rate determination: adds effective_period proof atoms citing Notice 25-06 and changes upstream_source_check status from checked_higher_authority_with_typed_holds to checked_higher_authority (effective-period grounding of rates).

triage.commit_summary: The commit pins the evidentiary basis for the Kansas tax-year-2026 individual income tax rate schedule in us-ks/policies/income_tax/2026_full_year_resident_core.yaml: it adds Kansas Department of Revenue Notice 25-06 to the module's source_verification citation list and upstream_source_check checked_paths, adds one `kind: effective_period` proof atom to each of the two rate parameters citing that notice, and rewrites the rationale to say the contingent rate reduction did not trigger for 2026. It also relaxes upstream_source_check.status from checked_higher_authority_with_typed_holds to checked_higher_authority; no formula, parameter value, version window, effective date, input, output, or scope changed anywhere in the module.

modules.description_quote: Kansas Department of Revenue Notice 25-06 establishes that the contingent rate-reduction conditions were not met and the statutory schedule remains in force for tax year 2026.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing in the encoded meaning was wrong: the pre-fix rates 0.052 and 0.0558 over 2026-01-01..2026-12-31 already match K.S.A. 79-32,110(a)(1)(B) and (a)(2)(B) ('For tax year 2024, and all tax years thereafter ... 5.2% of Kansas taxable income ... 5.58% of excess over $46,000'); the module merely lacked a cited authority showing that the 79-32,110c contingent rate reduction had not fired for 2026, so the change is provenance/grounding rather than a correction of encoded meaning.
modules.triage_notes: Read the full diff plus the pre-fix (8a97a9cece) and post-fix (4b822bdbad) module. The entire change set is: (1) one new corpus_citation_path (us-ks/guidance/revenue/notice-25-06/document-1) in source_verification.corpus_citation_paths and in upstream_source_check.checked_paths; (2) upstream_source_check.status checked_higher_authority_with_typed_holds -> checked_higher_authority (module-level metadata; no rule hold or fail-closed branch was removed -- the SB 82 gun-storage hold, the deferred_outputs list, and the 'are typed holds' sentence later in the rationale all survive unchanged); (3) a rewritten rationale paragraph; (4) two added proof atoms of kind effective_period, one on each rate parameter, both citing Notice 25-06 with excerpt 'there will be no rate reduction for tax year 2026'. The versions lines '{effective_from: 2026-01-01, effective_to: 2026-12-31, formula: 0.052}' and '... 0.0558' are byte-identical before and after, as is every other rule. Under the stated rubric this is proof-atom / citation-path / metadata / summary change with formulas, parameters, versions, effective dates, inputs, outputs and scope held constant, i.e. mechanical (provenance). Provision was read: resolve_provision.py on us-ks/statute/2026/79-32-110/block-1 (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union) confirms the 5.2%/5.58% schedule for 'tax year 2024, and all tax years thereafter', applied 'unless otherwise modified pursuant to K.S.A. 2025 Supp. 79-32,110c' -- 110c is the contingent-reduction hook, and it was already in the module's citation list pre-fix, so the pre-fix encoding was not ungrounded, only under-evidenced on the contingency. Quote caveat: the quoted sentence is an added rationale line inside the module diff, stored in a YAML block scalar and hard-wrapped across five '+' lines; I joined the wrapped lines with single spaces and changed no words. Commit message body is empty (subject only: 'Pin Kansas 2026 rate determination'); the linked PR 1083 body describes the whole Kansas branch (three commits: 8ba6de05e add, 8a97a9cec attest, this one) and has no reviews or review comments, so no reviewer text names a defect. Residual doubt, noted for the pruning reviewer: one could read the pre-fix state as asserting a 2026 rate whose continued force was unverified (a wrong_period_or_effective_date-flavored evidentiary gap), and the screen flag calls it 'effective-period grounding of rates' -- but since no encoded value, window, or branch changed, no downstream computation differs before vs after, which is why I did not classify it fidelity or unclear.

modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The PTE-refundability proof atom cited corpus page-1333, which does not contain the quoted excerpt (the sentence begins on page-1334), so the provenance pointer was mis-grounded — but the encoded meaning itself was not wrong.

Three hunks: (a) add `us-il/statute/public-act/104-0468/page-1334` to module.source_verification.corpus_citation_paths, (b) add the same path to module.source_verification.upstream_source_check.checked_paths, (c) change the third proof atom of rule il_pit_2026_credit_source_hold_applies from page-1333 to page-1334. Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus (resolve_provision.py, rulespec-commit 364586f6d1): page-1333 ends mid-sentence with '...If the SB3019 Enrolled LRB104 20255 HLH 33706 b Public Act 104-0468' and page-1334 opens with the atom's exact excerpt 'amount of the credit allowed under this paragraph exceeds the partner's or shareholder's liability for tax imposed under subsections (a) and (b) of Section 201...'. Per the stated triage rule that excerpt-only and citation-string-only corrections are provenance, this is mechanical, not fidelity — it is not untraceable_branch because no formula was re-grounded or removed and the substantive provision (the PTE entity-level credit refundability sentence, 35 ILCS 5/201 via P.A. 104-0468) is the same continuous text. page-1333 remains declared at module level after the fix but is no longer cited by any atom (neither is page-1290); that pre-existing looseness is unchanged by this commit. The bundle's attached PR is #1074 ('Encode Illinois 2026 full-year resident income-tax core', merged 2026-07-24), the parent encoding PR, whose body describes the general corpus-pin audit but says nothing specific about this page-1333/1334 correction; reviews, review_comments and issue_comments are all empty, so the commit subject is the only quotable maintainer statement. Commit body is empty.

item.subject: (screen-flagged) Holds unsupported South Dakota credit stages in an existing module: scope/retire correction.
item.screen_reason: Holds unsupported South Dakota credit stages in an existing module: scope/retire correction.

triage.commit_summary: The commit retracts the South Dakota 2026 resident personal-income-tax module's claim that no credit stage applies and that the post-credit and net-liability stages are substantively zero, because the only pinned authority (the Department of Revenue's January 2026 Sales and Use Tax Guide, "South Dakota does not have a corporate, unitary, or personal income tax") proves only the pre-credit zero. It deletes the unsupported Boolean rule sd_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies (formula false), adds three typed Judgment source-hold rules for nonrefundable credits, refundable credits, and signed net liability, declares the three downstream money outputs as module-level deferred_outputs whose zeros are fail-closed sentinels, and updates the four companion cases to assert "holds" instead of the retired credit-stage false.

modules.description_quote: Hold unsupported South Dakota credit stages
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module asserted, as a source-backed output, that no personal-income-tax credit stage applies (sd_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies = false) and that the after-nonrefundable-credit, refundable-credit, and net-liability amounts are substantively zero, all grounded on a sales-and-use-tax guide sentence that establishes only the absence of a personal income tax before credits and says nothing about credits, credit ordering, or signed net liability.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us-sd/guidance/revenue/2026/sales-and-use-tax-guide/document-1, 47,544 chars): the phrase 'personal income tax' appears exactly once, in the 'Tax Basics' sentence used as the excerpt; the document contains no personal-income-tax credit, refundable-credit, or net-liability material, confirming the pre-fix branches had no basis in the cited source. Single-module commit; it also rewrites module.summary and upstream_source_check.rationale, adds a module.deferred_outputs block, and rewrites the companion test (sd_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies: false replaced by three '... _source_hold_applies: holds' expectations) plus the encoding manifest and .axiom/toolchain.toml. Numeric formulas for the three money outputs stay 0, so execution values do not change; what changes is the retracted Boolean output, the new typed Judgment holds (dtype Judgment, entity TaxUnit, effective_from 2026-01-01 / effective_to 2026-12-31, formula true), and the claim status of the zeros - a reviewer could argue this is hold/provenance discipline rather than a value correction, which is the main residual doubt. Note a self-inflicted slip inside this commit: the 'Fail-closed sentinel pending complete nonrefundable-credit authority' source label was attached to sd_pit_2026_resident_personal_income_tax_before_credits (the stage that IS source-backed) while sd_pit_2026_resident_personal_income_tax_after_nonrefundable_credits (a deferred output) kept the substantive label; the immediate follow-up commit 99c78e257 'Correct South Dakota source provenance' swaps those two labels back and also repoints us-sd/statute/10/43/2/block-1 to .../operative-text. Additional supporting prose added by this diff inside the module: "The pinned authority does not establish the absence of independently refundable credits or a complete signed net-liability surface." PR #1065 has no reviews or review comments; its body describes the post-fix state ('credit, refund, and terminal-liability zeros remain fail-closed sentinels behind typed holds').

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical and as not-a-defect and both fail: the diff retires the output `sd_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies` (dtype Boolean, formula false), replaces it with three `Judgment` source-hold rules whose formula is `true` with a new `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` window, and rewrites the companion test expectations from `sd_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies: false` to three `... _source_hold_applies: holds` entries — encoded meaning and output surface, not bookkeeping. The pre-fix encoding asserted, as source-backed outputs, that no credit stage applies and that the refundable-credit and signed net-liability amounts are zero, all proved by the single excerpt "South Dakota does not have a corporate, unitary, or personal income tax"; I read that provision through the pinned release (corpus_release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union) and the Sales and Use Tax Guide's only credit/refund language is sales-tax trade-in, returned-merchandise and credit-card-fee text, nothing about personal-income-tax credits, ordering, or signed net liability. So those values had no basis in the cited source and the fix removes/re-grounds them behind typed holds, which is exactly untraceable_branch; the author's own subject calls them "unsupported". The nearest alternative kind, wrong_entity_or_scope (the summary retracts "Complete ... pipeline" and the screen label says "scope/retire correction"), is a consequence of the ungrounded values rather than a mis-targeted entity or population, so it fits worse.
verdict.quote:
-  - name: sd_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies
+  - name: sd_pit_2026_nonrefundable_credit_source_hold_applies
-    dtype: Boolean
+    dtype: Judgment
-        formula: false
+        formula: true
verdict.notes: Caveats for the reviewer. (1) Strength is uneven across the three held stages: `after_nonrefundable_credits = 0` follows arithmetically from `before_credits = 0` (nonrefundable credits cannot go below zero), so that zero was defensible; the genuinely ungrounded ones are the refundable-credit zero and the signed net-liability zero, since a refundable credit can exist without an income tax. The defect is real but narrower than "all credit stages". (2) No computed Money value changes: all three Money outputs still have literal `formula: 0` and the formulas never reference the new hold rules — the fail-closed status lives only in `source:` strings, the new module-level `deferred_outputs` block, and the new Judgment outputs. A consumer reading only the numbers gets the same zeros; the meaning change is carried by the retired Boolean output, the three new `holds` outputs, and the test expectations. (3) This commit also introduced an off-by-one in the source relabeling: `sd_pit_2026_resident_personal_income_tax_before_credits` (the one output the authority does support) was labeled "Fail-closed sentinel pending complete nonrefundable-credit authority" while `..._after_nonrefundable_credits` kept "South Dakota Department of Revenue, no personal income tax"; the very next commit 99c78e257 swaps those two lines back. (4) Provenance: this is an intra-PR self-correction, not a fix to long-merged content — `git log --follow` on the module shows only efd821a3e (create), 551f1ac46f (this hold), 99c78e257 (provenance), all in PR #1065 merged 2026-07-24. If the corpus is meant to capture defects that survived into merged production rules, flag it on that ground rather than on kind.

item.subject: (screen-flagged) Holds incomplete Nevada credit liability stages in an existing module: scope/retire correction.
item.screen_reason: Holds incomplete Nevada credit liability stages in an existing module: scope/retire correction.

triage.commit_summary: The commit reworks the Nevada tax-year-2026 resident personal-income-tax module so that only the pre-credit zero remains a source-backed claim: it deletes the `nv_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies: false` rule, adds three typed Judgment source-hold rules plus a module-level `deferred_outputs` block, and relabels the after-nonrefundable-credit, refundable-credit, and net-liability outputs as fail-closed sentinels rather than substantive zeros. It also adds a rule grounded in the constitution's official amendment-history source note to establish that the pinned prohibition text is current for tax year 2026, and updates the companion test to assert the holds instead of the retired credit-stage flag.

modules.description_quote: This authority proves zero natural-person personal income tax before credits. It does not prove that Nevada has no independently refundable credit or otherwise establish a complete signed net-liability surface.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module asserted, on the authority of Nev. Const. art. 10, section 1(9) and the excerpt "No income tax shall be levied upon the wages or personal income of natural persons.", that no credit stage applies and that after-nonrefundable-credit tax, refundable credits, and net liability before payments are all zero, but that provision only bars a tax on natural persons' wages and personal income and says nothing about whether Nevada has independently refundable credits or how credits order into a signed net liability, so those branches and values had no basis in the cited source.
modules.triage_notes: Single-module commit; only the module file, its companion test, the encoding manifest, the reverse index, and toolchain.toml changed. Provision was read through the pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, resolver reports fix_time_corpus_match: same_body): 26-word text confirms subsection 9 covers only the wage/personal-income prohibition plus the business-income carve-out, with no credit or net-liability content. The commit is an in-PR self-correction: its parent 825294c6 ("Complete Nevada 2026 resident zero liability") introduced the module claiming a "Complete Nevada full-year-resident natural-person personal-income-tax pipeline", and both commits landed in merged PR #1059, whose body describes only the corrected end state ("retain typed source holds for nonrefundable credits, refundable credits, and signed net liability before payments"; "downstream credit and net-liability stages remain explicitly held and fail closed"). The commit message body is empty; the quote used is from the module's own rewritten upstream_source_check rationale in the diff (YAML block scalar, so line wrapping was joined with single spaces). Note the three Money outputs keep formula: 0 — what changed is their status (source strings become "Fail-closed sentinel pending ...", plus the new deferred_outputs block and Judgment holds); the only formula/rule existence change is the deletion of nv_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies (was false) and the three added hold rules (formula: true, effective_from 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31). The companion test drops the `nv_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies: false` expectation and rewrites its header comment from "deductions, exemptions, surtaxes, and credits cannot change the legal zero" to exclude credits, confirming that the withdrawn claim was substantive. Alternative kind considered: wrong_entity_or_scope (the module retracted output surface it never had authority for); untraceable_branch was chosen because the decisive edit removes/re-grounds branches and values whose only cited basis was a provision that does not support them. The parallel rules nv_pit_2026_deduction_and_exemption_stage_applies and nv_pit_2026_surtax_stage_applies remain false on the same excerpt and were left untouched, which is a residual inconsistency a reviewer may want to note but is outside this commit.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical/provenance and as a mere conservatism policy choice, and both fail on one edit: the rule `nv_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies` (dtype Boolean, `formula: false`) is deleted outright from the module and from both companion test expectations, so the module's output surface and asserted meaning change, not just labels. Its sole proof atom cited excerpt "No income tax shall be levied upon the wages or personal income of natural persons.", and the pinned corpus text of Nev. Const. art. 10 § 1(9) (resolved at aada034367: corpus release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, body sha 865d525f…) says only that and that business income or revenue may still be taxed — it says nothing about credits, credit ordering, or refundable credits, so `credit_stage_applies = false` was a value with no basis in the cited source and the fix removes it. The fix's own module rationale states the standard explicitly ("This authority proves zero natural-person personal income tax before credits. It does not prove that Nevada has no independently refundable credit…"), which is the untraceable_branch test rather than an amount, boundary, period, or polarity error. I weighed reclassifying to wrong_entity_or_scope (the screen label says "scope/retire" and the summary retracts "Complete … pipeline"), but entity, population, period, and the retained outputs' formulas are untouched — the only meaning that changed is the removal of an ungrounded assertion, so untraceable_branch fits better.
verdict.quote: -  - name: nv_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies
verdict.notes:
Corroborating verbatim lines: in the companion test diff, "-    us-nv:policies/income_tax/2026_resident_zero_liability#nv_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies: false" (removed at two cases), and in the test header comment "+# Credit and net-liability amounts below are fail-closed sentinels guarded by" / "+# explicit typed source holds, not substantive zero-liability assertions."

Caveat a reviewer should see (why I set confidence at 0.7, not higher): all three downstream Money outputs (`..._after_nonrefundable_credits`, `..._refundable_personal_income_tax_credits`, `..._net_personal_income_tax_liability_before_payments`) keep `formula: 0`, the same entity/dtype/unit, the same effective_from '2026-01-01' with no effective_to, and byte-identical proof atoms; only their `source:` label strings change (e.g. "-    source: Nev. Const. art. 10, § 1(9), no natural-person personal income-tax system" → "+    source: Fail-closed sentinel pending complete refundable-credit authority"). Taken alone, that part of the diff is provenance/labelling, i.e. mechanical. The fidelity content rests on (a) the deletion of `nv_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies` (verified fully absent at aada034367 via `git grep` over us-nv and .axiom) and (b) the new module-level `deferred_outputs:` block plus three added `dtype: Judgment` rules (`nv_pit_2026_nonrefundable_credit_source_hold_applies`, `..._refundable_credit_source_hold_applies`, `..._net_liability_source_hold_applies`, each `formula: true`, windowed 2026-01-01..2026-12-31), which the tests now assert as `holds`. I did not read engine code for how `deferred_outputs` or a `Judgment` hold is enforced at runtime, so I do not claim the zeros stop being served — I rely only on the removed rule and the changed test surface.

Also added, unrelated to the credit question: `nv_pit_2026_constitutional_prohibition_current_for_tax_year` (Boolean true, grounded on the newly pinned source-note block with amendment-history excerpts), and the header change `corpus_citation_path` → `corpus_citation_paths` with `status: complete_current_authority` → `official_parameter_source`. That pairing is period-grounding evidence for tax year 2026, additive coverage rather than a second defect; the pre-fix module already carried effective_from '2026-01-01', so I did not treat it as wrong_period_or_effective_date.

PR #1059 has no reviews or review comments in the bundle, and the commit body is empty, so all fidelity evidence came from the diff itself plus the resolved provision text.

item.subject: (screen-flagged) Adds a guard on the WIC pregnancy income adjustment: branch/logic correction to an existing module.
item.screen_reason: Adds a guard on the WIC pregnancy income adjustment: branch/logic correction to an existing module.

triage.commit_summary: The commit adds a pregnancy guard to the WIC person-level eligibility pipeline so the 7 CFR 246.7(d)(2)(vii) unborn-child income adjustment can only establish income eligibility when the applicant is actually in the pregnant-woman category, instead of being a free-standing disjunct usable by any category. It also adds one companion test (unborn_child_adjustment_cannot_passport_nonpregnant_category) showing an infant applicant with the imported pregnancy-adjustment facts set is now income-ineligible and WIC-ineligible, plus a proof atom grounding the new condition in the 246.7(c) "pregnant women" subject predicate.

modules.description_quote: unborn-child adjustment gated to the pregnant-woman category
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix formula let the imported pregnant_applicant_income_guidelines_satisfied_with_unborn_children disjunct establish WIC income eligibility for any applicant category, although 7 CFR 246.7(d)(2)(vii) ("Income eligibility of pregnant women. A pregnant woman who is ineligible for participation in the program because she does not meet income guidelines...") scopes that route to pregnant women only, so a non-pregnant applicant (e.g. an infant) could be passported over the income ceiling.
modules.triage_notes: Single-module commit (module + its companion test only); the module diff is exactly two hunks: the added `kind: condition` proof atom (citation us/regulation/7/246/7/c, excerpt "pregnant women") and the formula change wrapping the unborn-child disjunct in `wic_applicant_is_pregnant_woman and (...)`. Nothing unrelated changed: no versions, effective dates, parameters, imports, or other rules moved. Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus release (us/regulation/7/246/7/d, expression_date 2026-07-13, fix_time_corpus_match same_body); paragraph (vii) is titled "Income eligibility of pregnant women" and its subject is "A pregnant woman". The root cause is a composition contamination: the imported 246.7(d) module gates on its own runtime input `applicant_is_pregnant`, while the pipeline carries a separate category input `wic_applicant_is_pregnant_woman`, and pre-fix nothing tied the two, so inconsistent caller facts fired the pregnancy route for a non-pregnant category (exactly the added test case). Kind call is between wrong_entity_or_scope (route applied to the wrong population) and unrepresented_clause (the source's pregnant-woman subject predicate was missing and the fix adds it); I chose wrong_entity_or_scope because the pre-fix defect is the branch reaching applicants outside the paragraph's population, hence confidence 0.65 rather than higher. Note for the reviewer: paragraph (vii) also says "The same increased family size may also be used for any of the pregnant woman's categorically eligible family members", which this guard does not encode, but that extension was never encoded in the imported (d) rule either, so it is a pre-existing gap rather than something this commit introduced. This commit is a repair round inside PR #1010 (merged 2026-07-26); the separate blind-review finding about the 185%-FPG vs operative State guideline is fixed by the later commit fc95ef853 "Fix WIC State eligibility boundaries", not here. The PR has no formal reviews/review_comments; the only quotable maintainer text is the PR body and one issue comment (blind review) that does not name this particular finding.

verdict.justification: The diff does change encoded meaning (it adds a `wic_applicant_is_pregnant_woman and ...` conjunct to a disjunct of `wic_income_eligible`), but the first reader's premise — that the pre-fix formula let the unborn-child route establish income eligibility "for any applicant category" — is only half true: the imported rule it calls, `us:regulations/7-cfr/246/7/d#pregnant_applicant_income_guidelines_satisfied_with_unborn_children` (unchanged by this commit), already begins `applicant_is_pregnant and ...`, so the source's "A pregnant woman who is ineligible..." predicate was represented in the encoding before the fix. The route could therefore only fire for a non-pregnant category when the caller supplied contradictory facts across two redundant, separately-declared pregnancy booleans (`#input.applicant_is_pregnant: true` together with `wic_applicant_is_pregnant_woman: false, wic_applicant_is_infant: true`, exactly the added test vector), which reads as cross-module input-coherence hardening at the composed surface rather than a formula that disagrees with the cited text. Cutting the other way, 7 CFR 246.7(d)(2)(vii) in the pinned release adds "The same increased family size may also be used for any of the pregnant woman's categorically eligible family members," so a hard gate to the pregnant-woman category is not obviously closer to the source than the looser pre-fix form; the evidence does not settle whether the old text was wrong.
verdict.quote:
+          or (
+            wic_applicant_is_pregnant_woman
+            and pregnant_applicant_income_guidelines_satisfied_with_unborn_children
+          )
verdict.notes:
Refutation evidence, all read this session. (1) `git -C /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us show 044fe328f2:us/regulations/7-cfr/246/7/d.yaml` — rule `pregnant_applicant_income_guidelines_satisfied_with_unborn_children` formula is already `applicant_is_pregnant
and applicant_ineligible_only_because_income_guidelines_not_met
and income_guidelines_would_be_met_by_increasing_family_size_for_embryos_or_fetuses
and not applicant_waives_unborn_child_family_size_increase`; `git diff --stat 044fe328f2 2cf80aa971 -- us/regulations/7-cfr/246/7/d.yaml` is empty, so the pregnancy predicate was present both before and after. (2) The companion test added by the same commit, `unborn_child_adjustment_cannot_passport_nonpregnant_category`, sets `us:regulations/7-cfr/246/7/d#input.applicant_is_pregnant: true` alongside `wic_applicant_is_pregnant_woman: false` / `wic_applicant_is_infant: true` — i.e. the only reachable fail-open needs mutually contradictory caller facts across two duplicate pregnancy inputs the pipeline never bound together. (3) Pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-cms-435-correction-immutable-scopes, body sha256 38bf1a18f32c3ad0dd5b66296e4467cb6542a3b5e2d598a4f21bfb3d547e28f8) for us/regulation/7/246/7/d, paragraph (vii): "Income eligibility of pregnant women. A pregnant woman who is ineligible for participation in the program because she does not meet income guidelines shall be considered to have satisfied the income guidelines if the guidelines would be met by increasing the number of individuals in her family by the number of embryos or fetuses in utero. The same increased family size may also be used for any of the pregnant woman's categorically eligible family members." That second sentence is the reader's own infant counterexample, permissively allowed by the source — the module has no family-linkage input to represent it either way, so the post-fix hard gate is not demonstrably more faithful. (4) Provenance flag for the reviewer: the proof atom the fix adds grounds the new guard on `us/regulation/7/246/7/c` with `excerpt: "pregnant women"`, and that string does not occur in paragraph (c) of the pinned text (it reads "infants, children, and pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding women"); the scoping language lives in (d)(2)(vii), not (c). (5) The first reader's justification quote, "unborn-child adjustment gated to the pregnant-woman category", comes from the PR #1010 body, which describes the shipped post-fix design, not a reviewer finding of a defect; the only review text on the PR (MaxGhenis blind review) raises the 185%-vs-State-guideline issue and never mentions this gate. If a reviewer decides the composed surface is authoritative and counts the unbound duplicate input as a real fail-open, wrong_entity_or_scope is the kind to keep, though "fail-open disjunct / cross-module input-coherence" (polarity_or_logic) is the more literal description of what changed.

item.screen_reason: Reworks the already-encoded South Carolina core: removes the section 12-6-1130(2) itemized tax addback rule and its inputs and replaces the EITC formula (98 deletions alongside additions).

triage.commit_summary: The commit reworks the just-encoded South Carolina tax-year-2026 full-year-resident income-tax core so it reflects 2026 Act No. 110 (H.4216): it repins the corpus to b157a201 (the Act 110 overlay merged as axiom-corpus#503), replaces the pre-Act-110 section 12-6-1130(2) state-and-local-tax itemized addback with a full federal Section 63 standard/itemized deduction reversal grounded on the newly enacted section 12-6-50(21), adds the entire filing-status/AGI-phased South Carolina Income Adjusted Deduction of section 12-6-1140(15) (bases, phaseout starts, denominators, next-lowest-ten-dollar rounding), and caps the section 12-6-3632 earned-income credit at two hundred dollars as Act 110 amended it. It also rewrites the input-domain coherence guard for the new itemized/standard input semantics, drops the now-unused SALT-in-itemized input, adds a federal-AGI input and a regular-workday ceiling, and expands the companion test file by roughly 1,259 lines.

modules.description_quote: reverses the federal standard or itemized deduction that Act 110 no longer adopts, applies directly supported Article 9 items and the filing-status/AGI-based SCIAD
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: For tax year 2026 the pre-fix module omitted three clauses Act 110 enacted in the cited sections: it added back only the section 12-6-1130(2) state-and-local-tax sliver (capped at itemized-over-standard excess) instead of reversing the whole federal Section 63 standard or itemized deduction that section 12-6-50(21) says is "hereby specifically not allowed or adopted", it granted no South Carolina Income Adjusted Deduction under section 12-6-1140(15), and it computed the section 12-6-3632 earned-income credit as an uncapped 125 percent of the federal EITC despite the statute's "but not to exceed two hundred dollars".
modules.triage_notes:
Single module in the commit; one chunk, fully covered. Provisions were read directly out of the corpus overlay this commit pins (axiom-corpus b157a201, file data/corpus/provisions/us-sc/statute/2026-07-24-sc-act110-us-sc-title-12-chapter-6.jsonl): 12-6-50(21) non-adoption of IRC Section 63(b)-(g); 12-6-1140(15) SCIAD bases 15,000/22,500/30,000, phaseout starts 40,000/60,000/80,000, denominators 55,000/82,500/110,000, reduction rounded to the next lowest ten dollars, no deduction when the fraction reaches one; 12-6-3632 amended by 2026 Act No. 110 SECTION 7 to add "but not to exceed two hundred dollars". All three post-fix encodings match that text.

IMPORTANT FOR BENCHMARK USE: resolve_provision.py at this commit returns PRE-Act-110 text for 12-6-50, 12-6-1140 and 12-6-3632 (it selects release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-cms-435-correction-immutable-scopes / provision file 2026-07-16-pit-central-us-sc-title-12-chapter-6.jsonl, not the overlay release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-sc-act110-current added by the pinned corpus commit). A judge shown only the resolver output would see no SCIAD, no Section 63(b) non-adoption and no $200 cap, and could wrongly score the post-fix module as ungrounded. The Act 110 text must be supplied from the overlay file.

Provenance nuance: this commit also repins .axiom/toolchain.toml axiom_corpus_ref 4c174389 -> b157a201. The older corpus DID already carry Act 110's 12-6-510 two-bracket rate schedule (1.99%/5.21%, $30,000 floor) but not the 12-6-50(21), 12-6-1140(15) or 12-6-3632 amendments, so the pre-fix encoding was internally consistent with its own pinned corpus while disagreeing with the actual 2026 statute. That makes it a real fidelity defect, but one a verifier can only catch with the complete source.

Kind is contestable: the removal of sc_pit_2026_candidate_itemized_tax_addback and its re-grounding from 12-6-1130(2) to 12-6-50(21) also reads as untraceable_branch (formula grounded on a provision Act 110 displaced for individuals), and the whole change could be framed as wrong_period_or_effective_date (2026-windowed versions encoding pre-amendment text). I chose unrepresented_clause because the bulk of the fix ADDS statutory clauses (SCIAD machinery, the full Section 63 reversal, the EITC cap) that the source states and the pre-fix module lacked. Note 12-6-1130(2) itself is NOT repealed in the Act 110 text; removing its rule is defensible only because the entire federal itemized deduction is now added back, so a separate SALT addback would double count - a reviewer may want to confirm that reading.

Ancillary changes in the same diff: (a) sc_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid's itemized/standard coherence guard rewritten for the new input semantics (federal_standard_deduction == 0 when itemizing, and vice versa) and two workday <= ceiling bounds added; (b) new derived sc_pit_2026_regular_workday_count_ceiling = days_between(period_start, period_end) + 1; (c) a redundant nursing-care condition (private_nursing_care_expenses == 0 or nursing_care_level_is_physician_certified) removed from sc_pit_2026_supported_profile_applies - the credit rule sc_pit_2026_candidate_nursing_care_credit already fail-closes to 0 without certification in the pre-fix file, so this widens the supported profile rather than fixing a defect; (d) EITC formula also gained a defensive max(0, federal_earned_income_credit_allowed); (e) inputs: sc_pit_2026_state_local_income_or_sales_taxes_in_federal_itemized_deductions dropped, sc_pit_2026_federal_adjusted_gross_income added, three descriptions rewritten; (f) several proof-atom excerpt strings lengthened (mechanical provenance).

Context: this is a fix-up commit on PR #1042 branch encode/sc-2026-e2e-resident; the original encoding is 89ab7ae57 and later branch commits are 9988f05f0 (input-contract YAML parsing) and 49f2659d1 (manifest attestation). PR #1042 has no reviews or review comments describing this rework - its body and the single issue comment describe only the final state, so no reviewer text names the defect.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this three ways (new-coverage-not-a-defect, untraceable_branch for the removed 12-6-1130(2) rule, amount_mismatch for the EITC change) and all three fail against the pinned source. Reading the Act 110 overlay at the toolchain corpus ref (us-sc/statute 2026-07-24-sc-act110 records), the source states three things the pre-fix module simply did not encode for TY2026: 12-6-50(21) "Section 63(b) through (g) ... which are hereby specifically not allowed or adopted", 12-6-1140(15) "a South Carolina Income Adjusted Deduction (SCIAD) equal to: (i) fifteen thousand dollars...", and 12-6-3632's "but not to exceed two hundred dollars" (2026 Act No. 110, SECTION 7) — and the fix adds each as a formula/parameter change, not as metadata. This is not merely added scope: the pre-fix module already listed us-sc/statute/12-6-50 in corpus_citation_paths, held none of these branches in deferred_outputs, and exposed a supported-profile taxable income and EITC that were therefore wrong for an ordinary supported filer, so the omissions are fidelity defects and unrepresented_clause is the fitting kind.
verdict.quote:
-          sc_pit_2026_candidate_net_capital_gain_deduction
+          sc_pit_2026_candidate_sciad
+          + sc_pit_2026_candidate_net_capital_gain_deduction
verdict.notes:
Source verification detail (important for anyone re-running this): resolve_provision.py selected release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-cms-435-correction-immutable-scopes (corpus commit cbf3d249), whose 12-6-50 record stops at item (20) and contains no SCIAD/EITC-cap text — it predates the Act 110 overlay. The toolchain ref the module actually pins is b157a201 (axiom-corpus#503), which adds data/corpus/provisions/us-sc/statute/2026-07-24-sc-act110-us-sc-title-12-chapter-6.jsonl; I read 12-6-50, 12-6-1140 and 12-6-3632 from that overlay via `git -C axiom-corpus show b157a201:...`. Do not conclude from the resolver output alone that the added rules are ungrounded; they are grounded, with the statute's amounts (15000/22500/30000 bases, 40000/60000/80000 phaseout starts, 55000/82500/110000 denominators, next-lowest-ten-dollar rounding, 200 EITC cap) matching verbatim.
Why not untraceable_branch: 12-6-1130(2) is byte-identical in the pre-Act-110 and Act 110 records (I compared the bodies), so the deleted sc_pit_2026_candidate_itemized_tax_addback rule was grounded in in-force text; its removal is a consequence of implementing 12-6-50(21) (adding back the whole federal Section 63 deduction subsumes the SALT sliver and would otherwise double count), not an independent re-grounding. Why not amount_mismatch: the pre-fix EITC formula had no cap at all (`formula: sc_pit_2026_eitc_match_rate * sc_pit_2026_federal_earned_income_credit_allowed`), so the fix adds a missing limitation clause rather than correcting a number. Why not wrong_period: every version window stayed 2026-01-01/2026-12-31.
Curation caveat for the reviewer: this is an intra-PR revision, not a post-merge repair. The module was created at 89ab7ae57 and completed at 68b3063a92, and both landed together in PR #1042 (merged 2026-07-24), so the defective state never reached main. The classification as a fidelity defect stands on the source comparison; whether an intra-PR iteration belongs in a "real defects" corpus is a separate curation call.
Secondary changes in the same commit, none of which change the kind: the supported-profile gate drops the nursing-care physician-certification conjunct (the credit rule at post line 1288 still branches on it, so no fidelity loss), the input domain adds a regular-workday ceiling and reworks the itemized/standard mutual-exclusivity condition, and a new sc_pit_2026_federal_adjusted_gross_income input is required by the SCIAD phaseout. Two proof-atom excerpt strings (12-6-1120 Section 78/86, 12-6-3330 Section 62) were also lengthened — provenance-only, mechanical.
Tooling hazard: the scratchpad directory appears to be shared across the parallel verifier subagents of this run. A file I wrote as scratchpad/pre.yaml was overwritten with another state's module (Delaware) mid-task; I re-read everything under sc68b_-prefixed filenames. Sibling verifiers should use unique basenames.

triage.commit_summary: The commit repairs the Wisconsin TY2026 full-year-resident income-tax module, which had been publishing completed annual gross tax, post-credit tax, and net liability computed from the continuous Form 1-ES estimated-tax bracket schedules. Because Wis. Stat. 71.06(3) requires annual tax to be determined from the Department's published Tax Table (bands of not more than $100, tax computed at the bracket midpoint, rounded to the nearest dollar), the fix demotes the Form 1-ES chain to private "estimated tax schedule ... probe" rules, adds a typed annual-tax-table source hold, and zeroes/fails closed the three public annual outputs, re-grounding their proof atoms from the Form 1-ES document onto us-wi/statute/71.06.

modules.description_quote: Independent review found that the original candidate incorrectly treated continuous Form 1-ES schedules as the annual Tax Table required by Wis. Stat. § 71.06(3).
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module grounded its public annual Wisconsin gross tax (and the post-credit tax and net liability derived from it) on the continuous Form 1-ES estimated-tax bracket schedule (base + rate * (taxable income - floor), proof atom us-wi/form/individual-income-tax/2026/1-es/document-1, excerpt "The 2026 Gross Tax is"), whereas Wis. Stat. 71.06(3) requires annual personal income tax to be determined from the secretary of revenue's published Tax Table using brackets of not more than $100 with tax computed at the middle of each bracket to the nearest dollar, so the annual liability chain rested on a provision/document that does not supply the annual tax it claimed to compute.
modules.triage_notes: Read the provision: resolve_provision.py on us-wi/statute/71.06 (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, provision file data/corpus/provisions/us-wi/statute/2026-07-16-pit-west-chapter-71.jsonl, fix_time_corpus_match=same_body) returns subsection "(3) Tax table. The secretary of revenue shall prepare a table from which the tax in effect on taxable personal income shall be determined... (b) The first 2 columns shall contain the minimum and the maximum amounts, respectively, of taxable income in brackets of not more than $100... (c) ...rates shall be applied to the amount of income at the middle of each bracket. The amount of tax for each bracket shall be computed to the nearest dollar." That confirms the reviewer's stated ground. Kind chosen as untraceable_branch under the rule that formulas grounded on the wrong provision belong there; an alternative reading is amount_mismatch (continuous-schedule tax differs from midpoint/whole-dollar table tax by a few dollars), but the fix removes/re-grounds rather than re-values, and the reviewer framed it as the wrong source document, so untraceable_branch fits better. Scope of the single-module diff: three public Money rules changed from a supported-profile computation to constant 0 with re-grounded proof atoms; a new Judgment rule wi_pit_2026_annual_tax_table_source_hold_applies (formula: true) was added and OR-ed into wi_pit_2026_complete_liability_source_hold_applies; six private candidate rules were renamed to *_estimated_tax_schedule_*_probe with source strings rewritten; module description/summary prose was rewritten to match. Those renames and prose edits are provenance/bookkeeping riding along with the substantive hold, so the decisive change is the gross-tax formula. Provenance doubt worth a reviewer's eye: the new proof-atom excerpt "shall determine income tax from the tax table" is NOT a verbatim substring of the resolved 71.06 text (the statute reads "shall prepare a table from which the tax ... shall be determined"); it is a paraphrase, though that is a separate provenance issue, not the fidelity defect. Provenance of the defect itself: it was introduced in the immediate parent caa6e96f8 "Encode Wisconsin 2026 resident liability end to end" on the same PR branch (#1037) and repaired here before merge, so this is an intra-PR encoder defect caught by independent review rather than one that reached main. The commit body is empty; all quotable evidence is in the PR body. Non-module files in the commit (encoding manifest, oracle-coverage-pending.yaml, companion test file) moved consistently with the hold. Follow-up commits touching the same module later: e45d2f9e4 "Floor Wisconsin completed taxable income" and e1296d6c1 "Consolidate Wisconsin Form 1-ES schedule (#1111)". Bundle contained exactly the one module index expected for this chunk.

So the pre-fix divergence is bounded by midpoint/whole-dollar rounding inside the table range (a few dollars), not a structurally wrong tax. And the post-fix value `0` is not the statutory amount either — it is this repo's fail-closed hold convention, paired with the new hold Judgment; the screening line itself called this a "scope/retire correction." item.subject: (screen-flagged) Prevents Hawaii food credit child overlap: logic/double-counting correction.
item.screen_reason: Prevents Hawaii food credit child overlap: logic/double-counting correction.

triage.commit_summary: The commit replaced the Hawaii TY2026 food/excise credit's two separate special-minor inputs (children receiving DHS support and children receiving Social Security survivor benefits) with a single deduplicated count of distinct special-support minors, and updated the fail-closed input-domain guard and the companion suite to match. It was made because summing the two overlapping categories counted a child who received both kinds of support twice in the food-credit qualified-exemption total, while HRS §235-55.85(c) treats such a minor child as one qualified exemption; the new suite adds a case asserting one minor with both supports counts once (qualified exemption count 2, credit $340 rather than 3 / $510).

modules.description_quote: Findings covering signed final liability, the §235-53 tax-table range, CDCC assistance and spouse rules, completed-result inputs, renter proration, MFS support, domain bounds, threshold coverage, MFS credit counterfactuals, special-support children, and overlapping DHS/SSA child counts were fixed and revalidated
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix formula added the DHS-support minor count and the Social Security survivor minor count as separate addends, so a minor child receiving both kinds of support entered the food-credit qualified-exemption set twice, whereas HRS §235-55.85(c) lets "a minor child receiving support from the department of human services of the State, social security survivor's benefits, and the like" be considered one dependent and one qualified exemption.
modules.triage_notes: Provision was read through the pinned corpus release (us-hi/statute/235-55.85 resolved successfully); subsection (c) states the special-minor allowance once, disjunctively over the support categories, so the union — not the sum — is the correct member set. Module diff has three hunks and all serve the one fix: (a) hi_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid's domain guard drops the two old >= 0 bounds for the single new input's bound, (b) hi_pit_2026_food_credit_qualified_exemption_count's formula replaces the two addends with hi_pit_2026_food_credit_unique_special_minor_count (the decisive change), (c) the inputs block replaces the two Integer inputs with one, described in the diff as "Distinct minor children not already in federal exemptions who receive Hawaii Department of Human Services support, Social Security survivor benefits, or both; each child is counted once across the union." No numeric parameter, rate, table cell, effective date, or proof-atom excerpt changed, so this is not amount_mismatch or a provenance-only edit, though the downstream credit amount was inflated for overlapping children. Kind is the uncertain part, hence confidence 0.62: I chose wrong_entity_or_scope because the defect is the household member set counted as qualified exemptions (a member counted twice); defensible alternatives are 'other' (double counting of overlapping categories) or polarity_or_logic (source categories joined disjunctively were mis-combined additively). Commit body is empty; the commit subject "Prevent Hawaii food credit child overlap" also names the defect. Companion test diff is otherwise a mechanical input rename plus two new/renamed cases: food_two_distinct_special_support_minors_each_count_once and the new food_one_minor_with_both_dhs_and_ssa_support_counts_once, which pins the corrected behavior. The bundle's corpus_citation_paths_seen for this file listed only us-hi/statute/235-51, but the governing citation for the changed rule's proof atoms is us-hi/statute/235-55.85. Only module index 0 exists in this commit (plus its .test.yaml and the encoding manifest), matching the expected chunk of one.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this and could not: the diff changes an executable formula, not metadata — `hi_pit_2026_food_credit_qualified_exemption_count` went from adding two separately-supplied, mutually overlapping category counts to adding a single deduplicated union count, and the replacement input's own description states "each child is counted once across the union". The pinned corpus text of HRS §235-55.85(c) reads "a minor child receiving support from the department of human services of the State, social security survivor's benefits, and the like, may be considered a dependent and a qualified exemption of the parent or guardian" — singular, so one child receiving both DHS support and survivor benefits may yield at most one qualified exemption, while the pre-fix encoding (whose two input descriptions each independently matched such a child) yielded two. That is encoded meaning disagreeing with the source, so fidelity holds, and the failure is in which household members enter the qualified-exemption set (the same person counted twice), which is the "household member set" branch of wrong_entity_or_scope. No numeric literal, comparison, date, or boolean branch changed, so amount_mismatch, boundary_direction, wrong_period_or_effective_date, and polarity_or_logic all fit worse.
verdict.quote:
-          + hi_pit_2026_food_credit_minor_child_dhs_support_count
-          + hi_pit_2026_food_credit_minor_child_social_security_survivor_count
+          + hi_pit_2026_food_credit_unique_special_minor_count
verdict.notes:
Bundle: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/diffs/us/249e8e6f6b/000.diff (3 hunks: domain-validity guard, the qualified-exemption formula, the inputs block).

Kind is a near-tie, and a reviewer may prefer a different label. The population in scope is identical before and after (minor children with DHS/SSA/"and the like" support, not already federal exemptions); what was wrong is the aggregation — a multiset sum over two overlapping categories instead of a union cardinality. If the taxonomy allowed it, "other: overlapping-population double count" would name it more precisely; polarity_or_logic ("mis-combined and/or") is arguable since the statute's category list is disjunctive at the child level, but the changed lines contain no boolean and no branch fires wrongly, so I did not reclassify.

Two caveats on the evidence chain, neither of which changes the verdict:
1. The first reader's quote is from the PR #1035 body's review-cycle paragraph, which summarizes the whole PR, not this commit. The commit-specific evidence is stronger: subject "Prevent Hawaii food credit child overlap" plus the formula change itself. The commit body is empty.
2. The companion test diff (230 lines) is a pure input rename — every changed case sets the new input to 0, and no new case exercises a child in both support categories. So the fix is not test-demonstrated; the defect is established by the input descriptions plus the statute's singular "a dependent and a qualified exemption".

Also checked and ruled out: no cap or min() was added alongside the union input, the proof atoms for this rule are unchanged (same §235-55.85 excerpts), effective window stays 2026-01-01/2026-12-31, and the parallel renter-credit exemption count was untouched. The only non-module files in the commit are the encoding manifest and the companion test.

This commit is a repair round inside PR #1035 (the PR that first added the Hawaii module), not a post-merge fix to shipped content — the defective formula existed only on the branch.
