item.screen_reason: Tightens Hawaii tax-table and MFS holds: scope tightening of an existing module.

triage.commit_summary: This intra-PR repair commit (PR #1035, "Add Hawaii 2026 resident tax bounded core") widened the HRS 235-53 tax-table source hold so it applies to every nonitemizer instead of only nonitemizers whose taxable income fell at or below the assumed $20,000 ceiling, and moved that hold from the shared supported-profile gate onto the four public tax/liability stages (adding three private candidate rules to keep the diagnostic schedule amounts). It also added the missing statutory MFS conditions the source states: the 235-55.6(e)(2)-(4) joint-return requirement with legally-separated and living-apart exceptions for the CDCC, MFS holds for the 235-55.85(b)/235-55.7(e) joint-return-counterfactual provisos on the food/excise and renter credits, the 235-55.85(c) minor-child DHS/survivor-benefit qualified exemptions, and several input domain bounds.

modules.description_quote: This PR therefore holds **all nonitemizer public tax/liability stages** rather than assuming $20,000 is the ceiling or substituting continuous §235-51 schedules.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix hold conditioned on `hi_pit_2026_taxable_income <= hi_pit_2026_statutory_minimum_tax_table_ceiling` with that parameter pinned at 20000, i.e. it treated HRS 235-53(a)(2)'s statutory floor ("the amount (not less than $20,000) determined by the director") as the Director's actual ceiling, so nonitemizers with taxable income above $20,000 were published a continuous 235-51 schedule tax that the source may instead route to the unpinned Director-prescribed table.
modules.triage_notes: Read HRS 235-53, 235-55.6, 235-55.7 and 235-55.85 through the pinned corpus release (resolve_provision.py succeeded for all four). 235-53(a)(1)-(2) confirms the ceiling is a Director-determined amount with only a $20,000 floor, so the pre-fix ceiling value and the branch it gated had no source basis; the fix deletes the conjunct (hold now = `not hi_pit_2026_elects_itemized_deductions`) and re-gates the four public tax/liability stages on `not hi_pit_2026_tax_table_source_hold_applies`. Companion-test deltas corroborate the behavior change: supported_profile_tax_before_credits goes 2024.632 -> 0 (and 3401.264 -> 0, 13046.056 -> 0) with tax_table_source_hold_applies flipping not_holds -> holds, and the 2024.632 value survives only in the new private hi_pit_2026_profile_candidate_* rules. MULTI-DEFECT COMMIT: the same module diff also fixes at least three further fidelity gaps, each an unrepresented_clause if scored separately - (a) hi_pit_2026_refundable_child_and_dependent_care_credit had no marital restriction at all, and the fix adds `(not MFS or mfs_is_legally_separated or mfs_living_apart_conditions_met)` matching 235-55.6(e)(2) "the credit shall be allowed under subsection (a) only if the taxpayer and the taxpayer's spouse file a joint return" with the (e)(3)/(e)(4) exceptions; (b) hi_pit_2026_food_credit_qualified_exemption_count omitted 235-55.85(c) "a minor child receiving support from the department of human services of the State, social security survivor's benefits, and the like, may be considered a dependent and a qualified exemption", and the fix adds the DHS and SSA-survivor counts plus a hold on the open-ended "and the like" category; (c) the food/excise and renter credits ignored the 235-55.85(b) and 235-55.7(e) provisos that separate filers "shall claim only the tax credit to which they would have been entitled had a joint return been filed", and the fix fails closed for MFS rather than encoding the counterfactual. I chose the tax-table item as the decisive path because it is first in the commit subject, drives the largest behavioral change, and is the one the PR body explains verbatim; a reviewer preferring the clause-level view could reclassify the kind as unrepresented_clause (or amount_mismatch for the $20,000 ceiling parameter, which the fix leaves in the file at 20000 but no longer uses in the hold). Direction caveat: because the tax-table hold left supported_profile_applies, this commit also NEWLY publishes supported_profile_taxable_income and supported_profile_refundable_credits for nonitemizers (test deltas 0 -> 9000, 0 -> 570, 0 -> 100); that widening is added grounded coverage, not a defect fix. Domain-bound additions to hi_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid (failure counts bounded by exemption counts, incapable_spouse_count <= 1) are fail-closed hardening rather than a source disagreement. Commit message body is empty; PR #1035 has no reviews or review comments, so the PR body is the only narrative evidence, and it describes the PR's end state rather than this commit alone - hence confidence below 0.8.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix hold rule conditioned on `hi_pit_2026_taxable_income <= hi_pit_2026_statutory_minimum_tax_table_ceiling` with that parameter pinned at '20000', and because `supported_profile_applies` required `not tax_table_source_hold_applies`, nonitemizers with taxable income above $20,000 were published a continuous §235-51 amount at the public tax, tax-after-nonrefundable-credit, and signed-net stages. HRS 235-53(a)(2) read through the pinned release defines the ceiling as "the amount (not less than $20,000) determined by the director for the tax rate category in which such taxpayer falls", so $20,000 is a floor on an unknown, category-specific ceiling, and (a)(1) imposes the Director's table "[i]n lieu of the tax imposed by section 235-51" up to that ceiling — the encoded threshold therefore had no basis in the cited source. The fix deletes the comparison outright and re-attaches the hold to the four public tax/liability stages, which is the removal of an ungrounded branch condition rather than a correction of a number or of a comparison's side. amount_mismatch fails because no corrected value replaces 20000, and boundary_direction fails because no strictness or floor/ceiling flip could ground a bound the corpus does not contain.

Post-state (26ebd1a18c) lines 2139/2184/2207/2231 add `and not hi_pit_2026_tax_table_source_hold_applies` to tax_before_credits, tax_after_nonrefundable_credits, net_income_tax_liability, refundable_excess_before_payments, while supported_profile_taxable_income (2099) and supported_profile_refundable_credits (2144) stay published — the hold is targeted at table-dependent stages, not blanket. The first reader's PR-body quote ("rather than assuming $20,000 is the ceiling or substituting continuous §235-51 schedules") describes exactly the pre-state this commit removed, so the quote corroborates rather than merely restates.

Laws 44-30-12(c)(10), read through the pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix), allows the modification only "in the case of any investment in a Rhode Island opportunity zone by the taxpayer for at least seven (7) years", i.e. per qualifying RI investment, yet the pre-fix module fed the subtraction two taxpayer-level inputs described merely as "Federal benefit allowed under section 1400Z-2(b)(2)(B)(iv)" and "...under section 1400Z-2(c)" — unrestricted as to Rhode Island and as to which investment produced them — gated by one taxpayer-wide seven-year flag. That is a genuine scope error against the source in two directions (federal opportunity-zone benefit from non-RI zones could be subtracted, and in a mixed-holding-period case the whole aggregate benefit was gated by a single boolean), not merely added precision: the pre-fix supported-profile guard admitted multi-investment taxpayers and computed a liability for them. modules.description_quote: Findings covering specialty taxes and recaptures, capital character, transitive fail-closed gates, caller-completed legal results, public-output gating, federal-EITC domain consistency, adoption proof completeness, and generated-artifact minimality were fixed and revalidated.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix domain admitted an internally impossible input (a positive federal earned income credit with zero federal EITC earned income), where the reduction-rate zero-denominator fallback returned 0 and the module silently paid a full 20% Montana credit instead of holding, but MCA 15-30-2318 states no such input constraint, so no statutorily possible case changes its answer.
modules.triage_notes: Three changes in one module diff, only one of which touches behavior. (1) Formula: mt_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid gains 'and ( mt_pit_2026_federal_earned_income_credit == 0 or mt_pit_2026_federal_eitc_earned_income > 0 )'. (2) Metadata only: module.description and deferred_outputs[0].reason change 'November 2025' to 'November 2026'; I read MCA 15-30-2120(7) through the pinned corpus and it says 'By November 1 of each year, the department shall multiply the subtractions ... by the inflation factor for that tax year' and 'The resulting amounts are effective for that tax year', so the new year is the right one for TY2026 — but this is a prose note about which corpus release is missing, not a formula, parameter, effective date, or output, so it is provenance/metadata (mechanical) on its own. (3) mt_pit_2026_adopted_child_is_eligible gains only a proof atom (excerpt 'in the tax year the adoption is final'); its formula already contained mt_pit_2026_adoption_became_final_in_2026, so that part is excerpt-only provenance = mechanical. WHY UNCLEAR AND NOT FIDELITY (recommend prune): I resolved MCA 15-30-2318 through the pinned corpus. Subsection (2) is 20% of the federal section 32 credit and (5)(b) defines 'Reduction percentage' as disallowed earned income divided by total earned income. Pre-fix, mt_pit_2026_earned_income_credit_reduction_rate returns 0 when the denominator is 0, and the pre-existing domain clause 'section_501d_disallowed_earned_income <= federal_eitc_earned_income' already forces disallowance to 0 in that case, so a 0 reduction and a 20%-of-federal credit is literally what the Montana statute prescribes for that input. The only thing wrong is that the input combination itself cannot occur under IRC section 32 (no earned income means no federal EITC) — a federal-law consistency constraint the cited Montana provision never states. Consistent with that, the added clause carries NO new proof atom, unlike every genuinely source-grounded condition in this module. A fidelity judge comparing the pre-fix module to us-mt/statute/15-30-2318 would have no source basis to flag it, so this looks like defensive domain hardening (scope the module never needed to claim) rather than an encoded meaning that disagrees with the source. Kind 'polarity_or_logic' is my best-fit-if-it-is-a-defect choice because the taxonomy lists 'fail-open vs fail-closed, default value' and the companion test added in the same commit is named 'positive federal EITC with zero earned-income denominator fails closed' (test file, not a module comment, so not used as the quote); 'wrong_entity_or_scope' is a defensible alternative since the changed rule is the module's input-domain gate. The quoted PR-body sentence names 'federal-EITC domain consistency' and 'adoption proof completeness' — both land in this commit — so the provenance of the change is clear even though its fidelity status is not. Other files in the commit are the companion test (+1 case), the regenerated signed manifest (hashes/timestamps/supersedes chain only), and a two-line reordering of unrelated us-la entries in oracle-coverage-pending.yaml; no unrelated Montana rule changed. The only PR discussion is a rebase note from PavelMakarchuk stating Montana module/test/manifest hashes were unchanged by the rebase; there are no PR reviews or inline review comments in the bundle. Bundle had exactly the one module index expected.

verdict.justification: The only substantive change is one added conjunct to `mt_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid` asserting an internal consistency invariant between two caller-supplied federal inputs (a positive federal EITC implies positive federal EITC earned income); MCA 15-30-2318, read in full through the pinned release, imposes no such constraint — subsection (2) fixes the credit at 20% of the federal credit and (5)(b) defines the reduction percentage as disallowed earned income divided by total earned income. For every input the statute actually decides, the pre-fix module already produced the statutory answer; the only inputs whose result changes are ones where the statutory denominator is zero (0/0, which the source leaves undefined) and which cannot arise because a positive IRC 32 credit presupposes positive earned income. Tellingly, the fix neither removes nor re-grounds the ungrounded `if mt_pit_2026_federal_eitc_earned_income == 0: 0` fallback — that branch is byte-identical pre and post and still reachable when both inputs are zero — and no proof atom was added for the new conjunct, confirming it is a defensive domain guard rather than a corrected reading of the source. The PR's own label for the finding is "federal-EITC domain consistency", i.e. an input-invariant hardening, not a disagreement with MCA text.

triage.commit_summary: Within PR #1027 (parent 669d5eb4 "Add Delaware resident income-tax core" is the initial encoding commit on the same branch), this commit rewrites the TY2026 Delaware full-year resident income-tax core module after independent review found that the encoding asserted the §1102(d) Director tax-table method definitely controls for all taxable income at or below $60,000 and capped the personal, other-jurisdiction, and child/dependent-care credits against schedule tax throughout that range. The fix represents the statute's "or such lesser amount as the Director may determine but in any event not less than $20,000" clause by adding a $20,000 minimum-ceiling parameter and three mutually exclusive method statuses (definite table at or below $20,000, uncertain from above $20,000 through $60,000, definite schedule above $60,000), restricts the credit candidates to the definite-schedule status, converts the supported-profile guard from fail-open `<= 0` tests to exact `== 0` tests plus a nonnegative input-domain guard and explicit residency/non-joint/standard-deduction/no-lump-sum conditions, renames the derived chain to `profile_candidate_*`, relabels three caller-completed inputs (§1634 fiduciary, §1122 sourcing, §1106(b)(2) trigger), and re-cites proof atoms to exact subsection excerpts from the recovered official document.

modules.description_quote: an overbroad §1102(d) table-status claim; a profile that was not fail-closed; credits capped against schedule tax when the table could control
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module encoded 30 Del. C. §1102(d)(1) as "table method applies iff taxable income <= $60,000", dropping the statute's qualifying clause that the Director may instead set a lesser tax-table-income ceiling "but in any event not less than $20,000", so it asserted the table method (and, by complement, capped credits against schedule tax) across the whole $20,000-$60,000 band where the source does not establish which method controls.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release: §1102(d)(1) verbatim is "...whose tax table income for the taxable year does not exceed $60,000, or such lesser amount as the Director may determine but in any event not less than $20,000, a tax determined under tables... prescribed by the Director of Revenue." Pre-fix rules were `de_pit_2026_tax_table_method_applies: taxable_income <= de_pit_2026_tax_table_income_ceiling (60000)` and `de_pit_2026_schedule_method_controls: taxable_income > 60000`; post-fix adds parameter `de_pit_2026_minimum_director_tax_table_income_ceiling = 20000` (proof atom excerpt "but in any event not less than $20,000") and splits into three mutually exclusive statuses, and the three credit rules now return 0 unless `de_pit_2026_definite_schedule_method_controls`, so credits are no longer capped against a schedule amount in the uncertain band. Kind is a judgment call between unrepresented_clause (the Director-lesser-ceiling clause was absent and the fix adds it, which is how I labeled it) and untraceable_branch (the pre-fix table/schedule status branch asserted more than the cited source supports); the numeric $60,000 itself was never wrong. This commit is a multi-thread hardening of a single module and also carries: (a) a second fidelity-relevant scope/logic thread — the supported-profile guard moved from fail-open `<= 0` comparisons to exact `== 0` plus a new nonnegative input-domain guard and newly required conditions (`is_full_year_resident`, `not is_joint_return`, `elects_standard_deduction`, `not uses_separate_spouse_mechanics`, `not has_section_1102_b_lump_sum_distribution`), i.e. the module previously produced full-year non-joint standard-deduction numbers without checking that profile and treated negative category amounts as in-profile (this alone would read as polarity_or_logic / wrong_entity_or_scope); (b) boundary-disclosure relabeling of three inputs the module had presented as raw but that are caller-completed (`fiduciary_adjustment` -> `completed_section_1634_fiduciary_adjustment`, `taxable_income_from_other_jurisdiction` -> `completed_section_1122_other_jurisdiction_taxable_income`, `potential_low_income_age_or_disability_exclusion` -> `completed_low_income_age_or_disability_exclusion_trigger`); (c) a purely mechanical/provenance layer — pervasive `profile_candidate_*` renames, expanded summary/rationale prose, and many added exact-subsection proof-atom excerpts. Defect was caught by pre-merge review inside PR #1027, so the defective state (669d5eb4) never reached main; if the corpus requires defects that were merged, flag this. Companion test file gained 737 lines and the apply manifest was regenerated; no other module changed.

verdict.justification: The pinned corpus text of 30 Del. C. §1102(d)(1) reads "whose tax table income for the taxable year does not exceed $60,000, or such lesser amount as the Director may determine but in any event not less than $20,000" — so the source fixes only a band ($20,000–$60,000) within which the operative table ceiling lies, and does not establish which method controls above $20,000. The pre-fix module dropped that qualifying clause entirely (its proof atom excerpt was only "tax table income for the taxable year does not exceed $60,000") and encoded a definite public judgment `de_pit_2026_tax_table_method_applies = taxable_income <= 60000`, with the complement `schedule_method_controls = taxable_income > 60000`; its summary even asserted "For taxable income at or below $60,000, section 1102(d) requires a Director-prescribed table", which the statute does not say. The fix adds the missing clause as a grounded parameter (`de_pit_2026_minimum_director_tax_table_income_ceiling = 20000`, proof excerpt "but in any event not less than $20,000") and splits the single boolean into three mutually exclusive statuses, adding the previously absent uncertain $20k–$60k branch. I tried to refute this as mere added precision, but the pre-fix rule made an affirmative, exposed status claim across the whole band, so this corrects encoded meaning rather than adding coverage the module never claimed.
verdict.quote:
-        formula: de_pit_2026_taxable_income <= de_pit_2026_tax_table_income_ceiling
+            source: {corpus_citation_path: us-de/statute/30/1102, excerpt: "but in any event not less than $20,000"}
verdict.notes: Kinds I ruled out: amount_mismatch (the $60,000 is verbatim in the source and was not wrong; $20,000 is new, from the omitted clause); boundary_direction (strictness stayed `<=`/`>` on both sides — the change is a new threshold created by the added clause, not a flipped bound); untraceable_branch (the `<= $60,000` branch did have source basis, it was just unqualified). Caveat for the reviewer: a defensible counter-reading is that $60,000 is the statutory default and the Director's lesser determination is an unexercised external fact, which would make the pre-fix a defensible default rather than a wrong encoding — I weighted against it because the module's own source_verification declares the 2026 Director ceiling absent from the pinned corpus, so asserting the maximum-ceiling reading as definite exceeds the source. Also note this commit bundles at least two further distinct fidelity issues named in the same PR-body sentence that are NOT covered by the flagged rule_path: (1) the fail-open profile guard, `de_pit_2026_federal_nol_carryback_deduction <= 0` → `== 0` plus a new `de_pit_2026_input_domain_is_valid` nonnegativity conjunct (polarity_or_logic); (2) credits previously capped unconditionally against schedule tax, now gated on `if de_pit_2026_definite_schedule_method_controls:` (also polarity/scope). If the corpus wants one kind per commit, unrepresented_clause is correct for the flagged rule; if it admits multiple, the fail-closed change deserves its own entry. modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The three spouse branches keyed only on the raw `la_2026_resident_filing_status_joint` input flag, so a return with a contradictory filing-status selection (the IT-540ESi line 3 list is five mutually exclusive statuses, and the module's own `filing_status_selection_valid` requires exactly one) still received the joint-return-only spouse disability exemption, active-duty exclusion and volunteer deduction — failing open on a return the encoding elsewhere treats as having no valid filing status, and on which the source gives no basis for counting spouse facts.
modules.triage_notes: Single rule module in the commit; the same two-line guard (`if la_2026_resident_filing_status_selection_valid and la_2026_resident_filing_status_joint`) is added to three separate rules in one file — identical hunk shape each time. Companions changed alongside it are mechanical: the companion fixture file (which flips the `conflicting_filing_statuses_fail_closed` fixture's spouse inputs from false/0 to true/6000, true/50000, true and adds assertions that `la_2026_resident_disability_income_exemption`, `la_2026_resident_active_duty_outside_louisiana_exclusion` and `la_2026_resident_volunteer_deduction` are all 0) and the `.axiom/encoding-manifests` hash file. Provisions read through the pinned corpus: La. R.S. 47:44.1(B) reads "Six thousand dollars of annual disability income received by an individual shall be exempt from state income taxation" (per-individual, so a second allowance depends on the spouse being on the return, i.e. a joint return), and the 2026 IT-540ESi worksheet line 3 enumerates Single / Married Filing Joint / Married Filing Separate / Head of Household / Qualifying Surviving Spouse as one choice. Caps are 6000, 50000 and 500, so under a conflicting-status return up to $56,500 of spouse amounts leaked; `la_2026_resident_partial_tax_table_income_before_held_adjustments` already failed closed on invalid status, so the leak surfaced in the exempt-income / deduction component outputs (which are asserted fixture outputs and feed the oracle surface) rather than in the partial tax figure. This commit is a pre-merge repair round inside PR #1026 (parent f1ed255931 is on the same branch), following an earlier round that first gated spouse items on joint returns at all; a later repair in the same PR replaced a flattened EITC rate import, unrelated to this module change. Main doubt for a reviewer: an alternative kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (joint-only spouse items applied to a return that is not validly joint), and a strict reader could call this defensive hardening against an input state the form forbids rather than a direct disagreement with source text — I kept polarity_or_logic because the kind list explicitly places fail-open vs fail-closed there and because the commit subject is "Fail closed Louisiana spouse components".

verdict.justification: The diff changes executable boolean logic in three formulas, adding `la_2026_resident_filing_status_selection_valid and` as a conjunct to the joint-only spouse branches of the disability exemption, the active-duty-outside-Louisiana exclusion, and the volunteer deduction, and the companion fixture flips from spouse flags false to true on the `filing_status_selection_count: 2` case while newly asserting all three components equal 0 — so encoded meaning, not bookkeeping, changed. The pre-fix module was internally contradictory against its own source-anchored filing-status rule: `la_2026_resident_filing_status_selection_valid` (proof-atomed to the IT-540ESi line 3 list, which the resolved corpus text confirms enumerates Single / Married Filing Joint / Married Filing Separate / Head of Household / Qualifying Surviving Spouse as one mutually exclusive choice) already forced the standard deduction and partial tax-table income to 0, and the parent file's own summary already asserted "Filing status fails closed unless exactly one recognized status is selected" — while these three branches still paid out on a contradictory selection. That is precisely the fail-open-vs-fail-closed / mis-combined-`and` case, which the kind list places under polarity_or_logic, and the commit subject "Fail closed Louisiana spouse components" names it directly.
verdict.quote:
-            if la_2026_resident_filing_status_joint
+            if la_2026_resident_filing_status_selection_valid
+               and la_2026_resident_filing_status_joint
verdict.notes: Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "Defensive hardening for an impossible input, so an enhancement rather than a defect" — killed by the parent file, which already documented the fail-closed contract in `module.summary` ("Filing status fails closed unless exactly one recognized status is selected") and already implemented it at `la_2026_resident_standard_deduction` and `la_2026_resident_partial_tax_table_income_before_held_adjustments`; the three spouse branches simply did not honor a contract the module had claimed. The five status flags are raw undeclared inputs (they appear only inside `la_2026_resident_filing_status_selection_count`), so the contradictory state is representable and the fixture exercises it. (2) "Mechanical" — rejected; the only bookkeeping is the manifest's two applied-file sha256s plus generated_at/tmpdir, which follow the real formula change. (3) "reclassify to wrong_entity_or_scope or unrepresented_clause" — considered, since the defect does concern filing status and does add a conjunct; rejected because the joint-scope condition was already present and correct for well-formed returns, the added guard is an already-encoded, already-source-proved predicate rather than a newly represented source clause, and the failure mode is exactly the fail-open default the polarity_or_logic definition enumerates. Genuine caveat for the reviewer, the reason confidence is not higher: the blast radius is confined to the three component outputs, because `la_2026_resident_partial_tax_table_income_before_held_adjustments` already returned 0 on an invalid selection, so the module's headline partial income and 3% tax figures were unaffected pre-fix. The wrong values were nonetheless published on declared module outputs ($6,000 / $50,000 / $500 for a return the encoding elsewhere treats as having no valid status), which is what the new fixture assertions pin. Provenance note: the defect and the fix both live inside PR #1026, which introduced the module, so this never reached main in the broken state; the quoted "Re-review found one conflicting-status component leak" line is the PR's own narrative of its review-fix cycle, and it matches the diff exactly. Post-fix grep confirms no bare `if la_2026_resident_filing_status_joint` joint-only payout branch remains (lines 365 and 423 are the status counter and the standard deduction, which is already inside a `selection_valid` gate), so the PR's "every spouse branch" claim holds.

item.screen_reason: Clarify boundary: NC charitable deduction now excludes the section 170 deduction attributable to a credit-backed donation rather than the donation value (scope of excluded amount).

triage.commit_summary: The commit changes the NC TY2026 resident income-tax pipeline so that the charitable-deduction carve-out for credit-backed qualified real-property donations subtracts the current-year section 170 deduction attributable to that donation instead of the donation's own value, renaming the corresponding module input and rewriting its description and the rule's source line. It also adds two companion fixtures (a limited credit-backed section 170 deduction case and a married-filing-separately under-cap case) and refreshes the signed encoding manifest; no MFS formula in the YAML itself changed despite the subject line.

modules.other_kind: wrong_quantity_basis (excluded amount measured as the donation's value instead of the section 170 deduction attributable to it)
modules.description_quote: The independent cycle found and fixed signed-income flooring, MFS cap handling, the current charitable-deduction exclusion, incomplete boundary/status coverage, deduction-attribution semantics for credit-backed property, and an untested MFS under-cap branch.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: N.C. Gen. Stat. 105-153.5(a)(2)a bases the NC charitable deduction on "The amount allowed as a deduction for charitable contributions under section 170 of the Code for that taxable year" and sub-sub-subdivision 3 makes a credit-backed qualified donation ineligible for that deduction, so the amount to remove is the section 170 deduction attributable to the donation, whereas the pre-fix formula subtracted the donation's own value and therefore over-excluded whenever that donation's section 170 deduction is smaller than the donation amount (percentage limits, carryforwards, property valuation rules).
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, corpus commit 01e00777cb, provision us-nc/statute/105/105-153.5); the operative text is quoted in pre_fix_wrong_because. The diff is a three-part semantic change to one rule: source string, formula subtrahend, and the renamed input nc_pit_2026_credit_backed_qualified_real_property_donation -> nc_pit_2026_section_170_deduction_attributable_to_credit_backed_donation, whose new description reads "Current-year federal section 170 deduction amount attributable to a qualified real-property donation that is the basis for an allocated section 105-153.11 credit; this deduction amount, rather than the donation's value, is excluded from the North Carolina charitable deduction." (usable as a module_comment quote if a reviewer prefers it). Proof-atom excerpt, effective dates, entity, period and outputs are unchanged, so this is not excerpt-only provenance. The subtrahend is a module input, so the fix changes the module's input contract rather than an internal derivation, but it is a genuine meaning change: the new fixture "limited credit-backed section 170 deduction preserves unrelated charitable deduction" (contributions 7000, attributable section 170 deduction 2000 -> eligible 5000) exercises exactly that distinction. Kind bucketing is the uncertain part: untraceable_branch is a near miss under its "value with no basis in the cited source ... re-grounds it" clause, but the pre-fix subtrahend did trace to carve-out 3 and was merely quantified on the wrong basis; wrong_entity_or_scope's listed senses (entity, population, filing status, geography, program scope, output surface) do not cover a mis-measured amount; so I used other. The commit subject also says "MFS deductions", but the MFS cap rule in the YAML is untouched - the MFS part of this commit is a new test fixture only. This is an in-branch fix inside merged PR #1023 (no reviews or review comments recorded). Two later commits touch the file (450ca0144 "Use canonical NC module source locator", d1ed1b594 "Repair NC TY2026 statute source backing"); both look like source/provenance repairs, not reversals.

verdict.other_kind: wrong_quantity_basis (the excluded amount was measured as the donation's value instead of the section 170 deduction attributable to it)
verdict.justification: The pinned corpus text of N.C. Gen. Stat. 105-153.5(a)(2)a sets the NC charitable base as "The amount allowed as a deduction for charitable contributions under section 170 of the Code for that taxable year," and sub-sub-subdivision 3 says only that "A qualified donation that is the basis for an allocated credit under G.S. 105-153.11 is not eligible for a deduction under this subdivision" — so the quantity to remove from that base is the section 170 deduction attributable to the donation, not the donation's own value. Pre-fix, the subtrahend input was documented as "Qualified real-property donation that is the basis for an allocated section 105-153.11 credit," i.e. the donation amount, so whenever the section 170 percentage-of-AGI limits or 170(e) basis reduction made the current-year deduction smaller than the donation, the module over-excluded and (through the max(0, ...) floor) could wipe out unrelated charitable deductions; the new fixture "limited credit-backed section 170 deduction preserves unrelated charitable deduction" (7000 contributions, 2000 attributable deduction, 5000 preserved) is exactly that case. No listed kind fits: no numeric literal, boundary strictness, clause, period, entity/population, or boolean operator changed, and the removed quantity was not untraceable (the statute does name the qualified donation) — it was the wrong measurement basis for the excluded amount, so "other: wrong_quantity_basis" is the honest kind. I could not refute the fidelity call: the pre-fix input semantics genuinely disagree with the cited text, and the fix re-states the excluded amount on the statute's own basis.
verdict.quote:
-            - nc_pit_2026_credit_backed_qualified_real_property_donation
+            - nc_pit_2026_section_170_deduction_attributable_to_credit_backed_donation
verdict.notes: Strongest surviving counterargument, which a reviewer should weigh: the change is carried entirely by an input rename plus its `description` and the rule's `source:` string. The arithmetic shape is byte-identical (max(0, contributions - X)), no parameter, version window, effective date, entity, or boolean changed, and the test edits are a pure alpha-rename except the one added fixture, whose expected values would come out the same under the old semantics too (supplying 2000 as a donation value yields 5000 as well). So a strict "formula/parameter must change" reading could call this a contract/documentation clarification (mechanical-adjacent) rather than a computed-meaning change. I still land on confirmed because the input's documented quantity is part of the encoded meaning — a binder populating this module from federal data supplies a materially different number after the fix — and both the pre-fix description ("Qualified real-property donation ... and is therefore excluded from the deduction") and the post-fix one ("this deduction amount, rather than the donation's value, is excluded") state the two incompatible bases explicitly. Secondary notes: the proof atom's excerpt and citation path are unchanged, so this is not an excerpt-only/provenance edit; the commit's parenthetical "(scope of excluded amount)" tempts a wrong_entity_or_scope reading, but that kind covers entity/population/program/output scope, not the measurement basis of a money amount. The PR-body quote the first reader used ("deduction-attribution semantics for credit-backed property" inside the cycle sentence) is real but generic; the diff and the statute, not that sentence, are what settle the call. Commit also bundles an unrelated MFS-cap fixture addition, which is not part of this rule's defect.

item.subject: (screen-flagged) Time-bound: Idaho pilot bounded to 2026, drops source-certified parity claim and relabels 2026 indexed amounts as caller-supplied projections.
item.screen_reason: Time-bound: Idaho pilot bounded to 2026, drops source-certified parity claim and relabels 2026 indexed amounts as caller-supplied projections.

triage.commit_summary: The commit bounds the three rule versions of the Idaho composed pilot income-tax liability pipeline to effective_to 2026-12-31 and rewrites the module rationale/summary to drop the claim that the 2026 rate and threshold are operative indexed law comparable "to the cent" against PolicyEngine, relabeling every year-specific amount as a caller-supplied projection with no source-certified parity claim. It also adds dense boundary fixtures (taxable-income floor, one cent below/at/above the supplied no-tax threshold, liability floor) to the companion test file so 2025/2027 probes fail closed, as part of PR #1017's cross-state TY2026 period-boundary cleanup.

modules.description_quote: bounds the projected/caller-supplied scaffold through 2026, adds dense floor/threshold fixtures, explicitly retains the official-source HOLD/no-parity boundary
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: All three versions opened at 2026-01-01 with no effective_to, so the module asserted that a configuration built entirely on unverified 2026 projections (the indexed no-tax threshold and the post-step rate) was valid for every period from 2026 onward, even though the cited section 63-3024 directs the State Tax Commission to reindex the threshold annually and the pinned corpus holds no source certifying any of those year-specific values.
modules.triage_notes: Single module in the commit. The only semantic delta is three identical '+ effective_to: 2026-12-31' hunks (one per rule version); the rest of the module diff is rationale/summary prose that removes the pre-fix claims that 'the operative 2026 rate and threshold are the indexed values PolicyEngine projects', the literal '$4,920 single / $9,840 joint at 2026' and '5.3-per-cent' figures, and the 'comparable to PolicyEngine id_income_tax to the cent' parity assertion. Formulas, inputs, outputs, entity, and citation paths are unchanged, so on its own the prose rewrite would be metadata/mechanical; the effective_to additions are what make this a period-scope correction. I read the cited provision through the pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix): us-id/statute/63-3024 resolves to legislature site navigation chrome only, with fix_time_corpus_match = row_body_empty_at_corpus_ref, i.e. the corpus row carries no operative statutory text, which corroborates the module's new 'corpus does not yet contain a Tax Commission source certifying the operative 2026 indexed values' rationale and the withdrawal of the parity claim. Residual doubt on the classification: because every year-specific amount is a caller-supplied input rather than a literal, no source sentence is directly contradicted by the pre-fix formulas, so a reviewer could read the bounding as fail-closed scaffolding hygiene rather than a source disagreement; I kept 'fidelity' because the encoded version window claimed validity the module's own cited authority (annual reindexation, no certified source) cannot support, and PR #1017 names it as a 'period-boundary' gap. Companion test file gained five boundary fixtures in the same commit (test-side, not counted here). Follow-ups in the same PR but NOT in this commit: removal of the incorrect legacy us-id/statute/63-3022D citation/index edge (63-3022D is still listed in this commit's corpus_citation_paths), and a later head fed5817295 that deleted a stale Idaho pending-validation waiver block after CI failed with 'pending validation fingerprint evidence mismatch'.

verdict.justification: The only meaning change is three added `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` lines; formulas, inputs, entity/period kind, proof atoms and citation paths are untouched, and the pre-fix module contains no year-specific literal at all — the threshold, both rates, the deduction subtraction and the exemption credit are all caller-supplied inputs, so nothing encoded goes stale in 2027. Resolving both cited paths through the fix commit's pinned toolchain returns only Idaho Legislature navigation chrome, with `"fix_time_corpus_match": "row_body_empty_at_corpus_ref"` at corpus ref 527a5be2, so the pinned corpus holds no operative text of 63-3024 that could make the open-ended window disagree with the source, and Idaho's single-rate structure has no 2026 sunset. The commit's own added rationale grounds the bound in corpus *absence* ("The corpus does not yet contain a Tax Commission source certifying the operative 2026 indexed values"), and the PR frames it as "Fail close 2026 state income-tax boundary modules" alongside withdrawal of an unsupported oracle-parity claim. That is a fail-closed governance/truthfulness scoping choice plus a provenance retraction, not a correction of encoded meaning against cited source text.
verdict.quote:
+        corpus does not yet contain a Tax Commission source certifying the
+        operative 2026 indexed values, so every year-specific amount is a
+        declared caller-supplied projection: the filing-status no-tax threshold,
verdict.notes: Refutation targets the classification, not the kind: if the corpus's convention is that an unbounded window on unverified-projection scaffolding is itself a period-truthfulness defect, then wrong_period_or_effective_date is the right kind and the first reader stands — my disagreement is whether any source-fidelity defect exists when the cited provision has no text in the pinned corpus. Verified facts for the reviewer: (1) module diff meaning change is exactly three `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` additions (rules[0..2].versions[0]); everything else is rationale/summary prose. (2) Pre-fix file (parent 07f5517d74) has zero numeric literals in any formula — all year-specific amounts arrive as `id_pit_pilot_supplied_*` inputs, so the post-2026 window could not produce a wrong number. (3) resolve_provision.py for us-id/statute/63-3024 and us-id/statute/63-3022D at commit 9d343d49a3 returns 956 chars of site navigation ("Senate Senate Leadership … How current is this law?") and reports row bodies empty at the toolchain corpus ref — no statutory rate, threshold, or effective-period text exists to be disagreed with. (4) Side effects worth a second look, both out of scope for this verdict: the bound now makes the module fail closed for 2027+ although the statutory single-rate mechanics continue (an under-claim with no statutory sunset), and the unchanged proof-atom excerpts ("5.3% of taxable income over $2,500, or over $5,000 for joint returns"; "a tax measured by Idaho taxable income") cannot be located in the resolved corpus body — a separate provenance issue this commit did not fix. (5) The same commit adds five 2026-period boundary fixtures (floor, ±$0.01 around the supplied threshold, credit floor) that exercise only caller-supplied mechanics; test additions do not bear on fidelity. If a reviewer prefers not to acquit outright, "unclear" is the next-best label; "mechanical" is wrong because version windows changed.

item.subject: (screen-flagged) Time-bound: WA and VT pilot pipelines bounded to tax year 2026 (effective period).
item.screen_reason: Time-bound: WA and VT pilot pipelines bounded to tax year 2026 (effective period).

triage.commit_summary: The commit adds `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` to the single version of every derived output in the Vermont and Washington pilot liability pipelines (three rules each), so both TY2026-only composed pipelines now fail closed outside tax year 2026 instead of claiming validity for every year from 2026-01-01 forward. No formula, parameter value, input, output, or scope text changed; the only other files touched are the two encoder apply manifests, and the PR frames the change as closing "TY2026 truthfulness and period-boundary gaps without changing the underlying tax formulas."

modules.description_quote: bounds the three WA and three previously open VT dependent outputs through 2026-12-31; VT’s two parameters were already bounded
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The three derived VT outputs were encoded with an open-ended window (effective_from 2026-01-01, no effective_to), asserting the module's TY2026-only composition applies to every later year even though its own summary scopes it to "Vermont 2026 individual income tax", its normal-tax input is a supplied completed 2026 return, and the schedules it stands in for are annually re-indexed by the Commissioner.
modules.triage_notes: Diff is three identical one-line additions of effective_to: '2026-12-31'. Decisive internal evidence: the module's two parameters (vt_pit_pilot_federal_agi_minimum_threshold, vt_pit_pilot_federal_agi_minimum_rate) were ALREADY bounded to 2026-12-31 at the parent commit while the derived rules that reference them were not, so a 2027 evaluation would have run derived formulas against parameters with no active version — an internal window inconsistency the fix removes. Commit body is empty; PR #1017 (https://github.com/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/pull/1017) is a consolidation of several state lanes (MI, RI, UT, ID, WA, VT), so its body and the three PavelMakarchuk issue comments describe more than this commit; the WA/VT bullet and the sentence "Closes the remaining cross-state TY2026 truthfulness and period-boundary gaps without changing the underlying tax formulas" are the parts that cover it. No reviews/review_comments on the PR; the three issue comments are CLEAN combined-head reviews and a CI waiver fix (Idaho only). Only other files in the commit are the two .axiom encoding manifests; no companion test/fixture files changed here. Residual doubt for the reviewer: because the VT statutory threshold ($150,000) and rate (3%) are not themselves sunset in 32 V.S.A. 5822(a)(6), one could read this as pilot-coverage conservatism (limiting claims to the validated 2026 slice) rather than a disagreement with source text; I call it fidelity because the encoded version window over-claimed periods the module cannot represent, which is exactly wrong_period_or_effective_date, and because the change alters evaluated behavior (2027 now fails closed). Provision text not re-read for VT — the module's own rationale already quotes the annual-indexing mandate and the corpus lacks the 2026 indexed tables.

modules.description_quote: Closes the remaining cross-state TY2026 truthfulness and period-boundary gaps without changing the underlying tax formulas
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: All three derived WA outputs were encoded with no effective_to, so the module asserted its 2026-only composed pipeline — built on a supplied PolicyEngine 2026 projected $284,000 standard deduction and 2026 supplied rates/threshold, per its own "2026 oracle slice" summary — remained valid for every year after 2026, even though RCW 82.87.060(1) makes the standard deduction annually adjusted under RCW 82.87.150.
modules.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 0: three identical one-line additions of effective_to: '2026-12-31', no formula/parameter/input/output/scope change. Provision read: resolve_provision.py for us-wa/statute/82/82.87/82.87.060 at this rulespec commit returns RCW 82.87.060 with "A standard deduction of $250,000 per individual... The amount of the standard deduction shall be adjusted pursuant to RCW 82.87.150", confirming the operative deduction is year-specific while the module supplies a single 2026 value. Weaker case than VT: unlike VT, none of WA's inputs are module-internal parameters bounded to 2026 (all deduction/rate/threshold values are caller-supplied), so the open-ended window did not create an internal inconsistency and the formula shape is not itself year-specific — hence lower confidence and a real possibility a reviewer prunes this to 'unclear' as pilot-coverage conservatism rather than a source disagreement. The claim the fix corrects is the period claim itself: the module's summary scopes it to the 2026 oracle slice while its versions claimed all future years, and the PR records that "explicit 2025/2027 probes fail closed" after the change. Commit body empty; see index 0 notes on PR #1017 being a multi-state consolidation.

verdict.justification: The cited source, 32 V.S.A. § 5822, imposes the tax "for each taxable year" with no sunset, and the (a)(6) greater-of test with its $150,000.00 threshold and three-percent rate is flat permanent text — only "[t]he amounts of taxable income shown in the tables in this section shall be adjusted annually for inflation" under (b)(2), and those indexed tables are explicitly deferred/supplied by this module — so the provision gives no basis for 2026-12-31 as an end date on these three derived outputs. The diff adds only three effective_to lines: every formula, parameter, input, output, entity and the TY2026 result are identical pre and post, and the PR frames the work as closing "period-boundary gaps without changing the underlying tax formulas." The 2026 bound comes from the pilot's own validation scope (an explicitly supplied completed 2026 return, the pinned Populace artifact) and the repo's fail-closed convention, not from the cited text; if anything the post-fix window now understates the statute's permanent reach, just as the already-bounded $150,000/3% parameters do. The closest defensible alternative is unclear — open-ended outputs sitting above 2026-bounded parameters could emit an ungrounded 2027 number — but that is module self-consistency and scope hygiene, not encoded meaning that disagrees with the source.
verdict.quote: +        effective_to: '2026-12-31'
verdict.notes: Verified facts: (1) pre-fix, the two parameters vt_pit_pilot_federal_agi_minimum_threshold ('150000.0') and _rate ('0.03') already carried effective_from 2026-01-01 / effective_to 2026-12-31; only the three derived rules were open-ended. (2) Resolved source text (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, provision us-vt/statute/32-5822, body sha256 57a339ae...) contains no sunset; the 2026 overlay (Act No. 164, Sec. 56) amends subsection (e) only and is itself permanent. (3) The (a)(6) $150,000 test is on federal AGI, which is not among "the amounts of taxable income shown in the tables," so it is not one of the annually indexed amounts — the annual-indexing argument in the first reader's reading does not reach the parameters or the greater-of structure this module encodes. (4) 'mechanical' is excluded by definition here because version windows/effective dates did change. (5) If the project's standard is that a module validated only for TY2026 must not assert later years, then wrong_period_or_effective_date is the mechanically correct kind and the first reader's call stands; that standard is a repo convention (PR title "Fail close 2026 state income-tax boundary modules"), not the cited statute, which is why I land on not_a_defect rather than confirmed. A reviewer who wants to keep the case should downgrade it to unclear rather than confirmed. (6) No later commit touches this file, so the 2026 bound was not revisited. (7) This verdict covers module index 0 (VT) only; the WA half of commit 07f5517d74 has a different source posture (RCW 82.87 with its own indexed deductions) and should be judged separately.

verdict.justification: The only meaning change in the WA module is three identical `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` additions to the three derived rules, and the cited sources supply no such terminus: RCW 82.87.040 reads "Beginning January 1, 2022 ... Beginning January 1, 2025" with no sunset, and RCW 82.87.060 simply indexes the $250,000 standard deduction under RCW 82.87.150. The module hardcodes nothing year-specific — the standard deduction, charitable deduction, both rates and the $1,000,000 threshold are all caller-supplied inputs (the 2026 projected $284,000 lives only in the companion test fixtures) — so `max(0, gains - std_ded - charitable_ded)` and the two-rate schedule remain true statements of RCW 82.87.040/060/080 in 2027 and later; the pre-fix open window did not disagree with the source text. The fix narrows the module below what the source supports, as a fail-closed declaration of the validated 2026 oracle slice (the PR itself says it closes "truthfulness and period-boundary gaps without changing the underlying tax formulas"), which is a project scoping/validation-coverage policy, not a corrected misreading of the statute. Note the pre-existing `effective_from: '2026-01-01'` is likewise a pilot-slice date rather than a source date (the tax began 2022, the additional rate 2025), which confirms these window endpoints track validation scope, not the provision.
verdict.quote: +        effective_to: '2026-12-31'
verdict.notes: Refutation targets the "fidelity" classification, not the kind: if a reviewer does treat this as a fidelity defect, wrong_period_or_effective_date is the right kind, so "reclassify" was never the alternative. The first reader's stated reading is factually off on the decisive point — it claims the module was "built on a supplied PolicyEngine 2026 projected $284,000 standard deduction and 2026 supplied rates/threshold", but those values appear nowhere in the module; they are only in pilot_liability_pipeline.test.yaml inputs (`wa_pit_pilot_supplied_standard_deduction: 284000`), so RCW 82.87.060's annual adjustment under RCW 82.87.150 does not make the unbounded formula false. Pre/post files confirm the WA module contains only three derived rules and no parameters (unlike VT, whose "two parameters were already bounded" per the PR), so there is not even an internal inconsistency between bounded parameters and unbounded dependents here. Verdict is not "mechanical": the version window is encoded meaning and the engine behavior for 2027 genuinely changes (probes now fail closed) — the change just isn't a correction against the cited source. A reviewer who holds that in this repo an open version window is itself an ungrounded claim about unvalidated periods could reasonably keep this as "unclear"; I would not accept "confirmed" without a source-side basis for a 2026-12-31 end date, and none exists in RCW 82.87.040/060 as resolved through corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix. triage.commit_summary: The commit reworks the Colorado 39-22-104 pilot liability pipeline so that Colorado taxable income enters through a single supplied completed-return boundary input instead of being derived inside the module from supplied AGI, supplied federal deductions, and aggregate subsection (3)/(4) amounts, while adding effective_from proof atoms, fuller statutory excerpts, an explicit inputs declaration, and a fixture grid expanded from 6 to 19 cases. It also removes the now-stale pending-validation fingerprint and known-validation-gaps waiver for the separate us-co/statutes/39/39-22-627.yaml module, and reframes the promoted output as the section 104 base tax before the section 627 temporary rate adjustment and before all credits.

modules.description_quote: retain one explicit completed-return Colorado taxable-income boundary
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix rule derived Colorado taxable income itself as max(0, AGI - supplied federal deductions + supplied additions - supplied subtractions), an IRC section 63 derivation that the cited Colorado provision only incorporates by reference and that its single proof excerpt (the subsection (2) modification clause) does not state, so the module asserted an upstream chain it had not encoded - but that arithmetic does not actually contradict C.R.S. 39-22-104(2), so no disagreement with the source text is demonstrated.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us-co/statute/39/39-22-104): (1.7)(c) imposes 4.40 percent on federal taxable income as determined under IRC 63 for taxable years commencing on or after January 1, 2022, and (2) modifies that federal taxable income by subsections (3) and (4). Both pre- and post-fix encodings are consistent with that text; rate, entity (TaxUnit), period, effective_from '2022-01-01', output names, and the max(0, ...) floor are unchanged, and the operand reorder in co_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability is meaning-neutral. Decisive evidence against a value correction: the six canonical fixtures keep identical expected outputs pre and post (13900/611.6, 43900/1931.6, 133900/5891.6, 27800/1223.2, 87800/3863.2, 267800/11783.2); only the input surface moved, from four supplied components to one supplied completed-return co_taxable_income, plus 13 new boundary fixtures. Neither the commit message ('Promote Colorado PIT base tax', empty body) nor the PR text says the old encoding disagreed with the source; the PR frames it as promotion and deliberate scope narrowing ('This is deliberately the section 104 base-tax surface'), and the three issue comments are review-cycle bookkeeping only (reviews and review_comments are empty). Alternative kind if a reviewer keeps it: wrong_entity_or_scope, since the pre-fix rationale claimed the pipeline computed 39-22-104 'liability before credits' when it actually produced the pre-39-22-627 base tax, and the post-fix summary narrows that claimed output surface; I chose untraceable_branch because the decisive formula change removes the ungrounded AGI-minus-deductions derivation. A pre-fix gap the fix does not close in-module: joint_300000 still expects 267800 with no subsection (3) deduction-limitation addback - the fix pushes that to the caller rather than encoding it. The commit also touches three non-module files (manifest re-signing, pending-validation-fingerprints, known-validation-gaps) whose removed entries are for us-co/statutes/39/39-22-627.yaml, a different module this commit does not change. This module is a hand-assembled composition (manifest 'manual_exception': 'composition', backend 'manual'), not encoder-generated; like the Alabama pilot it had no inputs: block before this commit, so the added inputs: declaration tightens an otherwise implicit contract. git log shows no later commit touching this file.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix formula `max(0, AGI - supplied_federal_deductions + supplied_additions - supplied_subtractions)` does not disagree with the cited text: C.R.S. 39-22-104(1.7)(c) itself imposes the rate "on the federal taxable income, as determined pursuant to section 63 of the internal revenue code", and subsection (2) then modifies it by the (3) additions and (4) subtractions — so the AGI-minus-deductions step was grounded in the cited provision's own incorporation clause, not an untraceable branch. The fix moves the caller/oracle boundary from four supplied aggregates to one supplied completed-return Colorado taxable income; all six retained canonical fixtures keep byte-identical expected outputs (13900/611.6, 43900/1931.6, 133900/5891.6, 27800/1223.2, 87800/3863.2, 267800/11783.2), so no encoded result changed. Everything else is provenance and prose: widened proof excerpts, new effective_period atoms for an unchanged 2022-01-01 window, a commutative reorder of the rate multiplication, a rewritten rationale/summary, and a waiver/fingerprint removal for a different file (us-co/statutes/39/39-22-627.yaml). The commit and PR frame it as a deliberate scope promotion ("Promote Colorado PIT base tax"), not a correction, and there is no review text calling the old formula wrong against the source.
verdict.quote: This is deliberately the section 104 base-tax surface. Section 627 and credits remain outside the promoted output.
verdict.notes: Refutation of "untraceable_branch": the cited provision text (pinned corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current-la-status-fix, provision us-co/statute/39/39-22-104, body sha256 5575bf68...) reads "(c) ... a tax of four and forty one-hundredths percent is imposed on the federal taxable income, as determined pursuant to section 63 of the internal revenue code, of every individual, estate, and trust." — so an IRC-63 derivation is expressly within the cited source, which defeats "a branch with no basis in the cited source". Decisive module-diff lines for the rework itself: "-          max(0, co_pit_pilot_adjusted_gross_income - co_pit_pilot_supplied_federal_deductions + co_pit_pilot_supplied_additions - co_pit_pilot_supplied_subtractions)" / "+          max(0, co_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income)", plus a new `inputs:` block declaring co_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income. Unchanged across the fix: entity TaxUnit, period Year, dtype Money, effective_from '2022-01-01', imported rate and its import hash sha256:4d1715dc..., both output rule names, and the max(0, ...) floor (so no boundary_direction change). Not "mechanical" either, since the formula and the input surface genuinely changed — it is a narrowing of the module's claimed upstream coverage with identical arithmetic at the boundary, i.e. an interface/oracle-boundary change rather than a fidelity correction. If a reviewer wants to keep it, the only live argument is that the pre-fix module asserted an upstream federal chain it had not encoded (its single proof atom excerpt covered only the subsection (2) modification clause); that is a proof-coverage/provenance weakness, not an encoded meaning that disagrees with the source, and I would still not promote it to fidelity.

modules.triage_notes: Read both full versions (git show of parent 034e299693d8e1b28001d6b2dc96476e31ac9f48 and of 033968c960) plus the whole 563-line diff; the module is the only rule file in the commit (the other two paths are the companion test fixture, 438 lines changed, and the encoding manifest). Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus release (us-nj/statute/54a:2-1): the new (a)(7) wide table (bounds 20000/50000/70000/80000/150000/500000/1000000; bases 0/280/805/1295.50/1645/5512.50/27807.50/72657.50; rates .014/.0175/.0245/.035/.05525/.0637/.0897/.1075) and the (b)(7) narrow table (bounds 20000/35000/40000/75000/500000/1000000; bases 0/280/542.50/717.50/2651.25/29723.75/74573.75; rates .014/.0175/.035/.05525/.0637/.0897/.1075) match the statute character for character, including the $1,295.50→$1,645.00 half-dollar discontinuity, and subsection c. does route a would-be head of household who is a nonresident alien to subsection a. So the post state is faithful, but nothing in the pre state disagreed with the source: the pre-fix module contained none of these numbers and carried an explicit disclaimer that it 'owns only the statutory active-bracket mechanics'. This is the promote pattern — scope/precision the module never claimed — so per the rubric it is not a fidelity defect; I recommend a reviewer PRUNE it from the defect corpus. Two secondary changes a reviewer may want to weigh, neither of which I think converts this into a fidelity defect: (a) every version gains `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` where the pilot's versions were open-ended from 2026-01-01 — this narrows the module to tax year 2026 and is more restrictive than the statute (the post-2020 schedule has no sunset), so it is a fail-closed design choice, not a source disagreement; (b) the pre-fix file declared no `inputs:` block at all for its nj_pit_pilot_supplied_* variables while the post-fix declares two inputs — structural/schema, not fidelity. No reviews, review comments, or issue comments exist on PR #982 and the commit body is empty, so the PR body is the only stated rationale; it describes a promotion ('Promote the complete ... schedules'), never a corrected error. Confidence is set below 0.5 per the unclear convention, but my substantive read is fairly firm that this is a scope promotion rather than a defect fix.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute the "unclear" reading and instead found the evidence settles it the other way: every rule that existed before the commit keeps its meaning, so nothing encoded was corrected. The pre-fix module declared its scope as delegated authority (`status: composed_from_supplied_current_authority`, a pattern used at the same parent commit by the us-ca, us-ny, us-nm, us-id, us-ky, us-md, us-mn, us-ne and us-me pilots, so it is a sanctioned scaffolding stage rather than a one-off excuse), its `base + rate * max(0, income - floor)` formula matches the statutory "X plus Y% of the excess over Z" table form exactly, and its old fixtures computed statutorily correct answers from the supplied brackets (e.g. 280 + .0175*9,000 = 437.50 under (b)(7); 805 + .0245*8,000 = 1,001 under (a)(7)). The commit "Promote New Jersey 2026 income tax schedule" internalizes the (a)(7)/(b)(7) tables, the filing-status selector and the subsection (c) NRA routing — coverage the module never claimed — and I verified every new threshold, base and rate against the pinned corpus text (release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current, body sha256 90d8d163…) with no discrepancy. The only meaning change to a pre-existing rule is the added `effective_to: '2026-12-31'`, which narrows below the statute (the (7) schedules run "for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2020" with no sunset), so it is a fail-closed pilot boundary, not a period correction.
verdict.quote:
-      status: composed_from_supplied_current_authority
+      status: official_parameter_source
verdict.notes: Refutation attempts that failed, for the reviewer's record. (1) unrepresented_clause: the whole bracket table, filing-status split and subsection (c) are newly added, but the pre-fix header explicitly disclaimed them and routed them to the caller, so this is added scope, not a missing clause the module purported to encode — the rubric's "coverage the module never claimed" carve-out applies squarely. (2) wrong_period_or_effective_date: the pre-fix rules were open-ended (no effective_to) and the fix caps them at 2026-12-31, but the statute's (a)(7)/(b)(7) paragraphs have no end date, and the pre-fix module held no year-specific parameters (they were caller-supplied), so nothing could go stale; the cap is the pilot's "All rules fail closed outside tax year 2026" choice. (3) amount_mismatch: there were no numbers in the pre-fix module to be wrong; all new values check out against the pinned text, including the deliberate $1,295.50→$1,645.00 half-dollar discontinuity and the inclusive "Not over" upper bounds encoded as `<=`. (4) Rename `nj_pit_pilot_supplied_taxable_income` → `nj_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income` is a rename only. Two genuine hygiene observations that are not fidelity defects: the pre-fix file had no `inputs:` block at all, so its three `supplied_*` symbols were undeclared free variables; and the pre-fix pilot borrowed PolicyEngine's own bracket selection, making its oracle agreement partly circular. Neither is a disagreement with §54A:2-1. Commit body is empty, PR #982 has zero reviews/comments, and the PR text reads entirely as promotion ("Promote the complete ... schedules"), never as a correction.

Refutation attempts and why they fall short, for the reviewer to weigh:
(1) "Promote pattern, not a fix." The commit subject is "Promote Delaware 2026 income tax schedule" with an empty body, and the PR body never says anything was wrong — its "Review cycle" section lists only presentation/provenance and branch-shape findings. Real counter-pressure, but the PR does record "validation-gap ratchet: resolved Delaware waiver retired", and the deleted `known-validation-gaps.yaml` entry for `us-de/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml` sits under `validate_failures:` whose file header reads "Modules failing encode validate (source grounding etc.)". Caveat: that waiver list is a bulk consolidation-time burn-down (every entry points at the same issue 782, same owner, same 2026-10-08 expiry), so it is not a targeted finding about this module.
(2) "The pre-fix boundary was declared, so nothing false was claimed." The old rationale did say the floor/base/rate/deduction/credit "are declared caller-supplied inputs" and that "The pipeline adds no numeric literals of its own". But the encoded function is still not § 1102(a)(14): outside the six pinned grid cases it returns `base` even for taxable income below the supplied floor, and the companion test had to hand-feed floor 25,000 / base 1,001 / 0.0555 (and 60,000 / 2,943.5 / 0.066) per case. The schedule was outside the encoding, not encoded.
(3) "Provenance only, therefore mechanical." Does not hold: formulas, parameters, entity grain (new Person-grain rules and a `de_pit_pilot_taxpayer_of_tax_unit` data_relation), and version windows (`effective_to: '2026-12-31'` added) all change. This is far more than excerpt or citation strings.
(4) Alternative kinds considered. `unrepresented_clause` is arguable — the source states a six-band schedule the encoding lacked and the fix adds it — but the fix's center of gravity is removing/re-grounding ungrounded values and the 1110 credit branch, so untraceable_branch fits at least as well and the kind definition explicitly covers "formulas grounded on the wrong provision." `wrong_entity_or_scope` describes a real change (TaxUnit-only → Person+TaxUnit, output moved from after-nonrefundable-credits to `de_income_tax_before_non_refundable_credits_unit`) but nothing in the source made the old scope wrong; that is consequence, not defect.
(5) Honest residual: note that §§ 1108 and 1110 do exist in real Delaware law, so the old outline (AGI − standard deduction, tax − personal credit) is not contrary to Delaware statute as such; what it lacked was any basis in the *cited corpus source*. A reviewer who reads "cited source" as the statute rather than the certified slice could downgrade this to unclear or not_a_defect. The new module also stops modeling the deduction and credit entirely, so this is a boundary redraw as much as a correction.

Against pruning: the pre-fix module DID claim its terminal rule was the 12-700 liability, and the fix replaces that formula's meaning rather than merely adding outputs — so it is not cleanly the additive-scope carve-out either.

Alternative kind: untraceable_branch is nearly as defensible. modules.description_quote: import the official $26,050 threshold, $332 base amount, and 2.75% excess rate
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix schedule rule levied a positive tax on the first $26,050 of individual nonbusiness taxable income (a 1.27448% "first-bracket effective rate" times min(income, threshold)), but ORC 5747.02(A)(3) states "If the balance thus obtained is equal to or less than twenty-six thousand fifty dollars, no tax shall be imposed on that balance" — that no-tax clause was absent from the encoding, and the 1.27448% rate it used instead is the rate 5747.02(A)(2) prescribes for estates, not individuals.

(A)(2) confirms 1.27448% is the ESTATES rate for 2026, which the pre-fix rationale had imported as the individual "first-bracket effective rate". Behavioral proof the meaning changed: the companion test file adds below_no_tax_threshold (taxable 20,000 -> schedule_tax 0) and exactly_at_no_tax_threshold (26,050 -> 0); under the pre-fix formula those would be 0.0127448*20,000 = $254.90 and $332.00204. CONFOUNDS a reviewer should weigh: (1) this is a promote-pattern rewrite, not a targeted fix — the commit message is a bare subject with an empty body and neither it nor the PR body names a defect; PR #975 is titled "Encode Ohio 2026 individual income tax liability" and has no reviews or review comments. (2) The pre-fix module's own prose disclaimed the region: "It deliberately models only the ordinary resident wage earner above the $26,050 no-tax threshold" — but nothing in the rule enforced that, the version was open-ended from 2026-01-01, and the formula returned a nonzero tax at any income, so the encoded meaning still disagreed with the source. (3) The same commit narrows scope (drops the supplied 5747.025 personal exemption and 5747.98 exemption credit, retargets from PolicyEngine oh_income_tax_before_refundable_credits to oh_income_tax_before_non_refundable_credits, replaces five supplied inputs with one declared input) and adds effective_to '2026-12-31' to all three rules — those are redesign/fail-closed choices, not defect corrections, so a reviewer wanting a clean single-defect instance may prefer to prune. ALTERNATE KINDS, same hunk: untraceable_branch (the first-bracket term was a formula grounded on the wrong provision, 5747.02(A)(2) estates, and the fix removes it) and wrong_entity_or_scope (estate rate applied to individuals); a secondary amount_mismatch also exists inside the module's own claimed above-threshold scope, where the derived base $332.00204 (0.0127448 x 26,050) replaced by the statutory $332.00 overstated tax by $0.00204 for every above-threshold filer. FOLLOW-UPS on the same file: 79ec7714d "Ground Ohio 2026 PIT in H.B. 96 analysis" (32 minutes later, same PR) and aa886454e "Bound Ohio 2026 nonbusiness income tax schedule (#1105)" on 2026-07-26. Other files in the commit are the encoder apply manifest and .axiom/index/provisions_to_rules.json (bookkeeping).

verdict.justification: I tried to refute the reading and it survived against the pinned statute: ORC 5747.02(A)(3) says "In the case of individuals ... If the balance thus obtained is equal to or less than twenty-six thousand fifty dollars, no tax shall be imposed on that balance", and the pre-fix `oh_pit_pilot_schedule_tax` (source line "5747.02(A)(3)", TaxUnit, no guard) instead levied `first_bracket_rate * min(taxable_income, no_tax_threshold)` — a positive tax up to $332 on that exact balance. Above $26,050 the pre and post formulas agree to $0.002 (332.00204 vs 332.00), so the entire behavioral delta of the formula edit is the sub-threshold no-tax carve-out the fix adds, which the encoder records as a new proof atom of `kind: condition` carrying that statutory sentence verbatim. That is the definition of unrepresented_clause: a clause the source states was missing, and the fix adds it.
verdict.quote:
+            kind: condition
+              excerpt: "If the balance thus obtained is equal to or less than twenty-six thousand fifty dollars, no tax shall be imposed on that balance."
-          oh_pit_pilot_supplied_first_bracket_rate * min(oh_pit_pilot_taxable_income, oh_pit_pilot_supplied_no_tax_threshold)
+          if oh_pit_pilot_taxable_income <= individual_income_tax_no_tax_threshold:
verdict.notes: Refutations attempted and their outcomes. (1) untraceable_branch does NOT fit better, and the first reader's secondary claim is wrong in substance: 1.27448% is indeed the (A)(2) estate rate, but (A)(5) directs that "To recompute the tax dollar amount corresponding to the lowest tax rate in division (A)(3) ... the commissioner shall multiply the tax rate prescribed in division (A)(2) of this section by the income amount specified in that division" — so 0.0127448 x 26,050 = $332.00204 is the statute's own construction of the (A)(3) base amount, not an ungrounded estate-rate import. The first term was legitimate above the threshold; only its unconditional application below the threshold was wrong. (2) The pre-fix module did document the gap in prose ("It deliberately models only the ordinary resident wage earner above the $26,050 no-tax threshold" and "reproduces the statutory ... form for filers above the no-tax threshold"), which is the strongest not_a_defect argument; I rejected it because the rule carried no domain guard and fails open with a wrong positive number under its own (A)(3) citation, and the fix encodes the clause rather than documenting it. This is why I hold confidence at 0.78 rather than higher. (3) The first reader's cited quote ("import the official $26,050 threshold, $332 base amount, and 2.75% excess rate") is about parameter provenance (supplied caller inputs -> `imports:` of encoded 5747.02 parameter rules) and does not by itself support the kind; the diff and statute text do. (4) The commit is mixed: most of the 216-line diff is scope redesign (boundary moves from AGI minus supplied personal exemption to completed-return taxable nonbusiness income; the 5747.98 exemption credit is dropped so the output is now tax before nonrefundable credits) plus a new `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` although (A)(3)(c) reads "For taxable years beginning in 2026 and thereafter" — that window closure is conservatism, not a source-driven correction, and should not be counted as wrong_period_or_effective_date. (5) Boundary strictness is correct in both directions: statute says "equal to or less than", fix uses `<=`. Verified against corpus release us-rulespec-snap-2026-07-21, provision us-oh/statute/5747.02, body sha256 c65d945f29da16a0bdc5c424843434da27f0120ae0ab32722e9551436fce3980. Supporting evidence for the estate-rate derivation is in the pre-fix companion test at 98d0d93c98:us-oh/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.test.yaml ("first-bracket effective rate 0.0127448 (the $332.00204 base amount / 26,050)"), all six of whose fixtures sit above the threshold — no fixture exercised the region where the defect bites.

The reader's period reading is also mechanically false as stated: the pre-fix module carried no numeric literals at all (thresholds and rates were caller-supplied inputs `mt_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_floor_1/2` and `..._rate_1/2`, and its own rationale said "The module adds no operative numeric literals"), so it could not have "silently return[ed] the 2026 rates for post-2026 periods." The reader's quote is a sentence in the post-fix rationale describing the new design, not evidence of the pre-fix flaw; the real commit body is empty and its subject is "feat: complete Montana 2026 PIT schedule." The unbounded `effective_from: '2026-01-01'` window against a text that "(Terminates December 31, 2026)" is a genuine secondary flaw, but the added `effective_to` is applied uniformly across a wholesale rewrite whose stated and dominant correction is the missing subsection (2) clause.
verdict.quote: +        formula: mt_pit_pilot_ordinary_income_tax + mt_pit_pilot_capital_gains_tax
verdict.notes:
Two fidelity flaws are bundled in one commit, so a reviewer must pick the headline kind. (a) unrepresented_clause: subsection (2)'s express carve-out ("Except as provided in subsection (2)") and its 3.0%/4.1% bands were absent; the fix adds `mt_pit_pilot_net_long_term_capital_gain`, `..._nonqualified_taxable_income`, `..._capital_gain_lower_band`, `..._capital_gains_tax` and folds them into the existing liability output — changing the value of an output the module already published. (b) wrong_period_or_effective_date: every pre-fix version had `effective_from: '2026-01-01'` with no `effective_to`, contradicting "(Terminates December 31, 2026--sec. 7, Ch. 227, L. 2025.)" and the module's own pre-fix rationale ("applies through December 31, 2026"). If the corpus tracks the reader's kind by what the encoding asserted rather than what it computed, (b) is defensible and the verdict becomes confirmed.

Caveats that argue for keeping confidence moderate: the pre-fix module explicitly declared `deferred_outputs` for both subsection (3) definitions and scoped itself to a "no-capital-gains pilot" ("Candidate 2026 ... pipeline for an ordinary full-year resident wage earner ... No capital gains or credits are active"), and every rule is named `mt_pit_pilot_*`. A reviewer applying the "new coverage the module never claimed" rule strictly could push this to not_a_defect. I did not, because the liability output was unguarded (no input or condition restricted it to zero-gain filers) and the deferrals covered only the two definitions, not the liability itself.

Also note the head-of-household $71,250 addition is NOT an amount_mismatch: pre-fix the threshold was the caller-supplied `mt_pit_pilot_supplied_bracket_floor_2`, so HOH was reachable if the caller passed $71,250; the fix internalizes the parameter rather than correcting a wrong number.
