triage.commit_summary: The commit rewrites the South Carolina pilot income-tax pipeline (us-sc/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml) from a composition that accepted the active bracket's cumulative base, floor, and marginal rate as caller-supplied inputs into a module that encodes S.C. Code section 12-6-510(C)(1)'s two-bracket 2026 schedule itself as four private, proof-grounded parameters (1.99%, $30,000, 5.21%, $966) plus an explicit threshold branch, and narrows the runtime boundary to a single TaxUnit input sc_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income. It also bounds every version to tax year 2026 with effective_to '2026-12-31' so 2025 and 2027 fail closed (section 12-6-510(C)(2) makes later top rates depend on annual revenue determinations), and refreshes the companion fixtures from a six-case PolicyEngine grid to eight hand-computed boundary cases plus the signed applied-files manifest.

modules.description_quote: Replaces the supplied-schedule South Carolina pilot with the complete two-bracket schedule enacted by 2026 Act 110 in S.C. Code section 12-6-510(C)(1).
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix module did not represent section 12-6-510(C)(1)'s schedule at all - the $30,000 bracket threshold, the 1.99% and 5.21% rates, and the $966 subtraction were caller-supplied inputs rather than encoded, and the 2026-only schedule carried no effective_to - but the module openly declared that supplied-input scope and, with its documented inputs, reproduced the statutory amounts exactly, so no wrong number was ever produced.
modules.triage_notes: Single-module commit (index 0 is the only module file); companion test file and .axiom/encoding-manifests/.../pilot_liability_pipeline.json also changed (fixtures rewritten from 6 PolicyEngine-grid cases to 8 boundary cases; manifest is bookkeeping). Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus release (us-sc/statute/12-6-510): (C)(1) states '$0 $30,000 1.99% times the amount' and '$30,000 or more 5.21% times the amount minus $966', and (C)(2)(a) makes the top rate from Tax Year 2027 contingent on a 5% individual-income-tax revenue projection, with (C)(2)(b) eventually collapsing the schedule to a single rate on all income - so the encoded rates, floor, subtraction, and the new '< floor' boundary (lower bracket is 'but less than $30,000', upper is '$30,000 or more') are all source-faithful, and no boundary defect is introduced. Reason for 'unclear' rather than 'fidelity': this is a promote/hardening change, and I verified the old and new formulas are algebraically identical given the pre-fix module's documented inputs (597 + 0.0521*(TI-30000) == 0.0521*TI - 966; at TI=30,000 both brackets give $597; at TI=50,450 both give $1,662.445). The pre-fix upstream_source_check status was literally 'composed_from_supplied_current_authority' and its rationale disclosed the delegation, so the module never claimed to encode the rate schedule - which matches the task's 'scope the module never claimed' carve-out. Secondary candidate kind is wrong_period_or_effective_date: the PR states 'Bounds every policy-bearing amount and calculation to tax year 2026; 2025 and 2027 fail closed because later rates depend on future revenue determinations,' and the pre-fix versions had effective_from '2026-01-01' with no effective_to; I did not choose it because the pre-fix formulas were fully caller-parameterized, so the open-ended window did not freeze any stale statutory rate into 2027+. One genuine over-claim in the pre-fix file: sc_pit_pilot_schedule_tax carried two proof atoms citing the table cells '$0 $30,000 1.99% times the amount' and '$30,000 or more 5.21% times the amount minus $966' as grounding for versions[0].formula, although that formula contained none of 1.99%, 5.21%, $30,000, or $966; the fix makes the formula actually implement those atoms (this is the strongest argument for calling it a fidelity correction). The fix also drops an ungrounded max(0, ...) clamp on sc_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability, which is behavior-neutral under the new schedule, and renames the boundary input sc_pit_pilot_supplied_taxable_income to sc_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income while adding an explicit 'inputs:' block that the pre-fix file lacked. PR #966 has zero reviews and zero review comments; the two issue comments are post-merge main-refresh gate reports by the author and contain no defect description. Screening note 'Unsure (promote pattern)' agrees with this triage.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix module explicitly declared, in its status (`composed_from_supplied_current_authority`), rationale, and summary, that the active bracket's base, floor, and marginal rate were caller-supplied rather than encoded, and it documented the $597 cumulative base as exactly equivalent to the statutory 5.21%-minus-$966 expression; I verified that equivalence (0.0521 x 30000 - 966 = 597, and 597 + 0.0521*(y-30000) = 0.0521*y - 966) and confirmed against the pinned corpus text of 12-6-510(C)(1) that the lower/upper bracket boundary at $30,000 is continuous, so no bracket-selection error could produce a wrong amount at the boundary either. The companion fixtures corroborate this: every expected value shared between the old and new fixture sets is byte-identical (30,000 -> 597, 300,000 -> 14,664), so the fix corrected no number, threshold, rate, or boundary. The added `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` is a consequence of newly hardcoding 2026 constants, not a correction: the pre-fix version carried no year-specific value at all, so its open-ended window was not a timeless encoding of superseded text. Under the stated rule that a change merely adding scope the module never claimed is not a defect, this is a declared-scope promotion (commit subject "Promote South Carolina 2026 income tax schedule", PR "Promote South Carolina 2026 PIT schedule"), not a fidelity correction, which refutes the unrepresented_clause reading.

-        the active bracket's cumulative base tax, floor, and marginal rate as
-        caller-supplied current-authority inputs. The upper-bracket inputs use
-        a $597 cumulative base at $30,000, exactly equivalent to the statutory
-        5.21-percent-minus-$966 expression. Deductions, exemptions, special
verdict.notes: Strongest counter-argument, if a reviewer wants to keep this at "unclear" rather than drop it: the pre-fix `sc_pit_pilot_schedule_tax` rule was sourced "S.C. Code section 12-6-510(C)(1), two-bracket 2026 schedule" and carried two proof atoms on `versions[0].formula` quoting both table rows ("$0 $30,000 1.99% times the amount" and "$30,000 or more 5.21% times the amount minus $966") while that formula contained neither rate nor the $30,000 threshold. That is an over-claim of proof coverage relative to the formula, and the fix converts those to `table_cell`/`amount` atoms on real encoded parameters. I judged it not a fidelity defect because the atoms are `kind: formula` (shape grounding, and the cumulative-base-plus-marginal form does mirror the two-row table), and because three other places in the module declared the supplied-input scope. Note also that `composed_from_supplied_current_authority` is free text, not a schema-enforced enum (no hit for it in axiom-encode `src/` at this worktree HEAD), so "declared scope" rests on the module's own prose, not on validator machinery. Other diff changes are non-semantic in effect: `max(0, sc_pit_pilot_schedule_tax)` -> `sc_pit_pilot_schedule_tax` is a no-op (schedule tax is non-negative once taxable income is floored at zero, and equals 597 at the bracket floor), and the input rename `sc_pit_pilot_supplied_taxable_income` -> `sc_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income` plus the new `inputs:` block only formalize the boundary. Ruled out reclassifications: wrong_period_or_effective_date (pre-fix encoded no year-specific value), amount_mismatch and boundary_direction (all shared fixture outputs unchanged; boundary continuous at $30,000), wrong_entity_or_scope (entity TaxUnit unchanged on both sides). Neither version encodes (C)(1)'s "income brackets indexed in accordance with Section 12-6-520" or (C)(2) rate reductions; the post-fix handles that by failing closed outside 2026, which is a design choice, not something the pre-fix got wrong.

triage.commit_summary: The commit promotes the Arizona 2026 individual income tax out of placeholder-pilot form: it adds a new parameter module encoding the 2.5 per cent tax-year-2026 rate from the Arizona Department of Revenue's official 2026 Form 140ES booklet, and rewrites the composed liability pipeline to import that rate, accept a completed-return Arizona taxable-income boundary, drop the AGI-minus-supplied-standard-deduction derivation and the supplied nonrefundable-credit subtraction, and bound both rules to 2026 with effective_to. The stated reason (PR #967) is that the pinned A.R.S. 43-1011 snapshot predates the flat-rate schedule and does not establish the 2026 numeric rate, so the form booklet becomes the singular controlling numeric source; the change also retires the module's known-validation-gaps waiver.

modules.description_quote: imports the official Arizona Department of Revenue 2.5% rate from the 2026 Form 140ES booklet and records A.R.S. 43-1011 as the higher-authority cross-check
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: this file is net-new, so nothing in it was wrong pre-fix; the only pre-existing gap is that the operative 2026 Arizona rate had no encoded grounding anywhere (the pilot pipeline took it as a caller-supplied input), which the new module now supplies from the controlling agency source.
modules.triage_notes: Added file (61 lines): a single parameter rule individual_income_tax_rate = 0.025, effective_from 2026-01-01 / effective_to 2026-12-31, cited to us-az/form/individual-income-tax/2026/140es-booklet/document-1. I read the provision through the pinned release (resolve_provision.py, corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current, fix_time_corpus_match=same_body) and both rate excerpts are verbatim in the source: 'For tax year 2026 estimated tax payments, the tax rate for estimating your tax liability is 2.5%.' and '19 Multiply line 18 by 2.5% (.025) to calculate your Arizona estimated tax liability.' So the new module is faithful; it adds coverage rather than correcting a prior encoded meaning, which is why I classified unclear with kind none per the rubric's 'adds scope the module never claimed is not a defect' clause. A reviewer should probably prune this index from a defect corpus: there is no pre-fix state for a judge to flag. The module also carries an explicit upstream_source_check saying the pinned A.R.S. 43-1011 snapshot predates the live flat rate and does not establish the 2026 numeric rate, which is the only defect-shaped statement in the file and it is about the statute snapshot, not about a prior encoding of this rule.

modules.description_quote: promotes Arizona 2026 individual income tax before nonrefundable credits at the completed-return `az_taxable_income` boundary
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix rules asserted a bracket-base-plus-marginal flat tax and an 'Arizona taxable income = AGI - supplied standard deduction' derivation whose proof atoms cited provisions that do not establish them (43-1011's constitutional cap 'the combined tax rate ... may not exceed four and one-half percent' and a stale 43-1041 snapshot 'the standard deduction is $12,200'), so the operative rate and deduction had no basis in the cited source; but every numeric was an openly declared caller-supplied input, so the module asserted no wrong value.
modules.triage_notes: Read the full pre-fix file at parent 7c0ebc4eb4 and the post-fix file. Three substantive deltas, any of which could be argued as the kind: (1) re-grounding - formulas previously proven by the 43-1011 4.5% combined-rate cap and the stale 43-1041 $12,200 deduction excerpt now import an encoded rate and cite Form 140ES worksheet line 19 (this is why I chose untraceable_branch, and the PR's stated reason is source grounding); (2) scope - az_pit_pilot_schedule_tax is deleted, the AGI->taxable-income derivation is replaced by a supplied completed-return taxable income, and az_pit_pilot_income_tax_liability keeps its name but no longer subtracts the supplied nonrefundable credit, so it now means tax before credits (alternate kind wrong_entity_or_scope); (3) periods - both rules gain effective_to 2026-12-31 where pre-fix they ran open-ended from 2026-01-01 (alternate kind wrong_period_or_effective_date; PR: 'uses a singular controlling numeric source and limits both modules exactly to tax year 2026'). Arithmetic for the covered slice is unchanged (2.5% flat), and the test fixtures were rewritten to the new boundary rather than corrected in value, which is the main reason I did not call this fidelity. The manifest records manual_exception=composition, i.e. this is an assembled pipeline, not encoder output, and the commit retires its known-validation-gaps 'validate_failures' waiver (issue 782 is about the waiver mechanism generally, not about this module's defect). I read the source: worksheet line 18 subtracts total deductions and exemptions from line 14, so the pre-fix 'AGI minus standard deduction' derivation also omitted exemptions and itemized deductions - the fix removes that derivation rather than correcting it. Caution for reviewers: this commit itself introduces a bad proof excerpt - 'Figure this tax on your estimated Arizona taxable income.' does not appear in the pinned document (the actual sentence is 'Figure this tax on your total annual income.'), and follow-up commit a76b6afda 'Tighten Arizona taxable-income boundary proof' (17 minutes later) replaces it with 'Step 1 Estimated Arizona Taxable Income'. PR #967 has no reviews or review comments, only author status comments about rebases; the commit body is empty.

verdict.justification: Module index 0 is a net-new file: the diff is a pure addition ("new file mode 100644", "@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@"), the parent commit has no such path, and `git log --follow` shows 9615ec7118 as the only commit that ever touched it, so no encoded meaning in this file was wrong before the change. Read through the pinned release, the 2026 Form 140ES booklet confirms both proof excerpts verbatim and the 2.5% rate the module encodes as `0.025` for 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, so the module states the source correctly rather than correcting a prior misstatement. The only thing the change remedies is absence: the pre-fix pipeline explicitly and transparently declared the operative rate a caller-supplied input ("the operative flat rate PolicyEngine applies is supplied here as a declared caller input ... supplied here pending their own indexed encodings"), which is a documented scope boundary, not an encoding that disagrees with the source. Under the rule that new coverage a module never claimed is not a defect, this is a promotion/enhancement, so I refute the "unclear" hold for this file and call it not_a_defect.

verdict.notes:
Source verification (read-only, pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current, provision file data/corpus/provisions/us-az/form/2026-07-21-az-140es-2026.jsonl line 2, fix_time_corpus_match: same_body): the booklet contains both encoded excerpts verbatim — "For tax year 2026 estimated tax payments, the tax rate for estimating your tax liability is 2.5%." and worksheet "19 Multiply line 18 by 2.5% (.025) to calculate your Arizona estimated tax liability." So the amount, the effective window, and the entity/period scope of the new parameter all check out; there is nothing here to call an amount_mismatch, wrong_period, or scope defect.

Where a reviewer should look instead: if this commit carries a fidelity defect at all, it is in module index 1 (us-az/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml), whose pre-fix proof atoms grounded the flat-tax formulas on A.R.S. 43-1011's constitutional cap excerpt — verbatim removed line: excerpt: "the combined tax rate ... may not exceed four and one-half percent" — a provision that does not establish the operative 2026 rate, while the rate itself came in as az_pit_pilot_supplied_marginal_rate. That pattern (formula grounded on a provision that does not support it) is the untraceable_branch candidate, and the fix re-grounds it on the 140ES worksheet plus an import of this new rate module. That analysis belongs to module index 1; module index 0 is the new grounding source, not the defect site.

Also note the commit/PR framing is promotion, not repair: subject "Promote Arizona 2026 PIT encoding", PR title "Promote Arizona 2026 individual income tax", body "promotes Arizona 2026 individual income tax before nonrefundable credits". The PR's "first independent review identified an inexact excerpt and unsupported input-domain claim" was fixed inside the PR before merge, so it is not visible in the parent-to-commit diff and should not be read as a pre-existing encoding defect. Residual uncertainty (why 0.73, not higher): a reviewer who scores defects at commit granularity rather than per-file could attribute the pipeline's re-grounding to this file as its vehicle; at file granularity the pre-fix state is nonexistence, which cannot be wrong against a source.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix module contained no numeric of its own — bracket base, bracket floor, marginal rate, standard deduction and nonrefundable credit were all declared caller inputs, and the removed rationale says so outright, so with the parameters the fixtures actually supplied (base 0, floor 0, rate 0.025) it computed exactly the flat 2.5% liability the new module computes; nothing in the diff corrects a value, a strictness, a date window that fired wrongly, or a branch that produced a wrong answer. What the diff does is re-scope: the upstream boundary moves from AGI-minus-supplied-deduction to a completed-return `az_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income` input, the output narrows from after-credit liability to before nonrefundable credits for PolicyEngine parity, and the rate is newly grounded in an imported 2026 Form 140ES rate module — i.e. claims are removed and precision is added, which this rubric says is not a defect. The commit subject is "Promote Arizona 2026 PIT encoding", the PR has zero reviews and no correction language (its only "fixed" line refers to an intra-PR review of the *new* modules), and the same commit retires this module's `known-validation-gaps.yaml` waiver, so the pre-fix file was an openly declared non-validating pilot, not a believed-correct encoding later found wrong. The first reader's basis — that the removed proof atoms cited 43-1011(E)'s 4.5% surcharge cap and 43-1041(A)(1)'s "$12,200" — is a choice-of-source/excerpt problem (I resolved both provisions at the pinned release and both excerpts are present in the cited text, the 43-1011 one with an ellipsis), which the rubric classifies as provenance, not fidelity.
verdict.quote: -        caller-supplied inputs. The pipeline adds no numeric literals of its own;
verdict.notes:
Verification done: pinned release us-rulespec-snap-2026-07-21 (corpus commit 1979c15c65). us-az/statute/43-1011 in that snapshot stops at subsection A paragraph 6 (graduated 2.59/3.34/4.17/4.50 brackets by filing status, post-2018) plus subsection E's combined-rate cap; it contains no flat 2.5% rate. us-az/statute/43-1041(A)(1) does contain the verbatim string "the standard deduction is $12,200", subject to subsection H inflation indexing, and 43-1041(B) states deductions "are to be subtracted from Arizona adjusted gross income in computing taxable income" — so the removed AGI-minus-deduction derivation was itself traceable to the cited statute, just not to the excerpt chosen.

Strongest surviving counter-case, if a reviewer wants to keep this as untraceable_branch: under the pinned snapshot, 43-1011 prescribes a four-bracket filing-status-dependent schedule, yet the pre-fix `az_pit_pilot_schedule_tax` encoded a single supplied-bracket form and its `source:` line asserted "43-1011, flat tax" while its only proof atom quoted the surcharge cap. The sibling new module concedes "the pinned statute snapshot predates the live flat-rate schedule and does not establish the tax-year-2026 numeric rate". If you treat the pinned snapshot (not real 2026 Arizona law) as the yardstick, the pre-fix formula did disagree with its cited text and the fix re-grounds it — that reading is defensible, which is why my confidence is 0.58 rather than higher.

Why I still say prune: (1) the pre-fix module disclosed every limitation in its own rationale and shipped under a `validate_failures` waiver (issue 782, expires 2026-10-08) retired by this same commit — the diff line removed is `  "us-az/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml":` with `fingerprint: "sha256:be4718240767ca7ec8c3576518d48d33eaf6e043913cf1278647cf66dd4d43ff"`; (2) the pre-fix file declared no `inputs:` block at all, so the promotion is also schema hardening; (3) old and new never disagree on a computed quantity for the same real-world facts — they compute different quantities (after-credit vs before-credit liability) from different boundaries.

Runner-up kind if the reviewer overrides to a fidelity verdict: I would take untraceable_branch over the alternatives, with wrong_period_or_effective_date a distant second (both rules gain `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` so 2027 fails closed; but the pre-fix open window carried no year-specific literal, so calling it wrong against the source is weak).

Screen note accuracy: the "108 lines" figure is the file-level stat (108 changed lines in pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml); the new 2026_rate.yaml is a separate added module (index 0) carrying the only numeric literal in the change, 0.025.

modules.triage_notes: Single-file commit (git show --stat: 1 file, 52 insertions, 55 deletions); no test files, no manifest/index files, and a one-line commit message with an empty body. Diffed the extracted rule bodies (name/kind/dtype/entity/period/unit/effective_from/effective_to/formula) between parent 84447d7775 and 586401e4c4: byte-identical, so every formula ('0.052', '0.0558', '46000', '23000', max(0, ...), the two-branch schedule) and both 2026-01-01/2026-12-31 windows are unchanged. The only hunks touch module.source_verification (list field corpus_citation_paths of three statute paths collapsed to the singular corpus_citation_path pointing at us-ks/guidance/department-of-revenue/forms/2026/k-40es/document-1), the prose rationale and summary, the seven per-rule 'source:' label strings, and the eight proof-atom corpus_citation_path/excerpt/table header-row-column strings. Per the triage rule that excerpt-only and citation-string-only corrections are provenance, this is mechanical. Both provisions were read through the pinned corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current (corpus commit c5af541326): the statute carries 'For tax year 2024, and all tax years thereafter: ... Not over $46,000 | 5.2% of Kansas taxable income Over $46,000 | $2,392 plus 5.58% of excess over $46,000' (and the $23,000/$1,196 counterpart), and the K-40ES carries 'TAX COMPUTATION SCHEDULES ... Schedule l - MARRIED FILING JOINT ... $ 0.00 $46,000 ... 5.2% of line 5 $46,000 ... $2,392 plus 5.58% of excess over $46,000' plus the Schedule II analogue - identical numbers, and both the old and the new excerpts are verbatim in their respective documents, so there is no hidden amount change and the old citations were not fabricated. Two notes for a reviewer. (1) The rationale reframing is substantive in wording only: the pre-fix text already acknowledged 79-32,110c's annual rate-reduction mechanism and already bounded the module to 2026, so this is not a wrong_period_or_effective_date fix. (2) The summary edit adds a new documentation paragraph about the PolicyEngine oracle reading ks_agi through a filing-status zero-tax threshold and states 'The module therefore does not import the model-specific zero-tax threshold' - that corrects an over-broad prior claim about the oracle's inputs but adds no rule and changes no scope the module claimed, and summaries are explicitly mechanical; it is worth a reviewer's glance only if the Kansas zero-tax threshold is later judged an unrepresented_clause, which would be a separate defect this commit neither introduced nor fixed. This commit is part of PR #965 (merged 2026-07-22) and follows the repo's recurring 'Conform <state> PIT source metadata' + 'Re-attest' pattern visible on the same branch for GA and NC; PR reviews and review_comments arrays are empty, and the two issue comments are post-merge refresh gate reports with no semantic findings. It also re-grounds every proof atom from generic 422.5/422.7 excerpts onto the specific 422.5(1)(a)/(2)(b)/(3)(b) sentences, drops the 422.7 citation, bounds all three rules to the 2026 tax year with effective_to, and records a deferred_outputs entry for the 422.5(1)(b) post-credit nonresident/S-corporation apportionment.

modules.description_quote: Replaces the prior Iowa ordinary-wage pilot with a completed-return 2026 regular versus alternate-tax selector.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix liability rule, sourced to "Iowa Code section 422.5, tax imposed on taxable income", returned only the regular tax (max(0, ia_pit_pilot_schedule_tax)) and contained no trace of the 422.5(2)(b)/(3)(b) rule that the regular tax "shall be the lesser of the alternate state individual income tax rate of four and three-tenths percent times the portion of the net income in excess of thirteen thousand five hundred dollars" (thirty-two thousand at 65+) "or the regular tax liability computed without regard to this sentence" — but the module had self-declared a narrower slice, so the omission may have been declared scope rather than a defect.
modules.triage_notes: Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus (resolve_provision.py, corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current, expression_date 2026-05-09, fix_time_corpus_match=same_body). 422.5(2)(b) and 422.5(3)(b) both state the alternate-tax lesser-of at 4.3% above $13,500 / $32,000, and the fix's three new proof atoms quote exactly those sentences, so the added clause is genuinely source-stated and was genuinely absent pre-fix. Reasons I did not call this 'fidelity': (1) the commit body is empty and the subject is just "Promote Iowa 2026 PIT selector"; no maintainer or reviewer text anywhere in the PR says the prior encoding was wrong — the PR, its three issue comments (all mainline-merge refresh notes from PavelMakarchuk), and the empty reviews/review_comments lists only describe a promotion and its parity numbers. (2) The pre-fix module scoped itself to the "ordinary resident childless wage-earner slice", and 422.5(2)(b)/(3)(b) apply only to married-filing-jointly, head-of-household, and surviving-spouse filers, so most of the pre-fix declared population is outside the alternate tax; the PR's own parity run reports "Alternate-tax selections: 1, weight 30.328622509627227" out of 976 positive-weight Iowa tax units, i.e. the missing clause almost never binds. (3) This is a wholesale 90-line rewrite, not a targeted fix: the input boundary moved from ia_pit_pilot_adjusted_gross_income minus a supplied subtraction to a supplied completed-return ia_pit_pilot_state_taxable_income, the bracket-base/floor/marginal-rate mechanic was replaced by taxable_income * supplied_regular_tax_rate, and six new supplied inputs were introduced. verdict.justification: The pre-fix module explicitly declared itself a narrow pilot ("the 2026 ordinary resident childless wage-earner oracle slice", every tax-law amount a caller-supplied input), and the commit/PR frame this change as promotion, not correction ("Promote Iowa 2026 PIT selector"; "Replaces the prior Iowa ordinary-wage pilot with a completed-return 2026 regular versus alternate-tax selector"); no commit, PR, or review text asserts the old encoding gave a wrong answer. The 422.5(2)(b)/(3)(b) lesser-of clause cannot change any answer inside that declared slice: with the alternate rate 4.3% applied to net income above 13,500/32,000 versus the 3.8% regular rate on taxable income, the alternate tax is lower only when the net-income-to-taxable-income gap is far below the 2026 standard deduction the pre-fix fixtures used (16,100 single / 32,200 married) — for those filers the break-even taxable income is negative, which is why the promoted module's full-populace run selects the alternate branch for just 1 of 976 units. The change also replaces the entire input contract (AGI + subtraction + bracket base/floor/marginal rate → completed-return state taxable income, modified income, two rates, two floors, two eligibility booleans), retires all six fixtures without altering a single pre-existing expected value, and adds 2026 effective_to bounds and a deferred_outputs block — the signature of moving the composition boundary to a broader target, not of adding a clause the old module got wrong. Post-fix the module still leaves 422.5(2)(a)/(3)(a) nonimposition and alternate-tax eligibility itself to supplied caller inputs, confirming that the supplied-boundary convention is unchanged and only the scope moved.

verdict.notes:
Refutation evidence for the reviewer, all read this session:

1. Scope disclaimer in the pre-fix file (git show 923562e6:us-ia/policies/income_tax/pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml): summary limits the module to the "ordinary resident childless wage-earner oracle slice" and its rationale says "Values that vary by filing status, bracket, annual indexing, or the choice between standard and itemized deductions remain declared caller inputs". Post-fix summary targets "the 2026 before-credit target" at completed-return TaxUnit boundaries — a different, broader claim.

2. Source text (pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-22-current, corpus c5af541, provision us-ia/statute/422.5, expression date 2026-05-09): 422.5(2)(b) is mandatory for MFJ/HoH/surviving spouse over $13,500 ("In lieu of the computation in subsection 1 ... the regular tax imposed under this subchapter shall be the lesser of the alternate state individual income tax rate of four and three-tenths percent times the portion of the net income in excess of thirteen thousand five hundred dollars or the regular tax liability computed without regard to this sentence"), with the 65+/$32,000 variant at 3(b). So the clause is real and mandatory — the reason this is not a defect is scope, not the statute being permissive.

3. Binding check (arithmetic, run this session): alternate is lower iff 0.043*(TI + D - floor) < 0.038*TI, i.e. TI < (580.5 - 0.043*D)/0.005 for the 13,500 floor, where D is the net-income-minus-taxable-income gap. D = 32,200 → threshold -160,820; D = 24,150 → -91,590; D = 16,100 → -22,360. Those are exactly the deduction amounts the pre-fix fixtures used (16,100 single, 32,200 married), so no standard-deduction wage earner in the declared slice could ever have been mis-taxed by the omission. Only an atypical small-D profile (the new fixture uses D = 5,000) triggers the branch, matching the PR's "Alternate-tax selections: 1" out of 976 positive-weight units.

4. Rewrite signature: the fixture file was entirely replaced (git show 26969d5f91 -- ...test.yaml); not one pre-existing case's expected liability changed. A targeted fidelity fix would normally keep cases and move an expectation, or add a case that fails against the old formula. Checking the old married_60000 case by hand: alternate 0.043*(60000-13500) = 1,999.50 vs regular 1,056.40 — regular still governs.

5. File history (git log -- pilot_liability_pipeline.yaml): 6c30d0501 "feat: add twelve state income tax liability pilots" → 6f84cbc18 "fix: address state tax review findings" (Iowa delta was two trailing blank lines only) → 26969d5f91 "Promote Iowa 2026 PIT selector" → e0dccaf04 "Encode Iowa alternate-tax floors privately". The promote-then-parameterize arc is a pilot-to-production pattern across states, not a defect repair. oracle-coverage-pending.yaml entries for the three Iowa rules are byte-identical pre and post.

Residual risk that keeps this below 0.75: the pre-fix liability rule's own source line was the unqualified "Iowa Code section 422.5, tax imposed on taxable income" with the generic excerpt "A tax is imposed upon every resident and nonresident of the state", so a strict reviewer can argue the rule claimed the whole section and therefore owed the mandatory lesser-of clause regardless of the module summary's slice language. If the reviewer weights the rule-level citation over the module-level scope disclaimer, unrepresented_clause at low confidence is the fallback; it should not be graded "confirmed" either way, because the same commit also re-grounds every citation, swaps the entire input surface, and adds 2026 effective_to bounds, so no single diff line isolates a clause repair. A secondary candidate a reviewer might raise — the taxable-income rule moving off 422.7 ("The term 'net income' means the taxable income as properly computed for federal income tax purposes") onto 422.5(1)(a) — is provenance plus boundary change, not a demonstrated meaning error.

triage.commit_summary: The commit brings four Georgia income-tax modules up to current law: it closes the previously open-ended (timeless) versions of the pre-2024 personal exemptions, standard deductions, age/blindness additional deductions and the 30% child-care credit rate at their true last effective year, and adds the amended amounts from SB 56 (2023, effective TY2024), HB 1021 (2024), HB 136 (2025) and HB 463 (2026), each with new proof atoms citing the session-law corpus paths. It also rewrites the 48-7A-3 low-income credit's age-65 enhancement from a multiplier that doubled the entire tax unit's credit into one additional credit unit for each of the taxpayer and the spouse aged 65 or over (the Georgia DOR IT-511 worksheet arithmetic), renaming `age_credit_multiplier` to `additional_age_credit_units` and updating the companion tests.

modules.description_quote: repair Georgia PIT law through 2027, including 2026 standard/dependent amounts
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The module encoded superseded text timelessly: its single open-ended versions asserted a $3,000 dependent exemption and $7,400/$3,700/$2,700 personal exemptions for every year from 2003/2013 onward, so it returned pre-2024 law for 2024+ even though HB 1021 raised the dependent exemption to $4,000 for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2024, HB 463 raised it to $5,000 for 2026, and SB 56 (Sections 2-2 through 2-6, applicable to taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2024) replaced the taxpayer/spouse personal exemptions.
modules.triage_notes: Read the cited session laws through the pinned corpus release: HB 1021 (2024) revises 48-7-26(b) to '$3,000.00 $4,000.00 for each dependent' and is 'applicable to all taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2024'; HB 463 (2026) revises it to '$4,000.00 $5,000.00 for each dependent'; SB 56 Section 4-1(2) makes Sections 2-2 through 2-6 applicable from TY2024. The fix adds effective_to '2023-12-31' to the three personal-exemption parameters and to the derived personal_exemption_deduction selector (correct: after TY2024 O.C.G.A. 48-7-26(b) contains only the dependent exemption), and adds versions[1] 4000 (2024-2025) and versions[2] 5000 (2026-) to dependent_exemption_amount. It also converts module.source_verification.corpus_citation_path to corpus_citation_paths listing the three acts, which is provenance bookkeeping riding along with the substantive change. Follow-up commit 5474dca0e ('Complete state income tax RuleSpec campaign', same PR) adds SB 56 effective-date excerpts and a deferred_output for 2027+ because HB 463's $125 annual increases are contingent on revenue-condition delay tests. Companion test file gained 24 lines of new-period cases in the same commit.

modules.description_quote: the DOR-backed low-income age calculation
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The age-65 enhancement was applied at the wrong scope and to the wrong member set: it multiplied the entire tax unit's credit (schedule amount times all dependents) by 2 whenever the filing taxpayer was 65 or over, instead of adding one credit unit for the aged individual, and it ignored the spouse's age entirely, so a joint return on which only the spouse was 65 or over received no enhancement even though 48-7A-3(b) says 'Each taxpayer 65 years of age or over may claim double the tax credit' and (a)(1) deems each spouse on a joint return a dependent.
modules.triage_notes: Read the full provision text of us-ga/statute/48/48-7A-3 through the pinned corpus. Important tension a reviewer should weigh: the literal sentence is 'Each taxpayer 65 years of age or over may claim double the tax credit', which on a flat reading supports the PRE-fix formula (schedule amount * dependents * 2 = 48 in the updated test case) rather than the post-fix one (8 * (3 + 1) = 32). The maintainers' basis is administrative guidance, not the statute sentence: the PR body says the repair covers 'the DOR-backed low-income age calculation' and that 'independent Georgia review found and drove fixes for contingent 2027 deductions, transition proofs/tests, DOR worksheet support'. Follow-up commit 5474dca0e (same PR) makes that explicit by adding corpus path us-ga/form/it-511/2025/document-1 and an upstream_source_check rationale: 'The official Georgia DOR 2025 IT-511 worksheet supplies the operational joint-return arithmetic: one age unit when either spouse is 65 or older, two when both are, with those units added to the number of exemptions before multiplication by the schedule amount.' At the time of THIS commit the new formula's only proof atom still cites the statute excerpt about doubling, so the module briefly asserts DOR arithmetic under a statutory citation. I kept classification 'fidelity' because one component is squarely source-grounded regardless of the DOR reading (the pre-fix encoding gave a 65+ spouse on a joint return nothing at all, contradicting 'Each taxpayer 65 years of age or over'), and because the whole change was review-driven and described as a repair; confidence is only 0.5 because the kind is arguable (amount_mismatch for the 2-vs-+1 multiplier, unrepresented_clause for the omitted spouse, or 'other' for wrong aggregation structure) and because a judge reading only the statute could defend the pre-fix formula. Mechanics of the diff: rule renamed age_credit_multiplier -> additional_age_credit_units, dtype Decimal -> Integer, new input spouse_is_65_years_of_age_or_over, and the credit formula changes from '* age_credit_multiplier' to '* (dependents_entitled_to_claim_count + additional_age_credit_units)'. Companion test renames the doubling case, changes its expected credit from 48 to 32, and adds a new joint-return case where only the spouse is 65+. No other rule in the module changed.

item.screen_reason: Corrects NY SNAP composition's exposed benefit surface: statutory chain carried cents and diverged from FNS QC on 33 of 847 reviews by one dollar; moves issued benefit onto the 273.10 whole-dollar chain, binds claimed-homeless deduction to zero to remove a double homeless path, and removes duplicate inline bridges.

triage.commit_summary: The commit re-points New York's SNAP issued-benefit output from the pure-statutory 7 USC 2014(e)/2017(a) chain, which computes in cents, onto the 7 CFR 273.10(e)(1)-(2) whole-dollar chain, by adding three derived rules to the NY OTDA FY2026 benefit-calculation composition: snap_total_allowable_shelter_expenses bound to NY's 18 NYCRR 387.12(f)(3)(vi) allowable shelter costs (which carry the homeless shelter-expense substitution), snap_claimed_homeless_shelter_deduction bound to zero so only one homeless path stays live, and snap_benefit gated on snap_eligible with NY's initial-month proration. It was motivated by the SNAP QC administrative oracle: replaying 847 FY2024 New York QC reviews, the statutory surface diverged from FNS's recomputed FSBEN on 33 reviews by one dollar each, while the 273.10 chain reproduced 847/847 exactly; the commit also deletes the now-duplicate inline bridges in programs/us-ny/snap/fy-2026.yaml and refreshes the reverse index and encoder apply manifests.

modules.description_quote: The New York SNAP composition's public benefit surface rode the pure-statutory 2014(e)/2017(a) chain, which carries cents — the 2014(e)(2) earned-income deduction is unrounded and the composed excess-shelter cost subtracts the half-income share unrounded — where FNS's QC Minimodel and New York's own eligibility systems compute in whole dollars under the 7 CFR 273.10(e)(1)(ii)(A) election, encoded in the 273.10 chain since #826.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The composition exposed New York's SNAP benefit off the pure-statutory 2014(e)/2017(a) allotment, which carries cents and omits NY's initial-month proration and the 387.12(f)(3)(vi) homeless shelter-expense substitution, instead of the 7 CFR 273.10(e)(1)-(2) whole-dollar issuance computation that FNS and New York actually apply, so the issued amount was wrong by one dollar on 33 of 847 FY2024 NY QC reviews.
modules.triage_notes: Module diff is purely additive (three new derived rules appended; no existing rule, version, parameter or effective date changed), but this is still a meaning change to an already-claimed output rather than a new surface: programs/us-ny/snap/fy-2026.yaml already listed snap_benefit in `outputs`, and this commit deletes that spec's inline `conditional_value` snap_benefit bridge (`when_true: snap_monthly_allotment`) and its `sum_terms` snap_total_allowable_shelter_expenses bridge (household_shelter_costs_incurred + snap_utility_allowance_for_shelter_costs) in favor of the composition's rules. The spec's own removal comment records the behavioral deltas verbatim: the new binding 'unlike the removed bridge, carries the homeless shelter-expense substitution' and the composition 'exposes the issued benefit with New York's initial-month proration, which the removed conditional_value bridge lacked'. Evidence read: companion test us-ny/policies/otda/snap/fy-2026-benefit-calculation.test.yaml adds a case asserting snap_benefit 217 while us:statutes/7/2017/a#snap_regular_month_allotment is 216 on identical facts (inline test comment: 'statutory chain floors 216.85; the issued 273.10 whole-dollar benefit is 217'), plus an EID-cents case (180) and a homeless case (allowable shelter 198.99, claimed_homeless 0, benefit 119). I verified in us/regulations/7-cfr/273/10.yaml at this commit that the 273.10 chain really does round (floor on the earned-income deduction, floor(x + 0.5) on excess shelter cost, floor on the allotment) and that snap_monthly_allotment lives there, and in us-ny/regulations/18-nycrr/387/12/f/3/vi.yaml that snap_allowable_shelter_costs substitutes the standard homeless shelter allowance. KIND IS THE UNCERTAIN PART, hence confidence 0.55: classification 'fidelity' is solid, but the label could reasonably be (a) wrong_entity_or_scope, chosen here because the taxonomy lists 'output surface' explicitly and both the commit subject and PR body describe a 'public benefit surface' riding the wrong chain; (b) amount_mismatch, since the observable harm is a cents-vs-whole-dollar rounding divergence of exactly $1 on 33/847 reviews; or (c) unrepresented_clause, since the 273.10(e)(1)(ii)(A) rounding election, the 387.12(f)(3)(vi) homeless substitution and the 18 NYCRR 387.10 initial-month proration were all absent from the exposed benefit. untraceable_branch fits poorly: the statutory chain is correctly grounded in 2017(a), it is just not the issuance computation. Step 4 not run: the module's only corpus_citation_path is us/guidance/usda/fns/snap-fy2026-cola/page-1 (the FY2026 COLA guidance, boilerplate composition-source atoms), which cannot settle the rounding question; the operative 273.10 rounding excerpts were read from the imported module's own proof atoms instead. Note the proof atoms on all three new rules cite that composition source rather than the operative provisions — the PR body still claims 'Proof atoms cite the operative sources', but a later commit in the same squashed PR reverted them to the composition source to satisfy the proof validator, so the PR body is stale on that point. The commit is a squashed 7-commit PR with two review rounds (gpt-5.6-sol REQUEST-CHANGES then APPROVE; a Claude clean-room review); the reviews array in the bundle is empty, so the review content is only available as narrative in the PR body. Rest of the commit is mechanical: reverse-index regeneration and .axiom/encoding-manifests refreshes. Follow-up flagged by the authors: axiom-oracles#269 must drop its run-time pins of snap_total_allowable_shelter_expenses and snap_claimed_homeless_shelter_deduction, which now collide with these rules.

verdict.justification: The first reader's mechanism — that the exposed benefit "rode the pure-statutory 2014(e)/2017(a) allotment ... instead of the 7 CFR 273.10(e)(1)-(2) whole-dollar issuance computation" — is refuted by the repository: at the parent commit the only `snap_benefit` in NY scope is the program-spec bridge `when_true: snap_monthly_allotment`, and `snap_monthly_allotment` is defined solely in `us/regulations/7-cfr/273/10.yaml` (source `7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)`), while the statutory 2017(a) chain's output is named `snap_regular_month_allotment` and was never the exposed surface. What the module addition actually corrects are two NY clauses the prior chain omitted: the issued benefit now takes New York's initial-month certification-period proration (`snap_initial_month_allotment_after_minimum_issuance`), which the commit itself says "the removed conditional_value bridge lacked," and the 273.10 shelter input is rebound to `snap_allowable_shelter_costs` (18 NYCRR 387.12(f)(3)(vi)), carrying the homeless shelter-expense substitution and NY's SUA/LUA/IUA that the removed bridge's `snap_utility_allowance_for_shelter_costs` term (federal state-option placeholders, all `formula: '0'` in 7 CFR 273.9) contributed as zero. That is a required condition/deduction missing from the encoding and added by the fix, so it is a fidelity defect of kind unrepresented_clause, not a wrong entity/scope or wrong output surface.
verdict.quote:
+          if snap_eligible:
+              if household_initial_month:
+                  snap_initial_month_allotment_after_minimum_issuance
+              else:
+                  snap_monthly_allotment
+          else:
+              0
verdict.notes: Evidence trail, all read at parent ead0b4e6 in /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us: (1) `git grep "name: snap_benefit"` over us/, us-ny/, programs/us-ny/ returns exactly one hit, programs/us-ny/snap/fy-2026.yaml:134 — the removed `pattern: conditional_value` bridge whose `when_true: snap_monthly_allotment`; (2) `git grep "name: snap_monthly_allotment"` over the whole tree returns exactly one hit, us/regulations/7-cfr/273/10.yaml:447, `source: 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)`; so the pre-fix issued surface was already on the whole-dollar 273.10 chain and the "carries cents / statutory chain" framing in the PR body does not describe the composed output. (3) The cents story is true only of the parallel statutory chain (`snap_allotment_before_minimum`/`snap_regular_month_allotment` in us/statutes/7/2017/a.yaml) and of the module's own `ny_snap_excess_shelter_cost`/`snap_excess_shelter_deduction`, which 273.10 never consumes (it uses its own `snap_excess_shelter_deduction_for_net_income`). (4) The removed shelter bridge summed `snap_utility_allowance_for_shelter_costs`, which in us/regulations/7-cfr/273/9.yaml is the sum of three `*_state_option` rules each with `formula: '0'`, while NY's real allowance rules are named `snap_standard_utility_allowance` etc. in us-ny/regulations/18-nycrr/387/12/f/3/v/a.yaml — so the old 273.10 shelter input silently dropped NY's utility allowances as well as the vi homeless substitution. (5) The module diff is purely additive (three appended rules, nothing existing altered) and the companion test diff is 411 insertions / 1 deletion with no changed expected value, so no previously encoded module meaning was overwritten; the corrected surface is the program's, carried by these new bindings. A reviewer who wants to keep this case should record the kind as unrepresented_clause (missing 18 NYCRR 387.10 proration and 387.12(f)(3)(vi) shelter substitution), and should treat the PR body's 33/847 one-dollar narrative as unverified against the pre-state code. If a reviewer instead weights the shelter-input rebinding as the dominant delta, untraceable_branch (formula grounded on the wrong provision — 273.9's zero state-option placeholders — re-grounded on 387.12(f)(3)(vi)) is the second-best kind; wrong_entity_or_scope is the one kind the code does not support.

item.subject: (screen-flagged) Wrong amount: module carried the superseded printed $143 homeless shelter deduction cap and clamped the COLA-adjusted amount down for every homeless unit (oracle found $37 mismatch on all seven CO FY2024 units); rebinds min() to the annually adjusted maximum and removes the stale parameter.
item.screen_reason: Wrong amount: module carried the superseded printed $143 homeless shelter deduction cap and clamped the COLA-adjusted amount down for every homeless unit (oracle found $37 mismatch on all seven CO FY2024 units); rebinds min() to the annually adjusted maximum and removes the stale parameter.

triage.commit_summary: The commit rebinds the SNAP homeless shelter deduction cap in `us/regulations/7-cfr/273/10.yaml` from a hard-coded $143 parameter to the imported FY-COLA policy value `snap_homeless_shelter_deduction`, deletes the stale `snap_homeless_shelter_deduction_cap` parameter, and documents the supersession in the module summary and a new `upstream_source_check`. The reason: 7 CFR 273.10(e)(1)(i)(G)'s printed $143 is the FY 2019 base value that 7 USC 2014(e)(6)(D)(ii) indexes each October 1, so the min() clamp was cutting every homeless unit's correctly supplied COLA amount back to $143 — caught by the SNAP QC administrative-data oracle as an exact $37 mismatch on all seven Colorado FY 2024 units (companion test updated to the FY 2026 memo amounts, deduction 198.99 and allotment 270).

modules.description_quote: all seven Colorado FY 2024 QC units claiming the standard homeless shelter deduction mismatched by exactly the gap between the regulation's printed $143 and the FY 2024 indexed maximum ($179.66, recorded as $180 in the whole-dollar QC file)
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The module capped the homeless shelter deduction at a hard-coded $143 — the superseded FY 2019 base figure printed in the CFR — for a version effective 2025-10-01, so it produced a dollar amount below the controlling annually indexed maximum (198.99 for FY 2026, 179.66 for FY 2024) that 7 USC 2014(e)(6)(D)(ii) and the USDA COLA memoranda set.
modules.triage_notes: Single-module commit (plus its companion test and encoding manifest). Diff evidence is exact: the `snap_homeless_shelter_deduction_cap` parameter (formula `143`) is deleted and `min(snap_claimed_homeless_shelter_deduction, snap_homeless_shelter_deduction_cap)` becomes `min(snap_claimed_homeless_shelter_deduction, snap_homeless_shelter_deduction)` binding the already-imported us:policies/usda/snap/fy-2026-cola/deductions output (new proof import atom added). Companion test flips the homeless case from deduction 143 / net 148 / allotment 253 to 198.99 / 92.01 / 270, confirming the pre-fix values were wrong money amounts, not just bookkeeping. The provision WAS read through the pinned corpus release (us/regulation/7/273/10): 273.10(e)(1)(i)(G) literally prints "Subtract the homeless shelter deduction, if any, up to the maximum of $143", so the encoding matched the printed CFR text but disagreed with the controlling source chain (statute indexing + COLA memo), which the fix now records in `upstream_source_check`. Kind call: amount_mismatch is primary (a wrong dollar threshold, oracle-measured as an exact $37 gap, per the commit subject and body); wrong_period_or_effective_date is the defensible alternative reading since this is arguably timeless carriage of superseded text under an effective_from of 2025-10-01 — hence confidence is 0.82 rather than higher. The rest of the diff (module summary rewrite, upstream_source_check block) is documentation consistent with the same fix and changes no other formula, version, scope, or date.

verdict.justification: The diff changes executable meaning, not provenance: it deletes the `snap_homeless_shelter_deduction_cap` parameter whose sole version formula was `143` and rebinds the `min()` in `snap_homeless_shelter_deduction_for_net_income` to the imported FY-2026 COLA value (198.99 in `us/policies/usda/snap/fy-2026-cola/deductions.yaml:61`), and the companion test moves the deduction from 143 to 198.99 and the allotment from 253 to 270. I read 7 USC 2014(e)(6)(D) through the pinned release: clause (i) prints "$143 a month" and clause (ii) states "For fiscal year 2019 and each subsequent fiscal year the amount of the homeless shelter deduction specified in clause (i) shall be adjusted", so a version effective 2025-10-01 carrying the FY2019 base figure is a numerically wrong threshold against the controlling source, exactly as the oracle's uniform $37 gap on the seven Colorado FY2024 units shows. I tried the competing kinds and they fail: no effective_from/effective_to, version window, or period kind changed (ruling out wrong_period_or_effective_date — the 2025-10-01 window was and remains correct, only the value inside it was stale), and the pre-fix value was verbatim traceable to the rule's own cited provision (e)(1)(i)(G), which is the right provision for this deduction, so it was not an untraceable or misgrounded branch. It is also not mechanical or an enhancement: the module already imported the FY-2026 COLA module for the deduction itself, so the clamp actively pulled a correctly supplied current-year amount down to a superseded number.
verdict.quote:
-        formula: |-
-          143
...
-          min(snap_claimed_homeless_shelter_deduction, snap_homeless_shelter_deduction_cap)
+          min(snap_claimed_homeless_shelter_deduction, snap_homeless_shelter_deduction)
verdict.notes:
Evidence trail for a reviewer: pre-fix parameter block at `git -C /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us show 623703a46e:us/regulations/7-cfr/273/10.yaml` lines ~95-110 (`snap_homeless_shelter_deduction_cap`, `effective_from: '2025-10-01'`, `formula: 143`); import target value confirmed at `17c4a96dfb:us/policies/usda/snap/fy-2026-cola/deductions.yaml:61` (`snap_homeless_shelter_deduction: 198.99`); behavioral proof in the companion test diff (`snap_homeless_shelter_deduction_for_net_income: 143 -> 198.99`, `snap_monthly_allotment: 253 -> 270`).

One genuine tension worth recording, which is why I did not go above ~0.86: the module's own cited corpus text (7 CFR 273.10(e)(1)(i)(G), resolved through the pinned release) literally reads "Subtract the homeless shelter deduction, if any, up to the maximum of $143" with no indexing language on its face, so a strict "cited source text only" reading would call the pre-fix encoding faithful. The defect survives that reading because the statute the CFR implements carries the adjustment clause in the same subparagraph, and the fix records this explicitly via the new `upstream_source_check` with `checked_paths: us/statute/7/2014` and the FY2026 COLA memo page. If this corpus later adds a kind for "encoded a superseded printed base figure where the source indexes annually", this case is its canonical example; under the current kind list, amount_mismatch is the closest and the only one whose definition is fully satisfied.

The rest of the commit (summary rewrite, `upstream_source_check` block, new import proof atom with hash) is provenance/metadata and would be mechanical on its own; the classification rests entirely on the removed `143` parameter and the `min()` rebind.

item.subject: (screen-flagged) Corrects 42 USC 415(i) which 'baked one determination year into a year-general statute module' (scope/effective-period fix, replaces hard import with free input).
item.screen_reason: Corrects 42 USC 415(i) which 'baked one determination year into a year-general statute module' (scope/effective-period fix, replaces hard import with free input).

triage.commit_summary: The commit makes the 42 USC 415(i) cost-of-living statute module year-general: it drops the hard import of the year-specific 2026 SSA COLA percentage (2.8%) and takes the applicable increase percentage as a free input `cola_applicable_increase_percentage`, with each determination year's value supplied by its own policy file. The reason given is that 415(i)(2)(A)(i) directs the Commissioner to determine the applicable increase percentage each year beginning with 1975, so the percentage is a per-year determination rather than statutory content; the companion 2026 policy module only has its deferred-outputs rationale reworded to match, and the test file's change is comment-only.

modules.description_quote: The cola/2026 deferred-outputs rationale is updated to reflect the free input rather than an import.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing in this module's encoded meaning was wrong; only the prose rationale describing how the downstream statute module consumes the percentage was stale (it said 415(i) imports the value, which after this commit it no longer does).
modules.triage_notes: Diff touches exactly one field: module.deferred_outputs[0].reason (a free-text rationale string). The rule that emits social_security_cola_2026_applicable_increase_percentage, its value (2.8%), dtype, effective dates, proof atoms, and source_values are all unchanged (verified by reading the full diff; no other hunks). Module-level metadata/prose only, so mechanical per the rubric. It is a dependent edit of the index-1 fix, not an independent defect.

modules.description_quote: The statute-level PIA cost-of-living module hard-imported the year-specific 2026 COLA policy and baked one determination year into a year-general statute module
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The single version window effective_from 1975-01-01 multiplied the primary insurance amount by the 2026 determination's percentage (2.8%) in every year, whereas 42 USC 415(i)(2)(A)(i) requires the applicable increase percentage to be determined by the Commissioner 'each year beginning with 1975', so the encoding applied one year's determination timelessly across all years.
modules.triage_notes: Provision read via resolve_provision.py on us/statute/42/415/i/2 (corpus pinned to the commit): confirmed 'The Commissioner of Social Security shall determine each year beginning with 1975 ... whether the base quarter ... is a cost-of-living computation quarter' and that the increase is 'by the applicable increase percentage' with no percentage stated in the statute, so the per-year-determination framing in the commit message is grounded. Decisive diff: the module-level import of us:policies/ssa/cola/2026#social_security_cola_2026_applicable_increase_percentage and its matching proof import-atom are removed, and the formula term changes from social_security_cola_2026_applicable_increase_percentage to the free input cola_applicable_increase_percentage; the summary gains an Input contract paragraph. Nothing else in the module changed: the dime-rounding parameter, the floor() rounding rule, effective_from dates, entity, period, dtype, and the 415(a) PIA import are identical. Kind is a judgment call between wrong_period_or_effective_date and untraceable_branch: no date/version field literally changed, but the defect is a single determination year baked into an all-years (1975-onward) window, which the commit and the screening label both frame as the year/effective-period problem; the untraceable_branch reading is that the percentage term was grounded in SSA guidance for one year rather than in the cited statute. Hence confidence held below 0.8 on kind, not on the fidelity classification. The PR notes only the 2026 determination exists in the corpus ('the structural win is that the statute no longer carries any year'), so no currently-executable output changes value today; the meaning change bites for any year other than 2026. Test file us/statutes/42/415/i.test.yaml changed comments only (hand-verification arithmetic restated, 3,263.20 x 1.028 = 3,354.5696 -> 3,354.50); the encoding manifest change is bookkeeping (hashes, encoder version 0.2.1153 -> 0.2.1155). No PR reviews or comments exist on #554, so the commit/PR body is the only stated-reason evidence.

verdict.justification: The change is a real fidelity correction, but nothing period-shaped was actually edited: every version window in the module stays `effective_from: '1975-01-01'`, `period: Year` is unchanged, and no version was added, split, or closed. What the diff removes is a value with no basis in the cited source — the statute text resolved from the pinned corpus (`us/statute/42/415/i/2`) states only "by the applicable increase percentage" and fixes no number, yet the module imported the SSA-guidance-grounded 2.8% figure from `us/policies/ssa/cola/2026` and a proof atom of `kind: import` pointing at it. The fix deletes that import and re-grounds the term as the free input `cola_applicable_increase_percentage`, which is exactly untraceable_branch's stated shape ("a value with no basis in the cited source (the fix removes or re-grounds it), including formulas grounded on the wrong provision"), not an effective-date or version-window disagreement.
verdict.quote: -  - us:policies/ssa/cola/2026#social_security_cola_2026_applicable_increase_percentage
verdict.notes:
Decisive diff lines (all verbatim from 001.diff): removal of the `imports:` line quoted above; removal of the proof atom block `- path: versions[0].formula / kind: import / import: / target: us:policies/ssa/cola/2026#social_security_cola_2026_applicable_increase_percentage`; and the formula swap `-          * (1 + social_security_cola_2026_applicable_increase_percentage)` / `+          * (1 + cola_applicable_increase_percentage)`.

verdict.notes: Drop this case from the real-defect corpus. Evidence checked: (1) diff 000 (whole-file deletion) header shows the retired module already carried `corpus_citation_path: us/statute/42/1396a/a/10`, as does every one of its six proof atoms — identical to the destination module, so the "synthetic" element was only the repo path `us/policies/hhs/medicaid/eligibility.yaml` and the `us:policies/...#` output namespace. (2) `git show 3e67b2a2:us/statutes/42/1396a/a/10.yaml` confirms the destination already held former_foster_care_age_ceiling_years=26, adult_expansion_age_ceiling_years=65, adult_expansion_income_limit_poverty_line_rate=1.33, SLMB 1.10 (1993) / 1.20 (1995) and inpatient_hospital_durational_limit_exception_age_ceiling_years=1 — the deleted file's copies were byte-equal in value and date, so no parameter value, boundary, or version window moved. Only child_ssi_deeming_age_ceiling_years=21 was unique, and it reappears unchanged as ssi_child_age_ceiling_years=21, effective 1974-01-01 (a rename). (3) Composite branch-for-branch: other mandatory (A)(i) / adult expansion (VIII) / former foster care (IX) / optional (A)(ii) / Medicare cost-sharing (E) / COBRA (F) all survive; `<=` against 133 percent is preserved on both sides (statute: "does not exceed 133 percent of the poverty line"), and the income comparison merely restates fraction-of-poverty-line as dollars times poverty_line_for_family_size. Two residual nuances a reviewer may want, neither sufficient and neither mentioned in the commit or PR: the deleted helper `former_foster_care_mandatory_eligible` carried `effective_from: '1974-01-01'` for an ACA-2014 subclause, but it was only ever reachable through a composite dated 2014-01-01 and the surviving statute-module parameter `former_foster_care_age_ceiling_years` keeps the same 1974 repo-floor convention; and the old single input `person_entitled_to_or_enrolled_in_medicare_part_a_or_b` slightly over-broadens Part B versus the statute's "or enrolled for benefits under part B", which the new split input fixes — an input-name refinement, not a change in encoded logic. If the harness taxonomy prefers to bucket meaning-preserving relocations rather than discard them, "mechanical" (rename/namespace move/provenance) is the alternative; I did not choose it because the module file was deleted and the formula text was restructured with a new import, which fails mechanical's "formulas and inputs unchanged" letter.

verdict.justification: The candidate reading treats the added `is_medicaid_eligible` composite as supplying coverage the source requires, but the sibling file deleted in the same commit (`us/policies/hhs/medicaid/eligibility.yaml`) already contained that exact composite — same rule name, same Person/Month/Judgment scope, same `effective_from: '2014-01-01'`, same six-disjunct structure (other mandatory group, adult expansion, former foster care, optional group, Medicare cost-sharing, COBRA), and already grounded on the identical `corpus_citation_path: us/statute/42/1396a/a/10`. So the commit is what its subject says — "Move Medicaid eligibility composite to statute source" — a repo relocation, not a correction of encoded meaning, and the statute module's prior state was explicit abstention (`deferred_outputs` for the mandatory and optional group outputs), which cannot disagree with the source. The only substantive addition, the `qualified_pregnant_woman_or_child` disjunct via the 1396d(n) import, was previously subsumed in the opaque input `person_is_in_mandatory_group_under_subparagraph_a_i_other_than_adult_expansion_or_former_foster_care`, so subclause (A)(i)(III) was never unrepresented — it became computable, which is precision, not fidelity; likewise `ssi_child_age_ceiling_years: 21` is a rename of the deleted module's `child_ssi_deeming_age_ceiling_years: 21` with the identical excerpt "who are under 21 years of age".

Formula rewrites between the two locations are meaning-preserving restatements: `not person_entitled_to_or_enrolled_in_medicare_part_a_or_b` → `not ..._part_a and not ..._part_b` (De Morgan), and `household_income_as_fraction_of_poverty_line <= rate` → `income_determined_for_adult_expansion <= rate * poverty_line_for_family_size` (same comparison in dollar form); no threshold, boundary strictness, date, entity, or polarity changed. Source text (pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, provision sha256 d8bf3b8e…) confirms (A)(i)(III) "who are qualified pregnant women or children as defined in section 1396d(n)" and (A)(i)(II)(cc) "who are under 21 years of age", so the new content is grounded — it is just not a correction of anything that was wrong. Residual uncertainty (why 0.76 not higher): the removal of the two `medical_assistance_available_to_*_groups` deferred outputs means the statute module's declared output surface did change, and a reviewer who counts "module stopped deferring" as fidelity work could argue unclear; I judge that an abstention-to-coverage move, which the task rules classify as new coverage the module never claimed. If forced off not_a_defect, the next-best label is unclear, never unrepresented_clause.

triage.commit_summary: The commit adds a new module encoding the 42 USC 402(a) old-age insurance benefit entitlement predicate (fully insured under 414(a), attained age 62, and filed an old-age application or was entitled to disability insurance benefits for the month before attaining retirement age), then rewires 42 USC 426(e)(2) to import that entitlement output in place of the local free-input cross-reference placeholder `individual_is_entitled_to_benefits_under_section_402`. The stated driver was tooling, not a discovered meaning error: PR #541 having encoded the first 402 modules made axiom-encode's encoded-cross-reference-placeholder check reject 426(e)'s local placeholder, parking the module under `validate_failures` in known-validation-gaps.yaml (rulespec-us#553); the parent 426.yaml changed only its import hash pins for 426/e outputs.

modules.description_quote: **Encode 42 USC 402(a) old-age entitlement** — new `us/statutes/42/402/a.yaml`:
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the file is brand new (status 'added'), so there is no pre-fix encoding that could disagree with the source — this is new statutory coverage, not a correction.
modules.triage_notes: Recommend a reviewer PRUNE this index: a fidelity judge benchmark item needs a pre-fix module to flag, and none exists here. I read the provision through the pinned corpus (us/statute/42/402/a, release us-rulespec-foundation-v3-2026-07-15) and the new encoding matches the source predicate: '(1) is a fully insured individual (as defined in section 414(a)...)', '(2) has attained age 62, and', '(3) has filed application for old-age insurance benefits or was entitled to disability insurance benefits for the month preceding the month in which he attained retirement age' -> formula `individual_is_fully_insured and age >= old_age_insurance_benefit_minimum_age_years and (filed_application or prior_DIB)`, parameter 62. Known incompleteness (not a defect being fixed, but worth flagging as possible future-defect material): the module encodes only the entitlement conjunction and omits the 402(a)(A)/(B) beginning-month rules and the 'ending with the month preceding the month in which he dies' termination, and 414(a)/423 remain unencoded leaf free inputs (the module's Input contract says so explicitly). modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix conjunct was an ungrounded local free input meaning entitlement to any benefit under section 402, whereas 426(e)(2) read in context means entitlement to old-age insurance benefits specifically ('so entitled to old-age insurance benefits'), so the pre-fix condition was arguably broader than the provision — but the pre-fix excerpt 'entitled to benefits under section 402' is itself verbatim source text, so the pre-fix encoding was literally faithful.
modules.triage_notes: I read the provision through the pinned corpus (us/statute/42/426/e, release us-rulespec-2026-07-13). 426(e)(2) reads: 'in the case of an individual under age 65 who is entitled to benefits under section 402 of this title , and who was entitled to widow's insurance benefits or widower's insurance benefits based on disability for the month before the first month in which such individual was so entitled to old-age insurance benefits...'. The diff (a) adds a module-level `imports:` entry for us:statutes/42/402/a#individual_is_entitled_to_old_age_insurance_benefit, (b) replaces the proof atom kind `condition` (excerpt 'entitled to benefits under section 402') with an `import` atom pinned to the new 402/a module, and (c) swaps the formula conjunct `individual_is_entitled_to_benefits_under_section_402` -> `individual_is_entitled_to_old_age_insurance_benefit`. Nothing else in the module changed (other four rules, the 65 and 50 parameters, effective_from '1974-01-01' all untouched). Why UNCLEAR rather than fidelity: both the commit message and PR frame this as cross-reference wiring forced by axiom-encode's encoded-cross-reference-placeholder check ('426(e) now imports that entitlement output instead of the placeholder, so the placeholder check passes'), not as a discovered disagreement with the statute; the placeholder was an honest stub with the same intended meaning. Why not MECHANICAL: the formula and the module's input set genuinely changed (a free leaf input became a computed upstream output driven by fully-insured/age-62/application facts), so the module's evaluated meaning changed. If a reviewer keeps it, the defect is scope: 'any section 402 benefit' narrowed to 'old-age insurance benefit under 402(a)'. Note the sibling conjuncts already referenced old-age conversion, which partly constrained the pre-fix breadth in practice. Commit also removed the 426/e entry from known-validation-gaps.yaml#validate_failures and updated three companion test files (402/a 6 cases, 426/e 5 cases incl. a new non-entitled negative case).

verdict.justification: Module 0 (`us/statutes/42/402/a.yaml`) is a brand-new file — the diff opens with `new file mode 100644` and `--- /dev/null`, 0 pre-lines against 109 post-lines, so there is no pre-fix encoded meaning in this module that could have disagreed with 42 USC 402(a). Every rule in it (`old_age_insurance_benefit_minimum_age_years` = 62 from 402(a)(2), and the `individual_is_entitled_to_old_age_insurance_benefit` conjunction of fully-insured + age >= 62 + (application filed OR prior DIB entitlement)) is first-time statutory coverage the module never previously claimed, with 414(a)/423 left as documented honest leaf inputs rather than fabricated branches. The only arguably corrective change in this commit lives in a different module file, `us/statutes/42/426/e.yaml` (index 2), which swaps the local free input `individual_is_entitled_to_benefits_under_section_402` for an import of the new 402(a) output; that is where any fidelity question belongs, not here. I therefore refute "unclear" and resolve it to not_a_defect: new coverage, not a correction.
verdict.quote: This encodes 42 USC 402(a) old-age insurance benefit entitlement:
verdict.notes: Diff header for this module: "new file mode 100644" / "--- /dev/null" / "+++ b/us/statutes/42/402/a.yaml" with @@ -0,0 +1,109 @@ — nothing to correct. Reviewer should look at module index 2 (us/statutes/42/426/e.yaml) instead if this commit is to yield any defect case; its decisive lines are `-            excerpt: "entitled to benefits under section 402"` replaced by `+            kind: import` / `+              target: us:statutes/42/402/a#individual_is_entitled_to_old_age_insurance_benefit`, and in the formula `-          and individual_is_entitled_to_benefits_under_section_402` → `+          and individual_is_entitled_to_old_age_insurance_benefit`. Even that one is weak as a fidelity defect: the pre-fix 426(e) predicate was a same-meaning local placeholder for section 402 entitlement, and the PR's stated trigger is a tooling check, not a source disagreement — PR body: "`axiom-encode`'s encoded-cross-reference-placeholder check now sees section 402 as encoded and rejects the local placeholder, so 426(e) was parked under `validate_failures`". The one substantive shift there is narrowing "benefits under section 402" (any 402 benefit) to 402(a) old-age insurance benefit specifically, which the PR defends on the source ("The 426(e)(2) statute references entitlement to **old-age insurance benefits** under section 402"); if a reviewer wanted a kind for that module it would be wrong_entity_or_scope, but it reads more as placeholder-to-import wiring than a corrected meaning. No provision lookup was needed for this verdict since the module has no prior text to compare against the source.

verdict.justification: The pinned corpus text of 426(e)(2) says verbatim "in the case of an individual under age 65 who is entitled to benefits under section 402 of this title", so the pre-fix conjunct `individual_is_entitled_to_benefits_under_section_402` and its proof-atom excerpt "entitled to benefits under section 402" were literally faithful to the cited source — there is no source basis for calling the old text wrong. The change was driven entirely by a tooling gate: PR #541 made section 402 "encoded", which made axiom-encode's encoded-cross-reference-placeholder check reject the local leaf input, parking the module under `validate_failures`; the fix re-grounds that leaf on the newly-encoded 402(a) output. The companion-test diff is decisive: not one expected output changed (all four pre-existing cases keep their same `holds`/`not_holds` verdicts; only input plumbing changed, with `age: 50` bumped to `63` purely to clear 402(a)'s own age-62 gate so the same outcomes still hold), and the sibling conjuncts (`..._for_month_before_first_month_entitled_to_old_age_insurance_benefits`, `..._upon_becoming_entitled_to_old_age_insurance_benefits`, `current_month_is_first_month_of_old_age_insurance_entitlement_or_later`) already carried the old-age-conversion requirement, so the pre-fix formula was not operatively broader than the provision. This refutes the first reader's wrong_entity_or_scope reading: the quoted PR line asserts the new import is semantically correct, not that the prior encoding disagreed with the statute.
verdict.quote: Because #541 encoded the first `402/*` modules (402(q)/(w)), `axiom-encode`'s encoded-cross-reference-placeholder check now sees section 402 as encoded and rejects the local placeholder, so 426(e) was parked under `validate_failures`.

(1) Module diff /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/diffs/us/09960abf54/002.diff changes exactly one formula token: "-          and individual_is_entitled_to_benefits_under_section_402" / "+          and individual_is_entitled_to_old_age_insurance_benefit", plus the matching proof atom flipping from kind: condition (excerpt "entitled to benefits under section 402") to kind: import with a pinned hash, and a new top-level imports: block. No parameter, version, effective_from, dtype, entity, period, or output surface changed. (2) Pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, provision sha256 71ca5a98...) confirms the pre-fix excerpt is verbatim statutory text; the narrowing to old-age benefits comes only from the later "so entitled to old-age insurance benefits" back-reference, i.e. an interpretive gloss, not a contradiction of the encoded phrase. (3) git -C /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us diff 044e91ad8a 09960abf54 -- us/statutes/42/426/e.test.yaml shows zero flipped expectations; the only added case (not_entitled_to_old_age_benefit_blocks_old_age_conversion_deeming) is new coverage for the new import, which the rubric treats as not-a-defect. (4) Caveat worth a human eye: this is a genuine input-surface change (a free leaf became an upstream import), so it is not strictly "mechanical" under the letter of that category either; if the corpus wants a bucket for gate-driven cross-reference re-grounding, this is a clean exemplar of it. The only route back to "fidelity" would be arguing the pre-fix free input could be set true by an individual entitled to some non-old-age 402 benefit, but the sibling conjuncts already foreclose that combination.
