triage.commit_summary: The commit re-encoded `statutes/26/36B/b/3/A.yaml` (26 USC 36B(b)(3)(A), the ACA applicable-percentage table) with axiom-encode 0.2.522 on the codex backend, rescaling every income-tier threshold from percent points (133/150/200/250/300/400) to ratios (1.33/1.50/2.00/2.50/3.00/4.00), adding two new indexed parameter rules for the tier lower/upper bounds so the linear-interpolation formula reads its endpoints from parameters instead of inline literals, and adding proof-atom excerpts plus more specific `source:` labels. The companion test file was rescaled in lockstep (133 -> 1.33, 141.5 -> 1.415, 350 -> 3.5, 401 -> 4.01) and its test periods moved from 2026 to 1990 to match `effective_from: '1990-01-01'`; the PR describes the change as a units conversion ("from percent points to ratios") rather than as a correction of a misreading of the statute.

modules.description_quote: convert ACA applicable percentage table income inputs from percent points to ratios
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix module compared `household_income_as_percent_of_poverty_line` against 133/150/200/250/300/400, which matches the statute's literal tier labels ("Up to 133%", "133% up to 150%", ...) and the variable's own name, so the post-fix ratio thresholds are a unit-convention change whose correctness cannot be established from the source text alone.
modules.triage_notes: Provision was read through the pinned corpus release (us/statute/26/36B): the table header is "In the case of household income (expressed as a percent of poverty line) within the following income tier:" with rows "Up to 133% | 2.0% | 2.0%" through "300% up to 400% | 9.5% | 9.5%". Statute therefore expresses tiers as percents, and the encoded input is named `household_income_as_percent_of_poverty_line`, yet the fix compares it to 1.33/1.50/..., so the post-fix literals are arguably LESS aligned with the statutory expression than the pre-fix ones; this is the main reason I did not call it fidelity. No unit is declared anywhere in the module (the input is a free input, never declared with a unit), and `git grep` at this commit shows the variable appears only in this module and its test file; `axiom-programs` has no ACA compose spec, so no downstream consumer pins a ratio convention that would make 133 wrong. Tests were rescaled by exactly the same factor, so they cannot discriminate between the two conventions. Despite the screening label, NO boundary direction changed: both pre- and post-fix use `<= threshold -> tier`, so 133%/1.33 lands in tier 0 both before and after (the statute's own rows overlap at the endpoints). Other changes in the diff are meaning-preserving or provenance-only: 0.02 -> 0.020 and 0.04 -> 0.040 are cosmetic; the new tier lower/upper-bound parameters hold the same values already inlined in the old interpolation formula; tier 5 flat-9.5% and the out-of-table 0 result are unchanged (pre-fix `if tier == 5: initial`, post-fix interpolates 9.5% -> 9.5%; pre-fix `else: 0`, post-fix `if tier < 0: 0`); the added `excerpt:` strings and refined `source:` labels are provenance. The formulas were also collapsed to single lines, a regeneration formatting artifact that inflates the diff. Commit body is empty; PR #326 has no reviews or comments, and the encoding manifest records only a backend/version change (openai 0.2.505 -> codex 0.2.522), so no maintainer statement names a defect. Follow-up commit 6596bfa39 ("Re-encode ACA applicable percentage tiers", same day) keeps the ratio values but re-grounds the tier formula on `applicable_percentage_tier_upper_bound[...]` instead of inline literals; commit 86ec136fd later moves the file under `us/`. Recommendation for the reviewer: this is a good candidate for pruning from a fidelity-defect corpus, since the pre-fix encoding was internally consistent and matched the statute's percent expression, and the change is best read as a repo unit-convention normalization (the PR also cites an `interval-table-audit` check) rather than a correction of encoded meaning versus the source.

verdict.justification: The statute's table (read through the pinned release) labels the tiers "Up to 133% ... 300% up to 400%" with the row key "household income (expressed as a percent of poverty line)", so the pre-fix comparisons against 133/150/200/250/300/400 on a variable named `household_income_as_percent_of_poverty_line` were a literally faithful reading, not a wrong number; the post-fix 1.33/1.50/... is a rescaling of the same source values, which the PR itself calls a "convert ... from percent points to ratios" of the module's undeclared input. I evaluated both file versions with the encoder's own numeric-grounding evaluator against the resolved 26 USC 36B text and both are fully grounded (pre: 32 literals, 0 ungrounded; post: 23 literals, 0 ungrounded), and `_percent_fraction_context_supports_conversion` in validator_pipeline.py explicitly treats "0-1000 percent or 0-10 as a fraction" as two conventions for FPL thresholds, so neither scale is the source-mandated one. Replaying both formulas over a 0-5.0 FPL grid gives identical applicable percentages at every point (0 mismatches, tier boundaries and the out-of-table branch included), so encoded meaning is unchanged. What actually drove the regeneration is structural, not fidelity: the pre-fix file trips the CI-blocking `non_selector_interval_bound_literal` audit five times (row bounds 133-300 hard-coded in `applicable_percentage`'s interpolation), and the fix moves them into the new indexed `applicable_percentage_tier_lower_bound`/`_upper_bound` parameters, after which that audit is clean.
verdict.notes: Refutes the "amount_mismatch" reading and goes past "unclear" to not_a_defect, on three independent checks a reviewer can rerun. (1) Grounding parity: `uv run python` calling `evaluate_numeric_grounding_values_scoped(content, module_source_text=<36B text>, module_citation_path="us/statute/26/36B", proof_source_texts={"us/statute/26/36B": text}, require_body_bound_proof_evidence=False)` returns 0 ungrounded literals for BOTH the parent (925261a3) and the fixed (36d716ec3a) module — the toolchain's own source check accepts 133 and 1.33 equally against "133%". (2) Behavior parity: replaying the two formulas on the same real-world FPL ratio over a 0-5.0 grid (5001 points) gives 0 differences; pre-fix tier 5 returning `initial[5]` and post-fix interpolating 3.00-4.00 both yield 9.5% because initial=final=0.095 there, and the -1 sentinel reaches 0 in both. (3) Motivation: `find_interval_table_reencoding_candidates` (src/axiom_encode/harness/validator_pipeline.py:17627) reports 5 CI-blocking `non_selector_interval_bound_literal` issues on the pre file ("`applicable_percentage` formula contains source-table row bound literal `133` outside structural selector arithmetic") and none on the post file — this is the interval-table hygiene refactor the PR's `interval-table-audit ... issue_count=0` line reports, plus a unit-convention rescale riding along. Residual doubt (why 0.75, not higher): within the module, "2.0%" is encoded as 0.020 (dtype Rate) while "133%" was encoded as 133, so one could argue the pre file read two cells of the same table on two scales, and any caller supplying a ratio would have been misclassified into tier 0. But `household_income_as_percent_of_poverty_line` is an undeclared input that appears nowhere else in rulespec-us at this commit (checked with scoped `git grep` across statutes/26, statutes/42, statutes/7, statutes/5, statutes/37, regulations, policies), no repo doc states a units convention, and the pre-fix tests pinned the percent-point contract (133/141.5/175/350/401) — so the mismatch is with an unstated caller convention, not with the statute. Also note the later commit 6596bfa39 ("Re-encode ACA applicable percentage tiers") keeps the ratio values and only rewrites source strings and the selector to use `applicable_percentage_tier_upper_bound[...]`, i.e. more of the same structural churn. Not mechanical: formulas changed and two parameter rules were added, so the mechanical bucket does not apply.

item.subject: (screen-flagged) PR body includes 'Repair New York SNAP benefit composition'; changes snap_eligible formula in the existing otda composition, removes/replaces 18 NYCRR 387.14(a)(1) proration rules, and re-encodes 387.14(a)(5) categorical rules with changed imports.
item.screen_reason: PR body includes 'Repair New York SNAP benefit composition'; changes snap_eligible formula in the existing otda composition, removes/replaces 18 NYCRR 387.14(a)(1) proration rules, and re-encodes 387.14(a)(5) categorical rules with changed imports.

triage.commit_summary: This commit merges rulespec-us-ny PR #5 ("Compose NY SNAP income and allotment inputs"), which wires the New York SNAP FY 2026 benefit composition to the gross-income, excess-shelter and initial-month-allotment inputs it was missing, and re-runs the supervised encoder over 18 NYCRR 387.14(a)(1) and 387.14(a)(5). The two re-encodes re-ground the initial-month provision on what it actually says (dropping a whole-allotment rule, floor() rounding and an "in job stream" qualifier the provision never authorizes) and add the categorical-eligibility inclusions and exclusions the prior 387.14(a)(5) encoding omitted, while the final "Repair New York SNAP benefit composition" commit replaces fail-open household aggregations ("at least one member eligible") with "no member ineligible" tests.

modules.description_quote: Repair New York SNAP benefit composition
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The household-level SSN and student screens were satisfied whenever at least one member passed (count_where(member_of_household, snap_member_ssn_requirement_eligible) > 0), a fail-open aggregation that let a household with SSN-ineligible or student-ineligible members clear the gate, whereas the member predicates (7 CFR 273.6, 273.5) make the household test 'no member is ineligible'.
modules.triage_notes: This file is module.kind: composition (assembled rather than encoder-generated), so a reviewer may prefer not_a_rule_module; it is format: rulespec/v1 and its rules carry real formulas, so I kept it as a rule module. Three formulas changed meaning: snap_ssn_eligible and snap_student_eligible flip from count_where(..._eligible) > 0 to count_where(..._ineligible) == 0, and snap_work_requirement_eligible drops its 'count_where(..._eligible) > 0 and' conjunct (which fail-closed a household where no member was affirmatively work-eligible, e.g. all exempt). I confirmed on main that us/regulations/7-cfr/273/6.yaml defines snap_member_ssn_requirement_eligible as 'not snap_member_ssn_requirement_ineligible', so the pre-fix formula resolved fine and was simply wrong logic, not a dangling reference. The snap_eligible change (snap_income_eligible -> (snap_income_limit_exemption_for_categorically_eligible_household or snap_standard_income_eligible)) is semantically neutral: it just follows the rename/narrowing in index 2, where the old snap_income_eligible was exactly that disjunction. The commit also ADDS five rules (member_of_household data_relation, snap_gross_monthly_income, snap_monthly_household_income, ny_snap_excess_shelter_cost, snap_excess_shelter_deduction, snap_initial_month_allotment_after_minimum_issuance) plus proof-atom metadata on every rule; that added wiring is new coverage, not a defect fix. Note the fix is incomplete: snap_residency_citizenship_eligible still uses count_where(..., snap_member_citizenship_or_alien_status_eligible) > 0, the same fail-open pattern. The proof atoms for all these composition rules cite us/guidance/usda/fns/snap-fy2026-cola/page-1 (the FY2026 COLA memo), which says nothing about SSN/student/work screens, so the 'cited source' anchor for this module is weak; the defect is nonetheless a real inversion relative to the federal member-level rules it composes. The pre-existing companion test ssn_ineligible_household_gets_zero_allotment uses a one-member household and passes under both formulas, so the defect was invisible to the module's tests.

modules.description_quote: Apply encoder refresh for 18 NYCRR 387.14(a)(1)
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: 18 NYCRR 387.14(a)(1) only sets the initial-month benefit level and defines "initial month", yet the pre-fix module derived the household's entire SNAP allotment from it (if snap_eligible: ... else: snap_regular_month_allotment, else 0), applied a floor() rounding step, and narrowed the farmworker rule to households "in job stream" — none of which appears in the cited provision.
modules.triage_notes: I read the provision through the pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-ny-snap-2026-07-17, corpus commit df57dc57, source_as_of 2021-09-15); the resolver warned 'no_toolchain_corpus_pin' and fell back to that release. The text covers only proration from the application day (or the SSA pre-release applicant's release day) to the end of the initial month, plus the (i)/(ii) definition of 'initial month' including the more-than-30-days rule for migrant or seasonal farmworker households — it says nothing about general allotments, eligibility gating, or rounding. git grep at the fix commit finds no other definition of snap_allotment, so the rule was removed outright rather than relocated. Secondary candidate kinds a reviewer may prefer: (a) wrong_period_or_effective_date — effective_from moved '2025-10-01' -> '0001-01-01', i.e. the pre-fix encoding wrongly pinned a long-standing regulation to the FY2026 COLA start date; I did not make this primary because index 2 kept '2025-10-01' in the same commit, so the change is inconsistent and reads as a re-encode side effect. (b) unrepresented_clause — the post-fix initial_month_of_certification spells out the (i) 'following any period during which the household was not certified' arm that the pre-fix opaque input initial_application_month left implicit. The re-encode also trades the explicit day-count proration math for opaque proration_factor_* inputs, and drops the imports of us:policies/usda/snap/fy-2026-cola/maximum-allotments, us:regulations/7-cfr/273/10 and us:statutes/7/2017/a. The commit message is generic ('encoder refresh'), hence confidence below 0.8. Companion test file was rewritten to match (four cases covering application-day, pre-release, farmworker >30 days, and not-initial-month).

modules.description_quote: Apply encoder refresh for 18 NYCRR 387.14(a)(5)
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix encoding reduced clause (a) to a single opaque "all members receive family assistance/safety net/SSI" input, so it omitted the source's expressly included recipients (authorized but not yet paid, suspended or being recouped, and determined eligible but unpaid because the grant is less than $10), and it omitted clause (iii)'s bar on counting individuals ineligible to participate in SNAP as part of an otherwise categorically eligible household.
modules.triage_notes: I read the provision through the pinned corpus (same release as index 1). Confirmed missing-clause additions: (a)(1)-(3) now encoded member-level via member_has_family_assistance_nonemergency_safety_net_or_ssi_categorical_status plus a new $10 parameter (excerpt 'grant is less than $10'); clause (iii) now encoded as 'and not household_member_ineligible_to_participate_in_snap'. Two further grounding fixes in the same module that a reviewer may weigh instead: (1) the 130 percent arm previously used the federal parameter snap_gross_income_limit_130_percent_fpl_48_states_dc, whereas the reg states 130 percent of the Federal poverty limit — the fix adds ny_snap_categorical_eligibility_130_percent_fpl_ratio = 1.30 times the 100 percent FPL standard, and adds the 'households not meeting one or more of clauses (a) through (d)' residual restriction (that restriction is logically inert inside the OR, so it changes structure more than result); (2) snap_income_eligible, previously defined here as 'ny_snap_categorically_eligible or snap_standard_income_eligible' under the authority of (a)(5)(i), is renamed/narrowed to snap_income_limit_exemption_for_categorically_eligible_household = ny_snap_categorically_eligible, with the disjunction moved to the composition (index 0) — arguably a wrong_entity_or_scope fix, since (a)(5)(i) states only the exemption. The income concept behind clauses (b)-(e) also moves from snap_gross_monthly_income to snap_total_gross_income imported from us:regulations/7-cfr/273/10. Imports were narrowed to hash-pinned symbol targets and proof atoms added throughout; those parts are mechanical. The added module summary (verbatim in the diff) describes the coverage: 'Clause (a) covers households in which all members are recipients of family assistance, nonemergency safety net assistance and/or SSI benefits, including authorized-but-unpaid, suspended or recouped, and under-$10 grant cases.' Commit message is generic, so confidence is held below 0.8.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as composition wiring or a forced rename and could not: both `snap_member_ssn_requirement_eligible` and `snap_member_ssn_requirement_ineligible` exist as sibling rules in the imported `us/regulations/7-cfr/273/6.yaml` (with `snap_member_ssn_requirement_eligible: formula: not snap_member_ssn_requirement_ineligible`), and the same eligible/ineligible pair exists in `273/5.yaml` for students, so the edit was a free choice of aggregation semantics, not a repair of a dangling reference. The pre-fix household screens passed whenever any one member cleared the member predicate (`count_where(..., *_eligible) > 0`), i.e. fail-open, while 7 CFR 273.6(a) read through the pinned corpus requires "the social security number (SSN) of each household member or apply for one before certification" — so the flip to `count_where(..., *_ineligible) == 0` changes encoded meaning in exactly the fail-open→fail-closed direction the first reader described. The companion change to `snap_work_requirement_eligible` drops a redundant-but-fail-closed `count_where(..., *_eligible) > 0` conjunct, which is the same boolean-combination family. This is a formula change, not proof-hash or metadata bookkeeping (those are present in the same diff but are not what the reader cited), so mechanical and not_a_defect both fail.
verdict.quote:
-        formula: count_where(member_of_household, snap_member_ssn_requirement_eligible) > 0
+        formula: count_where(member_of_household, snap_member_ssn_requirement_ineligible) == 0
verdict.notes: Evidence checked: diff 000.diff; pre/post of policies/otda/snap/fy-2026-benefit-calculation.yaml at 29d5044 and a495db3292; imported member predicates in us/regulations/7-cfr/273/6.yaml (lines 25-44), 273/5.yaml (lines 267-284), 273/24.yaml (lines 330-346); 7 CFR 273.6 text via resolve_provision (corpus release us-sc-snap-2026-07-15, provision sha 0520761c903c...). Caveats a reviewer should weigh: (1) the commit is a 4-bullet squash — most of the diff is composition glue (new member_of_household data_relation, snap_gross_monthly_income, snap_monthly_household_income, ny_snap_excess_shelter_cost, snap_excess_shelter_deduction, snap_initial_month_allotment_after_minimum_issuance) plus proof-atom metadata, which is mechanical/additive; only the four Judgment formulas carry the defect. (2) The snap_eligible change (`snap_income_eligible` → `(snap_income_limit_exemption_for_categorically_eligible_household or snap_standard_income_eligible)`) is a mixed case: `snap_income_eligible` does not exist as a rule anywhere under us/regulations/7-cfr, us/statutes/7 or us/policies at HEAD, so part of it is a dangling-reference repair, and the added disjunct is closer to unrepresented_clause (categorical eligibility exemption from income limits) than to polarity. If the corpus wants one kind per case, polarity_or_logic still dominates (2 of 4 rules are pure fail-open flips, a 3rd is a conjunct removal). (3) The post-fix household screen is itself stricter than 273.6(c) — "The disqualification applies to the individual for whom the SSN is not provided and not to the entire household" — so the fix is directionally correct against 273.6(a) but the composition still lacks per-member exclusion; that is a separate, unfixed gap, not a reason to reject this case. (4) No companion test exercises the multi-member fail-open path: the `ssn_ineligible_household_gets_zero_allotment` case uses household_size 1, where both the pre and post formulas yield not_holds.

verdict.justification: I tried to refute the classification and could not. The pinned provision text of 18 NYCRR 387.14(a)(1) states only that the initial-month benefit level is based on the application day (or the release day for SSA Pre-release joint SSI applicants), that benefits are prorated from that day to the end of the initial month, and what "initial month means" — it says nothing about household eligibility, regular (non-initial) month allotments, rounding, $10 minimum issuance, or a "job stream". Yet the pre-fix module, with every rule carrying source: 18 NYCRR 387.14(a)(1), defined the household's entire snap_allotment gated on snap_eligible with a snap_regular_month_allotment fallback, applied floor(), routed through snap_initial_month_allotment_after_minimum_issuance, and narrowed the farmworker clause to migrant_or_seasonal_farmworker_household_in_job_stream, importing us:statutes/7/2017/a, us:regulations/7-cfr/273/10 and the FY2026 maximum-allotments policy to do so. The fix deletes all three imports and every one of those branches, leaving exactly the two propositions the provision states, and relocates the allotment composition to policies/otda/snap/fy-2026-benefit-calculation.yaml ("Repair New York SNAP benefit composition") — a textbook re-grounding of formulas built on the wrong provision. Mechanical is excluded (formulas, rule names, effective dates, inputs and outputs all changed, and the companion test moved from asserting snap_allotment: 298 to initial_month_benefit_level: 0), and not_a_defect is excluded because the removed branches were affirmatively sourced to a provision that does not contain them.
verdict.quote:
-          if snap_eligible:
-              if snap_initial_month_proration_applies:
-                  snap_initial_month_allotment_after_minimum_issuance
-              else: snap_regular_month_allotment
-          else: 0
verdict.notes:
Competing kind considered: wrong_entity_or_scope, since the decisive change narrows the module's output surface from the whole household allotment to the initial-month benefit level. I kept untraceable_branch because the kind definition explicitly covers "formulas grounded on the wrong provision," and because two further removals (the floor() rounding step and the "_in_job_stream" narrowing of the farmworker clause) are pure untraceable-element removals rather than scope changes. A reviewer who prefers scope framing would not be unreasonable.

Two caveats that do not change the kind but qualify the fix's quality:
1. The same diff moves effective_from from '2025-10-01' to '0001-01-01' on both surviving rules. That is a separate, defensible wrong_period_or_effective_date correction (the regulation's corpus source_as_of is 2021-09-15, so the FY2026-COLA-style date was wrong), but it is bundled and unmentioned in the commit message.
2. The post-fix initial_month_of_certification joins clause (i) and clause (ii) with "or": household_certified... and (not_certified_during_prior_period or (is_migrant_or_seasonal_farmworker and applies_following_more_than_30_days)). The source treats (ii) as the stricter special rule for migrant/seasonal farmworker households, so under the new encoding such a household with a 10-day break still satisfies (i) and counts as an initial month. The pre-fix module handled that case correctly via snap_initial_month_proration_exception (break_in_participation_days <= 30), and the fix deletes the test that covered it ("migrant_seasonal_short_break_receives_regular_month_allotment"). The fix therefore removes untraceable content while plausibly introducing a new polarity_or_logic gap — worth a separate candidate if the corpus tracks regressions.

Provenance corroboration: the encoding manifest shows the pre-fix file was produced by a run whose citation field was "18 NYCRR 387.14(a)(1) companion-test coverage repair" (axiom_encode 0.2.64), while the fix is a clean re-encode of citation "regulations/18-nycrr/387/14/a/1" (axiom_encode 0.2.426) — consistent with the pre-fix content having drifted beyond the provision.

Also note the post-fix composition still consumes snap_initial_month_prorated_allotment, which this module no longer defines; it must now resolve from the imported federal us:regulations/7-cfr/273/10. I could not verify that at commit a495db3292 because federal modules lived in a sibling repo before the monorepo consolidation (PR #395).

Read-only throughout: only git show/diff/ls-tree, sed, cat, and the resolver script.

verdict.justification: The pinned corpus text of 18 NYCRR 387.14(a)(5) states that clause (a)'s "[c]ategorically eligible recipients include" (1) all-member households "authorized to receive ... but who have not yet received payment", (2) "individuals whose ... benefits are suspended or being recouped", and (3) "individuals determined eligible ... but who are not paid such benefits because the grant is less than $10", and clause (iii) states that "Individuals ineligible to participate in SNAP cannot be included in any household which is otherwise categorically eligible for SNAP." The pre-fix module reduced clause (a) to one undefined leaf input (`formula: household_all_members_receive_family_assistance_nonemergency_safety_net_or_ssi`), so a household whose members were authorized-but-unpaid, suspended/recouped, or under the $10 grant floor evaluated false against a source that says such households "must be considered categorically eligible", and clause (iii) had no representation at all; the fix adds a Person-level status rule with all three limbs plus a `$10` parameter, and adds `and not household_member_ineligible_to_participate_in_snap` to `ny_snap_categorically_eligible`. This is a meaning change (formulas, a new parameter, new inputs), not proof-atom or metadata bookkeeping, so "mechanical" is refuted; and the pre-fix rules cited exactly these provisions in their own `source:` fields (`18 NYCRR 387.14(a)(5)(i)(a)` and `18 NYCRR 387.14(a)(5)`), so "new coverage the module never claimed" is refuted too. The companion test diff adds `under_ten_dollar_grant_member_has_public_assistance_categorical_status` with `member_family_assistance_or_nonemergency_safety_net_grant_amount: 9`, pinning the added clause as the intended behavioral change.
verdict.quote:
+          member_receives_family_assistance_nonemergency_safety_net_or_ssi_benefits
+          or member_authorized_to_receive_family_assistance_nonemergency_safety_net_or_ssi_benefits_but_not_yet_paid
+          or member_family_assistance_nonemergency_safety_net_or_ssi_benefits_suspended_or_being_recouped
verdict.notes: Kind is right but the commit bundles several distinct fidelity changes; a reviewer picking a single rule_path should anchor on `member_has_family_assistance_nonemergency_safety_net_or_ssi_categorical_status` / `ny_snap_categorically_eligible` rather than the listed `rules[ny_snap_categorically_eligible].versions[0].formula` alone. Other same-kind additions in the same diff: clause (e)'s residual restriction ("households not meeting one or more of the definitions set forth in clauses ( a ) through ( d ) above") was absent pre-fix and is added as `and not <each of the four other paths>`; and clause (ii)'s three disqualifications were inlined rather than added (they were already present as `ny_snap_categorical_disqualification_applies`). Two secondary changes are of a different kind and should not be mined as separate defects without more work: (1) the 130 percent limit was re-grounded from the imported federal `snap_gross_income_limit_130_percent_fpl_48_states_dc` to a locally derived `snap_net_income_limit_100_percent_fpl_48_states_dc * 1.30`, and the income input moved from `snap_gross_monthly_income` to `snap_total_gross_income` (import re-grounding, likely numerically equivalent); (2) the module dropped its `snap_income_eligible` output (`ny_snap_categorically_eligible or snap_standard_income_eligible`) in favor of `snap_income_limit_exemption_for_categorically_eligible_household` — an output-surface narrowing that reads as wrong_entity_or_scope if anyone wants to score it separately, since (a)(5)(i) only exempts categorically eligible households from the income limits and does not define program-wide income eligibility. Caveat on the fix itself (not a reason to downgrade the verdict): the post-fix encoding of clause (iii) as `and not household_member_ineligible_to_participate_in_snap` denies categorical eligibility to the whole household, whereas the source says ineligible individuals "cannot be included in" an otherwise categorically eligible household, i.e. they are excluded from the household composition. Corpus provenance: release us-rulespec-ny-snap-2026-07-17, provision record 0f790884-9215-5866-b2d0-5f014a399e59, text sha256 546a6615c0187870b7e932fce9cadedf60ca48f32af956323221c830640d9096; `selection_basis: no_toolchain_corpus_pin`, so the release was chosen by fallback rather than matched to the commit's toolchain pin. The PR attached to this bundle (#395) is the monorepo consolidation, not the authoring PR, so it carries no review text about this module; the only message-level evidence is the generic body line "Apply encoder refresh for 18 NYCRR 387.14(a)(5)" — the diff and source text carry the verdict, not the message.

modules.triage_notes: This is the real defect in the commit and the only module where an outcome changes. Read 10 CCR 2506-1 4.401 through the pinned corpus (us-rulespec-2026-07-13): '(4) ... The combined income of the others with whom the individual who is aged sixty (60) and older and a person with disabilities resides (excluding the income of the individual ... and his or her spouse) must not exceed one hundred sixty-five percent (165%) of the poverty level.' The fix adds co_resident_gross_income_limit_165_percent_fpl_48_states_dc = table[clamp(co_resident_group_size,1,8)] + max(co_resident_group_size-8,0) * additional_member and points the comparison at it; the companion test adds two new cases proving the behavior change (co_resident_group_size 3 -> limit 3665, income 3000 holds, income 3666 not_holds), whereas pre-fix a household_size of 1 forced the 2152 limit regardless of how many co-residents were being tested. I chose wrong_entity_or_scope because both point at the member set; a judge answering amount_mismatch (wrong FPL table cell) would also be defensible. The 'must not exceed' -> '<=' direction was already correct and is unchanged, so this is not boundary_direction. The fix adds a co-resident-keyed limit rule and re-points the comparison at it, and the new companion test `separate_household_allowed_uses_co_resident_group_size` makes the meaning change concrete: with `household_size: 1` but `co_resident_group_size: 3`, the limit moves from 2152 to 3665, flipping a $3,000 co-resident group from denied to allowed. That is a wrong population / household member set (plus the rule's declared entity moving Person → Household), not a wrong number, a missing clause, or an ungrounded branch — the 165% FPL table itself was and remains the correct source parameter. It is a correction rather than new coverage, because the module already asserted this comparison and the old assertion produces the wrong answer whenever the co-resident group size differs from the applicant household size.

Three kinds compete and a reviewer should know why I picked scope:
- unrepresented_clause (first reader's pick): the taxonomy's signal is "the fix adds it". Here the fix removes the rule and defers; nothing on rules[tier_2_employee_tax_collectible_by_employer_deduction] is added back. The missing tier 1 component is also not a condition/exception/carve-out but half of the output's coverage.
- amount_mismatch (what the screen text suggests: "wrong amount / missing contribution base"): the 3231(e)(2) contribution-base omission is real but lives in module 3201 (statutes/26/3201.yaml, module index 0), whose deferral reason says applying the rate to raw compensation "would ignore the cross-referenced base limitation". Three real changes land together in this one module and I had to pick one kind: (a) entity TaxUnit -> Person, chosen as decisive because the source phrase settles it; (b) the import re-anchoring from the parent 1401 module onto the 1401(a)/1401(b)(1) children, which could equally be read as untraceable_branch (formula grounded on a coarser/stale provision module); (c) the amount consequence -- the companion test expectation moved 7650 -> 7064.775, i.e. 0.5*0.153*100000 versus 0.5*0.153*(0.9235*100000), because the new chain routes through 1402(a)/(b) net earnings and the section 230 contribution-and-benefit base, which the old parent 1401 module ignored (it multiplied a raw self_employment_income input by the rates). The encoder run root is named "164-f-seca-wage-base-v8", which supports the SECA-base motivation. The 'other than the taxes imposed by section 1401(b)(2)' carve-out was already correctly represented pre-fix (additional Medicare tax was never summed), so this is not an unrepresented_clause. Non-fidelity noise in the same diff: proof spans added, import hashes updated, block-style YAML reflowed to flow style, the third rule's local sha256:local import proof atom dropped, and the module summary regressed to a typo ("In the case of an an individual") while dropping the "(1) In general" heading. No PR reviews or comments exist on PR #60 (reviews, review_comments, issue_comments all empty) and the commit body is empty, so the defect is evidenced by the diff plus the statute rather than named by a maintainer; the PR body's "Keep the deduction person-scoped" reads as a description of the result, not an admission that the prior encoding was TaxUnit-scoped, which is why confidence is below 0.8. PR body also notes a 32(c)(2) regeneration in the same effort was blocked and is not in this commit.

verdict.justification: The pinned corpus text of 26 USC 164(f)(1) reads "In the case of an individual ... an amount equal to one-half of the taxes imposed by section 1401", and section 1401 imposes its tax "on the self-employment income of every individual", so the deduction is per-individual; the pre-fix module declared both derived rules at `entity: TaxUnit` and drew their SECA components from the parent `statutes/26/1401.yaml` rules `self_employment_oasdi_tax` / `self_employment_hospital_insurance_tax`, which I confirmed are themselves `entity: TaxUnit` and are computed on an aggregate `taxable_self_employment_income_for_section_1401` with no per-person contribution base. The fix changes both rules to `entity: Person` and re-anchors the imports to `us:statutes/26/1401/a#old_age_survivors_and_disability_insurance_tax` and `us:statutes/26/1401/b/1#self_employment_income_tax`, which are `entity: Person` and run off 1402(a)/1402(b) per-individual net earnings and the section 230 contribution base — the companion test expectation moves 7650 -> 7064.775 accordingly. That is a change to the encoded entity, population and input surface, not bookkeeping, and no competing kind fits better: the 1/2 parameter, the 1401(b)(2) carve-out, the `if taxpayer_is_individual ... else: 0` logic, and the 1990-01-01 effective date are all unchanged, and the pre-fix formula was grounded on the correct provision (section 1401) merely at the wrong scope, so untraceable_branch and amount_mismatch do not apply.
verdict.quote:
-    entity: TaxUnit
+  entity: Person
verdict.notes: Two corrections to the first reader's write-up, neither of which changes the kind: (1) the parent 1401 module's rules are TaxUnit-scoped, not "household-scoped" — verified at eba8177e:statutes/26/1401.yaml, where self_employment_oasdi_tax and self_employment_hospital_insurance_tax both carry `entity: TaxUnit`; (2) the reader's quote is from the PR body's import bullet, which is weaker evidence than the diff, and the same PR body also says "Keep the deduction person-scoped", which mischaracterizes its own change since the diff plainly flips `entity: TaxUnit` -> `entity: Person` on both derived rules. A better quote is the entity line itself. The pre-fix base also lacked 1402(a)'s net-earnings reduction and 1402(b)'s cap (hence 7650 vs 7064.775 in the test), but that defect lives in statutes/26/1401.yaml; 164/f.yaml's own defect is the entity and the import scope. Remaining diff content is cosmetic or provenance: added proof spans, YAML reflow from block scalars to flow style, removal of the `sha256:local` self-import proof atom, and a new "an an individual" typo plus a dropped "(1) In general" in the module summary — the summary typo is worth a reviewer note as a regeneration-quality nit, not a fidelity issue.

modules.triage_notes: Largest diff in the commit (328 lines) but I checked it for meaning rather than shape. (a) Band logic: the pre-fix nested if-chain used `< 2.5` then `>= X and < Y` pairs; the post-fix chain drops the redundant lower-bound conjuncts and keeps the same `<` upper comparisons, so every band boundary is identical -- ratio 2.5 still lands in band 2, ratio 9.0 still lands in band 12. The pre-fix chain also ended in an unreachable `else: 1` fallback (after `>= 8.5 and < 9.0` fails, the value is necessarily >= 9.0, which the preceding branch catches); removing dead code is not a behavior change, so I did NOT score this as untraceable_branch. (b) I parsed both revisions with PyYAML and compared the two rate tables numerically: both columns are equal across all 12 bands (the only textual delta is `12: 0.0` -> `12: 0`). (c) The eleven new `*_band_threshold_*` parameter rules hold exactly the literals that were already inline in the pre-fix formula (2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 6.1, 6.5, 7.0, 7.5, 8.0, 8.5, 9.0); they add proof atoms and new module outputs but no new meaning -- per the rubric, added outputs the module never claimed are not a defect, which is why I classified mechanical rather than fidelity, though a reviewer could reasonably downgrade to 'unclear' on the grounds that the module's output surface grew. (d) The summary was rewritten from a mangled multi-line reflow to the verbatim corpus text -- I read us/statute/26/3241 through the pinned release us-rulespec-2026-07-13 (corpus commit 612d20ca) and the new summary matches the provision body exactly, including every threshold and rate; this is a provenance/summary fix. (e) Remaining edits are string-level: `corpus_span` wording, `row_key` changed from the prose 'average account benefits ratio interval band' to the rule name, and effective_from re-serialized from the quoted string '1990-01-01' to an unquoted YAML date (same date, encoder serialization change -- worth a reviewer glance if the loader treats the two differently, but it applies uniformly and the tests pass). (f) The companion test file grew assertions for the new threshold outputs and swapped two probe ratios (6.3 -> 7.2, 2.0 -> 2.4, 0 -> 9), but every retained expectation keeps its old value (0.221/0.049, 0.181/0.049, 0.082/0) and the new ones match the statutory table, confirming no value drift.

modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix formulas let negative inputs propagate — most sharply in `cooperative_reduction`, where a negative QBI allocable to qualified cooperative payments produced a negative 199A(b)(7) 'reduction' that would have increased the deductible amount instead of reducing it — but the statute states no explicit 'but not below zero' floor at any of the four sites, so the clamps may be defensive rather than a source-mismatch repair.
modules.triage_notes: Only modified module in this chunk. Two independent changes: (a) new module-level deferred_outputs for 199A(c), (d) and (h), which is pure metadata (mechanical), and (b) four formulas that wrap operands in max(0, ...): `cooperative_reduction` (199A(b)(7)), `qbi_deduction_before_minimum_active_qbi` (199A(a), now max(0, min(combined QBI amount, taxable-income limit))), `cooperative_production_deduction_before_wage_limit` (199A(g)(1)(A)) and `cooperative_production_deduction` (199A(g)(1)(B), clamping W-2 wages). I read 199A through the pinned corpus release: (b)(7) says only 'shall be reduced by the lesser of— (A) 9 percent ... or (B) 50 percent ...' and (g)(1)(A) 'an amount equal to 9 percent of the lesser of— (i) ... or (ii) ...'; neither carries a zero floor, and 199A(c)(1) defines QBI as a 'net amount' that can be negative with (c)(2) handling losses by carryover. So the clamps encode an implied non-negativity rather than quoted text, and the only stated motive in the commit body is the generic 'Repair RuleSpec validation coverage' / 'Repair validation tail for refreshed RuleSpecs' — consistent with a validator-driven clamp. A reviewer should decide whether 'a negative statutory reduction that increases the deduction' counts as a fidelity defect; if kept, `cooperative_reduction` is the strongest single instance because there the sign flip inverts the direction of the adjustment.

Corpus resolution caveat for the record: `selection_basis: no_toolchain_corpus_pin` / `fix_time_corpus_match: no_corpus_ref` — the provision text came from fallback release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, not a pin carried by the commit. verdict.justification: The four changes only wrap already-existing operands in `max(0, ...)`, and the pinned source text has no floor to represent: "but not below zero" occurs zero times in the resolved 26 USC 199A text (corpus release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, body sha256 0af6c1cc…), and the one relevant "(if any)" — 199A(a)(2)'s "20 percent of the excess (if any)" — was already encoded pre-fix as `qbi_deduction_rate * max(0, taxable_income_computed_without_section_199A - net_capital_gain)`, untouched by this diff. Three of the four clamped quantities are non-negative by construction or by their own definition (W-2 wages under 199A(b)(4)/6051(a); QPAI is "the excess (if any)" under 199A(g)(3)(A)), so those clamps are no-ops, and the one substantive case — negative QBI allocable to cooperative payments in (b)(7) — is not handled by a statutory floor at all: 199A(c)(2) routes a negative net QBI to a succeeding-year loss carryover, which `max(0, ...)` does not encode. The apply manifest records a hand repair on top of the unchanged generated encoding (`"model": "manual-repair-v1"`, `"tool": "axiom-encode deterministic/manual repair"`, generated_output_sha256 unchanged), and axiom-encode at that exact commit (c0bc4a92) ships a house convention for exactly this shape — `repair-nonnegative-floors` / "Benefit, allotment, credit, deduction, allowance, and subsidy outputs must use `max(0, ...)` before downstream minimums or eligibility branches" — i.e. defensive hardening, not a source-mismatch repair.
verdict.quote: +              cooperative_reduction_rate * max(0, qualified_business_income_allocable_to_qualified_cooperative_payments),
verdict.notes: Refutation of the first reader's "unclear / missing_nonnegativity_floor": (1) Source check via the pinned release resolver — 199A(b)(7) reads "shall be reduced by the lesser of— (A) 9 percent ... or (B) 50 percent ..." with no "but not below zero"; 199A(g)(1)(A) reads "9 percent of the lesser of— (i) the qualified production activities income ... or (ii) the taxable income"; 199A(g)(1)(B)(i) "shall not exceed 50 percent of the W-2 wages". No floor clause at any of the four sites. (2) The module already carried unrelated, pre-existing `max(0, ...)` floors (trade_or_business_deductible_amount, trade_or_business_excess_amount, qbi_taxable_income_limit), so the house style predates this commit. (3) The clamped identifiers are unbound external inputs — the module has no `inputs:` block; they appear only inside formulas — so this is input hygiene on values the module does not compute. (4) Encoder-side convention exists and is enforced: src/axiom_encode/harness/validator_pipeline.py at c0bc4a92 defines find_nonnegative_amount_reduction_issues / repair_nonnegative_amount_reductions ("Mechanically floor supported nonnegative amount reduction formulas") and cli.py exposes `repair-nonnegative-floors` (model "nonnegative-floor-v1"). Caveat for the reviewer: that lint's own patterns would NOT match these four formulas (no "-" operator and no identifier containing "max" in the pre-fix expressions; `cooperative_reduction` doesn't even match the benefit/credit/deduction name pattern), so the clamps were hand-applied in the same spirit rather than emitted by that tool. (5) Residual reason a reviewer could keep this as "unclear" rather than "not_a_defect": the (b)(7) pre-fix formula genuinely could return a negative "reduction" that inflates the deduction, and "reduced by" arguably implies a non-negative subtrahend — but that is interpretive, and the statute's actual mechanism for negative QBI is the 199A(c)(2) carryover, which the fix does not add. (6) The other part of the diff (the `deferred_outputs` block for 199A(c), (d), (h)) is module-level coverage bookkeeping: no rule in this module produces those outputs, so nothing became non-executable — unlike module 151 in the same squash. No PR reviews, no test-file change for 199A (199A.test.yaml sha256 unchanged in the manifest), and the commit/PR text never mentions floors or 199A.

verdict.notes: Kind held at unrepresented_clause after considering two alternatives. (1) untraceable_branch for the 28% rule: the pre-fix rule was cited to "26 USC 1(h)(1)(F), 1(h)(4)" and taxed the 28-percent rate gain directly, which is (h)(4)'s defined term rather than (F)'s statutory base, so "grounded on the wrong provision" is arguable — but the fix keeps the gain term and wraps it in a min() cap, i.e. it adds the missing limitation rather than removing or re-grounding a baseless branch, so unrepresented_clause fits better and covers both formula changes under one kind. (2) not_a_defect as scope expansion: rejected for the reason in the justification; note that the fix does introduce a brand-new external input (`input.net_capital_gain_taken_into_account_as_investment_income_under_section_163_d_4_B_iii`, added to every test case), so a reviewer who treats a new required input as new scope rather than as the encoding mechanism for an existing clause could land on unclear. A third change, `adjusted_net_capital_gain_limited` going from `min(adjusted_net_capital_gain, taxable_income)` to `min(adjusted_net_capital_gain, max(taxable_income, 0))`, is a defensive floor with no explicit source phrase requiring it; on its own that element would be not_a_defect/unclear and it is not load-bearing here. The remaining ~80% of the 414-line diff is mechanical: `span:` keys replaced by `excerpt:` strings, module summary replaced with corpus text, block-scalar reflow of unchanged scalars (e.g. `'0.20'` to a literal block), and source-cite string edits such as dropping ", 1(j)(5)" from the 20% rate. Commit body is empty ("\n") and the subject is the generic "Regenerate capital gains rate RuleSpec", so no commit-message evidence exists; the verdict rests entirely on the diff, the test deltas, and the resolved corpus text (provision file sha256 1b0b185ca3335eb06c4fe10af488a8984bdd2cedd4087badf78583c267af7b7b). The same commit also touches statutes/26/199A.yaml (13 lines), which imports this `net_capital_gain` rule; that module was not assessed here.

modules.description_quote: (c) Relief from taxes in cases covered by certain international agreements During any period in which there is in effect an agreement entered into pursuant to section 233 of the Social Security Act with any foreign country, the self-employment income of an individual shall be exempt from the taxes imposed by this section to the extent that such self-employment income is subject under such agreement exclusively to the laws applicable to the social security system of such foreign country.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module had no representation of §1401(c) at all, so it imposed the OASDI, hospital-insurance, and additional-Medicare taxes on the taxpayer's entire self_employment_income even where a section 233 totalization agreement makes that income subject exclusively to a foreign social security system and therefore exempt from the taxes imposed by this section.
modules.triage_notes: Two independent fidelity defects are fixed in this one module; I coded the primary kind as unrepresented_clause for the §1401(c) exemption because an entire subsection of the cited section was absent from the encoding and its omission changes all three taxes. SECOND DEFECT (wrong_entity_or_scope): the pre-fix `additional_medicare_self_employment_threshold` match had only arms 1, 2 and 0, while the pre-fix module summary itself documented the input convention as "0 single/other case, 1 joint return, 2 married filing separately, 3 head of household/other case" — so head-of-household (3) and status 4 had no arm despite clause (A)(iii) "in any other case, $200,000"; the fix adds `3 =>` and `4 => additional_medicare_self_employment_other_threshold` at rules[additional_medicare_self_employment_threshold].versions[0].formula. NOT a defect: the MFS arm changed from `additional_medicare_self_employment_joint_threshold / 2` to a new `additional_medicare_self_employment_separate_threshold` rule equal to joint * (1/2) — semantically identical, pure parameterization of clause (A)(ii)'s "½ of the dollar amount determined under clause (i)". Large parts of this diff are mechanical regeneration noise: added module.proof_validation, per-rule metadata.proof.atoms, source strings narrowed to exact clauses (e.g. 26 USC 1401(b)(2)(A) -> (b)(2)(A)(i)), quoting/block-scalar reflow of unchanged formulas, and the summary being replaced with verbatim statute text. PROVISION READ: I resolved us/statute/26/1401 through the pinned corpus release at this rulespec commit (resolve_provision.py, exit 0) and confirmed subsection (c) and clauses (b)(2)(A)(i)-(iii) are present in the source text exactly as now summarized. The new (c) machinery introduces three new inputs (international_social_security_agreement_under_section_233_in_effect, ..._is_subject_exclusively_to_foreign_social_security_laws_under_agreement as Judgment/boolean, and ..._amount_subject_exclusively_...), and the companion test file gained a case `international_agreement_partially_exempts_self_employment_income` exercising a 40,000 exemption; no test was added for filing status 3 or 4, so that half of the fix is untested. Commit message and PR give no rationale (body is the subject line repeated; the bundle's pr field is null), which caps confidence below 0.8.

modules.description_quote: (2) Application to estates and trusts In the case of an estate or trust, there is hereby imposed (in addition to any other tax imposed by this subtitle) for each taxable year a tax of 3.8 percent of the lesser of— (A) the undistributed net investment income for such taxable year, or (B) the excess (if any) of— (i) the adjusted gross income (as defined in section 67(e)) for such taxable year, over (ii) the dollar amount at which the highest tax bracket in section 1(e) begins for such taxable year.

modules.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus (resolve_provision.py, us/statute/26/1411, expression_date 2026-07-13): the corpus text carries (a)(2) and (e)(2) verbatim, confirming both were missing pre-fix. Co-occurring second defect in the same module: every rule's effective_from moved 2026-01-01 -> 2013-01-01, which is a wrong_period_or_effective_date correction (section 1411 has applied since taxable years beginning after 2012 and its $250,000/$200,000 thresholds are not indexed, so a 2026 start date was indefensible) — but the 2013 date is not stated anywhere in the provision text, so I made the in-source clause omission the primary kind. Also added in this diff: 1411(c)(3) working-capital income and the 1411(c)(4) active partnership/S-corporation disposition exception in net_investment_income_gross_items, and the 1411(d) MAGI input renamed to `amount_excluded_from_gross_income_under_section_911_a_1` with 911(d)(6) now supplied by the new module at index 9. Second point: the 'SS-excess gated on 3+ children' item is behaviour-neutral — the pre-fix gated the 3-or-more-children test inside `ctc_phase_in`, the post-fix gates it inside `ctc_social_security_excess` and takes max() in `ctc_refundable_limitation_increase_amount`; the results agree. BUT this module also carries a likely REGRESSION that a reviewer must weigh: every version's effective_from moved 2026-01-01 -> 2018-01-01 while the imported IRS authority `us:policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/child-tax-credit` was dropped and the dollar amounts hard-coded as literals (ctc_child_amount 2200, ctc_refundable_per_child_cap 1400). The corpus text of 24(i) says the $1,400 in (h)(5) is indexed for taxable years beginning after 2024 and the $2,200 in (h)(2) is indexed for taxable years beginning after 2025, and the $2,200 figure itself only applies from 2025 (it was $2,000 for 2018-2024) — so dating those two parameters to 2018 encodes superseded/unindexed amounts even though the 2018 date is correct for the structural (h)(3), (h)(4) and (h)(7) provisions. That mix is why I did not make wrong_period_or_effective_date the primary kind. Also re-grounded out of this module: the 24(c)(1) age-17 qualifying-child definition, the 24(b)(1) $50-per-$1,000 phase-out rules, and the `ctc` total — all now expected from elsewhere, leaving the (h) module without a total-credit output.

Two secondary formula corrections worth noting: `eitc_maximum` moved from the Rev. Proc. published maximum-credit table to 32(a)(2)(A)'s 'credit percentage of the earned income amount' (phase_in_rate * earned_income_amount), and `eitc_phased_in` moved from `min(eitc_maximum, earned_income * rate)` to 32(a)(1)'s `rate * min(earned_income, earned_income_amount)` — numerically these differ only by the Rev. Proc. rounding of the published maximum. `eitc_before_eligibility` changed from `min(P, max(0, M-R))` to `max(0, min(P, M-R))`, which is algebraically identical for non-negative P. modules.description_quote: Re-encode 26 USC 63(c) with upstream dependencies
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module computed standard_deduction as basic_standard_deduction_amount + additional_std_ded_amount with no 63(c)(5) cap, so a taxpayer for whom a section 151 deduction is allowable to another taxpayer received the full basic standard deduction instead of the statutory limit of the greater of $500 or $250 plus earned income (inflation-adjusted), e.g. $16,100 rather than $5,450 for a 2026 dependent with $5,000 of earned income.
modules.triage_notes:
Read the module diff, the full pre-fix and post-fix module bodies, the companion test diff, and the 26 USC 63 provision text via resolve_provision.py (us/statute/26/63 at this rulespec commit); 63(c)(5) and 63(f) both resolve and are quoted below.

Primary defect (the one I classified): 63(c)(5) was present in the module's own cited summary but wholly unencoded pre-fix. The fix adds rule `basic_standard_deduction_limited_for_dependents` with an explicit proof atom `kind: exception` carrying the verbatim 63(c)(5) text, imports `us:statutes/26/63/c/5#dependent_standard_deduction` (that module already existed at the parent commit, adae20d1a, so this is purely a failure to wire the clause in), and rewrites `standard_deduction` to `if standard_deduction_ineligible: 0 else: basic_standard_deduction_limited_for_dependents + additional_std_ded_amount`. The new test `dependent_basic_standard_deduction_limited` pins the behavior at 5450 for earned_income 5000.

Second, co-occurring defect in the same commit (would be wrong_entity_or_scope / untraceable_branch if scored separately): `num_additional_standard_deduction_conditions` was `count_where(member_of_tax_unit, is_aged_65_or_over) + count_where(member_of_tax_unit, is_blind)`, counting every tax-unit member including dependents, while 63(c)(3) points to 63(f), which entitles additional amounts only "for himself" and "for the spouse of the taxpayer" (verified in the resolved provision text). The fix replaces the local count with the 63(f)-sourced input and deletes the `member_of_tax_unit` data_relation rule. I picked unrepresented_clause because the screen description and the larger, value-changing hunk are the 63(c)(5) addition, but a reviewer building the corpus could legitimately split this module into two seeded defects.

Also changed but non-substantive: several proof-atom `kind: formula` -> `kind: definition` relabels and excerpt-string expansions (provenance only, mechanical), and `source:` metadata strings updated to cite (5).

Evidence caveats for the reviewer: the commit body is empty and the subject is generic, so the only quotable text naming the defect is inside the diff itself as the added proof-atom excerpt ("In the case of an individual with respect to whom a deduction under section 151 is allowable to another taxpayer ... the basic standard deduction applicable to such individual ... shall not exceed the greater of— (A) $500, or (B) the sum of $250 and such individual's earned income."), which is source text rather than an authored comment, so I quoted the commit subject instead and held confidence at 0.79. The bundle's PR (rulespec-us#25, merged 2026-05-12) is the PR that contains BOTH the defective parent commit adae20d1a and this fix; its body describes the original encode, not this correction, and contains no reviews or review comments. That means the pre-fix state was only ever on the PR branch, never on merged main — the defect is real but was self-caught within the same PR. History is linear (adae20d1a -> 2175d5239a). Follow-up commits touching the same file: 86e2549dc (2026-05-12, "Encode upstream IRC 63 dependencies"), 095d680d4 (2026-05-23), 86ec136fd (2026-06-10, path move to us/).

verdict.justification: The refutation attempt fails on every angle I tried. The pre-fix `standard_deduction` formula was `if standard_deduction_ineligible: 0 else: basic_standard_deduction_amount + additional_std_ded_amount`, with no reference anywhere in the module to 63(c)(5); the fix inserts a new `basic_standard_deduction_limited_for_dependents` rule whose proof carries an `kind: exception` atom quoting the (5) cap and routes the sum through it. This is not "coverage the module never claimed": the module's `corpus_citation_path: us/statute/26/63` resolves (release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, body sha256 7fa5f5d7…) to text whose paragraph (1) reads "Except as otherwise provided in this subsection" and whose paragraph (5) states the dependent cap, so encoding (1) without (5) contradicts the cited provision on its own terms — and the cap module `us:statutes/26/63/c/5#dependent_standard_deduction` already existed at the parent commit, so the encoder simply failed to wire an available, required clause. The added test `dependent_basic_standard_deduction_limited` (earned_income 5000 → standard_deduction 5450, vs 16100 in the non-dependent case) pins the numeric consequence, confirming the first reader's kind and illustration.

-          if standard_deduction_ineligible: 0 else: basic_standard_deduction_amount + additional_std_ded_amount
+          if standard_deduction_ineligible:
+              0
+          else:
+              basic_standard_deduction_limited_for_dependents + additional_std_ded_amount
verdict.notes: Verification performed: bundle JSON, full diff, pre-fix and post-fix c.yaml, the parent-commit copy of statutes/26/63/c/5.yaml, the c.test.yaml diff, and the provision text through resolve_provision (corpus_release us-rulespec-2026-07-13, corpus_commit 612d20ca, resolved_text_sha256 7fa5f5d7…). Three caveats for the reviewer, none of which overturn the verdict: (1) The commit carries a SECOND, independent fidelity change on the same module — `num_additional_standard_deduction_conditions` goes from `count_where(member_of_tax_unit, is_aged_65_or_over) + count_where(member_of_tax_unit, is_blind)` to the input `additional_standard_deduction_entitlement_count_under_subsection_f`, and the `member_of_tax_unit` data_relation is deleted. The pinned 63(f) text entitles additional amounts only to "himself" and to a spouse for whom a 151(b) exemption is allowable, so the old count over all tax-unit members would over-count aged/blind dependents; that sub-defect is better described as wrong_entity_or_scope (or untraceable_branch — a formula grounded on a member-set the cited provision does not use). Note the PR body offers a competing, non-fidelity motive for that specific deletion: "Depends on TheAxiomFoundation/axiom-rules-engine#35 for correct namespacing when this module is compiled with other tax modules that also declare member_of_tax_unit." If the corpus wants one kind per case, the anchored rule_path (rules[standard_deduction].versions[0].formula) is squarely the 63(c)(5) clause, so unrepresented_clause stands; if the corpus can carry a secondary kind, flag the 63(f) count separately. (2) Provenance: `gh api .../pulls/25/commits` shows the parent adae20d1a4 ("Encode 26 USC 63(c) standard deduction") and this commit 2175d5239a are BOTH in PR #25, merged 2026-05-12 — so the defect was introduced and corrected pre-merge within the same PR, never on main. That is a real fidelity correction against the source, but if this corpus is meant to hold defects that survived into shipped/merged content, this case is an intra-PR self-correction and the reviewer may want it tagged as such. (3) Minor: the new `basic_standard_deduction_limited_for_dependents` is `entity: TaxUnit` while the imported `dependent_standard_deduction` in c/5.yaml is `entity: Person` — an entity-lift the diff does not explain; irrelevant to this classification but worth noting if anyone mines this module again. modules.triage_notes: Diff of the rules: section between parent 71bb5ecc06 and 97ba4dc683 shows exactly one addition and zero modifications: the new kind: source_relation record. Every executable rule is byte-identical -- ny_snap_public_assistance_categorically_eligible keeps formula household_all_members_receive_family_assistance_nonemergency_safety_net_or_ssi, and all parameters, versions, effective dates (2025-10-01), entities, periods, and outputs are unchanged. Minor latent inconsistency, not a defect introduced or fixed here: engine docs say a `restates` record means computation belongs to the target, yet the module keeps its own executable local derived rule for the same clause. The added source_relation record survives to HEAD (us-ny/regulations/18-nycrr/387/14/a/5.yaml:148). Residual doubt (why 0.76, not higher): the change adds a whole rule record rather than only an excerpt or citation string, so a stricter reader could call it 'adds provenance coverage the repo wanted' -- but under the rubric that is provenance, and no formula, parameter, version, effective date, input, output, or scope moved, so mechanical rather than unclear.

modules.triage_notes: Single module in the commit (chunk covers all of it); no test files changed, other_files is only the encoding apply manifest. Verified the regression: `git show ca94764e80` removed the identical `sets_snap_telephone_utility_allowance` block (present since the original encoding), and this commit restores it byte-for-byte; the relation still exists at rulespec-us HEAD (us-ny/regulations/18-nycrr/387/12/f/3/v/c.yaml). Read the cited provision through the pinned corpus release: the text is the bare NY telephone-allowance paragraph and does not itself cite 7 CFR 273.9, so the federal delegation basis is inferred from the scheme, not quoted from the provision. Checked that `sets` is executable rather than pure metadata: axiom-rules-engine HEAD docs/rulespec.md says same-kind `sets` records with `source_relation.value` 'lower into delegated parameter bindings or derived formula hooks', and src/rulespec.rs `apply_source_relation_sets` rewrites the target binding with the value; the federal target `snap_individual_utility_allowance_state_option` in us/regulations/7-cfr/273/9.yaml is a derived rule whose formula is '0', and it feeds `snap_utility_allowance_for_shelter_costs`. (I read the engine at HEAD, not at the May 2026 pinned toolchain, so the lowering mechanism is verified for today's engine.) Kind is a judgment call: the commit subject frames it as 'provenance', which would argue for mechanical, but the relation is executable so the omission changed composed meaning; alternative labels a reviewer might prefer are wrong_entity_or_scope (the module's output reached no program surface) or other ('missing cross-jurisdiction delegation binding'). The only other diff hunk is whitespace re-indentation of the nested-if formula, which is semantically identical. The PR (#395) is the unrelated US monorepo consolidation that absorbed the standalone us-ny history, so its body and (empty) reviews say nothing about this defect.

verdict.justification: The only substantive addition is a `kind: source_relation` record — what the engine's own format doc calls a "legal/provenance edge" — plus a whitespace-only reformat of an otherwise byte-equivalent formula; the parameter (32), the eligibility rule with both exclusions, the entity, the period, `effective_from: '2025-10-01'`, the module summary, and the unchanged companion test's expected outputs are all identical before and after. The first reader's mechanism claim (the federal slot "stayed at its default of 0") is false as of this 2026-05-09 commit: `snap_individual_utility_allowance_state_option` and `snap_state_standard_utility_allowance_delegation` did not exist anywhere until 6ada8df79 on 2026-06-14 ("Add SNAP utility allowance hook concepts"), and `known-dangling.yaml` at the time recorded that "7 CFR 273.9(d)(6)(iii) was never encoded" — so the restored `sets` edge pointed at nothing and could not lower into any binding (that same June commit also had to change `entity: SnapUnit` to `entity: Household` before the hook would bind). Reading the provision through the pinned release confirms it states only the telephone-allowance definition, the two exclusions, the October 1 2025 date, the statewide scope, and $32 — all already encoded pre-fix — and says nothing about the federal individual-allowance option, so no clause of the cited source was unrepresented.

verdict.notes: Refutes both the kind and the classification. Evidence trail: (1) axiom-rules-engine/docs/rulespec.md: "source_relation: legal/provenance edges... Most source relations are non-executable metadata; same-kind `sets` records with `source_relation.value` lower into delegated parameter bindings or derived formula hooks" — executability requires the upstream slot to exist. (2) `git log --follow us/regulations/7-cfr/273/9.yaml` shows the three `*_state_option` hooks and `snap_state_standard_utility_allowance_delegation` were first added 2026-06-14 in 6ada8df79, five weeks after this commit; that same commit deleted seven `known-dangling.yaml` entries commented "7 CFR 273.9(d)(6)(iii) was never encoded". Caveat for the reviewer: the edge did later become load-bearing, so if the corpus wants "content regression restored by a later-executable provenance edge" treated as fidelity, this case would be the exemplar — but on the stated rule (fidelity = encoded meaning disagrees with the cited source text) nothing the provision states was missing, and unrepresented_clause in particular is not supportable.

item.screen_reason: Regeneration corrects NY telephone allowance eligibility to require the household incurred basic service cost for one telephone (previously granted whenever heating/cooling and utilities allowances did not apply) and replaces the paraphrased summary with regulation text.

triage.commit_summary: The commit re-ran the supervised encoder over 18 NYCRR 387.12(f)(3)(v)(c) (NY SNAP standard allowance for telephone), rewriting the single module plus its companion test, the FY2026 benefit-calculation policy test, and adding a new encoding manifest. The regeneration corrected the encoded meaning by requiring that the household actually incurred or anticipated the basic service cost for one telephone before the $32 allowance applies — previously the allowance was granted to any household that merely did not qualify for the heating/cooling or utilities allowances — and replaced the paraphrased module summary with the verbatim regulation text.

modules.description_quote: (c) The standard allowance for telephone consists of the cost for basic service for one telephone.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module granted the $32 telephone standard allowance to every household that merely failed to qualify for the heating/cooling or utilities allowances, omitting the source's requirement that the allowance consists of the cost for basic service for one telephone — i.e. that the household actually incurred or anticipated such a cost.
modules.triage_notes: Provision WAS read through the pinned corpus release (resolve_provision.py, us-ny/regulation/18-nycrr/387/12/f/3/v/c): text confirms 'The standard allowance for telephone consists of the cost for basic service for one telephone', so the added conjunct is source-grounded, not new unclaimed scope. Decisive diff: eligibility formula changed from 'not snap_heating_cooling_standard_allowance_eligible and not snap_utilities_standard_allowance_eligible' to the same two negations ANDed with the new input household_incurred_or_anticipated_basic_service_cost_for_one_telephone; snap_individual_utility_allowance was rewritten to a nested if-chain that also gates on that input, so a household without telephone cost now yields 0 instead of 32. Companion test regulations/18-nycrr/387/12/f/3/v/c.test.yaml adds case 'no_telephone_basic_service_cost_prevents_telephone_allowance' expecting snap_individual_utility_allowance: 0, and policies/otda/snap/fy-2026-benefit-calculation.test.yaml pins the new input to false in its shared base case — behavioral change confirmed, not cosmetic. The commit ALSO made non-fidelity changes in the same module: (a) the module summary was replaced with verbatim regulation text (provenance/mechanical); (b) the parameter was renamed ny_snap_telephone_utility_allowance_amount -> telephone_standard_allowance_amount with the same 32 value, effective_from 2025-10-01 and dtype/unit unchanged (rename only); (c) the rule snap_telephone_allowance_eligible was renamed to snap_telephone_standard_allowance_eligible; (d) the source_relation rule 'sets_snap_telephone_utility_allowance' (a 'sets' relation onto us:regulations/7-cfr/273/9#snap_individual_utility_allowance_state_option with a delegation basis) was DROPPED entirely and not replaced — that removes a cross-reference/delegation assertion rather than a computed value, so I did not treat it as the defect, but a reviewer may want to check whether losing that relation was intended. Evidence quality caveat: the commit body is empty and the subject is generic ('Regenerate NY SNAP telephone allowance'); the attached PR (#395) is the unrelated US monorepo-consolidation PR that absorbed this history via git subtree, so its body/reviews say nothing about this change. The only text that names the defect is the post-fix module summary quoting the regulation, hence confidence held below 0.8. The encoding manifest (.axiom/encoding-manifests/.../c.json) records a supervised encoder run (openai-gpt-5.5 backend, run dir axiom-encode-ny-telephone-11) but carries no prose rationale.

verdict.justification: The pre-fix formula for `snap_telephone_allowance_eligible` was `not snap_heating_cooling_standard_allowance_eligible and not snap_utilities_standard_allowance_eligible`, so any household failing the other two standards received the $32 telephone allowance; the fix adds a required conjunct `household_incurred_or_anticipated_basic_service_cost_for_one_telephone` and threads the same gate through `snap_individual_utility_allowance`, which is an encoded-meaning change, not bookkeeping. The pinned corpus release (us-rulespec-ny-snap-2026-07-17, record a14d03c7) confirms the source's first sentence — "The standard allowance for telephone consists of the cost for basic service for one telephone." — which the pre-fix encoding represented nowhere, and the companion test adds `no_telephone_basic_service_cost_prevents_telephone_allowance` asserting not_holds / 0 where the old module returned 32. I tried to refute this as amount/date/entity (all unchanged: $32, effective_from 2025-10-01, Household/SnapUnit), as polarity (no operator inverted — a conjunct was added), and as mechanical (renames and the summary-to-regulation-text swap are present but ride alongside a real formula change), and none of those hold; the only surviving counter-reading is that the first sentence is definitional rather than an eligibility gate, which the sibling provisions (a)/(b) incurrence tests make unlikely.
verdict.quote:
+          household_incurred_or_anticipated_basic_service_cost_for_one_telephone
+          and not snap_heating_cooling_standard_allowance_eligible
verdict.notes: Commit message is bare ("Regenerate NY SNAP telephone allowance", empty body) — the "(screen-flagged)" sentence in the task brief is screening output, not maintainer text, so the evidence here is the diff, the companion test, and the resolved source text, not a quoted admission. Two other changes ride in the same regeneration and a reviewer should look at them separately: (1) the commit deletes the `source_relation` rule `sets_snap_telephone_utility_allowance`, which had target `us:regulations/7-cfr/273/9#snap_individual_utility_allowance_state_option` with a delegation basis — that is a coverage/linkage removal, not part of the reviewed defect, and it is the one plausible candidate for a competing kind (untraceable_branch or wrong_entity_or_scope) if a reviewer thinks the relation, not the eligibility gate, is the decisive edit; (2) renames (`ny_snap_telephone_utility_allowance_amount` → `telephone_standard_allowance_amount`, `snap_telephone_allowance_eligible` → `snap_telephone_standard_allowance_eligible`) and the summary replacement are mechanical noise that should not be read as additional defects. Residual risk on the kind: the added gate is grounded in a definitional sentence ("consists of the cost for basic service for one telephone") rather than an explicit "is available only to households which incur…" clause, so a strict reader could call the new input an interpretive addition; I weigh that as minority because (a) and (b) in the same subdivision both gate on incurred cost and the added input name mirrors (a)'s `household_incurred_or_anticipated_heating_or_cooling_costs_separate_from_rent_or_mortgage`. Source text verified verbatim via resolve_provision (corpus commit df57dc57cf, provision line 1158, body sha c7a2e121…).
