verdict.notes:
Evidence trail (all read this session, read-only):
- Diff `000.diff` is a pure deletion: `deleted file mode 100644` / `@@ -1,36 +0,0 @@`. Nothing replaces `child_benefit_weekly_amount`; the output disappears.
- Signed retirement manifest `.axiom/encoding-manifests/policies/govuk/child-benefit.json` at 829ab1a255 states, verbatim: `"reason": "PolicyEngine model wrappers retired from the rules registry: survey/take-up constructs are consumer concerns; legal content lives in the statute and regulation modules"`. This is a scope/layering rationale ("consumer concerns", "registry"), not "the encoding disagrees with s.141". (Note: this is from the manifest JSON, not the module diff or commit message, so it is offered as evidence, not as the decisive quote.)
- `git show 829ab1a255:statutes/ukpga/1992/4/141.yaml` is present and not in this commit's file list; it encodes `entitled_to_child_benefit_for_week` as `len(child_benefit_children_or_qualifying_young_persons_for_whom_person_responsible) > 0` — no take-up gate. The legal encoding was already correct and unchanged, so nothing law-facing was corrected here.
- Provision resolved through the pinned release (corpus commit 66dcb07c, provision file sha256 d6f79950…): s.141 reads "A person who is responsible for one or more children or qualifying young persons in any week shall be entitled, subject to the provisions of this Part of this Act, to a benefit (to be known as “child benefit") for that week…". So the first reader is factually right that s.141 says nothing about whether a family would claim, and the retired module's condition atom excerpt `"entitled to child benefit"` is not even a verbatim substring of s.141. That mis-grounded proof atom is why I did NOT return `not_a_defect`.

Why not `confirmed` (untraceable_branch): the untraceable-branch reading is literally satisfied (the `would_claim_child_benefit` gate is removed) but only incidentally — the fix removes the correctly-grounded s.141 import in the same stroke, and the same reason retires a module with no such branch. Reading it as a branch-removal fix misdescribes the unit of the change.

Live alternatives a reviewer should weigh:
1. `not_a_defect` — retirement as pure architecture/layering: the module was honestly self-labelled a "PolicyEngine-alignment surface", it passed the repo's proof validation at the time, and no rule was corrected. I rejected this only because of the false s.141 condition atom and the module summary presenting the take-up gate as part of the s.141 surface.
2. `confirmed` as the first reader had it, if the corpus counts "removes an unsourced branch, among other things" as untraceable_branch regardless of the change's unit.
3. `unclear` — defensible; the fix's stated reason never says the old encoding contradicted the source.

Corpus-design flag: this is a whole-module retirement (five modules, tests, and manifests deleted; `.axiom/toolchain.toml` bumped 0.2.621 → 0.2.647), screen-flagged on the `retire` verb. If the corpus is meant to be in-place fidelity corrections to rule modules, retirements may warrant their own bucket rather than a defect kind — the PR discussion frames them as debt removal ("the PolicyEngine wrapper surfaces were the biggest \"derived from another model rather than from law\" debt in the UK corpus"), and the author himself said "Ah I see I should have got the encoder to do this rather than claude... will refile".

verdict.justification: I tried to refute this as architecture-only pruning and could not: the deleted module declared `proof_validation: required: true` with `corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2008/794/118` and attached `kind: condition` / `kind: formula` proof atoms to `versions[0].formula`, so it asserted that reg 118 grounds its formula. Reading reg 118 through the pinned release (corpus uk-rulespec-2026-07-12, text sha 0bc17510) shows it is titled "Calculation of tariff income from capital" and does nothing but deem capital over £6,000 (£10,000 in prescribed accommodation) equivalent to £1 weekly income per complete £250 up to £16,000 — it defines no ESA award, no eligibility gate, and no subtraction from a reported receipt, so both the gate branch and the subtraction were ungrounded, and the actual reg 118 content already lived correctly and separately in `regulations/uksi/2008/794/118.yaml` (pre-existing at the parent commit, reusing the very same excerpts). The retirement manifest's own reason — "PolicyEngine model wrappers retired from the rules registry: survey/take-up constructs are consumer concerns; legal content lives in the statute and regulation modules" — plus the deletion of a whole rule and formula makes this a removal of encoded meaning with no source basis, not proof/metadata bookkeeping.

verdict.notes: Strongest surviving counter-reading, for a reviewer: the change could be called wrong_entity_or_scope, since the retirement reason frames it as a layering decision ("survey/take-up constructs are consumer concerns") and the taxonomy lists "output surface" under that kind. I kept untraceable_branch because nothing about the entity (Family), period, or population disagreed with a source — there was no source for the surface at all, and untraceable_branch explicitly covers "formulas grounded on the wrong provision" whose fix "removes or re-grounds" them. Second counter-reading: the module self-labelled as a "PolicyEngine-alignment surface", so one could argue it never claimed to encode reg 118's award rules; that is what holds my confidence at 0.72 rather than higher, but it is outweighed by the module's own required proof atoms citing reg 118 text for that formula. Supporting facts verified read-only: all three operands (`income_related_esa_eligible`, `reported_income_related_esa_for_year`, `income_related_esa_tariff_income_for_year`) are free inputs supplied only by the companion test file (`git grep` at parent c067a43138 over `policies/`), defined nowhere in law in the repo; the module carried no `imports:` (unlike the child-benefit and SDA wrappers in the same commit, which did import statute outputs, so those siblings are closer to true de-duplication and may warrant a different call). PR #44 review evidence is thin: Copilot errored out, and the maintainer comment "Ah I see I should have got the encoder to do this rather than claude... will refile" is about who produced the change, not about whether the encoding was wrong. Note the resolver reported `fix_time_corpus_match: provision_file_absent_at_corpus_ref`, so the provision text is from the earliest release after the toolchain corpus ref, not the exact fix-time slice; reg 118's text has been stable since 2008, so this does not change the reading.

The fix removes the whole ungrounded surface, which the kind definition explicitly covers ("the fix removes or re-grounds it, including formulas grounded on the wrong provision"), and the retirement manifest concedes the point ("legal content lives in the statute and regulation modules"). The residual doubt, which caps my confidence, is that this was a blanket class retirement of five PolicyEngine wrappers rather than a per-module fidelity finding.

The module's second proof atom quoted that ÷12 sentence verbatim to justify `max(0, hb_pre_cap - benefit_cap_reduction)`, and the first atom paraphrased the London-residence "in receipt of housing benefit" clause into "claimant receives housing benefit" to justify the `would_claim_housing_benefit` gate — so both atoms are mis-grounded, not merely imprecise excerpts. verdict.justification: The retired module's only unique content was an entitlement branch keyed on the survey input `reported_severe_disablement_allowance_for_year` — which carries no `kind: condition` proof atom at all, unlike its sibling wrappers in the same commit — and a `52` whose sole grounding was SI 2013/376 Sch 4 para 7, which the pinned corpus resolves to the Universal Credit housing-costs rule "Where the period in respect of which a renter is liable to make a relevant payment is not a month, an amount is to be calculated as the monthly equivalent… weekly payments are multiplied by 52 and divided by 12"; the module's excerpt truncates before "and divided by 12", converting a renter monthly-conversion rule into annualization authority for a disability benefit, and the rule's own `source:` field names a third instrument (Claims and Payments Regs 1987) that is not the cited path. The signed retire manifest states the reason as "survey/take-up constructs are consumer concerns; legal content lives in the statute and regulation modules", and the PR thread names the `reported_*`-input wrappers as model-derived rather than law-derived debt. Strongest counter-argument a reviewer should weigh: this is a wholesale retirement, framed architecturally ("consumer concerns", "legal content lives in the statute and regulation modules"), and no re-grounded SDA entitlement module replaces it in this commit, so someone could read it as a layering/scope decision rather than a fidelity correction; I rejected that because the retired content is affirmatively ungrounded (no condition atom; wrong-provision constant) and because the non-duplicated portion of the wrapper is precisely the ungrounded portion. Supporting detail worth noting: the deleted test expects 6206.20 = (103.85 + 15.50) x 52, i.e. everyone with reported receipt was paid the maximum rate *including* the higher-rate age-related addition — a further condition with no source behind it, same kind. verdict.justification: I could not refute the first reader's kind, and the evidence now settles what was ambiguous for them: the pinned corpus text of WRA 2012 s.8 reads "The amount of an award of universal credit is to be the balance of— the maximum amount (see subsection (2)), less the amounts to be deducted (see subsection (3))" with deductions defined solely as earned and unearned income, so the deleted formula's `- benefit_cap_reduction_for_year` term is bound by a required proof atom (excerpt "the amount of an award") to a provision containing neither a cap nor any reduction. The repo itself shows the re-grounding rather than mere deletion: the immediately preceding commit c067a43 encoded SI 2013/376 reg. 81 (benefit cap reduction, monthly, including the reg 81(2) childcare-element carve-out the wrapper's flat subtraction lacked), and the separately encoded statutes/ukpga/2012/5/8.yaml at the same citation path contains only max(0, maximum amount − deductions) with no cap term. That matches untraceable_branch as defined ("a value with no basis in the cited source ... including formulas grounded on the wrong provision", where "the fix removes or re-grounds it"). Mechanical and test_only are excluded because a rule, its formula, its output surface and its period were removed outright, and not_a_defect fails because the module made a proof-bound claim about s.8 that s.8's text does not support.
verdict.quote:
-    source: PolicyEngine UK universal_credit final receipt wrapper over Welfare Reform Act 2012 s.8 award amount
-          max(0, universal_credit_pre_benefit_cap_for_year - benefit_cap_reduction_for_year)
verdict.notes:
Refutation attempts and what survives, for the pruning reviewer:

1. "Mechanical / provenance-only" — fails. The retirement deletes a rule with a formula, an output (`universal_credit_annual_amount`), entity Family and period Year, plus its companion test file. Formulas and output surfaces did not stay the same, so the excerpt/citation-string carve-out does not apply. Note it is also not a citation-repointing fix: had the citation been the only problem, repointing to reg 81 would have sufficed.

2. "Not a defect, just dedup/architecture" — the strongest counter-case, and a reviewer may still prefer it. The commit message says only "their legal content lives in the statute and regulation modules", and the signed retirement manifest (.axiom/encoding-manifests/policies/govuk/universal-credit.json) gives a class-wide reason: "PolicyEngine model wrappers retired from the rules registry: survey/take-up constructs are consumer concerns; legal content lives in the statute and regulation modules". That boilerplate does not describe this module — the UC wrapper has no survey or take-up construct (its inputs are `universal_credit_pre_benefit_cap_for_year` and `benefit_cap_reduction_for_year`); the take-up language fits the child-benefit wrapper in the same commit, whose formula is `if would_claim_child_benefit: child_benefit_weekly_entitlement else: 0`. So the removal was driven by module class, not by a per-module fidelity finding, and the wrapper's arithmetic (post-cap UC = pre-cap UC less cap reduction, floored at nil) is defensible UK law under WRA 2012 s.96 / SI 2013/376 reg. 81. What defeats this reading is that the defect is judged against the *cited* source: the module's `corpus_citation_path` and its one formula proof atom are s.8 only, with `proof_validation: required: true`, and s.8 contains no cap.

3. Competing kinds considered and rejected as weaker. wrong_entity_or_scope has real support (summary: "This PolicyEngine-alignment surface returns the annual Universal Credit amount used by PolicyEngine UK and HBAI"; a consumer/reporting surface retired from a law registry), but entity (Family) and program (UC) are right, so the mis-grounded cap term is the sharper error. wrong_period_or_effective_date is a live secondary: the wrapper is `period: Year` with `effective_from: '0001-01-01'`, while s.8 and reg 81 both operate per monthly assessment period and the reg 81 module uses `effective_from: '2013-04-29'` — but annualization was the wrapper's declared purpose, not a misreading of the source. unrepresented_clause (reg 81(1)(b)/81(2) childcare-element carve-out) does not stick because the reduction entered as an opaque input.

4. Benchmark-shape caveat: the "fix" here is a whole-module deletion, so this case teaches "delete the surface" rather than "correct the branch". If the corpus is meant to contain localized formula corrections, prune it on that ground rather than on kind. Confidence is held at 0.62 because the fix message is generic and class-wide even though the diff and the source text are not ambiguous.

triage.commit_summary: The commit (squashed PR #87, three sub-commits) adds two net-new encoder-generated statutory modules — UC Regulations 2013 regulation 90 (individual/couple/apprentice minimum-income-floor thresholds) and National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015 regulation 4A (age-banded and apprentice hourly rates, importing reg 4's national living wage rate) — after corpus#224 ingested those provisions, and bumps the toolchain corpus ref so CI can resolve them. It then hand-wires a regulation 62 minimum income floor into the already-merged composed UC award pipeline behind a new `uc_pilot_is_gainfully_self_employed` flag that defaults to false, so the pre-existing supplied-earned-income path and all eight pre-existing award test cases are byte-for-byte unchanged.

modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix pipeline never applied the regulation 62 minimum income floor to a gainfully self-employed claimant's earned income, but it stated that omission in its own comments and required the caller to supply already-floored earnings, so the gap reads as a declared interface boundary rather than an encoded meaning that contradicted the source.
modules.triage_notes: This is the only module in the commit with a pre-fix state, and it is the borderline case the screen flagged. Evidence AGAINST calling it a fidelity defect: (a) the pre-fix module explicitly declared the exclusion — the removed comment read "For gainful self-employment the caller supplies uc_pilot_earned_income_monthly already floored to the regulation 62 minimum income floor (the regulation 90 thresholds are not in the corpus slice, so the floor cannot be computed here)" and the removed prose block listed the MIF under "Deliberately excluded"; (b) the new path is gated on a brand-new input flag defaulting to false, so no previously computable output changes — the companion test diff adds `uc_pilot_is_gainfully_self_employed: false` and `uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_notional_deduction_monthly: 0` to all eight pre-existing cases with every expected output unchanged, and only four new cases (below-floor, above-floor, couple, non-gainful) were added; (c) the commit body itself says the change is "preserving the existing supplied-input path"; (d) the post-fix module is still partial and declares NEW exclusions (start-up-period exemption, reduced expected hours under reg 88, the reg 90 apprenticeship and reg 3(3) single-claim couple thresholds), which is characteristic of a scope extension rather than a correction. Evidence FOR: reg 62 does require the deeming, so a caller feeding raw self-employment earnings would previously have gotten an award too high, and the PR frames it as closing a "gap". Per the task rule that added scope a module never claimed is at most `unclear`, I did not label it `fidelity`; a reviewer should probably prune it. The new logic itself looks source-consistent (strict `<` against the threshold matches reg 90(1)'s "equal to or exceed", couple floor = 2x individual per reg 90(3)(a), 52/12 monthly conversion, reg 62(5) notional deduction supplied and floored at zero), so there is no secondary defect hiding in the hunk. Module is a hand-edited `uk/policies/` pilot module signed via `sign-applied-files`, not `module.kind: composition`. The commit also touched only the three encoding manifests and `.axiom/toolchain.toml` (corpus ref bump) outside the modules and tests; I did not need to resolve the provision text because the classification question here is scope/authorial-intent, not what the source says.

triage.commit_summary: The commit extends the already-merged composed Child Benefit pipeline (rulespec-uk#76) with eight new rules encoding the High Income Child Benefit Charge (ITEPA 2003 ss.681B-681H) — the £60,000 threshold, the £200 taper step, the 0.01 per-step fraction, the floor'd appropriate-percentage points, the 100%-capped charged fraction, the floor'd charge, and a new post-charge net Child Benefit output — plus test cases, a re-signed encoding manifest, and toolchain pin bumps. It was done because the ITEPA charge provisions had only just been ingested into the corpus (axiom-corpus#221), unblocking the documented gap tracked in rulespec-uk#75 so the UKMOD oracle can compare net Child Benefit against UKMOD's paid bch_s rather than a reconstructed pre-charge figure.

modules.description_quote: This pilot deliberately encodes only the section 141 entitlement (the gross, pre-charge amount). The High Income Child Benefit Charge (ITEPA 2003 sections 681B-681H, introduced by Finance Act 2012 Schedule 1) that claws Child Benefit back through the income-tax system for a partner with adjusted net income over the threshold is NOT encoded here: those charge provisions are not yet in the Axiom corpus
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix module did not encode the ITEPA 2003 ss.681B-681H High Income Child Benefit Charge, but it never claimed to — it declared only the SSCBA 1992 s.141 gross entitlement, explicitly and correctly documented the HICBC omission as out of scope, and had the oracle compare against UKMOD's reconstructed pre-charge figure, so nothing it did encode disagreed with its cited sources.
modules.triage_notes: Recommend pruning: this looks like scope addition, not a fidelity correction. Evidence: (1) I diffed the pre-existing block byte-for-byte — the two imports and all seven pre-existing rules (uk_cb_pilot_benefit_weeks_per_year, _enhanced_weekly_rate, _other_weekly_rate, _number_of_children, _number_of_other_children, _weekly_entitlement, _annual_entitlement) are IDENTICAL across parent 8ed2dffb and eb61ae53; no formula, parameter, version, effective date, entity, or unit of any existing rule changed. The whole module diff is (a) rewritten module.source_verification.rationale and module.summary prose, (b) three new corpus_citation_paths for ss.681B/681C/681H, and (c) eight appended rules. (2) The added provisions were not among the pre-fix module's cited sources — they are newly ingested corpus content (axiom-corpus#221), so the pre-fix encoding could not have represented them and the removed prose says so explicitly (quoted above). (3) The pre-fix module was internally consistent: it exposed gross entitlement and the oracle compared it against UKMOD bch_s + bchrd_s (pre-charge); the fix changes the comparison surface to net, which is a new output, not a corrected one. (4) I classified as 'unclear' rather than 'not a defect' only because the rubric caps such changes at 'unclear'; defect_kind unrepresented_clause is the hypothetical kind if a reviewer decides the pipeline's implied contract was 'Child Benefit as paid' all along, in which case the missing clawback clause would be the defect. That reading is weak given the explicit written exclusion. Provision read: I resolved uk/statute/ukpga/2003/1/681C through the pinned corpus release and the text confirms the new encoding ('L is £60,000; X is £200', '100%, or if less, the percentage determined by the formula', and the s.681C(3) round-down of both the charge amount and the percentage), so the added content is itself faithful — no new defect introduced. Commit also touches non-module files (.axiom/encoding-manifests/... re-signed manifest, .axiom/toolchain.toml pin bumps to corpus 6bc9344 and axiom_encode 0.2.1168) and the companion test file (six new cases at ANI £20k/£70k/£80k/£90k); those are bookkeeping and verification, not module semantics. PR #84 has no reviews and no review or issue comments, so there is no maintainer/reviewer statement calling this a correction — the only stated reason, in both commit body and PR body, is 'Extends ... with' and 'Closes #75', the language of a tracked gap being filled.

verdict.justification: A structural comparison of the pre and post module shows every pre-existing rule is identical (uk_cb_pilot_benefit_weeks_per_year, _enhanced_weekly_rate, _other_weekly_rate, _number_of_children, _number_of_other_children, _weekly_entitlement, _annual_entitlement all unchanged in formula, version, effective date, entity, dtype and unit); `imports` and `format` are unchanged, and the only edits are the module rationale/summary prose plus eight newly appended HICBC rules and a new net-of-charge output. Nothing the pre-fix module encoded disagreed with its cited sources: it cited only SSCBA 1992 s.141, SI 2006/965 reg.2 and SI 2013/376 Sch.4 para.7, labelled its output "the gross entitlement before the High Income Child Benefit Charge", stated the omission explicitly with an issue link, and had the oracle compare against UKMOD's reconstructed pre-charge figure (bch_s + bchrd_s). The HICBC lives in a different Act (ITEPA 2003 ss.681B-681H) that this commit adds to corpus_citation_paths for the first time, and the commit had to bump `axiom_corpus_ref` to the HICBC ingest merge because those provisions were only just ingested — so the clause could not have been an unrepresented clause of a cited source. This is new scope and a new output surface the module never claimed, not a correction of wrong semantics, so it fails the unrepresented_clause test rather than merely being under-evidenced.
verdict.quote: adds a **post-charge net Child Benefit** output so the axiom-oracles `uk-child-benefit` suite can compare net Child Benefit against UKMOD's paid `bch_s` directly (UKMOD nets its separately-reported clawback `bchrd_s` into `bch_s`).
verdict.notes: Verification performed: parsed both blobs (parent 8ed2dffb0a vs eb61ae53e8) and diffed rule-by-rule — 0 removed rules, 0 changed rules, 8 added rules (uk_cb_pilot_hicbc_income_threshold, _hicbc_taper_step, _hicbc_taper_rate_per_step, _adjusted_net_income, _hicbc_appropriate_percentage_points, _hicbc_charged_fraction, _hicbc_charge, _annual_entitlement_net_of_charge); only module.source_verification and module.summary changed at module level. Commit-wide stat is consistent with additive scope: test file +69/-0, plus a re-signed encoding manifest and a toolchain pin bump (both mechanical). The first reader's quote is the pre-fix disclaimer, which is itself the evidence that the omission was declared and deliberate ("those charge provisions are not yet in the Axiom corpus"), and under the repo's grounding rule encoding the £60,000 threshold before the ITEPA ingest would have been ungroundable. A reviewer wanting to keep this in the corpus would have to argue the module's stated purpose ("UKMOD oracle slice") implicitly claimed net Child Benefit — but the pre-fix text pins the comparison to the reconstructed pre-charge bch_s + bchrd_s, so that argument fails. I did not need to resolve the ITEPA provision text, since the verdict turns on what the pre-fix module claimed and cited, not on the correctness of the newly added HICBC arithmetic (which is unrelated to whether the old state was wrong). Recommend pruning this candidate from the real-defect corpus, or retaining it only as a labeled negative example of added coverage.

item.screen_reason: Source-grounding fix on merged Carer's Allowance module: annualization rule's source changes from 'PolicyEngine UK annual benefit wrapper' to the Claims and Payments Regulations citation and a formula proof atom grounded in uksi/2013/376 sch 4 para 7 is added (mis-grounded proof).

triage.commit_summary: The commit re-labels the `carers_allowance_weeks_in_year` helper in policies/govuk/carers-allowance.yaml from the free-text source "PolicyEngine UK annual benefit wrapper" to "Social Security (Claims and Payments) Regulations 1987 weekly-benefit annualization rule", flips that rule's single proof atom from kind `formula` to kind `amount`, and adds a new `formula` proof atom on `carers_allowance_annual_amount` citing uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/schedule/4/paragraph/7 with the excerpt "weekly payments are multiplied by 52". No formula, parameter value, version, effective date, input, output, entity, or scope changed; the only other file touched is the encoder apply manifest (hashes, encoder version 0.2.616 -> 0.2.617, signature), so the commit is a provenance/proof-metadata pass over an already-merged module rather than a correction of encoded meaning.

modules.description_quote: Align Carer's Allowance annualization helper
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing in the pre-fix encoded meaning disagreed with the source: the helper already evaluated to 52 and the annual formula already read weekly_rate * weeks_in_year both before and after, so the commit changed only the free-text source label and proof-atom provenance, and the new label it introduces ('Social Security (Claims and Payments) Regulations 1987') does not even match the provision actually cited (Universal Credit Regulations 2013 Sch 4 para 7).
modules.triage_notes:
Only module in the commit; whole diff is 31 lines and I read it in full plus both pre- and post-fix files. Three changes, all provenance: (1) rules[carers_allowance_weeks_in_year].source string swapped from 'PolicyEngine UK annual benefit wrapper' to 'Social Security (Claims and Payments) Regulations 1987 weekly-benefit annualization rule'; (2) that rule's proof atom kind flipped formula -> amount; (3) a duplicate-grounding proof atom (kind: formula, same citation path and excerpt) appended to carers_allowance_annual_amount. The parameter value 52, the derived formula, effective_from '2026-04-06', entity Person, periods, imports, and the module summary are byte-identical pre and post, which is why this is mechanical (provenance) and not fidelity under the stated rule that excerpt/citation-string corrections are mechanical.

Provision WAS read via resolve_provision.py (corpus release uk-legislation-pilot, corpus commit 66dcb07, provision file data/corpus/provisions/uk/regulation/2026-06-03-uk-universal-credit.jsonl line 43, expression date 2026-04-30, fix_time_corpus_match=same_body). uksi/2013/376 Sch 4 para 7 is the Universal Credit Regulations 2013 housing-costs-for-renters monthly-equivalent rule: 'Where any relevant payment is to be taken into account under paragraph 6, the amount of that payment is to be calculated as a monthly amount... weekly payments are multiplied by 52 and divided by 12'. So two things about the post-fix state are worse, not better: the new source label names SI 1987/1968 while the citation path is SI 2013/376, and the atom excerpt truncates '...multiplied by 52 and divided by 12' to '...multiplied by 52', turning a monthly-equivalent conversion for renters' rent into an apparent annualization warrant for a Carer's Allowance benefit amount. This matches the screen flag's own '(mis-grounded proof)' note: the commit adds a mis-grounded proof atom rather than removing one, so it is not an untraceable_branch fix.

Follow-up confirming the mis-grounding: commit 60501ec (2026-06-10, 'ground policy surfaces in ingested sources') rewrites the same rule's source to 'Universal Credit Regulations 2013, Schedule 4 paragraph 7 (weekly amounts converted over 52 weeks)', flips the atom kind back to formula, and changes the excerpt to 'calculated as a monthly amount' - i.e. a later commit corrected the label this commit introduced. That commit also adds a real missing clause (carers_allowance_weekly_earnings_limit, GBP 204) and drops entity/period, but that is a different commit and out of scope here.

Parent commit 06d7bd1 is the PR-37 merge that added the module; PR 37's body describes only that addition (validation commands and an EFRS oracle comparison with zero mismatches) and says nothing about this follow-up change - there are no reviews, review comments, or issue comments on the PR, and the commit body is empty, so the only quotable description is the commit subject, which is generic. No test files changed in this commit (the module's companion .test.yaml is untouched), consistent with no behavioral change. Other file: .axiom/encoding-manifests/policies/govuk/carers-allowance.json (applied-file sha256, generated_output_sha256, axiom_encode 0.2.616->0.2.617, generated_at, HMAC signature) - pure bookkeeping.

Doubt worth a reviewer's eye: one could argue the pre-fix 'PolicyEngine UK annual benefit wrapper' source made the 52 an ungrounded modeling convention and that re-grounding it is an untraceable_branch fix. I rejected that because the corpus_citation_path on that rule's proof atom was already uksi/2013/376/schedule/4/paragraph/7 before the commit (only the human-readable label said PolicyEngine), and because the replacement grounding is itself wrong - the commit does not establish any statutory basis for annualizing Carer's Allowance by 52.

item.subject: (screen-flagged) Re-anchors merged NI s.8 module's source grounding: every corpus_citation_path moves from uk/statute/legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1992/4/section/8 to uk/statute/ukpga/1992/4/8, proof atoms are replaced, and companion tests are rewritten.
item.screen_reason: Re-anchors merged NI s.8 module's source grounding: every corpus_citation_path moves from uk/statute/legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1992/4/section/8 to uk/statute/ukpga/1992/4/8, proof atoms are replaced, and companion tests are rewritten.

triage.commit_summary: The commit re-ran axiom-encode over Social Security Contributions and Benefits Act 1992 s.8 so the single NI module statutes/ukpga/1992/4/8.yaml keeps its RuleSpec path while every source_verification and proof-atom corpus_citation_path moves from the un-normalized `uk/statute/legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1992/4/section/8` to the normalized `uk/statute/ukpga/1992/4/8`, with the module summary rewritten, condition/exception proof atoms replaced by import atoms, and the companion tests regenerated with renamed cases and new (still self-consistent) input/output numbers. No rate, threshold, effective date, entity, period, unit, input set, or output set changed, and the one formula that was rewritten (main band) is algebraically identical to the version it replaced, so the change is provenance/regeneration rather than a correction of encoded meaning.

modules.description_quote: Re-encodes Social Security Contributions and Benefits Act 1992 section 8 through axiom-encode so the NI component surface keeps the existing RuleSpec path while using the normalized corpus citation path `uk/statute/ukpga/1992/4/8`.
modules.pre_fix_wrong_because: Nothing in the pre-fix encoding disagreed with s.8: the only defect was provenance, in that source_verification and every proof atom cited the un-normalized corpus path uk/statute/legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1992/4/section/8 instead of the normalized uk/statute/ukpga/1992/4/8.
modules.triage_notes: Only module in the commit (chunk covers index 0 of 1; bundle also has statutes/ukpga/1992/4/8.test.yaml and .axiom/encoding-manifests/statutes/ukpga/1992/4/8.json). The whole file was re-emitted by the encoder, so the diff is large, but I compared pre (a26968f5) and post (cee3c3d1) line by line: format, module.proof_validation, all five rule names, kinds, dtypes, entity (Person), period (Week), unit (GBP), inputs, outputs, parameter values (0.08, 0.02) and effective_from dates (2024-04-06, 2011-04-06, 2024-04-06, 2024-04-06) are all unchanged. The one substantive-looking edit is main_primary_class_1_contribution's formula, which went from `main_primary_percentage * min(max(0, earnings - PT), max(0, UEL - PT))` to `main_primary_percentage * max(0, min(earnings, UEL) - PT)`; these are algebraically identical for every ordering of earnings/PT/UEL (including UEL < PT, where both yield 0), so it is a reformulation, not a correction. Other changes are metadata: module summary rewritten from the raw heading-plus-subsection-(3) excerpt to a prose restatement; rule `source` strings loosened from s.8(2)(a)/s.8(2)(b) to s.8(2) and from s.8(1), (3) to s.8(1); proof `condition` and `exception` atoms dropped and `import` atoms added (the displacement conditions for s.6(6) and ss.116-120 still appear in both component formulas, so the encoded logic is unchanged). The companion tests were renamed and re-parameterized (earnings 1200/PT 200/UEL 1000 -> earnings 1000/PT 200/UEL 800, expected 64/4/68 -> 48/4/52); both sets of numbers satisfy both the pre- and post-fix formulas, so the test rewrite is regeneration, not an expectation fix. Commit message body is empty; the PR body (#9) states the purpose is the normalized citation path plus the axiom-encode#531 path-aliasing dependency, and reports a PE-UK oracle run with 0 mismatches, which is consistent with no behavioral change. No PR reviews or review comments exist. I did not need Step 4 (provision resolution) because no numeric value, boundary, clause, date, or scope changed; if a reviewer wants it, the decisive question would only be whether the band cap wording supports the min(earnings, UEL) framing, which both versions already encode identically. Follow-up history on this path: only f6b6048 'Move UK content under uk/', a relocation, so no later fidelity repair contradicts this reading.
